[Man] In particular, “Jangsaengpo Old Town” which features a diorama-like reproduction of people carrying out everyday activities is the most popular attraction among tourists.  [Woman] From the butchery where people would butcher freshly caught whales, then onto the whale restaurant that used to sell boiled whale meat! Walking through every single street makes me feel like I’ve been transported back in time to the bustling village of Jangsaengpo.  [Man] At one point, ‘being the county mayor or being the harpoon gunner’ was a legitimate debate.That’s how popular whaling was Another popular feature at the village is the harpoon gunners home. Wouldn’t it be fun to actually see a real harpoon gun?  [Woman] Was harpooning like the next up-and-coming job? I bet people were rewarded quite handsomely because the success rate was so high.  [Man] Back then, people could tell which ship had caught a whale just by listening to the horn. Watching butchers butchering a whale was like a game for the village people.   [Woman] As the butchering comes to an end, the sun begins to set. I think I can almost hear someone’s mom yelling, “Come on in for dinner.” Jangsaengpo is an old town that brings up the nostalgia of home and feels warm and generous.  [Man] When the time comes, whales travel the East Sea for thousands of kilometers, and return to the waters of Jangsaengpo. The reason why whales return to Jangsaengpo in Ulsan is because it is their home.   [Woman] Jangsaengpo, on the shores of the East Sea, used to be the home of gray whales. Today, the gray whale is an endangered species. Why did gray whales call Jangsaengpo their home?  [Interview with Park Chang Hye-gyeong, a Cultural and Tourism Commentator working in the Ulsan area. ] The tidal changes in Ulsan are not as severe as some other regions. The water is relatively shallow, and has a higher degree of salinity. These conditions make Jangsaengpo the perfect place to give birth to new calves. People also believe whales would have eaten the seaweed in Ulsan, which grows in vast quantities, to recover after giving birth to their babies.  [Woman] Apart from Jangsaengpo, you can also see whales migrating back to Korea at ‘Cape Ganjeolgot which is the very first place in Korea where you can see the sunrise. Cape Ganjeolgot is such a popular destination, right?  [Man] Tourists from all over country head over there on New Year’s Day. Along with Jangsaengpo, Bangeojinhang Port in Ulsan and Guryongpo Port in Pohang are famous for whale-watching. Bangeojinhang is also known for its modern history street. So, taking a tour of Bangeojinhang after Ganjeolgot and Jangsaeongpo might just be the final touch that finalizes your travel plans. Watch the sunrise at Cape Ganjeolgot, watch some whales at Jangsaengpo, and learn about local history in Bangeojinhang.   [Woman] If you walk along the seawall at Bangeojinhang, you’ll get to see sculptures inspired by whales.Apparently, they were created on the theme of “Wish towards the sea.” If you look closer, though, you might realize that they are reproductions of illustrations from the Petroglyphs at the Bangudae Terrace.   [Man] Thousands of years ago, prehistoric people used to hunt whales and draw their achievements on the Petroglyphs at the Bangudae Terrace.  [Woman] Fishermen from Jangsaengpo also set sail into the open ocean with dreams of catching whales.For the locals, whales were a symbol of hope and dreams.  [Man] The East Sea, where all the wales used to be, has a warmth that makes it feel like home. Like the whales returning home to the East Sea, we hope you can travel to Ulsan, with hopes and dreams of a better tomorrow.

stories.title: Cheonjeon-ri Petroglyphs of Ulju
stories.audioTitle: The first petroglyphs discovered in Korea
stories.script: The first petroglyphs discovered in Korea   Cheonjeon-ri Petroglyphs of Ulju are the first petroglyphs found in the country. Petroglyphs refer to images carved on rocks by prehistoric peoples. The Cheonjeon-ri Petroglyphs were discovered near upper Daegokcheon Stream in December, 1970. The rectangular rock with the carvings is about 9.5-meters wide and 2.7-meters long. It is inclined by about 15 degrees downward and does not receive much sunlight, so it was well preserved from natural weathering. The images engraved on top of the rock, which were presumably created in the Bronze Age, depict people, deer, snakes, birds and fish, as well as geometrical patterns, such as spirals and lozenges, among others. These are interpreted as religious symbols that were inscribed in prayer for good harvests from hunting and fishing, the main sources of livelihood back then. The figures at the bottom of the rock, which are assumed to have been formed in the Silla Dynasty period, illustrate patterns of a cavalcade, boats with sails, horses and dragons, as well as others, along with written words with over 800 characters. Of the characters, some 300 were identified to have been engraved during the reign of King Beopheung of the Silla period. The letters indicate names and titles of 'hwarang' or an elite youth group in the era, which have been of great help to the research on the Silla history.

stories.title: Taehwagang Grand Park
stories.audioTitle: The simnidaebat field that stretches along the crystal clear stream
stories.script: The simnidaebat field that stretches along the crystal clear stream   Taehwagang Grand Park is the largest waterside park in the country. It was created along Taehwagang River, which runs right through downtown Ulsan. Taehwagang River was once dying with foul smells due to industrialization, but the restoration project that continued for some 10 years from 2002 transformed the river into a clear stream with first class water quality. With the revival of the river, the waterside field was reborn as Taehwagang Grand Park where a dense green shade with bamboos, rape flowers and forage barley flourish. In particular, the bamboo field created between Taehwagyo Bridge and Samhogyo Bridge stretches as long as 4km, thus the name 'simnidaebat field', which means a 4-kilometer-long bamboo field. The origin of the bamboo field dates back to the Japanese colonial era when the residents began to plant bamboos to prevent frequent floods that caused heavy damage to the farmlands. The bamboo forest is very popular as a walking course that is green throughout the year. It is refreshing to stroll under the cool shades of tall bamboo trees while listening to the sound of the leaves rustling with the wind. Also, the park is full of colorful flowers. There are flower gardens planted with seven flower species including poppies, cornflowers and gypsophila. When the spring comes, as many as 60 million blossoms are in full bloom all around the place, which just looks  like a paradise.

stories.title: Taehwagang Grand Park
stories.audioTitle: King Seongjong’s favorite pavilion Taehwaru and Simnidaesup (Simni Bamboo Grove) at the Taehwagang Grand Park
stories.script: The Simnidaesup (Simni Bamboo Grove) at the Taehwagang Grand Park sits along Taehwagang River, a major river that flows through the heart of Ulsan.      In summer, the Park is home to more than 8,000 White Herons, and in winter, it offers shelter for 100,000 or so Rooks and Jackdaws. Moreover, Taehwagang Grand Park is well-known for having the largest bamboo forest trail in the country  Taehwaru Pavilion offers panoramic views of Taehwagang River. But it has more than just beautiful views. It also has plenty of secrets to tell.  King Seongjong was the sixth monarch of the Goryeo Dynasty. One year, on his way to Seorabeol (capital city of the Shilla Dynasty), the King made his way to Ulsan. There, he hosted a banquet at the Taehwaru Pavilion which was hailed as one of the eight must-see attractions in the Ulju region at the time.   Taehwaru Pavilion was originally built as a bell tower for Taehwasa Temple by Buddhist monk Jajang during the reign of Queen Seondeok of Shilla.   Thanks to its outstanding views, Taehwaru Pavilion has been quoted in more than 100 poems written by top poets in Korean history such as Kim Si-seup, Kwon Geun, and Seo Geo-jeong.    According to the History of Goryeo, King Seongjong hosted a banquet and ate a large fish caught from the sea.  Historians have hypothesized that Taehwaru Pavilion was near the East Sea, rather than the Taehwagang River.  Based on this theory, some have argued that the large fish the King ate may have been a whale which used to inhabit the waters off the coast of Ulsan since prehistoric times.            Meanwhile, the dense bamboo forest of Simnidaesup (Simni Bamboo Grove) has become a popular place for healing and recuperation along with Bomun Tourist Complex in Gyeongju and Sabang Memorial Park in Pohang.

stories.title: Taehwaru Pavilion
stories.audioTitle: The pavilion with a clear view towards Taehwagang River
stories.script: The pavilion with a clear view towards Taehwagang River   When you walk along Taehwagang River, your eyes will be drawn to the Taehwaru Pavilion built on top of the cliff over the river. The pavilion has a spectacular view and is one of the three pavilions in the Yeongnam region, coupled with Chokseongnu Pavilion of Jinju and Yeongnamnu Pavilion of Miryang. It is written in <Samguk Yusa(or History of the Three Nations)> that Jajang Yulsa, a Buddhist monk of the Silla Dynasty period, established a temple called Taehwasa and created the Taehwaru Pavilion in the precincts during the reign of Queen Seondeok. However, the pavilion was presumed to have been completely destroyed during the Japanese invasion of Korea in 1592. Regrettably, there was no record about the shape and style of the structure, so it was newly constructed in April, 2014 with reference to the traditional entasis (a slight swelling or bulge in the middle of a column) of the Goryeo Dynasty period when the pavilion was in its heyday. The pillars and rafters of Taehwaru Pavilion were carved with shapes of dragons, as there was a legend that a dragon lived under the water beneath the pavilion. And, the edges of the eaves have carvings of the face of 'cheoyong', the main character of a famous ancient tale of the city. The overall architecture features many curves and delicate arrangement, showing a simple and elegant appearance. When you stand on the second floor of the pavilion, you can see the clear view of the long stream of Taehwagang River and the wide bamboo field in Taehwagang Grand Park.

stories.title: Seongsan Ilchulbong
stories.audioTitle: UNESCO World Heritage Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak)
stories.script: UNESCO World Heritage Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak)  Seongsan Ilchulbong has been long known as the best scenic beauty among 10 Yeongju Scenic Views. Its picturesque beauty has been recognized by the world and was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage in 2007, and as a World Geopark. It is indeed the best tourist attraction site in Jeju where over one million people visit each year.   Seongsan Ilchulbong was created as the magma underground combined with water and suddenly erupted about five thousand years ago. It is called ‘the standard of hydro-volcanic studies’ and possesses high volcanic geological values. What is worth noting here is the various structures of stratification and bomb sack. It is not too much to say that Seongsan Ilchulbong is a natural learning field for geology.    Not only that, Seongsan Ilchulbong induces beautiful emotions from any angle, be that from the sky or from the ocean, and all year around. You will be deeply moved by its magical scenic view. At the foot of Seongsan Ilchulbong, there is a rock engraved with the poem <The Good Old Seongsanpo Sea> by poet Saeng-Jin Lee, which will remind you of the meaning of Seongsan Ilchulbong.    Must-sees at Seongsan Ilchulbong, which will lure you more and more every time you see it~!  First, hiking at Seongsan Ilchulbong~! It takes approximately 30 minutes to walk from the parking lot to the crater at the top. You must see Deunggyeongdol Rock and the crest on your way up.  The legend has it that Grandmother Seolmundae who created Jeju used to do needlework on Deunggyeongdol Rock. Furthermore, you can find the traces of Ilgyeondae at the crest, from which chief masters of Jeju used to enjoy watching sunrise.  It will be a more valuable hiking experience if you looked at Seongsan Ilchulbong with understanding of its volcanic ecological characteristics and legends.   Second, the diving and fishing demonstration of women divers at Wumutgae~! Located at the foot of Seongsan Ilchulbong, women divers demonstrate diving and fishing twice a day at Wumutgae Beach. It will be a valuable event with which you will be able to feel the strength of Jeju women divers that have weathered the fierce sea of Jeju.   Third, Gwangchigi Beach~! You can feel the grandness of Seongsan Ilchulbong while looking the fortress walls floating on the sea at Gwangchigi Beach. Where the sand and waves meet fiercely, Gwangchigi Beach will resonate in your heart.   Like the beautiful sunrise that beams red light which springs out from the sea, and sunrise that rises through darkness, we wish that you will be able to dream a new hope for tomorrow at Seongsan Ilchulbong.   Subtitles The rock engraved with Lee Saeng-Jin Deunggyeongdol Rock The Trace of Ilgyeondae Wumutgae Beach Gwangchigi Beach The Sunrise at Seongsan Ilchulbong  Hiking Trails at Seongsan Ilchulbong

stories.title: Hangpaduri Hangmong Historic Site
stories.audioTitle: The Relic of Sambyeolcho of Goryeo Dynasty
stories.script: The Relic of Sambyeolcho of Goryeo Dynasty  (A Documentary Painting of Sambyeolcho)  Located in Goseongnam-gil, Aewol-eup, Jeju-si, Hangpaduri Hangmong Historic Site has a special historic meaning as Sambyeolcho, a special capital defense unit, strongly resisted the Mongol invasion until the last possible moment. In their effort to defend against invaders, they passed Ganghwa Island and Jin Island and finally came to Jeju and built the Hangpaduri Fortress. Here, you will be reminded of the meaning of Sambyeolcho.   Introduction of Hangpaduri Hangmong Historic Site  (A Documentary Painting at the Exhibition Hall)  Korea has been invaded numerously for the last 2000 years.   (Sambyeolcho)  Among them, Goyreo’s resistance against Mongol invasion was the longest defense struggle in Korean history, which continued for over 40 years.   Sambyeolcho was the main force and the last soldiers of the battle against Mongolia. In 1273, Sambyeolcho came to Jeju after Jin Island was captured and built the Hangpaduri Fortress as their base. They resisted for two more years against the enemy and fought until their deaths.   In 1977, Hangpaduri Hangmong Historical Site was designated as a National Historic Remains No. 396. A Hangmongsooneui memorial monument and exhibition halls at Hangpduri Hangmong Historic Site show the tragic history.  Places you must visit – Subtitles IN Let the image drift away)  Things you should not miss at Hangpaduri Hangmong Historic Site where you can feel Korean history of resisting against Mongol invasion.   First, Hangpaduri Mud Fortress~! It is the only mud fortress in Jeju, which was originally built as a double structure consisting of inside and outside fortresses.    The outside fortress was about approximately 6 km long and the circumference of the inside fortress was about 700 m, but only some parts of the outside fortress have been restored.   The mud fortress in Hangpaduri is distinguished from other fortresses made of stones.   Things you should not miss at Hangpaduri Hangmong Historic Site Second, Jangsu Spring~!  There are many places around Hangpaduri Fortress that have stories related to Sambyeolcho, and Jangsu Spring is one of them.   Jangsu Spring is a spring water where General Kim Tong-Jeong jumped and landed, leaving his footprints from which the spring gushed out. The story tells that when General Kim Tong-Jeong was fleeing the fortress, he jumped over the fortress wall and his foot got stuck in a stone and left a mark.   Still bubbling up between the stones, Jangsu Spring continues to flow without drying up.   Things you should not miss at Hangpaduri Hangmong Historic Site Third, the stone hit by arrows~!  When Sambyeolcho soldiers were training archery, they used this tone as a target. It is a big basalt stone with several holes on it showing how strong Sambyeolcho was back in the time.   Hangpaduri Hangmong Historic Site embraces the traces of Sambyeolcho. It is a valuable historic site that reminds us of the history.

stories.title: Jeongbangpokpo Falls
stories.script: Jeongbangpokpo Falls is the only coastal waterfall in Korea, cascading directly into the sea. It is considered one of the three renowned waterfalls of Jeju Island along with Cheonjeyeon and Cheonjiyeon. While the latter two waterfalls are renowned for their powerful currents, Jeongbang is celebrated with its elegance, gently descending in a spectrum of colors, shimmering brightly.  Legend has it that long ago, a cluster of gold clouds emerged from the ocean, from which a gold dragon emerged. The dragon gazed into the water for a while before joyfully dancing and disappearing.  During your visit, make sure not to miss the rock bearing the inscription of Seobulgwacha. Seobul, a rabbit character from various Korean folktales, embarked on a journey to Jeju alongside thousands of young boys and girls under the orders of Chinese Emperor Qin Chi Huang. Their quest was to find the herb of eternal youth. When Seobul saw the Jeongbangpokpo Falls, he was enchanted by the mesmerizing scenery of it and left an inscription on the rock, stating “Seobul is passing by here.” Some speculate that the name of the city, “Seogwipo,” might have originated from this tale.  Sonammeori of Jeongbangpokpo Falls is associated with a somber history. Between 1947 and 1954, during an uprising and armed repression, over ten thousand people were killed and lost. Sonammeori is known as the site where most of those subjected to summary execution were sacrificed.   Jeongbangpokpo Falls is also renowned for its mineral water, considered one of the four best mineral water alongside Manyeon Falls in Hwasun, Surak Falls in Gurye, and Yakdae Falls in Cheongdo. On approximately July 15th in the lunar calendar, during the Buddhist All Souls’ Day, people often visit Jeongbangpokpo Falls to drink and bathe in its mineral-rich waters. This practice is a folk remedy believed to alleviate arthritis and neuralgia. It’s recommended to try taking a sip before leaving.

stories.title: Oedolgae Sea Stack
stories.script: Oedolgae Sea Stack derives its name from ‘a lonely rock’ as it stands solitary amidst the sea. Estimated to have formed 1.5 million years ago from cooling lava ejected during a volcanic eruption, the rock is categorized as a ‘sea stack’ and recognized as Tangible Cultural Property No. 79.  Oedolgae Sea Stack is adorned with various nicknames, one being the ‘General Rock.’ In the late Goryeo period, Mokhos of Won rebels caused turmoil in Jeju. General Choi Young disguised Oedolgae Sea Stack to resemble a giant general to intimidate the rebels taking refuge on Beomsum Island. When the Mokhos saw the massive general, they were frightened and started committing suicide, earning the rock its moniker.  It is also referred to as ‘Halmang Rock,’ ‘Halmang’ being Jeju dialect for 'old lady.’ The name originates from a local legend about an elderly couple. The husband, a fisherman, once went out to sea on a good fishing day but encountered a storm on his way back and got lost at sea. The old lady waited for him endlessly and ultimately turned into a rock due to the prolonged wait.  At the top of the rock lies an extensive grass field while the surrounding area is a popular fishing spot. The breathtaking scenery behind Oedolga Rock at sunrise is truly mesmerizing. Jeju Olle Route 7, beginning at Oedolgae and ending at Wolpyeong Port, further enhances Oedolgae’s appeal as a must-visit destination.

stories.title: Yongmeorihaean Coast
stories.script: Moving closer to the ocean along Sanbangsan Mountain, a rugged cliff resembling a dragon plunging into the sea comes into view.  Yongmeorihaean Coast is the oldest hydro volcanic formations in Jeju. Volcanic ashes erupted from craters, forming different colors and slopes. Layers of sandstone were stacked for tens of millions of years, forming the peculiar undulating cliffs. They were born after the numberless times of the waves bumping against and wearing off the cooled lava.  Legend has it that Yongmeorihaean Coast symbolized the spirit of an emperor destined to rule the world. Upon learning this, the Chinese Emperor Qin Shi Huang dispatched a man named Hojongdan to sever the dragon’s head. Arriving at the coast, Hojongdan cut off the tail of the dragon, and then attempted to strike its head. As he moved forward, red blood rose, and the mountain began to weep, the tears flowing for days afterward.  These magnificent stretch of cliffs have also served as the backdrop for commercials and movies. It takes only about 30 minutes to take a walk around, but exploring in darkness or a bad weather might be dangerous, so it is advisable to check conditions beforehand.

stories.title: Manjanggul Cave
stories.audioTitle: Everything about Lava Tunnels, Manjanggul Cave
stories.script: Everything about Lava Tunnels, Manjanggul Cave  Located in Gimnyeong-ri, Gujwa-eup, the world’s longest lava tunnel Manjanggul Cave which was known as ‘Manjangee cave’ by the locals, was revealed to the world only in 1958.   Various lava tube tunnel structures make Manjanggul Cave appear even more mysterious. The significant value of the cave was recognized and was designated as a UNESCO World Natural Heritage in 2008.   In 1962, Manjanggul Cave was designated as Natural Monument No. 98 along with Gimnyeongsagul Cave. It is 8,928 m long with a width of up to 23 m and a height of up to 30 m. From 1977 to 1986, a Korea-Japan joint investigation on Manjanggul Cave was executed.   A natural cave created by the sinking activity of lava, Manjanggual Cave has a variety of interesting structures inside including stone pillars and stalactites that make a splendid world-class view. It will be no exaggeration to say that it is a lava tunnel museum.  Moreover, Manjanggual Cave possesses significant academic values, as it is a habitat for various rare species such as bats, earth centipedes, Sinopoda koreana, Nesticella brevipes, mites, and blue-green and green algae.   Only certain parts of Manjanggul Cave are open to public. The other parts are open for academic purposes only.  Must-see things at Manjanggul Cave! First, the Stone Turtle~! The Stone Turtle shaped just like Jeju Island is a lava boulder representing Manjanggual Cave. It definitely is one of the best masterpieces lava ever created.   A lava boulder refers to a rock that dropped from the tunnel’s ceiling while lava was flowing until the rock stopped at some point. The Stone Turtle is assumed to have been created as hot lava was stuck to the corner of the stopped lava boulder.     In short, it shows the mystique of lava tunnels.    Must-see things at Manjanggul Cave! Second, lava columns~!  They are created as lava which had flowed down to the floor from the ceiling hardened and piled into column-shapes.   Such lava columns are found in many lava tunnels, but the 7.6 m high lava column in Manjanggul Cave is known to be one of the largest one in the world.    Some of the lava flowed from the ceiling had flowed into both direction of the floor and formed structures of lava toes.   The lava tunnel formed together with a volcano hundreds of thousands of years ago, Manjanggul Cave holds a mystique of Jeju Island. You can find everything about a lava tunnel at Manjanggul Cave.  (Subtitles  - UNESC certificate)

stories.title: Seopjikoji
stories.script: A Dramatic View of Seopjikoji  Located in Sinyang-ri, Seongsan-eup, Seopjikoji is famous for its superb coastal view with Seongsan Ilchulbong stretching out like a folding screen as a backdrop. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, known for one of the best tourist attractions in East Jeju along with the Sinyang Beach nearby. Seopjikoji boasts a majestic view of volcanic island completed after numerous volcanic activities.   Introduction of Seopjikoji  Seopjikoji is a hill covered by red volcanic ashes called ‘Songi.’ It stretches out from Sinyang Beach to the ocean for about 2km.   ‘Seopji’ means the topography that produces many great people and ‘Koji’ means a cape jutting out into the sea in Jeju dialect.    Seopjikoji is one of the main tourist attractions that represent Jeju with its excellent harmony of picturesque hills and the ocean. It often appears as a background in movies and TV dramas, including ‘Eyes of Dawn’, ‘Danjeokbi yeonsu’, ‘Cinderella’, and ‘All In’. Among them, the TV drama ‘All In’, with Lee Byung-Hun and Song Hye-Gyo as main characters, was sensationally popular not only in Korea but also in Japan, China, and Southeast Asia.   Beautiful legends dwell in beautiful places. The legend of Seonnyeo Rock is that the son of King of Heaven fell in love with a fairy, but eventually incurred the wrath of the king and turned into a rock, standing upright at Seopjikoji.   Things you should not miss –Subtitles IN  Things you shouldn’t miss at Seopjikoji of splendid view. First, Seopjikoji lighthouse! Seopjikoji lighthouse is located on a steep hill. Watching the blue light of the ocean harmonized with a picturesque scene of seaside from the lighthouse is a must do at Seopjikoji.   Second, Seopjikoji Bongsudae~! Because Japanese invasions occurred often, the Bongsudae was built to make a fire and signal the invasion. It remains in its original form to this day.   Third, the ‘All In’ House  The film set, in which the main female character lived in the TV drama ‘All In’, was turned into a museum and has been attracting many Japanese and Chinese tourists.  There is no greater artwork than nature. The dramatic view of Seopjikoji directed by nature will leave a deep impression in your heart.

stories.title: Jusangjeolli Cliff
stories.audioTitle: A Masterpiece of Nature, Jusangjeolli Cliff
stories.script: A Masterpiece of Nature, Jusangjeolli Cliff   The Open Coast of Seogwipo  In the coast of Seogwipo, where invigorating waves breaking briskly off the shore will instantly refresh your heart, there is something other than deep blue sea that attracts people’s gaze: the Jusangjeolli Cliff.    The rectangular or hexagonal basalt columns of Jusangjeolli Cliff standing against waves surely are miraculous works of nature with God’s touch.   Introduction of Jusangjeolli Cliff  Cliff in Daepo-dong  Located in Daepo-dong, Seogwipo city, Jusangjeolli is also called “Jisatgae Jusangjeolli”.  The Sign of Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff  The great and miraculous work of nature was designated as a Natural Monument No. 443 in 2004, and also as one of the UNESCO Global Geoparks in 2010.   The Vertical Pillars of Jusangjeolli Cliff  As hot lava cools down, its volume decreases, splits vertically, and creates rectangular ~ hexagonal stone pillars.   Various Images of Vertical Pillars  Jusangjeolli Cliff are created as basaltic lava flew from a crater of 1100℃ and rapidly cooled down. Such are only seen in a few places in Korea. Among them, Jusangjeolli in Daepo show off the largest scale in the nation with the height of 30~40m and width of 1km.   Tracking at Jusangjeolli  The white foam rushing through breaking waves seems to create an illusion of a sad tale of a stonemason, standing in front of a majestic creation of lava.  Sometimes, rough waves rush up as high as 20 meters or more creating a spectacular scene.   Tourists Visiting Jusangjeolli  Jusangjeolli Cliff is in the limelight as a theme tour destination with its exquisite scenery and refreshing sea breezes.  Especially, this place attracts many photographers as the lava pillars show different charms at different times.   Waves breaking off against Jusangjeolli Cliff  You can feel the miraculous and magnificent nature with your entire body looking at the waves breaking through the stone pillars creating white foams.  It is a place you must visit once in a lifetime.  An impression you get will never be forgotten.

stories.title: Bijarim Forest
stories.audioTitle: Bijarim Forest: A Forest of a Thousand Years
stories.script: Bijarim Forest: A Forest of a Thousand Years  Bijarim Forest is a unique forest in which over 2800 of old bija, or nutmeg trees between 500~800 years old, cover up the sky. It is the first forest for therapeutic walk in Jeju and the largest forest of one species of tree in the world.   It is a place of healing, where phytoncide spewed from the forest will make your body and mind healthy.   Located in Pyeongdae-ri, Gujwa-eup, Bijarim Forest remains green throughout the year since leaves don’t fall out even during the winter. Bijarim Forest has been designated as a Natural Monument No. 374.   Classified as a taxaceae, over 2800 bija trees are growing naturally in Bijarim Forest. They are also called ‘Bijanang’ or ‘Bijonang’ in Jeju. They possess special values, since they only grow in Jeju Island and some parts of the southern part of Korea.   The name ‘Bija’ is derived from the fact that the way its leaf stretches out resembles the Chinese character ‘bi(非)’. There are female and male bija trees. The bija fruit has a hard and peanut-looking seed inside.   In the old days, people used to eat bija seeds to get rid of parasites inside the body. People also extracted oil from seeds. Particularly, go boards made of bija trees boast the best quality.   Forest bathing in a forest of dense bija trees is said to have a natural healing effect. The evergreen trees emit phytoncide that makes blood vessels flexible, calms mental and physical fatigue, and stabilizes biorhythm. You will find your body and mind getting cleared as you walk along the paths in Bijarim Forest.   The Bijarim Forest walking trail is separated into two courses. The short one takes about 40 minutes and the other takes about 1 hour and 20 minutes. Strollers and wheelchairs are allowed in the short course so that all can enjoy the nature of Bijarim Forest freely.   Things you should not miss – Subtitles IN Things you should not miss at Bijarim Forest, the forest of a thousand years that heals your body and soul.    First, the bija trees of a thousand years~! In the center of the forest stands the oldest tree in Jeju Island, which reaches 14 meters in height, 6 meters in girth, and a perimeter of 15 meters. The tree is over 820 years old and is called ‘the grandfather tree of bija trees.’  Second, bija love tree, known as Yeollimok~! The roots of the two trees stick together and become one tree, which is called ‘Yeolli.’ Accordingly, Yeollimok represents the eternal love that never changes. Along with the grandfather tree of bija trees, Yeollimok is a symbolic tree of Bijarim Forest.   Bijarim Forest brings clear and bright energy to people of today who are under the pressure of speed and stress. Bijarim Forest is a forest of a thousand years that is created together by nature and people.  (Fresh Leaves, Tree Measuring More than the Both Arms’ Span Around, Tree of a Thousand Years, Morning Air)

stories.title: Saryeoni Forest Path
stories.audioTitle: Saryeoni Forest Path: A Luxurious Forest Path That Represents Jeju
stories.script: Saryeoni Forest Path: A Luxurious Forest Path That Represents Jeju  Nowadays, hiking in forest is very popular worldwide. The forest paths in Jeju are attracting many people as well. Among them, the most loved forest path would be that of Saryeoni Forest.   Extended from Bijarim-ro, Bonggae-dong, Jeju-si, to Saryeoni Oreum in Hannam-ri, Namwon-eup, Seogwipo-si, Sayeoni Forest is definitely a mysterious masterpiece living up to the meaning of its name, “a divine place.”  Introduction of Saryeoni Forest Path Sayroeni Forest Path is located on the beautiful Bijarim-ro. The path is 15 km long with an altitude of 550 m.   Saryeoni Forest is a typical tropical mountain district and there is a dense natural forest of various species of trees, including Konara Oak, hornbeam, snowbell, Cornelian Cherry, sun tree, and cedar, stretched out widely on both sides of the path  Saryeoni Forest is also a home to various animals such as badger, Jeju ferret, fairy pitta, goshawk, and ussuri mamushi.   Saryeoni Forest attracts many visitors, since walking in a forest and breathing in clean and refreshing air are known to help resolve stress and improve stomach and cardio respiratory functions.   Jeju City selected 31 representative sites in Jeju that are relatively unexplored compared to the existing tourist attractions in July 2009 and Saryeoni Forest is one of them.   In a corner at the entrance of Saryeoni Forest Path, a poem <Saryeoni Forest Path> by the poet Do Jong Hwan attracts people’s attention. In the poem, he praises Saryeoni Forest Path as follows:  “On a day when I feel like I’ve climbed over a sand hill in a desert, On a day when I can’t manage things that are boiling up like lava, On a day when my mind have long been a dried stream, I want to walk along this path for a long time with a person who listens to my    words in silence with a smile.”  Except for Mulchat Oream and Saryeoni Oreum, the path is even, so, it is easy for children to walk along too. The path is also relatively wider than other forest paths, making it wide enough for a whole family to walk together hand in hand.   Things you should not miss – Subtitles IN Things you should not miss at Saryeoni Forest Path, a forest path representing Jeju. It’s Mulchat Oreum!  There is a lake on top of Mulchat Oreum. The name ‘Mulchat Oreum’ was derived from the shape of Oreum, which looks like a castle. Entrance is limited to prevent damages.   At Saryeoni Forest Path, you will be able to loosen up and walk leisurely through a beautiful forest as you play and rest along.   Subtitles: Hiking in Bijarim-ro / People Visiting Saryeoni Forest Path / Thick Trees in Saryeoni Forest Path/ Various Species of Trees

stories.title: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall
stories.audioTitle: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall: A Natural Wonder Even the Sky Fell in Love With
stories.script: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall: A Natural Wonder Even the Sky Fell in Love With  There are many waterfalls with vigorous water streams pouring down from steep rugged cliffs in Jeju. Among them, Cheonjiyeon Waterfall is definitely the best in terms of with size and scenic view.    ■ Introduction of Cheonjiyeon Waterfall  Seogwipo Harbor, Various Rugged Cliffs with Rock Formations, Various Vegetation, Dense Forest, Contents of Jeungbotamraji Let the images drift away)  As you start your way up from the old Seogwipo Harbor, you will reach the waterfall boasting a magnificent view with its rugged cliffs and fantastic rock formations. A luxuriant forest of diverse subtropical evergreen and fern trees covers the area.   The <Jeungbotamraji>, drawn up by 12 Jeju scholars right after Korea regained independence, explains about Cheonjiyeon very well. It praises the beauty of Cheonjiyeon as follows:   “It is located at Yeonwoecheon stream, about 2km to the west of Seogwi-ri, Seogwipo. The double waterfalls flow quickly as if it would fly away. It is approximately around 30.3 m long. It has quiet and secluded feelings to it as it is very close to the ocean, yet surrounded by hills and mountains.”  Cheonjiyeon Waterfall inside the valley, which is 1 km long, with a height of 22 m, a width of 12m, and the water depth of 20 m, pours down between fantastic rocks as if it would pierce right into the earth’s axis. You will feel chills even in the summer time.   The area around Cheonjiyeon Waterfall is designated and protected as a Nature Reserve to protect the original form of nature. Accordingly, any activity of logging, collecting plants, or capturing wild animals is prohibited.   ■ Things you should not miss – Subtitles IN  The Dense Forest at Cheonjiyeon Waterfall  Things you should not miss at Cheonjiyeon Waterfall that boasts a picturesque view.  Dampalsu Trees (Ellipticus Elaeocarpus)  First, Dampalsu trees, or Ellipticus elasocarpus~! Dampalsu tree is a subtropical tree. In Korea, Dampalsu trees are only found in Jeju Island, as they cannot survive in the cold. The wild Dampalsu trees around Cheonjiyeon Waterfall area have been designated as a Natural Monument No. 163  Giant Mottled Eel   Things you should not miss at Cheonjiyeon Waterfall Second, giant mottled eel~! It is a southern tropical fish that grows into as big as 2 m of body length. The habitats of giant mottled eel range from Jeju, southern part of Japan, and to Southeast Asia. They are classified as a Natural Monument No. 27.   ■ Epilogue Cheonjiyeon Waterfall pours down so quickly between high cliffs and dense forest as if it would fly away. It is a natural wonder even sky would fall in love with.

stories.title: Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls
stories.audioTitle: Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls with the Legend of Seven Fairies
stories.script: Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls with the Legend of Seven Fairies  Jungmun Tourist Complex  Jungmun Tourist Complex is Jeju’s first comprehensive tourist complex established in 1973 in accordance with Jeju Island comprehensive tourist development.   Jungmun Tourist Complex + Cheonjeyeon Waterfall  There is a waterfall within Jungmun Tourist Complex that holds a legend of seven fairies: the Cheonjeyeon Falls, in which the seven fairies that serve the King of Heaven bathed and played.   ■ Introduction of Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls  Cheonjeyeon Waterfall, where seven fairies descend from the heaven and take a bath, is the only three-tiered waterfall in Jeju. The water stream started at the foot of a mountain above Jungmun-dong falls into the 1st, then to the 2nd and the 3rd. Eventually, the water reaches the ocean.   Psilophytales, Ellipticus Elaeocarpus  At the valleys of each side of the 1st waterfall, a variety of plant life thrives including thick evergreen trees, plant vines, and shrubs. Moreover, the area is a subtropical forest zone designated as a Natural Monument No. 378, where rare plants such as psilophytales, Ellipticus elaeocarpus are grown.  People Visiting Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls  In ancient times, it was thought that standing under the water coming from the east cave of the 1st waterfall on the 15th day of the 7th lunar month can cure any disease and many people visited the falls around that time of the year. However, entering is now prohibited.    A White Column of Water Pouring Down   Any troubled mind will be cleared just by looking at the white column of water pouring down from the rugged cliff with fantastic rock formations. Chenjeyeon Waterfall is one of Seogwipo’s main tourist attractions along with Jeongbang and Jeonjiyeon Waterfalls.   Things you should not miss – Subtitles IN  Things you shouldn’t miss at Cheonjeyeon Waterfall that holds a legend of the seven fairies.   First, Ellipticus elaeocarpus or Dampalsu trees~!  Dampalsu trees are a tropical evergreen that grows in subtropical regions. In Korea, it can only be found in Jeju Island.   Over 20 Ellipticus Elaeocarpus, Sign Explaining about Ellipticus elaeocarpus   Along with Ellipticus elaeocarpus around Cheonjiyeon Falls, over 20 Ellipticus Elaeocarpus growing around Cheonjeyeon Falls make a picturesque view. They are designated and protected as a Local Monument No. 14.  Seonimgyo (Seonim Bridge)  Things you shouldn’t miss at Cheonjeyeon Waterfall Second, Seonimgyo~!  Cheonjeyeon valley + White Seonimgyo  Located at a valley that goes up to Cheonjeyeon Falls, Seonimgyo (128 m) is an arch bridge that has seven fairies from the legend carved on both sides.   Seonimgyo + Tourists  It is a popular tourist site, because you can see the coast of Seogwipo, as well as the valleys.   Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls + Stream of Water + Seonimgyo  The legend of seven fairies makes Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls that much more magical and beautiful. It is such a beautiful waterfall that makes you believe that a fairy will come down from heaven and play there any time soon.

stories.title: Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest
stories.audioTitle: The Healing Forest, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest
stories.script: The Healing Forest, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest   Jeolmul Oreum + Water Spring + A Forest Trail of Longevity  In harmony with the cool breeze blowing from the sea, phytoncide from cedar will clear your body and mind at Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest.   There are Jeolmul parasitic volcano famous for Jeolmul Water Spring, a soil trail tracking course where you can feel primeval nature, and a Forest Trail of Longevity to comfort and refuel tired bodies and souls.     Recreation Forest Tracking + Cedar Forest Stretching into the Sky, House in the Forest, A Walking Acupressure Path to Walk Barefooted  ■ Introduction of Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest Let the image pass)  Opened in 1997, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is mostly comprised of cedars that spew phytoncide which is beneficial to our bodies. On top of that, with its convenient location close to downtown Jeju, it is attracting not only Jeju people, but also tourists.   There are various facilities that allow visitors to spend great time with their families or loved ones: such as the house in the forest, Forest Culture Recreation Center, a water spring, a seminar room, trails that have acupressure effect, and the Forest Trail of Longevity with pure soil trails. Especially in the summer, it is packed with visitors who came to wash away the summer heat.   ■ Places not to be missed – Subtitles IN  Natural Recreation Forest of Dense Forest, Jeolmul Oreum, The Temple at Jeolmul Oreum, An Observatory, Ilchulbong, Yaksuam Temple, Jeolmul Water Spring  Must-visit places at Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest that will heal your bodies and souls~! First, Jeolmul Oreum~! It was named as Jeolmul Oreum, as there was a Jeol, a temple, nearby.  You can easily climb up to the top along the hiking trails.  There is a circular crater at the top, and people can walk around it and get a view around the Oreum.    At the observatory at top of the Oreum, visitors can also see in one glance from Ilchulbong in the east to Jeju-si.   On the way up, there is a temple called ‘Yaksuam’ and a water spring in the east called ‘Jeolmul.’  The water spring supposedly never dries up even in the driest season, and has clean water springing up all year round.     The Forest Trail of Longevity   Must-visit places at Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest  Second, the Forest Trail of Longevity~!  It is a natural soil trail formed within Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest consisting of thick cedar forest, and primeval soil trail.   In July 2009, Jeju city selected and announced ‘31 unexplored natural wonders in Jeju city’ that are not well-known to tourists, and the Forest Trail of Longevity was one of them.   Soil Trail Tracking  The winding soil trail across dense cedar forest is 11.1 km long and it takes approximately three and half hours to reach to the end of the trail.    Images of People Walking in the Natural Recreation Forest  Serotonin, which is also known as the happy hormone, will be released as you walk down the forest path and bring peace to your mind.   Jeolmul + Cedars + An Acupressure Trail Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest will heal and open up closed minds.

stories.title: Seongeup Historic Village
stories.script: Welcome to Seongeup Historic Village, where you can experience Jeju’s folk customs brought to life. The village has preserved and recreated a traditional Jeju town, replicating the life from the 1400s to the late Joseon Dynasty. Seongeup Historic Village served as the main district of Jeongeuihyun, one of the three administrative districts in Joseon, earning the designation as an Important Folk Material No. 188 in 1984.  Situated in Hallasan’s Jungsangan in Pyoseon-myeon, Seogwipo-si, at an altitude of 125 meters, Seongeup Historic Village housed Jeongeuihyeon for five centuries after its establishment in 1423. It stands as one of the few remaining town castles in Korea. Similar to Nakan Folk Village in Suncheon, there are inhabitants residing in Seongeup Historic Village. The village authentically preserves Jeju’s distinctive housing culture, notably the unique house structure consisting of two units called Angeori and Bakgeori. Surrounding the village are invaluable cultural treasures such as the city of Jeong Eui Hyun’s government office, Magistrate's office, administrative office, and local confucian school, offering insights into Jeju’s folk culture.  The village is adorned with remarkable trees, including Zelkova and nettle zelkova trees, each over 500 years old. Designated as Natural Monument No. 161, the zelkova tree, with its layers showcasing historical carvings, embodies the history of Seongeup Historic Village itself.  During your visit, several highlights should not be missed. Firstly, Jeong Eui Hyun’s government office, measuring 904,758 meters in width and 3,939 meters in height, stands as one of Korea’s best-preserved town castles and is a prominent filming location for movies and TV dramas. Originally located in Goseong-ri, Seongsan-eup, it faced invasion during the Japanese occupation. Additionally, Ilgwanheon, akin to a mayor’s office, earned designation as Jeju Tangible Cultural Property No. 7 in 1975.  Finally, the local Confucian school where Confucian scholars and students studied, holds the designation of Jeju Tangible Cultural Property No. 5. Seongeup Folk Village invites visitors to immerse themselves in the Jeju of 500 years ago, embracing the taste and charm of Jeju’s folklore.

stories.title: Seongeup Historic Village in Seogwipo
stories.script: Seongeup Historic Village holds the prestigious designation of being the nationally recognized Important Folklore Material No. 188. It encompasses the former capital of Jeonguihyeon during the Joseon period. Jeju was administratively divided into three zones during this era, with Jeonguihyeon chosen as the island's capital in 1423, the 5th year of King Sejong's reign. It served as the seat of the hyeon office until 1914, making it the 500-year capital of Jeju.  The location of Jeonguihyeon is quite unique within Jeju. Unlike three-quarters of all Jeju villages situated along the coast, Seongeup was a mountain village approximately 8 kilometers away from the nearest sea. Hence, when the village was established, it was surrounded by forests. During the Joseon Dynasty, this area thrived as the administrative, military, and educational hub but declined post-1914, leading to decades of deterioration.  Initially encompassing 3,191,711 square meters, the designated protection zone was later reduced to 794,213 square meters in 1987. The village is home to approximately 390 traditional Jeju straw-roofed houses, with 14 owned by five households currently designated as conserved structures.  At the village's center, a thousand-year-old zelkova and a 600-year-old hackberry stand side by side, designated as Natural Monument No. 161. Among these, Jeonguihyeon, the capital, established in 1423, saw the restoration of some walls, the south and west gates. The village also preserves 12 Dol Hareubangs, grandpa stone statues. Visitors can explore Jeju's administrative agency during the Joseon Dynasty and gain insights into our ancestors' lives on this island during that era.

stories.title: Go Chang-hwan's Historic House in Seongeup Village, Jeju
stories.audioTitle: Go Chang-hwan's Historic House in Seongeup Village, Jeju
stories.script: Believed to date back to the 19th century, Go Chang-hwan's Historic House once operated as an inn in Jeongui Village, a name that still persists to this day. Positioned adjacent to the Jeonguihyanggyo Local Confucian School, the house comprises anchae, the main building, and heutganchae, a shed.  Anchae, also known as Angeori, is a typical three-cell structure commonly found in the region south of Hallasan Mountain. Moving left to right, it houses a kitchen, daecheongmaru (a wooden floor hall), the main bedroom, and a smaller bedroom situated behind the kitchen. Gopang, a pantry-like area for storing grains, is positioned behind the main bedroom. Toenmaru, a wooden-floored veranda, graces the front of daecheongmaru and the main bedroom. Remarkably, the right door of daecheongmaru features horyeongchang, a small window for brief conversations with someone outside.  A wide mulpang (water room) rests in front of the kitchen, housing a mulgudeok (basket for water bottles). A substantial vegetable garden thrives behind anchae, complemented by dense vegetation and woodland.  Adjacent to anchae stands an antiquated bathroom called tongsi, while a modern counterpart can be found near the house's entrance. On the opposite side of angeori, heutganchae, a single-cell structure used to store straw mats and household tools, invites inspection.  Go Chang-hwan's Historic House in Seongeup Village is designated as Important Folklore Cultural Heritage No. 70.

stories.title: Go Pyeong-o's Historic House in Seongeup Village, Jeju
stories.audioTitle: Go Pyeong-o's Historic House in Seongeup Village, Jeju
stories.script: Believed to have been built in the late 18th century, Go Pyeong-o's Historic House holds the esteemed designation of being Important Folklore Cultural Heritage No. 69. Spanning an expansive area of 1,163 square meters, the house boasts a prominent Imungan Gate that stands out along the Nammun Gate Street. It epitomizes the typical style of a private house in Jeju, comprising anchae (angeori), bakkatchae (bakgeori), gopang, mokeori, and tongsi.  An integral part of Jeju's customs involves the gifting of anchae to a son upon his marriage, as parents transition to reside in bakkatchae, forming the foundation of a larger family household.  The bakkatchae in this house was previously occupied by public officials from the Jeongui Village office. Unfortunately, mokeori was dismantled in the mid-1970s. Two bathrooms are present, with the second one installed when Go Pyeong-o married and began living with his parents.  An ancient camellia tree graces the area behind anchae, while a vegetable garden adorns the rear of bakkatchae. Across the street, outside daemungan (main gate), stood a well-known as 'Nammuntong,' also referred to as 'Wonnimmul' because only magistrates, called Wonnim, were believed to have used its water. Furthermore, the proximity of a well designated for public officials nearby suggests that this house was once their residence.

stories.title: The Blacksmith's House in Seongeup Village, Jeju (Go Sang-eun's Historic House)
stories.audioTitle: The Blacksmith's House in Seongeup Village, Jeju (Go Sang-eun's Historic House)
stories.script: Go Sang-eun's Historic House, constructed in the 16th year of King Gojong's reign, stands as a significant relic of Jeju's history. Constructed by Go Sang-eun's great-grandfather, the current resident's ancestor, this house once operated as a blacksmith's shop, reflecting the traditional practices prevalent on Jeju Island. Reflecting the customary placement of forges at the heart of villages, this house is situated along the road connecting Nammun Gate to Gaeksa in Jeongui Village. Nearby, the intersection south of Gaeksa features a pond named Nodoribangjuk, while the southern part of the house faces a renowned site called Nammuntong (Gwancheongmot), historically used by public officials.  The house's interior layout comprises angeori (anchae) and mokeori forming an 'L' shape. Distinct from other residences in Seongeup Village, which often consist of three to four buildings, this house features a simpler layout, emphasizing core functionalities. Notable characteristics include the absence of external spaces like olle (narrow paths leading up to the house) and uyeong (vegetable gardens), as well as the lack of a primary gate.  Originally serving as a blacksmith's shop, the house underwent modifications to become a residential dwelling. Additional structures, including Daecheongmaru, a shed, small and main bedrooms, and gopang, were integrated, while a kitchen was established in mokeori.  Designated as Important Folklore Cultural Heritage Number 72, Go Sang-eun's Historic House signifies its cultural and historical significance within Jeju's heritage.

stories.title: Han Bong-il’s Historic House in Seongeup Village, Jeju
stories.audioTitle: Han Bong-il’s Historic House in Seongeup Village, Jeju
stories.script: Han Bong-il’s Historic House, a traditional Jeju residence situated in the eastern part of Seongeup Historic Village, dates back to the early 19th century. Surrounded by a cozy landscape, the house epitomizes the traditional architectural style, featuring hackberry trees and an imposing Imungan Gate.  From the front yard, the view encompasses neighboring house rooftops Yeongjusan Mountain to the north, offering a wonderful scene. The ambiance of the house itself exudes serenity and elegance.  The central part, daemungan, comprises three rooms, flanked by shemak sheds on both sides of the entrance. Upon entering the gate, angeori (anchae) is situated to the left, while bakgeori lies the opposite. Angeori houses a kitchen and a small bedroom on the left, while the main bedroom sits to the right, adjacent to the gopang, a storage area for grains.   Bakgeori consists of three rooms, with a small gudeul, a traditional floor heating system, positioned behind the sangbang. The low foundation of the house contributes to its inviting and snug atmosphere.  Retaining its original appearance with minimal alterations over the years, Han Bong-il’s Historic House stands as an exemplary representation of traditional Jeju architecture. Its preservation of authentic features has earned it the designation of Important Folklore Material No. 71.

stories.title: Gaekjujip House in Seongeup Village, Jeju (Jo Il-hun's Historic House)
stories.audioTitle: Gaekjujip House in Seongeup Village, Jeju (Jo Il-hun's Historic House)
stories.script: Jo Il-hun's Historic House, built in the late 18th century, holds a captivating history. Initially functioning as a pub and inn for peddlers, its layout encompasses five buildings?angeori, bakgeori, mokeori, a warehouse, and Imungan Gate?arranged in a square over an expansive area of 1,074 square meters  In the past, this site hosted a malbange, owned by Jo. A malbange is a millstone typically powered by a horse or a cow, purportedly installed by Jo's grandfather. The presence of such a millstone within a private home was rare in Jeju, hinting at the household's affluence, potentially belonging to a significant landowner in Seongeup.  A distinctive feature of Jeju houses is the jeongnang, serving as the boundary or main gate. Jo Il-hun’s House retains jeongjumok, wooden structures supported by stone columns with holes, which are still visible today. The front yard displays an array of farming and living tools, including two plows, numerous cabinets, and various traditional farming implements housed in bakgeori. Additionally, a stone manger for animals to drink water and a tethering device for horses and cows are discernible. Remnants of an old peddler's inn, such as dongwe, a storage space for coins is also present.  Traditionally, Jeju houses feature olle, narrow pathways leading to the residence. However, this house, designed in an urban style, is distinguished by a main gate rather than an olle.  Jo Il-hun's Historic House proudly bears the distinction of being designated as Important Folklore Cultural Heritage Number 68, a testament to its cultural and historical significance.

stories.title: Yongduam Rock
stories.script: Located near Yongyeon Pond, Yongduam Rock is a symbolic tourism spot in Jeju Island and the closest attraction to the airport. It formed when volcanic lava cooled upon reaching the coast and underwent coastal erosion.  “Yongdu” and “Yongmeori” both mean the “head of the dragon.” It was named after the shape of a dragon soaring to the sky from the sea. Legend says that a python living in the valley of Yongyeon aspired to become a dragon after a thousand years. When it attempted to soar into the sky, it was accidentally struck by an arrow from the God of Hallasan Mountain. This caused it to fall back into the sea. Frustrated and saddened, it lifted its head towards the sky in a final roar, forming the rock in its distinctive shape.  It is best to take in the view from a distance of about 100 meters, especially on days when the waves are vigorously crashing. Visitors can hike or drive along the coastal road of Yongduam, where numerous restaurants and coffee shops line the way. At night, the twinkling lights from the fishing boats at the sea make it an especially romantic place to visit.

stories.title: Yongyeon Pond
stories.script: Yongyeon is a pond in the Yongdam-dong area of Jeju. It’s located at the downstream near Yongdam-dong Beach, where water from a valley flows in.  The rock is about 8 meters high. In the past, rituals were performed here to pray for rain during drought. It was also called Chwibeyongdam or Seonyudam, as poets and scholars used to ride boats on the water. There, they enjoyed art and the moonlit nights under the rocks. It was also where locals of Jeju celebrated the arrival of a new governor.  The Yongyeon Cloud Bridge is the link between the two sides of Yongyeon Pond. It offers a scenic view with its red pavilion and emerald stream. The bridge is particularly beautiful at night, making it a perfect spot for an evening walk.   It is said that Yongyeon Pond never runs dry even during droughts. There is a legend that a dragon which lived here ascended and brought rain. It is also known to have been a playground for dragons.  Every year, Yongyeonyabeom, a traditional summer night event where people ride boats adorned with lights, takes place at Yongyeon Pond. This event has been listed as one of the 12 Scenic Views of Yeongju and its reappearance festival continues to this day.

stories.title: Udo Maritime Park
stories.audioTitle: Udo Maritime Park: An Island Inside of Island
stories.script: Udo Maritime Park: An Island Inside of Island  Udo is the biggest island among 62 islets of Jeju.  Udo Viewed from Jongdal-ri / People Visiting Udo / Udopalgyeong (8 Scenic Views of Udo) / View from Udobong  Udo was named because it resembles a lying cow. It is a famous tourist attraction welcoming 3.4 million visitors every year. The entire island is a lava region and it is an island inside island that possesses a primeval beauty.   Introduction of Udo Maritime Park  Udo was a deserted island until about 150 years ago. People started to live in Udo as a state-owned farm was established in 1697. There are over 600 households residing in Udo now.   The Scenic View of Udo Coast / Women Divers / Stone Walls Stretched Out Like a Panorama  You will be able to find original forms and customs of Jeju at Udo that are gradually disappearing, such as women divers and traditional stone walls stretched out endlessly.    Jeju Olle Trails / People Walking on Olle Trail / People Traveling on Scooter and Bike / Beautiful Scene of Udo  Udo also attracts many people who love walking on Olle Trails. You can also explore Udo on a bike, bus, or scooter.   Images from Siwolae / Images from The Mermaid  Udo is a popular location for shooting of movies, TV dramas, or commercials with its superb scenic view. With movies including <Siwolae> starring Lee Jung-Jae and Jun Ji-Hyun and <The Mermaid> starring Jeon Do-Yeon and Park Hae-Il, the scenic view of Udo became more popular.   Things that should not be missed – Subtitles IN  The Sign Introducing Udopalgyeong / Udopalgyeong  The representative scenic spots of Udo are summarized as “Udopalgyeong” - the eight attractive sites of Udo. They were discovered and named in 1983 by a teacher and folk historian Kim Chan-heup of Yeonpyeong Middle School in order to spread the beauty of Udo.   Jugan Myeongwol / Haesik Cave  The first Udopalgyeong is Jugan Myeongwol. Jungan Myeongwol is a sea cave and its name was derived from the fact that the sunlight from outside creates an image on the cave ceiling that looks like a moon.      Yahangeobeom  The second Udopalgyeong is Yahangeobeom. It was named after its splendid scenery of fishing boats lighting up the summer night sea that are viewed from the northeast side of the beach.   Cheonjingwansan  The third Udopalgyeong is Cheonjingwansan, which means the beautiful and wonderful scenery of Hallasan and the panorama of Oreums observed from Dongcheonjindong Port.  The fourth Udopalgyeong is Jidocheongsa, which refers to the complete landscape view of Udo observed from the top of the peak Udobong along with clear and blue sea, waves breaking into white bubbles, and the sparkling sandy beach.   Jeongpomangdo  The fifth site of Udopalgyeong, Jeongpomangdo, is the scenery of Udo viewed from the coast that lies in between Jongdal-ri, Gujwa-eup and Hado-ri.  The sixth Udopalgyeong site, Huhaeseokbyeok, is the rocky cliff standing with its back toward the sea. It refers to Gwangdaekoji, the grand vertical cliff standing in the east.   The seventh Udopalgyeong site, Dongangyeonggul, means a whale cave at eastern coast. It refers to the sea cave in the Geommeolle Beach (black beach).    The eighth Udopalgyeong site is Seobinbaeksa, which refers to the scenery of the coral sand beach glistening in silver light.    An island inside of island, Udo is the most scenic island in Jeju. If you are traveling through Jeju, visiting Udo is a must!

stories.title: Seogwipo Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery
stories.audioTitle: Meet Lee Joong Seop, the Genius Painter, at Seogwipo Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery
stories.script: Meet Lee Joong Seop, the Genius Painter, at Seogwipo Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery   Located on Lee Joong Seop Street in Seogwi-dong, Seogwipo-si, Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery was founded in 2002 to honor the artistic soul of the genius painter Lee Joong Seop, who resided in Seogwipo with his family during the Korean War and worked on his paintings.   Introduction of Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery The Portrait of Lee Joong Seop   One of the greatest artistic geniuses of Korean modern art along with Kim Hwan-Ki, the tragic painter from Pyeongannamdo produced masterpieces while staying in Seogwipo from January to December 1951 with his wife and two sons.    Seogwipo bears important temporal and spatial meanings in Lee’s works. His works in Segwipo, including <The Fantasy of Seogwipo> and <Landscape Overlooking Seop Island>, are reflecting happy memories he had with his family in Seogwipo despite the ongoing war.     Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery founded to trace Lee’s stay in Seogwipo consists of two exhibition spaces.  The Regular Exhibition Hall on the first floor display Lee Joong Seop’s works and related data shedding light on the painter’s life and artistic world.   The Special Exhibition Hall on the second floor display the gallery’s collection and works by other artists residing in Jeju.  In addition, you can get a view of the subject matters of Lee’s works, such as Seop Island, Moon Island, and Sae Island, at the observatory on the third floor.  Things you should not miss – Subtitles IN The Forest in Lee Joong Seop Park  Things you should not miss at Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery where you can feel the presence of Daehyang Lee Joong Seop~!  Lee Joong Seop’s Residence + Thatched House   First, Lee Joong Seop’s residence~!  The Room the Artist Resided + Artist’s Portrait  Lee fled to Seogwipo with his family and stayed at this small room of 1.4 pyong.  Although he couldn’t afford to have proper meals and had to live on sweet potatoes or crabs, his stay at Seogwipo was remembered to be the happiest time in his lifetime.   Tracking on Lee Joong Seop Street  Things you should not miss at Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery  Second, Lee Joong Seop Street~!  The Street Sign of Lee Joong Seop Street  Seogwipo-si renamed the street as Lee Joong Seop Street to establish and vitalize a street of culture and tourism in 1996. In this car-free street, there are art workshops, creative residence, galleries, and cafes along with Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery. In addition, art market or flea market takes place on the weekends filling Seogwipo with the scent of arts and culture.     The tragic art genius Lee Joong Seop left masterpieces including The White Bull, A Married Couple, and The Fantasy of Seogwipo.  You will be able to feel the artistic soul of Lee Joong Seop, who lived his life like a flame, at Lee Joong Seop Art Gallery.

stories.title: Lee Jung Seop Art Museum, Seogwipo
stories.audioTitle: Lee Jung Seop Art Museum, Seogwipo
stories.script: Happy Road of Lee Jung-seop — Lee Jung Seop Art Museum    The place you’re looking at is an art museum that commemorates Lee Jung-seop who was a genius artist. This place was opened as Lee Jung-seop Exhibition Hall in November 2002 and came to have the current appearance in 2003. Then, in 2004, a narrow trail, a walkway and Lee Jung-seop Park were established and the venue was registered as a Class 1 art museum. In 2008, a creative studio and craft workshop of Lee Jung Seop Art Museum were also completed.  The round-shaped exhibition hall consists of two floors, with Lee Jung-seop’s works and relics in the permanent exhibition room on the first floor and planned exhibits on the second floor. The museum has in store 137 items including nine original works of Lee Jung-seop and his silver foil paintings. There is also Lee’s palette that was donated by his wife, Lee Nam-deok. The palette is known as the gift he received together with a special award he won at an exhibition in Japan.  Lee fled to this area with his family in 1951. For a little less than a year, they had to suffer from poverty; they even had to go to a beach and catch crabs for meals. But this period is said to be his happiest days spent with his family. Perhaps this is why the works he made in Jeju are the most splendid and the brightest ones. If you look at the works such as Scenery With Seopseom Island in the Distance and Wave and Fish, you can feel the joy of Lee Jung-seop in his days in Jeju. His silver foil paintings are very famous as well. He created about 300 small paintings on silver foils from cigarette packs. Some of his silver foil works were the first paintings by a Korean artist to be exhibited at the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

stories.title: Marado Island Marine Park
stories.audioTitle: Located at the southern end of Korea: Marado Island Marine Park
stories.script: Located at the southern end of Korea: Marado Island Marine Park  Marado Island situated at the Southern end of Korea, Gapado Island famous for Green Barley Festival,  Songaksan Mountain, a parasitic volcano embracing the mysteries of a volcanic island, Marado Island Marine Park consists of Marado Island, Gapado Island, and Songaksan Mountain and presents a grand sight with islets favored by nature and deep blue sea.   Introduction of Marado Marine Park  It takes about half an hour to get to Marado from Songaksan Mountain ferry terminal or Moseulpo Port. The oval-shaped island was created as a volcano erupted independently in the sea.   Marado now has a population of over 100 people, but it used to be a deserted island covered with a thick virgin forest.  In 1883, 5 households of Kim, Na, Han, and others started cultivating the land by the slash-and-burn method, and since then, people started living in Marado. In 1982, Marado was separated from Daejeong-eup Gapa-ri and became Mara-ri.   The rugged cliffs and splendid rock formations in Marado evoke a mystique. Beside from the fact that Marado is the southernmost island of Korea, Marado is also drawing attention with its numerous subtropical marine lives and picturesque view. Accordingly, Marado was designated as Natural Monument No. 423 in July 2000.   Gapado constitutes Marado Marine Park with Marado. It is an island located 5.5 km off to south from Moseulpo Port in Daejeong-eup.   Gapado was introduced under the name of ‘Kepat’ in Hamel’s Journal, a book written by Hendrik Hamel from the Netherlands describing his 14 years of stay in Joseon Dynasty after having drifted to Jeju area in 1653.   The whole island looks like a plate with its even topography. On top of the prominent fishing activities by Haenyos or woman divers, Marado is also known for barley cultivation. Every spring around April when barleys start sprouting, Green Barley Festival takes place attracting many visitors.   Songaksan Mountain area that arouses a sigh of admiration just by looking at is also a part of Marado Marine Park.   Songaksan Mountain, also called as ‘Jeolmuli’ or ‘Jeobyeoliak’, still has remnants from the Japanese occupation, such as an airfield constructed by the Japanese army, antiaircraft artillery, and a fortress.   There is a cave under the shoreline cliffs the Japanese army dug up as their military camp site, illustrating the pain and sorrow from the Japanese occupation period.    If you climb on top of Songaksan Mountain, you can see Gapado Island, Marado Island, and Hyeongje Island in one view. Moreover, Marado is especially famous for its rich variety of aquatic species including black porgy, rudder fish, and saw-edged perch, which confirm Marado as a representative tourist attraction site in Jeju.   Among many marine parks in Jeju, Marado Marine Park stands out with its primeval beauty.   (Marado, Blue Barley, Gapado, Glorious Songaksan Mountain, Blue Sea of Marado, Fishing Activities by Women Divers, History of Marado, Primeval Picturesque View, Green Barley Festival, Althr Airfield, The Top of Songaksan Mountain)

stories.title: Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest
stories.audioTitle: Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest: A Mecca of Jeju Healing Trip
stories.script: Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest: A Mecca of Jeju Healing Trip  Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest is located in the center of road no. 1100 that goes across the west part of Hallasan and connects Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si. Phytoncide emitted from densely standing hinoki cypress trees of around 60 years of age will relax your body and soul. It is a Mecca of Jeju healing trip where various tropical, subtropical, and polar trees are dispersed.   Introduction of Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest  Opened in 1995, Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest is located at an altitude of 600~800 meters. It is the best recreation forest in Jeju with a relatively large size that can take in up to 1,500 people per day (the optimum size for 700 people).   On top of the forest bath with dense hinoki cypress trees, you will be able to find different charms of Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest at different times, with royal azaleas blooming in the spring, a cool, clear stream in the summer, autumn foliage in the fall and snowy landscapes in the winter.  Especially, the view of Baekrokdam, Yeongsilgiam, the urban district of Seogwipo, and the ocean watched from the observatory at the top of Beopjeongak induces a sigh of exclamation with its majestic scene.   Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest has become the best recreation forest in Jeju thanks to the excellent walking trails. There are two courses, the ecosystem exploring course and healthy walking course, both of them providing a healing space to visitors.   Things you should not miss. Things you should not miss at Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest, which is a Mecca for Jeju healing trip~!  First, the campground~! Due to high popularity, it is hard to get reservation for the campground in Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest, where you can breathe in the forest’s clean air as much as you please. During summer, some people stay over a month. It is a much-loved place by those who love camping.   Second, the pool~! The pool in Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest is a much-loved place by family with young children. Here, you can have a unique experience of enjoying playing in the water in the forest.   Third, Visitors’ Center~! Coffee, newspapers, books, and computers are provided in the center to achieve the visitors’ satisfaction.   You can forget about any worries and sorrows for a while and repose and calm your body and soul at Seogwipo Natural Recreation Forest. It is the oldest recreation forest in Jeju and a Mecca of Jeju healing trip~! (Dense Forest, People Enjoying Camping, Happy Smiles)

stories.title: Jeju Stone Park
stories.audioTitle: The Symbol of 21st Century Jeju Culture, Jeju Stone Park
stories.script: The Symbol of 21st Century Jeju Culture, Jeju Stone Park  Jeju Stone Park is located in Gyorae-ri, Jocheon-eup where a broad prairie stretches. Built to celebrate the 21st century which is the era of culture, Jeju Stone Park embraces the history and culture of stones, which have been the root of the creation of Jeju, the volcanic island, and its culture.   Jeju Stone Park is the symbol of 21st century Jeju culture and a World Cultural Heritage Site created with stones, soil, trees, iron and water. The main theme of the park consists of the legends about Grandmother Seolmundae, who created Jeju Island, and the stones of Five Hundred Generals.   - The legend of Grandmother Seoulmundae Vast Ground, Various Stone Culture, Dongjaseok, Bangsatap, Outdoor Exhibition Space  Opened in 2006, with an investment of 185.2 billion Korean Won on the 1 million pyong, which is around 331 ha, of a vast ground, Jeju Stone Park is where visitors can see and experience the Jeju stone culture and the history of Jeju people. It is still constructing and will be completely constructed by 2020.  At Jeju Stone Park, you can see everything about the unique Jeju stone culture including the birth process of Jeju, Dongjaseok, Bangsatop, and Stone Hareubang, and eyewitness the original form of Jeju culture.   Jeju Stone Park mainly consists of 4 sections: Jeju Stone Museum, Jeju Stone Culture Exhibition Hall, Outdoor Exhibition Space, and Jeju Traditional Thatched-roof Houses.   You will have a valuable time at Jeju Stone Park by exploring what meanings stones bear in the lives of Jeju people.   Things that cannot be missed – Subtitles IN Diverse Contents of the Stone Museum, Various Data on Volcano, Stone Culture Exhibition Hall, Video Clips of Stone Culture  Must-see things at Jeju Stone Park, the symbol of 21st Jeju culture! First, Jeju Stone Museum~! It is an exhibition space with the theme of Jeju volcanic activity introducing and explaining about 9 subjects including space and earth, the geological structure of Korea peninsula, volcanic activity of Jeju, parasitic volcano, and caves. The museum will help you understand the birth process of the volcanic island Jeju.   Must-see things at Jeju Stone Park Second, Jeju Stone Culture Exhibition Hall~!  At Jeju Stone Culture Exhibition Hall, you can see historical artifacts of different themes, such as clothes, food, living, production, occupation, and play.  You can also watch rare and interesting video clips containing wise lifestyle of Jeju people that have been using stones in their normal lives, creating a unique history of Jeju stone culture.    Must-see things at Jeju Stone Park Third, the outdoor exhibition space~!  The displays of stone culture of from the prehistoric age to Joseon period are exhibited in chronological order. The displays include the unique religion of Jeju, Dongjaseok, and Jeongjuseok.   There are displays related to the life and death of Jeju people, their faith, and lifestyle.   Must-see things at Jeju Stone Park Fourth, Jeju traditional thatched-roof houses~!  To imitate ancient Jeju villages, traditional Jeju houses such as Segeori house, Biseokgeori, Dugeori, and horse mills are on display. Here, you can reconstruct the lives of ancient people .  -The Inside of a Thatched House  In addition, across from the ancient village, you can also examine communication facilities using stones that are prevalent in Jeju, including Bongsu, Yeondae, and Dodatbul.   When you travel, you see as much as you know. The key to fully see and understand Jeju, you need to understand the volcanic island Jeju’s stone culture first.  Jeju Stone Park, where you can experience the original forms of Jeju culture, will make your trip to Jeju fruitful and meaningful.

stories.title: Seogwipo Marine Park
stories.audioTitle: Seogwipo Marine Park, the Best Scenic Beauty in Seogwipo 70-ri.
stories.script: Seogwipo Marine Park, the Best Scenic Beauty in Seogwipo 70-ri.  As one of Seogwipo’s 70 scenes, Seogwipo Marine Park is well known as the essence of Seogwipo tour.  Seogwipo Marine Park is a splendid harbor with vertical strange-looking rocks, an island floating on green waves, and a port stretch out like an entrancing oriental painting. It definitely has the best scenic beauty in Seogwipo 70-ri.   Introduction of Seogwipo Marine Park  Seogwipo Marine Park was designated as one in 2007 in order to maintain the order of ecosystem and maximize the resource utilization through preserving marine ecological resources, and also to create a new form of tour content.   With the total area of 19.54㎢, Seogwipo Marine Park was designated as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2002, along with Jungsangan area with an altitude of 200 meters or more including Hallasan National Park, and the districts around Yeongcheon Seogwipo-si and Hyodoncheon.   The beautiful Seogwipo Marine Park gives you a feeling that you might fall into the sea with one false step.   Aside from the picturesque view, Seogwipo Marine Park is drawing attention as silver magnolia trees, a very rare species of trees worldwide, grow there. The region is also a marginal area in the south where black wood pigeons (Natural Monument) breed.   On top of that, it is also a home to various southern species that have high academic values.   Things you should not miss – Subtitles IN  Things you should not miss at Seogwipo Marine Park~! First, Munseom~! Munseom is an oval-shaped island comprised entirely of vertical columnar joints of trachyandesite. Also, there is a luxuriant evergreen subtropical forest. Munseom has been designated and protected as a Cultural Heritage Monument No. 45 by Jeju Special Self-Governing Province.  The ocean around Munseom is famous community for soft coral. As such, it is known as a heaven of scuba divers.   Second, Beomseom~! (Tiger Island) Beomseom is surrounded by steep cliffs that are 80 meters high. There are great columnar joints of trachyte and sea caves. The top of the island has an even topography and there is a well in the south side of the top.  There used to be several people residing in Beomseom, but now it is deserted.  The legend has it that Beomseom is named after its shape that resembles a tiger.   Third, Seopseom~! Located 400 meters away from the coast of Bomok village in Seogwipo-si, Seopseom used to be called Supseom due to the thick forest.   Various evergreen trees and over 180 species of rare plants, and 450 species of subtropical plants make a luxuriant forest harmonizing with strange-looking rocks. Among them, spleenwort (bird’s nest fern) has been designated and protected as a Natural Monument No. 18.   There is even a song called <Seogwipo 70-ri> that sings about the picturesque view of Seogwipo Marine Park. It certainly is one of the best scenic beauties in the world.

stories.title: Hallasan National Park
stories.script: Hallasan National Park  Where is the highest mountain in South Korea? It’s none other than Hallasan Mountain!
