Located at the center of Jeju Island, Hallasan Mountain was formed by volcanic activity and boasts breathtaking natural scenery, with towering cliffs, carved-looking slopes, and uniquely shaped rocks scattered across shallow valleys. Recognized for its beauty, Hallasan Mountain was designated a natural monument in 1966 and became Korea’s 7th national park in 1970.  Hallasan Mountain is characterized by distinct plant distributions according to altitude. In the lower regions, you’ll find warm-climate, subtropical plants such as camellia trees and citrus, which thrive in warmer areas. In contrast, the higher regions feature clear vegetation zones with subalpine plants, such as Korean fir and stone apricot trees, which flourish in colder climates and at high altitudes. The park is home to over six thousand plant and animal species, and its ecological significance has been recognized by UNESCO, which designated Hallasan National Park as a World Natural Heritage site, a Biosphere Reserve, and a Geological Park.  Many people have climbing Hallasan Mountain on their bucket list. Composed entirely of basalt, Hallasan Mountain’s trails can be slippery, and weather conditions can change rapidly. With proper preparation, however, a day hike of trails under 10 km is manageable. Note that camping and cooking are prohibited throughout the park, so you’ll need to complete your hike within the day. Also, specific entry and descent times are enforced, so be sure to check these before starting your hike.  Enjoy your climb!

stories.title: Hallasan Mountain Baekrokdam Lake
stories.script: Baengnokdam Lake of Hallasan Mountain  In Korean, “Bae” means “white,” “Nok” means “deer,” and “Dam” means “lake,” giving Baengnokdam Lake its name, the lake of the white deer. Legend has it that mountain gods would ride white deer, who drank from the lake. Baengnokdam Lake, an oval-shaped crater lake formed by water accumulated in the volcanic crater at Hallasan Mountain’s summit, located on South Korea’s highest peak. This area shows signs of erosion but has well-preserved original geological features, offering both scientific value and stunning natural beauty. The basin within Baengnokdam Lake is grassland. On a clear day, roe deer can be seen grazing or drinking from the lake, and they have made the surrounding fir tree forest their home. Who knows? Perhaps they’re descendants of the legendary white deer!  Many rare alpine plants, such as fir trees, Diapensia lapponica, Leontopodium hallaisanense, and columbine, thrive around and within Baengnokdam Lake, adding high ecological value to the area. The Diapensia lapponica, which grows on Hallasan Mountain’s rocky walls, stands only 2 cm tall, making it one of the world’s smallest plants.  The two summit trails to Baengnokdam Lake on Hallasan Mountain include the Seongpanak Trail, which is 9.6 km and takes approximately four hours thirty minutes one-way, and the Gwaneumsa Trail, which is 8.7 km and takes about five hours one-way. Since February 1, 2020, a reservation system has been implemented, so you must make a reservation in advance through the Hallasan Visit Reservation System for both trails. Due to Hallasan Mountain’s unpredictable weather, trail access may be fully or partially restricted depending on conditions, so be sure to check the Hallasan National Park website for any updates before your visit.

stories.title: Halla Arboretum
stories.audioTitle: Healing park in the city, Halla Arboretum
stories.script: Healing park in the city, Halla Arboretum  This is a place filled with a variety of trees and various species of wildflowers that span four seasons. Walking through the woods during each of the seasons can make the experience feel fresh and new.   Serving as a park for the study and the preservation of natural environment, there are a lot of endangered and rare plants. This is Halla Arboretum, a place with healing power.  You can rest and relax in Halla Arboretum, which attracts many tourists.  Approximately 200,000 square meters of park, with 1,100 kinds of trees and plants including native and exotic plants, totaling about 100,000 plants.   In the Arboretum, there are 10 exhibition gardens, including Aquatic Botanical Garden for forest trees, bush trees, rare species of trees and plants.   You can enjoy other amenities for forest bathing and physical training, as well.    The scent of trees, wildflowers, and herbal plants bring you the best experience in the country. Walking through the woods and scented gardens can help improve your body and mind.  If you want to walk more, how about trying to trek to the top of Gwangi Oreum? Walking a 1.7 km trail, you can have fresh air and forest bathing.  Another attraction is the Eco Experience Center.  It offers an opportunity for Jeju locals, students, and tourists to learn about the environment and nature and to acquire education through experiences.    You will learn the life processes behind seaweed, fish, insect, amphibians, reptiles as well as plants on Hallasan Mountain.  Every year, an exhibition for the environment is held, serving as a good place for children to learn about nature.   The ECO Experience Program is operated on an annual basis, gaining frequent attention from people.  Ecological tours of Oreum including Gotjawal, which are run by the Hallasan Mountain Research Institute. The program has tours by theme, giving you a chance to travel Halla Arboretum and get explanations from ecological experts.   You can meet the earthly smell, the embracing scent of forest, colorful forests, seasonal wildflowers of the season, and the sound of birds.  This is what the Mother Nature of Jeju brings you. Enjoy it all here at Halla Arboretum.

stories.title: Donnaeko
stories.audioTitle: A waterfall in the lush green forest in the Donnaeko
stories.script: A waterfall in the lush green forest in the Donnaeko.   A beautiful garden in a virgin forest with a waterfall.  Natural scenery with crystal clear water that flows year-round.  This is Donnaeko.  Donnaeko is Jeju’s best valley for fresh water swimming in the summer. Let’s go and see the virgin forest and its surrounding valley of Donnaeko.   Forests fill the air with more than just a fresh scent. Enjoy a perfect place to hike!  Ice cold water flows from Hallasan Mountain, making it an awesome place to play in the valley.   Donnaeko is an icy valley, and its meaning refers to an entrance where boars used to drink water.   Equipped with a physical training center and camping amenities, Donnaeko is a place that is attracting many visitors, including students and teenagers.  A gentle trail allows you to enjoy a fragrant scent from the forest and listen to sound of water. Strolling down the boardwalk will help you relax and feel better.  Donnaeko Resort has finished renovations, ready to keep everyone entertained. Amenities for kids and an outdoor performance hall are also fully equipped to handle all visitors.  The highlight of Donnaeko is the Wonang Falls. The twin streams of the waterfall seem beautiful and appealing like a Wonang, which refers to couple of mandarin ducks. Lava solidified to form the Wonang Falls, named after Wonang (a couple of mandarin ducks) because it has twin streams like a couple.  As described in its name, the waterfall boasts beautiful scenery, creating fascination for anyone.  Donnaeko is considered as a place where Jeju locals used to gather together to avoid the hot summer.  In Jeju, there is a tradition of eating chicken and getting splashed with water on Baekjung Day. This is because it is told that your neuralgia can get recovered after showering under the cascading water.   The same is true for today. In the summer, Donnaeko is filled with tourists and visitors who are seeking to get splashed with water.  Donnaeko, a virgin forest surrounded by Hallasan Mountain, will be remembered as a beautiful valley that makes you want to come again.

stories.title: Gyorae Natural Recreation Forest
stories.audioTitle: Embrace yourself in the forest and feel the healing power. Gyorae Natural Recreation Forest
stories.script: Embrace yourself in the forest and feel the healing power. Gyorae Natural Recreation Forest  Gyorae, a forest famous for its natural environment and groundwater. Gyorae Natural Recreation Forest is the only recreation forest in Korea located within a Gotjawal forest. Gyorae offers you a natural forest.   Give yourself a rest with healing power of the Gotjawal. Take time to heal yourself.   The foot of Neupseori Oreum and Keunjigri Oreum. The nation’s first Gyorae Natural Recreation Forest created within the Gotjawal Forest.   The forest is divided into four zones: a recreation area with traditional thatched houses and an outdoor performance hall, a camping area, an ecological experience area for observing Gotjawal, and a forest bathing area with trails up Keunjigri Oreum.  And a trail site, offering four trail paths toward Keunjigri Oreum. Visit here and you can experience all of them together.  You can also observe various kinds of plants which survive in a pile of stones in the forest. Follow a path through the forest for an hour, then you will deeply learn about the surrounding nature and begin to assimilate with it as well.   The Oreum trail allows visitors to glimpse the traditional life of Jeju people, including charcoal kilns and forest paths.  Crossing grassland, the top of Keunjigri Oreum boasts a spectacular view of various Oreums and Hallasan Mountain.   Your journey to Gyorae Natural Recreation Forest will be something that you will not easily forget in your lifetime. You can experience Jeju’s unique housing culture by staying in traditional thatched houses scattered throughout the forest.  The stone wall that lines the border of the house  offers a new visual experience to visitors.   You can stroll through the woods, and improve your body and mind. You will also see the nature of Gotjawal through a clear view from a clean tourist site.  Take some time to rest up in the Gyorae Natural Recreation Forest within the Gotjawal Forest. Then, the wonderful nature of Jeju will embrace you.

stories.title: Songaksan Mountain
stories.script: Songaksan Mountain, located to the south of Sanbangsan Mountain, was formerly known as Jeoluli Oreum. In Jeju dialect, 'Jeol' translates to 'wave,' a name derived from the waves crashing against the rocks. It is also known as '99-Bong' due to being surrounded by 99 small mountaintops. This largely uninhabited area boasts a scenic coastal road.  Jeju Olle Route 10 passes Sanbangsan Mountain. The trail begins at Geummorae Beach and ends at Moseulpo Port. Along this trail, hikers can relish panoramic views of Hyeongjeseom Islands, Gapado Island, and even the distant Marado Island. The path is relatively easy to walk but can get quite windy.  A ferry dock offers regular trips to and from Marado Island. Visitors can also explore the underwater world through a yellow submarine tour in the coastal waters. Moreover, the base of the mountain is renowned as one of the best fishing spots for Black Sea Bream, Rudder Fish, and Sawedged Perch, some of Jeju's most sought-after fish.  It's important to note that Songaksan Mountain holds a dark history, as it bears the scars of forced labor during the Japanese Colonial Era. The Japanese military requisitioned the local workforce to construct their military installations, leading to the destruction of the mountain's pine trees, camellias, alders, and oaks. Along the cliffs near the beach, there are seventeen artificial caves that were dug by Jeju residents under duress by the Japanese army.

stories.title: Andeokgyegok Valley
stories.script: Andeokgyegok Valley  In the beginning, when God created heaven and earth, and after seven days of clouds and mist, huge mountains began to rise, and streams wound their way between rocky cliffs, forming valleys.  Andeokgyegok Valley is the perfect place to take a rest and build a sense of virtue. Its name is derived from the sound it makes when spoken as its Chinese character.   At Andeokgyegok Valley, you can see rugged cliffs and a canyon harmonize together. Kim Jung Hee, a calligrapher also known as Chusa who was exiled during the Joseon Dynasty, said he frequently visited here because he found the scenery enchanting.  During spring and fall, you can walk along the valley from the entrance to the waterfall. In summer, the woods and forest offer cooling shade, making it the perfect escape from the heat. Down by the stream, you can enjoy playing in the water.  The volcanic island of Jeju features coastal cliffs, dense forests, and over three hundred species of plants, making Andeokgyegok Valley more unique and attractive.  The valley is surrounded by a series of cliffs, with water flowing over rocks and creating a stunning natural scene. The clear water enhances the beauty, while a variety of trees on both sides form a dense forest. This valley is home to numerous endangered and rare plants, which are protected through its designation as Natural Heritage due to its ecological significance. In the 21st century, “healing” has become a key theme in Korea. As soon as you enter the forest, the healing process begins.   The Andeokgyegok Valley, where the beauty of nature is preserved in its original state, connects to the third course of the Chusa Yubaegil (Jeju Exile Road), also known as “Road of Meditation.” This route attracts hikers and travelers who explore the area on foot. Thanks to “Gu Family Book,” a famous TV series, this place has become even more popular as a filming location.    Ancient moss that hints at the flow of time and crystal-clear water reflects the stones within the valley stream, people of all ages come with a light step to enjoy the beauty of Andeokgyegok Valley. With its stunning rocky cliffs, clear valley streams, and lush greenery all year round, come listen to the whispers of nature carried by the dense forest, and let its healing energy fill your body and mind!

stories.title: Roe Deer Ecological Observation Park
stories.audioTitle: A place where you can make deep connections with roe deer. Roe Deer Ecological Observation Park
stories.script: A place where you can make deep connections with roe deer. Roe Deer Ecological Observation Park   The foot of Hallasan Mountain is home to many plants and animals. Particularly, Jeju is famous for roe deer.   The Nature Learning Park provides ecological education, experiences, and hiking. Visit the park and get acquainted with roe deer.    Roe Deer Ecological Observation Park is located in Geochinoreum, Bonggae-dong.  Equipped with deer farms and various amenities, this has drawn a lot of curious travelers.  An observation park, allowing you to enjoy views of roe deer, is conserved in its natural state and protected to facilitate the breeding of roe deer.   For senior citizens and children who have difficulties with walking long distances, there is an observation room.  Visitors can follow a trail And can enjoy close up views of roe deer.   While walking through 2.6km of Geochinoreum trails, you can observe roe deer, and take time to free your mind. You will see yourself feel good and become relaxed.   In the exhibition hall, you can compare various kinds of roe deer in their natural appearance. In the filming hall, you can watch video footage about the life of the roe deer.  A wide variety of programs are offered to visitors including an eco-life experience program, feeding roe deer in this park, and an open space where people can enjoy all of these aspects.  The park allows visitors to observe roe deer. Children can wander into the grazing area and feed roe deer in this natural education site.  This is a resting place for people who are tired and weary. This is a place for family, couples, and friends who want to create precious memories in nature with roe deer.

stories.title: Suwolbong Peak
stories.audioTitle: The mystery of the volcanic island Suwolbong Peak
stories.script: The mystery of the volcanic island Suwolbong Peak  Designated for Bioregional Management in 2002. Selected as a World Natural Heritage Site in 2007. Recognized as a Global Geopark in 2010.   A place to obtain UNESCO designations in all 3 natural sciences. The westernmost point of Jeju.  Suwolbong Peak, designated as a Global Geopark site.  A Global Geopark site designated by Gosan-ri of Hankyung-myeon, has the largest plains on the island. Jeju Olle Trail course-12 goes through a part of Suwolbong Peak. That is how Suwolbong Peak has become known. At an altitude of 77m, the Oreum shows how magnificent the scenery is, revealing the sedimentary structures of.  In 2010, together with Hallasan Mountain, Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone, and Manjanggul Cave, Suwolbong Peak was registered as a Global Geopark site by UNESCO.  Stratification bedding arising out of volcanic activities is a typical example of a volcano. It is regarded as being important for its geological features. 	 Walk along the western seashore cliff of Suwolbong Peak, with pyroclastic deposits accumulating during volcanic activities. You can imagine how things were like 18,000 years ago, as shown through the precipitous wall of rock.  The rare plants on the cliffs that are designated and preserved as Natural Heritage not only have academic value but also offer pleasant views.   If you approach the seashore, you will experience magnificent scenery.   Various sizes of stones become stuck in each sedimentary layer.   Such stones are like volcanic bombs released from the crater during volcanic eruptions.  You can see them everywhere.    Let’s move on to Suwolbong Peak that is embraced by Mother Nature.   Getting to the summit of the peak, you can see Chagwido Island, possessing a wind power generator, port, and Dangsanbong altogether.   Artificial caves made by Japanese soldiers, Gosan Weather Station on top of the peak, and Gosanri locals who make a living through fishing. Suwolbong Peak possesses the lives of Jeju locals and their history.  Suwolbong Peak boasts marvelous views of sunrises and harmonized scenery like an artist’s masterpiece.   A Global Geopark site where you can rest and learn about history. Come and see for yourself.

stories.title: Jeju Chusa Hall
stories.script: Meeting Chusa. Jeju Chusa Hall  Jeju is said to be an island for tourists due to its beautiful scenery. However, it was basically a place of exile during the Joseon Dynasty.  It is here that Kim Jeong Hee invented his own style of calligraphy called Chusache. Let’s meet one of best scholars and artists from the Joseon Dynasty.  Exiled since being defeated in a power game. With his determination and devotion to art and learning, Kim Jeong Hee completed Chusache, his own style of calligraphy, and a masterpiece called Sehando.  During his life of exile, he taught Chinese classics and poetry to local youths and students.  He shared his life with Seon Master Choui, known as the Korean Tea Sage for the rest of his life. Seon Master Choui led to introduction of tea culture to Jeju.    As Jeju Chusa Hall was listed on the National Register of Historic Places, it opened in 2010, designed by the architect Seung Hyosang.   A single-story building with 1 basement level minimizes the building usage on the precious ground. The use of basalt and timber emphasizes Jeju’s localism.     Starting with “Haecheon Illipsang,” a portrait of Chusa when he was exiled to Jeju, there are many pieces of artwork, including calligraphy, sign boards, stone rubbing, and letter at the exhibition hall.  Sehando, a masterpiece of Chusa A famous story is an analogy between the pine tree and pine nut tree. Lee San Jeok’s character of fidelity is analogized with the pine tree and pine nut tree.  A signboard, Uimoondang, written by Chusa for the Daejeonghyanggyo Confucian School  A signboard, called Bojeongsanbang, in House of Dasan, Kangjjin, Jeollanam-do Province A signboard, written in “yeseo style”, was given to Daedunsa Temple of Haenam when he stopped by on his way into exile on Jeju A poem to admire the beauty of daffodils in bloom. Letters to express his love and longing towards his wife, Yaean Lee.  Up until three days before his death, he continued to write. His last work, called Bongeunsa Panjeon Hyunpan, is displayed here in Jeju Chusa Hall.  Chusa Hall, a memorial hall honoring Kim Jeong Hee, has an open space, making his pieces even more remarkable.  During his life in exile, he developed his unique calligraphic style known as the Chusache and produced the legendary painting, entitled 'Sehando.' He always pursued faithfulness to his principles and integrity, even during severe hardship. His honorable life will always be remembered.

stories.title: Jeju 4·3 Peace Park
stories.audioTitle: Beyond ideology, reconciliation and coexistence are achieved. Jeju 4.3. Sasam Memorial Jeju 4·3 Peace Park
stories.script: Beyond ideology, reconciliation and coexistence are achieved. Jeju 4.3. Sasam Memorial Jeju 4·3 Peace Park  Jeju Massacre, one of the deadliest armed conflicts in Korea’s modern history  Innocent men and women in Jeju were massacred 70 years ago.  As the people of Jeju fought for the event to be publicly recognized and to uncover the truth of what happened, those victims were eternally laid to rest in Jeju 4·3 Peace Park.  When South Korea tried to establish its self-government in 1948, armed conflict occurred right before the election.  While trying to suppress violent disputes, the lives of many Jeju locals were sacrificed. It is called Jeju 4.3 Incident.   As the people of Jeju fought to uncover the truth of the massacre, Jeju 4·3 Peace Park was established in 2008.   Biseol, a statue, which expresses motherhood, displays a mom who holds her baby at the very moment of death.  A monument where the name and gender of victims are carved to remember what happened on Jeju.   Jeju 4·3 Peace Park holds a memorial ceremony on every third day of April. Memorial tower is designed to show the wish of conflicts to be resolved, locals to be harmonized, and the nation to be united.  The altar is shaped in an arch to represent eternity, democracy, human rights and a resting place.  There are 15,000 spirit tablets inside the altar, honoring the deceased. Many people visit here to express their condolences to the victims.  Behind the altar, individual grave markers were built to comfort their victimized souls.  Jeju 4·3 Peace Park will serve as a place to remember the Jeju 4.3 tragedy and think about the importance of peace and human rights.  The outbreak of Jeju 4·3, the uprising massacre, and the attack of the army are displayed in six exhibition halls with vivid testimonies and photos.  Many people hid in caves to escape the violence, and nameless memorial stones now commemorate those who lost their lives there. We wish for all of them to become restored and to get their names recognized once again.  At Jeju 4·3 Peace Park, the Jeju 4·3 massacre will be  preciousness of peace, unity and humanity, and remind us of its importance.

stories.title: Chuja Provincial Marine Park
stories.audioTitle: A small archipelago of Jeju Chuja Provincial Marine Park
stories.script: A small archipelago of Jeju Chuja Provincial Marine Park  Chujado is a set of uniquely shaped islands with majestic scenery, known as a small archipelago of Jeju.  It is said to be a paradise of sea fishing for all seasons.  You are warmly welcomed to a home of dried yellowtail fish, Chujado. 	   Take a ferry in Jeju. After one hour, Chujado will become visible. Two main lands of Sangchuja and Hachuja are connected by a bridge. Chujado is consisted of 4 islands including Chupo, and Hoinggando, and 38 other islets.  You can see all the small islets, once you get to Chuja Provincial Marine Park.  Chujado is famous as one of the best places in Korea for fishing as there is an abundance of fish like rock bream or bass. That is why many fishermen are there.  When you hear the name of Chujado, dried yellowtail fish and salt-fermented anchovies will come to your mind. Low-fat white fish is preserved with bay salt. This is a product of local pride that you won’t see any other place than here, Chujado.  Let’s have a look at must-see places in Chuja.  There is Chujado Lighthouse where you can see Hallasan Mountain, and Dadohae.   From the mountaintop, you can experience the superb panorama of mountains, including Sajasoem.  Jeju Olle Trail is another famous place for visitors. You can appreciate the best scenery on Dondaesan Mountain.  Following the trail of Eundalsan Mountain with dense pine trees, you will see wild plants.   Behind Chuja Elementary School is the Shrine for General Choe Yeong.  In 1374, while General Choe i temporarily visited Chujado to suppress the rebellion in Tamra, locals taught him how to make fishing net and catch fish. The people of Chujado established this shrine to thank him.      A lighthouse park with a white tower. From the park, you can see Chuja Port, the neighborhood, a mountain, and a school as well as the beautiful view of the surrounding islets.   Pay attention to the sound created by the  waves of pebbles of the Mongdol Beach. At Mongdol Beach, you can also enjoy playing in water. Enjoy Chujado to the fullest.  If you need to get some rest and go to somewhere remote, head for Chujado!

stories.title: Halla Eco Forest
stories.audioTitle: A miniature of the environment of Hallasan Mountain Halla Eco Forest
stories.script: A miniature of the environment of Hallasan Mountain Halla Eco Forest  This is a place where a number of plants rest, providing us with comfortable resting spaces and natural phenomena.   A variety of animals and plants live together here at Halla Ecological Forest.   The wild grass area neglected for its destructed forest is restored into the original forest after nine years of effort.   Halla Eco Forest has several theme forests, including Aquatic Botanical Garden, Maple Tree Forest, and a place for a therapeutic walk in the forest. You can enjoy different views as seasons change.   Wild endangered and rare plants are protected at Halla Eco Forest.  As grassland is restored into forests, more people are visiting here.  Grey Frog Hawk and ant thrush registered as Natural Heritage, newly designated White-Backed Woodpecker, roe deer and badger who are endangered species of wild animal, and Jeju salamander find their place.  The Sootmoreu Forest Path reveals diverse forests. Sootmoreu, referring to a hill to burn charcoal, has become a place you should see.   White great tits flying in a flock and purple aconitum napiforme are waiting for you.  Water from the rock below 460m will satisfy visitors’ thirst.  Halla Eco Forest plays a vital laboratory role for plant proliferation.  The fern tree garden gives you an opportunity to see the various kinds of fern trees of Jeju. Other sites for transport process and experimental forest for warm temperature tree species are regarded as natural education sites.  Various experience programs allow children to observe the nature of animals and plants, leading them to learn about the importance of forests.   We can see living things in the forest. We will see ourselves becoming healthier than before.  Walk through Halla Eco Forest and take a gift from the clean air and Mother Nature of Jeju.

stories.title: Jeju Citrus Museum
stories.audioTitle: T/L Everything about citrus Jeju Citrus Museum
stories.script: T/L Everything about citrus Jeju Citrus Museum  Jeju Citrus Museum is a place dedicated to local citrus. You will learn everything about the fruit.  It helps recall childhood memories of adults and wisdom passing down from grandparents to grandchildren.  See, feel and experience Jeju's specialty product, the local citrus.   Citrus is always on display here at Jeju Citrus Museum.  The museum allows men and women to look at how citrus bears the fruit, and for kids to gain exotic experiences outside the classroom.  Jeju locals refer to the citrus tree as “the college tree”, because farming citrus helps parents pay for the college education of their children.   At the themed exhibition halls, there are various programs about the history of citrus, types of citrus, and cultivation methods. In the halls, there are images and displays that reveal the growing and farming of citrus.   Farming tools at the hall will help you learn more about the farming of citrus.   This is the World Citrus Hall where you can smell citrus and see the flower and fruit no matter when you visit. You can meet every kind of citrus coming from every corner of the world.   Citrus is different in its size and color. There is the horned orange which looks like a person’s hand. And there is the giant citrus, and the smallest one.   In winter, the experience program is popular as you are given a chance to pick citrus.  Another program offers you to cook with citrus, which you can join with your family and friends.  In the museum shop, a number of processed citrus products are offered, including citrus cookies, chocolates, pies, sweet jellies, and juices. Come and taste it all.   The trail at the foot of Wollabong is perfect for trekking, where you can rest, walk and play.  You can learn everything about Jeju citrus here at the Museum. This is where you can see, learn, and taste citrus. Visiting here with your family and friends will provide special memories for you.

stories.title: Jeju Folklore and Natural History Museum
stories.audioTitle: Jeju Folklore and Natural History Museum
stories.script: Jeju Folklore and Natural History Museum offers a comprehensive understanding of Jeju’s history. Through its exhibits detailing how Jeju citizens triumphed over challenges while cultivating the island for agriculture, visitors witness their resilience and wisdom in life.  The museum presents Jeju’s tradition and culture through its unique folklore and geological features. Together with the Natural Heritage Exhibition Hall, it highlights the magnificent landscapes of Hallasan Mountain, Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone, and the Geomunoreum Lava Tube System, all listed as UNESCO World Heritage sites.   In the Natural History Hall, visitors can explore the island’s origins. A major attraction is the opportunity to experience Manjanggul Cave. Additionally, the hall features a diverse array of animals and plants, including species like Dendrocopos leucotos, Brown-Eared Bulbul, Damaidae, various mushrooms and traditional tangerines.  The Folklore Exhibition Halls offer insights into the ancient lifestyle on Jeju Island. The first hall recaptures Jeju’s traditional architecture and unique customs related to rites of passage, marriages, funerals, and ancestral rituals. Notably, the globally recognized Jeju Chilmeoridang Yeongdeunggut, an intangible cultural heritage, illuminates Jeju’s distinctive religious practices. The second hall displays farming and fishing tools, providing insights into the island’s agricultural lifestyles.  In the Marine Exhibition Hall, a diverse range of marine life, including fish, seaweed, shellfish, and whales, is showcased. One of the notable displays is a 13m-long frame of a Bryde's whale, found and preserved in Jeju in 2004. The Outdoor Exhibition area further portrays the lives of Jeju's ancestors.  For those seeking a comprehensive understanding of Jeju Island's history and nature, the Jeju Folklore and Natural History Museum is an excellent starting point for their journey.

stories.title: Jeju Starlight World, Park and Planetarium
stories.audioTitle: Journey to the Universe, Jeju Starlight World, Park and Planetarium
stories.script: Journey to the Universe, Jeju Starlight World, Park and Planetarium  Jeju Starlight World, Park and Planetarium is a place where science inspires youth, the driving force of the 21st century.  Boundless imagination and stories about stars are revealed to curious onlookers.   Jeju Starlight World, Park and Planetarium is one of the best places in Jeju to ensure an entertaining evening.   Various programs, including a moon observation event, has made the park into a premier night attraction.  You can observe extrasolar planets.   Simply trying out the telescope in the observation room can bring the wonders of the universe to your eyes.  You can observe sunspots and solar flares during the day and beautiful planets like Jupiter, Saturn and other celestial bodies during the night.   The park has an abundance of rooms that have different things to experience and enjoy. A 4-D theater allows you to hear, smell, touch, taste and experience total virtual reality. Through the astronomical projector, you can rest your head back and watch a projection of the constellation as if you were looking up in the sky.   You can also ride a bike to virtually travel the solar system, or take the Time Tunnel that makes you feel like you are in the spaceship. Additionally, there are many other games that will capture the attention of children.  Last but not least, the highlight of this park is when you can listen to explanations and observe the night sky via telescope. In particular, you can have a good look at the seasonal constellation with a laser beam.  Adding to this, various kinds of experience programs and science activities are run by the Starlight camp, making it a great place for learning about the science of astronomy.   You can see, touch, feel, and experience the mysteries of the universe with your children. Take a trip to Jeju Starlight World, Park and Planetarium and unlock the dreams and imagination of children.

stories.title: Astronomical Science and Culture Center
stories.audioTitle: Astronomical Science and Culture Center with the Best View of the Star of the Old Man
stories.script: Astronomical Science and Culture Center with the Best View of the Star of the Old Man  Canopus, the Star of the Old Man, is said to give good health and longevity to whoever saw it.  The Place with the Best View of Canopus in Korea Let’s Take a Trip to the Beautiful Night Sky   A large refracting telescope and the signs of the zodiac. They all welcome you here at the Astronomical Science and Culture Center.  You can fully take in the beautiful sky in a way like you never thought possible. .   The main observatory and subobservatory are equipped with huge telescopes to observe the sun and planets..  You can observe sunspots during the day and beautiful planets and celestial bodies at night.   Whether it is sunny or rainy, or whether it is day or night, you can always experience the great universe.  Using the coordinate system, the movements of the heavenly bodies, you can learn about the constellation, and find glittering stars in the sky through an 8 meter dome screen in the planetarium.  In the exhibition room, there are images and display panels about 'Canopus,' the star symbolizing health and longevity, differing kinds of telescopes, along with insightful information about the sun, planets, and the evolution of the universe.  11) You can experience weight scale in the universe and no gravity mirror, increasing your interest in astronomy science.  Together with the Byulbit experience program, there are various programs that involve astronomical observations and images.   What do you think about taking in a movie with family on weekends? Apply for this program and you can watch a film, documentary, or animation about astronomy and space.  You can look up at the sky and deeply observe it in the Seogwipo Astronomical Science & Culture Center, a place where you will have fun with your children, while gaining valuable education.   When you were young, you might have looked up at the sky to search for stars. Come and relive those childhood memories with your children at Seogwipo Astronomical Science & Culture Center.

stories.title: Dokkaebi Road (Mystery Road)
stories.script: Imagine placing a ball on a tilted road. Typically, you would expect the ball to start rolling downhill. However, surprisingly, on this particular road in Jeju, the ball starts to roll up the hill instead. What would you do?  Following Road 1100 after passing the Jeju Art Museum, you will encounter this unique road. It is known as the ‘Dokkaebi Road’ or ‘Mystery Road.’  The name ‘Dokkaebi’ refers to mischievous hobgoblins found in Korean traditional fairy tales. The road has gained its names because when round objects are placed here, they appear to roll upward instead of downhill. Even water seems to move against gravity. Vehicles appear to defy logic and roll in the opposite direction. It's akin to witnessing magic.  You can conduct the experiment yourself. Place a water bottle or a ball on the road and observe its movement. Surprisingly, it will start rolling uphill. Isn't it fascinating? But do you want to know the truth behind this illusion?  In reality, what seems like an uphill slope is actually a descent of about 3 degrees. This optical illusion became known to the public in the 1980s. A couple of newlyweds noticed their taxi rolling uphill when they got out to take a picture. Now, it has become a popular tourist attraction. For safety, a bypass has been constructed, complete with a parking lot and walking trails for visitors.  Come and witness the mysterious road yourself and experience Dokkaebi’s magic trick.

stories.title: Seobok Exhibition Hall
stories.script: Seogwipo Art Travel — Seobok Exhibition Hall   A rock face of Jeongbang Falls has a writing engraved on it that reads “Seobulgwaji,” which means “Seobul has passed this place.” Some say that this is a proof of Seobok, an emissary of Qin Shi Huang, who once came to Jeju in search of elixir plant. Seogwipo Seobok Exhibition Hall talks about this story in detail.  According to the tale, Seobok traveled to the island with 60 boys and girls and over 5,000 men to find plants that would supposedly make Qin Shi Huang live forever. He left the writing of “Seobulgwaji” on a rock face, and some believe that this is the origin of the name, Seogwipo.  Seobok Exhibition Hall in Seobok Park opened in September 2003 and then reopened in 2009. It was built as a hanok but there is not many special aspects in terms of architecture. The outside walls and inner gate are replicated in the Chinese style. The exhibition hall has war horse statues, portrait of Seobok, two bronze carriages used in the Qin Dynasty, royal appeal and letter Seobok submitted to Qin Shi Huang, boat that Seobok is believed to have used, and replicas of Maaemyeong he made. You can also find the writing of “Seobok Park” which was donated by China through four occasions from 2005 to 2008, as well as Taesanseok Rock and murals within the park. The observatory and rest area are great places to rest your tired legs from the travel.

stories.title: Jeju Mok Gwana (Former Jeju Government Office)
stories.audioTitle: History of Jeju Jeju Mok Gwana (Former Jeju Government Office)
stories.script: History of Jeju Jeju Mok Gwana (Former Jeju Government Office)  Jeju Mok Gwana is the former central government office during Tamra to the Joseon Dynasty, serving as the center of administrative affairs, politics and culture.  When you are exhausted by the complexity of the city, how do you feel for taking a journey backwards to Jeju Mokgwana?  Located in the center of Jeju’s old city, Jeju Mok Gwana is a historic site where you can see the history of Jeju.  Jeju Mok Gwana was burned to the ground during the Japanese colonial rule and rebuilt shortly afterward.  There is Hamabi, a stone tablet indicating that anyone except the Head should dismount from a horse.   Going through Oedaemun Gate and heading inside, you will find a pond and an administrative building.   Jeju Mok Gwana reveals how things were like at that time.   There is Manggyeongnu Pavilion where people honor the King towards Hanyang, the Capital of Joseon. It also served as a watchtower to keep a look out for Japanese invaders.   Let’s take a look at Wooryundang, a banquet hall, and Yonheegak and Honhwagak, a workplace and imagine Jeju Moksa .   There is the Gyullimdang where Jeju Moksa used to grow tangerine orchards, make poems, or play Baduk. Until now, tangerine trees and stone towers remain there.   The History Experiential Program and Photo Zone are offered to visitors to see the vivid lives of Jeju Mok and experience as a Moksa, which will add more fun to your journey.  Goonroichung, which controls soldiers and Hojukbang which issues identification, are restored.   Jeju Mok Gwana is not just a place for historical remains but also a place to provide historical education.   As time goes on, the local heritage has increased in value. So why don’t you get out of the downtown area and go and see Jeju’s old Donghyun?

stories.title: Jeju National Museum
stories.audioTitle: The history and culture of Jeju  Jeju National Museum
stories.script: The history and culture of Jeju  Jeju National Museum   Here at Jeju National Museum, you can see Jeju’s unique geographical features, culture, history, and heritage.  Let’s head back to the prehistoric age.   Jeju National Museum is the figuration of traditional thatched house. It contains various materials about its unique culture and history, and more than 7,000 remains.   The museum is consisted of six exhibition rooms; Prehistory room, Tamra room, Goryeo room, Tamrasunsyukdo room, Joseon room, and Donation room.  The Prehistory room is where you can learn about the birth of Jeju, the settlement process of the first Jeju residents, and development of culture before Tamra.  The Tamra room reveals the birth of Tamra and exchanges with its surrounding nations.  In the Tamrasunsyukdo room, you can see treasure No. 652-6, Tamra Sullyeokdo, illustrating the governor of Tamra, Lee Hyung Sang. This picture book gives us an opportunity to look at Jeju, three hundred years ago  The records and articles of so-called drifters and the exiled are among items we need to see.  'Pyo Hae Rok' is a story about drifters who were on their way to take the civil service test but became lost due to the wind and waves and drifted to Okinawa. Along with Pyo Hae Rok, copies of the Journal of Hendrick Hamel, exiles of Kim Jung, Song Siyul, Kim Jung Hee, Choi Ikhyun and their keepsakes are regarded as something interesting.   The clothes and tools of female divers, shamanistic faith, and remains are the last part of the museum.  However, this is not the end. Children’s Olle, an experience center allows children to experience history and the ability to make a rubbing or wood board printing.  Furthermore, the museum holds various special exhibitions, permanent ones, culture classes, experience events, and performances as well.  Jeju National Museum operates meaningful and useful programs and provides materials.   This is a precious museum to learn about Jeju.

stories.title: World Natural Heritage Jeju Center
stories.audioTitle: Meet the wonders of a volcanic island, Jeju. World Natural Heritage Jeju Center
stories.script: Meet the wonders of a volcanic island, Jeju. World Natural Heritage Jeju Center  The entire island is like a “Volcano Museum”, showing how unique the topography of Jeju is.  The value of Jeju was proven when the island was designated as a Biosphere Reserve, World Natural Heritage, and Jeju Island Global Geopark, making it the only place on Earth to receive all three UNESCO designations in natural sciences.  A 'treasure island of environmental assets' that the world has to preserve. At the center of the effort is the World Natural Heritage Jeju Center.  Hallasan Mountain together with Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone It is located in front of Geomunoreum Lava Tube System, registered as a World Natural Heritage.  The Permanent exhibition hall, Special exhibition hall, and 4D video room allow you to experience a new Jeju.  At the center is the Permanent exhibition hall that has 7 themed rooms including the birth of Jeju, miniature, exhibitions, giving you opportunities to feel closer.   Particularly, take the circular elevator and you feel you are right there in the process of forming Jeju, from the ocean to Baengnokdam Crater Lake.   World Natural Heritage Jeju Center is worth a visit to gain education on understanding Jeju, the volcanic island, and become fascinated by the world because the center covers every living thing from animals and plants to marine ecosystems.  World Natural Heritage Jeju Center serves as a starting point to travel to Geomunoreum. Geomunoreum requires you to reserve in advance.  Going along with experts will give you detailed explanations on geological features and vegetation about Oreum, Gotjawal. Therefore, bringing your children will be a wise idea.  Join the International Trekking Festival which is held every year.  Jeju is a masterpiece of Mother Nature, and you can feel and experience everything about Jeju here at the World Natural Heritage Jeju Center.

stories.title: Jeju Haenyeo Museum
stories.audioTitle: Appreciate the portrait of Haenyeo Jeju Haenyeo Museum
stories.script: Appreciate the portrait of Haenyeo Jeju Haenyeo Museum  A ‘haenyeo’ is a woman diver who gathers marine products for a living, and fends off the challenges of working in the strong seas.  This is the only Haenyeo museum in Korea where we can see their life, joys and sorrows. Let’s listen to their stories, who have spent their lifetime under the water.  One of three anti-Japanese movements is “Jeju Haenyeo Movement”, which originated from Hadori, Gujwaeup. That is where the Museum is located.   Jeju Haenyeo Museum consists of three exhibition halls and experience halls for children.  Exhibition Hall 1 is about the life of Haenyeo divers. You can see Jeju’s traditional customs and fishing village life through the houses and clothes of Haenyeo, food replicas, and household goods.  Exhibition Hall 2 is about the job of Haenyeo divers. Clothing and tools used by Jeju Haenyeo, and a fireplace that helps warm up their body, allow you to see Haenyeo’s workplace.  Exhibition Hall 3 is about the sea which is the site of living of them. In Hall 3, you will see the site of living of not only Haenyeo but also if their husband.   It also exhibits Taewoo, a traditional boat of Jeju. You will see fishing activities, even from ancient eras, including anchovy fishing that used Taewoo.   If you come with your family and children, this is a must-visit place. Go to Haenyeo’s house to learn about food and the language they use.  Moreover, the museum reveals the myth of the Coral Haenyeo, a story about a brave Haenyeo, using cute figures.  There are various activities you can enjoy like trying on the attire of Haenyeo’s, boating, and catching some sea creatures.   The museum provides a regular Haenyeo singing performance to promote the value and superiority of the Haenyeo culture. Visitors and tourists can join in on the performance together and experience traditional Jeju culture.  Jeju Haenyeo, who has fought through strong seas, should be remembered and preserved as our heritage.  That is what Jeju Haenyeo Museum is for.

stories.title: Jeju Anti-Japanese Memorial Hall
stories.audioTitle: A leading role in the public movements of Jeju, Jeju Anti-Japanese Memorial Hall
stories.script: A leading role in the public movements of Jeju, Jeju Anti-Japanese Memorial Hall  The people of Jeju were actively involved in anti-Japanese independence movements during the colonial period.  Here at Jeju Anti-Japanese Memorial Hall, let’s take a look.  Beautiful scenery unfolds on Jeju Olle Trail course 19 where Jeju Anti-Japanese Memorial Hall, a leading role in anti-Japanese independence movements, is located.  This is where we pay tribute to deceased patriots who lost their lives in Jocheon Mansedongsan, the origin of the independence movement. This is where historical materials for independence during Japanese colonial rule are being displayed.  In the Memorial Hall, there are 470 kinds of documents, including recorded documents about anti-Japanese movements and activists, along with a video called ‘The End of the Japanese Army’.  Enter Jeju Hangil Memorial Hall, and you will see statues of Jeju’s descendants which express the spirit of the anti-Japanese resistance.  The hall is comprised of two floors of exhibition rooms where photos, records, and documents are displaying which highlight the independence movements of Jeju and the rest of the nation.  There is also a sword, a relic left by the Kim Hyung Jin, who led independence movements together with Kim Koo in China.  A miniature of 3 Jeju movements against Japanese colonial rule helps you to have a better understanding about the political efforts in the past.   You can observe the torture scene of anti-Japanese patriot. Looking at the scene between red bricks, you can indirectly visualize the experience.  Let’s proudly remember our Jeju’s ancestors who led these independence movements.  In front of the center is a ceremonial monument commemorating the March 1st independence movement. Its importance and meaning will always be passed down to our sons and grandsons.  Jeju Hangil Memorial Hall will be used to honor the great sacrifices of our patriotic ancestors and their contributions to the nation’s independence.

stories.title: Yesan Daeheung Slow City
stories.audioTitle: Simple Joys of Life Shaped by Peaceful Hands
stories.script: Simple Joys of Life Shaped by Peaceful Hands  Yesan Daeheung is the sixth slow city in Korea designated by Cittaslow International. It is located close to Yedang Reservoir, the largest reservoir in Korea, and encompasses Eungbong-myeon and Daeheung-myeon.   As visitors walk the alleys of this slow city, they will rediscover the meaning of “slow,” “small” and “persistence,” and hence remember the simple joys of life. Nearby attractions like Bongsusan Mountain, Yedang Reservoir, Imjonseong Fortress and Daeheungeupseong Fortress have great natural and historical value.   In addition, Yesan Daeheung Slow City has many stories to tell. One example is the “Story of the Good Brothers,” which was included in elementary school textbooks. This is a true story about Lee Seong-man and Lee Sun, two brothers who lived in Daeheung Village. Their strong brotherly love is still remembered to this day through events and festivals such as the Good Brothers Market, and the Gyochon-ri Ginkgo Tree Village Ritual.  The village welcomes people in search of the slow and simple joys of life, and the generosity and kindness of the villager can be felt along the Slow and Winding Trail and Palm Garden Trail.

stories.title: Good Brothers Park and the Houses of the Good Brothers
stories.audioTitle: Into the Story of the Good Brothers
stories.script: Into the Story of the Good Brothers  Good Brothers Park is the first impression people get of Daeheung Village. Situated by the entryway to the village, statues of the two brothers stand side by side at the entrance of the park, greeting visitors.   Although there are plenty of stories of brotherly affection, there is something special about the story from Daeheung Village. The story of the good brothers is a true story about Lee Seong-man and Lee Sun, two brothers who lived in this village between the late 14th and early 15th centuries (from the end of the Goryeo period to the early Joseon period). Worried and concerned about each other, both Seong-man and Sun spent nights going back and forth to each other’s houses leaving rice sheaves by the door.  Good Brothers Park has recreated the houses of the brothers. The younger brother Lee Sun’s house is located at the park entrance, and the older brother Lee Seong-man’s house is across the creek, past the watermill. Figurines placed between the two houses depict the lives of people at the time. Visit the homes and try to feel the love and warmth of the brothers.   “Beautiful actions remain fragrant for a thousand years.” This is just one of the writings attached to the columns of the houses; a reminder that not even time can change or fade the fondness and warmth between people.

stories.title: Good Brothers Market and the old Daeheung 5-day Market
stories.audioTitle: A Friendly and Vibrant Village Market
stories.script: A Friendly and Vibrant Village Market   The Good Brothers Market takes place in Yesan Daeheung Slow City every second Saturday of the month between April and November. In the open area of Good Brothers Park, local farmers and villagers sell various fresh farm produce, handicrafts and second-hand clothes. A variety of food stalls and fascinating performances add fun to the full atmosphere of the country market.   The Daeheung 5-day Market, which had been held every five days until the 1970s, is the predecessor of the Good Brothers Market. The traditional market was held on days ending with the numbers 4 and 9, and is said to have had a cattle market and a blacksmith’s shop, as well as crops, vegetables and fruits. Moreover, a wrestling competition held on market day was an exciting spectacle, which makes it possible to imagine the scale of the market back then. The Good Brothers Market, which was revived along with the slow city, also offers special experience programs such as making wish mobiles and making flower pots using plastic bottles, as well as folk games such as the Bobusang Nanjeon (peddlers’ brawl) and a music concert.   Although quiet and slow travel is the charm of a slow city, the warmth and friendliness shared by locals in the market will remind you of old friends and neighbors you’ve lost touch with.

stories.title: Stone Monument Street
stories.audioTitle: Travel to the Past through Stone Monuments
stories.script: Travel to the Past through Stone Monuments  The Good Brothers Road, which is the main street of Daeheung Village, was the path ahead of Oesammun Gate, three outer gates at the entranceway of the Daeheung Government Office during the Joseon Dynasty. The name “Stone Monument Street” is derived from the numerous stone monuments at the entrance of the road, which were erected to praise the good deeds and achievements of local government officers from Daeheung Village.    Although the sizes and shapes of the stone monuments are slightly different from each other, they represent the history of the village, connecting the present and the past. The oldest stele among them is one that was erected in 1578 to commemorate Governor Yu Mong-hak’s administration. As a person advocating political reform, he was highly revered to the extent that he was deeply mourned by villagers when he died.   Among the recently discovered steles is a memorial stone for the chief of the village, who while in office gathered and preserved the stone monuments that were scattered all over the village. If you read the inscriptions on the old gravestones, you will feel as if traveling into the past.     As you walk along the street, you may be able to picture the history of the village as well as the ordinary people of the village who left no written record of their existence. The beauty of travelling in a slow city may be the ability to take a moment to reflect on your life in today’s fast-paced society.

stories.title: Wish Mobile Tunnel and Poem Tunnel
stories.script: Wishes Awakened by the Wind  The street with the Wish Mobile Tunnel and the Poem Tunnel is a newly rising tourist attraction located in the northern section of Good Brothers Park. The Wish Mobile Tunnel hangs mobiles made by visitors with their wishes written on them, and the Poem Tunnel displays poems written by elderly women of a neighboring village.  Colorful mobiles full of hopes and wishes welcome visitors to the 10m-long Wish Mobile Tunnel. Messages filled with love and affection are as diverse as the number of mobiles, and are interesting and fun to read. Take a moment to listen to the wind touching the mobiles made of cypress tree. It will bring peace and comfort to your heart and mind.   Anyone can purchase wish mobiles at the Slow Hand Workshop and write wishes to be hung in the tunnel.   The Poem Tunnel features poems written by grandmothers who live in the neighboring Mubong-ri village. Their poems are not refined, but their sincerity can be felt in each of the words. Take a few minutes to write your own poem.

stories.title: Slow City Visitor Center
stories.script: Slow City, Ask About Anything  If you are planning a slow yet productive trip to Yesan Daeheung Slow City, the first thing you should do is visit the Slow City Visitor Center. The center offers free travel guides and brochures, as well as maps for various attractions in the area, including trails and byroads in the village. Moreover, you can join a tour with a volunteer guide offered by the village residents for an exploration of the area.  The Slow City Visitor Center is located in the center of the village where many alleys and paths meet. The intersection in front of the Center is near Oesammun Gate, which once served as the village entrance. Because the gate was the entryway to the village for a long time, this is the perfect place to start a journey of the village.   The visitor center is the only building that has been newly established in the village since Daeheung was designated a slow city. The cozy one-story building with a low stone wall and a small garden reflects the life of a slow city. You can work on your itinerary in the small lookout shed, or the chairs in the yard.   We recommend to visitors, especially families, the traditional culture experience programs offered at the center, which includes traditional kite-flying. You can make your very own kite and fly them in the playground of Daeheung Elementary School.

stories.title: Daeheung Elementary School
stories.script: The Mirror of Daeheung Village  If you are planning a slow yet productive trip to Yesan Daeheung Slow City, the first thing you should do is visit the Slow City Visitor Center. stories.title: Good Brothers Monument and the Good Brothers Statue
stories.audioTitle: Where the Story of Good Brothers is Told
stories.script: Where the Story of Good Brothers is Told  If you stand in the plaza in front of the Daeheung Government Office the Good Brothers Monument and the Good Brothers Statue can be seen. The monument and statue were erected to pay tribute to Lee Seong-man and Lee Sun, two brothers who carried rice sheaves to each other’s houses all night long out of brotherly affection.  The two brothers were chief of Daeheung Village from the late Gorye Dynasty to the early Joseon Dynasty. Their strong brotherly love was clearly prominent in their daily lives, to the extent that they visited each other’s houses every day and night, and shared food with each other whenever they prepared delicious meals. They were also extolled as paragons of filial piety.  The names of the two brothers appear in Sejong Sillok, the Annals of King Sejong of the Joseon Dynasty. According to this history, the King selected 41 people who were exemplary in local society, and the brothers’ names were at the top of the list. They received heavy media coverage when their memorial stone were coincidentally discovered in 1970 near Gaebaengi Bridge. It seemed to remind future generations of the importance of family love.   In front of the monument stands the Good Brothers Statue made by sculptor Jeong Jeong-sik, along with a 200-year-old Zelkova tree. The statue portrays the moment when the two brothers encountered each other while on their way to and from rice piles. Take this time to sit under the tree and think about your loving family.

stories.title: Daeheung Government Office and Filming Site of “Hometown over the Hill”
stories.audioTitle: Relax at the Old Government Office
stories.script: Daeheung Government Office and Filming Site of “Hometown over the Hill” Relax at the Old Government Office  Daeheung Government Office and the Daeheung Guesthouse were the center of the old Daeheung Village. There used to be several other government office buildings around it, but only the Daeheung office building remains today.   Daeheung Government Office was built in 1407 and underwent renovation during the mid-Joseon Dynasty. It was transformed into the Daeheung-myeon Office during Japanese colonial rule in 1914 and continued to be used as a public facility until 1979. Later, the Daeheung-myeon Office moved to a new location, and the building was renovated to its current state.   The daecheongmaru, a traditional wood-floored porch, in the Daeheung Government Office is the most peaceful spot in the village. It is perfect for taking a rest and enjoying the landscape. The Zelkova tree outside the main gate also offers a great view.   The backyard of the government building is where the TV drama “Hometown over the Hill” was filmed. Dozens of earthen pots sit under the cherry tree creating a cozy atmosphere.   For a little history tour, behind the government building over the fence are the Placenta Monument of Princess Hwaryeong, the daughter of King Yeongjo, and the Anti-foreign Stele of Regent Heungseon Daewongun.

stories.title: Snail Art Museum
stories.audioTitle: Slow Art of a Slow City
stories.script: Slow Art of a Slow City  As it befits its claim as a slow city, Daeheung Village has an art museum named after the snail, a symbol of slowness. This museum mainly offers exhibitions that help you slow down and reflect on your life, as well as artistic creations produced by local residents and a collection of artifacts and household items possessed by individuals. Indeed, it can be referred to as a slow art exhibition that allows you to get a glimpse of the slow life of the local village artists.   The Snail Museum opened in 2013 when the office of the old health center branch in Daeheung-myeon, which had been used as the set for the KBS drama “Hometown over the Hill,” was transformed into the museum. As you appreciate the work on display, you might be deeply impressed by the homely, modest works produced by locals, rather than renowned artists. Their simple and modest works will give you comfort and peace of mind.     There are wooden sotdae poles and bird figurines made of banners all over the grounds outside the museum. The sotdae poles were made by local seniors to be used at the Nature Art Festival held in the slow city. Because no preservation treatment was used, the sotdae pole eventually fall apart, and then the elders rebuilt the poles. The slow pace of the village will bring peace and serenity.

stories.title: Stone Statue of Grandfather Mangtae in Dongseo-ri
stories.script: Stone Grandfather Guards the Village  A granite statue of “Grandfather Mangtae” stands at the entrance of Dongseo-ri Village on Yedang-ro Road. Like a village elder that watches over the village, the statue greets and welcomes visitors with a generous smile. Every year on the first day of February, villagers perform rituals in front of the statue to pray for a good harvest and the well-being of the community.   Although it is unknown when the stone statue was created, its form remains relatively unchanged despite the many years. If you hear the various tales about the statue from the locals, you will feel and respect the admiration they have towards it.  It has been told that a long time ago, various contagious diseases like typhoid and smallpox swept through the village, killing a number of people. Then an old man carrying a mangtae (woven basket) on his back appeared in the village one day and told the villagers that they should erect a stone Buddha statue to put a stop to the calamities. After they erected the stone Buddha as the old man had said, all the infectious diseases disappeared from the village. As rumors circulated that the stone Buddha worked marvels, people tried to steal the statue so villagers moved the statue to different locations. But each time the statue was moved the village suffered from misfortunes, so they moved it back to its original place. Say hello to the statue and maybe it will bring you good luck too.

stories.title: Daeheunghyanggyo Confucian School and the Ginkgo Tree Ritual
stories.audioTitle: A Love Tree Next to the Confucian School
stories.script: A Love Tree Next to the Confucian School  Along with the Daeheung Government Office, Daeheunghyanggyo Confucian School represents the history of Daeheung. Being a public educational facility of the Joseon Dynasty, memorial services for ancestors are performed here.  If you enter Gyochon-ri Village from Yedang-ro Road, Daeheunghyanggyo is behind the Gingko tree at the end of the field. The original school was built in 1405 on a hill within a pine forest, but was damaged during the Japanese Invasion of Korea in 1592 and the current school was restored at the present site later on.  The ginkgo tree in front of the school is as old and is historically valuable as the Confucian school. The tree, about 700 years old, is 20 meters high with an approximate circumference of 5.85 meters. Strangely, a Zelkova tree has been growing inside the ginkgo tree, and they have been growing together for about 150 years. For this reason, villagers call the two entwined trees the “love tree.”    The people of Daeheung Village perform a ginkgo tree ritual called “Haengjanggunje” early in January every year. After the ritual is performed in the Confucian school, it is moved to the ginkgo tree. The villagers show their respect and devotion by inviting a Buddhist monk to pray for the blessing and well-being of the community.  When fall comes, the colorful autumn leaves of the ginkgo and Zelkova trees present a magnificent spectacle. And people believe that if the leaves of the Gingko tree all fall at once, it is a sign for a good harvest year. As you look at the tree, which over the 700 years of its existence it only took up 20 meters of height, and shared its life with a Zelkova for over 150 years, you may be able to feel its humbleness and generosity.

stories.title: Baemaen Tree and Dongje Ritual
stories.audioTitle: The Baemaen Tree that Survived Through 1,000 Years
stories.script: The Baemaen Tree that Survived Through 1,000 Years  By a creek in Sangjung-ri an old Zelkova tree stands proud and tall. Approximately 1,050 years old, this tree is the oldest in all of Chungcheongnam-do Province.  It is a living witness that has watched over Daeheung Village and its people for a very long time.  The people of the village call the tree the “Baemaen Tree,” which literally translates to “tree with boats tied to it.  In 660, when General Su Dingfang of the Tang Dynasty led his forces into Daeheung Village to attack the restoration forces of the Baekje Kingdom, he had his boats tied to the tree, and scars said to be from the tied boats remain at the base of the tree to this day. For this reason, it is assumed that at the time part of this area was covered by the sea. You can sit under the tree and imagine what it would have been like 1,000 years ago?  Every year on the first day of February, locals perform a ritual around the Baemaen Tree to pray for a good harvest and the well-being of the community.   As a witness to the fall of the Baekje Kingdom, Baemaen Tree is a historical site.  To better explore the history of Baekje, you should also visit Imjonseong Fortress on Bongsusan Mountain which was the base camp of the restoration army of the Baekje Kingdom.

stories.title: Terraced Rice Paddy Path in Sangjung-ri and Dongseo-ri
stories.audioTitle: Crooked Fields of the Slow City
stories.script: Crooked Fields of the Slow City   By the boundary between Sangjung-ri and Dongseo-ri is a small path amidst the terraced rice paddies. Although the area is neither a scenic spot nor a tourist attraction, the terraced rice paddies present a beautiful landscape.   Originally, Daeheung Village had farming fields on high altitude areas and rice paddies in low altitudes. But with the construction of the Yedang Reservoir, the rice paddies were submerged by water, so the farming fields were turned into rice paddies. Since left over land on relatively hilly areas were used, they naturally formed terraced rice paddies, which is rare in Yesan.   There are various ways to get to the terraced paddy field, but we recommend that you take the first byway on the right past the “House of Breath and Rest” on Course 1 of the Slow and Winding Trail. The road is lined with wild flowers, and about 200 meters up the road, turn right. The beautiful terraced rice paddies will unfold before your eyes.  The terraced rice paddies are a unique site. The rows of rice paddies follow the winding contour of the land, offering a breathtakingly beautiful view along with the village and Yedang Resevoir just below the rice paddies.

stories.title: Slow and Winding Trail, Course 1: Path of Old Stories
stories.audioTitle: Path of Stories with a Nice View
stories.script: Path of Stories with a Nice View   Course 1 of the Slow and Winding Trail is a hiking trail that leads to Bongsusan Natural Recreation Forest and offers a magnificent view of Yedang Reservoir and the village. Every little byway and alley has a story to it, which is why this trail is referred to as the “Path of Old Stories.”  Vestiges of the Baekje Kingdom can still be seen along the trail leading to Bongsusan Natural Recreation Forest. The Baemaen Tree to which Tang Dynasty’s General Su Dingfang ordered his forces to tie their boats, and the trail in Imjonseong Fortress used to transfer supplies for the restoration forces of Baekje, tell us interesting stories of fierce battles.   On Good Brothers Street, which runs in front of Daeheung Government Office, stand a monument and statue of the Good Brothers, Lee Seong-man and Lee Sun. Visitors can sit under the Zelkova tree and enjoy the view, and maybe feel the brotherly love.   Tour maps of the Slow and Winding Trail are available at the Slow City Visitor Center. Discover intriguing stories and historical clues behind the beautiful stone fence and the 100-plus year old tree on Course 1 of the Slow and Winding Trail.

stories.title: Slow and Winding Trail, Course 2: Slow Path
stories.audioTitle: The Slower the Pace, the More Profound the Experience
stories.script: The Slower the Pace, the More Profound the Experience  Course 2 of the Slow and Winding Trail offers many different sights, including a forest trail, village road, and historic sites. The path is also known as the “Slow Path,” as resting areas can be found at every path and trail. Course 2 is ideal for experiencing “rest” and “relaxation,” the main themes of a “slow city” tour.  Just outside the Daeheung-myeon Office, visitors can see and feel the charm of the Slow Path. The first section, called the “Path along a Stream,” consists of a stone road and houses lining a stream, creating a remote and quiet atmosphere. Aegi Falls, located passed the wonderfully shaded Eunhajakgyo Bridge, at the end of the waterway and the Aramteo rest area, is the perfect place to take your first break.   If you turn north from the waterfall, you will encounter a remote and quiet forest trail called the “Road for Meditation,” and an observatory. Right when the trail begins sloping downhill, you will see another trail which was used by peddlers to come and go between Hongseong and Yesan. You can also take time to meditate and think of the aesthetics of slowness offered by the slow city under the shade of a ginkgo tree in front of the Daeheunghyanggyo Confucian School, where peddlers could have stopped for a short rest.

stories.title: Slow and Winding Trail, Course 3: Love Path
stories.script: Path to Ideal Love  Unlike Course 1 and Course 2, Course 3 of the Slow and Winding Trail is a one-way course. It starts at the visitor center and ends at a lookout shed atop a hill in Gyochon-ri. This path is referred to as the “Love Path” because of a huge, 700-year-old ginkgo tree in front of Daeheunghyanggyo Confucian School. When fall comes, the leaves of the giant ginkgo tree turn a brilliant yellow.   If you take a closer look at the tree, you will find a Zelkova tree growing inside the ginkgo tree. It is presumed that a Zelkova tree seed fell into a crack in the bark of the ginkgo tree. Because the two trees are so tightly entwined with each other, people call it the “Love Tree.” It is said that the two trees have grown together for as long as 150 years. You can take a rest under the tree, and maybe think about the meaning of love.   The ginkgo tree divides Course 3 into the first half and the latter half. The first half of the course consists of walking the historic village alleys and ridges between rice paddies and fields, while the latter half includes the Sosaem rest area and the Samsindang Shrine site located on a slight uphill that leads to the lookout shed. The view of Yedang Reservoir seen from the lookout shed is also stunning.

stories.title: Palm Garden Trail, Course 1
stories.audioTitle: Enjoying a Quiet Walk and a Pretty Garden
stories.script: Enjoying a Quiet Walk and a Pretty Garden  The “Palm Garden Trail” was created by connecting small gardens made by local residents. Close to 50 households opened the doors to their garden so that visitors can take short breaks.  Course 1 of the trail starts and finishes at the Slow City Visitor Center, turning back at the “House of Breath and Rest.” Tour maps of the gardens are available at the Visitor Center. The gardens along this trail have cute names, so try reading and visiting each garden. Only houses with the snail figurine are open to the public, so before you enter, make sure to check for the snail.   The house named “Scissorhand’s Climbing Rose Garden” is very popular, the owners’ care and dedication can be seen in the beautiful roses and Satsuki azaleas. You can also rest in the small pavilion and enjoy a cup of tea prepared by the owners.   If you prefer a quiet walk alone, you can walk up to the “House of Breath and Rest” and sit on the wooden benches and take a rest before continuing your journey.

stories.title: Palm Garden Trail, Course 2
stories.audioTitle: Path for Appreciating the Scenery of Daeheung Village and Yedang Reservoir
stories.script: Path for Appreciating the Scenery of Daeheung Village and Yedang Reservoir  Course 2 of the Palm Garden Trail goes around the Dongseo-ri region of Daeheung Village. Visitors can enjoy beautiful views of the entire village and Yedang Reservoir.    Because locals have generously opened their gardens to the public, visitors can enjoy the beautifully tended gardens and flower beds. The first garden on this path is “Myeong-jun’s Yard,” which is decorated with small earthen pots. At “Columbine Grandmother’s Garden” pretty columbines can be seen every spring.   If you walk passed the flower gardens you will come upon “Jinhoe’s Sky Garden.” The owner of the house collects antiques and other old things. Sinseollo (royal hot pot) pots, public telephones, folding screens, matchboxes, and other time-honored objects will make you feel as if you were traveling back in time. Right next to the garden is the village’s one and only barber shop, which is also filled with old things and antiques.   The deck at the Central Eco Park of Yedangho Lake offers a panoramic view of the Yedang Reservoir. The cool breeze and generous reservoir will wash away your worries.

stories.title: Palm Garden Trail, Courses 3 and Course 3-1
stories.script: Hyanggyo Village in Full Bloom  Courses 3 and 3-1 of the Palm Garden Trail start at the Stone Monument Street and lead to Hyanggyo Village, allowing visitors to look into the history and enjoy old stories of Daeheung Village.   The palm gardens at the Grass Bride’s Yard and the Gyochon Hanok Experience Hall, and the vast rice paddies on the way to Hyanggyo Village, colorfully greet and welcome visitors. Even the elders you meet while traveling the village will greet you warmly and generously.   The pine tree hill and the ginkgo tree you see in the far distance is where Hyanggyo Village is. The 600-year-old Confucian school in the middle of the village and the ginkgo tree will tell you something about the village’s long history.   Hyanggyo Village also features palm gardens created by the local residents. The house without a gate or a fence in front of the ginkgo tree opens its garden to all visitors. The “Pond with Frogs,” which is also the name of the house, is so small and cute it will make you smile. Since the owner stopped using herbicides in his yard, frogs and newts began appearing in the yard, and in the summer, you can hear the pleasant croaking of the frogs. Each house and each garden has a unique story behind it.

stories.title: Peak of Bongsusan Mountain
stories.audioTitle: The Main and Guardian Mountain of Daeheung Village
stories.script: The Main and Guardian Mountain of Daeheung Village  Situated behind Daeheung Village, Bongsusan Mountain is thought of as the mother and root of the village for it was formed as people began to settle at the foot of the mountain. The villagers are very fond of the mountain, and it is often referred to as Daeheungsan Mountain.  According to old geography books, Bongsusan was a guardian mountain.   People usually perform ancestral rituals at guardian mountains that were believed to protect the capital or village. Tourists usually visit Bongsusan Natural Recreation Forest and then head for Imjonseong Fortress, whereas the local residents hike up the tops of the mountain through Beoti Pass. The pass connects Daeheung and Hongseong villages, and offers panoramic views of the two villages. If you get a chance to look down onto the village, you will see a miniature world.   The rooftop observatory at the Yedang (Native Fish) Eco Experience Center of Yedang Reservoir offers a stunning view of Bongsusan Mountian and Daeheung Village. Bogsusan stretches its ridges and warmly hugs the slow and peaceful village.

stories.title: Bongsusan Natural Recreation Forest & Bongsusan Arboretum
stories.script: A Forest Enriching the Soul  The Bongsusan Natural Recreation Forest and the Bongsusan Mountain Arboretum situated on Bongsusan Mountain, provide visitors with a great place to take a break from life and relax.  The Bongsusan Natural Recreation Forest is equipped with lodging facilities and walking trails, and offers a great view of Yedang Reservoir and the village below. The sunrise over the reservoir is exceptional, and on hot summer days, swimming in the creek is very popular. Since the opening of the Bongsusan Arboretum in early 2015, approximately 1,500 species of plants have formed a “forest inside a forest.”  Hiking trails from the recreational forest head to Imjonseong Fortress and the summit. The trail south of the recreational forest leading to Dongnu, or east pavilion of Imjonseong Fortress offers a nice view. “Dongnu-gil” was misinterpreted by locals and is now called the “Dongmulwon-gil,” or Zoo Trail. Although not an easy climb, the pavilion offers magnificent views of Yedang Reservoir below.    Other than the trail to the pavilion, Bongsusan has many more trails in its forest. You can walk through trees, walk along the creek, or just stand amid nature while listening to the birds, and the wind. You will not have time to be bored.

stories.title: Imjonseong Fortress and Myosuni Rock
stories.audioTitle: Fortress of the Myosuns Who Protected Daeheung
stories.script: Fortress of the Myosuns Who Protected Daeheung  Imjonseong Fortress, which was the last bastion of the Baekje Restoration Movement, means “the place where the king is.” Perhaps due to the pride of the people of Daeheung Village, who were direct descendants of Baekje, Bongsusan was referred to as a fortress rather than a mountain. Imjonseong Fortress encloses the two eastern peaks of Bongsusan. The area where Nammun, or South Gate was located has been restored, and stones that were part of the fortress can also be found in other nearby areas.
