Since its foundation, the temple has served as a temporary residence to many great monks, such as, Doseon, Muhak and Hyojeong, and it came to be known as the most preeminent temple in the region of Yeongseo.”  “Perfectly positioned from a geological sense—as if a mystical turtle was spitting out a lotus flower, while nine sea dragons hang in the air like clouds—Guryongsa is known as the most ideally located temple, and as its name implies, as a residence for these mystical animals.”  “The primary reason for its fame, however, comes from the many respected monks who have cultivated their minds in this very temple for over a thousand years.”   “Guryongsa was founded by Great Master Uisang in 668, the 8th year of King Munm, the 30th ruler of the Silla Kingdom. In the late Silla and early Goyeo period, National Teacher Doseon proclaimed the concept of ‘Bibosachal,’ stating that founding a temple on a famous mountain could help the fate of the nation. Guryongsa is one of the temples founded for that purpose.”  “As it took an exceedingly long time for the Geumgang pine trees to grow high into the air, Guryongsa is surrounded by an ancient mystical legend.”  “Located within Chiaksa National Park in Wonju City, Gangwon-do Province, the traditional temple Guryongsa is subject to an endless stream of prayers from both monks and devotees.”

stories.title: The Legend of Guryongsa
stories.script: The Legend of Guryongsa   “Long long ago, about 1,300 years ago, Great Master Uisang, who had been practicing at famous sites throughout the country, arrived at Chiaksan Mountain…”  “Hmm…this is quite the spot! With Birobong Peak to the east, and Cheonjibong Peak in front, this would be the ideal location for a temple!”  “However, there was a deep pond at the location which was home to nine dragons. Great Master Uisang couldn’t just kick the dragons out so he pondered how to solve the situation, thinking, ‘What can be done?’ Suddenly...  “Upon hearing Great Master Uisang’s contemplation, the nine dragons caused a torrent of rain to fall from the sky, covering the mountain with water. They proposed to Great Master Uisang that if he could survive the rain, they would leave the mountain.”  “Suddenly, the pond dried up and the nine dragons began to flee. One of the dragons became blind, while those remaining cut the mountain in front into eight pieces before vanishing.”  “After the nine dragons disappeared, Great Master Uisang again filled the pond and proceeded to found his temple. To reflect the story of its founding, Great Master Uisang named the temple Guryongsa.”  ”Following this, to incorporate the linage of the nearby turtle rock, the character ‘gu’ meaning nine was changed to the character ‘gu’ meaning turtle, and the name Guryongsa came to be finalized.”

stories.title: Gwaneumjeon Hall (Guryongsa Temple, Wonju)
stories.script: Gwaneumjeon Hall of Guryongsa Temple  Gwaneumjeon Hall of Guryongsa Temple in Chiaksan Mountain is a hall located on the left hill. Gwaneumjeon Hall refers to the dharma hall enshrined with Gwanseumbosal, or Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, which refers to the Bodhisattva of Great Compassion.  The Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva that was enshrined in Gwaneumjeon Hall, is believed to have the power of seeing and healing humans in the world of Sahbah with a thousand eyes and a thousand hands as if the Buddha appeared in reality. Thus, the Gwaneum belief has taken an important position in Mahayana Buddhism since ancient times.  Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva can transform into 33 forms, and often takes the form of the moon or water. This symbolizes the belief that the reflection of the moon on the water teaches us to rid ourselves of useless desires in order to be saved.  The reason why many temples in Korea have erected Gwaneumjeon Hall is that Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva not only saves people from all difficulties, but also embodies the true nature of compassion aiming to assist in the comfort and connections of sentient beings.  Inside Gwaneumjeon Hall, you can find a statue of Gwanseum with a lotus flower, ‘Yangnyu Gwaneum holding willow branches,’ and eleven looks of ‘Sipilmyeon Gwaneum,’ along with ‘Haesu Gwaneum,’ ‘Baeg-ui Gwaneum,’ ‘Yongdu Gwaneum,’ and ‘Cheonsu Gwaneum’.

stories.title: Weontongmun of Guryongsa
stories.script: Weontongmun of Guryongsa   “On the way to Guryongsa, one passes a trail called Gold Pine Tree Road. When walking down Golden Pine Tree Road, the first gate of Weontongmun comes into view high in the sky.”  “The Iljumn, or One Pillar Gate, which symbolizes one mind, is most often found at the entrance of a temple. It suggests the teaching that before entering a sacred temple, all the afflictions or defilements of the mundane world should be washed away and one should step into the world of wisdom with one mind.”  “However, the Iljumn of Guryongsa was constructed atypically on stone pillars so that it is called Weontongmun. This implies that, like a cylinder, it is the gate that effortlessly leads to the wise teaching of the compassionate Buddha.”   “The reason why the name Weontongmun was used in Guryongsa is because it advocates the Gwaneum Belief, additionally, Gwanseumbosal, or Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, who washes away the afflictions of sentient beings, is enshrined within the temple. Moreover, the name Weontong suggests that nothing is obstructive, while also referring to the awakening of wisdom.”  “Carved upon the pillars of Weontongmun of Guryongsa are the words, ‘Yeokcheongeob ibulgo, hangmanse ijanggeum.’ This declares that the message won’t fade even after a thousand eons, and in ten thousand years, the temple will remain as it is today.”  “As I stand here before Weontongmun, I feel as if I am absorbing the well-rounded wisdom of the Buddha, though without hearing any spoken message.”

stories.title: Sacheonwangmun of Guryongsa
stories.script: Sacheonwangmun of Guryongsa   “A second gate, Sacheonwangmun, or the Gate of the Four Heavenly Guardians, can be found beyond Weontongmun. At some temples, Guemgangmun, or the Diamond Deva Gate, can be found, but the Gate of the Four Heavenly Guardians most often satisfies this function.”  “It can therefore be said that Sacheonwangmun is the first line of defense protecting the temple. The Four Heavenly Guardians refer to the beings in charge of the four quarters of heaven.”  “The Four Heavenly Guardians protect Mt. Sumeru, the imaginary mountain which is the center of the universe in Buddhism, in all directions, and they watch over the sentient beings in the mundane world, regardless of whether they are living according to Buddha’s teaching, by leading them to the correct path.”   “At Sacheonwangmun, one can find King Dhrtarastra to the east, the fearful guardian in white with a sword in his hand; King Vaisravana to the north, the guardian in black with a lute in his hand; King Virudhaka to the south, the guardian in the form of a blue dragon; and King Virupaksa to the west, the guardian in red with a stupa in his hand. These are the guardians which protect the north, south, east and west in the Pure Land of Buddhism.”  “Unlike those found at other temples, the Sacheonwangmun found at Guryongsa is two stories high, and it is known as the biggest among Korean temples. Upon entering, the Four Heavenly Guardians appear, standing in a dignified manner. Mandala, or circular magic diagrams which serve to filter out any negativity, can be seen painted on the ceiling of the second floor .”

stories.title: Bogwangru of Guryongsa
stories.script: Bogwangru of Guryongsa   “This is Bogwangru Pavilion of Guryongsa! Out of the three gates to the temple, this pavilion functions as Bulimun or the Non-Duality Gate!”  “Bulimun …? Dad, What is Bulimun, the Non-Duality Gate?”  “Bulimun is the last gate into a temple. The word ‘Buli’ means that wisdom is not dual and there is no discrimination in Buddhism. It is designed so that one must pass through Bogwangru in order to enter Daeungjeon!”  “Dad, I think I can see all of Guryongsa from here!”   “As the lower part of Bogwangru Pavilion is open, the passage in the middle leads to the front of Daeungjeon. This kind of architecture is commonly seen in temples built on steep slopes. What do you think? Doesn’t it make you feel cool?”  “Yes, Dad! The second floor of the Pavilion is really spacious and cool!!”  “It is said that the biggest straw mat in Korea once lay here upon the floor! The pillars on the second floor are simple cylinders, but they were decorated with lotus flowers and phoenixes to make them appear quite exquisite. The front of second floor is also left wide open!”  “You know what? After coming up here to Bogwangru, I feel that it was a good idea to visit Guryongsa Temple! Hehehe…!”  “I agree! Hahaha…”

stories.title: Daeungjeon of Guryongsa
stories.script: Daeungjeon of Guryongsa   “After passing underneath Bogwangru Pavilion, one comes to a dharma hall in a large open space. This is Daeungjeon, or the Great Hero Hall of Guryongsa Temple.”  “Daeungjeon, with three columns in front and two on the sides, has been embellished with various designs, and an elaborate paljak-jibung, or half-hipped roof, has been placed on top, making the side of the roof triangular.”  “Upon the outer pillars of Daeungjeon the words, ‘Dalmahasa dapgangnae, dongtosanha chunchorok,’ are written, which explains that Bodhidharma walked past on the river! Perhaps, this is why the mountains and fields started to bud in green despite the ice still clinging to the land.”  “Sejoninha dosollae, nogwonwonjung baekwahyang,’ which asks why Shakyamuni Buddha has come to Dosolcheon, the Tushita Heaven! Perhaps, it was because the fragrance of flowers is in full bloom at the Deer Park in Varanasi!”    Enshrined with Shakyamuni Buddha of the present, Daeungjeon is the main dharma hall of the temple and is therefore the most important. It is said that the word ‘Daeung’ came from the Lotus Sutra, which referred to Shakyamuni Buddha as a great hero.”  “Shakyamuni, the main Buddha, sits in the middle, alongside Manjusri Bodhisattva, or the Bodhisattva of Great Wisdom, and Samantabhadra, or the Bodhisattva of Great Vow and Action. Try to listen to the compassion in your mind and the sound of enlightenment in the hall.”

stories.title: Guryongsa and Birobong Peak (Guryongsa Temple, Wonju)
stories.audioTitle: Guryongsa and Birobong Peak (Guryongsa Temple, Wonju)
stories.script: Guryongso, Birobong Peak  Guryongsa Temple is located here at Chiaksan Mountain, and the Guryongsa Valley is covered with deep, flat, and lush forests in a cool stream that overflows, creating a unique atmosphere throughout the four seasons with abundant supply and clear water.  The landscape extends from Guryongso to Guryongsa Temple is beautiful, and the valley that passes through Guryong Falls to Seryeom Falls leading up the valley is breathtaking.  Guryongso at the edge of Guryongsa valley has extremely clean water so it is difficult to tell how deep it is! The legend of the nine dragons related to this place is the reason why this it is called Guryongso, or Nine Dragon Lake!  After reaching Birobong Peak, 1,288 meters above sea level of Chiaksan Mountain, there’s Guryongsa Temple! The stone tower is rugged but also magnificent and majestic.   To reach Birobong Peak, we also came up Namdaebong, Hyangnobong Peaks, and Maehwasan Mountain. The view of the mountain changes according to the season, so it attracts many climbers and tourists to visit Birobong Peak throughout the year!  It is clear that the fame of Guryongsa Temple grew due to its location near Birobong Peak. Standing here on Birobong Peak, it seems as if the majestic sound of the dharma bell from Guryongsa temple has traveled all the way to the top of the peak!

stories.title: Introduction
stories.script: Introduction   “Located in Yeongwol-gun, Gangwon-do Province, Bubheungsa Temple was founded by Precept Master Jajang in 643, the 12th year of Queen Seondeok, the 27th ruler of the Silla Kingdom. He founded the temple to pray for the prosperity of the nation as well as for the well-being of people at Yeonhwabong Peak on Sajasa Mountain. At that time, the temple was called Heungnyeongsa, and it was known  for housing the enshrined relics of Sakyamuni Buddha!”  “Bubheungsa is one of five Jeokmyeol Bogung in the country. ‘Jeokmyeol Bogung’ refers to a temple enshrining the relics of Sakyamuni Buddha. When Precept Master Jajang met Manjusri Bodhisattva, he received the relics of Sakyamuni Buddha personally and brought these to be enshrined in what is now  Bubheungsa Temple.”  “As a result of this, Bubheungsa became a Jeokmyeol Bogung, where Buddha's genuine sariras are enshrined, joining Sangwonsa in Odaesan Mountain; Jeongamsa in Taebaeksan Mountain; Tongdosa in Yeongchuksan Mountain; and Bongjeongam in Seoraksan Mountain.”   “Bubheungsa’s original site—when it was known as Heungnyeongsa was burned in 891, but rebuilt in 944, only to be destroyed again by the same cause. Following its reconstruction, it managed to survive for a thousand years until it was again reconstructed in 1902 by Venerable Daewongak, and renamed Bubheungsa.”  “We can only speculate as to the overall scope of the original structure by looking at the remains of Heungnyeongsa: three stone pagodas; Precept Master Jajang’s togul or hermitage; Jeokmyeol Bogung; a sarira stupa; Great Master Jinghyo’s Bointapbi and his stupa.”

stories.title: The Origin of Bubheungsa
stories.script: The Origin of Bubheungsa   “Bubheungsa of Sajasan Mountain is known as a Jeokmyeol Bogung, as it enshrines the relics of Sakyamuni Buddha. It was Precept Master Jajang who delivered the relics which led to Bubheungsa becoming a Jeokmyeol Bogung!”  “I see! Then, how did Precept Master Jajang come to enshrine the relics of Sakyamuni Buddha at Bubheungsa?”  “According to the Samgukyusa, or Reminiscence of Three Kingdoms, Precept Master Jajang travelled to Mount Wutai in China in 636, the 5th year of Queen Seondeok, the 27th ruler of the Silla Kingdom, where he met Manjusri Bodhisattva…  “Oh, Manjusri Bodhisattva, the one with great wisdom. You mean that he actually met the bodhisattva?”  “Isn’t that the power of Buddha’s teaching? After offering a sincere prayer in front of the statue of Manjusri Bodhisattva on Mount Wutai in China, Precept Master Jajang was able to meet the Bodhisattva. The result of this was that in 643, he brought the relics of Sakyamuni Buddha, along with the buddha’s only robe, from the Tang Dynasty to the Silla Kingdom in the 12th year of Queen Seondeok!”   “I see, so that’s how the relics of Sakyamuni Buddha came to be enshrined at Bubheungsa!”  “That’s right! Though the temple was called Heungnyeongsa at that time!”   “Is it true that Great Master Jinghyo put a lot of effort into building Bubheungsa in addition to Precept Master Jajang?”  “Indeed! As the National Teacher during the Unified Silla period, Great Master Jinghyo, a monk appointed by the country, greatly assisted in reviving Bubheungsa Temple!”  “It seems like Bubheungsa is more than just Bubheungsa! It's an homage to Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva.”

stories.title: Woneumru of Bubheungsa
stories.script: Woneumru of Bubheungsa   “Woneumru Pavilion of Bubheungsa is a unique two-story structure, with the first floor forming Guemgangmun, or the Diamond Deva Gate. This pavilion functions as the second gate, while the four Buddhist instruments are housed within the temple.”  “These four Buddhist instruments are Beopgo, a dharma drum; Unpan, a cloud-shaped gong; Mokeo, a wooden fish-shaped gong; and Beomjong, a great bell. ‘Beopgo is an enormous drum that is used to sound for all animals of skin or leather... ”   “Unpan is a cloud-shaped gong made of brass that is used to sound for all birds and any spirits capable of flying in the air.”   “Mokeo is a wooden fish-shaped drum carved out of a log which is used to sound for all underwater beings.”    “Beomjong is a Dharma bell that is used to sound for saving all sentient beings by and large.”    “The reason that the four instruments are played during a ceremony is to wish that all sentient beings rid themselves of their suffering and awaken to everlasting wisdom.”  “The word ‘Woneum’ in Woneumru Pavilion refers to the consistent gentle words of the Buddha. Whenever his words of wisdom are heard, they are received with simplicity and logic.”  “Even today, the gentle well-rounded sound emerges from Woneumru Pavilion of Bubheungsa to awaken and console the minds of the people.”   “Beopgo, Unpan, Mokeo, and Beomjong create the beautiful sounds that help awaken wisdom, and the wish that all the world’s sentient beings can attain compassion, wisdom and enlightenment as well as a peaceful mind.”

stories.title: The Mandala Hall of Bubheungsa
stories.script: The Mandala Hall of Bubheungsa   “The Mandala Hall exhibits the circular magic diagrams which symbolize the wisdom of the universe. Mandala is a Buddhist painting made by applying color to fine sand.”   “The Mandala Hall at Bubheungsa is the only one of its kind in Korea. It features a mandala that was created for a dharma ceremony by Tibetan monks in 2003. It is placed on the sacred altar along with the Buddha and Bodhisattvas to express the wisdom of the universe.”   “The original meaning of mandala is ‘possessing innate nature,’ which signifies  the idea that enlightenment has been given tangible form. The essence of all virtue in the universe has been depicted in the Buddhist mandala painting.”   “On September 4, 2012, a significant dharma service took place in front of the Mandala Hall, “The Dharma Ceremony for Making Amitabh Mandala and Five Dhyani Buddhas Tanghwa.”  “Amitabh Mandala was created to wish for the successful hosting of the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics as well as to hope for world peace. Seven Tibetan monks were invited to help create Amitabha Mandala and it will be enshrined in the Mandala Hall until 2018.”  “The previous mandala enshrined in the Mandala Hall lasted past its sojourning ceremony and was then divided into 108 eight bottles and given to Buddhist devotees. The reason that it was put into 108 bottles was to wish for the peace of all sentient beings based on the mind of compassion and prayer.”

stories.title: Great Master Jinghyo’s Bointapbi of Bubheungsa
stories.audioTitle: Great Master Jinghyo’s Bointapbi of Bubheungsa
stories.script: Great Master Jinghyo’s Bointapbi of Bubheungsa   “Great Master Jinghyo’s Bointapbi is a stele, or tombstone, which records in detail the reason that King Hyogong, the 25th ruler of the Silla Kingdom, gave the posthumous names ‘Jinghyo’ and ‘Boin’ to he who had be known in life as Venerable Jeoljung.”   “Designated as Treasure No. 612, Great Master Jinghyo’s Bointapbi was founded in 944, the first year of Hyejong, the second ruler of the Goryeo Dynasty. The body of the stele was placed on a turtle-shaped foundation while the top was decorated with a dragon head design.”  “This is a typical stone monument from the Silla and Goryeo periods made of granite. As the overall structure is well-preserved, excepting minor damage on its body, it holds significant historical value.”   “Great Master Jinghyo, an appointed National Teacher during the Unified Silla period, was a disciple of Seon Master Cheolgam Doyoon, who had founded the leading Buddhist group ‘Sajasanmun’ in the late Silla period. As his student, Great Master Jinghyo played an important role in reviving the ancient temple of Heungnyeongsa.”   “His Bointapbi provides an overall record his work; how he learned from Dharma Teacher Jinjeon and was ordained as a monk, how he took the precepts at Janggoksa Temple when he was nineteen, and how he strove to spread Buddha’s teachings until his entrance into nirvana at age 75.”  “Standing before his Bointapbi, you may be able to feel Great Master Jinghyo’s passion for reviving Bubheungsa, and his will towards Buddha’s teachings.”

stories.title: Samseonggak of Bubheungsa
stories.script: Samseonggak of Bubheungsa   “Located in front of Geuknakjeon, or the Hall of Utmost Bliss, Samseonggak, the Three Sages Shrine, is a simple hall with three columns in front and two on the sides. Samseonggak houses the Buddhist paintings ‘The Spirit of the Big Dipper,’ ‘The Solitary Sage,’ and ‘The Dragon King’.”  “The seven stars which make up the Big Dipper have been regarded as the god of the sky since ancient times, and this belief was adapted by Buddhism. The seven stars were known to govern natural disasters, misfortunes and disease as well as for being influential over births.”  “The Solitary Sage refers to the Pretyeka-buddha, who attained enlightenment all by himself. Even after Buddha entered nirvana, the Pratyeka-buddha is known to lead sentient beings.”   “The Dragon King of Water has always been with the people of Korea as the country is surrounded by water on three sides. The Dragon King is the object of the wishes and wills of all those who depend on fishing for living. This illustrates the tendency for Korean Buddhism to adapt itself to the land by embracing local beliefs.”  “The Samseong, or three sages’ beliefs, expressed in Samseonggak of Bubheungsa, divide all the ways of the world into three fields from a Buddhist perspective. This has implications for how closely our daily lives are related with Buddhism.”

stories.title: Jeokmyeol Bogung of Bubheungsa
stories.script: Jeokmyeol Bogung of Bubheungsa   “Among the Buddhist temples in Korea are five temples which do not enshrine any statues. In the dharma hall of these temples, there is an altar, but only a sarira stupa is kept. This type of dharma hall is known as a ‘Jeokmyeol Bogung, or Hall of Sublime Equanimity,’ and within these temples are enshrined the relics of Sakyamuni Buddha.”   “The relics of Sakyamuni Buddha represent Buddha himself, so temples like Bubheungsa, which enshrine his holy sarira, do not need to have any statues in their halls. A temple which enshrines part of his relics contains a hall called a Bogung, or jeweled palace.”   “There are five Jeokmyeol Bogung temples in Korea. In addition to Bubheungsa on Sajasa Mountain, there are Tongdosa on Yeongchuksan; Sangwonsa on Odaesan; Jeongamsa on Taebaeksan; and Bongjeongam on Seoraksan Mountain.”   “Precept Master Jajang met Manjusri Bodhisattva in person, which caused him to found a temple and lead the spreading of dharma. In 643, the 12th year of Queen Seondeok, the 27th ruler of the Silla Kingdom, he founded Heungnyeongsa with the relics of Sakyamuni Buddha, and this temple went on to become Jeokmyeol Bogung Bubheungsa as we know it today.”

stories.title: Buddhist Monk Jajang’s Togul (Beopheungsa Temple, Yeongwol)
stories.audioTitle: Buddhist Monk Jajang’s Togul (Beopheungsa Temple, Yeongwol)
stories.script: Buddhist Monk Jajang’s Togul of Beopheungsa Temple  Designated Tangible Property of Gangwon-do Province, Buddhist Monk Jajang’s Togul of Beopheungsa Temple is the cave which he used for ascetic practice. The interior of Togul is just big enough for a person to sit, and it is said that Buddhist Monk Jajang used to cover the area with thorn bushes when practicing.  The ‘togul’ cave utilizes the low slope of the hill behind it, covering the cave with its soil. This represents the original form of caves used by ancient monks for their practices, making it of great value.  In 638, the 5th year of Queen Seondeok of the Silla Kingdom, Buddhist Monk Jajang visited the Tang Dynasty. He first went to Cheongnyangsan Mountain where the statue of Manjusri Bodhisattva was located. As he was deep in prayer in front of the statue one day, the bodhisattva patted him gently and presented him with a hwadu, or critical phrase.  Jajang pondered it carefully yet couldn’t understand its meaning. Then, an old monk appeared and told him the following:  “One may learn ten thousand things, but there is nothing like this!”  It is said that the old monk gave him some relics and his robe, and then vanished. The relics that he received were the reliquary of Sakyamuni Buddha, and they have been enshrined in Jeongmyeolbogung Hall of Beopheungsa Temple ever since!  Sajasan Mountain, where the legendary lion ridden by Manjusri Bodhisattva is known to stay. The relics of Sakyamuni Buddha are enshrined in the temple, but the clear and fragrant sound of awakening still resonates through Beopheungsa Temple in Sajasan Mountain.

stories.title: Iljumun, the One Pillar Gate, of Gwaneumsa
stories.audioTitle: Iljumun, the One Pillar Gate, of Gwaneumsa
stories.script: Iljumun, the One Pillar Gate, of Gwaneumsa   [Curator]  The path that leads to Gwaneumsa is lined with stone walls, creating a striking and distinctive scene that changes with the weather – foggy, rainy, windy, or sunny. The path from “Iljumun,” the One Pillar Gate, to “Cheonwangmun,” the Gate of the Four Heavenly Guardians, is lined on both sides with 108 stone Buddha statues, symbolizing the 108 afflictions of Maitreya Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva of Future Buddha. It is a curious and mystical sight, all these Buddha statues standing silently along the basalt stone walls, with their different mudras.  These 108 stone statues came into place through the efforts of many individual devotees of Gwaneumsa. As you can see, in this temple, their dedications and work for Buddhism fill this place to overflowing.  [Visitor]  I feel very humble before so many Buddhas.

stories.title: Sacheonwangmun, the Gate of the Four Heavenly Guardians, of Gwaneumsa
stories.audioTitle: Sacheonwangmun, the Gate of the Four Heavenly Guardians, of Gwaneumsa
stories.script: Sacheonwangmun, the Gate of the Four Heavenly Guardians, of Gwaneumsa  [Curator]  After passing through “Iljumun,” the One Pillar Gate, “Sacheonwangmun,” the Gate of the Four Heavenly Guardians comes into the view. This is a place where, once you attain enlightenment and Buddhahood, even the heavenly beings that manage all four directions – the east, the west, the north and the south - in heaven will honor you and learn Buddha-dharma from you. In 1948, this gate was burnt down during the April 3rd Massacre in Jeju, where many locals were killed in a time of violent political instability. It was finally rebuilt in 1973.   The four heavenly guardians are always nearby the Buddha, protecting him. So, anyone who’d like to pay homage to him must pass through the gate first. That’s why the gate was built there.   King Dhrtarastra of the east, in blue, holds a sword in his left hand, and either makes a fist or holds a gem with his right. King Virudhaka of the south, in red, has a dragon in his right hand and a Mani gem in his left one. King Virupaksa of the west, in white, has a trident and a stupa. At last, King Vaisravana of the north, in black, has a lute.   [Visitor]  It makes me feel a little bit solemn. On the other hand, I also want to try those poses.   [Curator]  Many people are scared of their facial expressions, but you may not be when you consider why they are there. The guardians just want you to put down all your worldly desires and worries before going into the temple.

stories.title: Haewoldang Venerable Bongnyeogwan’s Monument of Gwaneumsa and Haewolgul Cave
stories.audioTitle: Haewoldang Venerable Bongnyeogwan’s Monument of Gwaneumsa and Haewolgul Cave
stories.script: Haewoldang Venerable Bongnyeogwan’s Monument of Gwaneumsa and Haewolgul Cave  [Visitor]   Is this the venerable Bongnyeogwan? What did the venerable actually do?   [Curator]  During the reign of the 19th King Sukjong of the Joseon Dynasty, about 500 buildings of the temple were closed down, along with many shrines, because they were told that there were too many evil spirits in Jeju. Then, it was Bhikkuni Bongnyeogwan who rebuilt the temple in 1908. During the Japanese Occupation period, some funds were also gathered here to support the resistance movement in the fight against Japanese. Haewolgul Cave was the place where Bhikkuni Bongnyeogwan stayed, hoping to be awakened, for three years.   [Visitor]  Now that I am looking at it closely, I can picture her exerting every effort towards her practice.     [Curator]  This place is sought by many devotees wishing to pray, regardless of bad weather or limited space. Here, only a couple of adults can fit, and they need to stoop down to stay inside.

stories.title: Jijangjeon Hall (Gwaneumsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.script: Jijangjeon, the Judgment Hall, of Gwaneumsa Temple  “Jijang Bosal,” the Bodhisattva of Hell, vowed to save all beings suffering in hell. So, he personally entered hell to teach these sinners how to save themselves. The Jijangjeon Hall of Gwaneumsa Temple was rebuilt in 1971 after being burned down during the April 3 Jeju Uprising. Bongnyeonggak Hall was created to hold memorial tablets for these deceased spirits of the tragedy and help them attain rebirth in the Pure Land by holding memorial services. It was also a place to praise the virtuous devotees of Gwaneumsa Temple.

stories.title: Daeungjeon, the Main Buddha Hall, of Gwaneumsa, and Wooden Seated Gwaneum Bodhisattva
stories.audioTitle: Daeungjeon, the Main Buddha Hall, of Gwaneumsa, and Wooden Seated Gwaneum Bodhisattva
stories.script: Daeungjeon, the Main Buddha Hall, of Gwaneumsa, and Wooden Seated Gwaneum Bodhisattva    [Curator]  Here, you can see the Sakyamuni Buddha in the center, and “Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,” the Bodhisattva of the Great Vow and Action, and “Manjusri Bodhisattva.” the Bodhisattva of Great Wisdom, have been placed here as his attendants in the Main Buddha Hall, as the center of the temple. Also, sculptors of the late 17th century produced a seated wooden statue of Gwaneum Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva of Great Compassion, which is also enshrined here.  It was designated Tangible Asset No. 16 by the Jeju-do government.   [Visitor]  How is this wooden seated Bodhisattva of Great Compassion special?   [Curator]  From the reliquaries in the statue, we found that it was created in 1698 and relocated after the temple was reconstructed by Venerable Bongnyeogwan in 1925. In addition, it has the distinctive features of Buddha statues produced in the late 17th century. Its graceful appearance, natural embossing, and refined lines all made it easily recognizable as one of the Buddha statues from that period, and so it was designated as a cultural asset.

stories.title: Beomjonggak, the Bell Pavilion (Gwaneumsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.audioTitle: Beomjonggak, the Bell Pavilion (Gwaneumsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.script: Beomjonggak, the Bell Pavilion, of Gwaneumsa Temple  As you enter the bell pavilion, every item here looks different from each other.  This building houses the four Buddhist musical instruments: the 'beomjong (dharma bell)' is made of bronze, the 'beopgo (drum)' made of cow skin, the cloud-shaped 'unpan (gong)', and fish-shaped 'mogeo (wooden drum)'. The meanings behind these are: the 'beomjong (dharma bell)' is to save sentient beings suffering in hell; the 'beopgo (drum)' is to save land animals; the 'unpan (gong)' is to save wandering spirits; and the 'mogeo (wooden drum)' is to save sea animals. The original building was burnt down in 1948 during the April 3 Jeju Uprising. This one was then reconstructed as a two-story pavilion in 1979.  If you want to experience a different charm of Jeju, come to Beomjonggak and immerse in such dignified atmosphere!

stories.title: Bangsatap Stone Tower of Gwaneumsa
stories.script: Bangsatap Stone Tower of Gwaneumsa  [Visitor]  I see a charming stone tower over there. Why is it placed here?   [Curator]  This is called Bangsatap Stone Tower. In Jeju, there has been a tradition of making stone towers for the well-being of one’s clan and village for generations. A tradition of placing a bird-shaped or human-shaped stone on top of the tower has been passed down over the years. Since this is a temple ground, a round stone was placed on top to represent the dharma wheel.   [Visitor]  So this is an example of the Buddhist culture and the local culture meeting harmoniously?   [Curator]  Yes, Bangsatop Stone Tower is an excellent example of how Buddhism was able to become integrated into the folk beliefs of Jeju. It was created for people who wish to get rid of their misfortune and attain good fortune, so it is very popular among those who are seeking to have their wished or prayers fulfilled.

stories.title: Samseonggak, the Three Sages Shrine, of Gwaneumsa
stories.audioTitle: Samseonggak, the Three Sages Shrine, of Gwaneumsa
stories.script: Samseonggak, the Three Sages Shrine, of Gwaneumsa  [Curator]  In Samseonggak, the three sages: the Mountain Spirit, the Spirit of the Big Dipper, and the Solitary Sage are enshrined. Samseong Belief came about from a local belief based on the three sages. This belief was absorbed into Buddhism in the localization process in Korea. In the Three Sages Shrine, a painting of the Dragon King under the sea is also enshrined. Because of its location, the island, the painting is extremely well-received by the people in Jeju Island.   [Visitor]  So this unique part of the culture is derived from its location.

stories.title: Great Maitreya Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva of Future Buddha, of Gwaneumsa
stories.audioTitle: Great Maitreya Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva of Future Buddha, of Gwaneumsa
stories.script: Great Maitreya Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva of Future Buddha, of Gwaneumsa  [Visitor]  What is that tall, shiny Buddha statue, covered in gold?    [Curator]  Maitreya Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva of Future Buddha, is to appear in the Pure Land of the Buddha 567 billion years after the Buddha has entered nirvana, and will save all sentient beings. In order to be born in his world, one must practice good deeds and attain wisdom. The Bodhisattva of Future Buddha was created with volcanic rocks for two reasons. First, he has been very popular among the people of Jeju, and second, these rocks are very common in Jeju, being part of a dormant volcano. The Great Bodhisattva of Future Buddha is here to wish for the prosperity and comfort of the people of Jeju and to pray for the Pure Land of the Buddha. It is one of the attractions you really must see on the island.

stories.title: Nahanjeon, the Hall of Disciples and Arhats, of Gwaneumsa
stories.audioTitle: Nahanjeon, the Hall of Disciples and Arhats, of Gwaneumsa
stories.script: Nahanjeon, the Hall of Disciples and Arhats, of Gwaneumsa  [Curator]   Do you see the statues of arhats behind the Great Bodhisattva of Future Buddha? These arhats are the disciples of the Sakyamuni Buddha. They took his teaching to heart, but decided to stay in this world. Even though they weren’t able to attain Buddhahood, they are saints who have already attained enlightenment. These saints, with supernatural powers, take on very distinctive and free-spirited appearances. The sixteen arhats in the hall resemble carefree, yet dignified and disciples of Mount Halla.   [Visitor]  How interesting! The arhats really look like Mount Halla, full of dignity.

stories.title: Beopgo, the Dharma Drum, of Yakchunsa
stories.audioTitle: Beopgo, the Dharma Drum, of Yakchunsa
stories.script: Beopgo, the Dharma Drum, of Yakchunsa  [Curator]  The dharma drum is about 2.4 meters in diameter, and its height is about the same as the Bell Pavilion. The temple is located in a naturally beautiful place, with both Mount Halla and the ocean clearly visible. Especially on a night with a full moon, you will be able to see the dream-like view of Yakchunsa, with the mountain and the ocean resting together in harmony under the moonlight. Because of such lovely scenery, it has been known to give inspiration to many literature lovers and composers.   [Visitor]   When can I hear the sound of the dharma bell? Can we hear them during the day, when there are many visitors?   [Curator]   The dharma bell is struck three times a day for the daily ceremonies: once early in the morning, once at sasi-before noon, and once in the evening. On special occasions, the dharma drum is also played. If you participate in one of the templestay programs, you can hear the bell.   [Visitor]  Oh, that is too bad

stories.title: Jonggak, the Bell Pavilion, of Yakchunsa
stories.audioTitle: Jonggak, the Bell Pavilion, of Yakchunsa
stories.script: Jonggak, the Bell Pavilion, of Yakchunsa  [Curator]  Jonggak, the Bell Pavilion, is located in the front yard of Daejeokgwangjeon, the Supreme Buddha Hall. It is placed on top of garden-level living quarters like a watch tower. The dharma bell weighs about 18 tons and was cast according to the features of the bell used during the Silla Dynasty period.

stories.title: Daejeokgwangjeon Hall (Yakcheonsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.script: Daejeokgwangjeon, the Supreme Buddha Hall, of Yakcheonsa Temple  Daejeokgwangjeon, the Supreme Buddha Hall, is located by the seaside, next to Seogwipo-si City. Its structure is basically taken from the Gakhwangjeon Hall of Hwaeomsa Temple and added some majestic elements. In particular, it applied the elements from the three-story structure of Mireukjeon Hall of Geumsansa Temple in Gimje of Jeollabuk-do Province. The building contains the wish that the people in Jeju Island live well even though they are in a barren environment surrounded by the ocean all around.  As you step into the temple, you may have noticed its significant size.   The name of this hall is technically Daejeokgwangjeon, the Supreme Buddha Hall because Vairochana Buddha, the Dharma-body of the Sakyamuni Buddha is enshrined as the main statue. This hall is 29 meters tall and is made of the lumber from Baekdusan Mountain, the highest mountain on the Korean Peninsula, best known for its mystical power. The statue itself is about 9 meters tall, including the pedestal, making him the largest wooden Buddha statue in Korea. The painting behind him included 53 small Buddha statues aims to adorn and illuminate the statue. They represent the 53 Zen knowledges encountered by the Zen disciple in the Avatamsaka Sutra during the quest in obtaining the Buddhist scriptures.   Apart from using material from Baekdusan Mountain, this hall has another highlight that is different from other temples.  Inside of the large Buddha Hall, there is an inner passage to another Buddha Hall on the second floor, where 80,000 gilt-bronze Buddha statues are enshrined. Upon seeing it, we can truly understand the scale of the participation of Yakcheonsa Temple’s ardent devotees towards completing this temple. On the third floor, there is a Rotating Sutra Case called “Yunjangdae”, which is stacked with Buddhist scriptures. It is said that if you turn this wheel once, it is equivalent to reading the scriptures once. Also, the pedestal is too high to be seen from the first floor because it is 25 meters from the floor to the ceiling. To get a proper view of the dharma hall, you need to walk up the stairs to the second or third floor. From there, you can clearly see the majestic view of the whole dharma hall, which is as high as an eight-story building!

stories.title: Amitabha Buddha, the Buddha of Infinite Light (Yakcheonsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.audioTitle: Amitabha Buddha, the Buddha of Infinite Light (Yakcheonsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.script: Amitabha Buddha, the Buddha of Infinite Light, of Yakcheonsa Temple  There are numerous Buddha statues enshrined in Yakcheonsa Temple. Let’s take a look at some of statues here.  The one on the right is Amitabha Buddha, the Buddha of Infinite Light. There is a special reason why the statue is enshrined here. The name 'Seogwipo' is derived from the aspiration of Buddhists to return to the Western Pure Land. Therefore, enshrining Amitabha Buddha in Yakcheonsa Temple in Seogwipo carries the wish for the swift fulfillment of Buddhists' vows. The Buddhas on both left and right are made of bronze. The four pillars inside illustrated the idea that the blue and yellow dragons offering the precious Cintamani that are more valuable than their lives to the Buddha. This also indicates a countless number of Buddhists from Korea as well as abroad who have participated in the completion of the temple. The wooden carving painting behind the Buddha is another unique feature of Yakcheonsa Temple.  The one on the left is “Bhaisajyaraja Buddha,” the Medicine Buddha that is closely connected with the name of the temple – the syllable ‘yak’ means medicine and the syllable ‘cheon’ is water. For a long time, this place has been known for its mineral water fountain with medicinal effect, many people decided to try it by themselves and come to believe in its healing powers. The Medicine Buddha was enshrined in the hope that his dignity and spiritual power can ease the suffering and cure the sicknesses of sentient beings.  While you are looking around the temple, why not take this opportunity to send a sincere prayer and see if the Medicine Buddha here in Yakcheonsa Temple indeed blesses you with good health!

stories.title: Datjip, the Canopy (Yakcheonsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.script: Datjip, the Canopy of Yakcheonsa Temple  As you may notice, there is a canopy-like roof over the seated Buddhas.  Actually, that is called a datjip. Datjip is a house-shaped structure built over the seated Buddha, distinguishing Korean Buddha halls from those in Japan by aiming to give the Buddhas a more dignified look. This was also constructed to signify the continuation following the architectural tradition of Korean Buddhism.

stories.title: Obaek Nahanjeon Hall (Yeongsanjeon Hall) (Yakcheonsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.audioTitle: Obaek Nahanjeon Hall (Yeongsanjeon Hall) (Yakcheonsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.script: Obaek Nahanjeon, Hall of Yakcheonsa Temple  Within walking distance around Daejeokgwangjeon Hall, there is another hall showcasing the five hundred arhats.   This hall is Obaek Nahanjeon, also called Yeongsanjeon, the Hall of Disciples or Arhats, and it enshrines five hundred arhats. Obaek Nahanjeon is the first place to be illuminated by the morning sunlight, as it is located on the second floor. Nahan is the abbreviation of the longer term that means Arhats, referring to saints who sever all afflictions and reach enlightenment. Therefore, they are worthy of offerings from the people in the world. Arhats are clothed in Buddhist robes made of natural-looking cloth. Each arhat has his own individual posture and facial expressions. They are also painted in different colors adding even more individualistic splendor. You may find it quite interesting to explore each one’s distinctive features as well as to look for an arhat who resembles you. You won't even notice how time flies.

stories.title: Gulbeopdang, the Dharma Hall in a Cave (Yakcheonsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.audioTitle: Gulbeopdang, the Dharma Hall in a Cave (Yakcheonsa Temple, Jeju)
stories.script: Gulbeopdang, the Dharma Hall in a Cave, of Yakcheonsa Temple  Moving on to Gulbeopdang, the dharma hall in a cave. The cave is commonly found in Jeju Island, and it is in the highest point of Yakcheonsa Temple. The Bhaisajyaguru Buddha here is enshrined at the center; Avalokitesvara, the Bodhisattva of Great Compassion in White Robe, on the left; and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva of Hell, on the right. On the right altar, Budong Myeongwang, and the Alia of the Destroyer, is enshrined, in the hope that he will protect all from misfortunes at Yakcheonsa Temple.  Gulbeopdang is an ideal place to take a short break. The sense of solace has also attracted many patrons to pray in this temple.

stories.title: Chuam Beach
stories.script: Chotdae Rock standing above the sea  Chuam Beach is a place crowded on the first day of the new year with people who come to see the sunrise. The word Chuam originated from unique-shaped rocks in a place once known as Yongchu, which means a swamp where a dragon lives.  Chotdae Rock, which is the symbol of this place, was named after how the rising sun seen at the tip of the rock resembles a candle that is lit. There is a painting of Kim Hong-do, a famous painter during King Jeongjo's reign of the Joseon Dynasty, near Chotdae Rock. Originally, Chotdae Rock consisted of two rocks standing side by side like a pair of chopsticks, but an earthquake in Gangwon-do region during the reign of King Sukjong caused a tsunami that ended up crushing one of the rocks, leaving just one rock. A legend has it that if you pray earnestly at Chuam Chotdae Rock, the rock will appear in the dream to make it come true, so if you have something in your mind that you really want to accomplish, consider visiting Chuam in Donghae.  Chuam Beach is shallow, which makes it a great place for family trips. It is the place where you can see an emerald-colored clear sea on a sunny day and rough waves crashing into the rocks on a windy day. Among many different rocks in the undulating seawater to the right of Chotdae Rock, you will find one that resembles a rabbit. An unknown tree, which seems as if it hadn't grown well due to sea wind, looks like the shape of a rabbit ear, making the rock look like a rabbit pricking up both of its ears and sitting down to nibble on a carrot. This rock and the one behind it are together called Hyeongje Rock. If you go around Chotdae Rock and walk down along the northern trail, you will find Geobuk Rock which looks like a good-looking turtle resting with its long neck protruded out on its way up a hill at the mid-slope of the mountain on your left.  Near the area, there is also a pavilion called Haeamjeong, which is known to have been constructed by Sim Dong-ro, the founder of the Samcheok Sim clan, for local residents in the late Goryeo period. It is a quiet and secluded pavilion where you can also check out a plaque made by Song Si-yeol, a famous scholar from Joseon Dynasty. Stop by this pavilion and hear the sound of waves from Chuam that sound like a bell before taking a stroll around a neighborhood park that also has a trail. This is Chuam Beach, a beach where anyone who visits once will be sure to visit again.

stories.title: Bukpyeong Fifth-Day Market
stories.script: Three times the generosity, eight times the happiness  Bukpyeong Market is the country's largest traditional fifth-day market full of joys and sorrows of the ordinary people which brings up the nostalgia of the good old days. Consisted of around 500 stores over a 13,223m2 land in Bukpyeong-dong, Donghae, Bukpyeong Fifth-Day Market is also called by its pure Korean words Dwittteureujang. It has a long history of over 200 years that started in the 20th year of King Jeongjo's reign in 1796.  It is held on days that end in 3 or 8 every month, which is why locals also like to call it the 38 Department Store. It is a humane, love-filled place full of discounts and giveaways. It is crowed with people shopping shoulder to shoulder with one another on a seemingly endless alley of shops.  Two of the most famous foods of the marketplace, someori gukbap (beef head meat and rice soup) and seonjiguk (ox blood soup), still use traditional cast-iron pots to cook slowly and thoroughly to keep the original tastes. There is also Gukbap Street which presents the nostalgic flavors to those who visit the marketplace. In addition, you can find ppeongtwigi (puffed rice) stores, oil shops and Bukpyeong Catholic Church near the performing stage that still preserve the modern architectural styles intact, and the traditional jumak (tavern) village, which has replicated the taverns from the old days, offers delicious makgeolli (unrefined rice wine) and pajeon (green onion pancake). The market has an abundance of things to see including old photographs that show the vibes and history of Bukpyeong Market from the 1970s.  The most energetic area of Bukpyeong Market, which seems as if everything that should be in a marketplace is there indeed, is the fish shops. They sell fresh fish including squids and plaice caught in the nearby East Sea as well as frozen and dried marine products. On Saturdays that also happen to be when the market is open, various traditional performances and events take place in the outdoor performing stage.  Bukpyeong Fifth-Day Market, one of the nation's three most famous traditional marketplaces that still maintains its long history and continues to evolve even today.

stories.title: Mureung Valley
stories.script: A paradise where Taoist hermits used to stay  Mureung Valley is one of Donghae's famous scenic spots and representative tourist attractions that stretches for about 4km from Hoamso Spring to Yongchu Falls with Dutasan and Cheongoksan Mountains of Donghae as its backdrop.  Some say the valley was named by Kim Hyo-won, a magistrate of Samcheok during the reign of King Seonjo of the Joseon Dynasty, when he visited Dutasan Mountain with local scholars in 1577 and instantly fell in love with the landscape here, thinking that it is comparable to that of Mureung Dowon, a mythical paradise.  Among the scenic highlights are Banseok Rock, Yongchu Falls and Ssang Falls. Let me first begin with Banseok Rock in Mureung Valley. Consisting of a single, 5,000m2-wide white rock, it makes one feel the magnificence of nature. The enormous rock forms quite a spectacle together with the surrounding rocks of unique, strange shapes and forms. If you take a closer look at the rock, you will see countless different styles of calligraphies. These are the traces of Joseon scholars who had stopped by here. They tell us how these scholars didn't want to leave this paradise and showed that their hearts remain here even though their bodies must leave.  Yongchu Falls is a triple waterfall on the cliff below Sinseonbong Peak. It is not only the no. 1 destination in Mureung Valley for many visitors since the old days but also the first scenic beauty of Donghae among many of the gorgeous natural sceneries the city has to offer. Resembling a dragon seemingly wriggling around before ascending to heaven, Yongchu Falls is considered as the most well-organized and stylish waterfalls in the country.  Ssang Falls is regarded as one of the three attractions of Mureung Valley in addition to Banseok Rock and Yongchu Falls. It is unique in that two streams of water falling from a 20-meter height are from two different sources of water. If you get a chance to see Ssang Falls after a rain, you will be amazed by the energetically and continuously gushing water that deafens everything around it. Though Yongchu Falls is the most famous waterfall in the valley, Ssang Falls features a different kind of charm from Yongchu Falls. It is said that when the Korean variety show “2 Days & 1 Night” filmed an episode here, Lee Seung-gi instantly fell in love with the gorgeous scenery.  Of course, there are many other things to see in Mureung Valley. If you wish to listen to more details, please stop by Mureung Valley Management Office to hear what culture and tourism guide can tell you.

stories.title: Mureung Health Forest
stories.script: As you often hear the terms like well-being, healing and 100-year life, it has become increasingly important to live with healthy minds and bodies. Near Mureung Valley, there is a healing forest that opened in January 2016 in line with this trend. Located past Cheongokgyo Bridge to the left of the Mureung Valley parking ticket office, Mureung Health Forest is equipped with perfect facilities for seminars, retreats and club activities, offering programs such as environmental disease prevention training and management. Children's Health Experience Center provides these training and experience sessions while the health counseling room where you can receive medical diagnoses from nurses offer five kinds of basic medical checkups for free.  Additional facilities include children's playroom, healthy nature restaurant and experience program room where visitors can participate in making experiences using different natural objects each day of the week. There are also accommodations for 2, 6 and 8 people named Mureung, Yongchu, Duta and Cheongok that use the names around the area. Moreover, a sauna and oxygen healing room made of eco-friendly materials such as salt, sericite and red clay enable visitors to enjoy the paradise nearby in a relaxing manner and relieve their travel fatigue.

stories.title: Cheongok Cave
stories.script: The nation's one and only natural cave in the city's heart  In the city of Donghae that features limestone topography, a small hole was found in the downtown area in 1991. This hole is later discovered to be a horizontal cave that extends up to 1,400meter in length, which was created about 400 to 500 million years ago. The cave was eventually named Cheongok Cave after the name of the area where it was discovered.  Cheongok Cave features the country's largest ceiling channels, curtain-style stalactites, and stalactite waterfall, which are found in limestone caves, and an array of unique-shaped stones as well as 20 kinds of speleothem such as stalactites, stalagmites and stone columns, thus serving as the perfect field trip location for children to learn about nature and earth science while wearing helmets to explore the cave.  Known to be the most critically endangered species, Korean Orange Whiskered Bats were discovered in this natural cave. They are commonly known as golden bats since they shine in the color of orange under the flashlight. They are cute mascots of the cave but are not seen very often. If you see a golden bat that flies inside the cave in late winter or early spring, it will be your lucky day.  Cheongok Cave, the temple of dreams built by small limestone drops over an endlessly long period of time, can be toured in about 40 minutes. After looking through the cave and going upstairs, you can also check out the cave library and a fossil exhibition hall. On a nearby trail, you can enjoy a park that has over 100 different species of wild flowers and doline, or karst, that holds the secrets of the cave's creation, at the top of the trail.   If you walk a bit more along the trail on the hill behind the cave, you will be able to check out the East Sea in a single view. There is also a rest area from which you can see Mukho Lighthouse in the distance, which makes it a good place for family picnics or strolls.

stories.title: Mukhohang Port
stories.script: Mukho is a dynamic port.  Mukhohang Port began its construction in 1931 and officially opened in 1941. Combined with two words Muk, which means an ink, and Ho, which means a lake Mukho means a place where it is good to write, but an old story has it that the water near the port looked like ink because of coal briquette powder. A small harbor that once transported anthracite became an international trading port in 1964 before ultimately evolving into a national port that transports anthracite and cement. In the 1970s, it became the country's no. 1 base of fisheries and reached its heyday. Over 700 to 800 ships came in and out of the port while carrying coal, cement or squids, and the port brought prosperity to Mukho.  As the coal mining and fishing industries fell into a slump, Mukhohang Port once again transformed into a tourist port. There is Suhyup Seafood Processing Center that features not only a live fish center, which offers visitors to Mukho natural live fish and fresh fish caught in the sea near Mukho as well as dried seafood, but also an observation deck from which the entire port can be seen in a single view. In addition, the waterside park hosts various performances and festivals and offers rest while Mukho Ferry Terminal nearby sells tickets for access to Ulleungdo and Dokdo Islands.  At Mukhohang Port where you can look forward to another transformation in the near future, enjoy a delicious meal with fresh seafood.

stories.title: Mukho Lighthouse
stories.script: The light of hope that shines Mukho  Mukho Lighthouse was built in 1963 to replace Kkamakbawi Rock, which had served as a milepost for fishermen to return home safely. This lighthouse whose light can be identified even from 42km away not only acts as a safety keeper but also makes Mukho a famous nightscape spot.  Mukho has been a filming location for countless TV series and movies including Love Me Once Again. The red suspension bridge that appeared in the TV series, Brilliant Legacy, is known as a famous place where love comes true. As you walk down from the lighthouse along the suspension bridge, you will see a statue of an octopus, which protects Kkamakbawi Rock and Mukho, and also find an alley of raw fish restaurants nearby.  At the lighthouse observatory that has been remodeled into a maritime cultural space, enjoy the beauty of sunrise and sunset over the vast sea to get away from the hectic daily lives and relax.

stories.title: Nongoldam-gil Street
stories.script: Painting the lives of Mukho people  It is said that foreign sailors were surprised twice upon their arrival in Mukho. On the night they came to the port, they were surprised by the small lights on the ridges seen from Mukhohang Port that looked like high-rise buildings, and the next morning, they were shocked by the fact that those lights are actually from small, tightly crowded houses sitting shoulder to shoulder like barnacles.  Such a scenery tells us how tough and relentless years that Mukho has had to endure. In the days when fish-luring lights had to be turned on all night long and when the lights at drying fields were brighter than the moonlight and starlight in the night sky, Nongoldam-gil and Mukho were restless places. Mukho's waters in the 1960s and 1970s were depicted as “splendid as flower fields of June by the lights of squid-catching boats every night.” People breathlessly walked up and down the steep Nongol-gil while carrying a bowlful of squids, and ran around from one rock to another on Geguseok-gil with a bucket and a bamboo stick hanging a saury at its end just to catch crabs that come ashore on waves and immediately hide in between rocks. At the end of an uphill along Sanjegol, a drying field dried squids in summer and pollacks in winter.  From dawn to late night, women gathered in the drying field, cut open the pollacks and cleaned the squids while talking about their families from the day before, complaining or joking all they want before starting a new day. Nongoldam-gil is a village that still holds the life stories of Mukho residents. Mukho's mothers have become grandmothers and lean on a street bench to catch a breath. The restless and breathless days are long gone and, today, it turned into a place where people can relax and take a break from their busy lives.  Deungdaeoreum-gil, Nongol 1-, 2- and 3-gil all head towards the lighthouse and each route takes about 20 minutes. Travel through time to the past, present and future of Mukho Nongol Village, which is becoming more and more popular as a rising tourist spot of Donghae.

stories.title: Mangsang Beach
stories.script: Marine recreation area for four seasons  Considered as one of the most famous beaches in Donghae, the seemingly endless 5km-long Mangsang Beach has a sandy beach and clear yet shallow water with a thickly wooded pine forest in its backdrop. Most people probably have an experience of traveling on a train and visiting the beach to enjoy the sea with friends. It is indeed a place of youth in people's memories as well as a nationally popular attraction crowded with people every summer. People say that when you visit Gangwon-do Province, you have to stop by Mangsang Beach to be able to fully appreciate the beauty of the eastern coast.  You might wonder: where does the name Mangsang come from? There used to be a soldiers' training ground here, a border region between Silla and Goguryeo, which was known as Masangpyeong, meaning a vast field viewed from on top of a horse. Some say Mangsang stemmed from Masangpyeong while others say that it originated from a scholar who looks at Masang, meaning horseback martial arts. This scholar is none other than Songgang Jeong Cheol, famously known for writing Gwandong Byeolgok. Jeong fell in love with a woman he randomly met here but had to let her go as her heart was already with someone else. He composed a poem from this experience and named it Mangsang.  Make beautiful memories with your family, friends and the loved ones at the endless and beautiful Mangsang Beach.

stories.title: Mangsang Auto Camping Resort
stories.script: A nature-friendly campground in harmony with nature  Home of 2002 International Camping & Caravaning Rally, Mangsang Auto Camping Resort near Mangsang Beach was chosen as a top 100 tourist attractions that Koreans must visit. The resort is what makes Mangsang a year-round attraction. Established as the nation's first-ever camping resort for cars, it is such a popular campground famous for its exotic atmosphere that visitors have to make a reservation at least two months prior to their visit.  In addition to the cozy cabins, cottages, lodges and caravans where you can relax while enjoying fresh air and sea breeze, there are a pine tree forest and hanok near the campground. You can also engage in traditional culture through traditional plays and tteok (rice cake) making experience.  Have a great time with your family at Mangsang Auto Camping Resort, an attraction full of youth and romance and a family getaway spot where you can enjoy both Eastern and Western cultures through traditional hanok and an auto camping resort.

stories.title: Eight Beautiful Sites of Danyang: Dodam Peaks
stories.script: Dodam Peaks  [Traveler] Welcome to the most mysterious and peaceful valley in the Korean Peninsula. The word “danyang” means “a sunlight-filled hidden paradise of gods.” Which is why Danyang is one of the most beautiful cities not only in Chungcheongbuk-do, but also in all of Korea.   This heavenly city is well known for eight very beautiful landscapes. All these famous places can be seen along the wide and deep meandering river in front of you. Oh no! Not enough time to see all eight? Don’t worry! There is a ferry that will take you up and down the river. Although you can’t see every corner of the eight beautiful sites, it’s a convenient way to take in the landscapes, and the whole trip only takes an hour. Okay, are you ready for the trip?   The first place you’ll see is Dodam Peaks, or the Three Peaks of Dodam. The word “dodam” means “isle and water” while “sambong” simply means “three peaks” in Korean. It became even more famous after one of the most revered scholars named ‘Jeong Do-jeon’ nicknamed himself ‘Sambong’ because he liked the view so much. Jeong Do-jeon is one of the founders of ‘Joseon’, the dynasty that ruled over Korea from the 14th century to 20th century. He’s one of the most prominent figures in history for being the one who laid the foundation for the new kingdom, and brought about some important economic changes by giving land to poor peasants. He often visited Danyang because it was his birthplace, and he was very fond of his hometown. There is an interesting story about him. Would you like to hear it?   These three rock peaks were originally located at the mouth of the river, but after a flood, they were moved here. So the folks living in the upper side of the river demanded the townspeople here to pay taxes since the peaks were originally theirs. This didn’t make any sense, not even to the 7-year-old Jeong Do-jeon. So Jeong Do-jeon stepped forward and said to the grownups, “Take them back then! Because we don’t need them!” Humiliated by a little boy, the folks from the upper town gave on collecting taxes. Whether the story is true or not, no one knows, but if it were, wasn’t he such a clever boy?  Each of the Dodam Peaks has a name, and they were named for a special reason. The peak in the middle is the tallest one, and it’s named the “Husband” peak. The one nearest to it is called the “Concubine” peak, and the one farthest from them is the “Wife” peak. They say it’s because the three peaks look like a married couple with a concubine, with the wife turning her back to them because she didn’t want to look at her husband, who had brought in a concubine to bear a son for him.  For some reason, the “Concubine” peak looks conniving and flirtatious next to the “Husband” peak.

stories.title: Eight Beautiful Sites of Danyang: Dodam Peaks
stories.script: Seok Gate  [Travele] Whew! We’re here at last! Wasn’t it quite a workout to climb all the stairs? But it’s all worthwhile. The second beautiful site you’ll see is the hole here.  Just look at the naturally formed stone arch! We think this is what’s left of a big lime cave after it collapsed. It looks like a rainbow that rose up in the middle of a dust storm after an avalanche. Don’t you think it’s strangely beautiful? The sparkling sky-blue water and the village across the river seen through this hole is a unique sight, and it’s something you can’t see every day.  At the bottom left of the Seok Gate is a cave that’s hidden from your sight. Strangely, there are 99 small puddles in the cave. The pools are called the ‘Jade Paddies' because the water in the pools are jade green. Isn’t it surprising that there are so many puddles of jade-colored water?  According to ancient myth, the puddles were created by an old fairy from Heaven who lost her hairpin while trying to draw some water from this place. According to the myth, she used her long nails to dig the dirt in an attempt to find her pin, and water gathered in the holes to form these big puddles that look like rice paddies. She didn’t find the pin, so she ended up spending the rest of her life here farming until she turned into stone. They say the stone statue was holding a bottle of wine in her hand and a tobacco pipe in the other since she loved to drink and smoke.

stories.title: Eight Beautiful Sites of Danyang: Sain Rock
stories.script: Sain Rock  [Traveler] We have followed the refreshing sound of the water flowing down and cleaning the stones to come to this place called “Sainam.” Sain Rock is actually a stiff cliff standing 70 meters tall over the transparent water. While this is one of the eight most beautiful sites of Danyang, it’s also one of the nine most picturesque ravines in Danyang. It looks like layers of red and blue curtains, which is what makes it look so unique.   Since old times, this beautiful sight has been depicted as a “Picture from Heaven.” It is said that the view was too beautiful even for Korea’s best known painter of the 18th century, Kim Hong-do, who was intimidated by such beauty. About 300 years ago, the King ordered him to draw Sain Rock. So he stayed here for over a year trying to paint the view. But ultimately gave up and returned to the palace empty handed. I’m not much of a painter, but I think it would be really hard to paint such view.   Shall we get closer to the cliff then?  There is a lone small temple on the left side of Sain Rock. I think even I could get enlightened if I stay in this temple. Go closer to the temple, and you’ll see a road to a shrine just behind Sain Rock. That’s a place of worship where people pray to mountain gods. It has a unique atmosphere. I recommend you to go up there if you have the chance.

stories.title: Eight Beautiful Sites of Danyang: Haseon Rock
stories.script: Haseon Rock  [Traveler] “Haseon Rock” is one of the three most beautiful sites in this ravine. Myth has it that it was where mountain deities used to play. This ravine is also a habitat of otters, which is an endangered species of the world. If you’re lucky, you will see a family of otters with the parent teaching the pups how to catch fish.   When the sun shines in this ravine, the three-tiered flat rocks turn white like freshly washed linen. They’re called “Haseon Rock”. Can you see the round rock on top of them as if it were the main character on an aquatic stage? It’s called the “Buddha Rock” because it is said to look like the Buddha who will come to this world to save his disciples.   The top of the rock is like a stage set by the best artist of all, ‘Nature’, and the stage changes according to the four seasons. In spring, azaleas and royal azaleas cover the surface to turn the whole place pinkish red like the blushing cheek of a young girl in love. A fluffy blanket of summer’s mist, colorful autumnal leaves in fall and snow-covered pine tree in winter stage the rock.   Hundreds of painters have visited this place in the past few centuries to paint the landscape here, but no painting was good enough to contain all the beauty of Haseon Rock. Sit on a rock and dip your feet in the cold water. You’ll soon feel freshness shooting up your feet all the way up you head. This coolness and freshness can only be felt in the heart.

stories.title: Eight Beautiful Sites of Danyang: Jungseon Rock
stories.script: Jungseon Rock  [Traveler] This is “Jungseon Rock”. It literally means “the center rock in the ravine where mountain deities played. Although this place doesn’t have impressive rocks like the ones you’ve seen earlier, the rocks here are unique in that they look like someone had intentionally sliced them into thick slices and piled them up together like white cheese. And in addition to all this, just the sound of the flowing stream will make you feel like you’re taking a refreshing shower.  The landscape here is not too overwhelming. Instead, it’s charming and harmonious, and this is why so many people come here. Most of the mountains in Korea are small, making them a perfect place for people to play in the streams. In summer this area is packed with vacationers because the water is clean and there are lots of tree shadows here.   If you look at the rocks closely, you’ll find one that is bigger and whiter than the others. Look closer, and you’ll see that eight Chinese characters are written on it. It was written by a scholar named “Lee Hwang” who was appointed as the governor in 1717. In the short passage, he praised the beauty of this place, particularly the water and rocks. Besides the rock, there are more rocks around here that are engraved with words, particularly people’s names. More than 300 names are engraved on them. The names were left by those who have been long dead, but we can tell that they left their names before leaving this place because they were very reluctant to leave this place and wanted to leave their heart here.

stories.title: Eight Beautiful Sites of Danyang: Sangseon Rock
stories.script: Sangseon Rock  [Traveler] Now, let’s go see Sangseon Rock, which is located at the top of the stream. This place offers a spectacular sight, since there are layers upon layers of rocks that look like stacks of books in a personal library of a bookworm. Cross the stone bridge that looks like a rainbow and when you reach the top of the ravine, you’ll see the green stream flowing under your feet. Follow the stream, and you’ll see rocks of various shapes. Some people think they look like tightly lined homes in a humble Korean neighborhood.   Many writers came to this place to marvel at the rocks. One of the records on this place written about 300 years ago describes this place like this: The strangely shaped rocks look like a bed and a desk, and on top of them are trees lying horizontally or scattered around. The stream looks as though it were flowing backwards, like a cauldron filled with water.” What do you think? Do you agree with the description?   Including the three tourist sites you have seen in this ravine, all of the Eight Most Beautiful Sites of Danyang are made of rocks. For this reason, Danyang is considered the best place to go among rock collectors. This city is a real “Paradise of Rocks”. Are you ready to explore the world of rocks more?

stories.title: Eight Beautiful Sites of Danyang: Gudam Peak
stories.script: Gudam Peak  [Traveler] Welcome! You have set your foot into yet another ravine! Here, you’ll see other hidden treasures of Danyang. They’re Gudam Peak and Oksun Peak. If you take a look around this place on a ferry, you’ll find yourself immersed in the awe-aspiring beauty. But if you have time, I recommend you to climb the trail between the two peaks. The water flowing around the mountain creates quite a sight to behold.   Are you ready to observe the beauty of Gudam Peak? On the whole, Gudam Peak looks like a turtle. It’s quite interesting because you’ll see a different turtle in every angle. The peak was named by the governor of this area “Lee Hwang” in 1548, and it literally means turtle. They say even its reflection on the surface of the water resembles the carapace of a turtle, so check it for yourself.   Do you want to hear an interesting story? They say that some 450 years ago, a Korean-version of Tarzan lived here. The legend tells that a man tied vines between the peaks and rode a crane-shaped ride to go back and forth. So people thought he was a mountain deity. He was actually a scholar who loved the nature here, and he settled here after retirement. He lived freely in nature for the rest of his life. I guess he was happier than a mountain deity.

stories.title: Eight Beautiful Sites of Danyang: Oksun Peak
stories.script: Oksun Peak  Traveler: Oh, there is a red bridge over there. It means that we’re almost at Oksun Peak. You’re about to see the sight of the last picturesque scenery of Danyang. The name “Oksun Peak” simply means “Jade-Colored Rock”. It was named so because it was said to look like a bamboo shoot growing after the rain. Like Gudam Peak, it was also named by Governor Lee Hwang.   He was both a politician and a poet. And he described the peak like this: The rock must have been engraved by a ghost since it has one thousand different shapes and exudes divinity, and the mountain deity is merrily riding the winds on the back of a crane. The water is as clear as a mirror, and it’s wide open to carry away the fog. The steep cliff reaches the sky, and it looks like a newly sharpened sword stuck in the middle of a mirror. Wow! Don’t you think the scenery of this place deserves this praise song?   Interestingly, he also “stole” Oksun Peak from the neighboring village. Is it possible for a person to move this 372-m high rocky peak from a neighboring village? Of course not! He liked it so much that he wanted it to be in Danyang. So he asked the governor of the neighboring village to give it to him. Obviously, the governor said no. So on his way back home, he wrote the words “The Gate of Danyang” on the cliff of Oksun Peak, making it a makeshift boundary between the two cities. The governor of the neighboring village was furious when he heard about this. But after seeing the devotion and sincerity of the handwriting, he was so deeply impressed that he gave Oksun Peak to Danyang. It would have been good to see how great the writing was, but unfortunately, none of it is left.   Near Oksun Peak is a rock named “Gangseon Rock.” Which was where the tombstone of Duhyang, a female entertainer who was in love with him, used to be. When the water is high, the rock can’t be seen, but when the water is low, it comes to surface. The two loved each other, but he had no choice but to return to Seoul after his tenure ended. After he left, she remained faithful to him, growing orchids and Japanese apricots, just like Madame Butterfly. But upon hearing of his death, she jumped into the water and committed suicide. The purity of her heart must be the reason why this lake is so clear.

stories.title: Ondal Tourist Sites: Ondal Open Film Set
stories.script: Ondal Open Film Set  [Travele] Okay, we’re about to enter the Ondal Theme Park built by the city of Danyang. If you pass the entrance, you’ll see the Ondal filming set, where many Korean dramas were filmed, as well as the Ondal Fortress and cave. But who exactly is ‘Ondal’ and why did they build a place like this? Could he be the Korean version of Mickey Mouse or Harry Potter?   Actually, Ondal is the name of a 6th century Korean general who had brought home numerous victories. Many places in this town are named after him because locals consider him as their biggest hero. Built in 2006, this film set was no exception. The local folks named this film set after him. Let's take a look around, shall we?  This is strange. Normally, film sets are constructed of wood so that they can easily be torn down after the drama is over. But  this wall looks like it’s made of concrete. This film set was built on a 13,000㎡ plot. They built various types of buildings in this large lot, and all the buildings were built to last even after the drama. Therefore a number of Korean periodical dramas were filmed here.   This place can be quite interesting even to those who are not familiar with Korean TV dramas. That’s probably because it also serves as a traditional architecture park with traditional Korean and Chinese buildings constructed after thorough research. It's also a museum where you can see and try on some of the costumes and props worn by the characters of the dramas. Put on a costume and imagine being part of a Korean drama.

stories.title: Ondal Tourist Sites: Climbing Ondal Fortress
stories.script: Climbing Ondal Fortress  [Traveler] Now, let’s go find traces of General Ondal. I’ll tell you more about him on our way there. In Korea, the story of how his marriage overcame social status is more famous than the movie “A Roman Holiday.”  When he was little, his family was so poor that they had to beg for food. People made fun of him calling him “stupid Ondal” because of his pale and funny appearance. At the same time, there was a young princess who cried all the time. So whenever she cried, her father would tell her: “If you keep on crying, I’ll make you marry Ondal.” After she grew up, she actually wanted to marry Ondal despite everything, and she ended up getting thrown out from the palace for doing so. But with her effort, Ondal later became a great general.   During his time, the Korean Peninsula was divided into three kingdoms: One in the north and two in the south, and there was an ongoing war between them. And being located at the very center of the three kingdoms, Danyang was a place of strategic importance. They built a fortress here because this place commanded a clear view of the enemy and could get ready before they come too close. But why did they name this place after Ondal? Ondal was a general of the northern kingdom here, and he died a heroic death while trying to protect his country. So people named this place in commemoration of the war hero.   But why is General Ondal depicted as a half-witted person in the story? That was probably because the higher ranked noblemen were jealous of him. He was merely a descendant of a noble family that was at the bottom of the hierarchy or totally bankrupt. But he ended up marrying the princess and won great victories in the war. So those in the ruling class must have been green with envy.   Wanting to regain lost territory, Ondal remained in the battlefield and ultimately was killed by an arrow. But according to legend, the coffin carrying Ondal’s corpse wouldn’t move from here, and people thought it was because his soul was still aching and could leave the battlefield. Upon hearing this, the princess came and cried caressing the coffin. And that’s when the coffin finally began to move. The small pavilion that was on the way to this fortress was where Ondal’s coffin had been stuck.

stories.title: Ondal Tourist Sites: Ondal Fortress
stories.script: Ondal Fortress  [Traveler] At last! We have arrived at Ondal Fortress! You have done a great job climbing so many stairs. While catching your breath, look at the scenery below you. Doesn’t the winding Namhan River, the cluster of houses along the blue river, and the mountain ridges colored in sky-blue make the hike up here worth it?
