During Jeonju International Film Festival, there are many spaces where the visitors can experience a number of different events. In a variety show called, “I Live by Myself,” a singer named Kim Dong-wan enjoyed the night market with a French actress, Roxane Mesquida.  The night markets are held every Friday and Saturday. They feature fusion menus that are rare. At Pungnam gate near the entrance to the market, visitors can enjoy spectacular light shows using media-facade. While enjoying these various dishes and sights, make sure to participate in funny events held at the Young Adult Mall.

stories.title: Entrance to Jeju’s Dongmun Market
stories.audioTitle: The top market of Jeju Island, the three-time winner of UNESCO’s Clean Nature Award
stories.script: The top market of Jeju Island, the three-time winner of UNESCO’s Clean Nature Award   Dongmun Market, the oldest in Jeju Island, is located between Jeju International Airport and Jeju International Passenger Terminal. Located in the heart of Jeju’s downtown, it is a favorite among Jeju residents and tourists alike.  At the market, it is possible to purchase Jeju’s regional products such as tangerines and “Hallabong” all year round.  Since the names and products of these citrus fruits all differ by harvest seasons and locations, be sure to ask before purchasing some. This is also the best place to try local specialty such as omegi-ddeok (rice cake), jayeonmom-guk (gulfweed soup), and bing-ddeok (Jeju style buckwheat pancake).  Customer Service Center offers the market map and foreign language assistance service, making the tourists’ market experience both easy and convenient.  Jeju Island, where Jeju Dongmun Market is located, is the world natural heritage registered at UNESCO, which offers many wonderful attractions. There are Jeju Confucian Temple and Yongdu-am Rock near the market where the line of tourists know no end. A little bit farther away from the market, visitors can enjoy Teddy Bear Museum, green tea tree farms, AquaPlanet, and Seongsan Sunrise Peak.

stories.title: Tasty Stories of Dongmun Market
stories.audioTitle: Tasting all the local favorites of Jeju
stories.script: Tasting all the local favorites of Jeju   At Dongmun Market, visitors can enjoy all local specialties of Jeju, including tangerines and hallabong, the two most representative fruits of Jeju. As Jeju is one of the areas that is the warmest in Korea, it is possible to grow tropical fruits in Jeju and is not hard to see cheonhyeohyang or hwanggumhyang at the market along with apple mango and dragon fruit originally from Southeast Asia or China.   Foods from Dongmun Markets are often featured in shows like “Running Man” or restaurant review programs that inform of tasty restaurants in Korea, and one of the most popular is omegi-ddeok (rice cake). Made mostly from glutinous millet, this rice cake covered in bean powder and red bean topping is best recommended to be eaten hot.     Jeju-do Province being an island, it is famous for seafood. Fresh hairtail or tile fish are among many that are available for the visitors to purchase at local fish market. They can be prepared for sashimi, and the leftover can be prepared for some spicy fish soup. If you are into seafood, you must make a stop at the market.

stories.title: Dongdaemun Market Association
stories.script: Dongdaemun Wholesale Fashion Market Korea’s Fashion Hub   Conveniently located between Dongdaemun Station on Line 1 and Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station on Line 4 of the Seoul Subway, it is easy to get to Dongdaemun Market, Korea’s fashion hub.   Dongdaemun Apparel Wholesale Market, which is found in the commercial area of Dongdaemun, was created by the merchant association of eight smaller markets: Pyounghwa Market, Tongil Arcade, Shin Pyounghwa Fashion Town, Fashion Nam Pyounghwa, Dong Pyounghwa Fashion Town, Techno Town, Kwanghee Fashion Mall, and Belpost.   Each market offers specific items, ranging from women’s and men’s apparel to fashion accessories. The variety adds flavor to your shopping. The area also provides competitively-priced goods and services for many international shoppers.   Dongdaemun Design Plaza, a well-known landmark nearby, is another place to enjoy your time in Dongdaemun. There, you may even have a chance to watch one of the popular fashion shows held in the area.   Although it is busy during the daytime, the area is filled with its most vibrant energy at night. Each market opens at different hours. In between trips to the bustling markets, look for the numerous stores and food stalls nestled in the spaces between buildings, and grab a bite to ease your hunger. Looking for a new outfit? Let’s head to Dongdaemun, the market that never sleeps, and pick out something that looks great on you!

stories.title: Dongdaemun Market’s Special Zone
stories.audioTitle: The Best Place in Dongdaemun for a Photo Shoot
stories.script: Dongdaemun Market Special Zone  The Best Place in Dongdaemun for a Photo Shoot   With over 100 years of history, Dongdaemun Market is not only the cradle of Korea’s garment industry, but also a leader in global trends, at the forefront of the fast fashion movement. Also, a zoning project was completed recently, giving artists the chance to depict the spirit of Dongdaemun Market in their artwork.          Tongil Arcade, on the Street of Light, has installed artworks made of stained glass over a viaduct. These glassworks visually portray Dongdaemun Market’s rich history to passersby.  In addition, “The Media Wall,” the stone wall in front of Techno Town, has been decorated with frescoes and fitted with media artworks, so that the entire area remains lit 24 hours a day. It reflects the dynamic images of Dongdaemun Market.   When you arrive at “Painting Square” of Fashion Nam Pyounghwa, you can enjoy its beautiful wall paintings, which depict various aspects of Dongdaemun Market. These are the work of an artist who also designed the main logo of the popular T.V. show, “Youn’s Kitchen.”  If you are here for just a day out, why not take a photo with these fabulous artworks? Then, you’ll always have a chance to look back on the scenes from your trip to Dongdaemun Market.

stories.title: Jagalchi Market
stories.script: Jagalchi Market, the largest fish market in South Korea   Among the many tourist spots in the Busan area, Jagalchi Market stands out as the most popular marketplace! Various theories explain the origin of its unique name. One suggests it originates from a stone field, known as ‘jagal’ in Korean, near Chungmu-dong in Busan. Another theory links the name to a fish called Jagalchi, while some associate it with the market's variety of unique fish, such as halibut, Spanish mackerel, and hairtail.  Initially, the market comprised a gathering of street vendors along the waterfront. However, following the construction of a modern building shaped like a flock of seagulls, it transformed into an indoor market. This new structure shielded vendors from the cold winter wind and featured underground parking facilities. The ground level boasts a vibrant array of freshly caught fish, king crabs, lobsters, and various seafood. The second floor houses shops selling dried fish and other seafood, along with restaurants offering ocean views, attracting many visitors.  Exiting at Jagalchi Station on Subway Line One in Busan, it takes just a minute to reach the market. Visitors can also explore other renowned landmarks nearby, such as Gukje or Nampodong International Market, Bupyeong Kangtong Market, and Busan’s International Film Festival Movie Street. These have become must-visit destinations for tourists looking to experience the full essence of Busan. A brief 5-minute walk from Jagalchi Market leads to Yeongdodaegyo Bridge, Korea's first bascule or drawbridge, raised daily at 2 p.m.  The latest attraction gaining popularity is the observation deck of Jagalchi Market. Accessible by elevator up to the seventh floor and then stairs to the rooftop, visitors can use telescopes to view the cityscape, including Namhang Pier and Busan's Yeongdo District. Undoubtedly, this observation deck is one of the best spots to admire downtown Busan and Yongdusan Park.

stories.title: Jagalchi Market Tourist Information Center
stories.script: A place to assist tourists in overcoming communication barriers   Jagalchi Market has become a must-visit stop for international tourists in Busan. It is also an attraction included in the city tour package. Referred to as Ajimae in the Busan dialect, married women arrive early at dawn to prepare their stalls, showcasing an array of fresh fish and seafood. Visitors can have the unique opportunity to select their preferred seafood for slicing or even cooking themselves, promising an unforgettable experience. Visitors can also try out local specialties, such as live octopus, dried seaweed sheets, or fresh seaweed. Of course, it would also serve as a perfect souvenir to take home.  Additionally, in order to assist international visitors facing communication problem, Jagalchi Market hosts a Tourist Information Center. Tour guides in the center are fluent in English, Japanese, and Chinese who provide comprehensive assistance regarding the market layout, various seafood types, and the market's distinctive buy-and-sell methods.   Ascending to the 7th floor of the market, guests discover a guesthouse offering a chance to savor Busan's nighttime seascape. This location offers an all-encompassing experience that shouldn't be overlooked. Don't miss the opportunity to witness the fresh seafood auction at dawn - a highlight of this vibrant marketplace!

stories.title: Suwon Nammun Market Association
stories.audioTitle: Established by King Jongjo, the 22nd Ruler of the Joseon Dynasty
stories.script: Suwon Nammun Market Association Established by King Jongjo, the 22nd Ruler of the Joseon Dynasty   Over two hundred years ago, King Jongjo was the 22nd ruler of the Joseon Dynasty. While in mourning for Crown Prince Sado, he planned and built a large city around his father’s tomb. This came to be known as Hwaseong Fortress in Suwon. Nammun, or the south gate, is also known as, “Paldalmun Fort.” Around Paldalmun Fort, nine markets sprang up surrounding the gate, and eventually combined to become Suwon Nammun Market, which is the biggest marketplace in the Gyeonggi-do Provincial area.   Historically, this is the one and only market that was created by a king, and boasts a 220-year-long history, filled with the spirit of tradition.   Gucheon-dong Hardware Market has preserved the culture of blacksmiths. Nammun or South Gate Rodeo Market, or Fashion Avenue 1 – is where all the fashionistas of Suwon come together, and is also a great place for locals! Motgol Market recreates the streets of the Joseon Dynasty, the last independent monarchy. Minarigang Market is filled with a variety of delicious side dishes to take home for meals. Simin Market offers men’s and women’s clothing, and Yeongdong Traditional Market display rows of five-colored silk hanboks, or traditional clothes dyed the street. Jidong Market offers sundae, a type of blood sausage, which is one of the most popular dishes in Suwon Nammun Market. Paldalmun Market is famous for its fried chicken. As you can see, Suwon Nammun Market offers something to see, something to eat, and something to do, all in one spot.   In addition to these, Eocha, or the Hwaseong Fortress tourist trolley, goes around Suwon Hwaseong Fortress and through the market. This place has been designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It even includes a local broadcasting station run by local merchants since it has been declared a special tourist zone, and is now best known for its seasonal festivals! Suwon Nammun Market is a place to enjoy yourself 365 days a year!!

stories.title: Suwon Nammun Market Jeojatgeori
stories.script: Suwon Nammun Market Jeojatgeori  Recreating History   If Suwon Nammun Market brought happiness to your eyes, why not visit Motgal Global Market next? This market offers you a taste of history through Jeojatgeori, the street stores of the Joseon Dynasty, the last independent monarchy!   In 2017, under the global brand market development project, all the stores in the area were decorated with roof tiles and cheongsachorong, or traditional Korean lanterns in red and blue silk. So, the minute you enter the market, you are pleasantly transported back to the marketplace of 220 years ago. Though the scene seems straight out of the Joseon Dynasty, tourists can buy anything from tteokbokki, or spicy stir-fried rice cakes, and sundae, or blood sausage, to simple side dishes for dinner.   The most popular activity for tourists visiting Suwon Nammun Market is the “Gold Plating Handcraft!” In this gold plating activity, participants can draw simple sketches of their choice on items like shot glasses, chopsticks or canvas, then mount gold leaf on them. As gold signifies the nobility of kings and the wealth of merchants, “Gold Plating” is an activity prized by visitors to Suwon Nammun Market. Participants can take their “one and only in the world” souvenirs of Suwon Nammun Market back to their homes.   Now, what’s there to eat in Suwon Nammun Market? Sundae or blood sausage from Jidong Market! Fried chicken from Paldalmun Market! If you are looking for something a little more exotic, check out the Food Trailer Zone. As dusk begins to fall around 4 to 5, the Jidonggyo Plaza area and the vehicle-free street of Paldalmun Market offer rows of food trailers, carrying foods full of charm and character. They offer a wide range of food from different countries: Taiwanese French fries, Brazilian dumplings, Japanese ramen, cube steak, salmon salad, pasta, and even juice served in lightbulbs!!! The variety of dishes from the Food Trailers will satisfy your eyes and mouth at the same time, and guarantee you a beautiful night out.

stories.title: Andonggu Market Association
stories.audioTitle: The Market Where Everything Is Together in One Place
stories.script: Andonggu Market Association The Market Where Everything Is Together in One Place   Andonggu Market Association is made up of Andonggu Market, which has retained its traditional appearance; Namseo Store Street, featuring a modern look; and Joongang Cultural Street, which harmonizes the traditional and futuristic markets in a single spot.   Famous for its popular dish, Andong Jjimdak, or braised spicy chicken with vegetables, the market has added to its convenience by providing ample space for parking, which can now accommodate 120 cars, as well as delivery service for this traditional market. Namseo Store Street is well-known for its tteokbokki, or spicy stir-fried rice cake, stalls. The whole alley is always filled with people, lining up to eat this popular street food. Additionally, the area boasts a famous bakery that was included in the Michelin Guide, as well as buskers and street performers to put visitors at ease, giving them a moment to relax and just enjoy the shows.   Strolling from Andonggu Market to Cultural Street, visitors can experience the genuine beauty of Korea, from its traditional charms and tastes to its modern features. Why not take a look at the three distinctive aspects of Andonggu Market Association that can be seen on every corner?

stories.title: Andonggu Market, Cultural Street
stories.audioTitle: Making a Space for Youth, Romance, and Tradition Together
stories.script: Andonggu Market, Cultural Street Making a Space for Youth, Romance, and Tradition Together   As the Mugunghwa train pulls into Andong Station, Cultural Street, the old center of town, comes into view right across the street. This is a popular hangout for many visitors: young, old, and even whole families traveling together.   Not only are the major events in Andong held here, but Cultural Street is the birthplace of culture. As it is the very center of Andong, it offers a wide range of amenities: clean benches; a stream passing through; movie theaters and street stages where people can enjoy cultural experiences; and even franchise stores. Taken together, these make the old center of town feel younger and more colorful.   To better serve international visitors, merchants receive foreign-language training to improve the quality of their services. Additionally, duty-free shops are currently being built, to add even more convenience for shoppers. The area will soon be reborn as a shopping heaven. Now, let’s go and enjoy the fun and excitement of Andong, in its streets filled with both traditional and modern beauty and charm.

stories.title: Seoul Suyu Village Market
stories.audioTitle: A Market Tour Is Better on a Full Stomach
stories.script: Seoul Suyu Village Market A Market Tour Is Better on a Full Stomach.   Located between Subway Line 4’s Mia and Suyu Stations, Suyu Village Market is an excellent example of how a traditional market can remain competitive among the jungle of larger department stores and supermarkets of Seoul. Constructed in the 1960s as a building, it was called Suyu Traditional Market or Suyu Market as people naturally gathered in the area.    With its customer-first mindset, the business owners and merchants association of Suyu Market have worked hard to provide clean, fresh, and varied products at affordable prices, helping to boost the local economy.   The most popular snacks of Suyu Market are twisted bread sticks made of sticky rice, baked by highly-skilled bakers, and millet pancakes, offering a taste of home. As satisfying soups, sundae guk, or blood sausage soup, ox blood soup, and simple but delicious gomtang, or beef-bone soup, are available. On top of that, a wide variety of jeon or pan–fried delicacies, are sold as excellent street food. The delicacy of Hongeo muchim, or seasoned skate, sold at Suyu Market is well-known and is now delivered all around the country.    As the streets can be confusing to newcomers, the streets’ store signs and leaflets of Suyu Market are color-coded to provide easy access to the different areas. Furthermore, to advocate communication and development for business owners and local residents, including customers, Suyu Village Library, Club Attic, and Sangsang Club offer various cultural activities, programs, lectures and events. The workmanship of the club members can be seen throughout the market, as these add greater charm to the area, and more attractions to enjoy.

stories.title: Incheon Singi Cultural Tourism Market
stories.audioTitle: Get Connected! Bringing A Unique Market to the World!
stories.script: Incheon Singi Cultural Tour Market  Get Connected! Bringing A Unique Market to the World!   Singi Market, the largest market in the Nam-gu District of Incheon City, has a unique coin called “Singi Tongbo.” On the way from the public parking lot to the market, a giant version of Singi Tongbo is on display, indicating that it is only used in Singi Market. The idea of using local currency came from Sangpyeong Tongbo, a coin used during the Joseon Dynasty, the last independent monarchy. A local saying goes, “When touching this, your financial prospects will greatly improve.”   One unusual aspect of the market is the baseball museum located in the public parking lot. In the museum, you can see how baseball arrived in Incheon, Korea for the first time, as well its history in the area. Many cherished items sought by fans, handprints, and autographed objects from famous baseball players and their teams are on display here. Also, Munhak Baseball Stadium of Incheon is located nearby, so fans can buy some snacks at the market and bring them along to the stadium to watch the game.  At the entrance to the market, visitors can see that the whole alley is filled with delicious snacks, such as hotteok, or stuffed sticky pancakes, and gangjeong or fried rice crackers. At a café on the ground floor of the public parking lot, visitors can enjoy various drinks, give lectures, or even participate in woodcraft making comfortably. Why not stop by at Sinji Market, charged with vibrant energy every day and recharge your own batteries?

stories.title: Jeongseon Fifth-day Market
stories.audioTitle: Fall in love with the excitement of a traditional Korean market
stories.script: Jeongseon Fifth-day Market Fall in love with the excitement of a traditional Korean market   The Jeongseon Fifth-day Market originated with the village market in the area during the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910). It is located between Songcheon Stream and Goljicheon Stream along the Joyanggang River. The market is open every five days on the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd and 27th of each month. It is also open on Saturdays, after having been designated as a culture and tourism market in 2012.  Let's take a tour of the marketplace, starting with the South Gate, where the Jeongseon Tourist Information Center is located. You can find many locally grown specialties at affordable prices, including wild mountain herbs such as gondeure (or Korean thistle), deodeok, gomchwi and hwanggi. As you will see, market visitors are often the happy recipients of an extra handful of vegetables from the merchants. On market day, lively performances presented on an outdoor stage make for a uniquely exciting trip.  A traditional market wouldn't be complete without a street food street. Jeongseon is famous for its delicious buckwheat noodles and gondeure rice, along with a variety of other tasty dishes including millet pancakes, buckwheat crepes and potato dumpling soup. Try a bowl of buckwheat noodles and gondeure rice accompanied by a combination plate of traditional Korean pancakes, including buckwheat, sorghum and mung bean. No matter what you may choose, you won't be disappointed.

stories.title: Jeongseon Arirang Market
stories.audioTitle: A Breath of Culture, the Greatness of Nature
stories.script: Jeongseon Arirang Market A Breath of Culture, the Greatness of Nature.   When riding a train departing from Cheongnyangni Station, one passes by Jeongseon Arirang Market, a small marketplace in a remote village in deep in the mountains. This symbolic cultural and traditional market of Korea is enriched with fresh produce and various high-quality agricultural specialties grown in a clean natural environment and the spirit of Arirang. It has been designated as a part of the UNESCO Intangible Heritage of Humanity. Changing with the times, modern facilities have been adapted to running the market. This place is the most popular on market days, filled with many attractions, appetizing food, and enjoyable activities on the second and seventh days of each month, as well as every Saturday.   On market days, busy feet are surely drawn to Jeongseon Arirang Performances. The elderly dance to cheerful yet sorrowful songs while the young are intoxicated by the cultural fragrance, clicking the shutters of their cameras nonstop.   Along the sides, Jeongseon Arirang Market is working to diversify the visitors’ ages, developing customized products for each generation, and running the Golden Chariot Street. The attraction of the Golden Chariot Street is not actually a gold chariot, but lines of people. Specifically, different types of fusion food, unique to this market, make the place seem younger. In the tavern area of Jeojatgeori, or street stores, rice wine and delicious-looking traditional dishes to go along with it, are waiting for visitors.   Jeongseon is one of the cities to host the Pyeongchang 2018 Winter Olympic Games. In the city’s downtown area, Jeongseon Arirang Market is a great place to visit. Why not take a train to Jeongseon to Jeongseon Arirang Market, a place filled with various types of authentic food, fresh produce, and quality agricultural specialties from the breath-taking nature of the region, and enjoy the world cultural heritage of Arirang?

stories.title: Everyday Olle Market
stories.script: Happy Road of Lee Jung-seop — Seogwipo Everyday Olle Market  Seogwipo Everyday Olle Market is the largest marketplace in Seogwipo opened in the 1960s. The market is divided into different zones, which include a seafood street, miscellaneous goods street, vegetable street and food town, and about 350 stores are currently in business. The 620-meter-long arcade facility opens and closes automatically. A package delivery system is available for visitors to quickly send local specialties and gifts in packages and travel lightly.  As the nearby Lee Jung Seop Street continues to attract tourists, many places in the market also offer delicious foods and snacks that the travelers would love. From desserts like Udo peanuts, tangerines and green tea to other Jeju specialties such as omegi rice cakes, snow crab croquettes, octopus bread and modakchigi (gimbap, tteokbokki and deep-fried dish combo), there are so many goodies that attract travelers every day.  You can obtain travel information at the Jeju Olle Information Center in the marketplace. There are various facilities such an outdoor performance stage, a fountain and a playground, and a space to park up to 250 cars and 18 large buses.

stories.title: Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market
stories.audioTitle: A Market Tour in Jeju Style
stories.script: Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market A Market Tour in Jeju Style   Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market is the largest market in Seogwipo City. The traditional market was naturally formed in the early 1960s, with about 60 years of history behind it. As it became a part of Course No. 6 of Jeju Olle Trails, it changed its name to “Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market.” The word “Olle” is a small trail leading from the main road to your house, in Jeju dialect.   The parking lot located in the market can accommodate 500 cars at once, and offers 30 minutes of free parking, so there is no need to worry about parking when going into the market. The environmentally-friendly waterway constructed along the alleys of the market provides an attractive resting spot. When looking up at the ceiling while shopping, visitors will be able to see the giant canvases portraying the beautiful scenery of Jeju. Great photographs depict a waterfall of Jeju in each of the four seasons.   Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market offers tours of various Jeju specialties and traditional dishes. Furthermore, the market offers free shipping for customers for their purchases to the place of their choice. Outdoor stages and parks along the way are great places to watch various performances and visit festivals, especially for the young, the future of market. Please come and enjoy!

stories.title: Gwangju Yangdong Bokgae Market
stories.audioTitle: The biggest market in Gwangju City
stories.script: Located in the west of the Metropolitan City of Gwangju, this market is the biggest in the area, as well as in Honam, or the Jeolla Province. Along the Gwangju Stream, there are seven markets in total: Yangdong Market, Bokgae Market, a fishery market, a livestock market, a dried seafood market, Gyeongyeolro market, and an industrial goods market. These seven markets, when combined together, are called Yangdong Market.  In the 1940s, several small markets sprang up around the Gwangju Stream, which was the start of Yangdong Market. As time went by, the streets became the part of the market, and the area was named “Yangdong,” meaning ‘live honestly.’ During the Japanese Colonial period, the Yangdong merchants not only raised funds for the May 18 Gwangju Democratic Movement, but also provided food to the civilian forces, as well as students around that time. They even took part in the protests themselves, truly living up to their name and winning the hearts of the citizens of Gwangju.  Yangdong Market can be accessed from all exits at the Gwangju subway station. At the entrance to each street, visitors can find a list of items being sold in each area. So, people can go directly to the street they need and shop efficiently.    Everywhere you look, there are murals and artfully-decorated benches, as well as event galleries all around this bustling market. Naturally, you will often see visitors taking photos in these photo zones. Starting from the staircase that leads to the second floor of the market, the whole area is decorated with pictures and wall paintings. As you take photos on your way up to the rooftop, you will find a hidden spot, where you can take in the panoramic view of the Gwangju Stream and the entire market.

stories.title: Gumi Saemaul Jungang Market
stories.audioTitle: Filled with happiness in Saemaul, the New Village
stories.script: As you get off at Gumi Station, look up, and you can see Saemaul or New Village Jungang Market right across the street. Since it is right downtown in Gumi City, it has always been a popular market for city dwellers. Then, one day, a green symbol of happiness began to fill this bustling place.  Starting from the entrance of the market, store signs decorated with three-leaf clovers come into view. The three-leaf clovers became popular decorations after the merchants decided to use these symbols to promote the market. Through the meaning of the three-leaf clover, “happiness,” merchants hope that all market visitors will be happy.  Saemaul Jungang Market is an all-inclusive Korean traditional market, with Soondae, or Blood Sausage Street; Jokbal, or Pigs’ Feet Street; Hanbok, or Korean Traditional Clothing Street, and Food Alley. Store signs are displayed clearly by each door, as well as street names, so they can be seen easily. Also, stores with many patrons also hang signs bearing a caricature of the store’s owner, to emphasize the trust customers have in that vendor.  Furthermore, visitors can join a tour program, and be guided around the market. They can even take part in a number of Korean cultural activities: rice cake making, trying on Hanbok, or traditional clothes, and picking fruits or vegetables. These will be a chance for hands-on experience, so visitors can add more memories to their rich lives.

stories.title: Sangseol Market in Buan
stories.audioTitle: The market holding the treasures of the West Sea
stories.script: Starting from the Buan Intercity Bus Terminal, walk along the road for about six minutes. There, you can get your first glimpse of Buan Sangseol Market.  As Buan sits on the west coast, there is plenty of seafood to go around. Even though the seafood is good all around the area, this market offers the freshest catches of all. Each season packs the market with a wide array of fresh seafood: mullets in the winter; octopus and blue crabs in the spring; bass and rock fish in the summer; and gizzards and croakers in the fall. Naturally, crowds of people from nearby cities like Gimje, Jeonju or Jeongeup travel to Buan Sangseol Market to get their hands on the best seafood.  In addition to seafood, visitors can also purchase other special regional products, grown in the rich soil of Buan, like Geomso Salted Seafood, Julpo Watermelon, Noeul Potatoes, and Buan Rice. The market is also well-known for Patjuk or red bean porridge, made entirely from domestically-grown beans and small, handmade dumplings in it. It became so famous that a whole street specialized in this dish sprang up. Just take your pick of the restaurants for a mouthful of the taste. After that, don’t forget to try some shrimp marinated in soy sauce and spicy catfish soup, which are two more well-known dishes at this market.  What’s more, a café called “See Jangan” is run by the market cooperative at Buan Sangseol Market. From artwork made by students who visited on field trips, to soft drinks at affordable prices, this venue offers local merchants a place to take a break. Why not take your time and stroll around the market?

stories.title: Busan Gupo Market
stories.script: Most famous for Gupo noodles, this market has held onto its location in Gupo-dong, Busan for a long time. It is one of the biggest markets in Busan City. Even though it is located in the middle of the city, a large number of vendors still fill the market once every five days, six times a month. On those days, a wide range of goods from all the surrounding areas completely pack its streets.  Gupo Market was mentioned in the book “Yeongnam Eupji or The Annals of Gyeongsang Province,” which was written during the Joseon Dynasty period. Originally, the market was only open once every five days, but was permanently opened in 1972, and has stayed that way ever since. In 1919, during the Japanese colonial period, an independence movement began in this area. For that reason, one of its streets is called “Gupo Manse-gil, or Independence Movement Road.”  The market is close to Deokcheon Station on the Busan Subway as well as Gupo Station on the KTX, a high-speed train line. Naturally, not only locals visit this market, but also many tourists, so at times it can be a bit challenging to move around the alleys of the market if you are bringing young children. To address this difficulty, a public kids’ café was recently opened on the third floor of the Gupo Credit Union building. While shopping, children can spend their time there and entertain themselves, maybe even making new friends. The facility is free for all children, even for several hours, and is equipped with a breast-feeding room, as well as mom’s café where women can take a break, too. The consideration the merchants have toward their customers and the continuation of 5-day market tradition flood this marketplace with affection. Also, every late October, a “Festival at Affectionate Gupo Market” is held. Why not join the festival and treat yourself to a little affection?

stories.title: Gongju Sansung Market
stories.audioTitle: A night out at Baekje Godo, the ancient capital of the Baekje Kingdom
stories.script: Gongju Sanseong Market is located in an area where the Gong Sanseong, or Mountain Fortress, can be seen in the city of Gongju, which was the capital of the Baekje Kingdom. In the beginning, Gongju Sangseong Market was held every five days. As it was one of the three major markets in the country, it is an all-inclusive marketplace with rich history and traditions. Though the market is now open permanently, it still attracts more visitors whenever additional vendors come once every five days, according to the tradition. Additionally, it is only a three-minute walk from Gongju Intercity Bus Terminal. Since it is so accessible, many elderly people from rural areas visit this market, as well.  Around the marketplace, a character called “Goma Gom,” or Thank You Bear, can be seen everywhere. This bear was designated as the mascot of Gongju City, originating from the ancient name for the area: Woong Jin; that is, the camp of bears. It is said that this character was created in an attempt to depict the hopes and dreams of the merchants and the citizens of the city. The bear carries their hopes and dreams for change in the spirit of the market.   The reason why Gongju Sanseong Market became known as the night market is the phrase “Bam Masil or Outing.” The regional specialty of Gongju is chestnuts, which is pronounced bam, the same as the word for night. Whenever the night market is open, visitors can watch busking performances, traditional classical shows, Nanta, or drum-beating groups, and more in the cultural square. In addition to live entertainment, visitors can enjoy snacks or meals from around the world from food trucks. In particular, Bam Makgeolli, or Chestnut Rice Wine, made from chestnuts grown locally in the Gongju region, is extremely popular with out-of-town visitors. Some fans even order it by mail after trying their first taste.   In addition to the noodle shops that are so famous among the people of Gongju, vendors sell many other popular local foods, like flat dumplings, mini kimbap, and blood sausage soup. As a matter of fact, Gongju Sanseong Market is an ideal place to go on a food tour, since all these restaurants serving delicious food are gathered together in one place. Around the singing stage near a fountain, there is a place where visitors can try on traditional clothes from the Baekje Kingdom period for free. Don’t forget to try them on!

stories.title: The Eco-Trail Entrance to the Imjingang Riverside
stories.script: Hello, we would like to welcome you all on your visit to the Eco-trail of the Imjingang Riverside. As you pass through the thick iron doors at the front, the face of the old watchtowers come into view, bearing the marks of time passing by, as well as endless lines of barbed wire. The military has placed the barbed-wire fence here in order to protect the civilian population. Soldiers used to patrol the area, but now CCTV cameras have taken on this role instead. Walking the eco-trail takes about three hours, as it is about 9.1 kilometers long, stretching from Pyeonghwa Nuri Park of Imjingak, Tongildaegyo, or the Freedom Bridge, to Choppyeong-do, Imjin Naru or the River Dock, and arriving at Yulgok Wetland Park. Starting this year, it became possible for visitors to explore the area, although some parts are still off-limits. In order to maintain a clear view of the area for security reasons, there are no tall trees or thick bushes that grow above the level of the barbed-wire fence. Nonetheless, walking the barbed-wire trail along the Imjingang River, you will definitely be rewarded with a unique experience.

stories.title: From Tongildaegyo to the Outdoor Exhibition Area
stories.audioTitle: From Tongildaegyo to the Outdoor Exhibition Area
stories.script: Walking along the metal fence, you will see a large, four-lane bridge cutting across the Imjingang River. This is Tongildaegyo, or The Freedom Bridge, which opened in the summer of 1998. This bridge became quite famous when late Ju-yung Chung, the founder of Hyundai Group, visited North Korea, leading a herd of cattle along the overpass. It gained even more significance as the bridge lies on National Route 1, which connects Mokpo City at the southwestern tip of the Korean Peninsula, and Sinuiju City at the northwestern tip.  Once you pass by Tongildaegyo, you will come to an outdoor exhibition area surrounded by the barbed-wire fence in a place that feels like the one and only world. With a contest held for university students, beginning back in 2010, this place started to display artworks inside the metal-fenced area, that is, the civilian-controlled area. Instead of using patrolling markers or infiltration-checking stones, this fenced-in area was reborn as a place of peace and art, following the laws of nature. If you had the chance to redecorate the place, what kind of artwork would you like to install here?   On the right, the work of artist Im, Dowon, “Wishing Hands” is displayed. With the heartfelt wishes of human hands, the artist attempted to convey our dearest hopes, depicting hands stretching up toward the sky. Until the day of reunification, we hope to fill this space with more artworks demonstrating our country’s most ardent wish.   Now, let’s begin the tour of the outdoor exhibition surrounded by the barbed-wired fence, in the one and only world. Feel free to take photos or take notes on the artworks shown in the exhibition.

stories.title: Hayami Towards Reunification
stories.audioTitle: Hayami Towards Reunification by Noh, Jun
stories.script: The artwork, “Hayami Towards Reunification” is the depiction of an animal character of the artist’s own design. Hayami’s heads are gradually and proportionally enlarged. They progressively become larger and larger as it walks ahead. This is to indicate that reunification is coming closer to us. Hayami is not simply colored in white, but rather with several pigments of paint mixed together, giving this piece a unique look. Though the relationship between North and South Korea is tangled and complex, ultimately we are one nation of people, and this shade of white signifies our unity.

stories.title: Fly High, Fly High, Paper Plane
stories.audioTitle: Fly High, Fly High, Paper Plane  by Ha, Won
stories.script: In childhood, we used to fly paper planes, folding a sheet of white paper, competing with each other and making bets to see whose could soar the highest and farthest. With the hope and dream of flying high and freely, the artist attempted to portray our hopes of soaring high above in the clear blue sky in many planes, going beyond any ideology. Fly higher and higher, Paper Plane.

stories.title: Open Peace
stories.script: Despite the fact that North and South Korea are a nation of one people, we have been pointing guns at each other over half a century. We must withdraw our guns and open the closed doors in our minds, in order to be one again. The giant, seemingly-unbreakable chains that bar the doors can break into pieces without any trace. On the day these doors open, there shall be peace that we ultimately long for.

stories.title: Soul Fish
stories.script: The DMZ, or the demilitarized zone, is no longer the land of the dead, filled with the sorrow of division and the tension of terror, but rather a valuable ecological area and a natural place where people can come and go as they wish. In the landscape of the DMZ beyond the iron fence, the resident fish of the Imjingang River, the natural treasures of this zone, swim vigorously through the water. These beautiful creatures reflect the beaming rays of sunlight. The clear blue sky beyond the metal fence appears in the water of the Imjingang River. The white clouds emerge as free-spirited souls that swim idly by, and gentle breezes become the breath of nature.

stories.title: The Passage
stories.script: In 2001, a field filled with dandelions and Oseongsan Mountain from the Anti-Communism Observation Post of the DMZ was heart-achingly beautiful. Then, a suffocating event of sorrow took place - the space of mounting tensions met the beautiful silence. The space was filled with both chaotic deaths and tranquil lives – it must be demolished, but it must also be kept. This place of endless, extreme conflicts and contradictions is shown here without any omissions; that is, the DMZ. This artwork attempts to illustrate the series of “The Passage,” and has been here since 2014. Serving as an observation officer at the beginning of his military duty, the artist of “The Passage” tried to recreate his journal entries in the form of installation art. He wanted to convey the progression of his feelings of vividness and familiarity in the DMZ that he experienced firsthand. He throws questions at us while simultaneously trying to organize the feelings that he dared not touch for decades.

stories.title: The Prejudiced View
stories.audioTitle: The Prejudiced View  by Lee, Seungkoo
stories.script: For a period of over sixty years, the people of North and South Korea have lived in different countries with differing thoughts and views. When will we be able to see one place, dreaming of one future? These acrylic panels of many colors are the representation of biased thoughts, forced upon the people because of the Korean War. Through these acrylic pieces, we can see the landscape on the other side of the fence. Yet, even though it is the same scenery, we see the land in different colors because of our various prejudiced thoughts. Why don’t we reconsider our biased ideas about North Korea?

stories.title: DMZ(2016)
stories.script: This is a piece of installation art – musical notes on a staff inside the spiky barbed-wire tunnel - mounted before the empty background of blue sky. At first, the song starts with simple symbols and rests, and some empty intervals appear, but as it progresses, more notes are added, and at last it becomes complete. Through the unique relationship between the rhythms that are played before the backdrop of the sky and the iron fence, it is the artist’s hope that you will take this chance to think over the meanings of nature, freedom, and unification.

stories.title: Tomorrow_Blue C
stories.script: The artwork attempts to depict wishes and understanding through the rhythmic elements of spiky, elongated lines. Just as a composer writes music, this artist installed the space with the essences of blueness and rhythm, hoping lighthearted dreams would have the chance to flap their wings. The long-drawn-out lines of the iron fence not only tells the story of the area, but also reflects on the time of restless souls. Without feeling rushed, the free-spirited nature of the area, like the extended lines, is filled with much longed-for wishes and sorrow beyond words. Likewise, the stories of nature take a ride on the air and wind, appearing in the shape of wings. They hope to send a gesture of hope to all things, whether humans can achieve these hopes or not, flapping their feathers in their attempts.

stories.title: HELLO
stories.script: At the DMZ of Paju City that has tragic history, we can’t step forward.  The wall of harsh reality that we can’t meet each other, say hello to each other, proves how thick and far the line of division is.  We have to break the wall of pain and shouldn’t pass down it to the nest generation.  The efforts will begin with saying hello to each other.  My work asks after South and North Koreans.  “Hello, everyone”

stories.title: The Life Companion
stories.script: Love is a basic emotion of human and the key that holds people together.  Because of love we left behind, we miss some one, we want to keep them in ourselves and our hearts ache with miss.  You, who will be sharing love with us, I hope you are the life companion who will live together with warm hearts.

stories.title: Reconciliation
stories.script: People is Position that we should go.  My work expresses the tragedy of national division that has lasted 70 years and hope for reunification. It takes the shape of clasped hands so that it carries a strong message and represents Korean’s solidarity.

stories.title: Faction
stories.script: ‘Faction’ is containing imagination of positive hope through which is reproduced in photographic image of filming site of ‘JSA: Joint Security Area (2000)’ in KOFIC(Korea Film Council)Namyangju Studio. Panmujeom, where South and North Korean forces stand face-to-face, is ideological reality place of tension and surveillance. However, the set of JSA which is reproduced Panmunjeom for the movie is the place of reenact to develop the story. After filming the movie, it has become the place for fun to visitors. The original Panmunjeom, historic and ideological border is recreated as a set of the movie, and it deals with reproducing in a different meaning by reediting the ironic fake space. It creates the image of coexistence of United Korea, when the layer of metaphysical ‘imaginary’ puts on the image of reproduced fake Panmunjeom.

stories.title: Clo Face, Suki Face, W. Suki Face, Odie Face, Kiki Face, Candy Face
stories.audioTitle: Clo Face, Suki Face, W. Suki Face, Odie Face, Kiki Face, Candy Face Noh, Jun
stories.script: As a sculptor, I hope that my works can provide fun and joy. I create animal characters to give enjoyment and rest to the people. In a moment of rest, maybe people can find forgotten warmth through my works.

stories.title: No more, No more
stories.audioTitle: No more, No more Kim, Jihyun
stories.script: There is no border line in front of me.  Here and there, everywhere is filled with peaceful sunshine, scent of grass and the singing of birds.  There is the border line in front of me.  At the line, there are still many people suffering and latent fear continues.  If I can remove the line in front of me, my children will meet beautiful nature and the wide world without fear or pain.

stories.title: Visible Sound
stories.script: Movements of nature make sound with story.  The nature around the wire fences exists as life so I hear it loud and clear.  I think because there are more stories than I saw and heard.  I became the image in the space and expressed instinctual body movements in drawing.  The expression is delivered in multiple colors and it changes its colors by movements of nature (air, wind, rain etc.)  The narrow lines in drawing show minute movements. It will become visible sound and resonate gently.

stories.title: ‘Baraem, Baram’
stories.script: My work ‘Baraem, Baram’ was made by using a 3D printer. I tried to show our reality that we can’t move toward to each other. From north or south, wind moves freely through the wire fences and it touches our land, our hearts. The word ‘Baraem’ and ‘Baram’ were derived from ‘Barada’ which means wish and it is a play on words. (Baram has two meanings: hope, wind) I want to express our desire to reunification through the words ‘Barada’ and ‘Baram’. The word ‘Baraem’ is grammatically incorrect but I sure that the message is clear.

stories.title: Icon
stories.script: DMZ has long been a forbidden area so it allowed other species to thrive. Now DMZ turns itself into the area of peace and ecology.  I made relief of DMZ’s typical animals with cement and installed on the wire fences. I tried to imprint identity of the Echo Museum Street through it. A set of nine animals includes five species mammals (marten, musk deer, wild boar, goat and hare) and four species birds (spoonbill, mandarin duck, eagle owl and swan). Total of 18 relief sculptures are installed on the wire fences.  I hope that this work will be the icon of peace and natural environment.

stories.title: As like Dandelion Spores
stories.audioTitle: As like Dandelion Spores ROE, Dongshik
stories.script: When I watch wind-blowing dandelions in silence the word simplicity, gracility and delicacy pop up in my head. However, that delicate dandelion seeds pop out of the poor ground. Like them, I hope my work “As like Dandelion Spores…’ will fly to the sky and bud out. Unfortunately, it stuck in DMZ.

stories.title: The Scenery 19482014
stories.script: South and North Korea set up two separate governments in 1948. Korea has been divided ever since. I constructed the scenery after the division through several images of structures.  I rearranged the artificial structures that couldn’t have been built if we were one country into artificial scenery on the wire fences. I try to show similarities and differences in construction between two countries through each monument. Disharmony in natural environments that have been protected in the most heavily fortified border and artificial structures between them, I dream of artifact’s natural selection.

stories.title: DMZ(2014)
stories.script: This work is installation of the notes of the song ‘Our wish is reunification’ in the barbed wire fences. This song has tragedy of national division and our desire to reunification. I sang a lot when I was a child. To this day, my heart aches when I sing it. I wish the wire fences and the notes of ‘Our wish is reunification’ will be in the museum as a relic in the near future. I hope we have one free Korea.

stories.title: Friend, Enemy, Neutral and Unknown
stories.audioTitle: Friend, Enemy, Neutral and Unknown CHOI, Sungrok
stories.script: This work is inspired by military terms that separate the others (Friend, Neutral, Unknown and Enemy). At the division era, I consider how the others be distinguished and I have the words  ‘Love, Hate, So-so, Don’t Know ’for it. These words are reactions when you look the others.  It is expression about the others you love or hate or ignore. In this stuffy or boring area, I show meaningful and meaningless messages to people like simple text messages we send every day.

stories.title: Free Brainwashing
stories.script: ‘Our wish is reunification’ is the song I have long been singing from a child but our wish hasn’t happened yet.  Regardless of our desire, the wire fences across the middle of the Korean Peninsula still remain standing. One professor said that ‘It is not enough to just wish, prepare or imagine reunification’. We can’t see them (North Korea) with our own thought. No, we don’t see them. Reunification never made if we think our interest only.  I hung mirrors on the wire fences. Through the fences I can see the other side or myself. Between reality and desire, you will ask yourself ‘What have I tried for reunification?’, ‘Did I sing the song just because I was made to?’

stories.title: Paradise
stories.script: Paradise is used as a metaphysical or religious term for a positive utopia.  It is conceptually a counter-image of the supposed miseries of human existence and reality; in paradise there is only peace.  The word “Paradise” is inherited from an old Persian root as pairi.daêza-. The literal meaning of this word is “walled (enclosure)”, from pairi- “around”+-diz “to create (a wall)” or a walled garden, in Christian terms the Garden Eden.  The DMZ created a human free zone. Also it divides two concepts of reality.   The Paradise is the hidden Utopia, the otherworld on the opposite side. I use images painted by Jan Brueghel the elder and Peter Paul Rubens in 1615 and 1623 in combination with a photo of the forbidden fenced zone. The last picture also depicts the fall of man, the moment before the expulsion from Paradise.   The Slovenian philosopher Slavoj Žižek, who recently was appointed as a professor at Kyung Hee University, argues that people’s deepest motives are unconscious and that ideology functions as a justification for the existing social order and that reality is constructed through its representation within ideologies.  The proposed project leaves very much room for interpretations and I leave it to the viewer to find answers. The title Paradise will be cut out of the image, that observation trough the image is possible from both sides. The image will also be visible from both sides.

stories.title: Blooming Place
stories.script: Blooming Place, exists in the world but maybe not.

stories.title: Purple Door_2013
stories.script: ‘The only divided country in the world’, ‘Red complex’, ‘the restricted area for civilians’, ‘DMZ’, ‘Our wish is to be reunified’ and so on. These words have been used for a long time. How long will it be used? Red means north and blue means south. In the center of Taegeukgi, the flag of South Korea, is an red and blue circle. The upper part of circle is in red and the lower part is in blue like our divided land. Red and blue make purple. I built the doors to open wire fence. The slightly opened purple doors…

stories.title: Between
stories.script: Politics, ideology, security system, national security, etc. there are humans between them regardless of logic. It’s safe to say that the ideas about humans have been ruled out for many reasons on this land in the last centuries. From now on, interest in humans should be the first consideration. Between them, there we are.

stories.title: North and South Korea as One, One toward the World
stories.audioTitle: North and South Korea as One, One toward the World  KOH, Seung Kwan
stories.script: I hope it breaks old ideology, makes all of wire fence into art works and will be the first step to the world’s longest art road not the boundary between north and south. It is a shame about the size of work because of lack of time and many limitations.

stories.title: Picto_Nord / Sud
stories.script: To make reunified Korea, I tried to blend dirt of South and North Korea and color on it. But it remained uncompleted work because I couldn’t get North Korea’s dirt. I left South Korea with regret but expect the exhibition in next year and another works to be completed.

stories.title: My Wish, Your Wish, and Our Wish
stories.audioTitle: My Wish, Your Wish, and Our Wish YOO, Young Ho
stories.script: Sometimes I hum a song entitled ‘Our wish is to be reunified’. And then I ask myself why we can’t think about unification more simply and earnestly like this song. This work is asking you about our wish by focusing the word ‘wish’ from the song. The work has been completed by hanging locks on the text ‘My wish, Your wish, Our wish’ written on the wire fence.

stories.title: Way
stories.script: This illustration provides a question what the divided situation is about, and to imaginize future re-united nation on a local territory as well.

stories.title: My eyes watch me through your scenery
stories.audioTitle: My eyes watch me through your scenery Ayako Kurihara
stories.script: Parallel relationship between me and others disappear like the horizon between the sky and the ground. The lens on the wire shows the scenery beyond the wire fence distortedly, the mirror reflects me. The color of the sky that is reflected the ocean. The color of the grassland in the sun light. Like them, I am waiting the moment it becomes the one.

stories.title: An Aggregation_1309 | Gateway
stories.audioTitle: An Aggregation_1309 | Gateway PAHK, Seon Ghi
stories.script: As a vehicle of communication and interaction, door was the way to connects person to person and space to space. By building doors on the wire fence, the symbol of division and severance, I long for unification of South and North Korea.

stories.title: Flying Rubber Shoes of Peace
stories.audioTitle: Flying Rubber Shoes of Peace  by Seong, Yeon-gwi and Yang, Si-hoon
stories.script: As you can see in front of you, this art piece, created from rubber shoes and flip flap flowers, is one of the installation artworks chosen for exhibition in the civilian-controlled area along the barbed-wired fence. This piece was chosen during a competition for university students in 2010 for the first time. At that time, there were only three artworks installed on the trail as a trial project. However, this is the only one remaining of the three, as the other two pieces were removed due to deterioration. Old and worn rubber shoes and flip flap flowers are sometimes replaced by visitors. Please adjust the shoes so that the sprouts can flutter their wings.

stories.title: The Bridge
stories.script: This piece was created by eL Seed, a French-Tunisian artist, reinterpreting the poem “Unable to Forget” about love by Kim, Sowol, an early contemporary poet born in North Korea. Hoping for the reunification of North and South Korea after such a long separation, the artist depicted his own interpretation of the poem onto the barbed-wired fence. This artist is known for creating public artworks containing hopeful messages in areas of conflicts and poverty around the world, by combining ‘calligraphy,’ or the art of writing, with ‘graffiti,’ or the art of wall painting.   This project is his first artwork showcased in Korea. The whole piece required the installation of huge aluminum panels that were laser-processed. With Arabic calligraphy, he installed “Unable to Forget,” the poem by Kim, Sowol backwards, so it is difficult to read from the south, but people from the north are able to comprehend the words. Through his artwork, he sends the message that division and conflicts are not just the problems of North and South Korea, but all of us. So, we must work together, going beyond political and ideological differences and walk the path toward ultimate harmony and peace.

stories.title: The Message of Peace
stories.audioTitle: The Message of Peace  by eL Seed & 127 participants at Inseong, or the Character School of CJ Donors Camp
stories.script: This is a collaborative artwork between the artist eL Seed and the youth who participated in Inseong, or Character School of CJ Donors Camp, along with their university mentors.  Under the large umbrella theme of ‘peace’ and ‘harmony,’ participants chose subthemes for a total of ten wooden panels, and portrayed their ideals and hopes for peace. Some of the participants used Band-Aids and healing ointments in their artwork. With these Band-aids, they hoped to convey a message of hope for reconnecting the divided land and healing wounds. Since the separation, a long time has passed. However, children have demonstrated that their aspirations for peace on this land are as high as adults’ hopes. On top of these messages of hopes created by the participants, the theme is written in calligraphy, filled with the inspiration of eL Seed, and harmoniously depicted in the bright colors of hope.    The youth who participated in this art project had the chance to look deeper into the theme of “The Relationship of You, Me, and Us” at Inseong. Furthermore, by working with an artist who spread the message of peace not only at an individual level, but also throughout the country and the world, he hoped it would give them an opportunity to ultimately explore their own reasons why they need to live harmoniously, pursue peace and find their own answers independently. In addition, he hoped to send a message of hope, that peace and harmony for the youth of today is not just their problem, but a concern for all of us.

stories.title: Formex, Digital Printing
stories.script: Everyone has different hearts. All of the different hearts point the sky and carry everyone’s wish. The hand contains person’s heart as much as face. The hand faces the sky.

stories.title: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - Daegwallyeong Pass Service Area
stories.audioTitle: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - Daegwallyeong Pass Service Area
stories.script: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - Daegwallyeong Pass Service Area  The beginning of a windmill road  The windmill road on Seonjaryeong Pass, the first section of Bau-gil Road, boasts of beautiful scenery and various stories throughout. And above all, as Bau-gil Road is named after the goddess of health in Babylonian mythology and the rock, a symbol of strength, the first section will impress you with the wish for health and hope.  The windmill road is also the main ridge of the Baekdudaegan Mountain Range, and it receives the spirit of the mountain at the top. Here you can make your prayer. The scenery made with dozens of wind power plants and strong winds blowing at an annual average speed of 6.7m/s further empowers the greatness of the place. The first step up the first section of the Bau-gil Road, where the wind of hope and the wind of nature meet, will give you a pleasant experience.  Daegwallyeong Pass Service Area is located at the top of the Daegwallyeong Pass section of the old Yeongdong Expressway, which was an old way to Seoul. It seems that it is only about 15 kilometers from downtown Gangneung to the top of Daegwallyeong Pass, but the comfort of the rest area was quite great since the road was tough.  The place, which made us feel relieved that we had crossed all the Daegwallyeong Pass, has been a sharp decrease in traffic since the new road was built. It was closed for a while because it no longer needed the function of the rest area, but it is now operating again by reducing the scale. A wind power plant was built at the down line of the Daegwallyeong Pass Service Area, which is the starting point for section 1 of the Bau-gil Road.

stories.title: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - Route to Seonjaryeong Pass
stories.audioTitle: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - Route to Seonjaryeong Pass
stories.script: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - Route to Seonjaryeong Pass  A place where your eyes stay on exotic scenery  The summit of Seonjaryeong Pass, where we can say it is the peak of this road, is 1,157 m altitude, but the summit of Daegwallyeong Pass, the starting point, is also 850 m altitude, so there is no burden of climbing the mountain. It is literally a path walking along the spine of the Baedudaegan Mountain Range. The road leading to Sky Ranch after passing through Daegwallyeong Service Area is full of windbreak forests, perhaps the reason for blocking the wind.  This is why you will see lots of wind power generators here. The scenery where trees and windmills coexist while blocking and using the wind is interesting. Seonjaryeong Pass is prosperous with people enjoying snowflake trekking in winter when the silver snowy field is spectacular. But that doesn’t mean other seasons are not interesting. Various wildflowers bloom in the place where the snow melts, and grass grows in the sheep ranch, so you can also see sheep grazing.  The forest path leading to the ranch road is full of fir trees, nut pine trees, and broad-leaved trees, and the trees and green leaves rising straight toward the sky convey the feeling of movement that couldn’t be felt in winter. The path that forms the valley is full of natural songs such as the sound of water in the valley, the sound of birds chirping, and the sound of leaves rubbing against each other in the wind.  When you walk along the forest road and enter the Seonjaryeong Pass, you will be greeted with windmills located in a wide meadow and mountain ridges lined up under your feet. The scenery created by a flock of sheep, windmills, and meadows is both exotic and harmonious, so it is even amazing beyond the admiration.

stories.title: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - Seonjaryeong Pass Milestone
stories.audioTitle: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - Seonjaryeong Pass Milestone
stories.script: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - Seonjaryeong Pass Milestone  Standing in the Baekdudaegan Mountain Range  The milestone of the Seonjaryeong Pass on the Baekdudaegan Mountain Range indicates that you have reached the top of the Seonjaryeong Pass. If you have enjoyed the mountain enough, it is time to see the sea at a glance. As you walk a little bit more, you will reach Daegwallyeong Samyang Ranch Observatory, where you can look down the East Sea/ You will also see a panoramic view of Gangneung-si, which embraces the ocean. The horizon of the East Sea that seems to merge with the sky, the Yeongdong Expressway that seems to reach within your arms, and the mountains with clear contrast and shade like well-drawn ink paintings make your eyes busy.  As you are awestruck by these landscapes, it seems time flies like an arrow. But if you leave your regrets behind and walk again, the slope will be gentle, leading to a course where you can finish the road comfortably without getting tired. As you continue with your journey while enjoying the scenery, you will reach the Daegwallyeong Service Area, your starting point and destination.

stories.title: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - A Heart-captivating Route
stories.audioTitle: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - A Heart-captivating Route
stories.script: Windmill Road on Seonjaryeong Pass - A Heart-captivating Route  The starting point of the impressive Bau-gil Road  Section 1 of the Bau-gil Road is full of spectacles: extra-large wind power generators, a sheep ranch with a spacious meadow, Seonjaryeong Pass famous for trekking attraction, and Daegwallyeong Samyang Ranch Observatory where you can see a panoramic view of Gangneung-si, which embraces the ocean. The prelude of the Bau-gil Road is so intense that it raises the expectation for the next section to the fullest. Every section has its own attractive elements, but section 1 plays a very good role as an inducement to attract people’s hearts. Leave all your worries here on this road where the wind blowing from the Baekdudaegan Mountain Range cools your heart. Bring home the hope awarded to you by the wind.

stories.title: Entrance to the Old Daegwallyeong Trail
stories.audioTitle: Entrance to the Old Daegwallyeong Trail
stories.script: Entrance to the Old Daegwallyeong Trail  A road where the deity indwells  Jaegunggol Valley below the summit of the Daegwallyeong Pass is where people gather in a quiet forest on April 15th of the lunar calendar. During the festival, choheongwan, the person who serves the first cup, holds a memorial service to General Kim Yu-shin, the guardian of the Daegwallyeong Pass. Then, a ceremony to honor the Male Tutelary Deity follows. The shamans wash away injustice through splendid exorcism and ask the deity to come to the human world. Once this magical activity of exorcism is finished, sinmokjabi, the one who collects lumber blessed by gods, climbs a mountain to greet the deity and finds a maple tree that shakes slightly to cut it at its root since the shaking signals that the deity has sat down on it. Lumber blessed by gods are carefully wrapped with fabrics of five cardinal colors, and the procession of scholars and shamans is led by sinmokjabi who leads down the old road along with music. And, once the procession reaches the downtown Gangneung-si, humans begin a feast. As you can see, the Old Daegwallyeong Trail connecting gods and the people is the second section of the Bau-gil Road.  The Old Daegwallyeong Trail is protected by General Gim Yu-sin, the mountain spirit that guards the Yeongdong region, and Beomil Guksa, the Guksaseonghwangsin. It is the road that Sin Saimdang took on her way to Seoul together with young Yulgok Yi I do and the road that was governed by Songgang Jeong Cheol. It is also where Gim Hongdo laid out his painting tools and painted Daegwallyeongdo after he fell in love with the scenery of the streets and where countless poets and calligraphers dedicated their writings and drawings. Last but not least, the road holds the dreams of the Yeongdong people who moved to Seoul with big ambitions for success.

stories.title: Old Daegwallyeong Trail - Ninety-nine bends
stories.script: Old Daegwallyeong Trail - Ninety-nine bends  Scenic Site No. 74  The Old Daegwallyeong Trail is 832 m above sea level, and its length reaches 13 km. With as many as 99 bends, the trail was designated as the Scenic Spot No. 74 by the Cultural Heritage Administration. It was a meaningful trail for the people of Gangneung-si in many ways. The Old Daegwallyeong Trail was the most traffic-intensive and crucial pass among the Baekdudaegan Mountain Ranges, and had a huge gateway to Yeongdong. The name Daegwallyeong was also given in that meaning. The first section is a course that steps on the ridges while the second section is a course that reveals the deeper look of the mountain while walking along the valleys. This is because the valleys flowing in the mountain and the stems of the mountain are vivid.  Shrine to State Preceptor Tutelary Deity is the first thing you meet on the downhill road, which marks the beginning of the second section in earnest. While looking around the shrine, which exudes a spiritual aura even in the quiet forest, think about the Tale of Beomil Guksa. The Old Daegwallyeong Trail blessed by the gods protects the Daegwallyeong Pass and governs the Yeongdong area, and this makes the place holy and sacred as if stepping on the land of the gods.

stories.title: Old Daegwallyeong Trail - Wonurijae
stories.script: Old Daegwallyeong Trail - Wonurijae  A road that will make you keep looking back  At the end of the trail stands a strange bathroom in the shape of a spaceship, and this was where “Wonurijae, which means a pass where one would cry twice, was located. It was the pass where the magistrates would take to come to Gangneung-si, and they would cry because the pass was too rough to climb and cry again on their way back to their provinces because they felt sorrow. Although a rough road, your fatigue will be relieved, and as you walk a little more along the road that gives you a magnificent view, you will have to choose whether to finish the hike or continue. If you are exhausted, you can take the route in the direction of the Daegwallyeong Museum, where you only need to go 1.2 km more. If you are still craving for the charm of the old trail, you can take the opposite route.

stories.title: Old Daegwallyeong Trail - Downhill Road of Section 2
stories.audioTitle: Old Daegwallyeong Trail - Downhill Road of Section 2
stories.script: Old Daegwallyeong Trail - Downhill Road of Section 2  The path where mountain deities indwell  Daegwallyeong Pass  Look at that mountain covered with cold winds and white snow It seems to be waiting for spring to come, but it is still far away Look at that mountain burning with azalea and royal azalea Even the clouds are too shy to pause and then pass by The ninety-nine bends of the Daegwallyeong Pass Tell me to be a wanderer under drizzle A poet by Shin Bong-seung / Composed by Park Gyeong-gyu  The Old Daegywallyeong Trail is where mountain deities protecting the Yeongdong area lives and where it treasures the countless years and the stories of the pioneers. Section 2 of the Bau-gil Road was where dreamers used to cross and where the deities would have protected the precious dreams of humans.

stories.title: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - A Path of Pine Trees
stories.audioTitle: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - A Path of Pine Trees
stories.script: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - A Path of Pine Trees  A marvelous pine road  The third section is a little burdensome for beginners because you will have to cross a large mountain from the start. But the way to it will make your steps light as you are fascinated with the pine trees that spread throughout the trail. You will have to climb a quite steep mountain, so if you are out of breath, take a short breath in the middle of your journey. The Bau-gil Road is not there for you to conquer; instead, it serves as a resting place where you can relax your body and soul.  Although all sections of the Bau-gil Road are full of pine trees, the pine trees of the third section seem to tell exceptionally many stories. Pine trees live for a thousand years. And every person has their own story. Have you ever wondered how many stories each tree has? You will be amazed by the majesty of pine trees that have grown densely enough to cover the sky, but the old, wounded pine trees that have grown in different shapes and that have split rocks and rooted in them are more noticeable.

stories.title: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Wounded Pine Trees
stories.audioTitle: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Wounded Pine Trees
stories.script: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Wounded Pine Trees  An oak bark and resin  People say that the peeled pine trees would be traces of building houses with an oak bark roof. Usually, oak bark is used to build a house, but the bark of pine trees is also used as well. The pine trees, which are round or partially peeled with their bare skin exposed, are full of scratches inside, and this means that people back then used to extract resin from pine trees. It was only 40 years ago when people actively collected resin, and the oil extracted from the resin was used as fuel for combat planes or exported.  Pine trees helped invigorate the country’s economy by being used as materials for house-building and fuels and through export. Sacrificed by the human's cruelty, they were left empty inside and couldn’t grow upright. Their wounds from the cuts have healed themselves, and this is how the pine trees lived throughout hundreds of years.

stories.title: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Eomyeongjeong Pavilion
stories.audioTitle: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Eomyeongjeong Pavilion
stories.script: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Eomyeongjeong Pavilion  This is the King's command!  After climbing the steep uphill three or four times, an elegant pavilion will catch your attention from the distance. It is the Eomyeongjeong Pavilion, which was built on the site where pine trees were cut down by the King’s command. When you climb the pavilion, you will see a phrase saying, “A pine tree that received a King’s command,” which has only stumps left on the glass floor. Looking down from the pavilion, you could see the scenery of that day more than a decade ago.  The 150-year-old Geumgang pine trees grew 94 cm in diameter and 25 m in length. The single timber was priced more than 8 million won in 2007. The Cultural Heritage Administration found, in the middle of the Geumgang pine trees of the Baekdudaegan Mountain Range, a girder for the restoration of the  Gwanghwamun Palace and carefully logged them after holding a memorial service.  There are about 200,000 Geumgang pine trees that can be used to restore cultural properties in Korea, and they are one of the world’s best species boasting of robustness and anti-rot features. Symbolizing pure native species, the Geumgang pine trees grow more than three times slower and straighter than ordinary pine trees, and they feature red stems and skin. The fact that you can walk on the road lined with the Geumgang pine trees for nearly four hours comes as a unique charm of the Bau-gil Road, and no other places will give you such experience.

stories.title: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Suljanbawi Rock
stories.audioTitle: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Suljanbawi Rock
stories.script: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Suljanbawi Rock  The pleasantness given by nature  Next to the Eomyeongjeong Pavilion, there is a path that leads to Suljanbawi Rock. You have to climb another steep mountain for about a kilometer. At the end of the steep ridge, a flat path spreads out as if to catch a breath for a while, and soon comes Metdwaeji Rest Area, a playground and food warehouse for wild boars.  As you walk a little further after passing through the dense pine forest, there is a groove of a similar size, where it seems to be a place where people would have enjoyed drinking on a wide rock. On top of it, there is the Suljanbawi Rock that resembles a well-served drinking table with a slightly larger groove that seems like where a kettle would be placed. You can catch your breath for a moment with a sip of cool water at the Suljanbawi Rock while watching a scenery of wind power generators turning slowly along the ridge of the Daegwallyeong Pass and clouds passing through.  After passing the Suljanbawi Rock, the roads that go down now spread out, making a little easier steps. Around the time the forest road comes out, the view of a wide vacant lot with a watchhouse for a forest fire is the highlight, and you can see to the east the downtown of Gangneung-si and the East Sea. To the south is the mountain range of the Daegwallyeong Pass.  Along the path, royal azaleas and azaleas comfort you in spring, wildflowers show off each other’s beauty in summer, and silver grasses blend in the pine forest in autumn. The path boasts different attractions from season to season.

stories.title: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Road to the Tomb of King Myeongjugun
stories.audioTitle: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Road to the Tomb of King Myeongjugun
stories.script: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Road to the Tomb of King Myeongjugun  Towards the stories of a thousand years  When you come down the road, you will arrive at the Tomb of King Myeongjugun, the final destination, and this is the tomb of Kim Ju-won, the fifth-generation descendant of King Taejong Muyeol of Silla and the founder of the Gangneung Kim Clan. The tomb retains a thousand years of history like a pine tree. After you see around from Sunguijae Shrine—which enshrines the ancestral tablet of Kim Ju-won who was raised by King Myeongjugun after being pushed out of the throne battle with King Wonseong of Silla—to the tomb, the journey of the 3rd section of the Bau-gil Road ends.  Perhaps because of the positive energy emitted by pine trees, the story of a thousand years passed down the road brings a deep impression and emotion to the heart. The 3rd section of the Bau-gil Road is a road with a deep echo that fills the body and mind.

stories.title: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Tomb of King Myeongjugun
stories.audioTitle: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Tomb of King Myeongjugun
stories.script: Tomb of King Myeongjugun - Tomb of King Myeongjugun  A man who could not become a king  The 4th section of the Bau-gil Road starts from the Tomb of King Myeongjugun to Haesari Village, famous for fatsia shoots, and Hangwa Village to Hapyeong plains and reaching the Sacheon Beach Park. It is an 18.3 km-long road from the Baekdudaegan Mountain Range to the East Sea.  The Tomb of King Myeongjugun is the tomb of Kim Ju-won, who tried to ascend to the throne but had to leave as a lord of Myeongju due to the floodwater. The tomb is the starting point for the 4th and 10th sections and also serves as the ending point of the 3rd section.
