This well-kept royal tomb makes it a suitable place for many people to gather and start. The 4th section is a course that departs from the Tomb of King Myeongjugun and descends to the east along the forest road. Large pine trees become your friends along the way down the pretty wide forest road. You will meet the Sacheon Haesari Village at the end of the road.  Sagimak Village has been called Haesari Village since some time ago. It is said that acorus is called haesari grass because they grow well just by the sunlight, and it is also named Haesari by calling haedabipul because they are medicinal herbs that become excellent solution to treat various symptoms. Haesari Village is said to be originated from acorus.

stories.title: Sacheon Dukbang-gil - Haesari Village
stories.script: Sacheon Dukbang-gil - Haesari Village  Sagmak, Sagimak  The original name of Haesari Village is Sagimak-ri. It had been called Sagmak and Sagimak since there was a mud hut for baking porcelain more than 200 years ago, and it is said that broken pieces of porcelain appear when digging the ground even until today.  The porcelain maksabal made in Haesari Village was sometimes loved as a drinking glass to soothe the joys and sorrows of the commoners and sometimes as a rice bowl when serving food to workers at rice fields. Maksabal made from Sagimak has gone now, the most popular specialty of Haesari Village these days is fatsia shoots. In spring, green-colored fatsia shoots sprout out their heads at the end of each branch with pointed thorns. There are about 100,000 fatsia shoot trees in Haesari Village and a fatsia shoot festival is held every spring. In particular, fatsia shoots produced here are so popular nationwide. With its excellent quality highly recognized, fatsia shoot was registered as Geographical Indication No. 41 by the Korea Forest Service.  Fatsia shoots, which refer to the fresh shoots of thorny ash trees, have an excellent little bitter taste so that it is by far the best to stimulate appetite in spring. They are delicious to eat raw after slightly blanching and even in a griddled pancake because of their fragrance. It is said that the elderly in the village often used to make doorposts by weaving thorny branches of fatsia shoots and hanging them on the door. They believed that doing this will get their family rid of evil spirits.

stories.title: Sacheon Dukbang-gil - Galgol Hangwa Village
stories.script: Sacheon Dukbang-gil - Galgol Hangwa Village  A place that maintains the taste of tradition  Sacheon Dukbang-gil is a path along the embankment of Sacheon from the time you leave the field of fatsia shoots. You can see a signboard of Galgol Hangwa Village on the other side of the road while looking at the stream and walking with pussy willows on the embankment.  Nodong-ri, Sacheon-myeon was called Galgol because of many reeds, but it has become more famous for Sacheon Hangwa Village and Gwajul Village these days. Just 30 years ago, it was an ordinary rural village for farming, but now the entire village revamped itself into Gwajul Village, which makes hangwa, or traditional Korean sweets, by keeping the technology of the tradition that has been passed down from 130 years ago.  In Sacheon, hangwa is not fried in oil but clean sand and is heated and fried. The secret to maintaining the unique taste of Gangneung Gwajul (gwajul, referring to a Korean biscuit) and the core of the manufacturing technology is constantly preserving the traditional biscuit making method, ingredients, and inflating technology. Sacheon Hangwa, which is more suitable for the old name gwajul than the name hangwa, is popular as a holiday gift because it has a unique texture that melts as soon as you take a bite, although its appearance is somewhat rough.

stories.title: Sacheon Dukbang-gil - Aeildang Village
stories.script: Sacheon Dukbang-gil - Aeildang Village  Following the traces of Heo Gyun  Passing the Sacheon Gwajul Village and crossing the passageway under National Road No. 7, there is a rare vast field in Gangneung-si. Called the Hapyeong plain, it is a representative rice production place in Gangneung-si. Golden waves roll through the plain in autumn. After passing the Hapyeong Village, you will meet the village of “Aeildang'', where the birthplace and house of Gyosan Heo Gyun’s maternal grandparent was located. There are only a few fields and farms now, and there is no way to find any traces of Aeildang.  The place where Aeildang was located is said to be one of the best places that inherited the spirit of Odaesan Mountain. Heo Gyun’s maternal grandfather, Kim Gwang-cheol, had only a daughter without a son; his son-in-law and daughter were prohibited from sleeping in Aeildang before he got a son.  However, Heo Gyun’s parents slept in Aeildang to avoid the eyes of their father-in-law, giving birth to Heo Gyun’s older brother Heo Bong, sister Heo Nanseolheon, and, finally, Heo Gyun. Therefore, stories say that the spirit of the great place that the Gangneung Kim clan was supposed to be born with was transferred to the Yangcheon Heo clan.  There is a “Monument to Gyosan” on the hill behind the site of Aeildang, where you can find traces of Heo Gyun. The monument, however, is not easy for first-timers to find because it is surrounded by bamboo forests on all sides. The Monument of Heo Gyun is engraved with a poem called Nusilmyeong, which is believed to have been written around his age of 40. Once you arrive at the monument, the East Sea will be captured at a glance. It seems like the memories that Heo Gyun recalled before his death were the ones of his hometown, Aeildang, where the blue sea overflowed and where he spent his childhood days.

stories.title: Gate of Gangneung Guesthouse - Gangneung-si Outside of the Dongdaemun Gate
stories.audioTitle: Gate of Gangneung Guesthouse - Gangneung-si Outside of the Dongdaemun Gate
stories.script: Gate of Gangneung Guesthouse - Gangneung-si Outside of the Dongdaemun Gate  The pride of the people of Gangneung-si  There is an old saying that there is Gangneung-si outside of the Dongdaemun Gate. The people of Gangneung-si used to mention this to mean that Gangneung-si is the best place to live outside of the Dongdaemun Gate. From this, we can feel that the pride of the Gangneung people was high. The trail to the Gulsansa Temple of the Bau-gil Road 6th section is the longest 18.8 km course. On this route, you can witness the history and culture of the city starting from Namhangjin Beach through the Jungang Market with plentiful foods to the Haksan Village where Beomil Guksa was born. In other words, the Bau-gil Road 6th section is the way to confirm the reputation of Gangneung-si outside of the Dongdaemun Gate.  The road, which started on the first section of Seonjaryeong Pass, is designed to naturally encounter the mountains, sea lakes, and forest of Gangneung-si all throughout. However, after the 5th section, the trail is blocked from Namhangjin where the 6th section starts and this is because of an airfield. Therefore, the 6th section was designed to boldly pass through downtown Gangneung-si and head to Haksan-ri. It is a special path where you can encounter the true side of the city.  If you start from Namhangjin in the morning and walk up along the Namdaecheon Embankments, you will reach the Gangneung Jungang Market by the time you get hungry. In addition to fresh seafood and agricultural products, there are a variety of foods available—potato pancakes, buckwheat pancakes, and beef head meat and rice soup—so that you can choose from whatever suits you. As you walk slowly after enjoying the delight of seeing and eating at the Jungang Market, you will soon reach the downtown Gangneung-si.

stories.title: Gate of Gangneung Guesthouse - Gate of Gangneung Guesthouse
stories.audioTitle: Gate of Gangneung Guesthouse - Gate of Gangneung Guesthouse
stories.script: Gate of Gangneung Guesthouse - Gate of Gangneung Guesthouse  Fall in love with entasis  There is a place where you can see for your eyes the history and culture of Gangneung-si. A place that is mingled with the Chilsadang Government Office that shrines the Dano ancestral tablet and a guesthouse centering around the restored Gangneung Local Government Office, the former site of Gangneung City Hall.  You shouldn't miss out a treasure of this place: entasis of Gangneung Guesthouse. The pillars of the guesthouse, which boast the perfect technique of entasis with a bulging middle and a narrow top and bottom, are known as the thickest wooden pillars in Korea. When I was young, I had no idea of the exact meaning of entasis columns and the historical significance of the guesthouse. To me, they were just thick pillars, and my grandmother would scold my sister, saying “don't go around showing your legs looking like the pillars of the guesthouse” whenever she saw my sister in short pants. I sometimes visit Imyeonggwan Guesthouse to carefully look at the pillars, and whenever I look at them, I think of my grandmother’s voice.

stories.title: Jeongdongjin Time Museum
stories.script: Jeongdongjin Time Museum  We are now at the Jeongdongjin Time Museum, which consists of an 8-car locomotive. It displays everything about time in a fun way.  How do you feel about one minute? It’s a short time to do anything, but it sometimes feels long, does it not? Time may be invisible, and each person feels it differently, but at least it's constant for everyone.  We humans have sought constant movement” to express time accurately. At the Jeongdongjin Time Museum, you can learn about the birth of time and its development as well as the logic behind the constant movement through diverse exhibitions.  They have a variety of clocks on display including an exquisite clock from the Medieval Period, a pocket watch that stopped the moment Titanic sank, a clock made entirely of wood, and the world's biggest bicycle clock made by a mathematician.  Make memories in the photo zones found all over the exhibition space. If you go up to the observation deck on the roof of the last car, you can enjoy a panoramic view of ​​Jeongdongjin beach.

stories.title: Jeongdongjin Hourglass Park
stories.script: Jeongdongjin Hourglass Park   Which train station is closest to the beach in the world? It's Jeongdongjing station. It used to be a small stop for transporting coal but became Korea's top tourist attraction after a Korean drama, the Hourglass, was filmed there. Aired on television in 1995, the Hourglass is considered one of the highest-rating TV productions in Korean drama history. With the growing popularity of the drama, the location became a popular tourist spot for sunrise viewing. Hourglass Park, located south of Jeongdongjin station, was established in 1999 to celebrate both the success of the drama and the new millennium. It features the world's largest hourglass, which takes a full year for all the sand in the clock to fall. When the sand runs out at midnight on January 1, the clock spins as a new year starts. Behind the hourglass is the world's largest sundial. The angle, the gnomon, and the earth show the geographic latitude of the Jeongdongjin, and the gnomon is always parallel to the Earth's axis. The shadow cast by the gnomon on the semi-circle sundial shows the time. A sundial is known to be very accurate, at least when there's bright sunlight. Visit the landmark of Jeongdongjin and create timeless memories.

stories.title: Anbandegi
stories.script: Anbandegi  The village of Anbandegi, situated in a highland area at about 1,100 meters above sea level, boasts the biggest highland vegetable farms in Korea. The area is called Anbandegi because the village's topography, which is wide and deep across the ridge, is said to look like an anban, in other words, a flat wooden board used to pound rice cakes on. ‘Degi’ is Gangwon dialect for a hill.  Anbandegi looks flat from a distance, but it's actually made up of steep slopes. The first people to settle here were the slash-and-burn farmers who cleared the stony land and cultivated crops, eventually founding a village and expanding the farmland. They transformed this once barren place into the fertile land we can see today.  At the Meong-e Observatory are walls made of rocks that were removed from a nearby field and a stone monument shaped like a meong-e (the stick that is placed around the neck of a cow so it can pull a plow) that was erected to commemorate the slash-and-burn farmers. From the Meong-e Observatory you can see a picturesque landscape formed by an emerald-green cabbage field at the edge of the ocean and snowy wind turbines. The sun rises over the sea of clouds above the fields in the morning, and the Milky Way brightens the night sky. You can enjoy the serene landscape even more if you walk along the narrow trail in between the fields of ripe cabbage.

stories.title: Jeongdong-simgok Badabuchae-gil Trail
stories.audioTitle: Stroll along this beautiful beach as the waves roll in
stories.script: Jeongdong-simgok Badabuchae-gil Trail Stroll along this beautiful beach as the waves roll in   Jeongdong-simgok Badabuchae-gil Trail is a 2.9-kilometer-long walking path along the beach. It receives its name from its location and shape of the land along the trail. “Jeongdong” refers to the eastward direction from the residence of the king in Hanyang, or present-day Seoul, which was the capital during the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910). “Simgok” refers to a village that is located inside a deep valley. Badabuchae-gil, or fan-shaped road, comes from the rock formations on the trail that resemble an open fan facing the sea.  Begin your journey from the ticket office and go down a set of steep wooden stairs to arrive at the trail, where you’ll be greeted by a breathtaking view of the coast. The nearby coastal terrace has a stepped landscape that follows the coastline. The seaside cliffs were carved by waves, which created protrusions and recessions along the surface. This created a flat, terraced surface with a gradual incline towards the sea that rises above the water. The fan-shaped rock formation is designated as Natural Monument No. 437. It’s the only coastal terrace in the country, and offers a glimpse of 23 million years of geological history.  You can expect to have a splendid view of the sea as you continue on your walk, eventually arriving at Mongdol Beach. Here, the mongdol, or round stones, including a turtle-shaped rock and a rock that looks like a soldier's helmet, have been shaped by the waves. The soldier's helmet formation stands in tribute to the legend of the great general Gang Gam-chan (948-1031) of the Goryeo Dynasty (918-1392), who was said to have defeated tigers that were threatening the local villagers.  The next stop is the fan-shaped rock observation deck. It’s built on top of a rock shaped like an open fan, and offers a view of the trail, where we started our tour. The final destination is Simgok Sea Observation Deck, which presents a stunning view of the ocean and is where visitors may feel as if they are floating above the water.

stories.title: Jeongdong-Simgok Badabuchae Trail
stories.script: Jeongdong-Simgok Badabuchae Trail  Jeongdong-Simgok Badabuchae Trail is a 2.86 kilometer section of the path connecting Jeongdongjin Station to the village of Simgok. It is named Badabuchae Trail because the local topography is said to resemble an open fan facing the ocean when seen from a bird's eye point of view. The Badabuchae Trail has been designated as Natural Monument No.437 in recognition of its status as the largest coastal terrace in Korea. A coastal terrace is a stepped slope formed where a sea cliff, with a wave-cut platform before it, is raised above sea level after many years of erosion and weathering. This coastal terrace was formed about 230 million years ago, but the hidden landscape was only revealed when the trail was created. If you follow the Badabuchae Trail, you will eventually arrive at Mongdol Beach, where pine trees rooted in rocks and red beach roses catch the eye and enchant the spirit. You will also come face to face with many strangely shaped rocks and stones, each the subject of a different folk legend. After that you could head along to the Jeongdong-Simgok Badabuchae Trail either from the parking lot of the Jungdongjin Sun Cruise Resort or from Simgok Port. Immerse yourself in Mother Nature’s mysteries by walking along the Jeongdong-Simgok Badabuchae Trail, the closest path to the ocean.

stories.title: Helmet Rock
stories.script: Helmet Rock  Can you see the rock rising above sea level? What do you think it looks like? Some people call it “Helmet Rock” because it looks like the head of a general wearing a helmet. Legend has it that long ago, there was a six-toed tiger at Bamjae Hill that transformed itself into a monk and attacked the local villagers. In those days there was only one route to Gangneung, which passed through Bamjae, so many people were killed by the tiger. One day, General Gang Gam-chan came to Gangneung to take up his post as the city’s newly appointed prefect. Gang was a renowned military commander of Goryeo who defeated the Khitans in the early eleventh century. The villagers pleaded with him to make Bamjae safe to travel, and Gang wrote a letter and had it delivered to the monk, who was actually the man-eating tiger, ordering him to leave the district immediately. After receiving the threatening letter, the tiger, who already knew about the prefect’s reputation, ran away taking his packs with him, and Bamjae was freed of its fear of the tiger. Several versions of this legend are transmitted orally in the Gangneung area. The Helmet Rock facing the East Sea reminds many people of the brave general who protected his people.

stories.title: Buchae Rock
stories.script: Buchae Rock  This rock is called “Buchae (fan) Rock,” because it is shaped like an open fan. In fact, the Jeongdong-Simgok Badabuchae Trail was named after this rock. If you follow the trail around the rock you will eventually come to an observatory where you can see all the sights on the scenic trail from a distance.   There is also a legend about this rock. A long time ago, an old man from the village of Simgok dreamed about a lady near Buchae Rock who implored him to save her. So the next day he got in his boat and sailed out to the rock, where he salvaged a crate containing the lady’s portrait. He felt sorry for her and left the painting on the rock, and everything went well with him after that. One night, the lady appeared to him once again in his dream. The old man brought the painting to the village and built a Seonandang in which to enshrine it. “Seonang” means a village guardian, while a Seonangdang is a shrine built to honor a Seonang. It may surprise you to hear that the portrait enshrined in the Seonangdang is said to be as new now as it was when it was first placed there. The villagers thus came to believe in the guardian, and even today they often visit Seonangdang to pray for good luck whenever something important comes up in the village.

stories.title: Haslla Art World
stories.audioTitle: Sweeping seaside views complement indoor and outdoor galleries
stories.script: Haslla Art World Sweeping seaside views complement indoor and outdoor galleries   Haslla Art World is an outdoor museum set in the midst of the mountains and the sea. The sculptors and couple, Park Shin-jeong and Choi Ok-young, built this museum in Jeongdongjin on a slope overlooking the ocean. It is not only a gallery for the arts but a place where visitors can relax and enjoy the beauty of nature.  Haslla Art World is an outdoor museum set in the midst of the mountains and the sea. The sculptors and couple, Park Shin-jeong and Choi Ok-young, built this museum in Jeongdongjin on a slope overlooking the ocean. It is not only a gallery for the arts but a place where visitors can relax and enjoy the beauty of nature. Haslla Art World is a kind of art garden made by artists themselves. It was christened after the traditional name of the Gangneung region. The indoor museum has a variety of exhibits, including one on the beloved fictional character Pinocchio and another featuring several stringed and jointed marionette puppets created in the European style.  At Café Hangsang, located just outside the museum, visitors can enjoy a cup of tea with a view of the ocean. There are two roads in front of the café that lead to the outdoor gallery. Seongseong “Broadleaf” Road passes through a wooded area filled with many broad-leaved trees. The name “Seongseong” comes from the Korean expression “seolleong seolleong,” which means “slowly and gently.” Seaside Garden Road takes visitors through the sculptures that are on display in the Seaside Garden, which has an “ocean” theme. The Sky Observation Deck above the garden road offers a splendid view of the artworks against the backdrop of the sea.  The Sky Observation Deck leads to the Stone Gallery, the Cow Dung Art Gallery and Pine Tree Garden. Inside the Stone Gallery, large stones are suspended in the air, giving them an otherworldly quality. Pine Tree Garden, made up of a dense grove of pine trees, is a work of art created by Mother Nature. The outdoor galleries were built to conform to the height and slope of the mountain in order to minimize the damage to the environment. When walking through these outdoor spaces, visitors might feel like they, too, are a part of nature.  In addition to these attractions, there are several programs for visitors to enjoy, such as marionette-making workshops, coffee tastings and cookie-baking classes.

stories.title: Haslla Art World
stories.script: 43. Haslla Art World  A building towers over the sea in Jeongdongjin. It’s called ‘Haslla Art World.’ The word Haslla is derived from a pure Korean word with no corresponding Chinese characters. It is the old name of Gangneung from the Goguryeo era. Occupying an area of 81 acres, Haslla Art World provides a magnificent ocean view from both inside and outside.   Land art refers to the works of art embodying the artist's imagination associated with Mother Nature. Haslla Art World itself is built against the sea backdrop, allowing the people inside to interact with the ocean from anywhere with the concept of land art in mind. The interior of the museum is divided into a contemporary art gallery and a space with kinetic art works, called the “Pinocchio and Marionette Museum.” Works of art that use natural or mechanical energy to move are called ‘kinetic’ art. There are puppets like Pinocchio and marionette dolls for visitors to try and play with.  Haslla Art World is a cultural and artistic complex. Aside from art galleries, there are many other facilities including cafes, restaurants, and hotel. Moreover, the mountain on which the building stands features a broad sculpture park. Take a walk and enjoy art with the sky, woods, and sea as backdrop. You will feel one with nature.

stories.title: Gangneung Coffee Street
stories.audioTitle: Ocean views lend an aura of romance to a stretch of coffee roasteries
stories.script: Gangneung Coffee Street Ocean views lend an aura of romance to a stretch of coffee roasteries   Anmok Beach is a favorite among couples on romantic outings who want to enjoy a cup of coffee by the sea. The coastal road spans 500 meters, beginning from the entrance of Gangneung Harbor to Anmok Sunrise Park, and there are more than 20 cafés set up along the beach.  In the 1980s, Anmok Beach was famously called a street café because several coffee vending machines were placed along the beach. It was a favorite haunt for couples who came to enjoy the view of the ocean along with a small cup of coffee. Although it came from a vending machine, rumor had it that it tasted like fine coffee thanks to the lovely seaside surroundings. Gradually, the vending machines were replaced by cafés serving freshly brewed coffee, leading to the coffee street that it’s become today.  The cafés along the coastal road are each filled with the fragrant aromas of their own signature blends. The shops include roasteries run by talented professionals, as well as famous café franchises. All of the fine establishments are decorated with handsome façades and lovely interiors and decked with seaside windows so that customers can enjoy their coffee while gazing out at the ever-changing view of the ocean. If you want to step outside for some fresh air, you can take your coffee to go and stroll along the shore. Or find a spot on the beach and feel the breeze as you sip your coffee and enjoy the charming seaside location.

stories.title: Gangneung coffee Street
stories.script: Gangneung coffee Street  Known as “Coffee City” in Korea, Gangneung has the highest number of coffee shops per person in the country. A street lined with coffee shops releasing coffee aroma into the air became a symbol of Gangneung. The start of Gangneung's coffee was a coffee vending machine in Anmok Street in a small fishing village in the 1980s. People who heard by word of mouth that they can enjoy tasty coffee and enjoy an ocean view with just a few coins started to visit the area. On top of that, the number of cafes ballooned after the year 2000 as famous brewers who led the coffee culture in Korea began to settle in Gangneung. Unlike most café chains, each coffee shop has unique flavor and aroma, making it a mecca for both tourists and coffee aficionados. Anmok Beach, now dubbed Café Street, is a must-see tourist spot.  Since 2009, the very first coffee festival in Korea has been held each year, bringing in more tourists. Gangneung deserves to be called the Coffee City of Korea, does it not?

stories.title: 2018 PyeongChang House
stories.script: 2018 PyeongChang House Become a Winter Olympics expert   The 2018 PyeongChang House can be found in front of the Gangneung Green City Experience Center. It provides a wide range of information about the Olympic events, and documents the activities that helped bring the 2018 Winter Olympics to Pyeongchang County.  The Olympic mascots Soohorang and Bandabi greet visitors at the entrance to the Promotional House. Soohorang, a white tiger that symbolizes Korea, is the mascot for the PyeongChang Winter Olympic Games. “Sooho” is the Korean word for “protection,” because the safety of the Olympic athletes, participants and guests is of the utmost importance. “Rang” comes from the Korean word for “tiger” and also refers to “Jeongseon Arirang,” the most famous folk song in Gangwon-do Province. Meanwhile, the mascot for the PyeongChang Paralympic Winter Games is Bandabi, an Asiatic black bear that symbolizes Korea and Gangwon-do Province. Bandabi represents courage and strength of will. The name comes from the Korean words “ban-dal”, or “half-moon” like the crescent shape on the Asiatic black bear’s chest, and “bi” which refers to commemorating the competition. Bandabi cheers on the paralympic athletes who push themselves beyond their own limits.  Once inside, you can see the card used by Jacques Rogge, the former president of the International Olympic Committee, to announce Pyeongchang as the next host of the Winter Olympic Games. Life-like sculptures depict athletes from each Olympic sport in dynamic poses, gripping ski poles and wearing goggles, helmets and other accessories that were used by former and current members of the national teams.  A wide range of exhibits and videos offer a detailed look at the 15 categories and 102 events planned for the PyeongChang Winter Olympics. Docents can also provide visitors with explanations to help them better understand the preparations that went into the Winter Games, including how the sports facilities and emblems were created.  On top of all this, you can even try your hand at ice hockey shooting. And the 4D Experience Hall next door lets you use realistic VR simulations to get a taste of some of the Olympic events for yourself, like ski jumping, bobsleighing and alpine skiing.

stories.title: Seongyojang House in Gangneung
stories.audioTitle: Experience 300 years of history in a traditional Korean house
stories.script: Seongyojang House in Gangneung Experience 300 years of history in a traditional Korean house   Among traditional Korean houses, or hanok, Seongyojang is a particularly well-preserved estate that was once the residence of the aristocratic family of Lee Nae-beon (1703-81). Lee lived during the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910) and was a descendent of Prince Hyoryeong (1396-1486), who was the second oldest brother of King Sejong the Great (1397-1450). Lee was said to have stumbled upon this location after chasing a weasel into the forest. He decided to build the house after being enamored of the beautiful surroundings. At the time, the house stood in front of Lake Gyeongpoho, making it accessible by boat. Its proximity to the lake gave it its name, Seongyojang, which literally means boat bridge house.  Let's take a look around the estate. The tour begins at Hwallaejeong Pavilion, which sits over a lotus pond and lies just outside the main compound. From here, you can see the old servants’ quarters, which form part of the outer wall. To the right of the main entrance stand the main living quarters of the Lee family and the east wing guest room called Dongbyeoldang. To the left is Yeolhwadang, where the male owner of the estate resided. Yeolhwadang got its name from the poem Returning Home by the Chinese poet Tao Yuanming. It has an elegant terrace, which was a gift from the Russian legation and is made in a Russian style.  Two other facilities, the Seongyojang House Museum and Daily Living Artifact Exhibition, contain approximately 500 relics offering a glimpse into how the aristocracy once lived. Visitors can also experience life in a traditional Korean house through a hanok stay and a variety of other programs including a tea ceremony, calligraphy workshop and ink-rubbing activities.

stories.title: Byeongbangsan County Park (Skywalk and Zip Wire)
stories.audioTitle: Spectacular views await those who venture to this mountain pass
stories.script: Byeongbangsan County Park (Skywalk and Zip Wire) Spectacular views await those who venture to this mountain pass   Byeongbangchi is an uphill pass that connects Gyulam-ri Village and the town of Jeongseon-eup. Area residents once used this pass to travel to and from Jeongseon-eup before the road was built in 1979. It is also referred to as Arari Pass because of its resemblance to the winding road in Jeongseon’s regional variation of the famous Korean folk song “Arirang.”  The skywalk, which is the area's most important landmark, is located on a 538-meter-high cliff on the side of Byeongbangsan Mountain. Shaped like a horse's hoof, the skywalk is made with reinforced glass, offering a dizzying view of the landscape below. Even the guardrail is made of glass, making visitors feel as if they are floating in the air. The skywalk offers a picturesque view of the Donggang River flowing around Bamseom, an island shaped like the Korean Peninsula.  The zip wire is another tourist attraction for which Byeongbangchi has become well known. It’s connected to the skywalk via a wooden deck and begins at an elevation of 607 meters. Visitors who take the ride can travel at speeds of up to 120 kilometers per hour all the way to Gwangha-ri Donggang Eco Experience Center. The exciting ride takes you over a distance of 1.1 kilometers, making it a popular choice with young travelers.

stories.title: Hwaam Palgyeong (The Eight Scenic Sites of Hwaam)
stories.audioTitle: Natural beauty in the form of deep caves, flowing water and stone pillars
stories.script: Hwaam Palgyeong (The Eight Scenic Sites of Hwaam) Natural beauty in the form of deep caves, flowing water and stone pillars   Southeast of Jeongseon-gun County in Gangwon-do Province lies Hwaam-myeon, a land of tall mountains and clear rivers. It is famous for its eight natural locations known as the Hwaam Palgyeong, or the Eight Scenic Sites of Hwaam. They can be found along Sogeumgang-ro Road, beginning at Jeongseon-eup Deokwoo Intersection. Now, let's take a closer look at these wonders of nature.  Our journey begins with Hwaam Cave (Scenic Site No. 4). This was once a commercial gold mine whose mine shafts and natural stalactites now offer a cave exploration experience that is unique in the country. From here, the road leads to Hwaam Mineral Spring (Scenic Site No. 1). Along the way, you can see Yongmaso Lake (Scenic Site No. 3), a pool of clear water rippling around wide, flat rocks. If you go further from here, you will see a large rock that is shaped like a crawling turtle. This is the Turtle Rock (Scenic Site No. 2), and it sits on the edge of a steep cliff.  Next, you will pass Hwaam Mineral Spring and arrive at Hwayang 2-gyo where you will find Hwapyoju Cliff (Scenic Site No. 5). On this cliff, two stone pillars stand side by side like the horns of a goblin. From here, the road takes you to Sogeumgang (Scenic Site No. 6), which in turn leads to Molundae Cliff (Scenic Site No. 7).  With magnificent mountains of rock that follow the ravine, Sogeumgang looks like a smaller version of the famous Geumgangsan Mountain, which is said to be the most beautiful mountain in the Korean Peninsula. Molundae Cliff lies at the highest point along the road. The stand of 500-year-old pine trees on top of the cliff and a view of the valley below give us a breathtaking scene. Our last stop is Gwangdaegok Valley (Scenic Site No. 8). Here, the sky, clouds and land surrounding Gwangdaesan Mountain appear to merge together, creating a mystical landscape.

stories.title: High1 Resort 8 views
stories.script: High1 Resort 8 views   Introduction to 8 Views First, View 1 of High1 8 Views is the spectacular “fireworks show,” a sightseeing event representing High1. View 2 is “Unamjeong,” a place known as the filming site of <Le Grand Chef>. View 3 is the mountaintop at an elevation of 1,340m, the inspiration for High1's independent brand “1340.” View 4 is the “Meditation Shelter” commemorating the World Meditation Congress where global meditation gurus participated, and View 5 is the “Raincoat Pond” where the wishes of the wife of a miner are nested. View 6 is “Untangodo,” a trekking course representing Korea that served as the path for transporting coal in the past; View 7 features the wildflowers filling the ski slopes, such as Shasta daisies. The last of the 8 Views is the High1 Hotel trail that runs along the High1 golf course, and expectations are running high as High1 Resort plans to install photo zones in each of the 8 Views and promote various events.

stories.title: High1 Resort 8 enjoyable attractions
stories.script: High1 Resort 8 enjoyable attractions    There are 8 kinds of joys in High1 Resort. The High1 ski resort with full length of 21 kilometers is the most preferred ski resort by skiers.  The High1 golf course, located at the highest altitude in Korea, is an 18-hole public course that is famous for allowing visitors to go on rounds amid the cool breeze even in midsummer.   The “High1 Music Festival,” featuring events such as New Year concert, mountain concert, and DJ festival, brings visitors to a world of diverse music. The Haneulgil trekking in the Haneulgil area has become a product representing High1 along with the various courses; the Casa Cinema performance, which shows only the essence of well-known musicals, has established itself as an attraction that can be enjoyed by the whole family.  The book café is a space for healing both body and mind, and the boars and elks that can be seen outside the window of the “Tourist Gondola” – which runs on the 2,832-meter midair track for 40 minutes – remind you that it is Gangwon-do Province.  In addition, the alpine coaster and snow activities available depending on the season will provide you with speed and thrill.  This ends the introduction to “High1 888.” As an old saying goes, “A thousand hearings are not worth one seeing.” High1 Resort, a mountain healing resort that can be enjoyed by the whole family, awaits you.

stories.title: High 1 Resort
stories.audioTitle: Enjoy a relaxing stay at this healing resort
stories.script: High 1 Resort Enjoy a relaxing stay at this healing resort   High 1 Resort offers a wide range of leisure facilities, including ski slopes, a golf course and a casino. Not only is it a popular spot for skiers and snowboarders, its many facilities ensure there is something for everyone who visits.  Let's take a closer look at what High 1 Resort has to offer. First, there are a number of slopes for skiers of all levels, from beginner to advanced. The slopes are connected by a network of gondolas and lifts that can accommodate up to 20,000 people per hour.  High 1 Resort is a popular location in every season. Wildflowers bloom from spring to fall along the Sky Road leading up to the mountaintop. To reach the summit, you can take a gondola or walk, and when you get there you will find the Alpine Botanical Garden, the highest botanical garden in the country. There is also a revolving restaurant, which is popular for its stunning views of the Taebaeksan Mountain Range.  High 1 Resort also has many other attractions to offer. The Alpine Coaster is a thrilling ride on a monorail, while the Wildflower Cart takes you on a relaxing and idyllic tour of the wildflowers in an electric vehicle. This combination of winter sports facilities and relaxing natural surroundings makes High 1 Resort a premier place for both recreation and mountain healing.

stories.title: Fireworks show
stories.script: The fireworks show is one of High1’s eight scenic views representing High1. Fireworks can be likened to love. Fireworks remind people of childhood memories. Fireworks flashing in the night sky have several meanings for people. Viewing High1 fireworks from the grass plaza of Gangwon Land at an altitude of 800 meters will give a fantastic feeling of being in the center of the fireworks. We invite you to the site of High1 Fireworks, where you can enjoy fireworks up close.

stories.title: Unamjeong
stories.script: “Unamjeong” is well-known as a filming location of the TV drama <Gourmet>. The drama was made based on a cartoon titled “Gourmet” by cartoonist Huh Young-man. Unamjeong is an architecture built in the style of Korean traditional house, featuring the beauty of smooth, curved lines such as eaves, which match its surrounding mountains well. At Unamjeong, top-class chefs serve best-quality food cooked with the best food ingredients. We invite you to Unamjeong, a place where you can have an amazing experience of healing through food.

stories.title: Mountain Top
stories.script: “1340” is the Mountain Top at an altitude of 1,340m where High1’s unique brand is derived. Drinking a cup of coffee leisurely at the revolving observation platform of the Mountain Top along the long ridge of Baekdudaegan Mountain Range will relieve your stress from the city life. The view of the clouds from the revolving restaurant on the Mountain Top will show unforgettable scenery. You can take beautiful photos at the Photo Zone at the Mountain Top and send postcards via a mailbox to remind you of beautiful memories.

stories.title: Meditation Rest Area
stories.script: The Meditation Rest Area held the “World Meditation Congress” participated in by four world-renowned meditation masters in Gangwon Land in 2016. To commemorate the event, the Meditation Rest Area was established and became the Mecca of healing. Gangwon Land made a 1.6km-long meditation path between the Mountain Top to the Macheon Peak of Baegunsan Mountain and installed hand printings. While walking along the path where the meditation masters passed through, reflect on the meaning of non-possession as a message delivered by the master.

stories.title: Dorongyee Pond
stories.script: “Dorongyee Pond” is a place that holds the wishes of miners’ wives. The pond was naturally created when the mine collapsed. It is a mountain swamp type of pond. As always, the safety of their husbands was the biggest concern for the miners’ wives.  Wives of miners who lived near Hwajeolryeong used to pray to the salamander living in the pond for the safe return of their husbands, and the name of the pond was derived from that. The shadow of the forest reflected on the pond will provide a beautiful memory to visitors.

stories.title: Untangodo Walkway
stories.script: Untangodo Walkway used to be a path that transported coal produced by this region in the forest. The path, which has that kind of historical meaning, is restored as a skyway. At Untangodo Walkway, which connects a high ground at an altitude of 1,100m and the ridge, visitors can enjoy a therapeutic walk and an open scenic view that cannot be experienced in cities. They can also see the life of miners through facilities that show the history of the mine. Today, the walkway has become Korea’s representative trekking course.

stories.title: Wild Flower
stories.script: The winter ski resort is white. Simply imagining the appearance of skiers who ski along the white slope will provide a refreshing feel. At High1 Resort, visitors can enjoy the refreshing feel of the white slope even in summer, during which the 8km-long slope -- which runs between the mountain base to Valley Hub and to the Mountain Top -- is covered with white wild flowers called Shasta daisies. Visitors can tour the slope full of white flowers onboard our cart or enjoy a lift. Shasta daisy means “patience, purity, and peace” in the language of flowers.

stories.title: High1 Hotel Walkway
stories.script: High1 Hotel Trail is a walkway leading to the golf course from High1 Hotel. At this golf course, visitors need not play golf; they can simply enjoy walking in the golf course. Along the forest path connected to the golf course, visitors can hear the sound of cuckoo and see squirrels and Eurasian Red Squirrels as well. High1 Hotel Walkway is the only place where visitors can enjoy a therapeutic walk in the forest as well as a view of the 18-hole golf course.

stories.title: Skiing
stories.script: The peak of High1 Ski Resort consists of the 1,340m-high Mountain Top, 1,376m-high Valley Top, and 1,250m-high Mountain Hub. The 18-side slope offering various levels of difficulties has total length of 21 km, and it is the most preferred resort by skiers and boarders.

stories.title: Golf
stories.script: High1 CC is a golf course located on the highest place in Korea. It is an 18-hole, 6,592m-long, par-72 public golf course. The quality all-season green grass and the modern, intricately designed course are sufficient to stimulate golfers’ thirst for challenge. The “KLPGA High1 Women’s Open Golf Championship” held every year is like the cradle of world-class female golfers. We would like to introduce the grass and courses trodden on by famous golfers.

stories.title: Music Festival
stories.script: High1’s music festival, which offers New Year’s Music Concert, Mountain Top Music Concert, Casa Cinema Performance, Seasonal DJ Festival, Rock Concert, Overseas Performing Troupe, and various fringe performances, leads visitors to a world of enjoyable music by catering to various music genres. It has become High1 Resort’s representative festival, providing the best things to enjoy and a memorable time for visitors.

stories.title: Haneulgil Trail
stories.script: The Untangodo Walkway -- which is one of High1 Resort’s eight scenic views – and the path that used to transport coals from Manhangjae Pass to the Hambaek Station are revived as the Haneulgil by using the abundant forest resources. Haneulgil Trail at an altitude of 1,000m can be enjoyed differently according to the length of path, which takes 1-4 hours. Along the trekking, visitors can enjoy several hundreds of wild flower species as well as the life and culture of the mining village.

stories.title: Casa Cinema
stories.script: The Casa Cinema, which presents only the best part of famous musicals, is becoming a popular tourist place for visitors. It shows world-famous musical performances such as “Grease,” ‘Mama Mia!” and “Chicago” for families, couples, and children to enjoy.

stories.title: Book Cafe
stories.script: There are several ways to take a rest. At High1, a resort offering many things to enjoy, there is a book café that offers a unique way to enjoy leisure time. The book café built on a hill has 4,000 books organized under themes of healing, environment, and travel, and it will also have a facility that screens videos. Gangwon Land Book Café is a space where families can experience healing.

stories.title: Tourism Gondola
stories.script: As a 2,832m-long airway running between Mountain Sky House and Mountain Top, Tourism Gondola takes about 40 minutes both ways. It is the most popular tourist course among family-unit tourists because it provides a tour of Gangwon Land Ski Resort in the most comfortable way. The boar family and deer spotted now and then outside the window of Gondola make visitors realize that Gangwon-do Province has beautiful nature.

stories.title: Alpine Coaster(Summer) & Snow Activity(Winter)
stories.script: Alpine Coaster is for the summer season, whereas Snow Activity is for the winter season.  The alpine coaster, which races into the forest through a single rail, provides thrilling fun in the hot summer. In addition, the High1 Ski Resort during the winter season offers various riding products that use snow mobile such as snow board, snow bike, and snow tank to provide special enjoyment for skiers and boarders who visit High1. The thrilling experience of racing on snow fields using a snow mobile will offer an unforgettable memory for visitors.

stories.title: Samtan Art Mine
stories.audioTitle: A former coal mine transformed into a space for art and culture
stories.script: Samtan Art Mine A former coal mine transformed into a space for art and culture   Samtan Art Mine is an art and cultural space that was once home to Samcheok Tanjwa Mining Station, a major coal mine that was closed in 2001. Its name reflects both its mining history and its new identity as a center for the arts. Samtan Art Mine features a variety of exhibition halls and an outdoor exhibition space. It became more widely known after it was used as a filming location for the popular TV drama “Descendants of the Sun.” Now, let's take a look at how this abandoned mine underwent its transformation.  Visitors should begin their tour on the fourth floor, where the ticket office is located. Once you have your ticket, pass the fourth-floor lounge to get down to the third floor, where the gallery called CAM 1 , or Contemporary Art Museum 1, and the beautiful Samtan Museum showcase a variety of artworks. This floor also displays some of the tools the miners once used, including old radios and gas masks, offering a unique viewing experience. Next, move down to the second floor, which houses roughly 100,000 works of art collected by Representative Kim Min-seok, the founder of Samtan Art Mine, during his 30 years of travel abroad. Most notably in this area, the showers that were once used by thousands of miners have been transformed into an exhibition space.  When you get to the first floor, head to the Rail by Museum, which features mining cars and cages, old tools and more. Afterward, make a stop at the outdoor exhibition space, featuring the Garden of Memories and Glass House, and wrap up your visit with a cup of tea at Restaurant 832L. It’s the perfect way to reflect on your visit to Samtan Art Mine, a fascinating space that brings together historical artifacts, modern artworks, and is a familiar TV location in popular culture.

stories.title: Daegwallyeong Sheep Farm
stories.audioTitle: Quality time with a wooly flock among rolling fields of green
stories.script: Daegwallyeong Sheep Farm Quality time with a wooly flock among rolling fields of green   Daegwallyeong Sheep Farm is a 10-minute drive from Daegwallyeong Interchange on Yeongdong Expressway. Visitors are met with an idyllic scene of sheep grazing on pastures that stretch out beneath a clear blue sky.  Upon entering the picturesque ranch, you will be greeted by the happy sounds of its occupants. A walking path encircles the entire ranch, offering an easy stroll that is just over 1 kilometer long. All of your senses will come alive as you listen to the sounds of the sheep, inhale the fresh scent of the grass and feel the cool breeze. When you reach the highest point of the walking path, you’ll be able to see the whole of Daegwallyeong-myeon, including a stand of wind turbines churning on the horizon.  Take your time and go at a leisurely pace. When you come to the end of the path you will find the feeding area for the sheep, which is a favorite attraction for children. First, exchange your ticket for a basket of hay. Then, try offering a handful to the friendly sheep. They will gobble up the whole basket in no time.

stories.title: Yongpyong Resort
stories.audioTitle: The birthplace of Korea's ski history
stories.script: Yongpyong Resort The birthplace of Korea's ski history   Yongpyong Resort opened in 1975 as Korea’s first ski resort. It was also the second ski resort in Asia to gain official recognition from the International Ski Federation. It has a wide range of slopes from beginner to advanced levels, with facilities for Alpine Skiing, Nordic Combined and Snowboarding. In particular, the Rainbow Slope will host the Alpine Skiing and Slalom events during the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics.  Starting at Dragon Plaza, a 20-minute ride on the Rainbow Gondola brings you to the Sky Garden. This was a filming location for the famous TV drama “Winter Sonata,” which led the Korean Wave in 2002, as well as the popular drama “Goblin” that wrapped up its run in 2017. From this vantage point, you can see a breathtaking view of the East Sea beyond a grove of ancient jumok trees. An old Korean proverb says that the jumok tree “lives for a thousand years, and stands for a thousand more.” The outstanding scenery makes this a great place to visit all year round.  At Yongpyong Resort, there are also plenty of leisure sports to enjoy. Take a mountain bike and cruise down the slopes of the popular MTB Park. Bicycles and safety equipment are both available for rent, so everyone can enjoy the ride. On top of that, the Mountain Coaster, off-road buggy carts and a variety of other activities will help you create your own memorable experiences.

stories.title: Alpensia Ski Jump
stories.script: Alpensia Ski Jump Reach for the gold!   Visitors to Alpensia Resort can see the ski jumping tower that will be used during the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics. It offers two ski jumps for different distances and an observation deck for spectators.  Let’s take a look around. There are two kinds of tours: the standard tour takes visitors around the observation deck, while the special tour takes them to the ski jump as well. Start out from the ticket booth on the first floor, and it’s just a short 5-minute ride on a monorail to the entrance to the ski jump tower, which is situated at an altitude of 930 meters. Visitors can take the elevator and ascend another 25 meters to see the ski jump itself. Next, pass the athletes’ waiting room and skyway to arrive at the ramp, which offers a majestic view of Balwangsan Mountain and Gorupogisan Mountain. Standing before the ski jump that will be used in the PyeongChang Winter Olympics certainly makes an impression. It’s even exhilarating to look through the metal latticework at the sheer length of the skyway.  The ski jump observation deck also has a café where you can enjoy a cup of coffee. And the early risers among you might just be lucky enough to catch a glimpse of the athletes practicing for their events.

stories.title: Odaesan Seonjae-gil Trail
stories.audioTitle: A forest road leading to the world of the Buddha
stories.script: Odaesan Seonjae-gil Trail A forest road leading to the world of the Buddha   Odaesan Seonjae-gil Trail lies between two temples -- Woljeong-sa and Sangwon-sa. Here, echoes of Buddhist scriptures resonate amid the beauty of nature. Seonjae is the protagonist of the Avatamsaka Sutra from Buddhist scriptures. He goes on a pilgrimage for enlightenment with the guidance of Munsu, the Bodhisattva of wisdom. Here, you can forget your troubles for a while and walk upon this road, with only yourself for company.  Seonjae-gil Trail begins with Sunhwan-gil, a path that starts at the parking lot of Woljeong-sa Temple and circles back from Iljumun Gate. In the past, the trail began in the road behind the temple, but this has changed since the fall of 2016. Along the way, thousand-year-old fir trees form a tunnel that seems to connect our world with the realm of the Buddha. At the end of the path returning to the parking lot, you will come upon the ancient Woljeong-sa Temple, built by the monk Jajang Yulsa (590-658) during the Silla Dynasty (57 BC-935 AD). Once inside, you will see an octagonal nine-story pagoda (National Treasure No. 48-1) and the stone statue of a seated bodhisattva (National Treasure No. 48-2).  A side path from Woljeong-sa Bumjongru leads you to the start of the main Odaesan Seonjae-gil Trail. The path follows the clear waters of Odaecheon Stream across the valley before turning into the forest. The series of dirt roads and wooden walkways make for a varied and enjoyable walk through the beautiful scenery.

stories.title: Lee Hyo-seok Memorial Hall
stories.audioTitle: Discover a field of buckwheat flowers as white as salt
stories.script: Lee Hyo-seok Memorial Hall Discover a field of buckwheat flowers as white as salt   The mountainside was covered with fields of buckwheat flowers whose burgeoning blossoms, sprinkled over the landscape like salt, seemed to suffocate in the moonlight.  This line comes from “When Buckwheat Flowers Bloom” by Lee Hyo-seok, one of the most famous short stories in modern Korean literature. Buckwheat flowers are an important feature of the small town of Bongpyeong, which is located in the Pyeongchang region.  Bongpyeong is the hometown of writer Lee Hyo-seok. The Lee Hyo-seok Memorial Hall displays artifacts and documents from the author’s life. Let's take a tour of the main building, the culture garden and the Lee Hyo-seok Literature Forest Road. First, the main building introduces visitors to the author's life and literary world. You can see a recreation of the writer's studio, which is based on a photograph from his house in Pyongyang, and an exhibition of the old Bongpyeong marketplace. In addition, there is a buckwheat exhibit where visitors can glean valuable information about buckwheat such as how it is sown, its health benefits, and even buckwheat recipes.  Upon exiting the main building, you will find the outdoor literature garden, where a bronze statue depicts Lee Hyo-seok writing at his desk. At the rest area next to the garden, there is a signpost for Munhak Mountain. You can follow the sign and take a short walk uphill to the Lee Hyo-seok Literature Forest Road. From this vantage point, you can see Lee Hyo-seok Memorial Hall and the surrounding area. Though the path is relatively short, there are wooden benches along the way for those who need a quiet break.

stories.title: Phoenix Pyeongchang Resort
stories.audioTitle: Excitement, adventure and a chance to recharge
stories.script: Phoenix Pyeongchang Resort Excitement, adventure and a chance to recharge   The Phoenix Pyeongchang Resort is a favorite resort among young skiing and snowboarding enthusiasts. During the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics, five freestyle skiing events and four snowboarding events will be held at this location. For aspiring athletes and leisure travelers, the slopes offer various levels of challenge including beginner, intermediate and advanced courses. The resort is nestled at the foot of Taegisan Mountain in a canyon-like environment designed to conform to the surrounding landscape. The area is known for having high-quality snow and ample snowfall in the winter.  Let’s take a tour of the slopes. The Panorama Run allows beginners to feel like experts in their sport. The slope starts off easy and gradually becomes steeper in the middle so you can enjoy a bit more speed. Overall, the slope is long and wide, but not too steep, so beginners can have an enjoyable experience. Meanwhile, an area called Extreme Park features half-pipes, table tops and rails, making it popular with snowboarders.  The Phoenix Pyeongchang Resort is a popular resort during all four seasons of the year. When the slopes are covered with grass instead of snow, visitors can enjoy extreme leisure activities like riding a zipline or an ATV. Take the gondola up to the peak, Mont Blanc, to an altitude of 1050 meters. Or enjoy a quiet stroll through the Wellness Forest Road, which is surrounded by conifers and birch trees.

stories.title: 1. Green Pool_Wave
stories.script: Green Pool_Wave  Welcome to the “Green Pool _ Wave”. Why don’t you sit down on the tube and imagine that the green lawn is a blue river in a romantic and relaxing atmosphere? Green Pool _ Wave was made by combining a fancy idea of a citizen to create a pool on the lawn and interesting interpretation of it by an artist. The artist was inspired by the Hangang(River) slowly flowing down and bending back and forth, and described beautiful waves on the lawn in a three dimensional manner. The wave of small hills creates a comfortable landscape while infusing vitality to the space and creating various forms of rest. The long bench going excellently well with the small hills provides citizens a place to sit down side by side or stroll around while enjoying the beautiful scenery of the Hangang(River). Why don’t you sit down on the big tube and have a breath of fresh air?   I am Jaehyeog Choi, and I am an artist.  When I first heard of the green pool suggested by a citizen, I thought it was a plain but very fresh idea.  Anyone who sits down on the tube installed on the lawn will recall beautiful romantic memories on the beach or riverside. Also, I thought it would be a good idea to add some more fun to the lawn. An interesting space would attract more people to play and take a rest there. Imagine, what if the lawn was a pool filled with water making beautiful waves? Wouldn’t it be much more fun? Hence, I added one more theme to the idea of green pool, which is “wave”. On the other hand, I thought an architectural element was necessary to serve as a frame of the space. That is why I made a long bench that goes absolutely well with the naturally waving landscape.   The space will become an excellent walking trail where some people sit down side by side and look at the Hangang(River), while others strolling around.

stories.title: 2. Untitled(2 People)
stories.script: Untitled(2 People)  I am Younghoon Haam, and I am a pictographer. I would like to talk about the form and feeling of people on rest. What do you think is rest for humans? The natural environment including sunshine, wind, earth, river, animals, plants and humans all together create various energies necessary for us.  The life rhythm of human depends on various changes in nature, changes in dawn before sunrise wet with dew, the rising sun in the morning and the daytime with bright sunshine, the evening with the glow of the sunset and the night time with quiet moonlight.   Likewise, we feel and accept various emotions caused by changes in nature, the colors of changing four seasons, temperature and weather, spring days with sweet-smelling buds and flowers, summer nature landscape in deep green forest, colorful autumn days and tranquil white winter landscape.   Humans need to take a rest, while being in harmony with the nature, which is the process of healing and recovery.  The Hangang(River) is one of the best places to take a rest for us all.   This artwork describes a shape of rest by using a simple line, with various natural environments around the Hangang(River) as a background. It is beautifully in harmony with the sky, land and flowing water of the Hangang(River), which is our shelter. Well, please tell me what do you think and imagine is the shape and feeling of rest?

stories.title: 3. Dokkaebi Stool
stories.script: Dokkaebi Stool   The super mirror polishing processing applied to ‘Dokkaebi Stool’ make the artwork become the most strange and artificial structure existing in the natural space along the Hangang(River). The simple cylindrical and straight shape and smooth surface of Dokkaebi Stool that is installed artificially will give you some special and unexpected fun.  The 24 Dokkaebi stools placed between pine trees, which are elaborately processed, absorb the images of their surrounding environment including grasses and trees, exactly like Dokkaebi does, who disappear when it wears a Dokkaebi hat, and thereby cause illusion as if everything disappears right in front of your eyes. I would like to provide a whole new experience to you with the most artificial object placed in a most natural space, which will function as a stool as well.   I am Jiyoun Kim, and I am a designer.  The Hangang(River), flowing through the center of Seoul, is a magnificent symbol. People exercise, date, take a walk or take a rest in the Hangang(River).  We all love the river as it is.  Walking along the river, however, you may find something is missing. You may need some artificial structures such as some places to take a rest or trash bins to dispose empty cans in your hand.  There already are many artificial structures around the Hangang(River). I tried to make an ironical situation in which people use an artificial structure in order to feel and enjoy the nature. In Korea, Dokkaebi is a legendary creature from folklore. You may encounter a Dokkaebi in unexpected places. It is a bit scary but friendly and mischievous at the same time. ‘Dokkaebi Stool’ may look like a strange structure installed in a natural. You may encounter Dokkaebi Stool in an unexpected place walking down along the Hangang(River). Why don’t you stop for a moment and listen to the sound of breeze blowing from pine trees when you encounter the stool?

stories.title: 4. House of Wind
stories.script: House of Wind  ‘House of Wind’ is an organic space where long and thin lines make small minimum units which make larger units together, thereby becoming larger units. Therefore, this space has a potential for further changes.  The geometrical and three dimensional structure looks like a ‘maze’ divided into spaces of various sizes. And there are small structures between the mazes, which will be used as ‘chairs’. This organic structure will serve as spaces for people to have fun, enjoy, take a rest and relax. Also, the change and balance created by the six colors of the wire rods give a sense of mystery to the overall space while being in harmony with the landscape of the Hangang(River). ‘House of Wind’ is designed to describe 2 spaces for play and rest in one concept. Some people may stroll or jump around while others take a rest or fall into thought in the House of Wind,   I am Jaiyoung Cho, and I am an artist.  ‘House of Wind’ is an installation artwork made of wire rods only. It is installed in an open space and therefore citizens who visit the Hangang(River) can walk into and around the artwork freely. The beautiful landscape around the Hangang(River) you may see between the thin wire rods and the movements of citizens in and around the House of Wind make whole new scenery while being in harmony with the geometrical and three dimensional space of various colors.  I think the space, which is open in all directions while going absolutely well with its surroundings, will serve as an excellent place for the wind as well as for all of us who need to have a breath of fresh air and relaxation. Would you like to become the wind and visit the House of Wind?

stories.title: 6. Hangang(River) Fishing Vessel Story 2 _ SWITCH
stories.script: Story 2 _ SWITCH  The Hangang(River) tells various stories and history of Seoul. For a variety of reasons, some part the riverside was once covered with concrete and has recovered its naturalness. The river has been driving force behind industrial development and now serves as an engine for citizens providing spaces to take a rest. Sometimes, the river is inundated but also various festivals are held all over the places around the Hangang(River).   I am Su-Jeong Park, and I am an architect.  The second story, SWITCH, is designed to show the concept of ‘change’ by using a fishing vessel, Kyeongdongho, with the Hangang(River) as a background. There are external elements changing every moment, such as four changing seasons, water level and so on. Although the scenery around the river looks the same all the time, it changes in a variety of ways as people visiting the place change all the time. SWITCH appears as a medium of such changes and brings new changes to the landscape and look of the river.

stories.title: 5. Hangang(River) Fishing Vessel Story 1_Blue Wind
stories.script: Story 1_Blue Wind  Fishing vessels visit the Hangang(River), which has become part of Seoul citizens’ daily life. What kind of diversity and pleasure will the fishing vessels bring to the Hangang(River)? Some amazing stories begin with the visit of 3 fishing vessels to the Hangang(River).  A land with a large river and broad space in Seoul provides citizens with unique places to feel and enjoy nature in their tiresome city life.  Fishing vessels pave the way for creating a space with full diversity for citizens to take a rest.   I am Hee-Jun Sim, and I am an architect.  The first story, Blue Wind, starts from a story imagining something that is invisible but exist from a fishing vessel called Namhaeho. The story tells a journey of Namhaeho, from ocean to land, a fishing vessel that was once used to catch fish and octopus the southern coast of Korea, and make people feel invisible breezes. The ceiling visualizes wind and serves as a shade for people to feel the breeze when wind blows. People may imagine water waves when they sit down or lie under the blue shade which waves when wind blows. There are pictures in the cabin of Namhaeho showing the stories of the vessel and relevant places. The fishing vessel becomes a place where people sit down under the blue shade, and share some trivial or incredible stories in their daily lives.

stories.title: 8. Re(MEMORY + JOURNEY)
stories.script: Re(MEMORY + JOURNEY)  I am Heesung Baek and I am an architect.  Memories are one of the most important materials for me, which is the same for this project. Recovering the lost memories of the Hangang(River) was the most important thing.  Many of you may remember the white sand beach that once existed in the Hangang(River). However, few people may know how large it was. If you are in the Hangang(River) Art Museum now, you are standing right on the site where a white sand beach once existed.   The magnificent scenery of beautiful white sand beach extended on several ten kilometers along the Hangang(River)… I wanted to enable people to recall such memories for some moments. We have a reason to recall such memories… If the city development had been undertaken just one kilometer away from the riverside with white sand beach, Seoul could have become a modern city with one of the most beautiful white sand beaches in the world. What do you think? Don’t you think that’s so regrettable?  I created this artwork out of such regret. So many modern development projects have been carried out without consideration of the value of nature. I hope you all monitor the development projects around you with such a sense of regret. Think as to whether there are any important memories that have disappeared without our knowledge, whether we can keep such memories and so on… Our memories become architectures, and the architectures give rise to clues to recall our memories for a brighter future for us all.   I am Jinho Jung, and I am an architect.  Architecture is a process of turning ideas and thoughts into a realistic space. Our team selected a concept designed to give old memories of the Hangang(River) back to citizens, and explored ways to enable citizens recall old memories while looking at the Hangang(River) from a specific space. A place where people can see bright light and recall old memories while feeling and touching closer to the Hangang(River). This will become a place providing lots of room for people to think, move and create … With such thoughts and ideas, we created an art museum on the barge. We had many twists and turns in the process due to the specific environment of the Hangang(River). However, we could build the Hangang(River) Art Museum thanks to the ideas, help and passion of many people. I hope to help citizens recall old memories of the Hangang(River) and put another memory into the barge.   I am Haein Lee, and I am a landscape architect.   I created a sand beach in the island where citizens can take off shoes and touch the sand. I also got an inspiration from the natural patterns created when water flew in and out of the sand beach, and made several green spaces on the island.. The first barge is created as an open space to look at the landscape from all sides, which is different from the inside of the air dome. The second barge is designed with lots of plants, thereby to provide a place for citizens to take a rest and relax amid natural environment of the Hangang(River) while feeling and touching the leaves of willow trees and water grasses, and taking a walk. The Bamseom Island may catch your eyes on the way back from the museum. The island was once a large white sand beach and the resilience of the island is really remarkable. Therefore, an architecture established on the island has a special meaning. We can see the skyline of the city and the group of willow trees over the artificial island. We expect that people will be able to recall old memories and experience hopes for the future through our artwork.

stories.title: 7. Hangang(River) Fishing Vessel Story _ Sea of Spring
stories.script: Sea of Spring  What does the Hangang(River) mean for us? What do you think or imagine when you visit the Hangang(River), looking at the river or appreciating small artworks in places around the river?   I am Su-Jeong Park, and I am an architect.  The third story starts from the name of a fishing vessel called Haechoonho. Haechoon means the spring of sea. Haechoonho tells us a story of rediscovering some lyric places around the Hangang(River). Haechoonho visits a small hill along the Hangang(River). The fishing vessel anchors here and serves as an excellent stage.  The storage of the vessel, which was once used to store fish, has now become a container to carry the lives of the earth and is now filled with cherry blossom. We expect to have an amazing time while listening to stories amid beautiful cherry blossom petals and flowers being scattered on the stage of ‘Sea of Spring’. We are waiting for spring.  An unfamiliar material, fishing vessel, is used as a space to make our rest more abundant. And the process of making the space more meaningful remains an area to be completed by citizens. Through such a process, we hope to discover stories that have been invisible and expect to give rise to various questions and thoughts on the Hangang(River) through imagination.

stories.title: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy
stories.audioTitle: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, where Tribute is Paid to the Thoughts and Life of  Gi Dae-seung
stories.script: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, where Tribute is Paid to the Thoughts and Life of Gi Dae-seung    Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy was built to pay tribute to the thoughts and life of Gi Dae-seung (penname: Gobong), a Confucian scholar of the Joseon Dynasty. He contributed greatly to the development of Neo-Confucianism with his extraordinary enthusiasm. There is a well-known story that he had a philosophical argument with Yi Hwang (penname: Toegye) and they exchanged 120 letters over 13 years.  In 1578 (the 11th year of King Seonjo), seven years after he passed away, local Confucian scholars built Mangcheonsa Shrine to hold memorial rites for him. The shrine was damaged during Imjinwaeran (the Japanese Invasion of Joseon) and was moved to the current location via Dongcheon (now Sanwol-dong). It took on the appearance of a prestigious Seowon (Confucian academy) after King Hyojong named it “Wolbong” and put a signboard on it in 1654.  Although it was demolished under an order of Heungseon Daewongun to eliminate Confucian academies (1868), it was restored starting with Bingwoldang Hall in 1941, followed by Oesammun (three outer gates), Jangpangak and Naesammun (three inner gates).  After looking around Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, walk along Philosopher's Trail and visit the tomb of Gi. The 10-minute walk is beautiful, as the pine forest and bamboo grove go well together.

stories.title: East and West Dormitories (Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy)
stories.audioTitle: East and West Dormitories (Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy)
stories.script: East and West Dormitories, where Scholars Stayed and Studied  Passing through Mangcheonmun Gate (Oesammun Gate), the main gate of Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, there are the East and West Dormitories. These dormitories were once where the scholars study at Seowon stayed. The East and West Dormitories are located to the right and left of Bingwoldang Hall respectively. East Dormitories named Myeongseongjae, refers to “Dedicate Oneself Fully to Illuminate Virtues” and West Dormitories named Jonseongjae, refers to “Reflect on Oneself.”  Bingwoldang Hall, where scholars were taught by strict rules, is on an elevated area above East and West Halls. Also, Bingwoldang Hall has a hipped and gabled roof, which boasts magnificence and dignity, while East and West Halls have a humble gambrel roof which looks like an open book laid face down.  East and West Halls resemble each other like twins but have a hierarchy. Following the principle of “right upper” and “left lower” of Yin-Yang and the Five Elements theory, senior students lived in East Hall and junior students lived in West Hall. The entrance qualification for Seowon was not strict, and most of the scholars in Seowons passed the Sogwa, the first state examination, in other words, the preliminary exams, Saengwonsi and Jinsasi.

stories.title: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy,Bingwoldang Hall
stories.audioTitle: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, Bingwoldang Hall, an Auditorium that Resembles the Personality of a Splendid Scholar
stories.script: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, Bingwoldang Hall, an Auditorium that Resembles the Personality of a Splendid Scholar    Right after passing Mangcheonmun Gate (Oesammun), the main gate of Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, is Bingwoldang Hall (Gwangju-si Monument No. 9). This is an auditorium where teachers and pupils read and studied Confucian books. Bingwol means “transparent like ice and clean like the moon on a snowy day.” It originates from “Bingsimseolwol,” a saying that King Jeongjo, the 22nd king of the Joseon Dynasty, granted to it, comparing it to the lofty academic virtue of Gi Dae-seung (penname: Gobong).     There is another story of origin for “Bingwol.” It is said to have been used in “Chijemun” (funerary ode) that was written in 1655 by King Hyojong, Joseon’s 17th king, who said the personality of Gi Dae-seung was “well-tempered gold, glorious jade (Jeonggeumyunok), the moon in clean water, and a transparent bottle (Suwolbingho).”   Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy was demolished in 1868 under an order of Heungseon Daewongun to eliminate Confucian academies. Bingwoldang Hall was rebuilt first during its restoration. The shrine is on higher stone walls than that of East and West Halls, and this shows respect for the place where scholars studied and teachers stayed.    Bingwoldang Hall is composed of seven kans (the space from one column to the next) in front and three kans on the sides, and the main living rooms are on the left and right sides with the floored hall in the center. The wood grain is impressively emphasized without special decoration or coloration under the dignified hipped and gabled roof. It shows the splendid spirituality of the scholars, who practiced a humble life.

stories.title: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy,Sungdeoksa
stories.audioTitle: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, Sungdeoksa Shrine, where Tribute is Paid to the Virtues of Gi Dae-seung
stories.script: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, Sungdeoksa Shrine, where Tribute is Paid to the Virtues of Gi Dae-seung    In the Joseon Dynasty, Seowons were used for “Ganghak,” fostering younger generations through education and “Jehyang,” performing ancestral rites. If Bingwoldang Hall, East and West Halls are spaces for “Ganghak,” Sungdeoksa Shrine is the place for “Jehyang.” The shrine’s name means “revere the virtues,” and the tablet of Gi Dae-seung (penname: Gobong) is enshrined here.  Sungdeoksa Shrine is on the back stairs of Bingwoldang Hall on the most elevated area of Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy. From the top of the high stairs, Jeonganmun Gate can be seen. Jeonganmun, which means “have a peaceful and silent mind,” is also called Naesammun meaning “three gates inside Seowon.”  Sungdeoksa Shrine looks like an independent space even though it is inside Seowon, as it is a sacred space where the tablets of ancestors of great scholars are enshrined. As the only building that has various patterns and colors in Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, it is elegant and dignified with its hipped and gabled roof in harmony with the beautiful colors. Every March and September, Hyangsaje Ritual is held, where a tribute is paid to the studies and virtue of Gi Dae-seung.

stories.title: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy,Jangpangak Hall
stories.audioTitle: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, Jangpangak Hall, where the Works of Gi Dae-seung are Stored
stories.script: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, Jangpangak Hall, where the Works of Gi Dae-seung are Stored    After entering the main gate of Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, there is an elegant building on the left side of Bingwoldang Hall. Jangpangak Hall was used to house woodblocks for printing books and is akin to today’s publishing company or library.  In Jangpangak Hall, which was a warehouse for storing valuable things, there are 474 woodblocks of the books of writings by Gi Dae-seung (penname: Gobong). Among them woodblocks for “Yangseonsaengwangbokseo” and “Yangseonsaengigiwangbokseo” are eye-catching.  Gi Dae-seung exchanged more than 120 letters with Yi Hwang (penname: Toegye), who was 26 years older than him, for 13 years starting from when he was 32 years old. Among them, was the debate over “Sadanchiljeong” (four impulses and seven emotions of humans), which they kept up for 8 years.  The letters were collected in the book “Yangseonsaengigiwangbokseo.” The letters that inquired after each other’s health and shared news of their respective families were collected in “Yangseonsaengwangbokseo”.  Also, visitors can see woodblocks for the major writings of Gi Dae-seung such as “Jujamunnok,” where Chu Shi’s works are summarized and compiled, and “Nonsarok,” which King Jeongjo greatly admired later.

stories.title: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy,Salon de Wolbong -
stories.audioTitle: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, Salon de Wolbong, a High-Class Humanities Program
stories.script: Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy, Salon de Wolbong, a High-Class Humanities Program    Wolbongseowon Confucian Academy operates various programs that reinterpret the scholar culture of the Joseon Dynasty in a modern way.
