In addition to about 50 camellias that are over 300 years old, three hackberries designated as nurse-trees as well as machilus, Japanese cinnamons and the native mandarin trees form colonies of their own. Thanks to the efforts of the locals who wanted to share this camellia colony with everyone, it won the Eoullim Award at the 8th National Beautiful Forest Contest and the 10th Supjigi Award.  Camellia trees are lined up for about 20 km on the path leading to the village. When the flowers blossom between winter and spring, the combination of red flowers and the shining green freshness forms a magnificent spectacle.  In addition to the camellia forest exploration for travelers, the village provides daily necessities-making and camellia soap-making experience using camellia fruits and natural objects as well as food experiences in which visitors can cook bibimbap and rice balls with camellia. Guesthouses and pensions are also available.

stories.title: Tomb of Kim Man-il in Uigwi-ri
stories.audioTitle: Tomb of Kim Man-il in Uigwi-ri
stories.script: This is the Tomb of Kim Man-il of “Seowinammoru” in Uigwi-ri. Kim Man-il is the one who raised over 10,000 horses in Jeju during the Joseon Dynasty. He first offered 300 good horses that can be used as war horses during the Japanese Invasion of 1592 (27th year of King Seonjo's reign). Kim presented about 1,300 horses in total over four occasions including the 33rd year of Seonjo's reign, 12th year of Gwanghaegun's reign and 5th year of Injo's reign. Because of such meritorious deeds, he was given the position of Jong 1-pum (1st rank in the secondary class) Sungjeong Daebu in the 6th year of King Injo's reign and was praised as Heonma Gongsin. Afterwards, Kim's private ranch began to be run as “Sanmajang” and the most outstanding horses were chosen and managed separately as “Gamma.”  The Tomb of Kim Man-il Grave is a burial mound featuring stone walls, which help understand the construction methods and structure of burial mounds and stone walls of Jeju from the 17th century. It is also different from typical private tombs in terms of size and shape. It is a round earthen mound tomb with a diameter of 5.4 m and a height of 1.5 m. Natural rocks of Jeju were installed at the boundary of the mound. This 1.5-meter-wide, 70 to 80-cm tall stone wall is of the random masonry method with four to five levels, and in the grave area, there are one stone table, one stone stele and two civil official statutes, which are all estimated to have been made in the same period. Among them, the statues of civil officials is of the Jeju style like Dol Hareubang which shows the island's original stonework culture.

stories.title: Otgwima Theme Town
stories.script: There is a stone post that says, “Home of Jeju Horses — Uigwi” in the front yard of Uigwi Village Hall. This is also the hometown of Kim Man-il who served an essential role in the history of Jeju horses. Kim Man-il raised over 10,000 horses in a vast ranch that spanned from Uigwi to Gyorae. He later offered the horses to help his country overcome a national crisis for which he became praised as Heonma Gongsin, and King Yeongjo bestowed valuable attires upon Kim and his descendants. That is why this area is called Uigwi Village or Otgwi Village. As you can see, Uigwi-ri was the central village of Sanmajang, which was the most thriving ranch in the country at the time.  In 2015, it was selected as a horse theme experience village by the Ministry for Food, Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, and eventually opened as a theme town. Inside the 66,115 m2 communal ranch, there are riding facilities where you can ride a Jeju horse. It also features a horse-riding education room, a circular riding experience ground, materials exhibition hall, Daemajang, a mounted archery ground, and tile murals visually narrating the life of Kim Man-il. The theme town also has a mini horse-riding path, an observatory, a cafeteria and other auxiliary facilities.  The village founded the Otgwi Youth Riding Club to educate young people on horseback riding and offer safety training and horse-riding experiences.

stories.title: Jeonguihyanggyo Local Confucian School
stories.script: In the 15th century, there were local Confucian schools in three villages — Jejumok, Daejeong Village and Jeongui Village — and they still exist today. Jeonguihyanggyo Local Confucian School is located next to the West Gate of Jeonguieupseong Fortress. When it was first constructed in the 5th year of King Sejong's reign (1423), it was built outside the West Gate in Jinsarihyeon but it was later relocated to the current location in the 15th year of King Heonjong's reign (1849).  Hyanggyo, or Confucian school, was a national education agency with functions as ritual holders and educators. It is said that a typical hyanggyo in Joseon Dynasty received land, books and servants from the government and taught about 30 students with one teacher. But the education part of its responsibility vanished after the Gabo Reform and only the ritual function has been maintained. Today, it holds rituals every spring and fall.  Jeonguihyanggyo Local Confucian School shows several characteristics. Unlike how typical Confucian schools face south, this one faces east. What remain today include Daeseongjeon Shrine, Myeongnyundang Lecture Hall, Dongjae and Seojae Dormitories and Sammun Gate. Daeseongjeon Shrine was constructed when the hyeon office was relocated from Goseong, Seongsan-eup to Seongeup in 1423. It enshrines the tablets of five Seongs, 10 Cheols, Songjo 4 Hyeon and Hanguk 18 Hyeons. 10 Songdeokbi, or memorial monuments, stand by the entrance, and there are five more inside the school.  It is the Tangible Cultural Heritage No. 5 of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province.

stories.title: Jeju Folk Village
stories.script: Jeju Folk Village, which was a filming location for a Korean TV series Dae Jang Geum, has a mini Dae Jang Geum theme park. Many other dramas like The Slave Hunters, The Great Merchant, Queen & I and King's Doctor were also filmed here, and Tamra the Island filmed over 80% of its scenes here. In particular, Tamra the Island is a fusion historical drama centered on Hamel, a Dutch man who drifted to Jeju in the mid-17th century, that depicts a variety of people in exile to Jeju haenyeo, portraying how Jeju looked like in the old days.  This is why Jeju Folk Village is a popular filming spot in Jeju for historical dramas and TV shows.

stories.title: Traditional Play Culture Support Council
stories.script: Traditional Play Culture Support Council, which is located in Pyoseon-myeon, opened after remodeling a discontinued school. With the goal of establishing upright values for youth by inheriting and preserving Jeju's traditional culture, it offers cultural experiences and character-building programs. It focuses especially on relating traditional Jeju culture and various games to disseminate the island's culture and develop cultural tourism content based on traditional games. On the other hand, it also provides training to raise traditional game leaders and volunteers.  At the council, visitors can learn about the history of Jeju's folk culture, dialect, traditional games and natural heritage, and also get a first-hand experience of Jipjulnori, spinning top making, Gonunori, Jinnori and many other traditional games played on the island for centuries. It also features a field, accommodations, experience sites, cafeteria and many other facilities, which makes it perfect for group workshops, and the council itself provides active support for external events such as provincial festivals.

stories.title: Eomeong Abang Feast Village
stories.script: “Eomeong” and “Abang” are words of Jeju dialect that mean mother and father. Eomeong Abang Feast Village is an experience town that has replicated the looks of an old farming village of Jeju. It is located in Sinpung-ri whose name means “a new and abundant village.” There are several prehistoric remains here including dolmens. As the first-ever experience village of Jeju, it has different kinds of accommodations available, from traditional houses and thatched-roof houses to modern guesthouses, making it a great place to stay a day or two and try the island’s traditional culture and natural environment.  It also has facilities that can only be found on Jeju Island such as a pigsty of native pigs, thatched houses and traditional wedding halls, allowing you to engage in a variety of traditional Jeju experiences including Jeju dialect class, traditional wedding, traditional thatched house experience, Eomeong Abang feast, native foods and farming experience. The farm center is good news for those aspiring to live in the countryside as through a connection program, families with children in elementary schools can stay at the center for a specified period to experience the life in a farming village. For these aspiring farmers, the village has remodeled vacated houses and currently runs a program through which it leases the houses for about a year and helps them settle down in the new home.

stories.title: Sincheonri Mural Village
stories.script: There is a special story behind how Sincheon-ri became a mural village. In 2013, when a movie titled Sunshine, which depicts a North Korean defector girl growing into a painter, was filmed here, nine paintings were drawn on the walls, which was the beginning of a mural village. As the news spread around, young artists gathered to take part in the Sincheon Art Village Establishment Project and painted about 100 works. This is how Sincheonri Mural Village was born.  The village belongs to Olle Course 3 and it is indeed a great place to walk and enjoy the scenery. There are cartoon characters that kids love, from Pororo and Shin Chan to SpongeBob, Minions and Olaf as well as fun replica paintings like “The Birth of Haenyeo,” which is derived from The Birth of Venus. There is also a mural of a flower shop that looks like a real flower shop as well as various looks of haenyeo, some of whom are drawn in cute illustrations while others are expressed in a more solemn manner. At the end of your walk, you are going to reach a small dock where you will find a unique painting of Jeju on the surface of a water tank.  Meanwhile, the sea of Sincheon-ri is known as a place where dolphins pass. If you have time, sit at a bench at the end of the sea and feel the pleasant energy delivered to you by the Jeju sea wind.

stories.title: Itami Course — Podo Hotel
stories.script: One of the most representative works designed by Jun Itami, Podo Hotel is a small hotel with 26 rooms located inside the Pinx Golf Club. It got its name due to a resemblance to a bunch of grapes when viewed from the sky above. It was designed based on Jeju’s oreum and traditional thatched house with elements of Jeju’s nature and Korean beauty.  This hotel especially presents comfort that makes people feel relaxed; as you enter from the side and walk along a long hallway that leads to the inside of the hotel, you will feel like taking a stroll on a familiar street. The fact that it is a single-story hotel whose ceiling is higher than other accommodations and that it is designed to introduce as much natural lighting as possible instead of relying only on artificial lighting makes you feel right at home. The roof is made of titanium zinc plates, and the beauty of Jun Itami’s architecture lies in how he focused on details to harmonize artificial materials that may feel heterogeneous with the round shape of the roof.  For the rooms, those on the side with the view of the sea are Western-style rooms whereas the side with a mountain view consists of Korean-style ondol rooms where you can enjoy spa inside a bathtub made of cypress. Harmonious mixtures of traditional Korean patterns such as rafters and plaid windows are found throughout the hotel, and the roof, which is designed with titanium, contains the meaning of “Let’s go back to the basics.”  Podo Hotel boasts a splendid history of awards, including the Beautiful Architecture of Jeju, the 2nd Asian Residential Culture Residential Landscape Awards, and Chevalier de l’Ordre des Arts et des Lettres in 2003.

stories.title: Itami Course — Pinx Golf Club
stories.script: The Pinx Golf Club is one of Jun Itami’s series of works built in this area alongside Bangju Church and Podo Hotel. Critics often refer to Itami as “having the craftsmanship as if he hand-makes architecture.” When we look at this building, it feels as if we are looking at a huge sculpture in harmony with nature.  It is interesting that its overall shape was designed to coincide with that of Hallasan Mountain you see behind it. What is also impressive is that it is well assimilated as if it is buried in the ground without going against the horizon, which is emphasized with a widened feel. For the exterior finish, Iranian red marble and Korean black bricks were used. Some praised it as a crystal of architectural beauty that harmonizes nature and art.  You can see the last hole from the restaurant lounge on the second floor and also get a clear view all the way south to even Sanbangsan Mountain and Marado Island.

stories.title: Itami Course — Bangju Church
stories.script: One of the last works of Jun Itami, Bangju Church embodies Noah’s Ark from the Bible. Creating a pond on top of a 400-meter-high oreum and floating an ark on it well displays the picturesque imagination of Jun Itami, also a painter during his career.  For the materials, water, light, wood and metal that actually appear in the Bible were used to show the harmony with nature sought after by the architect. The slightly curved roof line is attractive, and the metal plates covering the roof express diverse beauty depending on the light like jewels. As you can see, the roof touching the sky and the water space facing the ground form a harmony, which seemingly produces a scene where a large boat spreads out its paddles and moves forward whenever the wind blows and waves form in the tank. The interior features narrow windows evenly placed in between wooden walls, creating stripe patterns with natural light. Just before entering the chapel at the point where the roof bends, there is a small window inside that faces the sky. It symbolizes the window from the biblical story of Noah’s Ark: after the Great Flood, Noah sent out a dove through this window to check if the ground had dried up.  Bangju Church won the Architecture Award at the Kim SwooGeun Cultural Award in 2002 and the Grand Award at the Korean Institute of Architects Awards in 2010.

stories.title: Itami Course — Bonte Museum
stories.script: Opened in November 2012, Bonte Museum is a work created by Tadao Ando, a Japanese master architect having won the Pritzker Prize, the so-called Nobel Prize in architecture. He is famous for his architectural philosophy that considers harmony with the surrounding environment.  “Bonte” means “the purpose of exploring the original,” and the museum is designed with the concept of tradition and modernity adapting to the land of Jeju. It also features a harmony of exposed concrete, which is Ando's trademark, roof tiles containing Korean sentiments and traditional stone walls, and has five exhibition halls, a sculpture park and Bonte Cafe. Overall, it has a maze-like composition, which makes the movement inside interesting; when you go to Exhibition Hall 1, you get to walk on water while in Exhibition Hall 2, you walk under the water. The exhibits give you a chance to meet the masters of modern art from Yayoi Kusama to Nam June Paik. In particular, Exhibition Hall 1 displays a rich collection of folk crafts. There is an open space connecting the wide hall and the main exhibition hall underneath the deep eaves on the second floor, and you may also get a view of the sea and surroundings of Jeju Island through a large window.

stories.title: Ando Course — Hyeopja Beacon
stories.script: Hyeopja Beacon is a means of communication that utilized torchlight and smoke to deliver urgent political or military-related news. It served similar functions as the well-known Bongsudae. Unlike typical beacons installed at the top of a mountain, these types of beacons were built on hills or coastal areas.  Alongside Maldeungpo and Somaro, Hyeopja Beacon is one of the three beacons in Jeju that still maintain their original form. It is designated as Monument No. 23-2 of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province. Hyeopja Beacon has been able to maintain its original shape thanks to long and broad rocks that are piled up in layers, which help withstand lateral force. Ten layers of long plate stones are constructed in the irregular piling method. It is a trapezoidal stone structure whose entrance is 0.7 m wide and upper section is 8.6 m in both length and width and 3.1 m tall. At the top of the beacon, there is a flat and round fire pot with a diameter of 4.2 m where people made a fire back in the day.

stories.title: Ando Course — Bangdupo Lighthouse
stories.script: Bangdupo Lighthouse is located at the end of Seopjikoji Trail and has a nickname of “Wish Lighthouse.” It is a white, 7-meter-tall lighthouse at about 40 m above sea level. It is seated on top of Jeju's red volcanic foundation so the harmony among the red ground, white lighthouse and blue sea is impressive.  There is Seonnyeobawi Rock right underneath the lighthouse and a legend has it that seonnyeo, or fairies of Heaven, came down to earth every night and took baths here. One night, the son of the Dragon King of the Sea secretly watched the fairies taking a bath. The fairies eventually caught him and were no longer able to come down to this place ever again. The Dragon King's son prayed for the fairies to come back and in the end, received a promise that he would be able to marry a fairy when she comes down to earth on the 100th day. On the 100th day, however, the waves became so violent that the fairies weren't able to come down and the son of the Dragon King who was waiting for them eventually turned into a rock at this location. It is interesting that the rock was not a fairy but the youngest son of the Dragon King.  The view of Bangdupo Lighthouse and Seonnyeobawi Rock is especially beautiful from the Seopjikoji Trail. Thanks to such picturesque scenery, it has been a popular spot to film numerous TV series, including All In, Warm and Cozy and Orange Marmalade.

stories.title: Ando Course — Glass House
stories.script: The Glass House is another work by Tadao Ando along with the Yumin Art Nouveau Collection (formerly Genius Loci). It is not common for works of a master to be built in a series in one area so it would be nice to compare and appreciate the two works. While the Yumin Art Nouveau Collection feels as if it is perfectly assimilated into the environment, the Glass House rises above the ground and is visible from everywhere in Cape Seopjikoji. Similar to an UFO that has made an emergency landing, the building has a completely different vibe from Yumin Art Nouveau Collection.  It is actually a restaurant built on a beach with the sunrise view that looks like a V-shaped glass box installed on the second floor. Geometric planes with the exposed concrete and glass while excluding fancy decorations create uniqueness of the building. This also feels like a modern sculpture rather than a building. As you gradually get closer to the Glass House from afar, the view of Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone can be seen through the window created between the buildings that seem to be connected to each other. The first floor is located 3.6 m above the entrance, and the backside is closed whereas the front surface made of glass is wide open. Sunrise Park is a plaza built for people to see the sunrise and a view of the vast sea.

stories.title: Songdo Central Park
stories.script: Songdo Central Park is located in the center of the Songdo International Business Complex in Incheon. It is the first seawater park in Korea that uses water withdrawn from the sea. It is also an urban park that takes advantage of Korea's topographical characteristics.   The artificial waterway serves as a landmark and tranquil gathering spot in Songdo, where visitors can take in the park's many displays of cultural artifacts. It is a waterway with a length of 1.8 km and a maximum width of 110 m that flows across Central Park. The combination of lush vegetation and towering skyscrapers gives the area an exotic feel. Exotic sculptures and works of art line the long promenade. Water taxis, canoes, and boats are just some of the water leisure activities available from the boathouses in the east and west.   There is an observatory of the IFEZ Promotion Center located to the northwest. Located on the center's 33rd floor, it provides sweeping views of the surrounding area, including the park, Incheon Bridge, and Songdo International City. The park is even more stunning when illuminated by the city at night. With the moon boat glowing on the lake at night, Central Park is a sight to behold. As its name suggests, it is a boat in the shape of the moon. Passengers can listen to their own music via Bluetooth from their phones while taking in the beautiful nightscape of Songdo.

stories.title: Deer Park in the Songdo Central Park
stories.audioTitle: Deer Park in the Songdo Central Park
stories.script: Playing with the animals in downtown   Daughter : Dad, are we going to see beautiful animals at the park today?  Dad : Yes! There’s a Deer Park on the way to the center of the Central Park. We’ll arrive soon.  Daughter : Look! There’s a deer with horns. There’s a baby deer too!  Dad : Isn’t it cute? It’s called Formosan deer, which is from Korea, Japan and many other Asian countries. How limpid their eyes are!  Daughter : Yes it is. They look like as if they are posing for the people. How cute! It’s wonderful to see them this close. Can I touch the deer, Dad? It’s just an arm’s length.  Dad : If you feed or touch them too much, it will make the deer annoyed. Let’s only look and not touch them, okay? There are some cute rabbits when you walk through the Deer Park by the seaside.  Daughter : Can we see the rabbits close like the deers at the Deer Park?  Dad : Yes, we can see the Rabbit Island closely when we ride a water taxi.  Daughter : Then let’s look around the Deer Park! By the way, what’s that next to the watermill?  Dad : It is one of the eight scenic views of Songdo Central Park called “Songhajeong Pavilion.“ It is an ideal place to avoid the heat because the waterwheel is spinning right next to the lake.  Daughter : It will be great to take a picture over there. Wait, what are people doing over there?  Dad : That’s the acupressure trail where you can relieve fatigue by walking over the pebbles. Taking a walk along the dense forest and smelling the wood from the tress at Metasequoia Tree Road will refresh your mood in the Central Park.  Daughter : There are so many things to do in the Central Park! It will be wonderful to go on a picnic next time by carrying a lunch box.

stories.title: G-Tower Sky Park
stories.script: Dazzling panorama of Songdo   Dad : This place is called G-Tower where several executive offices of International Organizations including Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority (IFEZA), Green Climate Fund (GCF), UN agency and etc. are located. Let’s go to the Observatory on the 33rd floor of G-Tower where you can see a panoramic view of Songdo.  Daughter : Wow, I can see every part of Songdo just at a glance like what you said. Every place we’ve been to looks so small. There is Central Park, Hanok Village, Compact-Smart City and Tri-bowl.   Dad : Isn’t the view different from what see saw below? Because of a fine view you can enjoy up here, you can see amazing sunset and nightscape here in G-Tower.  Daughter : Oh, Dad! I see a long bridge over there.  Dad : That’s the Incheon Bridge. It is the biggest and longest bridge in Korea that connects Songdo International Business District and Yeongjongdo Island. In addition, the G-Tower has space for VR-ZONE, ECO-ZONE, and Multi-Room where you can experience virtual reality. You will know easily about Songdo there.  Daughter : Wow, let me try it!  Dad : Careful not to suffer from motion sickness after doing it too much.

stories.title: Songdo Hanok Village
stories.script: Friendly Hanok Village in downtown   Dad: Don’t you think a Korean traditional house, Hanok, lingers on your mind? In particular, Hanok village, which has Hanok hotel, restaurants, cultural experience facilities, event facilities and souvenir shops, makes you experience the past in this modern days.   Daughter: It really does. Experiencing Hanok Village in the downtown of Incheon allows visitors to experience the past, present and future that are connected with each other.  Dad: Yes. I hope there are more places to experience Korean traditional houses in the center of the city.  Daughter: You’re right. Many visitors from abroad can take the pic of the day here with the beauty of Korea.

stories.title: Songdo Tri-bowl
stories.script: Landmark of Songdo   Dad: Look at that! That’s the Tri-bowl, the land mark of Songdo. Isn’t it magnificent? Do you see that the buildings are shaped as three bowls? It’s a portmanteau of “Triple“ and “Bowl,” symbolizing the three areas of Incheon — Yeongjong, Chengna and Songdo — or sky, ocean and ground.  Daughter: The building makes me feel like I’m in a foreign country. It’s all connected with one another though it looks like a separate building. It’s so cool.  Dad: Yes. It was also acknowledged architecturally as it was awarded as “this year’s Korea Architecture Award“ in 2010.  Daughter: Impressive! What’s in that huge Tri-bowl?  Dad: In this stunning Tri-bowl floating on the water, exhibitions of contemporary art based on photography and free jazz performances are regularly held, as well as educational programs! In short, it’s a cultural space for citizens!  Daughter: I’d like to recommend this place to my big brother for his date with his girlfriend.  Dad: I guess it’s really a nice place for lovers to enjoy a romantic night view because of its splendid lights at night.

stories.title: Songdo Compact-Smart City
stories.script: Past, Present and Future of Songdo   Daughter : It looks like all the buildings are high and shiny in Korea!  Dad : Isn’t it amazing that the buildings looks like as if they are touching the sky?  Daughter : That high building over there looks like an ice cream we just had.  Dad : Oh, you’re talking about the Northeast Asia Trade Tower (NEATT). As you said, it acts as a landmark of new town of Songdo because of its shape like an ice cream. Besides, inside the building, it is used for business facilities and accommodations, which is a trading ground for domestic and global companies.  Mom : There are various buildings in a new town of Songdo. First, let’s go to Compact-Smart City where we can take a look at how Incheon has progressed over time.  Daughter : Mom, is this Compact-Smart City? It doesn’t really looks like as its name suggests.   Mom : If the Incheon Museum contains traditional culture of Incheon, with its port opened for more than 2,000 years which had been introduced to outer cultural influx, the Compact-Smart City is a place which shows how Incheon has evolved from past, present and future.  Dad : In addition, you will see the changing face of Incheon through various exhibitions and programs.

stories.title: Woninjae
stories.script: The House of Incheon Yi Clan   Dad: Hush! This is a private place where people live, so you shouldn’t make loud noises.  Daughter: Okay. We almost couldn't make it though, it‘s opened from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.  Dad: Yes, you are right. Let’s go inside anyway. Woninjae is built in front of the gravesite of Heogyeom Lee who is Jungsijo of Incheon surname Lee.  Daughter: What’s Jungsijo? It’s hard to understand.  Dad: Well, it means an ancestor who revitalized the declining family. This is from Heogyeom Lee during which Incheon Lee entered the ranks of the nobility during the Koryo Dynasty.  Daughter: So it means that the family became rich because of him, right?  Dad: Haha. To simply, you are correct. After that, all three of his granddaughters became queens of King Hyeonjong of Koryo. The first granddaughter, queen Wonsung gave a birth to Deokjong and Heongjong. The second granddaughter gave a birth to Munjong and then formed the powerful clique of aristocratic seventh generations from Munjong to Injong.  Daughter: So, it’s called the “Family Clan of Seventh Generation“ of the Koryo Dynasty, right? But why is it called Woninjae?  Dad: Woninjae means that Incheon Lee’s origin of each party is from Incheon.  Daughter: Ah, I get it. The roof is very colorful and antique as you can see in the Korean historical drama.  Dad: Yes. Particularly, Woninjae was built with the most beautiful tiled roof, which has architectonic beauty of the gambrel roof emitting traditional atmosphere.

stories.title: Nonhyeondong  sheep ranch
stories.script: Flock of Sheep in Incheon   Dad : Why don’t we go and see the sheep? There’s sheep ranch in Nonhyeon-dong near here.  Daughter : Wow, theres a ’sheep ranch in Incheon?  Dad : Yes, the sheep used to live in Gangwon-do Province but they adapted to Eco-Park Green Belt Construction Business. The sheep ranch itself isn’t big enough, but it’s a great place for outing as the park is huge.  Daughter : Great! Dad, there’s a big lake and a tower!  Dad : That’s the Namdong Tower. Because there’s observatory, restaurant, and swimming pool, it’s used as a leisure facility. At night, it emits various colorful lights. Let’s go there if we have some time left. There are various things to see at the Lake Park.  Daughter : I see many families are out here like us!  Dad : You’re right. There are many families and couples. Let’s come again bringing a lunch box next time.  Daughter : Sounds great! There are some people feeding the sheep.  Dad : Yes, but you should only give them the grass and leaves or they’ll get sick by eating vegetables like carrot or lettuce. Also, be careful not to get stabbed by the sheep’s hooves on your feet!  Daughter : I thought I had go to Gangwon-do Province to see the sheep but it’s so wonderful to see them here this close and to feed them as well.

stories.title: Nonhyeondong Forest of Hinoki Cypress
stories.script: Walk through the woods in downtown   Daughter : Dad, there is a forest over there!  Dad : Yes, it is called “Cypress Forest Barrier-Free Shared Road.“ Even people with disabilities can easily move around here. It’s a great opportunity to enjoy the forest in the middle of the city. The forest is rich in negative ions, so it has a cardiopulmonary function, and it helps to regain the vitality of the weary body, healing fatigue and cold.  Daughter : Yes, I’ve heard that taking the so called “green shower“ is good for health.  Dad : Also that tree is called Cypress Tree which contains plenty of phytoncide. Phytoncide refers to a tree that secretes natural antibacterial material to protect itself from insects and germs, which is particularly good for relieving stress.  Daughter : Wow, that’s why so many people are here. Look, there’s sunbed! Let’s take a rest there!  Dad : Okay. If there’s any book you want to read, there’s a Forest Library in the park, so you can visit there after taking a rest here.

stories.title: Nonhyeondong Playground of a Forest
stories.script: Various activities in the Playground   Daughter : Dad, while we are following the trail of cypress trees, I can see some other trees, too.  Dad : You’re right. This tree is called metasequoia, which is more than 30 meters tall. Due to the height, we can enjoy excellent view. Do you want to go to the playground in the forest over there?  Daughter : Sure! Here are some amazing rides like a swing.  Dad : Yes, it looks very fun. However, be careful not to fall down.  Daughter : Okay. There’s a fairy tale cabin over there. It’s very interesting that it’s different from our neighborhood.  Dad : I agree. Let’s take a look at Hanwha Historical Museum after the cabin. It’s a memorial hall containing the history of Korean gunpowder. The scale is small, but it will be fun to enjoy a variety of attractions and experiences.

stories.title: Incheon Butterfly Park
stories.script: Like a butterfly   Butterfly Park is decorated with butterfly even from the entrance, making you feel like as if you became a butterfly. You will see the huge park with fresh energy from the entrance and colorful scenery of butterflies that unfolds in front of you. Cotton candies and cute balloons in front of the park looks exciting. Let’s take a look inside.  If you want to smell the green sprouts growing rapidly and the soil of nature surrounded by dense forest and grass, spend time at the Garden of Soil and Aquatic Botanical Garden. A tent is provided to avoid the scorching sun. Isn’t it worth a visit?  Like the name Butterfly Park, there are spaces to observe the butterfly. First of all, you can see some sample of insects, such as butterflies, dragonflies, and spiders. If butterflies hide from the heat at the Butterfly Eco Center, take a breath and eat between meals at the Wild Flower Dongsan and Rest Area. You can calm your mind by seeing butterflies flying around and by feeding the rabbits with carrots. Take photos of cute animals; lie down, relax and enjoy the wide expanse of sky free from soaring skyscrapers.  Another special place only available in the Butterfly Park is Sound Dongsan. Listen to the resonance passing through the Sound Tunnel and a voiceless sound of xylophone made by woods.  If you walk 5 minutes from the Butterfly Park, you can enjoy a cool water from the valley with your kids.

stories.title: Sangokdong Mural Village
stories.script: To the imagination   A girl opens a closet in a room; a fairy tale story unfolds in another green grassland world! It is a Sangok-dong Mural Village, which is hidden behind apartment buildings and a market.  If you want to escape from the noisy and tiresome city life, Sangok-dong Mural Village in Bupyeong is a perfect getaway. The humble and quiet atmosphere of the low residential quarters soothes your mind.  A lonesome place once filled with the sign saying “Beware of the dog” is now crowded with people, full of mural paintings at all corners, which is a result of the Incheon Arts Association.  Change of four seasons can be clearly noticed in this place, where giraffes and polar bears get along together, and lush tress coexist with icy roads — the place had turned into a friendly  crime-free village.  Since we’ve heard many stories about residents who have lost their homes and villages knocked down for redevelopment, the case of Sangok-dong, Bupyeong is unique, where the residents revived their old village through communications and constructed themed mural village.  There are residents living in each house here, so please be quiet while walking through this village.

stories.title: Bupyeong Sinteuri Park
stories.script: Dancing with white horse   Bupyeong-gu Office Station. Turn your eyes and you’ll see the green space that lies in front of you; it’s the Bupyeong Sinteuri Park. The park is located on the way to the road from Bupyeong-gu Office Station to Gulpocheon Station, where you can hear the voices of cheers, shouts and laughter.  You can feel the passion of the athletes at the sports facilities such as soccer stadiums, tennis courts, and badminton courts. Night lighting for sports enthusiasts at gymnasiums are a popular  scenary in the Sinteuri Park.  There is no special admission in Sinteuri Park. You can exercise 24/7 at any time. In addition to the sports facilities, visitors can use other facilities such as playground, trails, Shadow House to visit with their families, lovers and friends.  The biggest attraction of Sinteuri Park is the fountain of white horse statue, which looks like the Palladium — the symbol of the park — is dancing with joy. This is why Sinteuri Park is called the “White Horse Park.“  If you arrive at the time of the fountain operation, you will be able to take the picture of the day, dancing together with the white horse in front of the white horse fountain.

stories.title: Bupyeong Market
stories.script: Add one basket of Incheon   Bupyeong Market is a typical traditional market in Bupyeong. There is a public parking lot near Bupyeong Market Station of Incheon Subway Line No.1, making visitors to come to the market easily. Even if you don’t have a car, you can easily take the public transportation such as subway.  The biggest attraction of the Bupyeong Market is a traditional market in downtown. If you walk a few steps away from the crowded marketplace, you can see the busy cars paassing by and people of the city of Incheon. If you turn back again, you can see the scenes of friendly market of Incheon. What a unique and attractive place!  If you really want to know and experience the city, you have to know the lives of the citizens; here at Bupyeong Market, you can experience the actual life of people living in Incheon — voices that ask for a lower price, people who are lined up in front of the restaurant, and crowded Incheon citizens walking through the marketplace.  Before visiting Bupyeong Market, there is only one thing you need to prepare: the basket to put in the stuffs you buy at the market. Put in the fresh vegetables, fish, and food such as sweet and sour chicken and bread. Finally, please take Incheon citizens, merchants and yourself in it!

stories.title: Bupyeongyuk Station underground shopping area
stories.script: A mall that has everything    Located at the Bupyeong Station, Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center is famous for its lively atmosphere. It is also called “Bupyeong Modoo Mall,“ the nation’s largest underground shopping center, which boasts a large scale of over 15 underpass shopping districts. Bupyeong Modoo Mall set the Guinness World Record for being the largest shopping place.  There are more than 1,000 stores in the underground shopping mall, which allow visitors to compare prices and do window-shopping at a variety of stores, including clothes, shoes, cosmetics, jewelry, mobile phones, restaurants, and grocery stores. You can find various kinds of goods here; as people often say, “If you can’t find what you are looking for in this place, that is nowhere to be found.“ After work or school, you can get off at the subway station and go shopping quickly and conveniently.  Are you afraid of getting lost in this wide underground shopping mall? Then set up the direction machine and mark the route by dividing the entire street with green, orange, red and blue roads.  There is “Bupyeong Rotary Market“ in the underground shopping center which is a youth culture shop managed by the youth. Not only can you experience a variety of culture, but also you can see the items containing the dreams of youth such as food, leather crafting products and facial mask sheets.  If you’ve fully enjoyed at the Bupyeong Station Underground Shopping Center and Modoo Mall, why don’t you move onto the Culture Street?

stories.title: Bupyeong Culture Street
stories.script: Full of Variety   Bupyeong Culture Street is not far away from exit nos. 24–30 of Bupyeong Station, which is known as a keyword of “Bupyeong restaurant“ on social media, known for its many famous restaurants and cafés.  Why don’t you visit board game cafés with your friends and enjoy board games and drink beverages? How about spending some romantic time at the proposal zone with your beloved ones after enjoying your meal and shopping? It will also be nice to spend some time with your family trying out various foods. It is a perfect place to hang around and shop alone as well.  Make your way to the exit no. 30 of Bupyeong Station, and you will see the Flea Market that opens from noon to evening every Saturday. The flea market sells various goods such as character goods, accessories, clothing, miscellaneous items, postcards and food, so you will lose the track of time. Shall we start looking around?  Flea Market is crowded with sellers and shoppers because of its cheap entry fee (KRW 10,000) and a lot of floating population from Culture Street. At the outdoor stage, everyone, from adolescent to middle-aged, can enjoy performances every weekend.  Now, let’s move on to the Theme Street.

stories.title: Bupyeong Theme Street
stories.script: Having fun at the fair   The Theme Street connected with Culture Street varies widely with different feelings of joy. The restaurant, video arcade and karaoke standing in a line of this street are some of the perfect places to hang out with friends. This Street is recommended for people who enjoy drinking alcohol or love spending time with their friends. There are various shops and restaurants in the alley along the street; you can decide where you want to go among multiple choices.  From September to October, the festival takes place throughout the streets of the Theme Street and Culture Street, which consist of Performance Madang with creative performances, Street Madang where visitors can see parade and busking, Experience Madang to enjoy pungmul (traditional Korean dance and music performed in Korea’s rural regions), art, traditional culture and etc., Contest Conference and Marketplace.  The Pungmul festival was held as a motif for the joy and amusement of Korea from traditional farming communities. Throughout the festival, the sound of kkwaenggwari (small gong), janggu (Korean drum), jing (gong), the figure of colorful flag and Sangmokkun (dancers who twirl the sangmo)’s twirling sangmo (traditional Korean hat), will paint the main street of Bupyeong.  The highlight of the festival’s opening ceremony, which begins on the last day of the festival, blocks the entry of the main street of Bupyeong’s eight-lane, and turns into a square for the parade. Let’s enjoy the time when the performers, citizens, and tourists can become one.

stories.title: Cheongna Middle Lake Park
stories.script: Healing place with dream and romance   Cheongna Middle Lake Park is a park located in Cheongna International City, which boasts of various things to see and enjoy. It is separated into Eco Cultural Space, Art Cultural Space, Tradition Cultural Space and Leisure Cultural Space; while walking through the lake, you will easily find every facilities.  Inside of the Leisure Cultural Space, there are Music Fountain, Urban Beach, Outdoor Music Hall, Multi-Plaza and etc. Music Fountain operates until 8 p.m. and closes on Mondays.  Multi-Plaza is the best place to go outing with your children which has various amusement facilities to enjoy.  In the middle of the lake, there are some artificial islands which have its own theme: Flower Music Island, Eco Festival Island, Iris Island and Waterfowl Island. The City-Tower is planned to be built as well.  You might not be able to walk all around the park at once; you can take a rest at interesting shaped benches that are surrounding the lake. Dont you want to spend some quality time with your beloved, families, and friends at this lake?

stories.title: Dream Park Wild Flower Garden
stories.script: Trash turns into flower blossom   Dream Park is a wild flower park constructed on Sudokwon Landfill Site, where visitors can meet many work of arts made by various kinds of wild flowers, recycling material and waste coming from a landfill. Passing through Metasequoia Garosugil Road, which is famous for being the filming location of the Korean drama “Goblin,“ you will see the entrance.  Wildflower Garden is constructed to observe the surrounding landscape and environment that changes its color every season, which is classified according to the period of florescence and place for growth and development. It can also be divided into Rock Garden, Marsh Eco Park, and Lily Park.  There are over 200 kinds of herbaceous plants with 58 kinds of chaplain and 49 kinds shrub of blossom separated into 18 places with scale of 62,500㎡ (about 18,700 pyeong) in Rock Garden, Sweet Smelling Garden, Hue Harmony Garden and etc.  When you enter the Wildflower Garden, you will be greeted by yellow rape blossoms and fancy poppies. Walking slowly through the guide of butterflies and bees, you can see the peony field with beautiful powder pink floral leaf. Seeing an opened flower garden and well-shaded street with trees under the cumulus, you can find the peace in you mind.

stories.title: Jeongseojin
stories.script: A friend of Jeongdongjin   Have you heard about Jeongdongjin in Gangwon-do Province? Jeongdongjin means the sea located at the far east of Gwanghwamun in Seoul by riding a horse; symmetrically from Jeongdongjin, there is Jeongseojin in Incheon. Jeongseojin is in Seo-gu, Incheon Metropolitan City, at the starting point of Gyeongin Ara Waterway.  While heading to Jeongseojin, you can see the enormous wind power generator. Don’t let that enormous wind turbine catch your eye and make sure to captivate the beautiful Rose Tunnel and peaceful reed marsh.  When you arrive at Jeongseojin and turn right, you can see the Noeuljong (Sunset Bell), a sculpture where you can hear beautiful music. While seeing the beautiful colors of sunset, you can find the footprints of many people who passed through this place. The pebble-shaped sculpture was made inspired by ebb and flood of the West Coast and the inner shape represents the restart.  While walking down the street, you will arrive at the Ara Tower before you know. How about looking at the pictures displayed in the lobby? It is a nice place to stop by with a cup of coffee. If you have learned about the history of and story behind Jeongseojin and Ara Waterway in the promotional hall, it is time to move to the observatory at the 23rd floor.  Let’s go to the Ara Waterway after the Ara Tower. There is a lake where Ara Waterway was built up for citizens to enjoy a walk, modeled bushland, Haesolgul and Kayak. You can see Jeongseojin here that changes throughout a year.  Jeongseojin is a beautiful place filled with families, friends and lovers. It is also a place full of stories from different people such as photographer who wants to capture every moment here and youth who crossed the country road with dreams. What stories are you writing in your life? Come and fill your story here at Jeongseojin.

stories.title: Fashion Jewelry Town
stories.script: Daegu Fashion Jewelry Town A place full of beauty  This building, which perfectly fits the city of fashion and jewelry, consists of two underground floors and eight ground floors. The first floor consists of jewelry stores and the second floor is home of businesses related to fashion, wedding supplies and beauty. The third floor has permanent and planned exhibition halls as well as an experience hall while the fourth floor consists of a design research center, education and seminar rooms, and a jewelry appraisal room. There is also a jewelry factory on the fifth to eighth floors where you can see everything about beauty in a single building. In particular, many soon-to-be-married couples preparing wedding gifts or jewelry-related engineers frequently visit the place. Another advantage of this place is the fact that there is no fixed price list because it is determined by the current market price.   <This guide was recorded by Park Jin of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Gyodong Jewelry Street
stories.script: Gyodong Jewelry Street  Gyodong Jewelry Street A street of luxury that satisfies your taste   Gyodong Jewelry Street started when a few watch stores were established in Gyodong Market in the 1970s. There were only a handful of watch stores and repair shops in the beginning, but more and more stores were setup in the area to form a street. As time passed, there were jewelry stores dealing with gold, which led the street to become a major jewelry street in downtown Daegu.  Stores here both sell and manufacture goods to meet custom-made orders. Many of the stores are reliable as they are headed by master craftsmen who have worked on this street for a long time.  After 6 PM, Gyodong Dokkaebi Market nearby offers tasty foods that satisfy both your eyes and mouths.

stories.title: Gukchaebosang Memorial Park
stories.script: Gukchaebosang Memorial Park Pay off the country’s debts  This is a park to commemorate the National Debt Repayment Movement. The National Debt Repayment was a movement insisted and led by Seo Sang-don. It aimed at repaying the debt that Japan had forced onto Joseon by quitting smoking and collecting gold rings, for instance. Everyone, including commoners and the Emperor Gojong, participated in this movement. Although the National Debt Repayment Movement was not successful due to the opposition from Japan, it still has great significance in that the entire population united under the idea of saving the country.  In addition, the park was established in Daegu, which is the city where the National Debt Repayment Movement first began, with the will to overcome the IMF (International Monetary Fund) crisis by remembering those times without falling in despair.  There is the Foreign Debt Redemption Movement Memorial Hall inside the park where you can see and hear stories from those days. There is also a large bell called “Dalgubeol Big Bell” where the bell-tolling ceremony is held every New Year’s Day.   <This guide was recorded by Park Jin of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Daeguhyanggyo Local Confucian School
stories.script: Daeguhyanggyo Local Confucian School The center of Daegu Confucians  This is a Hyanggyo, or a local Confucian school, located in Namsan-dong, Jung-gu, Daegu. Daeguhyanggyo Local Confucian School was founded in 1398 (the 7th year of King Taejo’s reign) in Gyo-dong to enshrine ancestral tablets of sages and to educate and edify locals.  A mud wall stretches long and horizontally to clearly divide left and right. On the left side, there are relatively recently built structures such as Myeongnyundang Lecture Hall and Nagyukjae while Daeseongjeon Shrine (Daegu Cultural Heritage Material No. 1) is on the right side.  Today, it still continues the tradition of Confucianism in the community by being in charge of teaching Chinese classics and giving etiquette lessons as well as hosting traditional weddings.   <This guide was recorded by Park Jin of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Banwoldang
stories.script: Banwoldang A department store established by Koreans  Banwoldang, which was the name of a department store established by Koreans along with Muyeongdang during the Japanese colonial period, is now gone, and only its name, Banwoldang, remains. It is said that the former Banwoldang building was located near Exit 22 of today's Banwoldang Station. At the time, Banwoldang was a two-story, wooden department store widely loved by people. Banwoldang has now been long gone without a trace, but the name still lives in Daegu to refer to places nearby such as Banwoldang Intersection and Banwoldang Station.   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Gwandeokjeong Martyrs' Memorial
stories.script: Gwandeokjeong Martyrs' Memorial The site of Daegu Catholic martyrdom  It is a representative Catholic martyrdom site in Daegu. During the Joseon Dynasty, there was a military training ground here where they selected military officers, and one side of it was used for execution of felons. The name originated from Gwandeokdang, which was Dosicheong, a military service examination center, established by Governor Min Baek-sang during the reign of King Yeongjo. Later on, persecution against Catholics started, which led to the execution of many Catholic believers living in the Gyeongsang-do region at the military training ground next to it. The tears of Catholics who were martyred in the late Joseon period are remembered at the Martyrs’ Memorial.  At the entrance of the memorial hall, there is a monument commemorating the martyrs and a statue of St. John Yi Yun-il. A stone torture device used to persecute martyrs is on display as well. In the basement of the memorial hall, there is a church where people can pray as well as the remains of the sacrificed saints. Please look around quietly with a heart of reverence and take pictures only after getting permission not to not disturb those who are praying.   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: St. Justin Seminary
stories.script: St. Justin Seminary The college days of the late Cardinal Stephen Kim Sou-hwan  It is a European-style theological school building with more than a hundred years of tradition. Bishop Demange, a French missionary, began to promote its establishment in 1911 after feeling the need for a theological school, and completed the construction in 1914. A mixture of Western Romanesque and Gothic styles, this building, though not splendid, is elegant. It is an important place in terms of not only its architectural value but also the history of Catholicism. Many students who studied here became priests and worked hard for the growth of Korean Catholicism.  A well-known figure who graduated from this school is the late Stephen Kim Sou-hwan who played an important role in Korean Catholicism. Kim is known to have studied here and ordained as a priest at Kyesan Catholic Church. It is still used as a theological school building today. There is a dormitory near the building so please be careful when you look around and take photos.   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Shrine of the Holy Mother in Daegu
stories.audioTitle: Shrine of the Holy Mother in Daegu
stories.script: Shrine of the Holy Mother in Daegu According to a vow dedicated to the Holy Mother   It was built by Bishop Demange by replicating Our Lady of Lourdes Cave in France. It is said that the bishop strove to replicate even the size and other details of the cave as much as possible so that it looks the same as the Lourdes Cave. Shrine of the Holy Mother in Daegu is a red brick building with a cave-like interior and a statue of Maria inside it. The proportional composition of each of the parts is beautiful and the structure of the bricks is elaborate, which is why the elements have well maintained their original forms to this day.  At the top of the building, it says “1911 EX VOTO IMMACULATAE CONCEPTIONI 1918.” 1911 is the year in which the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Daegu was first established and 1918 is the year when the three prayers that Bishop Demange had made to God all came true. “EX VOTO IMMACULATAE CONCEPTIONI” means “According to a vow dedicated to the immaculately conceived Virgin Mary without original sin.” It still serves as the place of prayer for many. Therefore, please take a look around quietly without disturbing those who are praying.   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres
stories.audioTitle: Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres
stories.script: Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres Living space of ascetics   If Dongsan is home to the Christianity culture, Namsan holds the history of Catholicism in Daegu. The Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres is a convent built in 1915 by Bishop Demange with the help of Bishop Robert. At that time, nuns were needed to take care of the elderly and orphans so a request for nuns was sent to the St. Paul Convent in France. The request was later accepted and the Sisters of St. Paul Chartres began to be built to help the nuns from France carry out their activities.  The architecture is of Romanesque and Gothic styles from which you can feel the tranquil beauty. The nuns who were here at the time volunteered to take care of orphans and the persons with disabilities, and the tradition is still alive today. Please remember that, because it is a convent, outsiders are not allowed to enter by themselves and can only be admitted after contacting the main gate information office.   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Lee Cheol-ho of Gurye
stories.script: Gurye Hyangje Julpungryu Story of Master Lee Cheol-ho   A master of Julpungryu who has spent all his life in preserving traditional cultures. “Julpungryu” is the type of music that old scholars played and listened to train their minds as they gathered in a sarangbang, or a guest room. Such music has mostly disappeared but it is still being passed down in two places, one of which is Gurye Hyangje Julpungryu, and the person who has served a decisive role for the continuance of the Gurye Julpungryu is Mr. Lee Cheol-ho. He trained to play the danso by himself and used his own funds to establish a preservation society in protection of traditional tunes. He also encouraged his children to major in gukak to carry on the family line.  Having lived a storybook life going from a boxer to a musician, Lee grew up listening to pungryu tunes at the side of his father who had frequent exchanges with musicians, however he did not study music starting at a young age. He actually learned how to box starting in middle school and became one of the greatest boxers in the nation as a high schooler. He was a rival to Kim Ki-soo who was famous as the first world boxing champion of Korea. But, in the 1960 Rome Olympics selection match, he lost to Kim and his participation at the Olympics was thwarted, becoming a dramatic turning point in his life. After leaving boxing for good, he maintained a quarry business for a while before running into Mr. Kim Mu-gyu, a teacher from his younger days, randomly at a cafe in Insa-dong, Seoul. And, thanks to the teacher, Lee then decided on his lifelong vocation.

stories.title: Hong Ssang-ri of Gwangyang
stories.script: Gwangyang Cheong Maesil Farm Story of Master Hong Ssang-ri   A well-educated daughter who became a farmer. A tearfully sad story which you can't help but giving a round of applause to. This is her life story. If you are with her only for a few moments, you will regain excitement and vigor for your life. Hong Ssang-ri was born a daughter of a famously wealthy house in Miryang, Gyeongsangnam-do. She was good looking, good at singing, confident, and eager to share with others. Then, when she became 23 years old, she got married to a man whose home was by Seomjingang River. What awaited her in this strange and remote place was a harsh trial, which included the need to care for her feeble husband and intense married life under her strict stepmother-in-law. The family's mining business had also gone bankrupt, prompting the loss of their lands and propagation of a huge debt.  Hong Ssang-ri! The name which has become a brand. She cried countless times and wanted to run away whenever she had a chance but what allowed her to persevere was the beautiful plum flowers of the farm. Though she was criticized by everyone, she consistently worked to turn the chestnut field into a plum flower field because she believed that was the only thing that could keep her going. She liked to cook different dishes with plums and continued to do her research. Pickled plums and the plum wine she made were popular among their guests. One of the regulars who loved her cooking was a producer at “MBC” who later helped introduce her to the world. “Cheong Maesil Farm” which she founded became the best plum brand and the city of Gwangyang even created a tour product called “Maehwa Plum Flower Festival” based on “Cheong Maesil Farm”. She was ultimately designated as a “Traditional Food Master” by the country.

stories.title: Geumhogang River Bank
stories.script: Let’s walk along the river bank   Geumhogang River Bank is one of Daegu’s rising attractions where you can walk along the river while feeling the river breeze. This is a place where you can see Geumhogang River, which goes around the upper part of Daegu to eventually meet with Nakdonggang River.  The river bank continues all the way along the river from Daesil Station on Daegu Subway Line 2 through the ARC Culture Center and up to Gangjeongbo. The bicycle path and pedestrian path are divided here so you can enjoy a safe walk in addition to biking and electric scooter riding. There are many families who come out to relax in the park and lawns next to the trail.  When you rent bicycles or scooters, most rental shops require you to wear safety gear and complete a training in advance on how to operate and ride safely. You also have to return them in time. If you ride a bike or a scooter, make sure to enjoy it safely by constantly checking your speed and pedestrians around you!   <This guide was recorded by Baek Ji-yoon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: The ARC
stories.script: Waves attracting attention day and night   The ARC Culture Center is located at the point where Nakdonggang and Geumhogang Rivers meet. Opened in September 2012, The ARC Culture Center is an architectural work of art that contains everything about rivers and water. The ARC, which is an acronym of “Architecture of River Culture” and “Artistry of River Culture,” refers to not only an elegant, geometric approach to the sky, earth and culture but also architecture and art that holds and values everything about the river culture.  This building was designed by world-famous architect Hani Rashid who was inspired by stone skipping that cuts across the river surface and fish jumping out of the water. Inside the ARC Culture Center, various exhibitions are being held under the theme of “Sympathy of River and People.” In particular, the blue “Greeting Men,” which fills the entire wall of the first floor lobby, are welcoming its guest.  If you go up to the observatory through stairs or the elevator, you can see Geumhogang and Nakdonggang Rivers at a glance. At night, beautiful lights shine brightly on the exterior walls of the building, adding to the night’s beauty.   <This guide was recorded by Baek Ji-yoon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Duryu Park
stories.script: A park where many people come and go   Duryu Park, one of the largest parks in Daegu, is a neighborhood park developed from 1965 to 1977. It is called “Duryu Park” since it is established on Duryusan Mountain along with Geumbongsan Mountain.  According to historical records, Duryusan Mountain was originally known as “Durisan” because of the round shape of the mountain. Then, when its name started to be written in Chinese characters, it was dubbed Jusan or Duryubong Peak, and recently, the name finally changed to Duryusan. Inside the park, there are E-World 83 Tower, a famous attraction of Daegu; Duryu Public Library, a place of study; various sports facilities that contribute to the promotion of citizens’ health; and Daegu Arts Center, a hall of civic culture.  Above all, it is widely loved by the citizens for small parks that have witnessed the historical events that took place in Daegu and for playgrounds and other facilities that anyone can access and relax in.   <This guide was recorded by Baek Ji-yoon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: February 28 Democratic Movement Memorial Monument in Duryu Park
stories.audioTitle: February 28 Democratic Movement Memorial Monument in Duryu Park
stories.script: Towards democratization   On February 28, 1960, students eager for democratization gathered and started a protest in Daegu. In the chaos created after the Korean War, President Rhee Syng-man became a dictator through rigged election. Students in Daegu who wished for the Republic of Korea to be reborn as an upright democratic nation put their lives on the line and ran out to Daegu Jungangno. Holding their first independent demonstration in which they shouted for freedom and justice, they revolted against the school becoming a political tool.  The students convened at the Gyeongsangbuk-do Provincial Office Plaza, which was in Daegu at the time, cried out, “We are just! Justice is alive!” and the police forces were deployed to suppress the resisting students. This demonstration had a significant influence on the whole country, eventually leading to the March 15 Masan Democracy Movement in the same year and helping to ignite the April 19 Revolution.  The memorial monument, which is now in Duryu Park, was originally erected on Myeongdeok Rotary in 1961. It was then relocated here in November 1989 to celebrate its 30th anniversary and was completed on February 28, 1990. Though the students who cried out for democratization have now become old men and women, young students today remember and carry on its significance.   <This guide was recorded by Baek Ji-yoon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Inmul Dongsan in Duryu Park
stories.script: The people that Daegu remembers   The road from the inside of Duryu Park to the outdoor performance stage is a small trail and a hill. It is “Inmul Dongsan” that pays tribute to many people that we need to remember, from Poet Yi Sang-hwa, Novelist Hyun Jin-geon, Patriot Park Hee-gwang, Patriot Cho Ki-hong, Painter Lee In-seong, Poet Choi Yang-hae, Poet Baek Ki-man and Poet Yi Jang-hui to a memorial tower for the independence movement of Daegu College of Education students. They are all people who were active in Daegu. There are statues and memorial towers of each of these people installed on the hill so you can meet them all as you take your time strolling on the path. Rose of Sharon and green trees you find here and there also serve as a reminder of the noble spirit and significance of the Inmul Dongsan. In particular, the memorial tower for the independence movement of Daegu College of Education students, which is the largest of them all, is a tower dedicated to the spirit of independence of the Daegu College of Education students who participated in the anti-Japan student movement in the 1940s. It would be nice to walk through the park and meet the people in history to take pride as their descendant.   <This guide was recorded by Baek Ji-yoon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Outdoor music hall in Duryu Park
stories.audioTitle: Outdoor music hall in Duryu Park
stories.script: The music hall on the green grassland   A place that offers a beautiful scenery in Duryu Park is the outdoor music hall. The lawn that stretches along the hill becomes an auditorium, and numerous performances held here become stages that spread happiness to the audience. Even on days without any performance, you can bring a mat and delicious snacks to enjoy a picnic if the weather is good. Daegu locals call this place by “Yadang” or “Duryu Yadang” for short.  Thanks to its wide open surroundings, it is a great photo spot where you can see the blue sky, green grass and a panoramic view of downtown Daegu. You can take jumping shots with your friends on a soft lawn, take neat pictures of the clouds traveling in the sky, or take landscape pictures of the city like the ones you can take from an observatory!  While you take the picture of your lifetime here at Daegu Yadang, make sure to throw garbage in trash bins and separate the recyclable waste!    <This guide was recorded by Baek Ji-yoon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Apsan Cable Car
stories.script: Apsan Mountain where you can go up while seated  The Apsan Cable Car, which has been a popular attraction of Daegu for a long time, takes its visitors up to the most famous observatory in Daegu. After passing Apsan Park, you can buy a ticket at the entrance and get on the cable car in the specified order. You can view both the downtown Daegu and Apsan Mountain on your way up on the cable car, which makes it a popular attraction for everyone.  The scenery of Daegu that slowly unfolds during the cable car ride will become an unforgettable memory. If you film a video on your way up, you will be able to keep the beautiful scenery forever.  Cable cars are running 365 days a year except on days when bad weather is predicted. The operating hours are announced every month so make sure to check the times before you go.   <This guide was recorded by Baek Ji-yoon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Apsan Observatory
stories.script: Must-see nightscape of Daegu!   How was the cable car ride or walk up to the observatory? This mountain is called “Apsan” since it is located in front of Daegueupseong Fortress, but it used to be referred to as Seongbulsan Mountain in the past. The name, “Apsan,” originated from how people back in the day thought based on geomancy that the south was where the main gate and the front side are located. This settled in people’s minds so today, most people call it “Apsan.”  If you have arrived on a cable car, you need to get off and walk up to the hill of the observatory. For those of you who can’t get to the observatory, don’t be too disappointed since you can also see it on the roof of the cable car building as well.  If you go during the day, you will be able to see downtown Daegu full of buildings, and if you go at night, you can get a 360-degree view of the city full of lights and street lamps. Please come and take a panoramic view of Daegu.   <This guide was recorded by Baek Ji-yoon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Suseongmot Lake
stories.script: A perfect place to go on a date   Suseongmot Lake, which can be seen when you take Daegu Subway Line 3 and get off at Suseongmot Station, is a place any Daegu local would have visited at least once. From kindergarten picnics to couple and family outings, it is a romantic place that you can’t help but visit again.  Suseongmot is an artificial lake that was originally made in 1925 during the Japanese colonial era for the purpose of supplying agricultural water. As the surroundings began to be developed in the 1980s, the lake was turned into a park and has become a place of picnics and relaxation for Daegu citizens along with Suseong Recreation Area.  The Suseongmot Festival (Suseong Festival), which started in 2013, is a well-known festival for many tourists and citizens. It is also popular by the splendid grand finale of fireworks that not only rise up into the night sky but also spread over the surface of the water.   <This guide was recorded by Baek Ji-yoon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour: 1_Awaiting Kim Kwang-seok
stories.audioTitle: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour: 1_Awaiting Kim Kwang-seok
stories.script: 1_Awaiting Kim Kwang-seok  Waiting for Kim Kwang-seok Bus Journey with Kim Kwang-seok   Many visitors come to Daegu in search of Kim Kwang-seok. “Hello, everyone. This is Kim Kwang-seok.” They will be greeted by a friendly welcome and a bright smile on the Kim Kwang-seok Bus. You must be filled with expectations for a unique trip where you get to enjoy the songs of Kim Kwang-seok in Daegu, his hometown where he spent his childhood. However, out of his entire lifetime, the period during which he lived in Daegu actually wasn’t that long. Still, his younger days where he played around and appreciated the charm of Daebong-dong and Bangcheon Market and the beautiful nature of Sincheon Stream are expressed in the form of melodies and lyrics and continue to live within us today. His hometown, Daegu, made a street for him and holds the “Re-Singing Kim Kwang-seok Contest” to commemorate him. Of course, Kim Kwang-seok Bus is our small attempt to get a step closer to him. It looks like the bus has arrived. Now, comfortably take a seat and let’s set out on a tour of Daegu together with Kim Kwang-seok.   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour   2_Passing Sincheon, Daegu
stories.audioTitle: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour: 2_Passing Sincheon, Daegu
stories.script: 2_Passing Sincheon, Daegu  Road that passes Sincheon, Daegu Where The Wind Comes From   You've all sat down comfortably, right? Okay, let’s begin the tour. There is a stream that the bus is going to pass at least once. Its name is “Sincheon,” a stream that flows next to Daebong-dong where Kim Kwang-seok used to live. This stream goes around Daegu and eventually flows to Geumhogang and Nakdonggang Rivers, also serving as a shelter for Daegu citizens. Shade of a willow like your hair, beautiful flowers blossom every season. In a small rest area on the waterfront, you will be able to feel nature within the city. The view of Sincheon Stream and Daegu that we see as we pass over Suseonggyo Bridge next to Daebong-dong takes us to Kim Kwang-seok's younger days and brings us many different feelings. Everyone, don't forget to request a song by being immersed into the scenery. How about sending a little note to the DJ to request one of Kim Kwang-seok’s songs?   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour   3_Kim Kwangseok Story House
stories.audioTitle: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour   3_Kim Kwangseok Story House
stories.script: 3_Kim Kwangseok Story House  Kim Kwangseok Story House A day of Kim Kwang-seok   Have you all enjoyed Kim Kwang-seok's songs on the bus? Let’s go outside with these feelings still intact. Let’s head over to Kim Kwangseok Story House located on one side of the Kim Kwang-seok Road. This little house is filled with items that Kim Kwang-seok had used when he was still alive. It is a place where you can get a glimpse of the daily life of Kim Kwang-seok as a singer. Seeing him wearing an apron and standing with a huge smile as if he invited us to his home, instead of singing and playing a folk guitar, makes us smile. On the first floor, there are sofa, drawers and many other items that he used. In a space where you can find his traces, you can imagine how the life of Kim Kwang-seok as a human being was. When you go up to the second floor, you will be able to meet Kim Kwang-seok as a singer through his albums and a guitar that he received as a gift. Just like your friend's dad who would show all the gifts he has received in a display cabinet when you visit your friend's house, it feels like Kim Kwang-seok would’ve also boasted shyly by saying something like, “Well, these are my albums.” After listening to the songs played in headphones, leave a message of greeting on a branch of the wish tree, “Hey, Kim. Do you remember those days?”   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour: 4_Kim Kwang-seok Road
stories.audioTitle: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour: 4_Kim Kwang-seok Road
stories.script: On Kim Kwang-seok Road Kim Kwang-seok that we know   The long alley between Bangcheon Market and Sincheon Stream became Kim Kwang-seok Road. Kim Kwang-seok on every wall and corner welcomes new people each day without being forgotten on the street. His songs are played at an outdoor performance stage in the middle of the road. The stage is a popular spot for those who love him and his songs. If you’ve watched a good performance, please stand like the spring sprouts and give a round of applause. The street features a variety of food vendors and small galleries that won't make you bored for even a second. It is also great to take commemorative photos next to Kim Kwang-seok statues in several places along the road. Don’t just look at it from afar but approach him and make sure to take a picture with him before you leave. On the path to Bangcheon Market, there is the Kim Kwang-seok Road Information Center as well as a writing that summarizes his life on a wall. Let’s remember a man named Kim Kwang-seok whose life began in this place and move onto our next stop, the market.   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour: 5_On the way out of Bangcheon Market
stories.audioTitle: Kim Kwang-seok Bus Tour: 5_On the way out of Bangcheon Market
stories.script: On the way out of Bangcheon Market I Hope all you are doing well.   It is said that Kim Kwang-seok loved to enjoy some soju in a pub after a performance. Bangcheon Market located at the end of the Kim Kwang-seok Road is indeed a market that reminds us of him. The market, which isn’t that big, sees more people at night who come out to eat dinner. Restaurants and stores that are set up like food stalls are great places to wrap up a trip. Once he reached adulthood, Kim Kwang-seok mostly sang and performed in Daehangno area in Seoul, so he probably doesn’t know how the market has changed. But he would still be glad to sit next to many people who still remember him today and have a cup of soju, don’t you think?  How was the tour around Kim Kwang-seok Road and Daegu today? For those who remember his beautiful melodies, simple yet resonating lyrics, and sincere voice, this place would become a memory and a piece of their daily lives. It feels like he’s saying to us right now, “I Hope all you are doing well.”   <This guide was recorded by Kim So-yeon of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Yeojwacheon Stream (Romance Bridge)
stories.script: Blooming romance Do not miss out on one of the best cherry blossom attractions in Jinhae, a 1.5-kilometer-long Yeojwacheon Stream. Trees alongside the stream naturally form a tunnel of cherry blossom. Additional lightings and sculptures installed during the festival add to the beautiful cherry blossom even at night.  All 15 bridges over the Yeojwacheon Stream have a different name. The most well-known bridge is the “Romance Bridge” located across from the Jinhae Girl's High School. Widely known as the filming location for the popular Korean TV series called “Romance” that was aired in 2002, it is a photo spot for couples until today. If you take a photo on the bridge, it captures the moment as if two of you are the only people in the place. Here are some tips to enjoy the cherry blossoms along the stream. First, walk down the stone stairs below the bridge. You can find a perfect photo spot to shoot cherry blossoms blowing in the wind. But be careful during rainy days as the level of the stream may rise. Second, be careful not to bump your head on the big and thick cherry blossom branches. And do not cause damage to the trees by breaking or shaking branches. Your cooperation will contribute to beautiful scenery next year.  Third, enjoy the unique charm of cherry blossoms at night! As numerous people come to enjoy the night view, pay extra attention not to get hurt. Make sure to carry your camera or smartphone with a necklace or a wrist strap, and keep your eyes on your smartphone not to fall off the selfie stick.

stories.title: Boseong Byeolsindang - Cheoninjeong and Byeolsindang, Bongnae-myeon
stories.audioTitle: Boseong Byeolsindang - Cheoninjeong and Byeolsindang, Bongnae-myeon
stories.script: Encounter of Confucian spirits and folk religion   As you walk up a little bit from the village, you will see a stone staircase that leads to Cheoninjeong and Byeolsindang where local Confucian scholars gathered to talk patriotism. This stone staircase leads to two different paths. To one side, what welcomes you is a forest of bamboo trees, which symbolize the upright spirit of scholars.
