However, according to the “Painting of Eastern Palace”, the area from the pavilion to Chundangdae in Changdeokgung’s Secret Garden was an open space with almost no trees, which allowed it to be the perfect place for military drills and examination venues.  The traces of archery range are left in Gwandeokjeong Pavilion. Near the fence, there are shooting lines and stones used to place bows. It is presumed that the target was installed in front of them for archery training. If you stand behind the shooting line, you will be looking in the direction of Grand Greenhouse and garden.  King Jeongjo, an avid archer, frequently visited the Gwandeokjeong Paviliony. It is well known that King Jeongjo showed up in the archery range during the national examinations held at Chundangdae of Changdeokgung Palace. Now, let’s stand on the waiting line and appreciate the view of Gwangdeokjeong Pavilion.

stories.title: Gwancheondae Observatory (Changgyeonggung Palace)
stories.script: Gwancheondae Observatory was located south of Myeongjeongjeon Hall, the main hall of Changgyeonggung Palace. It was a government agency responsible for the observation of the movement of the sun, moon, stars, change of seasons, and the twenty-four solar terms, which were managed by the Meteorological Office (Gwansanggam).  According to the “Record of the Office of Astonomy and Geomancy”, Gwancheondae Observatory was built in 1688 during the reign of King Sukjong. However, all the buildings at the site of Gwancheondae Observatory were demolished during the Japanese colonial period; instead, a zoo was built. In 1986, as the restoration project of Changgyeonggung Palace began, the zoo was relocated to the Seoul Grand Park in Gwacheon, and the site became an open plaza where only a stone stylobates remained with the name of Gwancheondae.  There are several rumors about what kind of device was placed there. One of them was pointing to a latitude-measuring instrument called the Soganuidae, which was used to observe the constellations at night. Another indicated a sundial called Ilyeongdae, which was used to keep track of the season and date.  Therefore, only the stone stylobate with five holes drilled in the granite remained in the Gwancheondae Observatory, which is presumed to be the one that has been used to place apparatus. Nevertheless, no one can ensure what instruments were placed on it.

stories.title: Seoninmun Gate (Changgyeonggung Palace)
stories.script: The Seoninmun Gate of Changgyeonggung Palace is a small gate connecting to the south wall of Honghwamun Gate, the main entrance of the palace. Its name means widespread kindness”. According to “Note on the Eastern State,, Seoninmun Gate was originally called Seolinmun Gate and served as the main east gate for the officials to enter the palace. Seoninmun Gate was built during the reign of King Seongjong. However, it was destroyed during the Japanese invasion of Joseon. It was then later rebuilt during the reign of King Gwanghae and was destroyed again in 1857. The current gate was presumed to have been rebuilt during the reign of Emperor Gojong. Inside the Seoninmun Gate, there was the Royal Clothing Office. It was responsible for making clothes for the king. Also, there was a 400-year-old pagoda tree painted in the “Painting of the Eastern Palace”. Seoninmun Gate has witnessed several tragic incidents involving the royal family of Joseon. The first royal family member to leave the palace through the Seoninmun Gate was Crown Prince Sohyeon. He and his family returned to the palace after being taken hostage by the Qing for nine years. Sadly, the prince died two months later, and his wife was hated by his father, King Injo. The son of Crown Prince Sohyeon was supposed to take the crown prince’s position under the principle of succession. However, King Injo gave the title to Prince Bongnim, who was the younger brother of Crown Prince Sohyeon. Crown Princess Sohyeon complained about the result to King Injo, which led to his being punished from confinement. One day, King Injo found poison in his meal, and he believed Crown Princess Sohyeon was the instigator. He ordered the death penalty for the Crown Princess. As a result, she was sent out of the palace by passing through the Seoninmun Gate and passed away after drinking the poison King Injo gave her. Three sons of Crown Princess Sohyeon were exiled to Jeju Island until they passed away.  The second member was Royal Lady Huibin Jang, wife of King Sukjong. She was punished for her treacherous act, which led to the death of Queen Inhyeon. She died in the palace, and her dead body was sent out through Seoninmun Gate. The last one was Crown Prince Sado, the son of King Yeongjo. He passed away at Seoninmun Gate as he was locked up in a chest that was placed in the prince’s residence inside the gate.

stories.title: Wolgeunmun Gate (Changgyeonggung Palace)
stories.script: Wolgeunmun Gate is a small gate door on the right side of Hongwhamun Gate. It was built in 1779, during the reign of King Jeongjo. The term “Wolgeun” in its name literally means “monthly audience,” which originated from the story that King Jeongjo used to visit Gyeongmogung Shrine once or twice every month to pay his respect for his deceased father, Crown Prince Sado. The spirit tablet of Crown Prince Sado was enshrined there.   Gyeongmogung Shrine is currently located at the site of a university hospital across the road from Honghwamun Gate. During the reign of King Jeongjo, only the ancestral tablet of Crown Prince Sado was enshrined in the Gyeongmogung Shrine. It is said that King Jeongjo constructed Wolgeunmun Gate so that people could get to the Gyeongmogung Shrine more quickly.   The feature of Wolgeunmun Gate is that the large gate and the small gate are next to each other. It is speculated that the large gate was used by King Jeongjo, and the smaller gate was used by his retainers when visiting the Gyeongmogung Shrine. In addition, both gates of the Wolgeunmun Gate are not connected to each other because they are made of different heights. The curved shape of the large gate makes it the only gate with a curved roof, which is unlike any other gate in Changgyeonggung Palace.

stories.title: Overview of Deoksugung Palace
stories.script: Deoksugung Palace is one of the five major palaces in Korea. It is the imperial palace of the Korean Empire, which was proclaimed in 1897. Its former name was Gyeongungung Palace. Deoksugung Palace wasn't used as a palace in the beginning; in fact, it was once the residence of Prince Wolsan, the elder brother of King Seongjong.  The first time Deoksugung Palace was used as a palace was when King Seongjong returned from evacuation during the Japanese invasion in 1592. As there was no suitable palace for him to stay in, he took the rural palace in Jeongneung-dong as a temporary palace. Later, King Gwanghaegun moved his residence to Changdeokgung Palace and renamed the rural palace Gyeongungung Palace.  Due to King Injo’s coup, Deoksugung Palace was reduced in size and could not function as a palace. Then, following the Eulmi Incident in 1895, it reappeared in history. King Gojong, who moved to the Russian Legation due to the Eulmi Incident, returned to Gyeongungung Palace. After returning to the Gyeongungung Palace, King Gojong changed the country's name to “Korean Empire” and established a national system that was up to standard as an imperial kingdom. Gradually, Gyeongungung Palace acquired the scale and formality of an imperial palace.  However, due to a great fire in 1904, many buildings, including Hamnyeongjeon Hall and Seogeodang Hall, were burned down. In addition to the Japan-Korea Treaty of 1950 and the dethronement of Emperor Gojong, Gyeongungung Palace was drastically reduced in size.  Emperor Sunjong, who inherited the throne from Emperor Gojong, raised the title of “Deoksu” to wish Emperor Gojong to enjoy and live a long life. Thus, Gyeongungung Palace was called Deoksugung Palace afterwards.  Deoksugung Palace contains a heartbreaking history. If you walk around Deoksugung Palace, the imperial palace of the Korean Empire, you can see historic halls and pavilions with their own stories. The beautiful Stonewall Walkway at Deoksugung Palace will allow you to get a feel for the palace's turbulent modern history.

stories.title: Daehanmun Gate (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Daehanmun Gate is the main gate of Deoksugung Palace. Its original name was “Daeanmun Gate,” which means “national prosperity and welfare of the people”. It earned its current name in 1906, which contains the meaning “Hanyang (today’s Seoul) will prosper.  The main gates of the royal palaces were usually located in the south. Although Daehanmun Gate serves as the main gate today, the original main gate of Deoksugung Palace was Inhwamun Gate, which faced the south. However, Daehanmun Gate became the primary entrance due to its increased use and the narrowness of the road in front of Inhwamun Gate.  Like the main gate of Changgyeonggung Palace, Daehanmun Gate also faces the east. It is the only one-story main gate that consists of three entrances and two sections from the side. It has a hipped and gabled roof with eaves supported by multi-cluster brackets. The base and stairs of the gate are already buried underground.  Daehanmun Gate was not always located where it is now. It used to be located about 33 meters away from the current location. During the Japanese colonial period, the surrounding roads were greatly expanded, and it had to move westward from its original position. The expanded road took up a large part of the east of Deoksugung Palace. After the liberation from Japanese colonial rule, due to the second road expansion construction, the wall of the palace was moved further backwards, and Daehanmun Gate was left lonely in the middle of the road for a period of time before being relocated to the current site in 1970.

stories.title: Geumcheongyo Bridge (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: After passing through the Daehanmun Gate, it is the area of Deoksugung Palace. There is a bridge before reaching the main hall, which is called Geumcheongyo Bridge. It is a bridge over a stream called Myeongdangsu that flows between Daehanmun Gate and Jowonmun Gate. It acts as a border to separate the area of the palace from the outside.  Different from the bridges in other royal palaces, Geumcheongyo Bridge has two arches at the bottom with three abutments above. The road of the bridge consists of three sections, of which the middle path only allows the king to walk and is higher than the sides for the servants to walk on. The pillars were set up at four corners, and lotus buds were placed on them. Also, seven handrails were installed between the east and west. The Deoksugung Palace's Geumcheongyo Bridge is unique in that it has no other decorations, such as stone statues of imaginary animals.   During the Joseon Dynasty, there was a gate called Jowonmun Gate on the way to the main hall after crossing the Geumchongyo Bridge. However, it was destroyed in a fire at Deoksugung Palace in 1904. It was rebuilt later but was demolished during the Japanese invasion of Korea again.  The Geumchongyo Bridge is extremely valuable in terms of history and architecture. Let’s cross the bridge and explore more interesting aspects of the palace!

stories.title: Junghwamun Gate (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Junghwamun Gate is the main entrance to the main throne hall. The term “Junghwa” means “the righteous mind of not being biased”. Nowadays, it is easy to reach the main hall from any direction as the corridor surrounding the courtyard has been destroyed, but passing through the Junghwamun Gate was the only way to go to the main hall in the Joseon Dynasty.  Junghwamun Gate was built in 1902, along with the main hall. However, it was destroyed by a massive fire in 1904 and rebuilt with a single-tiered roof two years later, during the reign of Emperor Gojong.   Junghwamun Gate consists of three doors as entrances. The middle door was only used by the royal family, the left door by military officers, and the right door by civil officers. Looking up, the gate was built in a multi-cluster bracket structure with a hipped and gabled roof. If you look closely at the roof, you’ll notice seven ornaments on either side. They were only placed in the highest-class buildings in the palace. Thus, we can tell that Junghwamun Gate is one of the main buildings that represents the heart of Deoksugung Palace.  After passing through the gate, you can see a wide courtyard in front of Junghwajeon Hall, the main hall of Deoksugung Palace. Some ranking stones are placed there for the officials to stand next to during the morning assembly. The royal court of Junghwajeon Hall was the place that witnessed the rise and fall of the Korean Empire. It was the place where King Sunjong and Empress Sunjeonghyo held their wedding ceremony. However, a regency ceremony under the coercion of pro-Japanese collaborators was also held here in 1907.  The stairs connecting the royal courtyard and Junghwajeon Hall have three sections. The middle section has a stone slab called Dapdo, which is carved with two dragons symbolizing the empire. This is a unique characteristic of Deoksugung Palace, while other palaces have phoenixes carved on them.  As there are many hidden stories inside the palace, let’s move on to enter the main hall and explore more interesting stories!

stories.title: Junghwajeon Hall (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Junghwajeon Hall is the main hall of Deoksugung Palace. Its name shares the same meaning as Junghwamun Gate, which means “the righteous mind of not being biased”. It served as the office hall for the king to conduct state affairs, meet his subjects, and greet important envoys from foreign countries. It was also a place to hold enthronement ceremonies.  Junghwajeon Hall was built in 1902 together with the Junghwamun Gate. Unfortunately, it was burned down in 1904 and rebuilt during the reign of Emperor Gojong. Emperor Gojong successfully processed his modernization projects and intentionally built the hall building to show his authority. The name of the gate also reflected his hope for the Korean Empire that it could maintain its independence and peace among other great powers.  Junghwajeon Hall was originally constructed as a two-story building to show the dignity of the Korean Empire. After the great fire in Deoksugung Palace, the current hall building was rebuilt as a one-story building. It has a hip and gable roof called Paljakjibung, and the Gongpo supporting the eaves of the roof is set up on and between the pillars. The architectural style of the building is known as the Dapo style, which is the multi-cluster bracketing style. Looking inside the hall, its ceiling is decorated with two dragons, symbolizing the imperial family of the Korean Empire and their dignity. Also, behind the throne between the pillars, there is a folding screen featuring the sun, moon, and five mountains, which is called the “Irwoloakdo”, representing the wish for the nation to be prosperous under the rule of the king.  Although Junghwajeon Hall was slightly different from its original form after the fire in the palace, we can still see the characteristics of the late Joseon Dynasty in its architecture style and name.

stories.title: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.audioTitle: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art is located on the west side of the royal court of Jungmyeongjeon Hall. It is the youngest building in Deoksugung Palace which construction was completed in 1938. At that time, it was named “Yi Royal Family Museum of Art” and was the first building built to be used as a modern national museum of art.   The former name “Yi Royal Family Museum of Art” was used to demean the Korean imperial family during the Japanese colonial era. During this time, an organization called the Office of the Yi Dynasty was established as an affiliated organization of the Governor-General of Korea. It was responsible for managing all affairs of the imperial family, such as collecting items and treasures from all over the country and exhibiting them at Changgyeonggung Palace and Deoksugung Palace.  The Yi Royal Family Museum of Art held exhibitions in the east and west wings of Seokjojeon Hall. The east wing featured Japanese displays, while the west wing featured artifacts from the Korean Peninsula dating back to before the Joseon Dynasty. The exhibition was set up by the Japanese government to demonstrate to the world that Korea was an underdeveloped country.  Seokjojeon Hall served as a meeting place for the US-Soviet Joint Commission following the liberation of Korea from Japanese colonial rule until its conversion into a national museum in 1955. In 1973, the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, which was located in Gyeongbokgung Palace, was relocated to Deoksugung Palace and is now called the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art.  To visit the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, you need to purchase an admission ticket from Deoksugung Palace. Please remember to purchase the ticket beforehand.

stories.title: Seokjojeon Hall (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Seokjojeon Hall is the only hall in Deoksugung Palace that is entirely built in Western architectural style. Its name has suggested the meaning of “a hall made of stone”. The imperial family rarely used the hall except for receiving visits from state or imperial families, despite the fact that it was built for the imperial family as a residence hall.   The construction of Seokjojeon Hall was begun by an English architect introduced by the British Embassy in 1900. That’s the reason why it was unlike other buildings built with wood or mud in traditional Korean architectural style, but with stone. The construction was completed after 10 years due to the unstable situation in the Korean Empire. Therefore, there were fewer opportunities for it to fulfill its role during the Korean Empire era.  Seokjojeon Hall is a three-story building. Each level serves a unique purpose. There were servants' quarters on the ground floor, audience halls on the second, and the royal family's bedrooms, sitting rooms, and drawing rooms on the third. It has a triangular gable roof that has patterns of plum flowers representing the Royal Family’s surname, Lee of Jeonju, and was the emblem of the Korean Empire.  During the Japanese colonization, King Yeongchin stayed in Seokjojeon Hall whenever he returned to Korea. After the liberation from Japan, the US-Soviet Joint Commission Meeting was held in the hall, and it was used as a national museum of Korea and an art museum. Seokjojeon Hall is now open to the public. Shall we take a look around the interior to get a feel for the hall's culture and beauty?

stories.title: Junmyeongdang Hall (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Junmyeongdang Hall was newly built along with the reconstruction of Deoksugung Palace after the great fire of the palace in 1904. During the reign of Enperor Gojong, the first monarch of the Korean Empire, Junmyeongdang Hall was used as a place for young ladies to select a spouse for the royal family and for the emperor to meet with the vassals who managed the royal tombs of successive kings.   In 1912, two years after Japanese colonial rule began, Emperor Gojong celebrated his 60th birthday and gave birth to his beloved daughter, Princess Deokhye. The birth of the princess changed the role of the Junmyeongdang Hall. Emperor Gojong has turned the hall into a kindergarten for the princess. Not only Princess Deokhye but also the sons of nobles studied together at the hall. Emperor Gojong would bring children to Junmyeongdang Hall on occasion to hand out Chinese brushes and inks.  Feelings of the Emperor Gojong's love for his late-in-life daughter, Princess Deokhye, can be sensed in certain areas of the palace. If you go up the stairs of the hall, you can see the holes drilled in the handrail. The palace's hallways did not have handrails when it was first built. To prevent Princess Deokhye, a young child, from getting hurt, Emperor Gojong had all the handrails in the building repaired. Also, most of the pillars inside the hall were removed for the princess to play with her friends freely.  Emperor Gojong had showed his deep love to his daughter Princess Deokhye. Why don't you visit Junmyeongdang Hall while thinking about Emperor Gojong as a father, instead of an emperor of a country?

stories.title: Jeukjodang Hall (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Deoksugung Palace was proclaimed the Imperial Palace of the Korean Empire in 1897, but it had a relatively long history before it was used by the royal family. Therefore, there are many pavilions that were located in the palace and used before the name Deoksugung Palace was given.   Jeukjodang Hall is one of the oldest pavilions in the palace. King Seonjo, who fled to Uiju during the Japanese invasion of Korea in 1592, used it as an office after he returned to the palace. In 1623, King Injo ascended the throne, and King Yeongjo drew a plaque, GyehyeJeukjodang,” to commemorate his accession to the throne in the past. The meaning of the plaque was “King Injo was crowned in the year of Gyehye”.  King Injo named the hall Jeukjodang Hall. It was once called Taegeukjeon Hall during the reign of Emperor Gojong. However, its name was changed back to Jeukjodang Hall again after Junghwajeon Hall was built in 1902. The hall was once destroyed by the great fire of Deoksugung Palace in 1904, but it was rebuilt into the current building in March of the same year.   Jeukjodang Hall has a corridor connecting with Junmyeongdang Hall to the west. It has seven sections across the front and four sections on the side. In front of the hall, there are some stones placed in the courtyard. Originally, there were no fantastic stones as part of the landscaping of Deoksugung Palace. The stones in the courtyard were brought from Changgyeonggung Palace in 1984, as Jeukjodang Hall was once the royal bed chamber, which was supposed to have the stones placed nearby.

stories.title: Seogeodang Hall (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Seogeodang Hall is located southwest of Jeukjodang Hall. Its name suggested the meaning of “the house where an old king once lived”. This building once served as the king's temporary residence.  Seogeodang Hall is a historic building that was first built along with Jeukjodang Hall at the beginning of Deoksugung Palace. It was used by King Seonjo for 16 years upon his return from his refuge during the Japanese invasion of Korea in 1592. However, a fire in Deoksugung Palace destroyed it in 1904. The current Seogeodang Hall was rebuilt in the same year.   Seogeodang Hall is the only two-story building in Deoksugung Palace. Although it may look luxurious compared to other single-roofed traditional Hanok buildings, it is an ordinary building with no decoration. Instead, there is one impressive feature that can be found. The hall has two signboards, which are placed on each floor. The signboard on the first floor was written by Emperor Gojong in 1905, which together stated the year 1905 when the Eulsa Treaty was forced to be annexed, whereas the one on the second floor was written by a civil officer of the late Joseon Dynasty in 1904, when the hall was under reconstruction.   Like Jeukjodang Hall, Seogeodang Hall witnessed the long history of Deoksugung Palace. King Seonjo worked day and night in the hall to rebuild the devastated country after the Japanese invasion of Korea. The king's private quarters and royal council meetings were held there. Seogeodang Hall's simple yet distinctive architecture has revealed the past's events and created a classical elegance.

stories.title: Jeonggwanheon Hall (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Jeonggwanheon Hall is the exclusive relaxing and entertaining place for the imperial family of the Korean Empire. It is the only building in Deoksugung Palace whose name ends with heon,” which is usually used to name an annex or separate house. Its name, Jeonggwan, is interpreted to mean look ahead quietly. According to historical documents, it was also used as a repository for royal portraits.  Most of the buildings in Deoksugung Palace were destroyed by the great fire in 1904. However, Jeonggwanheon Hall survived the fire, and the original appearance built in 1900 was well preserved until now. Therefore, it is the oldest existing modern building in Deoksugung Palace.  Jeonggwanheon Hall has a unique architectural style. The building is a fusion of Korean and Western styles, which combine the traditional Korean roof with Western pillars. Except for the small space with a wall and a gate behind Jeonggwanheon Hall, the remaining space is visible from the outside. It is assumed that the space was used to prepare items or store tools instead of as a room due to its small size.   Looking inside the hall, the inner part is surrounded by brick, and the exterior decoration is designed with various animals and plants that symbolized different meanings in ancient times. A bat symbolizes happiness, a deer symbolizes longevity, a pine tree symbolizes longevity, and a dragon symbolizes the emperor. The hidden meaning of bats and grapes is a blessing on future generations.

stories.title: Hamnyeongjeon Hall (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Hamnyeongjeon Hall was the living quarter and bedchamber of Emperor Gojong, the first emperor of the Korean Empire. It was also used as a council office and leisure space. The king used to discuss state affairs with ministers and meet foreign envoys there. The fact that the emperor invited envoys to his privately used building signified his trust in the country the envoy represented. At the same time, the imperial family often held banquets in the hall. Thus, the meeting at Hamnyeongjeon Hall was significant.  Hamnyeongjeon Hall was first built in 1897. However, a large fire broke out at the hall in 1904 and destroyed many buildings in the Deoksugung Palace. Hamnyeongjeon Hall has ondol rooms located on both sides of a wide wooden lobby floor. Ondol is a traditional Korean heating method that keeps the room warm by lighting a kiln and sending the hot air under the floor. It is believed that the fire broke out when the ondol was being repaired. The fire spread from the hall to the outside and caused enormous damage. The current building was rebuilt in December of the same year.  Hamnyeongjeon Hall is an L-shaped building that has nine sections from the front and four sections from the side, connecting with the rear of the western section. It has a hip and gable roof called Paljakjibung. The installation of the sculptures on the eaves of the building is a visual representation of the need to ward off evil spirits. Sculptures like these, which sit atop the eaves of bedrooms, are unusual. Inside the hall, the ceiling is latticed, and windows are installed instead of walls.   Emperor Gojong was forced to abdicate by Japan in 1907 and spent a lonely time in Hamnyeongjeon Hall. In 1919, he passed away at the age of 68. When Emperor Gojong passed away at Hamnyeongjeon Hall, people all over the country mourned his death. This led to Korean Independence Movement Day. It is a large-scale anti-Japanese movement that spread nationwide.

stories.title: Deokhongjeon Hall (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Deokhongjeon Hall is next to Hamnyeongjeon Hall. It was the residence and royal council hall of the first emperor, Emperor Gojong. He used to conduct daily state affairs and receive domestic and foreign officers in the hall.   Deokhongjeon Hall is one of the most recently built buildings in Deoksugung Palace. It was built in 1912. Before its development, a hall called Gyeongsojeon Hall was built there as a spirit hall to enshrine the tablet of Empress Myeongseong, the wife of Emperior Gojong. Gyeongsojeon Hall was renamed Gyeonghyojeon Hall afterwards. However, it was burned down during the large fire at Deoksugung Palace in 1904. While the tablet of Empress Myeongseong was moved to the west of Junmyeongjeon Hall, the hall building was rebuilt on the site. Nevertheless, even after the reconstruction, the mortuary tablet was not moved back, and thus, the new building became the Deokhongjeon Hall in 1912.  The architecture of Deokhongjeon Hall shows the transition from traditional to modern society. The traditional Korean building was usually in a rectangular shape, but Deokhongjeon Hall was built in a square-like shape. Also, its base was built up with long square stones, and its pillars were built to perfect height with simplified column-top brackets to support the roof. There are dragon heads and miscellaneous images on the ridges of the hipped and gabled roof, which symbolize the desire to expel misfortune and prevent fire. Inside the hall, there is a light on the ceiling and a western-style curtain installed.  As Deokhongjeon Hall was built during the Japanese occupation period, the Office of the Yi Dynasty and noble guests lounge were set up in the hall. The Office of the Yi Dynasty was in charge of assisting Emperor Gojong, which in fact was to monitor the royal family. All the visitors had to be granted permission by the office before meeting Emperor Gojong. Therefore, Emprior Gojong and his family were barely able to meet their close courtiers and court maidens under the monitor of the office; instead, most of the visitors were Japanese or officials of pro-Japanese collaborators.

stories.title: Gwangmyeongmun Gate (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Gwangmyeongmun Gate served as the entrance to Hamnyeongjeon Hall, the residence hall of Emperor Gojong, who was the first emperor of the Korean Empire. When Emperor Gojong passed away at Hamnyeongjeon Hall in 1919, his coffin was taken out through the gate.  Gwangmyeongmun Gate was recently moved back to its original location and served its own role. However, it was relocated to play another role until 2016. During the Japanese colonial era, many buildings in Deoksugung Palace were demolished and moved from their current location to the southwest of Junghwajeon Hall. After the relocation, it was used as the entrance to the outdoor exhibition hall. Unfortunately, it returned to its original site as part of the restoration project that began in 2016.  Generally, the gates to the hall of the palace were built in a straight line in front of the hall. But if you look closely, you'll notice that Gwangmyeongmun Gate isn't quite aligned with the Hamnyeongjeon Hall that was constructed behind it. It was confirmed during the 2016 excavation of Deoksugung Palace that the stylobate was not aligned with the hall. In addition, Gwangmyeongmun Gate can be seen in its current spot on a map of Deoksugung Palace from the 1900s. Therefore, although it may look weird as an entrance gate that is out of line with the hall behind it, it was still moved back to its old site.

stories.title: The Pond (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: Walking along the fence of Hamnyeongjeon Hall, the bedchamber of Emperor Gojong, there is a pond. The pond did not exist in Deoksugung Palace at first, but it was built during the Japanese colonial era.  Emperor Gojong and his royal family have lived in the Deoksugung Palace since Japanese colonial rule began in 1910. However, after Emperor Gojong passed away in 1919, his family moved to stay at Changdeokgung Palace. Seven years later, the son of Emperor Gojong, Emperor Sunjong, passed away in 1926, and the Japanese government began to destroy Deoksugung Palace with the intention of eradicating all the traces of the Joseon royal family.  There was an organization under the Governor-General of Korea called the Office of the Yi Dynasty in 1931. It was responsible for managing the affairs of the royal family and the palace at that time. It was planned to convert half of the Deoksugung Palace into a park. Therefore, the construction of the west wing of Seokjojeon Hall began, and a number of buildings were demolished. The demolished buildings were replaced by playgrounds, lawns, a pond, and cherry trees, symbolizing Japan.  The pond was built in 1934 during the redevelopment project of Deoksugung Palace. Although the size of the pond has been reduced today, it originally covered the entire area, from the wall near Hamnyeongjeon Hall to the wall on the side of Seoul City Hall. People enjoyed the seasonal scenery of the pond and used it as an ice-skating rink even after liberation from Japanese colonial rule. There are still photographs taken in the 1960s that record the time citizens enjoyed skating on the frozen pond. The ice-skating rink remained until the 1980s, even after the restoration project of Deoksugung Palace began in the 1970s. At that time, there was a discussion about recognizing the palace as a cultural asset and restoring it to its original state. However, the citizens had opposed the suggestion, as they thought it made no sense to designate a park as a cultural asset.  Even though the pond at Deoksugung Palace still carries the sad memories of Japan's colonial rule, it is now a popular place for families and young couples to go ice skating.

stories.title: Yangijae Hall (Deoksugung Palace)
stories.script: There is a Hanok building behind the cathedral of the Anglican Church in Seoul called Yangijae Hall. It was originally built in Deoksugung Palace in 1905 but was moved to the current site during the Japanese colonial period until today.  Yangijae Hall was also called “Suhagwon”. It served as a modern educational institute for the children of the royal family and aristocrats living in the palace. They had to learn a lot of subjects, including Korean and Chinese characters, foreign languages, math, music, and gymnastics. All the classes were conducted in a modern style for about 2 to 5 hours every day. Also, there was a building called Hamhuidang Hall, which was connected to Yangijae Hall and served as a lecture hall.   However, the history of Yangijae Hall did not last long. It only operated until 1910. After Japan’s forced annexation of Korea, it is said that the Anglican Church of Korea leased and used some buildings, including Yangijae Hall. Following the death of Emperor Gojong, the Office of the Yi Dynasty either destroyed the buildings of Deoksugung Palace or sold them at a bargain price. During that time, even the Anglican Church of Korea purchased some of those buildings, including Yangijae Hall. Therefore, the original site of the hall was excluded from the area of Deoksugung Palace.  Nowadays, Yangijae Hall and other buildings are used as the offices and monastery of the Anglican Church of Korea. Yangijae Hall was originally used as an office before it was designated as a registered cultural asset in 2006, which has been carefully preserved.

stories.title: Excavation Site in Daesin-ri, Hwasun
stories.audioTitle: Excavation Site in Daesin-ri, Hwasun 화순 대신리 발굴지
stories.script: Excavation Site in Daesin-ri, Hwasun    [Cultural Commentator] The Excavation Site in Daesin-ri, Hwasun was dug up in 1999 to determine the characteristics of the dolmen site in Hwasun. The site where the excavation site was located used to be an ordinary rice field. In 1995, the dolmens in the Hwasun region were first discovered and reported to the academic community, which later led to an excavation survey.  [Tourist] How many dolmens have been found by the excavation survey at the excavation site in Daesin-ri?  [Cultural Commentator] 35 dolmens were excavated at the excavation site in Daesin-ri, Hwasun. Among them, four dolmens at the entrance to the protecting canopy were excavated and restored to their original form. They are also used for educational purposes because they maintain their original form.   [Tourist] What is on display inside the protecting canopy?  [Cultural Commentator] Inside the protecting canopy of the dolmen excavation site, you can examine the structure and shape of the burial chamber of dolmens.  [Tourist] Is there only a burial chamber?”  [Cultural Commentator] “No. In addition to the burial chamber, there are also artifacts found during the excavation. The burial chamber is preserved to maintain its original form, and the artifacts found include the ring wheel, grinding stone, grinding slab, undecorated pottery, and the stone arrowheads.  [Tourist] What is a ring wheel?”  [Cultural Commentator] The ring wheel is also known as Bangchucha, which is the most primitive type of spinning wheel, where short fibers are connected through back twists to form a long thread, or where long fibers are twisted to form a thread. The ring wheel had a round hole in the center, and through that hole, a rod that would serve as the axis of the wheel was inserted and fixed to make threads. The fact that the ring wheel was found inside a dolmen shows that clothing was made and worn in those days.  [Tourist] What about the grinding stone?  [Cultural Commentator] The grinding stone is also known as Seokbong, and it is a stone tool that is paired with the grinding slab to peel or powder grains, wild fruits, etc. through reciprocating motions.  [Tourist] Where are the capstones that used to be on top of the burial chambers?”  [Cultural Commentator] If you look to the right side of the protecting canopy at the Excavation Site in Daesin-ri, Hwasun, there is a place where dolmen capstones are gathered and displayed. In 2008, when the protecting canopy was built, the capstones were collected in one place, instead of being restored to their original state, in order to provide a first-hand view of the burial chambers inside the canopy.  [Narration] The Excavation Site in Daesin-ri, Hwasun has very important academic value in studying the meaning of distribution of dolmens and the process of their transformation.

stories.title: Dolmen and quarry in Hwasun Gamtaebawi Rock
stories.audioTitle: Dolmen and quarry in Hwasun Gamtaebawi Rock 화순 감태바위 고인돌과 채석장
stories.script: Dolmen and quarry in Hwasun Gamtaebawi Rock    [Man] The dolmen and quarry in Hwasun Gamtaebawi Rock are located between the Daesin-ri Excavation Site and Pingmaebawi Dolmen. One of the characteristics of Hwasun dolmens is that a quarry was found along with them. The Gamtaebawi Dolmen also has a quarry nearby.  [Woman] To build a dolmen, you need propping stones, also known as supporting stones, and a capstone to be placed on top of them. The stones are the most important. The quarry is where you can get these important stones. How did they excavate stones from the quarry?  [Man] The capstones used to build dolmens weighed from as little as several tons to as much as hundreds of tons. These capstones are obtained by naturally separating stones from the mountain nearby or by removing a capstone from the rock wall. When removing the stone, wooden wedges are inserted into natural cracks in the rock or after artificially digging out gaps in the rock. After that, water is poured over the wedge, and as the wood expands, the stones break off, and these broken off stones were collected for use.   [Woman] These traces remain in the Gamtaebawi quarry. The rocks in the quarry consist of volcanic tuff of the same volcanic rock family as the stones used in dolmens. Why did they use tuff? It is because it was easy to find the right shape of stones, as tuff, which was a sedimentary rock, had the characteristic of splitting into plates from weathering.  [Man] The stones quarried for use as capstones remain intact around the Gamtaebawi Dolmen quarry, and there are foundation dolmens or so-called go-board dolmens, exposed burial chambers without a capstone, and exposed burial chambers under a huge capstone that remain preserved in their original state, and thus their value as historical records is significant.  [Woman] Go-board dolmens have plate stones erected or a stone chamber underground made of broken stones or natural stones. After that, four to eight supporting stones were placed around it, and a large capstone was placed on top to build a dolmen, which is called a go-board dolmen because its shape is similar to that of a go board. These dolmens were once called southern-style dolmens because they were usually found in the Honam and Yeongnam regions.  [Child 1 & 2] “Rock-paper-scissors.”  [Child 1] “Yes, I won! We're going on top! Hey, you guys make the formation.”  [Child 3] “Why did you lose in rock-paper-scissors?” My back is going to get hurt.”  [Lumberjack] “Hey, all of you!” It's dangerous to play piling-driving by Gamtaebawi Rock! You are not supposed to be playing that now.”  [Child 2] “Oh, come on, We've gathered all the firewood we need. We were just taking a rest here.”  [Child 3] “By the way, why is this place called Gamtaebawi Rock?”  [Child 1] “How can you not know that, stupid!”  [Child 3] “So what if I don't know? Since when does that make me stupid!”·”  [Lumberjack] “Hey, guys, take it easy. Why is this placed called Gamtaebawi Rock? Because the bottom of this rock resembles a person, and it appears as if this person is wearing a gat. Gamtae is an old term for gat.”  [Child 3] Aha! Thank you!”   [Lumberjack] “I’ve got to go down now. You should all go back to the village before the sun goes down.  [Child 1, 2, & 3] Yes, sir!”  [Man] According to the villagers, lumberjacks and children gathering firewood took a rest or played games on Gamtaebawi Rock. Gamtaebawi Rock used to also serve as a playground.

stories.title: Hwasun Madangbawi Dolmen
stories.audioTitle: Hwasun Madangbawi Dolmen 화순 마당바위 고인돌
stories.script: Hwasun Madangbawi Dolmen   [Man] A dolmen appears as you climb a bit further up from Gamtaebawi quarry. This is the Madangbawi dolmen.   [Friend 1] “How much further do we have to climb?”  [Friend 2] “Just a little longer.”  [Friend 1] “Huh? “That must be it! Right over there.”  [Friend 2] “This is the Madangbawi dolmen.”  [Friend 1] “It's huge!”  [Friend 2] The Madangbawi dolmen has a large capstone that is 6.5 m long and 1.1 m thick. It's called that because the rock is as large as a yard.  [Friend 1] It's really large!  [Friend 2] The Madangbawi dolmen is a typical go-board dolmen.  [Friend 1] A go-board?  [Friend 2] Because it looks like a go board. It is a dolmen built by making a stone chamber underground and covering it with a large capstone. It's also called a foundation dolmen. Also, it was once called a southern-style dolmen.  [Friend 1] Go-board, foundation, ...and southern style?  [Friend 2] The grand-looking go-board dolmens like this one are found in the Honam and Yeongnam regions, so they used to be called southern-style dolmens in the old days. However, they are now referred to as go-board or foundation dolmens.”  [Friend 1] It's like they have one real name but several nicknames.”  [Friend 2] “Yes! That's right!”  [Woman] Around the Madangbawi dolmen, there is an oval-shaped partitioning stone indicating that this place was a cemetery. Near this dolmen, there is a small go-board dolmen and a table dolmen.   [Man] A table dolmen has a burial chamber constructed from large flagstones exposed to the ground. It has a burial chamber made of 4 or 6 wide flagstones, with a flat capstone placed on top of the burial chamber. They are called table dolmens due to their resemblance to a table. In the past, these dolmens were mainly found in the northern part of the Korean Peninsula and the Liaoning region of China, and thus they were called northern dolmens. However, as they were later found in the southern part of the Korean Peninsula as well, they are now called table dolmens.  [Woman] There is a Gaksibawi Quarry near Hwasun Madangbawi Dolmen. Hwasun Dolmens are characterized by their quarries, and the dolmens are located close to the quarry.

stories.title: Hwasun Pingmaebawi Dolmen
stories.audioTitle: Hwasun Pingmaebawi Dolmen 화순 핑매바위 고인돌
stories.script: Hwasun Pingmaebawi Dolmen   [Man] Pingmaebawi Dolmen is located between the Gamtaebawi Dolmen site and Bogeomjae Hill. It is located on the highest ground among the dolmens distributed in Daesin-ri.  [Woman] The world's largest Pingmaebawi Dolmen is made with a capstone weighting over 200 tons. It is a super-large capstone that is 7.3 meters long, 5 meters wide, and 4 meters thick.  [Man] The ping in Pingmae means throwing away or throwing stones, and mae means Mago. There is an accompanying legend of Grandmother Mago. Grandmother Mago refers to the god of the earth that appears in the mythology of the genesis in Korea. The mythology of the genesis with Grandmother Mago goes as follows.  [Woman] At the beginning of the world, the sun and the moon were hiding in the sky and the stars roamed freely, making it difficult to distinguish between day and night. Then, as a huge giant, Grandmother Mago woke up and stretched herself, and the sky cracked and the sun and the moon came out through the gap. People who saw the light rejoiced. However, the delight didn’t last long, and as Grandmother urinated, the ground was flooded in a flash. People worked hard to build banks, but to no avail. When Grandmother Mago built banks in acknowledgment of her fault, the sea was created in an instant.  [Man] Meanwhile, Pingmaebawi also has a fable related to Grandmother Mago.  [Grandmother Mago] I must build the Cheonbulcheon Pagoda of Unjusa Temple before dawn. I’m in big trouble.”  [Woman] Grandmother Mago was hurrying toward Unjusa Temple while placing stones in her apron. Then, a stone fell from the apron.  [Grandmother Mago] “Why is the stone falling off when I'm running out of time.”  [Grandmother Mago] “Oh, well. I’ve got to keep carrying the remaining stones.”  [Woman] At this moment, the stone that Grandmother Mago dropped was the Pingmaebawi Rock.  [Villager 1] “That was close!”  [Villager 2] “There is no chance for you to marry someone this year.”  [Villager 1] “Wait, does this even make sense? You have to throw a stone towards the hole in the Pingmaebawi Rock with your left hand and get it inside to marry someone?”  [Villager 2] It’s a legend handed down from generation to generation in the village. If an unmarried person throws a stone with their left hand and gets it inside the hole in the Pingmaebawi Rock drilled by Grandmother Mago, they will get married that year.”  [Villager 1] So I won’t be able to marry this year, either?”  [Villager 2] I'm sorry, but yes, what can we do about it. You will have another chance next year...”  [Villager 1] Next year! I will definitely get it then!!”  [Man] The Pingmaebawi dolmen was deliberately rounded at the bottom, then propping stones, also known as supporting stones, were placed beneath it to create a certain space. The rock behind the Pingmaebawi Rock is horizontal, and the surface of the Pingmaebawi Rock is slanted. This is proof that Pingmaebawi Rock was moved from another location.  [Woman] As the Pingmaebawi dolmen is located on a large, high ground, it is presumed to have served as a symbolic monument rather than as a tomb. There are 133 dolmens distributed in this area.

stories.title: Hwasun Dalbawi Dolmen
stories.audioTitle: Hwasun Dalbawi Dolmen 화순 달바위 고인돌
stories.script: Hwasun Dalbawi Dolmen   [Man] The Dalbawi Dolmen is located between Bogeomjae and the Gwancheongbawi Dolmen area.   [Commentator] Many dolmens and rocks are scattered at the foot of the mountain heading south along the road stretched between Hyosan-ri, Dogok-myeon and Daesin-ri, Chunyang-myeon. Long ago, people would pass through this place to travel from Boseong to Naju. They named it Dalbawi due to its shape. Because it resembled a full moon. Thus, this dolmen began to be called the Dalbawi Dolmen.”  [Tourist] Sir. This dolmen is quite huge, isn't it?  [Commentator] Yes, that's right. It is 5.56 meters long and 3.96 meters wide. This dolmen measures 1.98 meters in height. The Dalbawi Dolmen stands on its own, away from other dolmens.  [Tourist] I see. Could you tell us why?”  [Commentator] It is presumed to have been used as a monument to symbolize the graveyard of a group with blood ties. That means the Dalbawi Dolmen served as a headstone. The area around the Dalbawi Dolmen was examined in 2004.  [Tourist] Did they find anything here?’  [Commentator] Yes, stone arrowheads and stone pieces were found.  [Tourist] Arrowheads?  [Commentator] Stone arrowheads are hunting tools that began to be used during the Neolithic Age, and they have been continuously used during the Bronze Age since then. At the time during which the dolmen was built, we could presume that long-distance hunting tools such as bows and arrows were being used.   [Man] The Dalbawi dolmen is a go-board dolmen. Go-board dolmens are built by laying down or piling up stone mounds around the burial chamber in the rectangular, oval, or circular form then erecting the propping stones, or supporting stones, around them. A capstone is then placed on top of them. It's also called a foundation dolmen.  [Woman] Near the Dalbawi dolmens, small dolmens are lined up along the hillside. The dolmens around the Dalbawi dolmens have been identified as go-board and pad-stone dolmens, and typical go-board dolmens are largely distributed, especially those resembling the shape of a moon.  [Man] The pad-stone dolmens have a capstone placed right above the burial chamber built underground. Since they have no propping stones, or supporting stones, they are alternatively referred to as no-support, lid, or footstone dolmens. In this style, a burial chamber made of stone is almost always found, allowing us to presume that they were originally built to serve as tombs. This suggests that the Dalbawi dolmen is a monument symbolizing the graveyard of a group with blood ties such as family members and relatives, and that most of the small ones are tombs. Most of the artifacts excavated from the dolmens are found in this type of dolmen. Above the Dalbawi Dolmen, there is the Dalbawi Quarry, and Hwasun Dolmens have the characteristic of having a large quarry nearby.

stories.title: Gwancheongbawi Dolmen and Quarry in Hwasun
stories.audioTitle: Gwancheongbawi Dolmen and Quarry in Hwasun 화순 관청바위 고인돌과 채석장
stories.script: Gwancheongbawi Dolmen and Quarry in Hwasun   [Man] Gwancheongbawi Dolmen is located between the Goebawi Dolmen and Dalbawi Dolmen. If you climb up a bit further, a reservoir appears.  [Woman] Among the dolmens in Hwasun, dolmens are most densely located here, with the highest proportion of large dolmens. 190 dolmens are located here.  [Man] Among the dolmens on Gwancheongbawi Rock, the largest dolmens are located on the edge of the highest ground, while the remaining dolmens are arranged in three rows. A quarry is located above the dolmens, displaying the characteristics of Hwasun dolmens.  [Woman] Most of the dolmens on Gwancheongbawi Rock are go-board-shaped with propping stones supporting the capstones. Go-board dolmens were once called northern-style dolmens, and they are alternatively referred to as foundation dolmens. The burial chamber, which is built by piling up plate stones or natural stones, is located underground, and several supporting stones shore up a large capstone.  [Man] The dolmens on the Gwancheongbawi Rock are made of capstones measuring 180-600 cm, and the shape of the capstones are found to be rectangular and trapezoidal.  [Woman] There are traces demonstrating the ground being flattened before building dolmens, which is the characteristic of the Hwasun Gwancheongbawi dolmens, not found in Ganghwa or Gochang.  [Man] Honey!!” (Catching his breath) Did you hear the news?”  [Woman] No, what is the matter? What made you run yourself out of breath?”   [Man] “It’s the Boseong County Magistrate.”  [Woman] “What about the Magistrate?”  [Man] “You know there is a huge rock on the way up to Bogeomjae, right?”  [Woman] “Yes, I know that rock.”  [Man] He's there now listening to people's civil petitions. I heard people are flocking there to see him.  [Woman] Are you serious? Then we shouldn't stay here, either. The government office has been too far, and he’s here now by the huge rock. Hurry up and take the lead. We should go, too.  [Man] Can I take a little break before we leave? It was tough to run all the way here...  [Woman] No, we don't have time for this. If the county magistrate passes over Bogeomjae, it will be too late for us. Come on, we’ve got to go now. Come on!”  [Man] Gwancheongbawi was named after the fact that the Boseong Country Magistrate engaged in administrative affairs of listening to civil complaints by the huge rock on his way across Bogeomjae.

stories.title: Hwasun Goebawi Dolmen
stories.script: Hwasun Goebawi Dolmen   [Cultural Commentator] The Goebawi Dolmen is the first dolmen found at the entrance of Hyosan-ri, Dogok-myeon. It is located on high ground, and the size of its capstone is huge.  [Tourist] It's very big. But its supporting stones are relatively small.   [Cultural Commentator] It's a typical go-board dolmen with supporting stones shoring up a huge capstone. The Goebawi Dolmen is larger than the surrounding dolmens, and stands tall alone, overlooking the flatland from a high ground. The Goebawi Dolmen has no burial chamber, and the pieces of plain pottery were found from its surrounding area during an excavation. Due to these reasons, we can infer that it was used as an altar.  [Tourist] Sir, isn't the dolmen a tomb? That's what I learned at school.“  [Cultural Commentator] The dolmens were mainly used as tombs, but some were used as altars and headstones.  [Tourist] Headstones?  [Cultural Commentator] The headstone here refers to the stone that marks the area of the tomb.  [Tourist] What is plain pottery?  [Cultural Commentator] Plain pottery refers to the earthenware used during the Bronze Age, during which the dolmens were built, and it is called plain pottery due to its lack of distinctive patterns. This flat earthenware is made of clay mixed with coarse sand or agalmatolite powder, and it is then baked in a kiln. It is usually reddish or yellowish brown.  [Tourist] There are other dolmens too near the Goebawi Dolmen. What kind of dolmens are they?”  [Cultural Commentator] There are go-board dolmens, also known as foundation dolmens, and pad-stone dolmens nearby the Goebawi Dolmen. The pad-stone dolmens have a capstone placed right above the burial chamber built underground. They are also referred to as no-support, lid, or footstone dolmens. In these pad-stone dolmens, a stone burial chamber is almost always found, indicating that they were originally intended to serve as tombs.”  [Woman] The Goebawi Rock, which resembles a mouse, has a story embracing feng shui related to the surrounding area.  [Friend 1] Look, that Goebawi Rock is the cat rock.”  [Friend 2] Why is the cat rock standing here?”  [Friend 1] The mountain behind Seonggok Village, 100 m south of Goebawi Rock, which is also the ancestral mountain of the Pungsan Hong clan, is said to resemble a mouse according to feng shui. To put it bluntly, it's like a mouse grave.  [Friend 2] A mouse and a cat are incompatible with each other, aren't they? A mouse always gets attacked by cats.”  [Friend 1] But fortunately, the water flowing in front of the rock prevents the cat from pouncing on the mouse. That's why the village is peaceful and the ancestral mountain of Pungsan Hong clan is known to be a propitious site.

stories.title: Hwasun Dolmen and Prehistoric Culture Experience Cente
stories.audioTitle: Hwasun Dolmen and Prehistoric Culture Experience Center 화순 고인돌 선사문화 체험장
stories.script: Hwasun Dolmen and Prehistoric Culture Experience Center   [Man] The Hwasun Dolmen and Prehistoric Culture Experience Center is located next to the Information Center of the Hyosan-ri Dolmen Site. The Prehistoric Culture Experience Center is a space that offers visitors the chance to experience prehistoric culture with its restoration of a prehistoric village on 33,799 square meters of land.   [Tourist] Hello.  [Staff] “Hello, how may I help you?”  [Tourist] What is this place for?  [Staff] “This is an experience center built to display the lives of people in prehistoric times.”  [Tourist] It looks pretty big from the outside. How big is it?”  [Staff] There are 10 pit dwellings in the experience center. It consists of four watchtowers, two raised houses, three experience houses, four workshop houses, and eight education halls.  [Tourist] What kind of house is the pit dwelling?  [Staff] The pit dwelling is a building erected above a dug ground with a roof and without any walls. In archeology, it is referred to as a pit dwelling. It is a building structure created using the easiest methods to fulfill the need to avoid cold, rain, and wind while the concept of walls was not yet developed. It is estimated that the pit dwellings began to be built in Korea in the Neolithic Age, and some people remained to live inside the pit dwellings until as late as the early Iron Age.   [Tourist] “Ah, I see. Could you tell us about the watchtower and the raised house?”  [Staff] “The watchtower was installed in a location where the surrounding area was clearly visible to monitor. It is structured like a pavilion or an attic. It is a building that serves for defensive and surveillance measures. Most of the time, it was built on high ground, but if not, pillars were erected and the floor was raised high above the ground to accommodate the watchtower. A raised house is a house with a floor higher than the ground or the surface. Because they were distanced from the ground, they were not suitable for installing a heating system, so they were not ideal for residential purposes.”  [Tourist] Why did they build the house high above the ground?”  [Staff] It was to prevent damage caused by animals, moisture, and flooding. They were built for special purposes such as storing grain and holding religious events.   [Tourist] Is there any hands-on experience program related to the prehistoric culture at Hwasun Dolmen and Prehistoric Culture Experience Center?  [Staff] Yes, of course there is. The Prehistoric Culture Experience Center offers a variety of programs including making pottery, stone arrowheads, and wooden bows, hands-on experience for building a dolmen, and making tools used by prehistoric people.”  [Woman] The Hwasun Dolmen and Prehistoric Culture Experience Center is open from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., and is closed every Monday.

stories.title: What is dolmen?
stories.script: What is dolmen?  [Teacher] There are stone statues and tombs made of large, heavy, sturdy rocks in the world. Examples include the pyramids, which are large tombs in Egypt, Stonehenge, the mysterious megalithic monument in England, and the Moai statues, the huge face sculptures on Easter Island. It is called megalithic culture.  [Student] Is there also megalithic culture in Korea?  [Teacher] “Of course there is.”  [Student] What is it?  [Teacher] The representative megalithic culture of Korea would be the dolmens. “  [Student] The dolmen was part of the megalithic culture?  [Teacher] Most of the dolmens are prehistoric tombs with a large stone placed above a burial chamber made on the ground or underground. The dolmens are also called Jiseokmyo, which are made of a flat stone or an oddly shaped stone with supporting stones placed underneath.  [Student] Sir, dolmens aren't only found in Korea, are they?”  [Teacher] Starting from northern Europe, the dolmens are concentrated in the United Kingdom in Western Europe, throughout France, Switzerland, and the Iberian Peninsula, then in the northern part of the Mediterranean sea, the Middle East, India and Southeast Asia, and in China's Fujian, Zhejiang Province, Shandong Province, Liaodong Peninsula, the southern part of Jilin Province, the entire Korean Peninsula, and in Kyushu, Japan.   [Man] Dolmens were generally built on plateaus around a river basin and on low hills. Dolmens are more frequently distributed in slightly higher plains near mountains and hills and coastal areas than in large plains. In the river basin, they are largely placed to match the direction that the stream flows, mainly because the human dwellings primarily developed in those areas. The reason that there are no dolmens in the vast plains is that most of them were there before the areas were developed, and those areas were not used for human living. It is highly likely that the residential areas, farmland, and tombs were built here, as the plateau or a slightly higher hill was located at the foot of a sunny mountain, thus making it easy to get water and firewood for living while the hunting ground also remained close. It was because it was highly accessible.  [Woman] The dolmens are alternatively referred to as Dokbaegi, Baubaegi, or Dokbau, as they have natural stones buried underground, while go-board dolmens are alternatively called Gwanbau or Amdakbau. They may also be called Baebau, Geobukbau, Duggeobibau, or Gaeguribau depending on the shape of their capstones. A dolmen was also called Chilseongbau due to its shape of arrangement in connection with folk beliefs, or Janggunbau in a belief that a Janggun, meaning army general in Korean, moved the stones but then stopped. The names of the villages are sometimes related to dolmens, such as Juam, which resembles Baebawi Rock, Guam, meaning turtle rock, and Chilam, which means chilseong rock.

stories.title: Types of dolmens
stories.script: Types of dolmens  [Man] Dolmens are different from ordinary tombs because they are made with huge rocks erected above the ground. Their simple structure allows detailed insight. The dolmens are classified into table dolmens, go-board dolmens, pad-stone dolmens, semi-exposed dolmens, and exposed dolmens.  [Woman] The table dolmens have a burial chamber made with 4 or 6 wide flagstones that are exposed above the ground, with a flat capstone placed on top of the burial chamber. They are called table dolmens because they resemble a table. They are mainly located in the northern part of the Korean Peninsula and the Liaoning area of China, and thus they used to be called the northern style. Among the table dolmens, the large ones are estimated to have been built mainly as altars or monuments. Among these dolmens, the super-large dolmens, which are more than 8 meters long, 5 meters wide, and 2 meters high, are usually found in the Liaodong Peninsula and the Daedonggang River basin in Korea, and only one is built on each hillside or mountainside.   [Man] Go-board dolmens have a burial chamber built underground made of flagstones or broken and natural stones, and 4 to 8 supporting stones are erected around them with a large capstone placed on top. This is called a go-board dolmen because it resembles a go board. The go-board dolmens, which look magnificent as they are raised above the surface, are often devoid of distinct burial chambers. A large dolmen usually exists at the foot of a mountain, hill, or flat area at the end of a valley, but in a cluster of dolmens, it is located at the center or in an independent location.  [Woman] The pad-stone dolmens have a burial chamber with a lid right above the top. Since there are no propping stones, the pad-stone dolmens are alternatively referred to as no-support, lid, or footstone dolmens. For this type, a stone burial chamber is almost always found, indicating that they were originally intended to serve as tombs. Being widely distributed in the Liaoning Peninsula, the Korean Peninsula, and Kyushu, Japan, they are the most common type of tombs among the dolmen types. The capstone is thin in the north, but in the south it tends to be thicker. Most of the artifacts excavated from dolmens were also found in this type.  [Man] Semi-exposed dolmens have a structure like a stone coffin on the ground with a flagstone that is lower than the typical table-style flagstone or that has multiple overlapping flagstones. On the outer covering, the remaining styles are those with propping stones erected to match the height of the flagstone; with only the flagstone part without any propping stones; and with all propping stones missing. The burial chamber is also located either on the ground and in the semi-basement, and it is difficult to spot the location of the burial chamber without checking each and every part.  [Woman] The exposed dolmens are also called Jeju-style dolmens. The burial chamber is exposed to the ground, and multiple flagstones are erected along the edge of the capstone. The number of flagstones exposed to the ground amounts to six or more, forming a burial chamber similar to the flat shape of the capstone, while the burial chamber is usually shaped like an oval or square. The exposed dolmen is a unique type of dolmen only found on Jeju Island in Korea. Similar burial chamber structures have also been found in Zhejiang Province, China.

stories.title: Functions of dolmens
stories.script: Functions of dolmens   [Man] The dolmen, part of megalithic culture, has three key functions. First, the dolmen, a prehistoric tomb with a huge capstone placed above the ground or an underground burial chamber, serves as a tomb.   [Woman] In 1962, the National Museum of Korea conducted two excavations of dolmens in Hwangseok-ri of Chungcheongbuk-do.  [Archaeologist 1] “Huh? What are these?”  [Archaeologist 2] “What? What's going on?”  [Archaeologist 1] “Sir, I think you should see this. Please take a look.” What...? Is this what I think it is? It looks like a human bone, doesn't it?  [Archaeologist 2] “Yes! That's right. This is indeed a human bone.”  [Archaeologist 1] “Then it must have been a tomb.”  [Woman] Among them, a human bone of a [male] adult was found in its complete form, and its function as a tomb was reported to the academic world. Although no human bones have been discovered in Jeollanam-do, it is assumed to have served as a tomb given the size of the burial chamber inside the dolmen. The evidence demonstrating its use as a tomb is that dolmens are distributed in groups at each location, that human bones have been found, and that grave items buried during the construction of the tomb have been discovered.   [Man] Second, the dolmen served as an altar. The dolmens that have the characteristics of an altar have three different conditions from dolmens that served as tombs because they were the venue for religious events or ceremonies. First, each of these dolmens stands independently, maintaining a certain distance from the cluster. Second, it is supported by a large oddly-shaped stone capstone and large propping stones which show distinct size and appearance from other dolmens. Third, it is located on high ground overlooking the surrounding area. Based on the combination of these factors, it is assumed that such dolmens served as altars rather than tombs. A society building dolmens needed symbolic monuments to strengthen the cooperation and solidarity of different groups. It is thus estimated that dolmens were built and used as altars.  [Tribe member 1] “Move the stones, quickly!”  [Tribe member 2] “Why are we building this, anyway?”  [Tribe member 1] To show off the strength of our tribe. A few days ago, our neighboring tribe bragged about building a dolmen! The chief saw it, and said we should build one too! We can't let them beat us at it!”  [Tribe member 2] Of course! “We can do better! We should build it bigger and grander!  [Woman] The third function of dolmens is to serve as a headstone. They were used to demonstrate the authority and power of the group that built the monument, symbolizing the graveyard or being the graveyard itself. In some cases, dolmens form a cluster, and a dolmen that is unusually large compared to other dolmens or is located differently from other dolmens served as a headstone.

stories.title: How to build dolmens
stories.audioTitle: How to build dolmens 고인돌의 제작 방법
stories.script: How to build dolmens   [Man] The biggest feature of dolmens is that they used huge capstones. Dolmens were constructed based on the method of placing capstones on top of supporting stones above the ground. So how did they build dolmens?  [Woman] The most important thing in building dolmens was to obtain capstones. Capstones were difficult to obtain because they ranged from just a few tons to as heavy as hundreds of tons. It was necessary to trim the naturally separated stones from nearby mountains or to remove capstones directly from rock walls.  남1 [Chieftain] How much work have you done so far?”  남2 [Laborer] “Sir! We are now ready to remove the capstone. We have drilled several holes into the stone and we are now nailing wooden wedges into these holes. We are almost done with that as well.”  남1 [Chieftain] “Good. Then you'll have to pour water into the wooden wedges to soak them in it. Have you collected the water yet?  남2 [Laborer] Other tribesmen have already gone to get the water. You don’t need to worry too much, sir!”  남1 [Chieftain] This dolmen will demonstrate the power of our tribe. So make sure you build it with special care.  남2 [Laborer] “Sir! I will!”  [Man] When removing the capstone from the quarry, several holes are artificially drilled into the stone. And then wooden wedges are nailed into the holes. After that, the wooden wedges are soaked in water and the wet wooden wedges thereafter expand, causing the stone to be cut out.  [Woman] Various methods were used to transport such capstones. It is generally believed that a transportation route was opened to move the obtained capstones. It is assumed that the capstone was moved by paving a log rail underneath it, placing several logs across the rail, and then raising the capstone to make it easier to move. It is also assumed that they used Y-shaped wooden sleds or even ice in cold climate areas.  [Man] The burial chamber was built next once the capstone was moved. First, the tomb was dug up and plates or broken stones were used to shape the burial chamber. When the burial chamber was built, stone swords or burnished red pottery as well as weapons, accessories and earthenware were sometimes buried together.  [Woman] Once the burial chamber was complete, supporting stones were erected around it, and a hill was built with soil to make it easier to pull up the capstone.  남2 [Laborer] Build a hill out of soil! To raise the capstone!  남3 [Villager] Do we really have to work this much?  남2 [Laborer] Of course, you have to! Raising the capstone is the most difficult task. You have to do your best!”  남3 [Villager] Why is it difficult?  남2 [Laborer] It's because the capstone must strike a balance above the supporting stones. Otherwise, they'll just collapse! We can’t let our efforts be in vain! Hey there! Firm the soil!”  [Woman] Raising the capstone required a high level of civil engineering technology. Once the capstone is raised, they need to dig out the soil from the hill.  [Man] When the construction of the dolmen was completed, as the final event, people held a rite for the dead or a feast for the mobilized. This is an estimation based on the discovery of broken earthenware or stone tools around the grave. Dolmen construction was part of community ritual that required the mobilization of the same kin group as well as the labor force of the neighboring kin. The dolmen construction required a large number of people, including those who built a burial chamber, those who built a transportation route, and those who pulled up the capstone. Dolmens serve as an important historical source that informs the existence of communities that could mobilize this collective labor force.

stories.title: Whose dolmens were they?!
stories.audioTitle: Whose dolmens were they?! 고인돌의 주인은?
stories.script: Whose dolmens were they?!  [Man] There are many stories about the status of those who were buried underneath a dolmen. It is very difficult to determine the identity of the buried person. Many arguments were raised because the dolmens in Korea come in different shapes and densities depending on the region, and because they display various aspects in the cluster and shape of burial chambers.  [Woman] The person buried underneath a dolmen underwent a transformation in their status, as it took a long period of time to build each dolmen. The structure and layout of the burial chamber differs depending on the cluster of dolmens, making it difficult to assume that each tomb belonged to a particular class or stratum. That is why some argue that the dolmen served as a tomb for a ruler like a chieftain and their family members, as a joint tomb for a community of blood ties, or as a tomb for the fallen in battle.  [Man] Building a dolmen requires a large workforce. This is because a capstone weighing as little as a few tons to as much as several hundred tons had to be collected and transported. Thus, there must have been a lot of people to be mobilized as the workforce. Some view the dolmen as the tomb of a leader based on the bronze ware, ornaments, and other grave items excavated.   [Woman] While excavating a series of dolmens, one was found to have no burial chamber. What this suggests is that dolmens were not built solely to serve as tombs. Dolmens were also used as headstones and altars.  [Man] Why were dolmens built? They were built because powerful rulers began to emerge. In the Bronze Age, inter-tribal wars created classes, and rulers needed a reason to flaunt their power. In this process, they came up with building the dolmens. The most ideal way to show off and strengthen one’s authority and demonstrate the power of their tribe was to build a dolmen. The rulers of the time used the dolmen to strengthen their control and further unite the tribes. Dolmen served as a symbol of power and authority.

stories.title: Gochang Dolmen Museum
stories.audioTitle: Gochang Dolmen Museum 고창 고인돌 박물관
stories.script: Gochang Dolmen Museum   [Friend 1] “Do you have your ticket?”  [Friend 2] “Here it is.”  [Friend 1] The Gochang Dolmen Museum is the first dolmen museum in Korea.  [Friend 2] Is that so? It's huge in here.“  [Friend 1] It was built on 57,988 square meters of land, with a total floor space of about 3,852.8 square meters on a budget of 18.3 billion won.  [Friend 2] That's really something...  [Friend 1] The dolmen museum offers various artifacts from the Bronze Age and the dolmen culture found throughout the world! Also, if you buy a ticket at the entrance, you can take a tour train to explore dolmen ruins on courses 1 to 5.”  [Friend 2] And the Gochang Dolmen Museum lets you encounter the artifacts and living conditions of the Bronze Age and the dolmen culture throughout the world at a glance. As a museum specializing in dolmens, its offers both indoor and outdoor exhibitions.  [Friend 1] What does it have for the indoor exhibition?  [Friend 2] The inside consists of a special exhibition room on the first floor and a storage room for artifacts. The second floor is a permanent exhibition hall, where we can easily access academic materials related to the lifestyle and dolmens of the Bronze Age. The third floor gives us the chance to build a fire, draw rock art, and build a dolmen. Outdoor viewing telescopes are also available to offer views of the outdoor exhibition space and historic sites.  [Friend 1] So what about the outdoor exhibition?  [Friend 2] The external exhibition consists of a prehistoric village, an experience hall, and an exhibition hall. The prehistoric village has the village restored to when the dolmens were built to help us to easily understand the lifestyle of the people in the era of dolmens.   [Friend 1] Then let’s go to the indoor exhibition first!“  [Friend 2] Sure.  [Man] Gochang Dolmen Museum is a specialized dolmen museum, offering not only the dolmens in Gochang but also the World Heritage Sites in Hwasun and Ganghwa. It also gives you the chance to enjoy various learning information on the World Heritage Sites in Korea and the megalithic culture found throughout the world all in one place.  [Woman] Gochang Dolmen Museum is open from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., while its operating hours are adjusted to 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. during the winter season from November to February. The museum closes every Monday and on January 1st each year.

stories.title: Gochang Dolmen Site Course 1
stories.audioTitle: Gochang Dolmen Site Course 1 고창 고인돌 유적 제 1코스
stories.script: Gochang Dolmen Site Course 1   [Man] The Gochang Dolmen Site Course 1 is located at the eastern end of the dolmen site. There are 53 dolmens at the foot of the mountain and the ridge running from Jungbong Peak in Juklim-ri, consisting of one table dolmen, 12 go-board dolmens, 28 pad-stone dolmens, and 12 dolmens of unknown types.  [Woman] The table dolmens have a burial chamber made of 4 or 6 wide flagstones that are exposed above the ground, with a flat capstone placed on top of the burial chamber. They are called table dolmens because they resemble a table. They were once called northern-style dolmens because they were mainly found north of the Han River and in the Liaoning province of China.  [Man] The table dolmens shown in Room 2509 are shaped to form a modified table-like form. The capstone is 340 cm long and 150 cm high, and although it may appear like a go-board dolmen, there are two supporting stones of 220 cm and 80 cm long standing parallel to each other at 80 cm intervals in the lower structure, showing a mixture of table and go-board styles.   [Woman] On the other hand, the dolmen No. 2513 is a typical go-board dolmen with five supporting stones. The characteristic of this dolmen is that its supporting stones are decorated with patterns shaped like pillars. The supporting stones that support or prop the capstone directly hold the capstone while preventing any destruction to the burial chamber in the lower structure.  [Man] The pad-stone dolmens have a capstone placed right above the burial chamber built underground. The pad-stone dolmens that cover their burial chambers without any supporting stones are alternatively referred to as no-support, lid, or footstone dolmens. In this type, a stone burial chamber is almost always found, indicating that they were originally intended to serve as tombs.  [Woman] There is a legend of a man from the north and a woman from the south related to the dolmen No. 2509 in course 1. It is also a story that has been around for centuries in Maesan Village. The son of a chieftain who lived in Ganghwado Island had lost in a war, and sailed south with a few tribe members to arrive at the Maesan village through the Simwonman Harbor of Gochang. After that, he became close with the daughter of the chieftain of Maesan village, and went to obtain permission from her father to marry her.  [Son of Chieftain from Ganghwado Island] I would like to request your daughter's hand in marriage, sir. We are in love.”  [Daughter of Chieftain of Gochang] “Father, please say yes.”  [Chieftain of Gochang] You’ll never marry her. Not over my dead body. Sweetheart, he is just a failure who lost in the war and has fled to us. I can't allow someone like that to marry my daughter. Leave at once! God forbid! Not a chance!”  [Daughter of Chieftain of Gochang] Oh, father, I think this is the end for me.”  [Chieftain of Gochang] Open your eyes, my child. It's all my fault. Sweetheart! No!!!”  [Villager 1] After he was so adamant against her marriage, he has let her go. I feel sorry for her death.”  [Villager 2] “Hey, watch what you say. Our chieftain might hear you.
