The language of prickly water lily is known to be Good Fortune.” They named the revived wetlands Prickly Water Lily Wetlands after this lucky flower.

stories.title: Gangmun Beach (Gangmun Jinttobaegi)
stories.script: Gangmun Beach(Gangmun Jinttobaegi)  If you fancy a memorable trip to the ocean, why not take a trip to Gangmun Beach? Gangmun Beach is famous for its scenic views. With a variety of sculptures resembling a ring, a heart and a photo frame, you can take unforgettable photos against the blue ocean. You can also enjoy a good cup of coffee with a view at one of the coffee shops along the sandy beach of Gangneung, the city of coffee, where many famous coffee breweries are concentrated.  Gangmun Beach is also a popular destination for scuba divers. If you take a boat from the beach for about 5 minutes, you can experience a beautiful underwater world filled with natural rock formations, sea anemones, and large fish. You can also taste the fresh seafood that’s brought in every morning from the sea at the small port near the beach.  You can’t talk about Gangmun Beach without talking about “Jinttobaegi”. “Jinttobaegi” is Gangneung dialect for a sotdae, that’s to say a pole or pillar related with folk beliefs, with a carved bird perched on its top. The Gangmun-dong Jinttobaegi standing by the entrance of Gangmun village is particularly well known for its aesthetic beauty, and attracts many photo lovers.  Perched on top of the Jinttobaegi are three wooden ducks, each facing in a different direction, which express wishes for the wellbeing of the village and a good catch, and protection from wind, fire and water disasters.

stories.title: Site of the Birthplace of Heo Nanseolheon
stories.audioTitle: 12. Site of the Birthplace of Heo Nanseolheon
stories.script: 12. Site of the Birthplace of Heo Nanseolheon   * Woman: The Tale of Hong Gildong is the first novel written in Hangeul.  * Man: Really? Who is the author? * Woman: It was written by Heo Gyun, a prominent Korean politician and scholar of the Joseon dynasty. He criticized social iniquities such as discrimination against illegitimate children, and insisted that talents should be recruited regardless of their social class. * Man: He sounds like a great guy. * Woman: I'm sure it was not an easy thing to do in the strict class-based society of the Joseon Dynasty. By the way, we are at the site of the birthplace of Heo Gyun's older sister, Heo Nanseolheon. They learned to write poems from childhood, and with their father and two brothers, they came to be known as the “Five Great Stylists of the Heo Family.” Heo Nanseolheon was obviously the most distinguished of all of them. * Man: Even from her childhood? * Woman: That's right. She was kind of a child prodigy, who started writing poems at the age of 8, but she did not have a happy marriage, and she died at the young age of 27 while grieving over the death of her sons. * Man: She died too young… * Woman: But her short life is remembered because of her poems. Heo Gyun collected his sister's poems and published them in China with the help of an envoy from the Ming Dynasty. Later, her poems were also published in Joseon and Japan, making her the only woman in the history of the Joseon Dynasty to win fame in all three countries. I’ve heard she was quite famous in both China and Japan. * Man: Wow, that's incredible! * Woman: I know! Now let's go and look around the Heo Gyun and Heo Nalselheon Memorial Park.

stories.title: Heo Gyun and Heo Nanseolheon Memorial Hall
stories.audioTitle: 13. Heo Gyun and Heo Nanseolheon Memorial Hall
stories.script: Heo Gyun and Heo Nanseolheon Memorial Hall   * Male Narrator: How can I stay if I cannot even address my father as “Father” and my older brother as “Brother”? * Woman: That's a famous line from The Tale of Hong Gildong. * Man: The Tale of Hong Gildong? * Woman: Yes, that's right. It's the story of Hong Gildong, the illegitimate son of a nobleman, who stole from the rich and gave to the poor, and later founded Yuldo, an ideal country. It is the first novel written in Hangeul for the common people, who did not know the language of the ruling class, Hanmun. * Man: A-ha! So that’s why it is written in Hanguel. * Woman: The Tale of Hong Gildong reflects Heo Gyun's progressive thinking and his ambition to reform society. It instantly became a sensational hit, but he failed to achieve his ambition because he was executed on charges of treason. * Female Narrator:  “The sweet scent wafting from the swaying branches and leaves of an orchid lingers on the autumn breeze.  Its beauty might wane, but its pure fragrance never dies.  It breaks my heart and drenches my sleeve with tears.” * Woman: It is a poem called Gamwoo by Heo Nanseolheon. * Man: It's sad yet very beautiful. * Woman: She expressed the limitations she experienced as a woman in the Joseon Dynasty using elegant poetic diction. You can find her works in a book called The Collected Poems of Nanseolheon, which includes 213 poems and 3 prose pieces.  The works of Heo Gyun and Heo Nanseolheon, as well as those of other members of the Five Great Stylists of the Heo Family, are displayed in the Heo Gyun and Heo Nanseolheon Memorial Hall.

stories.title: Gangneung Green City Experience Center (E-zen)
stories.script: Gangneung Green City Experience Center (E-zen)  In 2009, Gangneung was selected as the first model low-carbon, green city in Korea. The Green City Experience Center -- dubbed “E-zen” -- in front of Gyeongpodae, is a zero-energy building symbolizing the eco-friendly city Gangneung. At E-zen, we don't use chemical fuels like coal or petroleum to avoid the emission of carbon dioxide, the culprit of global warming. The main energy we use is solar and geothermal power. It's enough energy for about 40 households to use for a year, and we are saving 30% of energy by supplying hot and cold water needed for the building through geothermal heat.  We have also minimized energy loss by installing triple-layered windows and using insulation materials that are twice as thick as those used in other buildings. The grass we planted in the building increases the insulation effects. The Green City Experience Center runs educational and experience-centered programs to stress the importance of nature and resources. You can see the process of generating eco-friendly energy at the renewable energy-themed park outside. Do not forget to visit the Lagoon Ecology Center at Gyeongpo Aquarium, located behind ‘E-zen’, to see a diverse group of aquatic organisms found in Gyeongpo Lake as well as the East Sea.

stories.title: Kim Si-seup Memorial Hall
stories.script: Kim Si-seup Memorial Hall  * Man: Maewoldang Kim Si-seup is the author of a book titled Geumo Sinhwa. * Woman: Geumo Sinhwa? * Man: It's a collection of five short stories, which are mostly about heroes who cross the boundary between reality and dreams, and who strive against fate. Kim Si-seup was an extremely gifted child who was already able to write poetry at the tender age of three. King Sejong, the fourth king of the Joseon dynasty, upon hearing the widespread rumors of a child genius, called him to the palace and tested his talent. Kim proved his intelligence and was given silk as a gift. * Woman: You mean King Sejong the Great, the Joseon king who created Hangeul? * Man: That’s right! The life of Kim Si-seup completely changed when he was just 21 years old. When the second son of King Sejong usurped the throne from his nephew, Danjong, and proclaimed himself king, Kim Si-seup burnt all his books and became a Buddhist monk. He wandered around the country and left behind numerous writings. He wrote Geumo Sinhwa when he was 31. * Woman: The very first Korean novel written in Chinese characters! * Man: Kim led a nomadic life for the rest of his days, but subsequent generations admired him. For instance, the fourteenth ruler of the Joseon dynasty, King Seonjo, ordered Yulgok Yi Yu to write a biography of Kim Si-seup, while the twenty-second monarch, King Jeongjo, bestowed upon him the posthumous title of Cheongganggong. In Joseon, a posthumous title was usually awarded to a king or scholar official after their death. * Woman: So that's how Geumo Sinhwa could be passed down! * Man: You can watch a documentary about the life of Kim Si-seup and an animated version of Geumo Sinhwa at the Memorial Hall. Don't forget to check out his autobiographical poem Tongbong Six Stanza while you’re there.

stories.title: Seongyojang House
stories.script: Seongyojang House   * Man: We are now at Seongyojang House, a residential complex dating from the Joseon period. It can also be referred to as a 99-kan structure, where “kan” refers to the space between two pillars. * Woman: A house with 99 kan? * Man: Yes. During the Joseon dynasty, only royal palaces could have more than 100 kan. In other words, Seongyojang was the largest residence any member of the ruling class could have.  * Woman: Who owned this complex? * Man: It used to belong to Lee Nae-beon, an 11th-generation descendent of Prince Hyoryeong, and his family. Gyeongpo Lake was situated right in front of Seongyojang House at the time it was built, and a bridge was built across the lake by connecting boats together. That is how the name of the bridge, Seongyojang, came about. Ah, by the way, a local legend has it that weasels guided the current site.  * Woman: Weasels? * Man: It is said that Lee Nae-beon ended up in this area while chasing a pack of weasels. The site appeared auspicious due to the proximity of water and a mountain, so he ordered a house to be built here. * Woman: What a mysterious story! * Man: The custom of leaving out some food for weasels as a sign of gratitude is still observed at Seongyojang. The house has retained its original form as an upper-class residence for some 300 years. You can also see the evolution of the housing of Joseon as new buildings were built here over the generations. It was the first private house to be designated as an Important Folklore Material in Korea. The Museum of Seongyojang exhibits numerous artifacts related to its 300-year history. * Woman: I can't wait to see inside! * Man: Then let’s go in!

stories.title: Hwallaejeong
stories.script: Hwallaejeong  * Woman: That gazebo reminds me of the lotus flower on the pond. * Man: It's even more beautiful with the surrounding trees, don’t you think? The gazebo is called Hwallaejeong. It was built in 1816, and was used by the head of Seongyojang in the summer.  * Woman: What does Hwallaejeong mean?  * Man: The name originates from the phrase in Thoughts from Reading, a poem by a Zhu Xi, a Chinese Confucian scholar of the Song dynasty. Hwallsurae means “clear water is continuously flowing”, and in fact, the water from the nearby mountain flows into the pond. Because there is no wall, you can open all the doors and enjoy marvelous views of the beautiful scenery, including lotus flowers in full bloom, in every direction. * Woman: That sounds wonderful! * Man: There is a tearoom in Hwallaejeong especially for guests. Seongyojang was famous for its lotus tea recipe. They placed the tea leaves inside a closed lotus flower overnight before serving it in the morning. * Woman: I guess they did it to infuse the tea leaves with the fragrance of the lotus flower. * Man: Right! Renowned figures of the Joseon literati visited Seongyojang and wrote poems and painted pictures during their sojourn. Writings by famous artists and scholars are still preserved on the horizontal board under the eaves and on the board of the pillar of Hwallaejeong.  I believe Hwallaejeong symbolizes style and elegance and is the most attractive spot in Seongyojang. It’s truly a place of art and culture.

stories.title: The Inner Quarters (Dongbyeoldang and Seobyeoldang)
stories.script: 19. Anchae(The Inner Quarters) (Dongbyeoldang, Seobyeoldang)  * Man: The inner quarters is known to be the first building of Seongyojang. * Woman: What is it used for? * Man: It is actually the living quarters of the female inhabitants of Seongyojang, including the wife of the eldest son of the family and other direct family members or linear descendants. The inner quarters consists of a 5 rooms by 2 rooms building comprising two rooms with a daecheong, or wooden-floored main hall, in the center. The  room on the right is a space for the lady of the house. The broad kitchen next to it will give you an idea of the size of the family she had to feed and take care of. The opposite room is for daughters-in-law, and is connected to a storeroom. * Woman: What was the storeroom used for? * Man: It's where you can make and keep small dishes and store kitchen tools.  * Woman: I see. So the main room connects to the kitchen, while the opposite room connects to the storeroom.  * Man: And the inner quarters connects to Dongbyeoldang to the east and Seobyeoldang to the west. Dongbyeoldang is the private quarters where the head of Seongyojang would receive guests, while Seobyeoldang was used as a library and study room. And the Oebyeoldang, which is located outside the main building, is still inhabited by the descendants of Seongyojang.

stories.title: Yeolhwadang
stories.script: 20. Yeolhwadang   * Man: This is the main residential area of the head of the household. If Hwallaejeong is suitable for summer, then Yeolhwadang is ideal for winter.  * Woman: It has a very peculiar appearance. At first sight, it looks like a western structure. * Man: Oh, that's because of the shape of the eaves. Yeolhwadang is a traditional Korean house built in 1815, the transitional period between the late Joseon Dynasty and the Korean Empire. It is said that a Russian ambassador to Korea gave the Western-style eaves as a gift, which were added on under the original eaves. * Woman: The name “Yeolhwadang” also sounds peculiar. Does it mean anything in particular? * Man: The first syllable, yeol, means “happiness”, while the second, hwa, means “talking”. So it literally means “having a friendly talk and living happily”. It is said that Seongyojang constantly received all kinds of visitors thanks to the generosity of the head of the house and the beautiful scenery. * Woman: To have a friendly talk at Yeolhwadang! * Man: Probably. Kim Jeong-hui, the most celebrated calligraphist of the late Joseon period, visited Seongyojang on his way back from Mt. Kumgang and wrote the following phrase: I would live as light as autumn leaves” on the horizontal signboard. The father of King Gojong, also known as the Daewongun, or Regent, also left behind a work of art here. A collection of 24 books that record the names of guests at Seongyojang has been preserved to the present day! Now you can guess how frequented this place was.  * Woman: How is it used now? * Man: Yeolhwadang is open to guests even today. There is a pipe organ in the wooden-floored main hall, and concerts are held there regularly. And concerts are held at the outdoor concert hall all year round.

stories.title: Site of of Dongjin School
stories.script: 21. Site of of Dongjin School  * Man: This is the site of Dongjin School, Gangwon-do's first modern private school. * Woman: You mean there was a school in Seongyojang? * Man: They took a storeroom of Seongyojang and built a school there in 1908 for local children who didn't have a chance to get any education. The owners paid all the students’ expenses including room and board, tuition fees, school uniforms, and textbooks.     * Woman: 1908 was in the time of the Korean Empire, wasn't it? * Man: Correct! They taught the students such subjects as geography, history, arithmetic, and music. Education on the Korean language and the history of the Joseon dynasty was particularly emphasized. What they did was to give the children a nationalistic education based on the modern sciences, and the Korean national anthem and the Student Song were included in the music textbook. Unfortunately, the school was forced to close down in its third year when the country was annexed by the Japanese. * Woman: That's a shame. What happened after that? * Man: Though the school was shut down, Seon-gyojang House secretly provided funds for the independence movement. When Korea was liberated in 1945, independence fighter and politician Kim Gu presented to Seongyojang House as a token of his appreciation for the family's patriotism three pieces of his writing, two of which are stored in the Museum of Seongyojang.

stories.title: Ojukheon House
stories.script: 22. Ojukheon House   * Woman: Ojukheon House was where one of the most symbolic figures in Korean history, Yi Yi, and his mother Shin Saimdang lived.  * Man: A house for a mother and a son! * Woman: Yukgok Yi Yi was both a scholar who conducted a comprehensive survey of Neo-Confucianism, which was the ruling doctrine of the Joseon dynasty, and a politician who wanted to carry out comprehensive reforms and change the country. His mother, on the other hand, was good at poetry and prose, and was mostly known for her extraordinary paintings. * Man: I see. So what is Ojukheon House like? * Woman: Ojukheon originally belonged to Lady Yi, the mother of Shin Saimdang. She gave her property to her five daughters and grandchildren. She also gave Yulgok a traditional Korean house in Seoul, and Ojukheon House to another grandson, Gwon Cheo-kyun,  * Man: Why did they name it Ojukheon? * Woman: It is said that after Gwon Cheo-kyun saw a grove of dark bamboo growing near the house, he took as his pen-name Ojuk, which literally means “black bamboo”. And later he named his house after his pen-name. * Man: And that's why it's called Ojukheon House! * Woman: Did you know that Ojukheon House also appears on the 5,000 won note? * Man: Right! The 5,000 won note also depicts Yi Yi, while the 50,000 won note features Shin Saimdang! * Woman: Yes, they are the first mother and son in the world to be featured on banknotes. So shall we go into their precious home, Ojukheon?

stories.title: Chochungdo Garden
stories.script: 23. Chochungdo Garden  * Woman: This is the garden where the flowers and grass often featured in Shin Saimdang's painting grew. * Man: Oh, I almost forgot that she was also an extraordinary painter! * Woman: Yes, she was never formally taught, but she started to paint by herself when she was young. There is an anecdote about a chicken that pecked away at one of her grass and insect paintings while it was laid out to dry in the yard, after mistaking it for real insects. * Man: That means her paintings were very realistic. * Woman: She was also a good copyist who could make an exact copy of a painting by the renowned landscape painter An Gyeon. She was extremely talented, and left behind numerous works that depict landscapes, grapes, grass, and insects. The Joseon literati even dedicated admiring poems and prose to her paintings. * Man: And it's Ojukheon where this extraordinary painter was born and raised? * Woman: After her father died, she stayed in Ojukheon to live with her mother. She married at the age of 19 and gave birth to Yulgok when she was 33. She is said to have lived in Ojukheon for a long time after that.       * Man: So it would not be an overstatement to say that Ojukheon House was her artistic playground. I am looking forward to see her painting depicting flowers in the garden. * Woman: Many of Shin Saimdang’s paintings are exhibited at the Yulgok Memorial Hall, including some of her landscape paintings and her grass and insects paintings.

stories.title: Ojukheon (Mongryong Chamber) and Munseongsa Shrine
stories.script: Ojukheon (Mongryong Chamber) and Munseongsa Shrine  * Woman: Ojukheon is the private quarters of the house. It was built in the early Joseon period, and has been designated as Treasure No.165.  * Man: You mean that both the house and the private quarters are called Ojukheon? * Woman: That's right. And they include the room in which Yulgok Yi Yi was born.  * Man: He was born in here * Woman: The room is named the “Black Dragon Chamber” after Shin Saimdang's birth dream of a black dragon flying into a room, which she had when she gave birth to Yulgok. It contains a portrait of Shin Saimdang now. * Man: This room is rich in historic meanings! * Woman: Yulgok, who was born in 1536, learned from his mother and was a child prodigy. He passed the Civil Service literary examination at the age of 13. But he secluded himself following his mother's death when he was 16, and mourned privately for the next 3 years. It was common practice among the Neo-Confucian literati class to live in a shack beside one’s parents’ graves in order to show filial piety. After completing the prescribed 3-year period of mourning, Yulgok went into retreat at Kumgang Mountain and devoted himself to the study of Buddhism.  * Man: What happened next? * Woman: He came back after a year. At the age of 29, Yi passed a higher civil service examination with the highest marks, and consistently received the top honors in nine consecutive civil service examinations. This is a record and the first and only time it occurred in the history of Joseon. * Man: He certainly sounds like the most intelligent man of his time! * Woman: I can't disagree with that. Yulgok is remembered in Korean history as one of the most revered politicians and influential thinkers of his day, who left behind numerous books. The Munseongsa Shrine, next to Ojukheon, enshrines Yi Yi's portrait, so it will be a good idea to check it out!

stories.title: Eojaegak Pavilion (Ojukheon House, Gangneung)
stories.script: Eojaegak Pavilion of Ojukheon House, Gangneung  Eojaegak Pavilion was built by order of King Jeongjo to praise the esteemed scholar Yi I, also known as Yulgok.  Yi I played an important role in undertaking a series of reforms aimed at improving the quality of life and advocated for the training of 100,000 soldiers to strengthen national defense, demonstrating his foresight as a politician. He was also a great scholar who compiled works such as Seonghakjibyo”, or “Outline of the Learning of the Sages to enlighten the King, and Gyeokmongyogyeol or The Secret of Expelling Ignorance, for those who begins their studies.   King Jeongjo, who greatly admired Yulgok Yi I, learned that Yulgok's handwritten manuscript of Gyeokmongyogyeol and his inkstone were kept at Ojukheon House. He had them brought to him, wrote a preface for Gyeokmongyogyeol, and inscribed the back of the inkstone with a note praising Yulgok. These items were then returned to Ojukheon House. Even after a long time, the ink stone and “Gyeokgmongyogyeol” are still keep in good condition as the purpose of Eojegak Pavilion was built to preserve them.   Next to Eojaegak Pavilion, there are two buildings. While the Sarangchae is where the male member of the household stayed, the Anchae is the living quarters for the lady and the other direct-female family members. Ojukheon House has an open structure that allows easy access between the Sarangchae and Anchae. If you have some free time in Gangneung, it is highly recommended to take a look at both areas!

stories.title: Yulgok Memorial Hall
stories.script: 26. Yulgok Memorial Hall  * Woman: The Yulgok Memorial Hall displays various mementos of Shin Saimdang and her children, including Yulgok Yi Yi, Yi Mae-chang, the eldest daughter, and Yi Woo, her youngest son. * Man: The ideal place to find out more about the family of Yulgok Yi Yi! * Woman: You're right. Shin Saimdang had four sons and three daughters; and Yulgok, Mae-chang and Woo were the three siblings who were as famous as their mother at that time. Mae-chang was even known as the little Shin Saimdang. * Man: I guess she was also good at painting? * Woman: Right! She inherited her talent from her mother and excelled at both literature and the arts. You can see Mae-chang's <Plum Blossom> and other paintings such as her ink painting depicting a bird at the Memorial Hall.   * Man: What about the youngest son, Yi Woo? * Woman: Yi Woo was good at painting and calligraphy as well as playing the geomungo. He was so attached to his brother Yulgok that he turned down his posting after passing the Civil Service literary examination, out of fear that he would be separated from him. * Man: The brothers must have been on very good terms with each other! * Woman: You can see Woo's painting <Chrysanthemum> and his calligraphy work at the Memorial Hall. Furthermore, his letters and annals, along with the book Yulgok Jeonseo, or The Collected Works of Yulgok, are on display there. You can also see Chochungdo paintings of flowers and insects painted on a folding screen and <A Study on Plum Blossoms> by Shin Saimdang.

stories.title: Municipal Museum of Gangneung
stories.script: Municipal Museum of Gangneung  * Woman: If you’re wondering what kind of life the people of Gangneung led, you should visit the Municipal Museum of Gangneung. * Man: What do they exhibit there? * Woman: The entire city of Gangneung deserves to be called a historic site, because so many relics and ruins have been found there. Relics unearthed from prehistoric settlement sites, such as polished stone tools and comb-pattern potteries, and others found in ancient tombs, such as a jar with a narrow neck and mounted dishes, are on display. In addition, there are many Buddhist relics that were excavated at the site of a famous old temple. The Seated Stone Bodhisattva of Hansongsaji Archeological Site, in particular, is considered to be very special. * Man: What is special about it? * Woman: Well, most Korean stone Buddha statues are made of granite, but the Seated Stone Bodhisattva of the Hansongsaji Archeological Site is made of marble. The carving technique is so elaborate and beautiful that it has been designated as a National Cultural Property. There are other artifacts that offer us a glimpse into the daily lives of the peole of Gangneung. Have you heard of the Gye? * Man: What is a Gye? * Woman: A “Gye” is a form of cooperative organization created to promote friendship. In Gangneung, there is a saying, “It takes only three people to organize a Gye.” The Gye has hundreds years of history, and the Gye-Cheob, or records of Gye meetings, are also exhibited in the museum. You can also see Jiseok, records of the personal information of the deceased; Myeonggi,” a funerary vessel buried in a grave for use by the deceased in the afterlife; and “The Eight Views of Gwandong,” a landscape painting depicting scenic spots on the East Coast.

stories.title: Ojuk Hanok Village
stories.script: Ojuk Hanok Village  * Woman: There is a marvelous Hanok village here! * Man: This is the Ojuk Hanok Village, which consists of houses built using traditional construction techniques. Our Korean forbears considered harmony with nature the most important element when building a hanok. They selected a site that does not interfere with the landscape, and designed the building by incorporating into it elements of the mountains, sky and wind, using the materials they could find around the house. * Woman: In other words, a hanok is purposely built so that people can live as a part of nature! * Man: Absolutely. At the Ojuk Hanok Village you can learn about the beauty and importance of hanok and experience a variety of traditional games and a crafts session. You can stay there overnight, too, if you wish to immerse yourself in a real hanok experience.  * Woman: You mean we can stay overnight in a traditional house? * Man: The rooms at the Ojuk Hanok Village are named after the content in Gyeokmongyogyeol, a book by Yulgok Yi Yi, one of the most prominent Korean Confucian scholars of the Joseon Dynasty, which he wrote for those just beginning their studies I hope you can enjoy the grandeur of a hanok at Ojuk Hanok Village, where you can experience the wisdom of life of our ancestors.

stories.title: Byeongsan Gamja-ongsimi Village
stories.script: Byeongsan Gamja-ongsimi Village   Gangwon-do's top agricultural product is potato. The area has high altitude and low temperature, which is suitable for growing potatoes. During the time when rice was scarce, potato was staple food for the people in Gangwon-do, and they ate ‘Gamja-ongsimi’, or potato dough soup, more than anything.   Potatoes are grated, drained, and mixed with the potato starch settling at the bottom of the drained water. The potato dough is balled into ongsimi and boiled in broth with vegetable. The chewy ongsimi and the thickness of the starch give it a savory taste. From the 1980s, restaurants specializing in ‘Gamja-ongsimi’ opened in Byeongsan-dong district, which has become today’s ‘Byeongsan Gamja-ongsimi Village’. There are about 10 restaurants serving gamja-ongsimi and other food made with potatoes such as gamja-jeok and gamja-songpyeon.  Gamja-jeok is made by mixing starch and grated potato, just like ongsimi, and then pan-fried. Gamja-songpyeon is rice cake stuffed with beans or red bean paste. It's a delicacy that you must try along with gamja-ongsimi when you visit Gangwon-do.

stories.title: Wolhwa Street
stories.script: Wolhwa Street   Wolhwa Street refers to a 2.6km section along the railroad. A walkway was created after the KTX railroad went underground and was inspired by the love story between Muwolang and Lady Yeonhwa after whom the street was named.  According to the story, Muwolang, a nobleman of the Unified Silla Kingdom, visited Gangneung and fell in love with Yeonhwa who was feeding carp in a pond. Muwolang soon had to return to his hometown Gyeongju, and Yeonhwa was being forced to marry another. Yeonhwa wrote a letter informing him of her situation and had a carp deliver it. Meanwhile, Muwolang bought a carp at a market to feed his sick mother and found the letter from Yeonhwa inside the fish. Muwolang immediately went to Gangneung and married Yeonhwa. There, the story of Muwolang and Lady Yeonhwa dated 1,300 years ago was revived. The romantic Wolhwa Street is filled with forest walkway, park, lovely cafes, and public square where diverse performances and events are held. There is a traditional market close by where you can try local Gangneung food. If you cross Wolhwa Bridge, you will see Wolhwajeong, a gazebo dedicated to Muwolang and Lady Yeonhwa. Keep walking along the forest trail, and you will arrive at Noam Tunnel where trains used to pass. It's one of the best photo spots in Gangneung, so take great photos against the beautiful background featuring a tunnel.

stories.title: Gangneng Jungang Seongnam Market
stories.script: Gangneng Jungang Seongnam Market  Jungang Seongnam Market in Gangneung is the oldest traditional market in the Yeongdong district east of Daegwallyeong in Gangwon-do. With more than 500 shops and stalls, it is definitely a must-visit place for authentic local foods.   This market is sectioned into 3 parts. The first floor is the traditional market where you will find all kinds of food and dried goods such as wild vegetables like fascia sprouts, gondeure thistle, and Fischer’s ragwort in spring, corn and potatoes in summer, and Gangwon-do's specialties such as pine mushroom in autumn. Be sure to try street food like sweet and spicy chicken, fish cake croquette, cream cheese garlic bread, and seed-stuffed pancake and check out the alley full of Ox Head Soup restaurants.   The second level houses a variety of restaurants. If you visit ‘Gangneung’, you should try its seafood! The most popular dish in all restaurants is Maeun-tang or spicy fish stew. In particular, spicy soup with shaggy sea raven, called Samsugitang, is the bestseller on the menus. It has long been a popular local food among the natives of Gangneung. The underground level houses Yeongdong's biggest fish market. Don’t miss fresh fish and other seafood like octopus that arrive every day. They are not only fresh but also reasonably priced.

stories.title: Gangeung Daedohobu Gwana (Government Office)
stories.script: Gangeung Daedohobu Gwana (Government Office)  * Woman: We're now at the Gangeung Daedohobu Government Office. * Man: What is a Daedohobu, by the way? * Woman: The Daedohobu were administrative agencies established in the large provinces during the Goryeo and Joseon dynasties. The Daehobu of Gangneung was founded in 1389 and became a political, administrative, cultural, and military center that oversaw Yeongdong, the eastern region of Daegwallyeong in Gangwon-do. * Man: Since this place is the government office of Daedohobu, it must have been in charge of administrative matters. * Woman: Yes. The Daedohobu Government Office was where the local government officials worked. Usually, government offices were divided into two places: the outer quarters, where the head of the office deliberated and decided upon state policies, and the inner quarters, where his family stayed. Unfortunately, most of these government buildings were torn down during the Japanese colonial period, leaving only the Chilsadang and Sammun Gate of the Imyeonggwan. The Chilsadang oversaw local administrative affairs, while Sammun Gate was the main entrance to the Imyeonggwan, which was the residence of central officials who traveled to the province.  * Man: So we can longer see the government office? * Woman: The good news is that - thanks to the restoration program started in 2006 - Amun, the main government office, Dongheon, a building where general administration and trials were conducted, and Uiwoonru, an elegant gazebo have all been restored to their original appearance. Shall we go inside the Daedohobu Government Office?

stories.title: Sammun Gate of Imyeonggwan
stories.script: Sammun Gate of Imyeonggwan  * Woman: This is the Imyeonggwan, a government institution used as a guesthouse. * Man: Who was it intended for? * Woman: It provided accommodation for central government officials or foreign envoys visiting the area. It was also a venue for the regular rites and ceremonies held to honor the king. It contained a wooden tablet symbolizing the king, and a ceremony in which the participants bowed toward the royal capital was performed there on the 1st and 15th days of each month. * Man: It sounds like an important place! * Woman: Yes, but sadly the original Imyeonggwan, which was established in 936, was torn down during the Japanese colonial period and not restored until 2006. However, Sammun Gate has stood in the same place ever since its construction. * Man: You mean it has stood there since the Goryeo Dynasty? * Woman: Yes. Sammun Gate was built at the end of the Goryeo Dynasty, and exhibits the characteristic style of Goryeo architecture. You can see that its pillars follow the Baeheulrim style. * Man: The Baeheulrim style? * Woman: Yes. This refers to the application of a convex curve to the center of a pillar. It gives an impression of full-bodied-ness from a distance as well as a sense of stability. The pillar of Sammun Gate is known to be the largest pillar, as well as the most notable example of the Baeheulrim style, among all remaining Goryeo wooden structures. * Man: I can see that it's a very valuable cultural property. * Woman: I agree. Sammun Gate of the Imyeonggwan is the oldest gate of any guesthouse, and has rightly been designated as National Treasure No. 51.

stories.title: Chilsadang
stories.script: Chilsadang  * Woman: Chilsadang is where the head of the office managed local affairs.  * Man: What does Chilsadang mean? * Woman: It means the Office of Seven Government Affairs. It was thus named because seven areas of government - including agriculture, population, education, trials, military, taxation, and the edification of local citizen - were administered here. During the Japanese colonial period, most of the buildings at the Daedohobu Government Office were torn down, but the Chilsadang, first established in 1867, the fourth year of the reign of King Gojong, the 26th ruler of Joseon, remains as it is. * Man: Is the Chilsadang a cultural property? * Woman: Sure, it is currently designated as a Tangible Cultural Property of Gangwon-do. Although the Chilsadang was a government office in the Joseon Dynasty, it is now a ceremonial venue used to announce the beginning of Dano Festival, the largest festival in Gangneung, as well as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * Man: Did you say the beginning of the Dano Festival? * Woman: Yes, Gangneung’s Dano Festival starts with the making of libations. People brew “sinju,” a sacred wine that is used in the traditional rites held here at the Chilsadang. The libation making ceremony is held on the 5th day of the April of the lunar calendar, and begins when the hosts of the ceremony enter the Chilsadang bearing yeast and rice. Then a ritual warding off of evil spirits is performed, followed by the brewing of wine.  * Man: Wow! That really is something I would love to see for myself! * Woman: Sure, the festival is open to everyone who wishes to participate in it. So be sure to come and check it out!

stories.title: Myeongju-dong Alleyway
stories.script: 38. Myeongju-dong Alleyway   Nowadays, Myeongju-dong Alleyway is one of those hot places that everyone wants to visit. Myeongju-dong had been the political, administrative, and cultural center of Gangneung from the Goryeo dynasty to the Joseon Dynasty. It's an old town with ruins of old government buildings and fortress along with old wooden houses, and tile-roofed traditional houses still remain as if time has stopped. Myeongju-dong Alleyway gradually changed following the restoration of the old government buildings, with a cultural complex for local artists and citizens created in a closed school after renovation.    An aged church became a performance hall, and an old mill turned into a stylish cafe. Old wooden houses are renovated into lively cultural venues for coffee-making experience and promoting a film festival.  Walk along the Myeongju-dong alleyway, where the old tradition and newcomer's hip culture harmoniously coexist.

stories.title: Myeongju Art Park
stories.script: Myeongju Art Park  We are at Myeongju Art Park, where all the changes in Myeongju-dong Alley started. A former elementary school, the building is renovated into a cultural and artistic space for local artists and citizens.  Myeongju Art Park has 3 floors. The first floor houses an exhibition space and a resting area as well as music studios suitable for rehearsing Korean traditional music gukak and orchestra. On the second floor are rehearsal studios for bands and dancers as well as a private studio for musicians and operatic singers. The third floor has a recording studio, a 164-seater performance hall, and even a guest room for visiting artists. The Myeongju Art Park is open to everyone living in Gangneung. For local artists and citizens who had a hard time finding a place to rehearse, it is particularly good news. The trail from the Myeongju Art Park leading to Chilsadang is a mural road painted by local artist Im Man-hyuk. The murals depict a happy child playing with seagulls, chickens, and donkeys. Enjoy the murals of a happy family.

stories.title: Unification Park (Unification Exhibition Hall)
stories.script: 40.Unification Park (Unification Exhibition Hall)  * Man: We're now at the historic Anin Beach. This is the place where North Korean troops attempted to land here the Korean War broke out in 1950. It's also the place where a North Korean submarine infiltrated on September 18, 1996.  * Woman: Wow, it’s an unbelievable history for such a beautiful place!  * Man: Unification Park was established to express hopes and wishes for the peaceful reunification of the two Koreas and to instill a sense of security in the place where so much tragedy and pain were inflicted on the Korean people. It is a large exhibition park where you can see diverse pieces of military equipment of the land, sea, and air forces, as well as a North Korean submarine. * Woman: So you learn all about the national defense in one place?  * Man: Yes. Also, if you go into the Unification Security Exhibition Hall, you can see the history of national crises and how the Korean people overcame them. It also presents information on the provocations and infiltrations made by North Korea and their methods, such as digging underground tunnels, and the equipment found in the submarine they used. You can also find out all about the efforts that have been made to secure peace on the Korean peninsula. If you go outside you'll see tanks and armored vehicles, artillery, retired aircraft of the Republic of Korea Air Force, and an aircraft that was used to carry the President of Korea. * Woman: A presidential aircraft! * Man: Yes, it was used as a presidential aircraft from 1969 to 1973, and was retired from service as an air force plane in 1998. Since then it has been displayed in the Unification Park. You are allowed inside, so why not take a closer look!

stories.title: Unification Park (Warship Exhibit Hall)
stories.script: Unification Park (Warship Exhibition Hall)  * Man: Can you see the three ships displayed on the beach over there? The Warship Pavilion is an exhibition hall showing both South and North warships on the shore of Anin, where the North Korean submarine attempted to infiltrate the South and was stranded. * Woman: Is the name of the biggest ship “Jeonbukham? * Man: Jeonbukham was built in 1944 as a US Navy warship, and was later handed over to the Korean Navy. Up until 1992 the vessel conducted many operations during the Second World War, the Korean War, and even the Gulf War. After being retired in 1999, it was hauled onto land for the first time in Korea. * Woman: It has had an exciting career! * Man: I know! The one in the middle is a wooden boat taken by North Korean residents when they defected. * Woman: Did they really use a boat as small as this?  * Man: Yes, they really did. In 2009, eleven North Korean residents escaped from Seongjin, North Hamgyeong Province, on this wooden boat and defected to South Korea via the sea near Jumujin. And the submarine next to the wooden boat is the North Korean submarine that attempted to infiltrate the South before being stranded. * Woman: So what happened after that? * Man: The North Korean spies in the submarine infiltrated the Gangneung area, but they were swept up after a vigorous chase across the mountains of Gangneung and Pyeongchang. Don't forget that visitors are allowed inside all three vessels!

stories.title: Solhyang Arboretum
stories.script: Solhyang Arboretum  Do you know which tree is the most common tree in Korea? It's the pine tree. Gangneung is famous for having the most dense pine forests in the country and providing a habitat for its native Geumgang pine tree, an essential building material of Korea’s royal palaces. Located in a Geumgang pine forest, the Solhyang Arboretum contains 250,000 flowers, plants and trees belonging to more than 1,000 different species.  There are two ways to enjoy the arboretum. The first route, the Sky Garden Road, will lead you to an eco-road which displays a tunnel of snowbell trees, a forest trail lined with pacific yews and arborvitaes, and a sky garden overlooking downtown Gangneung and the ocean.   The second route, called the ‘greenhouse trail’, features a rest area surrounded by a stream and crape myrtles, a garden filled with of a variety of needle leaf trees, and a greenhouse containing temperate and subtropical plants and herbs. The Solhyang Arboretum also forms a uniquely different landscape with each change of the seasons. Enchanting snowbell trees in spring, fragrant daylilies and purple plantain lilies in summer, colorful foliage in autumn, and pine trees that are greener during winter will make your visit to the arboretum worthwhile at any time of year.

stories.title: Mojeong Stone Tower Road in Mt. Nochu
stories.audioTitle: 51. Mojeong Stone Tower Road in Mt. Nochu
stories.script: Mojeong Stone Tower Road in Mt. Nochu  Mojeong Tower Road is a mountain path where nearly 3,000 stone towers are lined up at the foot of Mt. Nochu. Surprisingly, a single person built them all. Cha Sun-ok, who built the stone towers, originally had four children, but two of her sons passed away and her husband suffered from a serious illness. Out of desperation, she started to build a stone tower in 1986 to pray for peace in the family, and finally completed it in 2011, the year she passed away. Many people were touched by this story and started to call this path Mojeong (meaning “maternal love”) Stone Tower Road. If you pass through the entrance to the Mojeong Stone Tower Road, you will see a stone monument called Gudojangwon-bi.” It is said that Yulgok Yi Yi, one of the most prominent scholars and politicians of the Joseon Dynasty, wrote a poem about the stone while he was studying in Mt. Nochu. Yi was called Gudojangwon-gong”, or the 'nine-time winner’, because he took first place in the state examination nine times until he became a government official. Rumor has it that numerous Confucian scholars of the Joseon Dynasty from across the nation visited the monument to make wishes for good fortune in their official career. Once lost and then found again, Gudojangwon-bi, though the form of the writing cannot be recognized, attracts a constant flow of parents who wish for nothing but their children's success and wellbeing.

stories.title: Daehangnu
stories.script: Daehangnu  A small hill from which all of Mokpo can be seen  Daehangnu is the first of the five pavilions of the “Nojeokbong Course” leading up to Ildeungbong Peak, which is the head of Yudalsan. It is a small hill with an elevation of 76m that serves like an observatory. The name means “a pavilion waiting for a crane,” and is related to the〈Samhakdo Birth Tale〉. Since we are very short on time, let me skip the tale and instead guide you through a couple of vista points. First, could you please turn around to look behind you? We are standing towards the northern part of the mountain, the original city center of Mokpo. The original city center of Mokpo is a traditional village where natives have led their lives for three to four generations, and it is intertwined with maze-like alleys. And, to promote this place, the “Alley Tour Course” was set up since 2014. From the left, you see Aphaedo Island, Aphaedaegyo Bridge, Mokpo Station, Hadang New Town over the mountain, Nojeokbong Peak and New Millennium Citizens Belfry. Now, could you look towards Nampyeon, the south side? Haha, did you look at your Nampyeon, the husband, who came with you? From now on, I’ll call the north “Bukchon” and the south of this mountain “Namchon” so that you don’t get confused. In fact, these are the names generally called by our ancestors during the Japanese occupation period. Please look near the left side below the mountain. You can see a red brick building, which is the old Japanese consulate built in 1900. Besides this, there are many other modern-style buildings left in Mokpo. What do you think came to our ancestors’ minds as they witnessed more and more contemporary structures increasing in numbers on flat lands while they themselves lived in the mountains in thatched houses? Now, if you slightly shift your view to the right and look behind the church at your 10 o'clock, a flag is seen flapping about. It is a low rocky hill called Mokpojin Fort, which was installed in the 21st year of King Sejong’s reign in 1439 and is the beginning of Mokpo's history. Today, the fort no longer has the original appearance and only one lodging structure is restored. Nevertheless, it is No. 6 out of Mokpo 9 Views so make sure to stop by. Oh! And Yudalsan is also famous for beautifully blooming forsythia. When spring comes, the entire mountain and both sides of the way up as well as the surroundings of the pavilion are all colored in yellow. How is your season with mulberries? If you visited during another season, be sure to visit again for the spring. Besides this, there are many more stories still to be told about Mokpo. During your relaxing trip to Mokpo, I hope you have a chance to listen to a variety of Mokpo stories other than the one about mulberries!

stories.title: National Maritime Cultural Heritage Museum
stories.script: National Maritime Cultural Heritage Museum  Place filled with treasures of Shinan Ship  National Maritime Museum and National Maritime Cultural Heritage Museum are located in Gatbawi Culture Town of the port city of Mokpo. It is a marine history museum that promotes our ancestors’ footsteps and cultural heritage based on the themes of the sea, people, culture and history, where you can feel and experience the history and culture of the ocean. The National Maritime Museum began with an investigation into the seabed ruins of “Jeungdo,” a small island of Sinan-gun, Jeollanam-do, in 1975. After a fisherman netted six pieces of celadons from the sea in front of Dodeokdo Island, Sinan-gun, a total of 11 excavations for relics took place between 1976 and 1984, and a countless number of treasures were unearthed and revealed to the world. And the National Maritime Cultural Heritage Museum, the first-ever marine history museum in Korea, was established to exhibit these relics. The ship excavated at that time is called the “Sinan Ship” following the name of the area in which it was found. In 1323, the Sinan ship was heading from Qingyuan, China to Kyoto via Hakata, Japan when it was wrecked in the sea in front of the Sinan, Korea. The relics discovered in the Sinan ship were about 24,000 pieces of celadons and white porcelain, 28 tons of coins, rosewoods, and various spices. These relics are mainly exhibited at the National Maritime Museum, Gwangju National Museum and National Museum of Korea but the Sinan Ship is on display only in the National Maritime Cultural Heritage Museum in Mokpo where celadons, white porcelain and many other relics that were excavated in the Sinan Ship are also exhibited. Outside the exhibition hall, you can enjoy the seascape and watch traditional boats and, at the souvenir shop, you can purchase art brochures and antique souvenirs that show the history and relics of excavations in Korea. The permanent exhibition hall consists of four exhibition rooms, including the marine exchange room and Sinan Ship room on the 1st floor, the world ship history room and the Korean ship history room on the 2nd floor, and there is the central hall where you can enjoy a view of the sea as well as the children’s experience center and the planned exhibition room on the underground level. In particular, the underground central hall is a great place to make beautiful memories with simple drinks bought on the first floor and the sea in the background. The Sinan Ship room on the 1st floor, which is the main area of the National Maritime Cultural Heritage Museum, displays numerous celadons and white porcelains from the Sinan Ship from the Song and Yuan Dynasties. Since it is a beneficial education site where you may compare the histories of pottery among Korea, China, and Japan of Northeast Asia, we recommend those who are interested in the Korean maritime excavation history to make sure to stop by.

stories.title: Seosan-dong Sihwa Alley
stories.script: An alley of poetry and paintings  Sihwa Alley literally means an alley of a village with Si, or poetry, and Hwa, or paintings. Sihwa Village was originally called Seosan-dong, which was a well-known fishing village located at the foot of Yudalsan, Mokpo.It is a small hillside village with petite houses tightly lined up on every street. It was mostly inhabited by fishermen and, until recently, only the elderly lived here without any young people. But, as the Sihwa Village Project proceeded in this waning hillside town, it was reborn as an amiable and gorgeous village. Sihwa Village began its revival as a part of the “humanities city project,” which had been carried out by the city of Mokpo since 2015 in collaboration with various urban regions, universities and organizations. For three years from 2015 to 2017, 43 poems and 67 paintings by authors and painters in addition to 28 poems written by the residents were expressed in woodblocks and murals and exhibited on streets of Seosan-dong at the foot of Yudalsan. Over the course of the Sihwa Village Project, the streets once colored in dark gray were now wearing bright, splendid colors, giving the village a beautiful look. An interesting aspect of the Sihwa Village Project was that people of the village actively participated in decorating their hometown along with professional artists, poets and painters and, on the walls of each house, the story of the owner of the house is clearly expressed in words and images, which help us understand their joys and sorrows of life and the worlds of their inner children. Let me introduce to you a poem titled 〈My Life〉.  “Born in Jindo but married to a man in Hauido across the waters. I don't like my husband on the first night of our marriage so how should I live on…? He only loved me, though, but passed away at the age of 48 with a daughter left behind My life has passed with various chores while wearing a briquette A-frame on my back”  What do you think? Did you get the image of a tough life lived by a hard-working woman?  Recently, an artists' village called “Borimadang”has been established here in Sihwa Alley. Located at the uppermost part of Seosan-dong, Borimadang, or barley yard in Korean, this is a place where people literally used to dust off and dry barley. Since then, small and pretty art spaces have found their homes in empty houses located in the area that connects Sihwa Alley and Borimadang and, as artists have performed works of art, a newfound energy has filled up the village. “Yeonhee's Supermarket”also contributed significantly to the popularity of Sihwa Alley. This old supermarket building in Seosan-dong was utilized as a filming site for 〈1987〉, a movie about the June Democracy Uprising, and the city of Mokpo continued to preserve the movie set even after the filming finished in order to actively use it as a tourism resource. 〈1987〉was a massive hit in the theaters, bringing in over 7 million in cinema audiences, and, after it was known that Yeonhee's Supermarket, which served an extremely important role in the movie where main characters met, is located in Mokpo, the number of people visiting Sihwa Village increased rapidly. On the interior of the supermarket, there is also a large-sized air-raid shelter that was built during the Japanese occupation era. It is open for anyone to freely explore. As the historical site hidden inside a private home was utilized as a tour resource, the mystique and charm of the area started to shine brighter. Near the supermarket, you can also find Yeonhee's Music Cafe, old costume experience, Yeonhee's Stationery and many other things to see from which you may feel nostalgia of the good old days.

stories.title: Kim Woo-jin Street
stories.script: Kim Woo-jin Street  Together, let’s feel the traces of Kim Woo-jin, an ill-fated genius who lived a fiery life in the 1920s in Mokpo, a city of culture and art where beauty and romance form perfect harmony. This five-way street was not called a Ogeori as most five-way streets are known as; instead, people used the name Buljongdae because, in front of the Credit Union, there used to be a watchtower where people struck the bell to inform everyone whenever a fire broke out in the part of the town primarily inhabited by Joseon people. Hwashin Pharmacy across the street was where the movie, The Classic, was filmed and, next to it, an ice cream shop named Jongildang is located. A few decades ago, when the hot and humid weather began, children would walk around the streets and carry a bucket of ice creams, shouting, “Sweet and cold ice cream.” Baeknyeon Hanok on the right is a guesthouse that restored an old hanok as a part of the urban regeneration project, and Oraetteul Guesthouse is said to be where the manager of Kim Woo-jin’s house used to live. Everyone, do you see the shape of a woman in the hole at the bottom of the gate? This is said to be a painting created to let everyone know, in a funny way, that it is a female-only guesthouse. The wall of Oraetteul also shows some of the most notable plays by Kim Woo-jin and, in front of the small library, his annual reports and works are presented in a photo zone to welcome all visitors. Let’s now move to Bukgyo-dong Cathedral. This is the birthplace of Kim Woo-jin that becomes filled with the fragrance of Osmanthus asiaticus every spring. If you go inside, you can see a small stone sign that says, “Shrine of Kim Woo-jin's literature.” Do you think you can feel his breath here? At the time, it was a large mansion with high walls so people who passed by it often peeped into the house out of curiosity by stepping on the back of someone. It is said that Kim wrote poems, critiques, plays, and essays in the two-story building called Baeksujae, and also gathered fellow study-abroad students to hold parties and concerts with his beloved Yun Sim-deok. The main characters of the drama 〈The Hymn of Death〉 are Kim Woo-jin and Yun Sim-deok. After your trip to Mokpo, how about watching The Hymn of Death to reminisce your time on this street again?

stories.title: Okdani-gil
stories.script: 1. Okdani-gil  Who do you think is Okdan from Okdani-gil? One of the works of Cha Bum-seok, a playwright, is ≪Okdani≫, which is based on a real-life character. It is about the life and culture of our ancestors through the story of a woman named Okdan carrying around water buckets to sell.  From Mokpo Station, Okdani-gil leads to Jeonggwang Jeonghyewon, Nojeokbong and Moktmartre. For your information, it is not Montmartre of France but Moktmartre by using the word, Mok from Mokpo. Now, let’s begin with the story of Melakong Bridge near Mokpo Station. Melakong is the nickname of Park Gil-su who passed away at the age of 67 after 48 years of carrying luggage at Mokpo Station. He was a handicapped person who had difficulties controlling his arms and legs and also had a warped mouth, which made it tough for people to understand what he was saying. He helped his parents who were running a street stand in front of the station and cleaned the inside of the station while sleeping in the waiting room at night. And that is when he got the nickname, “Melakong” for his supposed resemblance as a disabled person to a movie character named Melakong. He was employed at the freight office in Mokpo Station thanks to his diligent and always-smiling attitude, and helped tens of thousands of healthy people with his handicapped body. When many people complained the nonexistence of a bridge over a stream next to Mokpo Station, Melakong obtained rebars and cement on his own and combined donations with his own funds to complete the construction of “Melakong Bridge” in 1964. He also opened “Melakong freight storage”, “Melakong free inn”, etc. to help a countless number of people. He was penniless and disabled but, by carrying out one good deed every year, he showed how a person should live a life. He was a proud citizen of Mokpo. Today, the stream is covered so “Melakong Bridge” has long been gone without any trace but it is still remembered by Mokpo locals as the most beautiful and heartwarming bridge.  The second place is Jeonggwang Jeonghyewon where the Venerable Beopjeong and Ko Un met with each other. As you pass through Anjeoja Street from Mokpo Station and walk up a little bit, you will find Jeonggwang Jeonghyewon on the right side that has an appearance of a Japanese temple, which was built by a Japanese man named Dohyeon Hwasang in 1917 under the name of Heungseonsa. Though it is a small temple of Mokpo, Jeonggwang Jeonghyewon is a romantic place where the Venerable Beopjeong who was greatly respected by many Koreans through his book, 〈Musoyu〉 and Ko Un, a famous poet both in Korea and worldwide, met with each other. After the Korean War, Ko who was a monk at the time came to Jeonghyewon in Mokpo to evangelize and, here, he met a university student named Park Jae-cheol whom he helped to turn to Buddhism. Later on, Ko also made arrangements for Park to write an essay and publish it on Hyundae Munhak. Park Jae-cheol is none other than the Venerable Beopjeong. At the time, Beopjeong had taken a leave of absence from school and was serving as the student manager of Buddhism at Jeonghyewon.  The third place is Nojeokbong Peak, which tells a tale of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, as well as Moktmartre. Nojeokbong, which had witnessed the clever tactics of Admiral Yi Sun-sin during the Japanese invasion, refers to the large stone peak in Yudalsan, Mokpo. It is a peak that was famously utilized by Chungmugong to defeat the invading enemies, and also where a highly advanced psychological warfare using the topography took place.   To overcome military inferiority during the invasion, he commanded to tie straw thatches together to cover rocks, making them look like large piles of Nojeok, or stacked grains of military provisions, which helped defeat the Japanese raiders without shedding any blood thanks to the wisdom of camouflage tactics. In that regard, Nojeokbong is a historical site of patriotism. These days, if you stand by Noinam Rock next to the stairs in front of Chungmugong Yi statue in Yudalsan and look towards Nojeokbong, it looks as if the face of a person points to the sky. Perhaps, it is Admiral Yi Sun-sin appearing before us. Now, enjoy the roads of Mokpo!  This script has been written by on the writing of “Choi Hee-ja”, a cultural tourism commentator of Mokpo.

stories.title: Mokpo Cultural Center
stories.script: 11. Mokpo Cultural Center  Let’s learn about the historical and architectural origin of today's Mokpo Cultural Center, which was the old Honam Bank Mokpo Branch building, shall we? Honam Bank Mokpo Branch was established by Honam locals who fought against the Japanese capital for the industrial growth of Mokpo. It is located in Ogeori, or the five-way intersection, which is the center of Mokpo’s commercial district, and it is a two-story rectangular building made of bricks and attached with red tiles on the surfaces to add a dose of stylishness. The red outer wall tiles were luxury goods imported from Russia, and each tile was wrapped separately with paper. What’s unique about this building is that it was constructed without any columns in the center of the building. Reinforced concrete and concrete slab buildings like modern structures would be possible but the architecture technology of the time that did not use any columns in the center of a building is truly admirable. There is also a theory that, over the years, the building has experienced fewer distortions than the old Japanese consulate. Today, the building still maintains the interior and exterior appearances from the time of construction without any discoloration, damage, loss or cracks on exterior tiles and bricks, which is why it is one of the greatest contemporary structures. Let me give you an example of that durability and solidity. During the Korean War, a North Korean armored vehicle crashed into this building but it was undamaged. Instead, it destroyed the armored vehicle. Also, the outer walls received a hail of gunfire but the tile bricks were only scratched on the surface without being damaged, telling us the painful history.  Honam Bank, which was established in the Japanese occupation era to develop the capital of our people, extended its scope of business even to the Gyeongnam region and operated independently against the colonial financial policies but it eventually suffered a misfortune of being forcibly merged by Dongil Bank on May 1, 1942 by the policy of the Japanese Government-General, which demanded integration of Korean banks. Afterwards, it was later renamed the Chohung Bank by a merger on October 1, 1943, and, when Chohung Bank merged with Shinhan Bank, it began to be used as Shinhan Bank’s Mokpo branch. Today, its function as a bank has died out and, instead, it is used as the Mokpo Cultural Center for the growth of local culture in the city. Mokpo, which grew into an industrial city after the opening of its port in 1897, had many modern financial structures. However, Honam Bank Mokpo Branch is the only building that still stands today and is a modern cultural property of a high value in that it was a bank founded and operated by Koreans.  This script has been written by on the writing of “Jo Dae-hyung”, a cultural tourism commentator of Mokpo.

stories.title: Mokpojin Fort
stories.script: 10. Mokpojin Fort  Beginning of the history of Mokpo  Mokpojin Fort, which was also known as Mokpoyeong or Mokpodae, was a military camp for the Joseon naval forces, and, since Manho, or ten thousand houses, were established here, it was also called Manhoyeong, Manhojin or Manhocheong. Geographically, Mokpo holds the mouth of the Yeongsangang River and is located in the hub connected to the sea. Moreover, it is seated on the path used as a tax grain transport route leading to Honam and southern Gyeongsang regions. For that reason, Mokpo gained attention as its importance was highlighted since the early Joseon Dynasty. The installation of Mokpojin was first permitted in the 21st year of King Sejong’s reign, and it is said that it came to have the appearance of a fortress by the 8th year of Yeonsangun's reign. Since then, Mokpojin served as a defense area of the southwestern sea of the Korean Peninsula but was eventually abolished by King Gojong’s Edict No. 141 on July 15 in the 32nd year of his reign. At the time of the opening of the port immediately after the abolition, a part of the building was left to be used as Muan Gamniseo, Japanese consulate or British Naval Base but it became too damaged later on and only the historical monument of Mokpojin remained. Then, it was partially restored to the present-day appearance in 2014. Thus, Mokpojin Fort finally transformed into a history park after about 120 years.  If you follow the uphill road in front of Holiness Church seated on the hill near Chowon Hotel, you will find the historical monument of Mokpojin, which is the first attraction you need to visit during your Mokpo exploration. The name, Manho, still exists but the ramparts are nowhere to be seen now, and only the stone monument, which has been weathered and cut away by the harsh times, quietly preserves its place. Today, Mokpo Manhobi and the walls and shafts of a handful of houses in Manho-dong show traces of Manhojin Fort. The exact date of the establishment of Manhojin Fort was April 15 in the 21st year of King Sejong's reign and, since Mokpo was a “fortress” against the Japanese invasion, the Uijeongbu recommended to dispatch ten thousand houses to the region and station military vessels. These proposals eventually obtained Sejong’s approval. This is the historic starting point of Manhojin Fort of Mokpo.  Now, enjoy the 6th View of Mokpo 9 Views that is Mokpojin Fort!  This script has been written by on the writing of “Choi Hee-ja”, a cultural tourism commentator of Mokpo.

stories.title: Mokpo Ceramic Livingware Museum
stories.script: Mokpo Ceramic Livingware Museum  Do you know of the Mokpo Ceramic Livingware Museum that leads the everyday handicraft culture? Since ancient times, Mokpo has been a place located at the end of the Noryeong Mountains with the beauty and scenery of Namdo that was home to a countless number of kiln sites based on quality kaolin and abundant firewood. Yeongam next to Mokpo is a region that produced Siyudogi, the first glazed type of pottery in Korea, during the period of Unified Silla. Also, thanks to the maritime trading activities of Jang Bogo in the late Unified Silla Dynasty, Gangjin began producing Korea’s first celadons boasting great reputation and quality as the soil, water quality, fuel, climate and other conditions for ceramics were excellent in the area of Yongun-ri, Daegu-myeon, Gangjin. Also, Muan is rich in iron and red soil, eventually becoming a leading production site for Buncheong ware since the Joseon Dynasty. In 1942, Korea’s first national capital-based Haengnam Jagi was founded in Mokpo that aimed at continuing the tradition of Korean ceramics. After the construction of a modern ceramic livingware factory, mass production became possible. Now, let’s take a look through the Mokpo Ceramic Livingware Museum.  The exhibition hall offers a view of the beautiful mountains and sea of Mokpo and, at the same time, there is also a space where you can enjoy both Korean and international pottery works including those of Lladró. Moreover, in the children's experience room, you can have various and simple pottery experiences such as cutting and pasting colored paper on mugs, plates and ramen bowls as well as attaching pattern stickers. Ah! There is also a pottery education program for adults, not children, so be sure to make your own pottery! The kitchen, which is decorated according to different eras, is also very interesting. You may experience an old kitchen from the 1920s where people put a sot on the wood-burning stove and set fire to the firewood to cook food and heat up a room. Then, you can check out the more convenient kitchen of the 1970s. In the 70s, multi-unit dwellings such as apartments were constructed where residents used briquettes instead of wood-burning stoves for cooking and heating, and the location of sinks and kitchen counters was heightened to make it easier for housewives to work in the kitchen. That is when nickel silver and stainless utensils began to be used a lot. What do you think? Don’t you think there are more diverse hidden stories than you imagined in the museum that you thought would only be full of ceramic stories? Now, shall we enjoy the museum?

stories.title: Mokpo Children's Sea Science Museum
stories.script: Mokpo Children's Sea Science Museum  Mokpo Children’s Sea Science Museum opened on February 5, 2013 with the goal to provide hands-on education on marine science to children, thus promoting scientific thinking and fostering future leaders of the 21st-century marine age. As the only sea science museum for children in the country, it features five major exhibition spaces under the theme of “sea”. Now, shall we start our tour on the first floor?  〈VR Sea Imagination Hall〉, simply speaking, is a digital sea. The submarine at the entrance produces lighting effects and sounds of machinery and its submergence, thus offering children a chance to feel as if they are diving deep into the waters. This is to stimulate their infinite imagination regarding the sea. Once you enter the hall after passing by the submarine, you can feel the free life of the sea creatures, microorganisms, and those that live deep in the sea near Mokpo.   VR Underwater Scooters spark the imagination and excitement through undersea exploration, jellyfish-hunting, shipwreck shark-hunting and treasure hunts. The VR Undersea Exploration Riders piques children’s curiosity of the sea with scenes that make them feel as if they were actually in a submarine and roaming through the sea. Also, a variety of activities can be experienced such as underwater life rescue, boss war, riders and rank system.  〈Deep Sea Exhibition〉is a space where you can understand underwater topography below 1,000m deep, living organisms around hydrothermal vents, exploration of underwater minerals, deep-sea submarine activities, and water pressure and depth. You may also watch them with your eyes and touch them with your hands. It enables you to control unmanned exploration ships and robotic arms for a virtual experience of collecting unlimited undersea resources in the Korean sea. Also, through the three deep-sea submarines to be used in scanning the mysteries of the deep sea, it helps you to experience how deep a person can dive and how high the water pressure and low the water temperature gets as you dive deeper. 〈Sea Eye Dome〉is a place where children can touch, see and feel the mud flat.  Moving onto the second floor, 〈Midsea Exhibition〉is a disphotic zone of the sea where light is dimly coming in between 200 and 1,000m under water. The reason why it is called a disphotic zone is that there are squids, jellyfish, etc. that use little amounts of light to camouflage. The Midsea Exhibition explains the kinds and living conditions of marine algae and offers a chance for children to experience puzzles involving the fish, scenes in which skate and tuna swim, and hunting of comb jellyfish, which catches food by shooting nets.  〈Shallow Sea Exhibition〉 is a photic zone about 200m below the surface of the sea to which light comes in. You can experience the sea environment and understand the infinite sea energy such as low and high tides and the causes of their creation, the power of waves, ebb and flow of the tide, and the principle of electricity generated when high waves occur. And you may also get on the model of the yacht, even moving the anchor yourselves to discharge the wind and feel the pressure; or you can experience the virtual Dadohaehaesang National Park on the wig ship model, which will be the high-tech water transportation in the future.  In the 〈4D Theater〉, you can join in on the adventure of the representative fish species in the Mokpo sea, including the yellow Corvina, red sea-bream and mottled skate, to travel off to the distant waters to save their friends in crisis in the deep sea. Why don’t you experience the diverse sea ecosystem here and learn how precious friendship and courage are? Now, take your time and enjoy the Sea Science Museum!

stories.title: Mokpo Skywalk
stories.script: Mokpo Skywalk  In Daeban-dong, one of Mokpo’s representative tourist attractions and a great place to visit with family, friends or lovers, there is a skywalk where you can walk on top of the sea. Located on the west of Yudalsan Mountain, Daeban-dong is also known as Daeman-dong. In the port city of Mokpo, there are many beautiful marine facilities such as the Mokpodaegyo Bridge and Marine Cable Car but, before the skywalk was established, there was actually no suitable place to enjoy this beautiful view at a glance. But, thanks to the creation of the Skywalk in July 2020, we don't need to worry about that anymore! The Skywalk is 54m long and 15m above the sea, and more than two-thirds of the floor is made of safe transparent reinforced glass and steel platforms. There is also an observation deck made of nets throughout the bridge so that you can experience the thrill of walking up high in the sky and above the sea at the same time. From the Skywalk, you can see the golden sunset of Dadohae, Mokpodaegyo Bridge, and the longest marine cable car in Korea that goes across Yudalsan and the West Sea. In particular, the cable car at night with its colorful lights will leave you breathless. Yudal Amusement Park under the Skywalk is a place where you can take a walk along the beach; it used to be a summer vacation spot for the Joseon people of Mokpo. There are many popular cafes nearby as well so it would be nice to enjoy a cup of coffee, right? Also, Daeban-dong has a lot of grilled clam carts near the Skywalk so you can enjoy a delicious dinner and a wonderful view at the same time. After sunset, a panorama of lights unfolds before you in Daeban-dong and the Skywalk. So this is where a great number people gather all the time. I hope you all have fun, too!

stories.title: Mokpo Marine Cable Car
stories.script: Mokpo Marine Cable Car  Enjoy a romantic Mokpo aboard the marine cable car  Mokpo Marine Cable Car, the longest cable car in Korea, was opened in September 2019. Thanks to a wide entrance doorway, even wheelchairs and strollers can conveniently get on and off the cable car, and travelers are able to enjoy the scenery of Mokpo from a spacious and pleasant cabin.  Get on the cable car at the Bukhang platform, pass the Yudalsan rocks boasting fantastic shapes, and get off at the Yudalsan platform, just a stop over. And get on the cable car again and proceed to the Gohado platform. This entire journey takes about 40 minutes for a round trip. The greatest appeal of the Mokpo Marine Cable Car is that it curves in an “L” shape at the top of Yudalsan before passing over the sea in front of Mokpo and crossing all the way until Gohado. Moreover, the fifth tower is the second tallest in the world at 155m high, which makes your eyes close at the extreme dizziness.  If you look at a ship entering Mokpo Port after turning around Gohado Yongmeori, it draws a white arc. Even Namnong Heo Geon, a master of Korean painting, called it “Yongdang Guibeom” and left a beautiful painting of it. If Norwegian painter, Munch, decided to paint the Mokpo Marine Cable Car during a sunset, it would be you screaming amongst the red-colored Dadohae scenery. Also, Mokpo's nightscape seen from the sky is not as fancy as a big city's but warms your heart nonetheless with subtle lights. Now, enjoy the Marine Cable Car in romantic Mokpo, one of Korea’s four major tourist hub cities!

stories.title: Yudal Amusement Park
stories.script: Yudal Amusement Park  If you follow the road around Yudalsan, you will get to Daeban-dong, which is also known as Yudal Amusement Park. Located between Mokpo National Maritime University and Shinan Beach Hotel, Yudal Amusement Park was opened as Yudal Beach in 1962 and became a tourist attraction. But, as sand continued to be swept away and the water became deeper, it lost its functions as a beach. Eventually, it was closed in June 2005 and has become the Yudal Amusement Park that we have today. And, now, there are several cafes in the park that are great photo spots. When you sit on the terrace with the sea view, you can take beautiful pictures with Mokpodaegyo Bridge and the Marine Cable Car in the background so these cafes are always crowded with customers. How about taking a beautiful picture with a cup of coffee? Mokpodaegyo Bridge, which is seen from the amusement park, opened in 2012 and connects Bukhang and Gohado of Mokpo. The length including an access road is about 4km, which is quite long. The shape of the tower and cable embodies the image of two cranes, the city bird of Mokpo, flying up in the sea. Does it look like that to you? Also, the amusement park is a great place to take a walk and enjoy the night view. Why don’t you enjoy a quiet and peaceful atmosphere here at Yudal Amusement Park and enjoy a cup of coffee or take a short stroll?

stories.title: Oedaldo and Dalido Islands – Oedaldo
stories.script: Oedaldo and Dalido Islands – Oedaldo  An island of love and lovers  Located in the sea about 6㎞ from the city of Mokpo, the beautiful island of Oedaldo faces Dalido to the east. It is said that the island, which is located on the west of Dalido and also solitarily detached from others, was named “Bakdariseom” in pure Korean, which means it is located on the outside of Dalido, or “Oedaldo,” which means a lonely poor hillside village. Today, it is a very small and beautiful island with fewer than 80 inhabitants from about 20 households. The coastline is monotonous and the northwestern part of the island has farmland so that people can cultivate crops but, unlike other islands, it is difficult to fish because of the fast tide currents in the adjacent sea. Therefore, marine products like stone laver, green algae, seaweed and oysters are collected by the coast while seaweed and abalones are the main products that are being cultured. Most Oedaldo residents carry out small-scale laver farming for a living but it had been quite difficult due to poor conditions and infrastructure. As a response, the city of Mokpo developed the theme of ecotourism across the entire island and opened two beaches in the village as part of an ecotourism course.
