It is called Buchunjeong Pavilion and Garden because of its beautiful landscape of Tamjingang River and surrounding forest  Buchunjeong Pavilion was originally named Cheongyeongjeong Pavilion. Mun Hui-gae built the pavilion during the Joseon period and named it after his penname, Cheongyeong. Mun Hui-gae helped his father organize the Righteous Army during Imjinwaeran, the Japanese Invasion of Korea in 1592, and fought together with his sons during Jeongyujaeran, the Second Japanese Invasion of Korea in 1597. His loyalty to the nation was ceaseless even after he resigned from the government post, so he went up the pavilion every day and bowed to the north, the direction where the king resided.  His grandson who witnessed his act built Manggundaebi Monument at the site to cherish his grandfather’s loyalty, and the writer Baek Gwan-hun engraved the word “Yongho” on a rock at the riverside under the pavilion. Baek Gwan-hun is also one of  eight famous writers of Gisan Village.  Later on, Kim Gi-seong, a member of the Cheongpung Kim Clan, bought Cheongyeong Pavilion, renovated it to its current state and changed its name to Buchunjeong Pavilion. Take the short walk to experience the spectacular views of the green forest surrounding the pavilion and imagine how the loyal subjects felt in this same space long ago.

stories.title: Sainjeong Pavilion
stories.script: Single-minded devotion to King Danjong  There were many loyal scholars in Jangheung-gun, Jeollanam-do. One of them is Kim Pil who was a vice minister to King Danjong in the Joseon Dynasty. When the Grand Prince Suyang staged Gyeyu Jeongnan Coup and came into power, Kim Pil went back to Jangheung-gun, his hometown. Afterwards, he built a pavilion, taught students and interacted with other loyal subjects of Danjong. It is said that Kim Si-seup, who was one of the Six Living Ministers, stayed here for more than 10 years.  Sainjeong Pavilion has typical topography of facing water with the mountains at the back. The scenery is stunning around the pavilion, with lush trees at the back and Tamjingang River flowing in front. In particular, the appearance of a wooden house with straight columns that become wider toward the end on a rectangle and a hipped and gable roof is in harmony with the surroundings. Later, Kim Gu visited here on the way to Shanghai while the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea was seeking asylum and wrote “Jeil Gangsan,” meaning best scenery, on a rock. Currently those letters are engraved on the rock.  Kim Pil stood here facing north and missed King Danjong. He used to draw King Danjong’s face on a snow-covered rock face when winter came. The memorial stone of Kim Pil who ended his remaining years in Sainjeong Pavilion is located down the mountain at the entrance to the stone stairway to Sainjeong Pavilion. Sainjeong Pavilion was named after “Sain,” his first government post in State Council by his descendants after his death.

stories.title: Jeongnamjin Water Science Museum
stories.script: Science of mysterious water to learn with five senses  Jeongnamjin Water Science Museum located on the riverside of Tamjingang River with its beautifully colored water is where you can experience the mysterious world of water. The science of how one drop of water can move the Earth can be discovered through various exhibitions. Visitors of all ages are welcome to enjoy the world of water science.  At the entrance on the 1st floor, a water tank filled with colorful tropical fish catches the eyes. Buy some tropical fish food and feed the hungry swimmers. There is also Doctor Fish Experience, which is promoted as effective for skin diseases. Making a Mini Aquatic Plant Fish Tank is a very popular activity among children.  The Water Science Experience Center on the 2nd floor is where children can learn Archimedes' principle and the principles of the waterwheel, Jagyeongnu, water clock from the Joseon period, and a dam, while operating scientific instruments by themselves. On one side, there is a 4D video gallery where children can experience an underwater world while travelling together with water. Science learning with the five senses continues on the 3rd floor. In the Water Circulation Experience Center, children can look at the circulation of water through various devices and there are instruments to add to the children’s experience. After the viewing, don’t forget to check out the view of Tamjingang River from the floor-to-ceiling window on the 3rd floor.

stories.title: Jangheung Dam Water Museum
stories.script: Science of water, history of the Jangheung Dam  The Jangheung Dam Water Museum is an exhibition hall and observatory created at the top of Jangheung dam. It is created as a part of environment-friendly water resource development by K-water as they construct the Jangheung dam. The Jangheung Dam Water Museum and nearby eco park boost great scenery. The water museum has a unique appearance of a small two-story building combined with a cylinder-shaped glass observatory. The view of the Jangheung Dam and Tamjinho Lake from the observatory inside the water museum is picturesque.  The Jangheung Dam Water Museum introduces the history and role of the Jangheung Dam that prevents flood damage in the Tamjingang River downstream and provides water for living to nine cities and counties in Jeollanam-do. The History and Culture Room on the 1st floor displays the pictures and artifacts of the area that were submerged when constructing the Jangheung Dam. The records of people in submerged areas who had no choice but to leave their hometown leaves a lingering impression. Hearing the voices of people in submerged areas while looking at old photos showing the history of the town is emotional.  The waterium on the 2nd floor entertainingly explains the circulation of water in the Earth and the development of civilization with water. You can learn about the principle of waterpower generation from a displayed diorama, and learn about the role of a multi-purpose dam, such as flood control, water supply and waterpower generation, from the model of the Jangheung Dam. There is no better place than the Jangheung Dam Water Museum for a family outing to experience the importance of water with children. Admission is free, but remember that it is closed on Mondays.

stories.title: Borimsa Temple
stories.script: Thousand-year-old temple filled with the aroma of tea   Borimsa Temple located at the foot of Gajisan Mountain in Jangheung-gun, Jeollanam-do is called “Three Borims” together with Borimsa Temples in India and China. It is where the Zen sect of Buddhism from China in the late Unified Silla period first settled in Korea. At that time there were Zen sect temples on 9 mountains around the nation that were called “Nine Mountain Zen Sect Temples.” Borimsa Temple can be considered the best among the Nine Sights of Jangheung-gun because of its long history and stunning scenery.   When you enter Borimsa Temple, gracing this site for one thousand years, you will see Iljumun Gate with “Borimsa Temple of Gajisan Mountain“ written and Sacheonmun Gate and then Daejeokgwangjeon Hall where Vairocana Buddha is worshipped as the main Buddha. Here you can see National Treasure No. 117 “Iron Seated Vairocana Buddha of Borimsa Temple, Jangheung-gun.” In front of Daejeokgwangjeon Hall, there stands National Treasure No. 44, South and North Three-story Stone Pagodas and Stone Lantern of Borimsa Temple, Jangheung-gun. The Stone Lantern contains the meaning that the Buddha’s light illuminates everywhere. Borimsa Temple is also full of national and local treasures, such as the East Stupa and West Stupa that show the history of Buddhist art.  Borimsa Temple is also the home of Cheongtaejeon Tea, traditional fermented tea of Korea. Cheongtaejeon in a token shape is still made with wild tea leaves every year. At the back of the temple, evergreen Japanese torreya forest as well as wild tea plants present a magnificent sight. Walk on the “Cheongtaejeon Tea Road” to experience the sensory pleasures of the forest trail and your mental stress will rapidly fade away.

stories.title: Jeongnamjin Observatory
stories.script: Observatory stood due south from Seoul  If you draw a straight line from Seoul due south, you will find Jeongnamjin Observatory, in Usando Island Tourist District, the representative marine tourist area in the southern coast. The observatory is comprised of an observation tower, Unification Plaza and “Yulryeo – the Beginning of Harmony,” a circular sculpture that symbolizes Jeongnamjin. Yulryeo refers to the tune of music or voice, but it also means the sound of the beginning of the world, so the art work can be interpreted that the sound of heaven and the sound of earth meet and harmonize. In Unification Plaza, there is a circular fountain that shoots out cool water in summer.  The observation tower, the trademark of Jeongnamjin Observatory, contains the imagery of the sun, yellow hemp sailboat, and waves. Each floor, including an observatory on the 10th floor, is decorated with its own theme. When you go up to the observatory on the 10th floor, you will see islands, which were jewels of the southern sea, including Sorokdo Island, Wando Island and Geumildo Island, as well as Samsan Embankment and Deungnyangman Bay.  The 7th floor of the observation tower is a literature-based movie theater showing Seopyeonje and Festival that are movies based on the works of Yi Chong-jun, the writer who represents Jangheung-gun. Story Hall on the 4th floor where tales and legends passed down about Jangheung-gun are introduced in animation is also interesting. You can find information about local specialties of Jangheung-gun at the Food Promotion Hall on the 3rd floor and information about various festivals held in Jangheung-gun at the Festival Hall on the 5th floor. Have the best photos of your whole life taken to remember the trip to Jangheung-gun in the Trick-art Photo Zone on the 2nd floor, and get travel information at the Travel Information Center introducing must-visit places in Jangheung-gun on the 1st floor.

stories.title: Sodeungseom Island
stories.script: Hot spot to see sunrise that comes with a legend  Do you know about Sodeungseom Island in Jangheung-gun? It is a very little uninhabited land but it is greatly famous for its breathtaking sunrises behind the island, making it one of the Nine Sights of Jangheung-gun. The name Sodeungseom Island originated from a long-ago story passed down for generations that the people in Nampo Village lit Sodeung, meaning “lantern,” on the island to pray for their families’ safe return from fishing.  You can witness Korea’s “Moses' Miracle” twice a day on the coastal waters of Sodeungseom Island. When the sea parts at low tide, it will take about 5 minutes to walk along the sea route from Nampo Village to Sodeungseom Island. In this tiny island, there is a statue of Grandma Dang, who is the guardian of the town, praying hard with two hands together. There is an old legend related to this statue that Grandma Dang appeared in a dream of one of the village elders and promised that she would protect the village if he performed an ancestral ritual for her on Sodeungseom Island. The Dang ritual for Grandma Dang is still held on the 15th day of the first lunar month every year. On Sodeungseom Island, there is also “Sodeung Grandma Lucky Postbox” that will deliver the mail you post after 1 year. Let’s send a letter that contains your earnest wish.  A must-see spot before entering Sodeungseom Island is Nampo Village, the filming location for Festival, a movie by director Im Gwon-taek that was based on a novel with the same title by writer Yi Chong-jun. Nampo Village is also well-known for oyster farming. When you have oysters grown on the mudflats of Deungnyangman Bay grilled with oak firewood, you will experience the true taste of grilled oysters full of the aroma of sea. Take a trip to Nampo Village’s Sodeungseom Island, a wonderful place full of exciting things to see, enjoy and eat.

stories.title: Seonhakdong Village
stories.script: Mustard flower village embracing a soaring crane  From the old days, Seonhakdong Village has been called “Sanjeo,” which means a village under the mountain. The person who gave it the pretty name of “Seonhak” meaning “flying crane” is writer Yi Chong-jun. Seonhakdong Village, which looks like it is embraced by the wings of a crane soaring in the sky, is the place visited by many because of its spectacular mustard flowers in spring and buckwheat flowers in autumn.  The trail where you can see the main contents of Seonhakdong Village Wayfarer, a short story set in Seonhakdong Village, and the world of its author Yi Chong-jun is created in the village. As you walk along the trial known as “Yi Chong-jun Literature Trail,” the distant coastal waters of Hoejin appear before your eyes. In addition, Seonhakdong Village Wayfarer by writer Yi Chong-jun is made into a movie Beyond the Years by director Im Gwon-taek, and it is said that the filming location of Beyond the Years about 500 m away from village entrance is the best spot to watch both Seonhakdong Village and the coastal waters of Hoejin. It will be perfect if you can see the amazing scene of a crane at the foot of the mountain, which is reflected on the sea there.  In particular, “Seonhakdong Buckwheat Festival” is held in October when buckwheat plants are in full bloom. During the festival period, you can enjoy buckwheat dishes in season prepared by the villagers, as well as various experience programs including buckwheat flour making, wish lantern releasing and soap making. Don’t miss the exciting performances that are the highlights of the buckwheat festival where the tourists visiting Seonhakdong Village and the villagers become one.

stories.title: Haedongsa Shrine (Ahn Jung Geun Shrine)
stories.script: Spirit of independence remembered in Jangheung-gun  Haedongsa Shrine in Jangheung-gun enshrines the ancestral tablet and portrait of patriot martyr Ahn Jung Geun, the only such shrine to him in Korea. Patriot martyr Ahn Jung Geun was from Hwanghae-do and is enshrined in Jangheung-gun, the land’s end of the southern region. Confucians and the Juksan Ahn Clan in Jangheung-gun regretted that no ancestral rituals were held for him since he had no descendants. So, the villagers proposed building the shrine to President Syngman Rhee and built the structure with their own money in 1955. This act seems totally normal since the area has historically produced a lot of upstanding military heroes. For reference, Ahn Jung Geun is from the Sunheung Ahn Clan and the 26th descendant of Ahn Hyang, a scholar in the Goryeo period.  The shrine is a simple building with 3 kans, in which the portrait, ancestral tablet, photos and a copy of Ahn Jung Geun are displayed, together with a visitors’ book. The signboard that says “Haedong Myeongwol” was written by President Syngman Rhee. It is said that the shrine got its name “Haedong” from this signboard.  Patriot martyr Ahn Jung Geun was born in Haeju-si of Hwanghae-do in 1879. He joined the armed resistance and fought in and out of Korea. He shot Ito Hirobumi to death in Harbin, China in 1909. During the trial, he wouldn't change his opinion that it was natural for him to kill Ito, the enemy commander, as a lieutenant general of the Korean resistance army. After writing his autobiography History of Ahn Eung-chil, Ahn Jung Geun died for his country in China’s Lushun Prison on March 26, 1910. Regrettably, his remains have not been found yet.

stories.title: Jangheung Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Hall
stories.audioTitle: 11. Jangheung Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Hall
stories.script: Heroes of Donghak in the last ferocious battlefield  Jangheung Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Hall is where you can learn about the background and development of Donghak Peasant Revolution in the latter era of the Joseon Dynasty and the activities of Donghak Peasant Army from Jangheung-gun. The memorial hall is built in Seokdaedeul that was one of the four ferocious battlefields and the last battlefield of the Donghak Peasant Revolution in Jangheung-gun. Seokdaedeul was where the second biggest battle out of Donghak Peasant Revolution battles was held and was a state-designated historic site in 2009.  The memorial hall built in the shape of a snail has a video room, an exhibition room and an experience room. In the video room, you can watch a video about Seokdaedeul battle in Jangheung-gun. In the exhibition room, a three-dimensional exhibition of scenes at the time of Donghak Peasant Revolution, and the activities of Yi Bang-eon, a leader of the local Donghak unit who was called the “General of Southern Region” and led the final battle, and Yi So-sa, a female leader who was at the head in every battle and boosted the morale of the Donghak Peasant Army, might make you choke with emotion.  After the exhibition, your whole family can participate in the many experience programs available. Enjoy the fun of time travelling to the past during “Young Boatman Yun Seong-do Experience,” “Jangtae (chicken cage) Rolling” and “Becoming Donghak Peasant Army.” Finalize your stay with a visit to the Monument to the Jangheung Donghak Peasant Revolution standing on a small hill overlooking Seokdaedeul. Don’t miss the introduction to the monument by Song Gi-suk, author of the saga Nokdu General.

stories.title: Bangchon Museum
stories.script: Meet the 500-year history of Bangchon Village  Bangchon Museum, located at the entrance of Bangchon Village, offers visitors a view of the 500-year history of Bangchon Village, the hub of Jangheung-gun and home of the Jangheung Wi Clan.  The museum is comprised of four indoor exhibition rooms and a small outdoor park. First, Exhibition Room No. 1 is filled with folk crafts including the old map of Bangchon Village that reflects its farming and housing culture. Exhibition Room No. 2 is a cultural space where you can experience wood blocks and rubbing. See artifacts and ancient documents of Yangban Sajok in Exhibition Room No. 3. Yangban Sajok means a distinguished family among Yangban, aristocrats.  In Exhibition Room No. 4, you can learn about the philosophy of Wi Baek-gyu, a scholar of the Realist School of Confucianism who represented the Honam Region and developed Gasa literature in Jangheung-gun, and see Jonjaejip, a collection of his works. After exploring the exhibitions rooms and enjoying the view of Cheongwansan Mountain at the observatory on the 3rd floor, go outside. It will be the perfect way to end the visit, walking around the small park with an endearing Farm Life Experience that displays foot-operated mills and large mortars.

stories.title: Hoeryeongjinseong Fortress
stories.script: The place where the history of Myeongnyang Battle began  Hoeryeongjinseong Fortress was built to root out Japanese raiders in the 21st year of King Seongjong's reign in the Joseon period. This is where the great victory led by Admiral Yi Sun-sin started. When Won Gyun lost at the Chilcheonryang Sea Battle, Bae Seol who was Naval Commander of Gyeongsang-do escaped with 12 damaged ships. Hoeryeongjinseong Fortress is where Admiral Yi Sun-sin who was reinstated as Navy Commander of Three Provinces took over 12 Panokseon ships from Bae Seol and repaired them, reestablishing the navy of the Joseon Dynasty and paving the way to win the historic victory.  When you enter Hoeryeongjinseong Fortress History Park, the first thing that catches your eye will be a stone work in the imagery of the 12 Panokseon ships. A relief on a huge wall showing the image of Hoeryeongjinseong Fortress in the old days and a scene from the Myeongnyang Battle is also impressive. When walking up a little bit more, you will see Hoeryeongjinseong Fortress. Now only about a 600-m long stone section of the fortress remains, and a 250-year-old hackberry planted in the memory of Admiral Yi Sun-sin is standing tall.  Hoeryeongjinseong Fortress is also the best spot to overlook Hoejinpo Port. You can see the beautiful scenery of the coastal waters of Hoejinpo Port on the fortress wall. Imaging what Admiral Yi Sun-sin felt when he was standing there, worrying about the fate of Joseon hung by a thread.

stories.title: Dongbaekjeong Pavilion
stories.script: Integrity of a scholar that blooms even in the snow  Dongbaekjeong Pavilion is a pavilion from the Joseon period facing south in Janghang Village. Within its low walls, Dongbaekjeong Pavilion is filled with Dongbaek, camellia, like its name. When you sit on the wooden floor of the pavilion, Hogyecheon Stream flows right in front of you and the picturesque pine forest surrounds the pavilion.  This pavilion was originally built by Kim Lin, who was the fourth state councilor of the State Council during the reign of King Sejo in the Joseon Dynasty, after he resigned from public office. The original name of the pavilion was “Gajeongsa,” which means a “temporary pavilion that has a room to sleep.” Kim Lin filled the garden with camellia when he built Gajeongsa Pavilion, and his descendent Kim Seong-jang renamed the pavilion more than 100 years later “Dongbaekjeong Pavilion” when he saw how lush the camellia had become. However, there is another hidden meaning in Dongbaekjeong Pavilion. Park Gwang-jeon who was an acquaintance of Kim Seong-jang wrote Dongbaekjeongseo, a book of Dongbaekjeong Pavilion, wishing that the descendants respect the pavilion’s name and think about its meaning. The book describes that the pavilion’s name had to be Dongbaekjeong because the righteous character of Kim Lin who abandoned a government post and came back to his hometown with single-minded devotion to King Danjong resembled the integrity of a camellia that blooms in the snow.  It is said that this pavilion was used for academic exchange and poetry reading for many scholars. That is why there are many tablets containing poetry among the 17 in Dongbaekjeong Pavilion. It is also interesting to see the history of Dongbaekjeong Pavilion from the signboard to densely hanging tablets including document, inscription and repair record. Like the poetry engraved on the tablet, you will feel as if you are in a scenic haven in the picturesque pavilion, enjoying the clean wind. On the 15th day of the first lunar month every year, the Byeolsinje Ritual is held in Hogye Village that faces Dongbaekjeong Pavilion across Hogyecheon Stream.

stories.title: Museum of Guijok-Walnut
stories.script: Everything about “Guijok-Walnut,” the local specialty of Jangheung-gun  “Guijok-Walnut” is a walnut variety natively grown only in Korea in Jangheung-gun, Jeollanam-do. Unlike other walnuts, it is not edible since there is hardly any kernel in it. However, it has been popular for the purpose of acupressure because of its hard surface. Guijok-Walnut is the precious walnut offered to the king in the Joseon period, because holding two pieces of Guijok-Walnut in a hand and rolling them is good for health and helps clear the head.  The Museum of Guijok-Walnut is where visitors can learn about this interesting plant. Although it is small in scale compared to museums in larger cities, it has its own unique atmosphere. A tall Guijok-Walnut tree and the “world’s largest stone walnut” greet visitors at the entrance.  Various sizes, shapes and forms of Guijok-Walnuts are displayed in the exhibition room. All Guijok-Walnuts exhibited here were collected by Director Kim Jae-won throughout his life. The value of Guijok-Walnut is determined based on its shape, and some of them are worth as much as 100 million won. Old books, papers, and other resources related to Guijok-Walnut are also in display. If you are lucky, you might meet Director Kim Jae-won and learn more about this well-designed exhibition from him.

stories.title: Birth Home of Yi Chong-jun
stories.script: Former home of the writer of Seopyeonje  Yi Chong-jun who expressed his special fondness for the southern region in his short story Seopyeonje is a writer from Jangheung-gun. The house where he was born and spent his younger days remains in Jinmok Village between Seonhakdong Village and Daembaegol Village. The small and simple birth home has been restored to its past style and is frequented by numerous readers and tourists.  Writer Yi Chong-jun explored the absurdity of the real world and the essential issues of human existence and has won major literary awards in Korea, such as the Dong-in Literary Award and the Yi Sang Literary Award. His stories were made into numerous movies, including Seopyeonje and Beyond the Years by director Im Gwon-taek and Secret Sunshine by director Lee Chang-dong.  In the birth home of Yi Chong-jun, collections of his important works are displayed on the main floored room and various documents such as pictures of the writer and newspaper interviews fill the wall of the main room. Snowy Road that is one of the most beautiful modern fictions is a short story about the author’s childhood, set in his birth home. After looking around the birth home, how about walking the Literature Trail Course No. 1 “Snowy Road” created along the mountain path that the protagonist of the story took with his mother? If you take this path after reading Snowy Road, you might able to feel the author’s thoughts hidden in the title “Snowy Road” that indirectly expressed his feelings for this mother.

stories.title: Haneulbit Arboretum
stories.script: An experience playground along the flower-filled path  Haneulbit Arboretum located at the foot of Hamjibong Peak in Jangheung-gun is a playground in a forest where flowers, trees and a pond come together. More than 300 varieties of trees and more than 1,000 species of wild flowers in a vast area create a truly breathtaking spectacle. A forest trail from the arboretum to the forest leads to Morning Garden, Wild Flower Garden and Eco Pond.  The Tulip Festival is held in spring in the Morning Garden when thousands of tulips are in bloom. A music concert and various performances are also held in an outdoor stage where tulips in many colors spread before you like a carpet. Wild Flower Garden is where the water in the valley flows and rare wild flowers bloom and Eco Pond is home to fancy carp and sturgeons that bring you peace of mind as they swim. The thick hinoki forest has a Healing Trail and lower wooden benches and is a good place to banish worldly thoughts and fatigue from everyday life while smelling phytoncide.  There are various experience programs offered for families. Forest Horse Riding Experience is perfect for beginners, Eco Experience offers the chance to plant a flowering plant and feed the carp swimming in the pond, and splash in the valley water in the fall and the fountain of the pond in summer. It will be an unforgettable memory to see flowers at the arboretum in the day and stay the night to take in the wonderous stars in the night sky.

stories.title: Jeongnamjin Astronomical Science Museum
stories.script: Explore space mysteries  The Jeongnamjin Astronomical Science Museum is where you can observe stars and experience the wonders of space. The way to the museum is also pleasant as it is located in the mid slope of Jangheung-gun’s Eokbulsan Mountain where a unique rock formation blends in with the surroundings. You can observe the solar spots in the scorching sun in the auxiliary observation capsule where the sliding dome opens during the day, and look at constellations in the main observation capsule that is a 7-m diameter dome.  The 2nd floor of the Astronomical Science Museum has the main observatory capsule, auxiliary observation capsule, planetarium, exhibition room and photo zone. First, in the main observatory capsule, there is a reflecting telescope and a refracting telescope. As these two telescopes automatically follow stars, anyone can easily see nebulae, star clusters and the Milky Way as well as other constellations. In the auxiliary observation capsule, it is possible to observe solar spots and solar prominences and the surface of the moon with 6 telescopes with different functions. Even if the day is cloudy and you cannot see the sun and starts, don’t be disappointed. You can see more clear and beautiful constellations on a dome-shaped screen in the planetarium.  Now, let’s go to the exhibition room and photo zone. The exhibition room is comprised of space learning corners. You can look at the history of space travel with “Cheonsang Yeolcha Bunyajido” that is the old constellation map of Korea in Space Learning Corner No. 1, and more in-depth learning, such as the history of constellations, planets in our solar system and Kepler’s laws, is offered in Space Learning Corner No. 2. After viewing, you can take a souvenir photograph of you wearing a space suit in the Space Suit Photo Zone at the entrance of the exhibition room.

stories.title: Mukchon Village Camellia Grove of Yongsan-myeon
stories.audioTitle: 29. Mukchon Village Camellia Grove of Yongsan-myeon
stories.script: Beautiful camellia flowers protect the village  Mukchon Village of Yongsan-myeon, Jangheung-gun, Jeollanam-do is the hometown of Yi Bang-eon, the leader of Donghak Peasant Revolution in Jangheung-gun, and the setting of a saga Nokdu General. At the entrance of the village, more than 140 three-hundred-year-old camellia trees form a forest. They were designated as Jeollanam-do Cultural Heritage Material No. 248 in recognition of their value. The camellia grove protects the Mukchon Village from wind, flood and fire and has stood like a guard in reality as well. It is said that they supplement the insufficient area of the Mukchon Village and promote peace according to Feng Shui geometry.  The camellia grove formed along the stream that flows in the fields of the Mukchon Village is at its peak from mid-March to early April. Camellia flowers bearing buds like red hearts stir the minds of tourists in early spring days. Unlike other spring flowers where petals fall one by one, the sad image of the whole camellia flower falling off touches the heart.  You could take a walk and meditate among camellia flowers that repeat blooming and falling from winter to spring or become sentimental while sitting on tables and chairs placed throughout the camellia grove. If you write a letter that starts with “I love you more than anyone else” that is the flower language for a camellia flower, it will be an unforgettable memory.

stories.title: Sumun Beach
stories.script: Fantastic collaboration of a clean beach and pen shells  Sumun Beach is the only beach in Jangheung-gun. It is a popular summer destination for families because of its warm seawater and shallow depth. Tall palm trees and an evergreen pine forest embracing the sandy beach complete the beauty of Sumun Beach. Walk on the trail decorated beautifully as a park and look at the picturesque faraway Deungnyangman Bay.  As a representative beach of Jangheung-gun, Sumun Beach has many amenities. Low bench-type wide beach umbrellas are in the campground, and a deck trail is built along the beach for easy mobility of users with a wheelchair or stroller. And don’t forget Andante, the spa resort that is the pride of Sumun Beach. This resort has various auxiliary facilities, including an outdoor water park and a 24-hour sauna. The red sunset seen from the hot seawater and green tea baths of Andante will give you an unforgettable memory.  Another source of pride in Sumun Beach is pen shells. Pen shells have mineral contents 5 to 20 times higher than other seafood, and their scallop is larger than that of general shells and is quite chewy. You can eat pen shells cooked in various methods, such as raw, grilled, seasoned and broiled, in the Pen Shell Food Street next to Sumun Beach. Jangheung Samhap, a combination of pen shells, beef and shiitake mushrooms, is a delicacy you don’t want to miss, as it is the representative dish of Jangheung-gun. Early May marks the beginning of pen shell season, and the Jeongnamjin Jangheung Pen Shell Festival is held in Kijogae Village near Sumun Beach. Be sure to visit the village to enjoy various programs including a pen shell auction and quick pen shell dish tasting during the festival period.

stories.title: Yuchi Recreational Forest
stories.script: A day to enjoy nature  The Yuchi Recreational Forest is located upstream of the Jangheung Dam where the water is clear and the air is crisp. It’s the best vacation spot in summer and a popular resort for families since it has the cool Woramcheon Stream and a forest with 400 varieties of thickly growing trees. Families with children visit the forest often when the water park opens during the summer.  A water park with showers and a large playing field are perfect places for children to play. Sun shelters and wooden pavilions to avoid the hot sun are good spots to relax. In addition, there is a forest trail full of phytoncide connected to the suspension bridge that is one of the main attractions of the Yuchi Recreational Forest. The whole trail is easy without uphill areas, so everyone can enjoy the forest.  There are various accommodations available depending on the size of the tourist group in the Yuchi Recreational Forest. In the House in Forest, there are accommodations for families, friends and couples, and in the Recreational Center, there are accommodations suitable for group users. The Recreational Center can be booked for a 231-㎡ room on the 1st floor or for the whole two-story building. Or you can use the campground if you wish to spend the night outdoors and truly enjoy nature. Please visit the Yuchi Recreational Forest after making a reservation via the Yuchi Recreational Forest homepage.

stories.title: Hanjae Park
stories.script: Heavenly flower garden with violet pasque flowers in full bloom  Hanjae Park is the largest natural pasque flower habitat in Korea. In March when spring comes, pasque flowers produce violet blooms in great abundance around the Hanjae Park area. You can see pasque flowers gathered here and there when you walk along the gently sloped trail.  When strolling up the hill watching the pasque flowers, the brilliant blue southern sea will slowly reveal itself over Hanjae Pass. The Hoejin-myeon area where Hanjae Park is located used be an island called Deokdo Island before Gwandeok Embankment was built. Numerous people frequented Hanjae Pass from old times, as it was the only pass that connected the east and west sides of the island.  Han Seung-won, the great man of Korean literature, was carried over Hanjae Pass as a baby. The pass he had crossed numerous times when he was young has appeared as a pass that protagonists crossed in his stories including The Paradise of Yours, The Foggy Village and Magpie Sunset. In addition, he reminisced about “the time when I played stick-tossing games and wrestled with my friends and went back home leading the cattle tinkling their bells and then eating red bean porridge” in his poem Hanjae Pass. There are monuments with many poems of his setting in his hometown engraved at the entrance of Hanjae Park.

stories.title: Jangheung Dawon (tea plantation)
stories.script: Taste Cheongtaejeon Tea, the traditional fermented tea of Jangheung-gun  Jangheung Dawon is where you can make and taste Cheongtaejeon Tea, the traditional fermented tea passed down from the Unified Silla period. Cheongtaejeon Tea is made by steaming wild tea leaves, pounding them in a mortar, making them in a circle shape and making a hole in the center. This is called Cheongtaejeon because it is in a coin shape, “jeon” means money,” and in a color like it is covered in a blue moss, “cheongtae” means blues moss.  Cheongtaejeon Tea making is held in the experience room next to the tearoom of Jangheung Dawon. You can participate in the process from grinding tea leaves steamed in a cast-iron pot, to making a shape and drying them. In reality, Cheongtaejeon Tea should be ripened in a clay pot for more than 1 year. You can taste Cheongtaejeon Tea that requires such time and care everywhere in Jangheung Dawon. We recommend tasting in an elegant tearoom facing a small pond, because the rich aroma of tea quickly eases your mind as soon as you step into the tearoom.  Cheongtaejeon Tea, which is brewed to drink like a common tea, is more reddish than general green tea. It was used as a household medicine when medicines were hard to come by because it is high in minerals and low in caffeine. Considering that Cheongtaejeon Tea after a meal adds warmth to the body and inhibits the growth of harmful intestinal bacteria, you can’t resist the appeal of Cheongtaejeon Tea.

stories.title: Gisan Village
stories.script: The home of “Eight Writers” who represent Gisan  People say “do not brag about money in Yeosu and do not brag about your blow in Beolgyo” when you go to Jeollanam-do, together with “do not brag about writing in Jangheung.” In particular, Gisan Village located at the foot of Sajasan Mountain in Jangheung-gun is famous as a town that produced outstanding writers in the Joseon period.  Starting with Baek Gwang-hong, eight writers including Baek Gwang-hun, Baek Gwang-an, Baek Gwang-seong, Im Hoe, Im Bun, Kim Yun and Kim Gong-hui are called “Eight Famous Writers of Gisan.” Baek Gwang-hong wrote Gwanseo Byeolgok (Song of the Sceneries of Gwanseo) to describe the scenery and lives in the Gwanseo Region, and it was the first Gihaeng Gasa in Korea, 25 years ahead of Gwandong Byeolgok (Song of the Sceneries of Gwandong) by Jeong Cheol. Gihaeng Gasa is a kind of literature in-between poem and prose that realistically describes what the writer saw, heard, felt and experienced.   A boundary stone “Eight Writer Traditional Culture Village” is standing at the entrance of Gisan Village and there are monuments engraved with the works of Eight Famous Writers of Gisan on the road to the village hall. In addition, you can see murals describing the story of them when you walk along the quiet and still stone walls that remain intact from the old days. How about mediating while strolling the village road where the writers walked in times long past?

stories.title: Geulseorit Trail
stories.script: An old trail filled with the atmosphere of learning  “Jeongnamjin Lohas Green Trail” is the representative trail of Jangheung-gun in Jeollanam-do. It was made by connecting the mountain trail, forest trail and village road that villagers have walked from long ago. This 9.5-km-long trail is divided into 4 zones, and the name of Course No. 4, the fourth zone, is “Geulseorit Trail.” Course No. 4 is the trail created above Gisan Village that was selected as the best village to live in Korea in 2008. The trail is named “Geulseorit Trail” because Gisan Village produced many famous writers in the Joseon period. “Geul” means learning and erudition and “Seori” means a big pile.  Eight writers who represented Gisan Village in the Joseon period were called “Eight Famous Writers of Gisan.” Among them, Baek Gwang-hong was praised as one of the “Eight Writers of Joseon” and he wrote Gwanseo Byeolgok (Song of the Sceneries of Gwanseo), the first Gihaeng Gasa in Korea that was 25 years ahead of Gwandong Byeolgok (Song of the Sceneries of Gwandong) by Jeong Cheol. Gasa is literature in-between poem and prose that emerged in the early Joseon period, which includes Gihaeng Gasa, Gyubang Gasa, and Seomin Gasa  Geulseorit Trail starts from the stone wall that people in Jangheung-gun walk along to go to Sajasan Mountain above Gisan Village to gather wood. Behind the Gyeonyeondae stone wall that still has the feel of the past, trees form a dense forest. When you walk leisurely along the trail, you will pass Jeongnamjin Lohas Town Promotion Hall and arrive at the yard of a traditional Hanok house where hundreds of large clay pots stand in a row. This is the Traditional Jang Experience Center operated by a village company. Here soy sauces and soybean pastes made by the villages are ripening.

stories.title: Fantasy Cup Museum
stories.script: 30. Fantasy Cup Museum  * Man: We'll now take a look around the Fantasy Cup Museum and the Jang Gil-hwan Gallery. * Woman: Two museums in one building! Awesome! * Man: Yes! Interestingly, the Fantasy Cup Museum is the first museum in Asia dedicated exclusively to cups. It displays more than 13,000 cups collected from 76 countries, including unusual ones you will never have seen anywhere else. * Woman: What kind of cups are they? * Man: There is a cup from Tibet made out of a human skull; an earthenware cup equipped with three handles from Silla, one of the three ancient states on the Korean Peninsula during the Three Kingdoms period; a 3,000-year-old cup found along the Silk Road; a coffee set used by Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom, which happens to be one of only two such sets in the world; a brass cup from which Adolf Hitler is said to have drunk vodka; and many more! There is an experience hall where you can make or design your own cup or feel the cups that are on display using an AR app. * Woman: It sounds like a fascinating place! * Man: As for the Jang Gil-hwan Gallery, it exhibits works by Jang Gil-hwan, an award-winning artist, and rare ancient Buddhist and Hindu works of arts of a kind rarely seen in any museum around the world.  * Woman: You mean works of art you can’t see unless you go to other countries, right? * Man: Correct! You can check out the new types of art Jang has explored, such as Coffee Painting” and “Ceramic Painting,” which are paintings on ceramic plate, and experience making your own coffee painting to take home with you!

stories.title: 1. Remains of Amsa-dong, Seoul. New beginning of humankind and their culture
stories.audioTitle: 1. Ruins of Amsa-dong, Seoul. The new beginning of humankind and their culture
stories.script: The ruins of Amsa-dong, Seoul, contains traces of the Neolithic people.   The Amsa-dong site represent areas where we can understand the living structure of people in those days.  Also, with the plentiful amounts of resources near the Han river, it has the traces of people using those resources for hunting, gathering, and fishing to form a community during the Neolithic.   When Neolithic houses and artifacts, that were buried in the sand for thousands of years due to the 1925 flood, the ruins were thought to have been destroyed and were not investigated.   However, after discovering parts of the comb-pattern pottery during the construction of a baseball field in Jangchung High school, serious research began.   In result, numerous remains were excavated, including remains of the Three Kingdoms era, and was able to witness the traces of habitation beyond the Neolithic.    In researching the Neolithic, Amsa-dong ruins were evaluated as an important heritage since this was the first time witnessing the habitation of people that formed a full village.   Excavation is still in progress until today and the interest in remains are constant as well.   It is expected to bring opportunities in looking into the Neolithic more thoroughly.

stories.title: 2. Comb-pattern Pottery
stories.script: The Neolithic era earthenware have various shapes.   Earthenware used by people in the Neolithic era, who lived on the Korean Peninsula is commonly recognized as the comb-pattern pottery.   It is named after engraving short oblique lines on the surface of the earthenware.   The comb-pattern pottery found in Amsa-dong ruins is one of the ornamental arts because it is filled with various patterns all around the pottery.   The comb-pattern pottery which the Neolithic people invented, was not only used for normal tools.   They were elegant, cultured people that added artistic value into a scientific invention.   Among the earthenware’s, there were some flat ones, but commonly shaped in round or sharp features.   Likewise, the exact reason is not clear on why the bottom is created sharply.   Most common reason is to save the pottery into a hole, but there are different opinions from scholars regarding the pottery to have symbolic meanings besides the functional side.   We can witness potteries with more different patterns besides the comb-pattern pottery.   There are various ways to put in a pattern.   Potteries were designed in various methods. For example, “Eung-gi”, a method of adding clay to the surface of earthenware to create patterns, “Chim-sun”, a method of using tools to draw long lines, “Ja-dol”, a method of using tools to make scratches vertically or in side ways to create patterns, and “Ap-nal”, a method using animals bone or shells to make continuous horizontal patterns.   In addition, secondary pattern engraving methods are fingernail pattern, fish bone pattern, rainbow pattern, double sawtooth pattern, bubble pattern, lightening pattern, and diagonal pattern.   It is not clear whether these distinctive patterns and unusual shapes represent the shamanistic act of the Neolithic people, a symbol of their group mark, or an artistic expression.   However, if art can be defined as a creative activity that creats wonderful pieces, these potteries can be recognized as art with the formative beauty of these patterns.

stories.title: 3.  Landscape changes and the climate of the New Stone Age
stories.audioTitle: 3. Landscape changes and the climate of the Neolithic
stories.script: Huge animals with lots of hair like the mammoth or giant deer lived during the glacial period, before the Neolithic. China, Korea, and Japan were united into one whole land with forests mostly filled with needleleaf trees.    Approximately 10,000 years ago, after the glacial period, ice melted, and the sea level rose; causing the Earth and its climate to change to what it is today.   Therefore, the four seasons of Korea become more distinct.   Broadleaf trees increased evidently, sea creatures like fish and shell fishes became abundant in the sea and rivers, and small animals like elk and deer appeared.   People of the Neolithic adapted to the new environment.   They were able to earn food resources easily through fishing in the river, gathering fruits in the mountains, and hunting together occasionally.   They started their settlement life unlike the past.

stories.title: 4. Trace of time, soil stratum
stories.script: The place we are currently standing now is the history of people from hundreds of thousands of years ago.   From time, soil built on the history of people in the past, and the descendants made new bases on top of that to live.  Through repeated process, the various items people used in the past are laying down in the ground.   Diverse cultural layers are formed in the Amsa-dong ruins, from the Neolithic era to the present day.   This soil layer was exhibited by removing the upper 5 soil layers, where excavation was conducted in 2016.   The basest of the soil layer is composed of the gravel layer, a layer of natural sediment on top, and the cultural layer of the early Neolithic era on top of that.   Especially, the cultural layer of the early Neolithic era was found in large areas of the remains.   In this layer, diverse remains were excavated, such as polished stone tools, the comb-pattern potteries, and the nesting places.   Above the early Neolithic era layer is the Three kingdoms era layer, and above that is the cultural layer of the modern-day.

stories.title: 5. Ecological environment of the Han River during the New Stone Age.
stories.audioTitle: 5. Ecological environment of the Han River during the Neolithic era.
stories.script: The Neolithic is a era where big changes were made in the natural ecosystem.   After the glacial period, due to the rapid warming of the climate, big animals moved North or disappeared, and small animals like deer started appearing.   Plant resources like acorns were easily earned because the forests changed from coniferous forests to deciduous forests.  Although it was not found in the ruins of Amsa-dong, various food resources such as shellfish and mackerel were found in the Neolithic shell mound remains.   Especially, acorns were assumed to be the main source of food for the Neolithic people.   It is estimated that they grinded the acorns in stones to remove the tannin taste and cooked it in various ways.

stories.title: 6. Invitation of the New Stone Age people in Amsa-dong.
stories.audioTitle: 6. Invitation of the Neolithic people in Amsa-dong.
stories.script: This place was excavated during 1975 from the National Museum of Korea. Many remains were found, including 11 habitations and items that were used, from the sand layer showing bright brown in color.   The excavation site is open and displayed, so that people can exhibit the place of the Neolithic era as it is.   Preservation treatment is completed, and periodic maintenance is held to prevent decomposition.   If you look closely at the place, you can see where the pillar stood, the place where the pottery was placed, the firepit location, and the blackened spot due to fire.   You can see places with 2~3 firepits, and places that overlap with different layers. This is where people lived and moved when their house broke down.   A dugout hut is big enough for 4~5 people to live.   The ground was dug within 50 centimeters in rectangular or circular shapes, pillars stacked, and the roof placed with reeds or flame grasses to be warm during the winter, and cool during the summer.   Most of the dugout huts were built southbound for better sunlight, and fire pits were place in the middle of the house.   This firepit was an important existence, cooking food, keeping the house warm, and brightening the environment.   It is assumed that they used charcoal fire instead of firewood to avoid fire.

stories.title: 7. New skills and tools
stories.script: The Neolithic people used the ‘sanding technology’, grinding two stones with each other, so that they can adapt to the new environment.   Sanding technology is using friction to make stoneware’s surface smooth, and brought a new toll called polished stone tools.   Big advantage of the sanding technology is that it can be reused easily.   When stoneware is broken or worn out, it can be processed again with the sanding technology.   Stoneware’s shape and size changes through time. Therefore, during reconstruction, there are situation where the stoneware is designed for a different use.   Effectiveness of a tool is advanced by sanding the edge. With the sanding technology, various tools such as stone axes, stone spears, bow, and arrow were made.   Considering the large amounts of remains in the archaeological site in Amsa-dong, we can notice that the Neolithic people made and used various tools for their convenient life.   They learned to survive by using tools such as bows and arrows to hunt small and fast animals, digging tools to dig out rooted fruits, half-moon knife and stone sickle to harvest grains, stones for grinding acorns or grains, and nets to catch fish in the Han river.   In particular, the net had weight hung on them, and you can spot their wisdom of digging each side holes for the weight from falling off during fishing.  New skills and tools of the Neolithic people, provided them a richer environment, forming a village and allowing them to stay in one place longer.

stories.title: 8. Obsidian
stories.script: Obsidian is a mineral made from rapid colling of lava, found usually in the Baekdusan Mountain or Japan, and normally was used as the arrowhead because of its strength and sharpness.   This obsidian found in the archaeological site of Amsa-dong during the 2017 excavation, did not seem to have been used for certain purposes based upon their shape.  It is expected to be a by-product of making tools, since there isn’t any evidences of working on stones.   Also, the quality of rocks is very poor.   Despite the use of high-quality obsidian since the late Paleolithic era, it is still a mystery on the reason for poor quality obsidian in the ruins of Amsa-dong.   However, when considering the origin of the obsidian, it can be distinguished as valuable information that explains the Neolithic people expanding the radius of their movements.

stories.title: 9. Jade Jewelry
stories.script: The Neolithic people loved decorating with jewelry they made.   Especially, they used clams to make masks, necklaces, and bracelets. Also they used animals bones or stones.   These jewelries were more likely to have shamanistic meanings of showing status or preventing bad spirits, rather than decorating oneself.   This Jade ornament was excavated from the ruins of Amsa-dong in 2016, having a narrow rectangle on top, which is like the ones found in the Janghand ruins of Gadeok Island in Busan and the ruins of Unseo-dong, Incheon.   Holes are pierced on the top of the Jade ornament for strings to be inserted.   Excavations of the Neolithic Jade ornaments are very rare in the central Han River basin, which indicates a valuable resource for studying the ruins of Amsa-dong’s art culture.

stories.title: 10. The appearance of earthenware and the New stone Age culture.
stories.audioTitle: 10. Arrival of pottery and the Neolithic culture
stories.script: The ‘pottery’ made from making clay in water and baking it, is the first invention of mankind to realize chemical change and use it.   Baked clay carries a whole new property, where it does not burn in fire and does not dissolve in water.   This invention in pottery, brought big changes to human life.   Using potteries to cook, resulted in the opportunity to eat various plant resources, and have stability in their dietary life by storing food.    This gave motivation for people to live in one place for long periods of time and live a happy stable life.   In the Paleolithic era, there were instances where people made jewelry through shaping soil, but the basics of pottery made from cooking in fire started from the Neolithic era.   The Neolithic pottery appeared all over the world around 10,000 B.C.   However, pottery was already produced in the East Asian areas quicker, around 15,000 B.C.   At the time potteries were mostly plain in decoration, but gradually developed into having diverse designs.   The comb-pattern potteries that were decorated by engraving on the surface, were usually produced in Northern Europe, Siberia, the northeastern districts of China, Korea, and Japan. On the other hand, in Southwest Asia and southern part of China, painted potteries were made by drawing on the surface of the potteries.   The first pottery that appeared in Korea formed a flat surface.   However, from around 5000 B.C, the surface of the potteries started transforming into circular chapes, and around 4000 B.C., the mainstream of the pottery’s surface was shaped round or sharp in the southern parts of the Korean peninsula.

stories.title: 11. Amsa-dong Comb-pattern pottery
stories.audioTitle: 11. The comb-pattern pottery of the Amsa-dong site
stories.script: The comb-pattern pottery excavated from the Amsa-dong ruins exhibit outstanding diversity of decorative patterns and high level of technical refinement.   Also, many of the potteries excavated in the Amsa-dong ruins present special values because they are preserved in their original forms.   Unlike the Eastern coastal area where raised pattern pottery is excavated, it is understood that the midwestern part of the Korean peninsula where the Amsa-dong ruins are located, used delicately decorated comb-pattern potteries made of bones or tree sticks since the early Neolithic era.  The Neolithic people that lived in the Amsa-dong ruins usually engraved patterns that looked like a fish bone by drawing repeated short straight lines or long crossing straight lines.   Also, the overall shape was formed by repeating circular lines, dot patterns, and short diagonal lines.   The comb-pattern pottery can be defined as the peak of art during the Neolithic era because they have numerous kinds of patterns like skein patterns, zigzag patterns, and dotted line patterns.   As you can see through the pottery of the Amsa-dong ruins, the Midwest of Korea can be considered as the origin of the comb-pattern pottery, since they have the most developed and delicate pottery.  The comb-pattern pottery was in its most perfect form during 5000 to 4000 B.C., where it was divided into three different parts and engraved delicately. However, we can witness the bottom part design being skipped and lacking in uniformity through time.   Through this, recent studies have considered the origin of the comb-pattern pottery is the Korean peninsula to the Northeastern part of China.   The reason is because the variety of pottery in these regions are not only outstanding, but also considered to be ahead of time. Also, the Korean peninsula and Northeast Asian regions are the birthplace of these diverse potteries.

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations-Samsunsan Arboretum
stories.script: Opened in April 2017 in Dangjin, Chungnam, Samsunsan Arboretum is home to over 1,160 plant types and serves as a place for people to relax, have fun and learn about nature as plant DNA is collected, preserved, and displayed. The arboretum has 10 facilities including an outdoor garden, greenhouse, Kids’ Dream Forest, Korean Peninsula Mini Park, an ecology pond, a meadow, and Sky Trail as well as 23 exhibition attractions including parks with a variety of rocks, hydrangea, fruit, maple trees, azalea and white birch and one park with lots of wind—so much to see! A wide range of scenery can also be taken in during each season while you and your family enjoy the playground, picnic site, café, and swimming pools. Samsunsan Arboretum also offers a variety of programs for both children and adults. The Forest Commentary is a walking tour around the arboretum with a forest guide. Forest Experience and play & handicraft programs are also available on weekends for kids. We are the perfect place for everyone—young people, senior citizens, singles, couples, families—anyone who wants to learn about nature or simply enjoy it. What makes Samsunsan Arboretum even more attractive is that there is no charge for admission or parking! Come to Samsunsan Arboretum for a dive into nature!

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations-Myeoncheon Eupseong Fortress
stories.script: Myeoncheon Eupseong Fortress was built in 1439, 21 years into King Sejong’s reign. He constructed the fortress to command the surrounding flatland and deter neighboring states from invading the country. The fortress holds historical significance due to its involvement in persecution of Catholics and a battle during the Donghak Agrarian Movement. Thanks to large-scale restoration efforts that began in 2007, the south gate and castle have been renovated. Within the fortress stand two gingko trees that are about 1,100 years old, planted during the Goryeo Era for General Bok when he was ill. His daughter had a dream in which a spirit of the mountain told her to brew liquor with azalea and stream water from Mount Ami, give it to her father after 100 days and plant a gingko tree in her front yard to help the general heal. She did as the spirit told her, and General Bok was indeed healed. Every Chuseok, people of the village celebrate the gingko trees, which are designated Natural Monument No. 551.   Shall we take a stroll along the fortress wall? Gunjajeong Pavilion rests under the gingko trees, and we can also see Geongonilchojeong Pavilion and Goljeongji Lake—both designed and created by Park Jiwon, one of the greatest thinkers of the Practical Learning movement in the last Joseon Dynasty. Here, cherry blossoms can be photographed in spring and lotus in summer. Enjoy a relaxing cup of tea like Park Jiwon did, before heading to Gallery Fortress, which holds an exhibition area on the first floor and a café and lounge on the second. The gallery offers programs for you and your group that help you see all the eye-catching scenes around the fortress. Just a five-minute walk from the gallery you will find a bookstore called      “Ancient Future.” Follow the path leading to a small shop called ”Azalea Store” to go back in time. Take a peek at the wisdom and memories of our forebears through their paintings at an outdoor gallery. Last but not least, taste the famous Myeoncheon bean soup noodles for the perfect way to conclude your journey around the fortress.  Every April sees the return of the Myeoncheon Azalea Folk Festival where you can try Myeoncheon azalea liquor, a national intangible heritage, as well as azalea-themed folk games and food. Don’t miss the chance to enjoy a walk down memory lane around the fortress and take in the festival!

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations- Waemok Village
stories.script: Waemok Village is the only place in Korea you can see both sunrise and sunset. Its name roughly translates into “heron neck” and was chosen because the village is long and its shape resembles a heron’s neck. On a map, Dangjin looks like the city juts north into the West Sea like a peninsula, while the coastline of the most northern part faces east, allowing you to see sunrise and sunset from the same location! Sunrise from Waemok Village is a cozier, more peaceful feeling than created by the sunrise seen from the East Sea coastline. Walk along the sandy, rocky beach and go fishing during the summer. Take a relaxing stroll on the deck along Waemok Beach. Also along the beach you’ll find Saebit Waemok—a popular spot for taking the perfect picture to post on social media.  Continuing on the deck will bring you to Yacht Sailing Gallery, built to support Captain Kim Seungjin, a well-known Korean sailor, during his round-the-world yachting trip. On the first floor is a free exhibition about that journey, while the training studio on the second floor offers summer yacht programs on Waemok Sea—the perfect opportunity for those interested in yachting. Waemok Village’s unique geography makes it a prime location for Waemok’s Sunrise Festival, held on every New Year’s Eve and New Year’s Day. Come for a wide variety of performances and programs, as well as fresh seafood available for you to enjoy. After the countdown to the new year, visitors can make their wishes during the sheaf-burning ritual. Rise to the beauty of sunrise and sunset at Waemok Village—the perfect place to start your year!

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations-Sapkyoho Lake
stories.script: Let’s head to Sapkyoho Lake, one of the main attractions in Dangjin! In the past, this body of water was part of an important sea route to China, and is now a popular tourist attraction thanks to Sapkyoho Seawall and Seohae Bridge, both constructed in 1979. Sapkyoho Hamsang Park is Korea’s first warship park boasting a retired naval vessel, as well as a marine science museum. Don’t forget Sapkyoho Lake Theme Park, with fun rides and a chance for a photo on its photogenic ferris wheel! Wait for nightfall for an even more stunning view thanks to the illumination and beautiful lights in the ocean park. Sapkyoho Lake is the perfect place to spend a day in the beauty of nature. One of the recommended accommodations is Dangjin Marine Camping Park with its breathtaking scenery of the West Sea. If you go deeper into the beauty around Sapkyoho Lake, there is a bike trail along the freshwater lake next to the seawall, a lake park, a baseball diamond and an ecology park. Sapkyoho Ocean Park is a place to not only become healthier, but where nature can be enjoyed at its observatory deck, sports facility, art hall, and trails. Fishing and a variety of other activities make it perfect for your family  Dangjin World Art Circus is a place of fun for kids and brings back memories for adults. A shellfish festival is held every October, during which a variety of events and activities are on offer, including performances from the Dangjin World Art Circus team, music concerts, fireworks, seafood auctioning, and bare-hand fishing. Be sure to visit Café Street and look at the grand scenery of Seohae Bridge, a landmark of the West Sea. Enjoy some fantastic time with family and friends at Sapkyoho Lake!

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations-Nanji Island
stories.script: The name of the beautiful Nanji Island roughly translates into “the island of orchid and ganoderma lucidum” because there are many orchids and ganoderma lucidum on the island. It is blessed with a sandy beach on shallow water, making the island perfect for swimming. Nanji Island was named one of the top ten islands in Korea thanks to its clear water and fine sand, while the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries selected Nanji Island Beach as one of the best beaches in the country. The Ministry of the Interior and Safety, the Korea Tourism Organization, and Yonhap News all selected Nanji Island as the must-visit island for 2016. Twenty minutes from Dobi Island by ship, Nanji is the perfect place for a family vacation. If you choose to take the cruise to Daenanji Island, bring a bag of chips to feed the seagulls hovering above you on the beautiful West Sea. Once you reach the pine forest and golden sandy beach, go swimming, fishing, or harvest some shellfish. Find the rare lotus spine and rogusa rose in the well-preserved nature along the coast, which is frequented by Eurasian oystercatchers. Daenanji Island’s mud flats are particularly appealing to migratory birds due to their abundance of food, while the many uninhabited islands nearby make the region an ideal place for nesting. Look around Nanji Island’s flowers and birds, and you will feel like you’re in some sort of paradise. Fishermen catch rockfish and other fish along the seashore near the beach and along the rocky coast. Back on Nanji Island, another fun activity is trekking along the Nanji Trail. Go fishing, swimming, or trekking, or simply take in the beautiful scenery here on Nanji Island!

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations-Hapdeokje
stories.script: Hapdeokje was one of the three main water reservoirs during the Joseon Dynasty, along with Yeonan Namdaeji in Hwanghae Province and Byeokgolje in Gimje. Experts believe that Hapdeokje, which is now used for irrigation, was constructed before the Goryeo Era. Only its curvy bank structure remains, but its importance was recognized and the reservoir designated as Chungnam Monument No. 70 in April 1989 and as a world heritage irrigation structure by the International Commission on Irrigation and Drainage in 2017. Hapdeok Irrigation Folk Museum is nearby, where you can learn about the wisdom of our ancestors who understood the importance of irrigation. The museum showcases this history and of our ancestor’s agricultural practices, with artifacts and over 20 irrigation tools for you to try out. Come for a whole new experience! Hapdeokje is currently undergoing improvements, but remains very much a well-preserved habitat for many endangered species including rare frogs, swans and spoonbills. Hapdeokje is a place that you must visit at least once in your lifetime. According to legend, the King of the underworld will scold those in the afterlife who had never visited Hapdeokje while they were here on earth. But of course, you won’t have to say no! An Agricultural Theme Park has floor fountains, a thatched-roof pavilion, a mill, thatched houses and gardens. At Hapdeokje Ecology Tourism Center, watch videos of the nature around Hapdeokje, a Chungnam monument and a world heritage irrigation structure. You can also see Hapdeokje’s flora and fauna using high-tech devices. Hapdeokje Yeonho Lotus Festival occurs every July, when the lotus flowers are in bloom. Come to Hapdeokje for both time with your family or friends and to enjoy the beautiful harmony of nature and people, of tradition and modernity.

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations- Gijisi Juldarigi Museum
stories.script: “The tie that binds us together.” Gijisi Juldarigi, or tug-of-war, is a five-hundred-year tradition passed down from the Joseon Dynasty at Gijisi, the hub of Joseon’s marine culture. In the past, villagers engaged in tug-of-war competitions to wish for prosperity and peace. Using four large bales of straw, over 40 days the residents today make the world’s longest and thickest rope. Every year in early March—according to the lunar calendar—about 100,000 people gather around this 200-meter-long, one-meter-thick rope to tug on a rope that weighs as much as 40 tons. If the northern village wins, they say the country will be peaceful, and if the southern village wins, it will be a good harvest year. Along with the tug-of-war, many folk events including national Pungmul competitions and Ssireum (Korean wrestling) matches take place, causing the tug-of-war to be designated as National Intangible Cultural Heritage No. 75 in 1982.   The tradition was also registered on the list of UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. It’s safe to say that not only is it a proud tradition of Korea, but it is also valued by the world. The birth of Gijisi Juldarigi dates back 500 years, when Korea was an agricultural society. It was combined with folk traditions and fishing village culture, surviving Japanese colonial times to become one of the main folk traditions of Korea today. Gijisi Juldarigi Museum opened in April 2011 to celebrate the spirit of the tug-of-war. Its three-story structure holds a permanent and special exhibitions and has an auditorium, meeting room, and office as well as a rope exhibition area that showcases the actual-size rope, and a demonstration room where people try their hand with a tug-of-war every April.   The museum is known both at home and abroad for its extensive content about tug-of-war. The permanent exhibition shows the geographical background of Gijisi Juldarigi, artifacts from farms and fishing villages in Dangjin, a rope frame, an explanation on rope-making, a miniature of Guksudang Shrine and Giji Market in the 1970s, interesting stories about the Juldarigi Preservation Committee and farming tools and 300 other artifacts. Come learn about the tug-of-war traditions in countries across the world and the Olympic version. Children can try their hand at twisting cords into rope, a bit of rope-tugging and view videos on the tradition. Build a special memory here at Gijisi Juldarigi Museum.

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations-Ami Art Museum
stories.script: Ami Art Museum was created by the artist Park Giho, and an installation artist named Goo Hyunsook, who transformed an abandoned elementary school into a fabulous gallery. At the heart of natural surroundings, the gallery aspires to focus on ecological art. An outdoor exhibition room serves as a nature center with sculptures and installation artwork. The office has over 2,000 books on culture, art, philosophy, and religion and also 200 works by famous artists from across the globe.    Their spirit and the beauty of nature that can be appreciated here are enough reasons to visit Ami Art Museum. The stone wall around the gallery and its green lawn, the ivy on the museum’s white walls highlight each other in harmony. Visitors who come often take photos to remember their time here, which is very easy to do when every corner of the gallery is a photo spot. The whole school zone serves as the art museum, allowing visitors to stroll about as they enjoy the place. Over 700 works of art and the natural surroundings will make you feel like you’re going back in time. The old school building and the exquisitely-flowered trail are two must-visit spots. Ami Art Museum is not just an art gallery, but a place to take in some music, culture, and architecture as well. It also helps the local community through cultural experiences for those who do not otherwise have such opportunities. The art museum works to create original cultural content and art projects that appeal to local residents. Be sure to stop by to take photos of your day and indulge in culture and art!

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations-Yeongnangsa Temple
stories.script: Yeongnangsa Temple is nestled on Mount Yeongpa in Jingwan-ri, Dangjin. The temple is built on flat land, so access is very easy, and since it’s surrounded by mountains, the area is the perfect place for a walk. Samsunsan Arboretum is also right behind Yeongnangsa. Although the exact year it was built remains a mystery, it is said that construction is related to Princess Yeongnang, daughter of Tang Dynasty’s Taejong. Princess Yeongnang wanted to build a temple in the East, so she came to Dangjinpo to choose a site, where a temple was built and named after her. Inside, Daeungjeon Shrine and Dongjong Bell are Chungnam provincial cultural properties. Daeungjeon is a unique shrine combining the Dapojip and Jusimpo styles, while DongJong is a small bell (77.1 cm high) fabricated in 1759. Part of the bell shows elements that were in fashion during the Goryeo Era, showcasing its historic significance. The temple is the only one in Dangjin mentioned in Sinjeung Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam (1530), or The Geography of Korea, and which still exists to this day. How about pressing pause on your busy life and finding some peace in a forest? Yeongnangsa Temple is well-known for temple stay, where you can rest, meditate, practice zen, and take in some traditional Korean tea to bring refreshment and healing and ponder how we can make this world a better place. Could life be any more peaceful than this?

stories.title: Dangjin 10 locations-Pilgyeongsa Temple and Shim Hoon Memorial Museum
stories.audioTitle: Dangjin 10 locations-Pilgyeongsa Temple and Shim Hoon Memorial Museum
stories.script: Shim Hoon, a Korean novelist and poet, playwright and patriot returned to his parents’ house in Bugok-ri, Dangjin from Seoul in 1932 when Japanese oppression became harsher. He designed and built Pilgyeongsa Temple with writing fees that he had earned from his novel      Jiknyeoseong. He won Donga Ilbo’s 15th Anniversary Fiction Contest with another novel entitled Sangroksu, which he had finished in just 53 days since beginning on May 4, 1935. Pilgyeongsa means “to form a field with a pen,” highlighting the artistic spirit of Shim Hoon. The name is said to come from Shim Hoon’s literature collection, called Pilgyeongsa Jipgi. The temple has five rooms when viewed from the front, and two rooms from the side. It looks like a simple, cozy thatched-roof house, but inside it is designed like a modern house in the 1930s. Plants are on Pilgyeongsa’s terrace, while behind the temple is a bamboo forest. The artistic value of the place was recognized in 1997, when it was designated as Chungnam Monument No. 107 in December that year.  Next to Pilgyeongsa is Shim Hoon Memorial Museum, where you can trace back his life through his literary journey. Pictures of Shim Hoon writing at a desk can be seen, and photos can be taken “with” him, as if he has come back to life. There is also the large pen stand that Shim Hoon actually used when he was writing Sangroksu. On the museum’s exterior can be seen the text of one of his most famous poems, When That Day Comes. Recite the poem and you will feel his deep desire for national independence.  In order to celebrate Shim Hoon, a resistance poet and a leader of enlightenment fiction, the City of Dangjin has hosted Shim Hoon Literature Camp and Shim Hoon Sangrok Cultural Festival annually since 1977. Since 1996, the Shim Hoon Literary Award has been given for inspiring novelists every year.    Are you ready, then, to follow the literary journey of Shim Hoon, a talented author who passed away at the age of 35?

stories.title: Solmoe Shrine
stories.script: Birthplace of Saint Andreas Kim Daegon, Korea’s first Catholic priest -  Solmoe is a pure Korean word meaning, “mountain of pine trees.” It is where Korea’s first Catholic priest, Saint Andreas Kim Daegon was born, and where his great grandfather Kim Jinhoo, grandfather Kim Jonghan, father Kim Jejun, and he himself all lived, giving it the nickname, “Bethlehem of Korea.”  Saint Kim Daegon was born on August 21, 1821 in Solmoe Shrine and sent to a priest school in Macau at the age of 16 in 1837 by a French priest named Father Maubant, who came to Joseon dreaming of founding a seminary in the country. For the 4 ½ years he spent in Macau, Father Kim Daegon studied Latin, philosophy, and Catholic doctrine. He left the Portuguese port city in China in 1842 and returned secretly to Joseon to help fellow believers and write Catholic Persecution of the Joseon Dynasty. In 1845, he was ordained in Shanghai, becoming Korea’s first Catholic priest. He was arrested in June 1846 after returning to Joseon, was tortured on over 40 separate occasions, and sentenced to death on September 15 for treason. He was martyred the following day at the age of 25. Solmoe Shrine was the location for Catholic Asian Youth Day and received Pope Francis in 2014. The inspiring atmosphere still lingers around the shrine. The year 2021 is the 200th anniversary of the birth of Father Kim. To celebrate this event, UNESCO has designated him a universal figure. Why don’t we take a stroll on the pine trail around the shrine and appreciate the sculptures and feel the holy atmosphere of the place?

stories.title: Hapdeok Cathedral
stories.script: Chungcheong’s first Catholic church – capturing the history of the early Catholic church in Korea - Hapdeok Catholic church was originally Yangchon Cathedral and was built in Sanggung-ri, Yesan in 1890. The church expanded after purchasing land in 1899 where it is now and became Hapdeok Catholic church. In 1929, Father Perrin constructed the Gothic-styled brick church that exists today. In 1960, New Hapdeok Catholic church was built in another area and the original cathedral became known as “Former Hapdeok Catholic church.” However, in 1997, the original cathedral became “Hapdeok Catholic church” again.  The historic and architectural value of the cathedral was recognized and the building designated as Chungnam Monument No. 145 in 1998. Built on a low hill, the building of the cathedral features two bell towers—one on each front corner. On the front façade of the cathedral are three entrances and three windows, all arched in shape like rainbows. The outer walls are red brick, with grey brick forming the perimeter of the windows and corners of the bell towers. The bottom of each window and each side of the bell towers are decorated with grey bricks forming a rhombus. The cathedral has grown in popularity on social media as the location of several famous movies and TV series. A photo of you and your loved ones at the cathedral will make the perfect keepsake of your visit.

stories.title: Sinri Shrine
stories.script: The Catacomb of Joseon and Jeju Island of the Mainland - Sinri Shrine is where Saint Daveluy, the fifth Diocesan Bishop of Joseon, lived. St. Daveluy first arrived in Gangyeong with St. Kim Daegon in October 1845, spreading the gospel for 21 years until he was martyred in 1866 in Galmaemot. He stayed in the house of Thomas Son Chasun, a Korean Catholic martyr, and wrote religious books or translated them into Korean with the help of Luca Hwang Seokdu.  He also collected information on Catholic leaders and martyrs in Korea, which later became the foundation of Dallet’s Catholic History of Korea and the 103 saints. Sinri was also considered the most important communication channel amongst Catholics under their harsh persecution in Joseon. It was the largest gathering place for believers and assisted missionaries secretly reentering Korea. That’s why Sinri Shrine is called the “Catacomb of Joseon.” Sapkyocheon Stream allowed for close communication with the Paris Foreign Missions Society in China and the cultural openness of Naepo region helped Saint Daveluy play a significant role in Sinri. The Martyrs’ Art Museum, the only sacred painting gallery in Korea, can also be found at Sinri Shrine.
