stories.title: Hongyemun Gate
stories.script: Hongyemun Gate   Hongyemun Gate is a stone gate built like a tunnel by cutting Eungbongsan Mountain at its mountainside and neatly piling up 13 m-tall and 7 m-wide granite stonework. The construction began in 1906 and completed in 1908. The gate is designated as Incheon Metropolitan City Tangible Cultural Heritage No. 49. The gate was constructed by Japan that aimed to expand its domain towards Manseok-dong as the Japanese population in Jungang-dong and Gwan-dong of Incheon grew rapidly. It was called “Hyeolmun” whose Chinese characters mean “a hole gate” because the Japanese literally made a hole through the mountain to build it. Its homonym, “Hyeolmun, on the other hand, means “a blood gate,” which implies the painful past when countless Joseon workers were forced to sacrifice their lives and blood to construct the gate.   Thanks to its beautiful, rainbow-shaped appearance and unique atmosphere, Hongyemun Gate has been the filming site for a countless number of dramas, movies, and TV commercials. It makes you feel the subtle sentiments as if someone you have been missing is on the other side of the stone arch made of both granite and red bricks. Japanese architectural style of the gate stands out and the original appearance has been preserved quite well.   The passageway is too narrow that two cars cannot pass through it at the same time, but its enormous height, similar to that of a five-story building, boasts a unique form. As soon as you pass the Hongyemun Gate, you will see an uphill path on the left, and at the end of this road, a panoramic view of the downtown welcomes you. As we need to climb up a tough uphill in order to get to the top and feel the cool breeze, Hongyemun Gate having endured a sorrowful past now heads into the future as one of the famous attractions of Incheon today.

stories.title: Pailou at Chinatown Entrance
stories.script: Pailou at Chinatown Entrance     The 1st pailou (archway) of Chinatown that reads Junghwaga is one of the most notable symbols of Chinatown donated by the city of Weihai, the sister city of Incheon. Junghwaga means a street of Chinese people who are at the center of the world according to Sinocentrism. The 2nd pailou is Inhwamun Gate, which is located next to Korean-Chinese Cultural Center. The name of the pailou, which features a splendid gold-colored dragon pattern, means that virtuous and bright light spreads—it holds the wish for the prosperity of Chinatown.    The 3rd pailou is Seollinmun Gate located on the uphill from Chinatown towards Jayu Park. The name, Seollinmun, means that Korean and Chinese people shall live in harmony as close, intimate neighbors. The 4th pailou is Hanjungmun Gate located near the entrance of Chinatown from Fairy Tale Village. Its splendor stands out from the traditional harmony of colors between red and gold. Hanjungmun means the gate that connects Korea and China and through which one enters into the Little China within Korea.    When the 4th pailou by the entrance of Fairy Tale Village in Songwol-dong was completed, Chinatown has now the full formation of four pailous standing in all four directions. These pailous that encompass Chinatown not only are boundaries that mark the beginning and the end of Chinatown but also contain the hope of Chinese living abroad who pray for the town's prosperity.

stories.title: Korean-Chinese Cultural Center
stories.script: Korean-Chinese Cultural Center   Korean-Chinese Cultural Center is a Chinese architectural-style culture space established by the entrance to Chinatown. It consists of a basement floor and five ground floors, and various facilities are found on each of the floors: a special exhibition room on the 1st, Korean-Chinese Cultural Introductory Room on the 2nd, Public Relation Room for Sister Cities on the 3rd, and a theater on the 4th.   The gallery on the 1st floor hosts exchange exhibitions between Korea and China as well as exhibitions of various themes for the vitalization of cultural and artistic activities of local artists. It is also possible to rent the gallery.   The Korean-Chinese Culture Introductory Room on the 2nd floor introduces China's history, culture, economy, and social lives and also displays relics related to cultural exchanges between the two nations.   The 3rd floor is the Public Relation Room for Sister Cities where it introduces cities in China with which friendly relations are formed and donations have been exchanged. It also exhibits materials donated from each region. There is also a space prepared for visitors to experience qipao, the traditional Chinese dress, and tangram, a traditional Chinese play.  The theater on the 4th floor is available for rent for local artists’ performances, various seminars, or hearings.   The Incheon Overseas Chinese History Hall, which is connected to the 2nd floor of the Korean-Chinese Cultural Center, introduces the history of settlement in Incheon by overseas Chinese. It also hosts exhibitions of relics they actually used back in the days and various other themes related to the people and for the vitalization of cultural and artistic activities of local artists.

stories.title: Steps between Qing and Japanese Settlements
stories.audioTitle: Steps between Qing and Japanese Settlements
stories.script: Steps between Qing and Japanese Settlements   Steps between Qing and Japanese Settlements is the border between the Japanese concessions, which was installed in 1883, and the Qing concessions, which was installed a year later. It is a stone staircase surrounded by landscaped spaces on both sides. The left side was the Qing concessions so you will see Chinese-style buildings while the right was the Japanese concessions where Japanese-style structures stand. With the staircase of 130-year history dividing the settlements of both nations, you can see that buildings with vastly different styles are established.   If you look a little closer, you will notice the difference in the stone lanterns on the left and right sides, and these are Chinese and Japanese lanterns, respectively. A typical Korean stone lantern has a planar, octagonal shape whereas a Japanese stone lantern features gwolsu, which is a pattern that is rolled upward and attached like a little child’s fingers, at the tip of the stone stupa roof. A common Chinese stone lantern is rectangular in shape and is known for its fancy appearance.   At the top of the staircase, you will find the statue of Confucius, which was donated by the city of Chengdu, China. This is why the statue stands on the Chinese side of the stairs. Because of its value and historical significance, the staircase is designated as Incheon Metropolitan City Monument No. 51.

stories.title: Three Kingdoms Mural Street
stories.script: Three Kingdoms Mural Street   The Three Kingdoms Mural Street features 160 murals of notable scenes from the novel, Romance of the Three Kingdoms, and stories of the novel's key characters. The paintings are explained quite well that, as you take enough time, you will feel as if you have just read the entire novel.   The murals well-describe the famous stories we know from the book, including the Oath of the Peach Garden and the Battle of Red Cliffs. So as you walk along the walls and read the murals, the entire plot will naturally unfold in your mind. You can also enjoy the details of the novel in drawings and ancient idioms.   Whether you have read the story before or have never read it in your life, the Three Kingdoms Mural Street will present you a marvelous experience of reading a book through murals.

stories.title: Uiseondang Shrine
stories.script: Uiseondang Shrine   Uiseondang Shrine is a shrine that already opened under the name of Hwaeomsa in the 1850s prior to the opening of the Incheon Port (February 1883). The name changed to Uiseondang to educate overseas Chinese and help them adapt well to the life in a foreign land and live with righteousness. In the late Korean Empire period, the shrine was well-known as a training ground for Shaolin Temple martial arts, so many people regarded the place more as a temple than as a shrine. After the Korean War, the number of overseas Chinese, as well as visitors, began to decline. In the end, the shrine lost its religious function; instead, it was run as a studio for training Bagua (eight symbols used in Taoist cosmology) of the Wudang Sect. Fortunately with donations from overseas Chinese and the assistance of the Chinese government, the structure went through a renovation in May 2006 and has continued to maintain its appearance to this day.   Designed in the Taoist style from Shandong region, Uiseondang Shrine is estimated to have been built around 1893. The shrine has five statues: a statue of Avalokitesvara to which people pray for peace in the afterlife; the statue of Guan Yu, which is believed to grant wealth; the statue of Fairy Godmother Samsin who is supposed to bless with a child; the statue of Dragon King that looks after the well-being of ships traveling to and from China; and the statue of Fairy Godfather Hosan (mountain spirit) who protects long journeys and mountain trails.   The earthen statue made by exquisite workmanship inside the shrine is valuable cultural heritage that shows the late Qing style. The petite and simple pagoda displays a unique contrast to the fancy-patterned shrine. Uiseondang Shrine is smaller than you think that you could pass by it without even noticing. The shrine is a place you must visit if you wish to feel the unique traits of China as well as the life, culture, and religion of overseas Chinese after the opening of the port.

stories.title: Jjajangmyeon Museum
stories.script: Jjajangmyeon Museum   The Qing concessions installed by Chinese after the opening of the Incheon Port resulted in the establishment of many Chinese restaurants in the Chinatown area. As dock laborers who worked at the Incheon Port nearby looked for cheap, simple Chinese food, a dish called jjajangmyeon was invented. Unlike zhajiangmian, which is mixed with traditional Chinese soybean paste known as tianmian sauce, jjajangmyeon added sweet caramel and maintained a proper level of water to suit the palate of Koreans. An instant hit at the time, jjajangmyeon became one of the most popular Korean dishes.   Jjajangmyeon Museum was constructed at the site where the building of former Gonghwachun restaurant, the birthplace of Korean jjajangmyeon, had been torn down. This two-story brick building built on granite stonework is modern cultural heritage that shows the lives of overseas Chinese at the time. Gonghwachun, which initially developed jjajangmyeon, enjoyed great success as a leading Chinese restaurant of Chinatown. However, due to the government’s policies that restricted the overseas Chinese exercising their property rights, Gonghwachun eventually went out of business in 1983.   Jjajangmyeon Museum exhibits relics related to jjajangmyeon and Gonghwachun, and has replicated the kitchen and the reception room of the former restaurant. It provides nostalgia to overseas Chinese and middle-aged people living in Incheon while stimulating the younger generation’s curiosity in the modern food culture. After taking a tour of the museum, you can try different jjajangmyeon dishes at Chinese restaurants in addition to many other things to eat.

stories.title: Fairy Tale Village
stories.script: Fairy Tale Village   As a part of a residential environment improvement project in 2013, the entire Fairy Tale Village in Songwol-dong was painted with colors, and sculptures with themes of globally renowned children's stories were installed. With the creation of 11 themed roads such as Dorothy Road, Red Hat Road, and Traditional Fairy Tale Road, the village has become a famous attraction filled with tourists all year round.  Most of the houses and buildings are the real-life versions of those in fairy tales. The power pole transformed into a giant tree from Jack and the Beanstalk, and the gas meter is the Tin Man from The Wizard of Oz. If you go further into the village, you will see a mural road decorated with Korean folktales. As you take pictures in front of huge paintings, you will feel as if you have become the main character in the tales. Regardless of your age, you will surely make special memories at this place.  The “Trick Art Story” across the mural street is also an indispensable must-see place in the Fairytale Village. This two-story building has 39 visually entertaining three-dimensional paintings that present an interesting experience. It is an exhibition hall where two-dimensional drawings come to life in three dimensions. You should enjoy this exciting experience inside the paintings.

stories.title: Wolmi Theme Park
stories.script: Wolmi Theme Park   Wolmi Theme Park is filled with exciting music and delightful screams of young people. Many people visit the amusement park because they can enjoy different rides while looking at the sea. The DJs' fun banter makes the rides enjoyable for the people riding on them, and the whole scenery brings smiles to the faces of even the passersby.   When you ride the Viking at Wolmi Theme Park, you can look far out into the sea, and its slope is so great that it is said to be the most thrilling pirate ship ride in the country. Tagada Disco Pang brings joy and laughter to people on the ride and those watching them, thanks to the DJ's funny banter. The Ferris Wheel, which boasts a diameter of 110 m and a height of 115 m, offers a panoramic view of not only the Incheondaegyo Bridge and the sea in front of Incheon but also the distant Wolmisan Mountain, Incheon Floodgate, Incheon International Airport, Jagyakdo Island, and Palmido Island.   There are various amusement parks in operation in Wolmido Island so you can have a great time anywhere you go. If you have children, you can engage in different experiences and plays at parks for children. In summer, children can have fun time in the water zone.

stories.title: Wolmido Cruise
stories.script: Wolmido Cruise   There are two different courses for the Wolmido Cruise. Course A is a performance course that departs Wolmido Island and passes under the Yeongjongdaegyo Bridge and Ara Waterway West Sea Floodgate before returning to Wolmido Island. The course takes up about an hour and 20 minutes, and passengers can watch performances on the deck. Course B is a fireworks course that departs Wolmido Island and passes the sea in front of Yeongjongdo Island and under the Incheondaegyo Bridge before returning to the island. It takes about an hour and 30 minutes, and, while on the boat, you can enjoy fireworks and beautiful nightscape.  The New Cosmos, a 700-ton cruise ship, was built in 2017 with a capacity of 670 passengers. It consists of three floors: a restaurant and a performing stage on the 1st floor; a cafe, VIP rooms, and another stage on the 2nd floor, and; an outdoor performing stage on the deck and a terrace on the 3rd floor from which the sea of Incheon can be viewed. At the 3rd-floor observatory, you can see seagulls flocking over in the cool sea breeze.  On the Wolmido cruise, you can enjoy the Jeongseojin Ara Waterway, the West Sea, the Yeongjongdaegyo Bridge and various performances on board. While enjoying the freshness of the sea and the joys of the performances, you can make one more good memory on Wolmido Island.

stories.title: Waterfront of Wolmi Culture Street
stories.script: Waterfront of Wolmi Culture Street   The Waterfront of Wolmi Cultural Street was established by reclaiming 5,667 ㎡ of shared water in the front center of Wolmi Culture Street. With the space equipped with water-related facilities, people can freely get close to the water and enjoy sightseeing and relaxation.  The “Wolmi Moonlight Musical Fountain” at the center of the waterfront space presents a fountain show together with music, which is an interesting sight to see. There are also a cloud hill and tide and sunset observation decks, which are high-quality vista points where you can see the Incheondaegyo Bridge from the front with the sunset on the west coast in the backdrop. If you go down the water-friendly stairs on the waterside deck, you will find waves rocking back and forth. This will give you an opportunity to get familiar with the water while feeling the sea yourself in a water-friendly space.  As you walk further into the Culture Street, you will see an outdoor stage shaped like an origami crane with its back towards the sea. With the stage open to everyone, you can make a reservation to make the stage all yours. Why don’t you stop by the performances held on the outdoor stage, the Wolmi Fireworks Festival, or the September 15 Incheon Landing Operation Festival?

stories.title: Wolmido Lighthouse Road
stories.script: Wolmido Lighthouse Road   Wolmido Lighthouse Road is a stroll path set up along the breakwater road where the lighthouse is located. Regardless of the time of the day, you can take a walk while enjoying a beautiful scenery. You will see a lot of people hanging out in the area. You can also walk along while looking at photographs of the landscape and the history of Incheon and Wolmido Island displayed on the railings. On the trail, there is a photo zone shaped like a frame, and it is the best place to take photos with the lighthouse and sea in the background. The road is especially exquisite when you can see the red sunset, which is why it attracts many people around that time of the day. At night, the railings of the lighthouse are lit, turning the lighthouse road into a gorgeous one. While walking toward the lighthouse, take time to appreciate the scenery of the sea and listen to the sound of the waves. On your way back, enjoy the view of Wolmi Theme Park, as well as Wolmi Park. The Moon Eye Wheel in Wolmi Theme Park is also lit up at night, adding more excitement to the walking path.

stories.title: Wolmi Park
stories.script: Wolmi Park   Civilian access to Wolmisan Mountain was prohibited for 50 years due to a military unit stationed there, but it was finally open to the public in 2001. That is why Wolmi Park is known as one of the most well-preserved ecological parks. There are various kinds of natural plants, including sea pine, Sargent's cherry, and oak; wild animals such as raccoons, squirrels, and elk; and different types of birds such as the long-tailed tit, Oriental tit, and varied tit.  Wolmi Forest once was a battleground among Western powerhouses and the starting point of Operation Chromite. If you look closer at the trees in Wolmi Forest, the young roots have been cut off; instead, numerous branches have grown to form large trees. The trees also show war wounds like chopped branches, split trunks, and debris from bombs lodged in the roots. As you will be overwhelmed by the trees that have become stronger and more beautiful as they have overcome the pains of war, you can learn the lessons that nature and history have to offer.  There is a Korean traditional garden that was created according to the city's park development plan when Wolmi Park was opened. The garden consists of Palace Garden, Byeolseo Garden, and Private Family Garden. In the Palace Garden, you can find the Buyongji Pond of Changdeokgung Palace; Aeryeonji Pond filled with lotus flowers; Amisan Chimney, and; a tiered garden. The Byeolseo Garden has Gukdamwon Garden, Soswaewon Garden, and Seoseokji. In the Private Family Garden, there are various attractions such as Yangjindang House and thatched houses of the traditional architectural style, as well as artificial ponds, streams, and rice paddies.

stories.title: Wolmi Cultural Center
stories.script: Wolmi Cultural Center   At the entrance of Wolmi Cultural Center, there is a wish postcard box and a slow mailbox. If you write a wish postcard to your loved ones and place it in the slow mailbox, the postcard will be sent out after a year. It will be a memorable experience to write a postcard that will arrive at the recipient one year later. Imagine how surprised he or she must be!  The 1st floor of the Wolmi Cultural Center is a traditional and cultural exhibition hall, which consists of a living culture exhibition room, a palace culture exhibition room, and a planned exhibition room. You can see ceremonies such as Gwanhonsangje, which refer to the four ceremonial occasions of coming of age, wedding, funeral, and ancestral rites; educational courses such as seodang (village school) and hyanggyo (local Confucian school); court music and court food, and the king's competitions and routines. You can also try on hanbok, the Korean traditional attire. Traditional wedding clothes, royal court clothes, shoes, and gachae (wig) are also available.  You can participate in Korean food making and tasting activities at the Korean Food Experience Center in the basement floor. You can encounter diverse experiences using traditional rice cakes, kimchi, royal samgyetang, royal tteokbokki, and bulgogi. You may participate in these activities after making a reservation.

stories.title: Wolmi Observatory
stories.script: Wolmi Observatory   Wolmi Observatory is where you can view the Incheon Port, the Incheondaegyo Bridge, and Incheon Coastal Passenger Terminal. Don't miss the chance to see the spectacular sunset of the West Sea. It takes about 30 minutes on foot to the top of Wolmisan Mountain (108 m) and 15 minutes if you ride the shuttle bus called the seal car.  As you climb the circular stairs of the Wolmi Observatory, you can see the West Sea with its blue waves and the Incheon Port below you. And in front of your eyes lies downtown Incheon and Jayu Park. You may enjoy a relaxing time with a cup of coffee at the observatory cafe, and you can also check out the square on top of Wolmisan Mountain and Yepo Square near the observatory.  Located at the top of Wolmisan Mountain, the observatory welcomes many people who come to view the Incheon Port, the surrounding islands, and the scenery. It is especially famous for magnificent night views. The 23 m, three story-high glass observatory offers a fantastic atmosphere at night; it is considered as one of the most romantic date spots.

stories.title: The Museum of Korea Emigration History
stories.audioTitle: The Museum of Korea Emigration History
stories.script: The Museum of Korea Emigration History   Exchanges with other countries are common these days; however, a century ago, the only means of transportation was ship, so foreign exchanges were a bit challenging. Incheon, which was the country’s first hub for maritime exchanges, is also where Korea's first official emigrant departed. The history of Korean emigration began in 1902 when the first official emigrant left for Hawaii on a ship.  In the museum's exhibition room, you can see the model of the ship Gaelic, which left for Hawaii at the time, as well as the painful looks of our ancestors who lived harder and with more determination than anyone else. In each of the four exhibition rooms, you can learn about the long and difficult journey of emigrants who left for Hawaii, the hard labor at sugar cane farms, the process of settling in Hawaii, the activities of the ancestors who devoted themselves to national liberation, and the current situation and hopes of overseas Koreans.  At the Museum of Korea Emigration History, you will also find our proud ancestors who sacrificed their lives for Korea's independence even in the midst of the hardships they faced. It is a valuable place where you can examine the emigration history and also learn the traits of pioneers.

stories.title: Incheon Port Floodgate
stories.script: Incheon Port Floodgate   The Incheon Port Floodgate has a high stature as the country's first and the largest of its kind in Asia. It was initially constructed to overcome the large ebb and flow of the tide of the sea in front of Incheon. An embankment was built to create Inner Port of Incheon, and a floodgate, a structure serving as the entrance to the Inner Port, was also constructed. The structure that connects the Outer Port and Inner Port of Incheon is the Incheon Port Floodgate. When a ship is on standby at the outer port, the water level is adjusted to open the water gate on the outer port side, and when the ship enters, the water gate is closed again to set the water level back to the original state. Then, the water gate on the inner port is opened to allow the vessel to enter.   When you visit the Exhibition Center for the Lock Gate of Incheon Port, you can learn about the principle of how a floodgate operates through various experiences, including videos played at the exhibition hall on the 4th floor. At the outdoor park on the same floor, you may enjoy the view of the Incheon Port Floodgate and the ships passing through it. The 5th floor observatory greets you with a panoramic view of the floodgate and the inner port, and you can also enjoy distant scenery through a telescope.   Once a year on Children's Day in May, the floodgate is open to the general public. Within the floodgate landscape area, families can relax and watch large cargo ships and passenger vessels passing through the gate. It will be a novel experience through which you see surprisingly huge ships, container boxes, and various items scheduled for export.

stories.title: Ocean Plaza at Yeonan Pier
stories.script: Ocean Plaza at Yeonan Pier  A rest area at city-center where waves rock back and forth  In the Ocean Plaza, there stands a seven-story Ocean Plaza Observatory Tower. The building features a ticket office for cruise ships going to Palmido Island as well as a cafe and an observatory. When you climb up to the observation deck, you can enjoy a panoramic view of the Yeonan Pier and the West Sea and also feel the energy of the fish market and the unique atmosphere of the port from which ships set out on the Yeonan sea route.  The Ocean Plaza features memorial monuments and matryoshka doll sculptures that commemorate the 100th anniversary of the Russo-Japanese War and the Russian soldiers who died in the sea in front of Incheon. You will also see St. Petersburg Plaza named after the city in Russia. In commemoration of the signing of an agreement between Incheon and St. Petersburg, both cities established a plaza named after each other to signify friendship and appreciation for each other. Thus, there is St. Petersburg Plaza in Incheon while there is also Incheon Plaza in St. Petersburg.  On one side of St. Petersburg Plaza, there is an outdoor performing stage, water play facility, and a musical fountain. The water play facility harmonizes well with the surrounding space, and it can be used as a typical playground in non-summer seasons. The musical fountain features fountain and sculptures in the shapes of scallop, octopus, islands, music, seagulls, water sprays, and seaweed with the West Sea in the backdrop. The fountain shows off fantastic dance moves to colorful lighting and exciting rhythm, and it is always crowded with families and lovers.

stories.title: Deep sea fishing
stories.script: Deep sea fishing Thrilling, unforgettable sensation on hands  If you plan to fish in the sea, you must get a full checklist, which includes the weather, date of departure, tides, and fishing conditions. After making a reservation of a boat, pack your fishing rod, fishing line, fish box, and bait and wear appropriate clothing. Arrive one hour prior to the departure time to prepare for boarding. If you pay a certain fee when going out for deep sea fishing, you may be provided with fishing gear, bait, and meal on board. Once you are on the sea, you just need to follow the ship’s rules and fishing etiquette and enjoy fishing!  When sea fishing, you must keep in mind that you should target the kind of fish that is caught the most and easiest during the particular season. As Korea is surrounded by waters on three sides, different fish species circulate in each season. In the West Sea, in particular, spring fishing begins late so you can catch sea bass, flounder, rockfish, fat greenling, ridged-eye flounder, and blackhead seabream only in May. During summer, you will see many red seabream, flathead grey mullet, and Pacific cod. Fall is the best season for fishing because in addition to the fish species you can catch in spring and summer, you can also find more species such as dotted gizzard shad, Japanese seerfish, Japanese halfbeak, mackerel, webfoot octopus, and common cuttlefish. Although it is quite tricky to go fishing in the West Sea during winter, fishing along breakwater provides another way to enjoy the sensation on your hands.  Even without going out the sea, you can still rent a fishing rod and set up a fishing chair near the Yeonan Pier. It is where even fishing novices can sufficiently enjoy fishing. Even if you caught nothing, don't be too disappointed. There is a fish market nearby where you can enjoy fresh marine products, the Yeonan Pier Plaza with many different things to see, and numerous tourist attractions.

stories.title: Sliced Raw Large-eyed Herring Street
stories.script: Sliced Raw Large-eyed Herring Street Sliced raw large-eyed herring, a popular menu of Yeonan Pier  The most popular menu on the Sliced Raw Large-eyed Herring Street, given by its name, is sliced raw large-eyed herring. The best part of this dish is that it has an affordable price and it is an all-season dish. sliced raw large-eyed herring is served with sweet and sour red chili pepper paste with vinegar and vegetables like cabbage, parsley, carrots and onions. It is a delicacy if you mix it with rice, just like a raw fish bibimbap. Its red seasoning is not too spicy, and its sweet-and-sour flavor harmonizes well with the savory taste of large-eyed herring. Together with marinated crab, vegetables and various other side dishes, you can enjoy a hearty meal of sliced raw large-eyed herring.  People say that grilled large-eyed herring is as delicious as grilled dotted gizzard shad in autumn. While grilled dotted gizzard shad is enjoyed in fall, grilled large-eyed herring represents the spring season. Its fatty flesh has an excellent savory taste. Grilled large-eyed herring is covered in coarse salt and grilled and served. You can enjoy its salty and savory taste by eating it whole from its head without removing the fine bones.  The sliced raw fish dish can only be made by domestic large-eyed herring, because it tends to die as soon as it gets caught. So, this species cannot be farmed for research purposes or be brought fresh from another region. large-eyed herring is from the herring family, and it is difficult for even fishermen to find a large-eyed herring that is alive because it dies almost as soon as it is caught—similar to any other fish of the herring family. You can get only one piece of the raw fish, each from the left and right sides of the spine, from a single large-eyed herring. If you eat it with ssamjang sauce, the savory taste increases twofold compared to other sauces. Depending on your preference, you can choose white-meat large-eyed herring if you like fresh sliced raw fish that has a simple and savory taste or the red-meat large-eyed herring if you prefer a sweeter and deeper taste.

stories.title: Incheon Fish Market
stories.script: Incheon Fish Market A fish market filled with fresh seafood caught in the West Sea  The Incheon Fish Market supplies fresh seafood, which is captured by Incheon fishermen near the West Coast. It is the only market in the metropolitan area and the biggest seafood distribution market in Korea. The vast West Sea of Incheon overflows with diverse and abundant fishery resources, which allows you to taste seafood that you do not often see or eat at reasonable prices. Moreover, the market is located close the Yeonan Pier, and there are many notable tourist attractions nearby.  The Incheon Fish Market supplies fresh seafood, which is captured by Incheon fishermen near the West Coast. It is the only market in the metropolitan area and the biggest seafood distribution market in Korea. The vast West Sea of Incheon overflows with diverse and abundant fishery resources, which allows you to taste seafood that you do not often see or eat at reasonable prices. Moreover, the market is located close the Yeonan Pier, and there are many notable tourist attractions nearby.  The most popular and famous marine product from the West Sea is the blue crab. The blue crab, which represents the fish market, is the most delicious between April and May and October and November when it contains much meat. If you get to visit during this season, you have to try blue crabs filled with an abundant nutrition of the coast near the West Sea.

stories.title: Palmido Island
stories.script: Palmido Island The island with the first lighthouse in the country  You can visit Palmido Island by taking the Palmido Cruise Ship from the Yeonan Pier. In the past, the scene of fishing boats returning from Palmido Island while waving flags that indicate full loads of fish was regarded as the eighth scenic view of Palmido Island, among the Eight Scenic Views of Yongyudo Island. The white lighthouse standing tall on the island by the entrance to Incheon Port serves as an indicator for the safe operation of ships entering and leaving the port. The Palmido Lighthouse in the past was designated as Incheon Tangible Cultural Heritage No. 40 upon completion of its duties over a century. Currently, a new lighthouse has taken its place.  The Palmido Island cruise ship departs from the Yeonan Pier and passes under Incheondaegyo Bridge until it arrives at the island. It takes about 50 minutes one way and operates three times a day. The Palmido-bound “Golden Fish” cruise ship was first introduced in 2015. Its face resembles a tiger, its body a fish, and the entire appearance a killer whale. This 196-ton ship has a maximum capacity of 203 passengers. The 1st floor has a karaoke room and a snack store while the 2nd floor has seats for groups of two to three. There is an outdoor rooftop observation deck on the 3rd floor.  Built in June 1903, the Palmido Lighthouse is the first modern lighthouse in Korea. It is located 71 m above sea level and is 7.9 m high with a diameter of about 2 m. During the Korean War, the KLO members (an anti-spy unit) recovered this lighthouse and turned on the light on September 15, 1950. The lighthouse also served as a guide to the success of Operation Chromite. When you visit the Palmido Lighthouse History Hall that highlights the historical value of the lighthouse, you can see how the Incheon Port has changed over the years.

stories.title: Yonggungsa Temple
stories.script: Yonggungsa Temple The temple that has protected Yeongjongdo Island since the Unified Silla Dynasty City Tangible Cultural Property No. 15  According to records, Yonggungsa Temple was established by Won Hyo in the 10th year of King Munmu's reign (670) in Silla. It was then rebuilt by Heungseon Daewongun in the 5th year of King Cheoljong's reign (1854) during the Joseon Dynasty, until it got its current name. In front of the Yosachae House located at the entrance of Yonggungsa Temple, there is a plaque that reads “Yonggungsa,” which as written by Heungseon Daewon himself.  The Gwaneumjeon Hall of Yonggungsa Temple was built as a house with a gambrel roof whose side looks like a walking man, and on the pillars, there remain four verse couplets written by Haegang Kim Gyu-jin. It is said that there used to be a Gwanyin Statue carved with jade in the hall, but it was stolen during the Japanese occupation period. Now, the hall enshrines a bronze Gwanyin Statue.  In front of Yonggungsa Guesthouse, a zelkova tree estimated to be about 1,300 years old still stands. The Yonggungsa zelkova tree, which is Incheon City Monument No. 9, is an enormous, 20m-tall tree with a circumference of 5.63 m, and it is also known as the grandfather or grandmother tree.

stories.title: Prehistoric monuments: Monument of Yang Juseong
stories.audioTitle: Prehistoric monuments: Monument of Yang Juseong
stories.script: Prehistoric monuments: Monument of Yang Juseong  14 monuments that hold the history and spirit of the time City Designated Cultural Property Monument No. 13  A number of monuments are gathered in front of the  Yeongjong-dong Senior Center. These are a collection of monuments that had been scattered throughout Yeongjongdo Island, and these were monuments of gratitude towards and historical records about cheomsa and cheomjeoljesa, which were public officials of Yeongjongdo Island.  Among these monuments, the Monument of Yang Juseong is a memorial to Yang Juseong who restored Yeongjongjinsa after it was burned to ashes by Japanese warships in the 12th year of King Gojong's reign (1875). He is also the one who strengthened the defense capabilities of Yeongjongjinsa together with various other meritorious deeds.  The monument, which is 91 cm high, 31 cm wide, and 3 cm thick, is long, rectangular in shape and has a simple form with polished, round upper corners. Because it is made of metal, the Monument of Yang Juseong possesses an extremely high value in terms of cultural preservation.

stories.title: Incheon Student Science Museum
stories.script: Incheon Student Science Museum An Incheon education site aimed at fostering wise, warm-hearted, global talents  The Incheon Education Science and Informatics Institute operates the Incheon Student Science Museum to help build expertise in science education at schools and to expand and spread scientific thinking. The Incheon Student Science Museum offers five exhibition halls: Kkumdori Hall, Natural History Exploration Hall, Basic Science Experience Hall, Future Science Hall, and Science Experience Hall.  The museum runs a variety of programs for all students, from elementary school to high school. The programs do not merely offer things to see and hear; rather, they allow children to touch, feel and experience the basic science principles, encouraging them gain more interest in future science.  The Incheon Student Science Museum operates an astronomical projection room where you can observe celestial objects and events through a large hemispherical dome screen. Moreover, there is a traditional science learning center, a rock learning center, and a hands-on learning center to lead the development of talents in science and popularization of science.

stories.title: Incheon Bridge Exhibition Center
stories.script: Incheon Bridge Exhibition Center Incheondaegyo Bridge, a bridge to the world  The Incheon Bridge Exhibition Center is a four-story building that not only shows the construction process of the bridge but also features various facilities, including spaces for experiences and rest, and an observatory. Located at the entrance of the bridge, the exhibition center is a special place where you can witness the excellence of Incheondaegyo Bridge.  On the 1st floor, you will see a brief introduction to the exhibition center along with a cafe for relaxation. There are also archives about Incheondaegyo Bridge's unique structure, including a project overview and history, as well as the awards that the bridge has obtained so far. The 2nd floor is where one can feel the robustness of the bridge's high-tech cables through a miniature bridge and various samples. The 3rd floor has a rest area and an experience space while the 4th floor features an observatory from which you can view the sea, Incheondaegyo Bridge, and downtown Incheon through a telescope.  From the observatory located on the 4th floor, you can also get a full view of the bridge and the beautiful sea, and you can also check out the key infrastructures of Incheon along the horizon, including Wolmisan Observatory, Incheon Port, Cheongnyangsan Observatory, Songdo Central Park, Northeast Asia Trade Center and many more.

stories.title: BMW Driving Center
stories.script: BMW Driving Center A unique place for automobile enthusiasts  The BMW Driving Center provides a variety of experiences. The Brand Experience Center exhibits BMW, Mini, and Motorrad vehicles as well as classic cars from the history of BMW. Here, you can check out and test-drive BMW cars and create unforgettable memories.  The driving track inside the center gives you a chance to perform systematic and professional driving. It offers a total of six courses, and visitors can get a chance to safely ride BMW and Mini vehicles on tracks that follow the International Automobile Federation (FIA) standards.  The BMW Driving Center also operates Junior Campus for children. Junior Campus has a laboratory, a workshop, and Kids Driving School, all of which can be experienced by making a reservation. It consists of programs through which children can explore various basic principles of science related to cars and understand eco-friendly energy. The Kids Driving School offers traffic safety education and driving experiences to help preschoolers understand traffic laws in different traffic situations.

stories.title: Yeongjong History Museum
stories.script: Yeongjong History Museum A cultural space holding the history and life culture of Yeongjongdo Island  From the prehistoric times to the present of Yeongjong Island! The Yeongjong History Museum tells the history and living cultures of Yeongjong Island all the way from the prehistoric times to the Goryeo and Joseon Dynasties and the modern era. In Exhibition Hall 1, you can examine the history and culture of Yeongjongdo Island from the prehistoric period to the Goryeo Dynasty while Exhibition Hall 2 displays everything from the Joseon Dynasty to the modern and contemporary era. Here, relics and artifacts from the prehistoric period, which were excavated during various development projects that began with the construction of Incheon International Airport, are on display. In addition, you can learn about the conflicts with foreign powers that took place off the coast of Yeongjongjin as well as the progress from the modern to contemporary periods. It also exhibits the scenes of work and life of the residents and Yeongjongdo Island on which urban development projects are on-going. In addition to the permanent exhibitions, it hosts special exhibitions and various educational programs to re-emphasize and promulgate the history and cultural values of the island.  Though an island, Yeongjongdo Island has open access in all routes, from air and sea to land. Normally, people come via Yeongjongdaegyo Bridge or Incheondaegyo Bridge by car, but the Yeongjong History Museum can be accessed more easily and conveniently via sea. You can also travel on a ship from Wolmido Island to Yeongjongdo Island, or vice versa. You can travel with your car loaded on a ship, if you prefer more convenience. Yeongjongdo and Wolmido are about 2 km apart from each other, so it is possible to get from one island to another in about 15 minutes by cruise ship. There is about one boat operating every hour, and the fee is inexpensive as well. If you travel at the right time, you may view the sea together with seagulls on your way to or from Yeongjongdo Island, which adds more fun to a nice trip. You may get on a ship by purchasing a ticket at Gueup Baeteo on Yeongjongdo Island or at Wolmido Quay on Wolmido Island.

stories.title: Seaside Park
stories.script: Seaside Park An urban rest area featuring rail bikes  The Seaside Park is divided into Sea Breeze Garden, Saltern Pond Garden, Waterfront, Songsan Mountain, Sky Cloud Square, and Yeongjongjin. The park features various sports facilities and playgrounds as well as an artificial rock waterfall, an outdoor performing stage, a sculpture fountain, an observatory, and a number of sculptures. Since it is a sea park, it also has a water playground, foot baths, a tidal flat, and even a saltern warehouse. Here you can enjoy a variety of things to see and a panoramic view of the sea at the same time.  In the middle of the Seaside Park, there are grounds for general camping and caravan camping. These campsites are located on the coast of Songsan Mountain, so they are seated right next to the waters. They are equipped with a natural environment within the city center, offering you a unique camping compared to other automobile camping grounds. Bicycle roads are also well-established, and you can rent water bikes.  Incheon's one and only rail bikes are also available here. It is a 5.6 km round-trip course that cuts across the park, and while stepping on the pedals of the four-seated rail bikes, you can get a view of the West Sea and its features such as Wolmido Island, Songdo, and Incheondaegyo Bridge. Scenic waterfalls and various elements are installed along the path to offer a different level of excitement.

stories.title: Incheon International Airport
stories.script: Incheon International Airport No. 1 airport where an exciting journey begins  Incheon International Airport is the country’s largest international airport opened on March 29, 2001. Thanks to its continuous developments, the airport has been selected for 12 consecutive years as the World's Best Airport Services. It is also a global airport with the 7th busiest airport by international passenger traffic and 2nd busiest airport by international cargo traffic.  Incheon International Airport was the outcome of Korea's greatest construction project ever and was built by reclaiming the tideland between Yeongjongdo and Yongyudo Islands. Eight years after the commencement of a breakwater construction project in 1992, the airport finally came to a historic moment on March 29, 2001 when it first opened. Incheon International Airport resulted in an airport comparable with any of the world's best airports. A few years after its opening, the second phase of the construction project began to meet the skyrocketing flight demands that surpassed anyone's expectations and to leap as a hub airport of Northeast Asia. As a result, Incheon International Airport Terminal 2 started its operation in 2018.  Incheon International Airport features a variety of convenience facilities for passengers and transit passengers and offers numerous attractions and entertainment, including themed events and exhibitions, cultural performances, and Korean culture experience spaces. With diverse experiences offered to passengers, the airport ranks one of the highest customer satisfaction worldwide.

stories.title: Wangsan Marina
stories.script: Wangsan Marina The center of Korea's largest marine leisure sports  Wangsan Marina hosted the yacht events at the 2014 Asian Games. Since then, it had only opened partially and operated a small number of facilities, but recently, all of the facilities were opened to the public. The largest yachting ground in the country, the center can accommodate 300 yachts in 266 wet docks and 34 dry docks. It is equipped with docks of various sizes to accommodate boats and ships of different sizes from 35 feet to 165 feet in length. In particular, Wangsan Marina is established offshore, so it has excellent access to the sea and makes it possible for boats and ships to enter and depart 365 days a year. It is a must-visit place for those who love water sports like yachting and boating.  With the official opening of Wangsan Marina, various convenience facilities, such as accommodations, sales facilities, yacht repair shops, and club houses, are being established. Here you can watch cool yachts that you could not normally encounter as much as you want. The place is full of spectacular facilities such as wet docks, as well as anchored yachts, a breakwater, a coastal road, and a lighthouse. In the future, you will also be able to rent and experience yachts, so it would be nice for you to get a first-hand experience of the water sports yourself.  Wangsan Marina boasts a remarkable natural environment as it is surrounded by Wangsan and Eurwang-ri Beaches and several islands. In particular, the tunnel at the entrance is a wonderful vista point from which you can see Wangsan Marina at a glance. If you come around sunset, you will get a chance to see a beautiful sunset at Wangsan Beach, which is considered the best among the Eight Scenic Views of Yongyudo Island.

stories.title: Eurwang-ri and Wangsan Beaches
stories.script: Eurwang-ri and Wangsan Beaches The nearest beaches from the city that will leave you awestruck  The most famous beaches of Yongyudo Island: Eurwang-ri and Wangsan Beaches When summer approaches, the most preferred vacation spot is the beach. Eulwang-ri Beach and Wangsan Beach are especially loved by many as they are the nearest to Incheon and boast a magnificent scenery. They are popular because they are convenient for one-day trips and are easily accessible using public transportation. Here you can experience sandy beaches and tidal flats at the same time, and the scenery of the beach and the sunset is extremely gorgeous. The water is not that deep and the slope is gentle, which makes it a safe place to play in the water. Families with children visit Eurwang-ri Beach and Wangsan Beach. The two beaches are close by, located at about a 5-minute distance from each other. Despite their close proximity, the scenery and atmosphere of the two are quite different. You can and choose the one you like better after considering the characteristics of each beach, or you can simply visit both since they are very close to each other.

stories.title: House of Jo Byeong-su
stories.script: House of Jo Byeong-su A traditional house that holds 120 years of history and the spirit of the independence movement City Cultural Heritage Material No. 16  The House of Jo Byeong-su is a typical middle-class residence with a middle molding located on an island in the West Sea. It consists of two buildings, the “ㄱ”-shaped daemunchae and anchae, so the house is of a “ㅁ” structure that is open on one side. Anchae features three cells on the front and 1.5 cells on the side. From daecheong (the main floored room) with a narrow toenmaru (a narrow wooden porch) installed, a long, two-cell main room that runs north and south is set up on the western side and a one-cell room to the east. In front of the room, a toenmaru with a raised bottom is placed, and there is a space in the back that was built to place a closet. A spacious kitchen that covers two cells is attached to the main room, and the ceiling on the cell toward the main room was lowered to create an attic accessed from the main room. This kind of floor plan is a typical central region-style residence commonly found in Gyeonggi-do and Chungcheong-do Provinces. It is also unique that the upper part of the middle molding above the front gate is plastered and has an octagonal lattice window.  The House of Jo Byeong-su is also known as the place where independence activists of Yongyudo Island planned the March 28th Independence Movement just after the March 1st Movement in 1919. Jo Myeong-won, one of Jo's uncles, attended the Declaration of Independence in Seoul in 1919 before returning to Yongyudo Island. It is said that the house's sarangchae, a guest house, was used to form a secret anti-Japanese group known as Hyeolseongdan together with Jo Jong-seo, Mun Mu-hyeon, and Choe Bong-hak. Here, they planned the March 28th Independence Movement. The March 28th Independence Movement happened on March 28, 1919. It is a demonstration for national independence led by Jo Myeong-won and the Hyeolseongdan members with over 150 island residents joining the movement.  Seen from the history, the House of Jo Byeong-su is filled with tradition and history feels that much more enticing as it still serves as an actual residence. The house is also operated as a guest house where visitors can have a hanok stay experience. It is not far from Incheon International Airport, so it is a popular attraction to visit for foreigners who wish to experience Korean traditional houses.

stories.title: Seonnyeo Rock
stories.script: Seonnyeo Rock The third scenic view of Yongyudo Island, a rock with a sad legend  Seonnyeobawi Beach, located on the way to Eurwang-ri Beach, is full of strange and peculiar rocks. Among them, Seonnyeo Rock stands taller than the rest out of the waters. The sharp rock harmonizes well with the seascape, and the waves that gently crash into the rock create a spectacular view. It is also considered as the four lands of life where many tourists visit to see the sunset. A small dock located in the back of Seonnyeo Rock features small, old fishing boats and fishermen, creating a simple yet breathtaking scenery of a countryside fishing village.  Seonnyeo Rock has a sad legend that has been passed down for generations. There was a hogun, a military commander, who oversaw the naval forces of Yeongjongjin. He had a concubine, but when their romantic relationship ended, the woman threw herself into the sea from a rock called Taepyeongam Rock in Yeongjongjin. No one collected her body so it floated near a port of Yongyudo Island. Regretting the past, the hogun buried her body years after. After the incident, Taepyeongam Rock from which the woman ended her life began to be known as Seonnyeo Rock, and it became a place where seonnyeo, or fairies, came down on a rainbow to play when the night was clear. It is also said that the rock resembles a praying woman, so if you make a wish here, it will come true.  Seonnyeobawi Beach is an attractive place from which you can see Seonnyeo Rock and other unique-shaped rocks. The view of the sea is wide open, and the beach is relatively quieter and calmer than others. It is recommended to visit other famous beaches nearby, including Eurwang-ri and Wangsan Beaches. If you get the chance to see Seonnyeo Rock, the third scenic view of Yongyudo Island, take time to enjoy the beautiful sunset, and your day will be even more perfect.

stories.title: March First Independence Movement Monument
stories.script: March First Independence Movement Monument Cries for national independence echoing throughout Yongyu-myeon  Between March 23rd and 24th in 1919, Jo Jong-seo, Mun Mu-hyeon, Choe Bong-hak and others who lived in Nambuk-ri, Yongyu-myeon, Bucheon-gun gathered at the house of Jo Myeong-won to form a secret association known as Hyeolseongdan and plan an independence movement. They resolved to carry out the plan on March 28th and made a Korean national flag out of cotton. Meanwhile, four people, including Jo Jung-seo, wrote about 80 letters that said, We will carry out the independence movement for our country, Joseon, so gather in the Gwancheong-ri Square on the 28th.'' The letters were distributed to each village.  On March 28th, the four leaders and representatives of each region—Yun Chi-bang, Kim Yun-bae, Yun Bo-shin, Yu Ung-ryeol, Gu Gil-seo and O Gi-seop—gathered in the Gwancheong-ri Square and carried out the demonstration for independence. Soon after, around 150 residents responded to the movement and started waving the Korean flags that they had made in advance, crying out for independence. As a result, 11 people, including Jo Myeong-won, were arrested and spent some time in prison. This series of events are recorded in the Judgment of 11 people including Jo Myeong-won, the Judgment of 10 people including Jo Myeong-won, and five volumes of the Independence Movement History Data Book.  At the entrance of the village, there stands a monument in remembrance of the independence movement. A myeon office used to be located at the three-way intersection of the village, and people called the area in front of the myeon office the Gwancheong-ri Square. You can see this is where the national independence movement took place. Residents of Deokgyo-dong, Incheon erected this monument on March 28, 1983 to commemorate the protest for independence that occurred in Yongyu-myeon. The monument's foundation is 1.5 m high, and the height of the monument is 2.9 m.

stories.title: Masian Beach and Jamjin-Muui Suspension Bridge
stories.audioTitle: Masian Beach and Jamjin-Muui Suspension Bridge
stories.script: Masian Beach and Jamjin-Muui Suspension Bridge Enjoy the sandy beach and tidal flat before going off to Muuido Island!  Encounter two different charms—a beach and a tidal flat Masian Beach boasts a long, 3 km beach. The sandy beach and pine trees along the beach creates a magnificent harmony that the beach is regarded as the fourth of the Eight Scenic Views of Yongyudo Island. There are many islands near the beach such as Jamjindo, Muuido and Silmido Islands, so you can enjoy a leisurely walk along the beach and enjoy the beatiful scenery. Masian Beach was called “Masian,” the old word for a saddle, because of the beach resembling a saddle. Its official name is “Masiran.” It becomes a sandy beach when water comes in, and once the water recedes, a vast tidal flat unfolds before you. It is a beach of two different charms where you can enjoy both sea bathing and the tidal flat experience. In particular, the tidal flat of Masian Beach is famous for its vastness that seems like it has no end. Also, the land is fertile and the tidal flat ecosystem is well established, which is why it is inhabited by many sea creatures. Masian tidal flats can only be enjoyed when the water recedes, so make sure to check the tide before going in. At the Masian Tideland Experience, you can rent equipment and participate in a clam digging experience. Here you can catch not only clams such as surf clams, Manila clams, and whelk but also webfoot octopus and small octopus. In addition, you can enjoy bare-handed fishing called Eojeon Imtong and ride a tidal flat carriage to drive through the tidal flat.

stories.title: Hanagae Recreation Area
stories.script: Hanagae Recreation Area A beach that represents Muuido Island  The Hanagae Recreation Area is one of the most popular attractions of Muuido Island along with the West Sea. From sea bathing and tidal flat experience to sea fishing and water sports, there are a variety of things to enjoy here. Hanagae Beach, whose name means that it is the largest tidal flat on the island, is a 1.5 km-long beach covered with fine-grained sand that feels just like flour. During high tide, the bungalows by the beach provide a unique experience as if you are in a floating house. With the beach facing towards the west, you can see the sun coloring the waters red as it sets into the sea.  The native villages here, Ponae Fishing Village and Kachinol Island Village, are traditional rural-themed towns where you can spend nights at these villages. They offer various programs including tidal flat experience, clam fishing, and deep sea fishing as well as an opportunity to share the warm affection with the village residents. In particular, if you go out to the tidal flat and just dig a little bit during low tide, you can catch as much clams as you want, from surf clams to turban shells, crabs, and Manila clams.  The recreation area also offers other experiences such as horseback riding, four-wheeled motorcycle riding, and Sea Sky World. Sea Sky World is a new-breed extreme leisure sports where you go down on a 413 m-long wire connected from a 25 m-high steel tower over the white sandy beach.

stories.title: Guksabong Peak and Horyonggoksan Mountain
stories.script: Guksabong Peak and Horyonggoksan Mountain A fantastic hiking trail while looking at the sea  After passing over the bridge that connects Jamjindo and Muuido Islands, you arrive at Muuido Island and the Guksabong Peak Trail begins. Guksabong Peak is a 230 m above sea level located in the center of Muuido Island, and from here, you can continue your hike to Horyonggoksan Mountain along the foot of the mountain or go down to Hanagae Beach.  Horyonggoksan Mountain, whose name originates from a legend that a tiger and a dragon fought there in the ancient times, is a low, 244 m-tall mountain, but it is still the tallest point on the island. As you go up and down the mountain and overlook the sea, you can see islands appearing like dots in the West Sea and the horizon roaming as it is covered in the sea mist. If you only wish to climb Horyonggoksan Mountain, you can start climbing from near the Hanagae Recreation Area.  Pine trees, Korean hornbeam trees, and oak trees form a thick forest, and here, you can also observe a variety of rare plants. On your way up, you will encounter rocks of different shapes. such as Horang Rock and Buddha Rock. You can also get a panoramic view of the West Sea and the islands in the vicinity. If you descend from the top to Hanagae Recreation Area, you can walk along the forest path on the beach hillside and encounter the “Road of Dream” where the dazzling sea unfolds under your feet.

stories.title: Somuuido Island
stories.script: Somuuido Island Enjoy trekking by the coast and the Eight Scenic Views of Nuri  In the old days, the only way to move between Muuido and Somuuido Islands was by boat. The western and eastern villages of Somuuido Island were blocked by mountains, which forced people to walk over the mountain path or travel by boat. Then, the island began to become revitalized after the construction of an overpass from Saemkumi to the western village of Somuuido Island and the establishment of Muui Bada Nurigil around the island.  The Muui Bada Nurigil is divided into eight sections. It consists of Somuui Footbridge Trail, Confronting Trail, Temuri Trail, Buddha Kaemi Trail, Mongyeo Beach Trail, Myeongsa Beach Trail, Haenyeoseom Island Trail, and Short Pine Tree Trail. You can trek each section and enjoy each of their characteristics. When the water recedes during low tide, you can enjoy a coastal trekking to Myeongsa Beach Trail and Janggunbawi Rock under Haenyeoseom Island Trail. There is a legend to Janggunbawi Rock; a long time ago, pirates who were spying to invade the island saw the rock's appearance, mistakenly believed it as an army, and ended up retreating from the area.  As you walk along the Muui Bada Nurigil, you can enjoy the Eight Scenic Views of Nuri, including Buddha Kumi, Mongyeo Beach, Mongyeo, Myeongsa Beach, Janggunbawi Rock, Dangsan and Ansan Mountains, the West and the East Villages, and Somuui Footbridge. In particular, once you climb up to Hadojeong Pavilion located at the top of Ansan Mountain (74 m), the tallest mountain on Somuuido Island, you can have a wide open view of the sea and small islands. To the southwest of Somuuido Island are Yeongheungdo, Jawoldo and Deokjeokdo Islands, and to the north are Ganghwado Island and Incheon International Airport. You can also get a full view of Palmido Island, Incheondaegyo Bridge, and Songdo International Business District to the east.

stories.title: Silmido Island
stories.script: Silmido Island A mystical island that can be accessed only when the sea opens up twice a day  For you to arrive at Silmido Island, you need to wait for a low tide to cross through the tidal flat. This path, which is created as the sea splits and the water recedes for two hours twice a day, is called “The Road of Moses.” While at Silmido Beach that overlooks the island, you just need have to wait for the sea to split while enjoying the blue sea, pine trees, and white sand. Silmido Beach is a beautiful, crescent moon-shaped beach that reaches 2 km in length, and the 100-year-old gorgeous pine trees make a shade to attract people on vacations.  Silmido is a small island attached to Muuido Island and consists of 6 km-long coastline and hills with an altitude of less than 80 m. It is an uninhabited island so there are no man-made facilities, and only uniquely shaped rocks are scattered around. Fine white sand forms up the eastern coast while the western coast is filled with strange-shaped rocks and stones. On a clear, sunny day, you can even see Baengnyeongdo Island and North Korea in the distance.  The west coast of Silmido Island is a site of painful history; it is where an anti-North Korean military detachment, founded by the Korean Central Intelligence Agency in the 1960s, engaged in hell-like military training. It is also the filming location of the film, Silmido, which was based on this background. The movie set has since been torn down so it can no longer be seen, but you can check out the gorgeous beach view of Silmido Island.

stories.title: Naval Battle of Hansan Monument
stories.script: Naval Battle of Hansan Monument  The giant stone stele standing on the mountain peak in Tongyeong overlooking the Yellow Sea is the Naval Battle of Hansan Monument. Built in 1979, to commemorate the Battle of Hansando Island, the Naval Battle of Hansan Monument sits on a pedestal shaped like a Geobukseon battleship, and stretches 20m into the sky. The head of the pedestal, called “Yongdu,” points toward Tokyo, Japan, to stand watch as a symbolic guardian protecting the country against future invasions from the sea.  When you climb the mountain and stand in front of the Monument, you can get a panoramic view of the Hansanman Bay area and a bird’s eye view of Jeseungdang Hall. It is the perfect place to immerse yourself in the determination and resolution Admiral Yi Sun-sin displayed during the Battle of Hansando Island.

stories.title: Jeseungdang Hall
stories.script: Jeseungdang Hall  “Jeseungdang” in Korean means “House of Victory.” During the Joseon Dynasty, it served as what we would call today as a naval command center. Originally, Jeseungdang was called “Unjudang,” meaning “a tent where generals devise strategies during war.”  Unfortunately, however, Unjudang was burnt down by a fire during the Japanese Invasion of Korea in 1597. Later on, when Cho Gyeong - the 107th “Samdo Sugun Tongjesa” (Naval Commander of the Three Provinces) - rebuilt Unjudang, he renamed it Jeseungdang.  While stationed at Jeseungdang (three years and eight months), Admiral Yi Sun-sin slept and ate at the compound, led military strategy sessions during the day, and developed new weapons during the night. Moreover, he wrote most of his personal diary, “Nanjung Ilgi,” in addition to several poems at Jeseungdang.  One particular wall in Jeseungdang features a poem titled “Hansando Yaeum” written in Admiral Yi’s own handwriting.

stories.title: Stele of descendants for the achievements
stories.audioTitle: Stele of descendants for the achievements
stories.script: Stele of descendants for the achievements  A “Stele for the Achievements” is a monument or memorial stone erected to celebrate the achievements and charitable deeds of a person for posterity. The stele at Jeseungdang is a monument erected to commemorate the admirable deeds of Admiral Yi Sun-sin’s descendants. “Samdo Sugun Tongjesa” (Naval Commander of the Three Provinces) Admiral Yi Sun-sin is a household name. His achievements are pretty well-known among the general public. But what about his descendants? What did they do to deserve their own steles?  A Samdo Sugun Tongjesa was the title given to the commander-in-chief of the navy stationed in the three southern provinces of the Joseon Dynasty - Gyeongsang-do, Jeolla-do and Chungcheong-do. The position was first created during the Japanese Invasion of Korea in 1592, and the inaugural Samdo Sugun Tongjesa was none other than Admiral Yi Sun-sin himself. Following in the footsteps of Admiral Yi, 208 admirals were appointed as Samdo Sugun Tongjesa across a period of 303 years. Among the 208, 12 were direct descendants of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Six of them were revered for their exemplary service. So much so that the locals erected steles to celebrate their charitable deeds in eternity. Admiral Yi once said that there are no weak soldiers under a fierce general. His bravery and patriotic spirit certainly lived on in his descendants, and inspired them to serve the community for generations.

stories.title: Suru Watchtower
stories.script: Suru Watchtower  “In the Hansando Island, under the bright moon, while standing alone on the watchtower over the water, with a big sword held tightly in my hand, I am falling into a deep pit of agony, the melody of a flute from somewhere adds more concern.”  This is the famous “Hansandoga” poem written by Admiral Yi Sun-shin. Every Korean would probably have heard or read that poem at one time or another in their lives. But did you know that the Suru Watchtower at Jeseungdang is the very watchtower where Admiral Yi was standing alone under the moonlight that night, thinking about his country?  A “Suru” is a type of watchtower where soldiers or generals can observe the movements of the enemy. Each lookout on duty at the Suru Watchtower was tasked with raising the alarm in the event he detected enemy movement on the horizon. By lighting a beacon at the watchtower, flying a kite, or blowing a boat horn, the lookout could communicate with military posts in Godongsan Mountain to the east, Mireuksan Mountain to the west, and Mangsan Mountain to the south. Since the Suru Watchtower looks over the sea, you might think it uses the Chinese character that means “water” for the “Su” part of its name. In fact, however, it uses the Chinese character for “defense.” So, Suru means a “defensive watchtower.” In 1976, the government built a new Suru Watchtower with concrete as part of its restoration project. However, in 2014, the old concrete structure was demolished for a new wooden watchtower.

stories.title: Memorial Monument
stories.script: Memorial Monument  The Memorial Monument was erected to celebrate the rebuilding of Jeseungdang Hall.  Jeseungdang was the operational command center where Admiral Yi Sun-sin worked with his generals to devise strategies and develop new weapons. When King Seonjo stripped Admiral Yi of his rank and replaced him with Won Gyun as the 2nd “Samdo Sugun Tongjesa” (Naval Commander of the Three Provinces), the Japanese navy annihilated the Joseon navy during the Japanese Invasion of Korea in 1597.  Jeseungdang also fell victim to the invading Japanese forces and was burnt to the ground. Fortunately, Admiral Cho Gyeong - the 107th Samdo Sugun Tongjesa - rebuilt Jeseungdang and erected the Memorial Monument to celebrate the achievements of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. The first monument, which was made out of sandstone, became severely weathered and damaged over the years with wind eroding most of its features away. To supplement the old monument, Yi Gyu-seok - the 198th Samdo Sugun Tongjesa and descendant of Admiral Yi Sun-sin - made a new monument and placed it alongside the old version. Today, the monument on the left is a monument erected by Admiral Cho Gyeong, and the one on the right is the monument erected by Admiral Yi Gyu-seok. Most notably, the latter features a Korean translation of the text carved into the monument using Chinese characters (Korean translation appears on the back of the monument).

stories.title: Chungmusa Shrine
stories.script: Chungmusa Shrine  Chungmusa Shrine is a shrine dedicated to the spirit of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Most notably, it houses the portrait of Admiral Yi. Chungmusa was built in 1932 by the Jeseungdang Preservation Society established by a group of confucian scholars in the Tongyeong region. Although the shrine was renovated in 1967, it was demolished a few years later to make way for a whole-new structure built in 1976 as part of the government’s restoration project. The “Chungmusa” signboard hanging in front of the shrine today was also commissioned when the new shrine building was built in 1976.  Originally, the shrine housed a portrait of Admiral Yi painted by painter Sang-bum Lee. In 1952, the original portrait was replaced by a new portrait painted by Un-ho Kim. In 1978, the portrait painted by Un-ho Kim was replaced by a new piece painted by Hyung-mo Chung. The portrait of Admiral Yi painted by Hyung-mo Chung still hangs inside Chungmusa today. Upon completing his version of Admiral Yi’s portrait, Chung  revealed the fact that he painted the portrait based on the physique and physiognomy of Admiral Yi’s descendants since there were no paintings showing the actual appearance of the Admiral.  Aside from the portrait of Admiral Yi, the shrine also houses parts of the “Seogancheop” (Caligraphy Album, National Treasure No. 76), and a review on the history of the Song Dynasty in China written by Admiral Yi in the form of a traditional folding screen. Every year, the local residents in the Tongyeong area and Navy officials organize a memorial service at Chungmusa Shrine and Jeseungdang Hall to perform traditional ancestral rites and to carry on the legacy of Admiral Yi Sun-sin.

stories.title: Hansanjeong Archery Range
stories.script: Hansanjeong Archery Range  Hansanjeong was an archery range where Admiral Yi Sun-sin and his officers honed their archery skills. The building that stands today at Hansanjeong was built in 1976 as part of the government’s restoration project. At one point during the Joseon Dynasty, Hansanjeong also served as a testing ground for young military officials and officers. Admiral Yi leveraged his authority to hold regional military service examinations at Hansanjeong, and successfully commissioned more than 100 military officials and officers. Today, the distance to target at Hansanjeong is roughly 145m - the same distance for archery trials at military service examinations held during the Joseon Dynasty. The group of officers who trained at Hansanjeong with Admiral Yi featured those who had passed the special regional military service examinations held at the request of the Admiral himself.  Hansanjeong was not a typical archery range built to help soldiers and officers improve their archery skills and host military service examinations. It was the only archery range in the country to have targets placed across a body of open water (i.e. the Yellow Sea). In other words, Hansanjeong was built to help soldiers and officers learn how to adjust to different conditions (e.g. limited visibility due to poor weather conditions, difference between visibility at sea and on land, tidal differences between high tide and low tide, etc.) they might come across during a naval battle. This makes Hansanjeong the perfect example that illustrates just how pragmatic and wise Admiral Yi Sun-sin was in military affairs.

stories.title: Hansanmun Gate
stories.script: Hansanmun Gate  Jeseungdang is a shrine dedicated to Admiral Yi Sun-shin, a guardian and patriot who dedicated his life to his country and his people in a time of crisis when the survival of the Korean people was at stake. Hansanmun Gate, which is positioned just after the ticket office, is the first gate to Jeseungdang. As you enter the gate paying respects to the spirit of Admiral Yi, you will find yourself on a trail with evergreen pine trees and the beautiful turquoise sea stretching into the horizon. Simply put, Hansanmun Gate gives you a wonderful and pleasant start to your visit to the inner compound of Jeseungdang.

stories.title: Sanmun Gate (Ticket Office)
stories.script: Sanmun Gate (Ticket Office)  Tongdosa Temple is one of the “Three Jewel Temples” (three historically most valuable Buddhist temples in Korea), and one of seven major Vindhyavana temples in Korea. The Temple is also referred to as a “Buddhist Treasure Temple” due to the fact that is houses genuine Sarira of Sakyamuni (Buddha). Tongdosa Temple was originally built in 646 (15th year of Queen Seondeok’s reign, Silla Dynasty) by a Buddhist monk named Jajang Yulsa when he returned from his travels across the Tang Dynasty in China with the Sarira of Sakyamuni, robes previously worn by Sakyamuni, and more than 400 chests of Buddhist sutras. The shape of the mountain where the Temple is located is similar to that of Vulture Peak, where Sakyamuni frequently held his sermons. The name “Tongdo” was chosen to convey the fact that the enlightened teachings of Buddha from Vulture Peak have reached all the way through to Silla (here, “Tong” means “to flow through” and “Do” means “enlightenment”). Thanks to its impressive cultural heritage and invaluable treasures, Tongdosa Temple was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in June 2018.

stories.title: Budowon Cemetery
stories.script: Budowon Cemetery  Budowon Cemetery at Tongdosa Temple houses stupas and stone tablets of high priests who served at the temple throughout its history. Currently, Budowon features stupas, stone tablets, and more than 60 stone monuments, including Stele of restoration and Stele of achievement. The sheer number of artifacts at Budowon reflects the temple’s illustrious history and proud tradition of producing enlightened Buddhist monks. Every year, on September 9th, according to the lunar calendar (i.e. the day of “Gaesandaejaeil”), Budowon at Tongdosa Temple hosts a “Budoheonda” ceremony to offer tea to Buddha.

stories.title: Seongbo Museum
stories.script: Seongbo Museum  The Tongdosa Seongbo Museum was built to safely and effectively preserve and exhibit the cultural artifacts and treasures housed at Tongdosa Temple. Moreover, the Museum hosts permanent exhibitions as well as special exhibitions to give Buddhists and the general public an opportunity to immerse themselves in Buddhist culture.

stories.title: Haejangbogak Hall (Buddhist University Lecture Hall, Library)
stories.audioTitle: Haejangbogak Hall (Buddhist University Lecture Hall, Library)
stories.script: Haejangbogak Hall (Buddhist University Lecture Hall, Library)  Haejangbogak is currently used as a lecture hall and library for the Buddhist University at Tongdosa Temple. Classrooms for the Buddhist University are divided into Introductory classes, Main classes, and Scripture classes, and the library is open to Buddhists, local residents, and the general public visiting Tongdosa Temple

stories.title: Samseongbanwolgyo Bridge
stories.script: Samseongbanwolgyo Bridge  Samseongbanwolgyo Bridge was built in 1937 by Buddhist monk Gyeongbong. The phrase “Samseongbanwol” in Korean means “three stars and a half moon,” which is a reference to the teachings of Buddha.

stories.title: Iljumun Gate
stories.script: Iljumun Gate  The outermost gate of a Buddhist temple is often called an Iljumun.  The Iljumun Gate at Tongdosa Temple is particularly well-known among the general public thanks to its signboard written by Heungseon Daewongun that reads “Yeongchuksan Tongdosa.” The phrases on each pillar reads, “Bulji Jongga” and “Gukji Daechil,” which means that Tongdosa Temple is the head of the Buddhist order in Korea, and a major temple of the country.

stories.title: Yukhwadang Hall (Administrative Office)
stories.script: Yukhwadang Hall (Administrative Office)  Yukhwadang is currently used as the administrative office that oversees all administrative affairs involving Tongdosa Temple.

stories.title: Cheonwangmun Gate
stories.script: Cheonwangmun Gate  Inspired by the legend of the Four Heavenly Kings helping Sakrodevandra protect Buddhism on the slopes of Mount Sumeru, Tongdosa Temple features a Cheonwangmun Gate (Gate for the Four Heavenly Kings) to call upon the Four Heavenly Kings of Buddhism as guardians and protect the temple from evil spirits. The gate was also built to erase distracting thoughts from the minds of people entering the temple.

stories.title: Garamgak Shrine
stories.script: Garamgak Shrine  Garamgak is a shrine dedicated to “Garamshin,” which refers to various gods protecting Buddhist rituals. It is a rare building, hardly seen in other Buddhist temples.

stories.title: Beomjongnu Pavilion
stories.script: Beomjongnu Pavilion  The “Beomjong” (bell) housed inside Beomjongnu at Tongdosa Temple is a musical instrument that communicates the teachings of Buddha, and a tool used for the salvation of humankind. In addition to the Beomjong, Beomjongnu features other items used for specific Buddhist rituals, including “Mokeo” (wooden drum), “Unpan” (bronze plate), and “Beopgo” (Buddhist drum).
