According to geomancy, it is recorded to have the first spot of strong energy among the four spots in South Jeolla Province, where the energy is known to influence the birth of civil and military officials, which makes it more famous. Maybe this is why there are three universities around the area and it is easy to see official ancestral tombs in the mountain.

stories.title: Neureoji area
stories.script: There is a place called Neureoji, one of the outstanding attractions in the Yeongsan River region.   The word Neureoji means that the river meanders slowly in a big curve like a bottle gourd. Especially it is a place that boasts of unique and beautiful scenery resembling the Korean Peninsula when viewed from a high place.

stories.title: The Forest of Encounter
stories.script: The Forest of Encounter It is easy for the elderly to find the Forest of Encounter because it is located at the entrance of Mulmajigol.     This forest is the perfect place for family outings as it has wood education facility, sports facilities including multi-purpose workout machines for grown-ups, adventure facilities for teenagers, and even wooden tables for families to enjoy meals.

stories.title: The Forest of View
stories.script: The Forest of View    After you walk for 1km from the Forest of Contemplation, you will get to the Forest of View, the viewpoint on the top of Yeonjingsan Mountain.   Would you like to enjoy the wonderful scenery of the meandering Yongsangnag River, which is the main river of South Jeolla Province from the viewpoint?

stories.title: Standing Stone Buddha of Yaksasa Temple
stories.audioTitle: Standing Stone Buddha of Yaksasa Temple
stories.script: Yaksa yeorae (Medicine Buddha) is short for Yaksa yuri gwang yeorae, which is the medicine Buddha of healing people.   He holds medicine in the left hand and spreads the five fingers of the right hand  outward, signaling the comfort he offers to people.   This stone statue is 310cm high, 120cm wide, and 45cm thick. It has a fleshy protuberance on the crown of the bald head with long ears and expressionless face.

stories.title: Bridge of Time
stories.script: When you get to the Water Lily Park, you can see the uniquely designed Bridge of Time.   Its shape looks like a wristwatch when viewed aerially.   Don’t miss the popular photo zone favored by many tourists for the beautiful shot of lush lotus and bridge in summer.

stories.title: Traditional Garden
stories.script: The Traditional Garden has a pond with a pavilion whose two pillars are built in the water.  The pond has the meaning of the traditional view of the world that the sky is round and the Earth is square.

stories.title: Observation Deck
stories.script: If you are at the Observation Deck in the Hoesan white lotus pond, you can see the Muan white lotuses closely at the Observation Deck.   Do you know that the Muan white lotus has the largest flower, leaves, and roots among water lilies in Korea, and that its flowers bloom last and for the longest time? The color on the edge of the petal changes slowly from light pink to white.    The roots of the Muan white lotus get thicker in September. The beautiful plant has both a shy maiden’s freshness and a lady’s gentle smile.

stories.title: Eco Pond
stories.script: The Eco Pond is an artificial pond. There are flowers such as large water lilies, regular water lilies, and least water- lily growing in the water; other flowers such as water rose of sharon, water canna, and iris grow near the water.    The large water lily represents the aquatic plants in the pond. It blooms elegantly on the water. This perennial plant is also called Australian water lily since it grows in Northern Australia.    It grows well at high temperature and in deep water. Its flower and petals are large, and its stamens sit in the wide open part between petals. Its leaves have thorns on the edge. The flowers of the water lily, which bloom from June to September, are famous for their gentle color and elegant beauty.

stories.title: Auto Camping Zone
stories.script: The Auto Camping Zone within the Heosan White Lotus Pond area has 20 convenient caravans and 23 auto sites and cooking and barbecue areas, including convenient facilities such as toilet and showers, drinking fountains, and pavilions. With all these facilities, many people enjoy this perfect place for camping every season.

stories.title: Namdo Sori Ullimteo Center
stories.script: Namdo Sori Ullimteo Center is a traditional music performance venue located in the new city of Namak.    The concert center is designed in a hanok style that shows the beauty of Korean traditional culture. The main building and its adjacent Provincial Library with hanok roof are famous tourist spots and located at the center of academy and art for the new city of Namak.     Every Saturday at 5 p.m., the South Jeolla Provincial Traditional Music Ensemble, which was founded in 1986, performs at the concert center. Famous art performances from Korea or abroad are also held frequently.

stories.title: The Entrance of Birthplace
stories.script: The Birthplace of Choui-seonsa is the place where Choui was born. As the greatest monk who was also called Daseong, he was born on April 5 in the 10th year of the reign of King Jeongjo in 1786. He lived there for fifteen years and later moved to Eunheungsa Temple in Naju.   Afterward, he moved to Daeheungsa Temple where he practiced under the then-great Monk Wanho Yunwoo and earned fame.   Chusa Kim Jeonghui wrote Gyesong, which about his lifelong friend and a famous scholar of the Zen Master  Choui, depicts his noble personality.

stories.title: House of Zen Master  Choui
stories.script: The House of Monk Choui was rebuilt in modern days. In the poem he wrote titled Guigohyang, the house where he was born was ruined during his lifetime, and only the descendants of his brothers remained in the hometown.   The restored house of his birth is a thatched house of a typical rural village.

stories.title: Daseongsa Shrine
stories.script: Daseongsa is a shrine where a Memorial rite is performed for Zen Master Daseong Choui. There is a rite of serving tea in front of his statue every lunar year on his birthday, April 5th, and also every lunar year on the second day of August when Zen Master Choui passed away.   The Daseongsa Shrine is open only to visitors who make a reservation via phone call.

stories.title: Yonghobaengnojeong Pavilion
stories.script: Yonghobaengnojeong Pavilion of Chusa Kim Jeonghui,  which used to be in Yeongsan, Seoul, was restored in Muan.    Yongho is an old name for Yeongsan, and Baengnojeong means that the pavilion had a view of white herons playing in Hangang River.   Zen Master Choui is said to have spent two years there playing and making poems with his same-aged friend, Kim Jeonghui.

stories.title: Mokwooam Temple
stories.script: Mokwooam Temple located deep in Mountain Seungdal was built by a monk named Jeongmyung, who came from the forbidden Western Regions, in the 24th year of the reign of King Seongdeok of Silla and rebuilt by Monk Wonmyeong from Imcheonsa Temple of the Yuan Dynasty during the late Goryeo.   According to an old story, Monk Wonmyeong had a dream wherein a cow appeared in Chongjisa Temple on Mt. Baekun and moved to the place where the hermitage is currently located. After the dream, the monk went to check the place and found the footprint of a cow on a rock in the place.  Later he built the temple out of weed and named it Mokwooam, which means cow.

stories.title: Transport Aircraft C-123K Provider
stories.script: There is a large airplane that catches the eye right behind the ticket office. It is the transport aircraft   C-123K Provider.   This transport aircraft was introduced in 1973 from the United States for transporting people and cargo. It was also used for special forces drill and was retired in 1994.   This aircraft is familiar to the people as it was featured in several films such as the Korean movie Welcome to Dongmakgol, which was released in 2005. Visitors can get into the aircraft.

stories.title: Holtong Beach
stories.script: Holtong Beach is located about 15km north of Muan International Airport, a natural park with a beautiful view of lush pine trees and long white sand beaches.  It is a popular summer resort for visitors to enjoy sea bathing, camping, and sea fishing.   It is also a perfect place for windsurfing, the flower of marine sports, because the wind blowing between the surrounding islands makes calm waves and the water around the seashore is shallow. No wonder, this beach attracts many surfers.

stories.title: Doripo port
stories.script: Doripo port is at the northwest end of Haejebando peninsula, which forms the boundary between Muan-gun and Yeonggwang-gun and Hampyeoung-gun. The beach around the port is a great place for sea-bathing because of its long sandy shore and large forested area.  There are sashimi restaurants around the Doripo port. The area is close to Chilsan Sea bordering Yeonggwang-gun and Hampyeong-gun and is famous for fishing bream and sea bass.     The sunset at Chilsan Sea on the other side of Doripo port is also spectacular. Especially, the port is known for the sunrise and sunset taking place in the same spot, so it is a popular attraction for many tourists to enjoy the sunrise on New Year’s Day.

stories.title: Mudflat Experience Field
stories.script: On the way to the Sunrise Observation Deck is a Mudflat Experience Field where a field of reeds and the mudflat create beautiful harmony.   Visitors can touch and feel crabs, snails, and gobies living there, so it is a great place for young children to experience nature and ecology.   When experiencing the mudflat, visitors should check the tidal level, and children should be accompanied by their guardian.

stories.title: Mudflat Exploration 1(Shrubby Sea-bite)
stories.script: In fall, there are salty plants spreading red across the wide Muan mudflat. These are shrubby sea-bites.  Shrubby sea-bite is an annual salty plant growing 15~50cm tall with a thick stem.   Especially in fall, the plants across the mudflat turn plum-colored like autumn leaves, making for a breathtaking sight.

stories.title: Mudflat Exploration 2(Sand Crab)
stories.script: Many sand crabs live in the Muan mudflat. Visitors can easily see them boasting of their large right red pincers.   Sand crabs, a family of Hippidae, burrow in the muddy sand, making a hole that can reach as deep as about 80cm. It is amazing to see them moving in groups to search for food.

stories.title: Mudflat Exploration 3(Japanese ghost crab)
stories.script: Japanese ghost crabs are some of the most common crabs in a red clay mudflat. They are characterized by their rectangular body and thin, short eyestalks.   They burrow a hole slantwise in the mudflat for habitation. In Muan and Sinan, South Jeolla Province, Japanese ghost crabs are used as octopus baits; given their reduced quantity, however, they are imported from China.    Especially, they have a perfect body condition for scooping organic matter from the surface of the mudflat because the tip of their tongs turn into a spoon-like shape.

stories.title: Mudflat Exploration(Sand-bubbler crab)
stories.script: It is easy to find the homes of sand-bubbler crabs in a sandy mudflat.   If you find very small sand beads being stacked side by side, that is where sand-bubbler crabs live.   They continue to move from place to place, and they are just the size of a small bean. They feed by filtering sand and leave behind balls of sand. That is why they are called Yeopnang crab, meaning bead crab. They are characterized by hairs and regular strips on the leg.

stories.title: Transport Aircraft AN-2 Antonov
stories.script: You can see four aircraft right across from the ticket office in the theme park -- one transport aircraft, one helicopter, and two jet trainers, all used in the 1960s and 1970s.   The first aircraft is Antonov, a former Soviet-equipped transport aircraft designed for low speed of 160km/h, low-altitude flight, and radar evasion.   The second one is Huey. It is a helicopter used for various purposes. It performed operational support, lifesaving, fire extinguishing, flare dropping, emergency patient transport, airborne troops dropping, and feeding of wild animals in winter, so it was also called Taxi of War.    The third one is Shooting Star. As a jet trainer, it was used in high-level flight training as the final test to train jet pilots.   The fourth one is Trojan, a jet trainer. This is the alternative to the outdated T-6 (Independence-day airplane) in the Korean air force.

stories.title: 108-step Swing Bridge
stories.script: Over the Hoesan White Lotus Pond is the 108-step Swing Bridge. The number 108 represents the Buddhist teaching that people go through 108 kinds of agony in life.    As you walk along, you can see wooden signboards bearing wise words from Buddhism and monks. Try to fill your heart with the good spirit of the words as you walk across the bridge slowly.

stories.title: Homeland Security Exhibition Hall
stories.script: The Homeland Security Exhibition Hall is designed to promote the history of homeland defense of the Republic of Korea. This educational place gives a glimpse of the history of the Korean army, navy, and air force, which developed from the voluntary and independent soldiers from 1910, and the development of the weapon system.

stories.title: Simulation Experience Center
stories.script: In the simulation experience center located at the center of the Military Theme Park, you can enjoy lifelike military experience through equipment such as airplane and tank.   As you operate the airplane or tank while watching the high-quality 3D panorama graphic screen, you will feel like a pilot or a member of a troop.   There are also various plastic models of airplanes and tanks. Thus, this is a popular place for highly curious kids to visit.

stories.title: Marine Safety Experience Center
stories.script: The Marine Safety Experience Center is designed as an experience facility in Muan-gun, Jeolla Province to increase citizens’ ability to cope with crisis management.    It aims to offer an opportunity for all people including residents and primary and secondary school students and young children to experience and increase the ability to respond to various disasters such as fire, storm, flood, aircraft accidents, earthquakes, and radiation or industrial accident.

stories.title: Mokpo Modern History Museum Hall 1 Information
stories.audioTitle: Mokpo Modern History Museum Hall 1 Information
stories.script: Hello. Welcome to the Mokpo Modern History Museum. I am your commentator for the Mokpo Modern History Museum, Smart Docent.   How much do you know about the Mokpo Modern History Museum? In 1981, it was recognized to have value in terms of architecture and history, and was thus designated as National Historic Site number 289 of the Republic of Korea.  Mokpo Modern History Museum is the oldest building in Mokpo. Following the opening of Mokpo Port in October of 1897, the Mokpo Japanese Consulate was established in October of 1898, and was thus built as the consulate building. The reason why the Japanese consulate was established here, in Mokpo, was because the area below it was a Japanese village, and it wanted to protect its citizens, monitor supplies going to Japan, and manage the commercial area.  The Mokpo Modern History Museum building served a number of purposes over time. It was constructed in 1900 and was used as the Japanese consulate until 1907. Later from 1914, it was used as the Mokpo gu-government office from 1914, and then Mokpo City Hall from 1947 after Korea gained independence. From 1974 it was used as the Mokpo Municipal Library and from 1990 to 2009, it functioned as the Mokpo Culture Center. From 2014 until now, it has been used as the Mokpo Modern History Museum Hall 1.  The Modern History Museum is also famous for being the filming location of Hotel Del Luna. This building was built in the Renaissance style. It was built in a symmetrical square shape using red bricks back in 1900 to be used as a consulate, with the main gate protruding outward from the center of the building. There is a belt of? string of Belt-like string of bricks between the first and second floors, and white bricks neatly ornate the left and right sides of the window. Upon entering the History Museum, there is an exhibit about the history of the opening of Mokpo Port and the history of Joseon on the first floor, and on the second floor, there is an exhibit on the history of resisting Japanese imperialism and the introduction of foreign cultures.  Admissions to the Mokpo Modern History Museum Hall 1 is 2,000 KRW for adults, 1,000 KRW for teenagers, 500 KRW for elementary school students, and free for pre-school children. There will be more detailed information provided once entering the history museum. We hope you have a good trip.

stories.title: Exhibits information
stories.script: The Modern History Museum Hall 1 that was opened in 2014 is a historical exhibition hall for learning about the start of Mokpo to modern history, and is said to be a treasure chest of modern history. Displays are on exhibit across two floors with a total of seven themes. On the first floor, themes 1, 2, 6 and 7 that are special exhibits of modern cities are on display. ‘Theme 1. Departing to Mokpojin.’ It was called Manhojin back in the Joseon Dynasty because a manho, or(senior military officer), was assigned to this position for the Joseon Navy, and today it is called Mokpojin. Visitors can learn about the role and appearance of the southwestern sea defense base of the Korean Peninsula ranging from the installation to operation of Mokpojin. ‘Theme 2. Redeparting to the Open Port Area.’ In 1897, Mokpo voluntarily opened its ports by the decree of King Gojong, thus becoming an open port and turning Mokpo into one of the three main ports and six main cities of the nation. Visitors can see how Mokpo gained its fame as the home of the ‘three white commodities (rice, cotton, salt).’ ‘Theme 6. Join the Manse Movement.’ This is an experience-based section of Mokpo Modern History Museum Hall 1. In the backdrop of the manse movement, or(independence movement), that began at Jeongmyeong Girls’ High School on April 8, 1919, there are various items such as school uniforms, hats, and glasses from that era, allowing visitors to experience the Manse Movement directly and feel the love of country by the patriotic martyrs. ‘Theme 7. Modern City Special Exhibit.’ A wide range of modern architecture was built in Mokpo, which was the region that most actively accepted foreign cultures since opening its ports. In particular, models of buildings around Mokpo Station and the Ogeori (five-way intersection) such as the Dongbongwonsa Temple, Honam Bank, Yangdong Church, Japanese consulate, and Japanese houses around the Ogeori, the heart of the city, have been recreated elaborately and put on display, allowing visitors to see what Mokpo looked like when it first opened its ports.

stories.title: Exhibits information
stories.script: Themes 3, 4 and 5 are on display on the second floor. ‘Theme 3. Becoming the First Line of Resistance.’ During the Japanese Occupation, Mokpo was suppressed through the installation of the Japanese consulate, Oriental Development Company, Mokpo Prison, Mokpo Police Station, etc., but Mokpo made historic efforts to resist the oppressors through events such as the March 1 Manse Movement, April 8 Manse Movement, and the Youth Movement, which can be seen here.  ‘Theme 4. Spreading Foreign Cultures.’ Since the opening of its ports, Christianity, Catholicism, and Japanese Buddhism called Dongbongwonsa (Higashi-Honganji) were spread, while Mokpo Shimsang Public Elementary School for Japanese children, Mokpo Girls’ Middle School, and Moontae Middle School for Koreans were opened, thereby spreading various aspects of civilization such as religion, education and culture. ‘Theme 5. Age of Pop Culture,’ After its opening the Mokpo Theater (1920) and Pyeonghwa Theater (1927) were built. They screened modern films and held various performances, resulting in an increase in cultural activities such as operas, drama, and pop music. Please enjoy your time here.

stories.title: Nearby tourist attractions
stories.script: Nearby tourist attractions  When coming down the stairs of the museum, there is a statue of a young girl. Behind it is a Japanese air-raid shelter and when going up the side road behind the museum, there are the Nojeokbong Art Park, Yudalsan (Mt.), and Nojeokbong Peak.   Behind the Mokpo Modern History Museum Hall 1, there is an air-raid shelter showing the remains of Japan’s preparations for war.  Air-raid shelters are artificial caves mostly made to be used for shelter against air raids from 1941 to 1945, the period of the Pacific War.  Visitors can enter the air-raid shelter behind the Mokpo Modern History Museum Hall 1 and it also has on exhibit Koreans forced into labor to dig these air-raid shelters.

stories.title: Information on Nojeokbong peak
stories.script: Nojeokbong stands 60m above sea level and it is a stone peak that was created as Yudalsan (Mt.) dropped to the ocean and then surged upward. Nojeokbong is a small stone mountain just 60m above sea level, but it is said to contain the spirit of Admiral Yi Sun-shin to defend the nation by defeating Japanese invaders. There is a story about Admiral Yi Sun-shin’s distinguished tactics using volunteer militia to defeat Japanese invaders at Nojeokbong. It is said that he had this stone peak covered with straw to look like piles of grain to make it appear as if his troops had a mountain of provisions, and then poured white clay on the upstream of Yeongsangang (Riv.) so that the river would appear as if being filled with water used for washing rice, thus making the Japanese invaders believe that Admiral Yi had many troops at his disposal, making them stop and retreat. This is the so-called Nojeokbong story.  The patriotic spirit of Yudalsan to defend the nation flows through Nojeokbong, and therefore, during the Japanese Occupation, the Japanese living in Mokpo built a large road between the main mountain range of Yudalsan and Nojeokbong in an attempt to cut off its energy. This created a shortcut from Yudal-dong to Juk-dong, which today makes the location of Nojeokbong appear to be a place, broken off from the veins of Yudalsan.  The Japanese also called Nojeokbong ‘Noinbong’ to intentionally distort the real history of Nojeokbong.  Separate from this, there is actually a stone called Noinam in front of Nojeokbong. Noinam is a place name that appears in an old map of Mokpojin that was produced in the late Joseon Dynasty. It is a rock that faces Nojeokbong and it looks like an old man (noin) protecting the grain stacks of Nojeokbong.  Look for the large stone face of Nojeokbong! The large stone face that looks like Admiral Yi Sun-shin giving commands protects Mokpo, the gateway to the southwestern seas, together with the statue of Admiral Yi in front of it. It is said that the energy emitted from Nojeokbong has health benefits, so try making a wish together with the fertility wood.

stories.title: Information on the Mokpo Shimsang Public Elementary School Auditorium
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Mokpo Shimsang Public Elementary School Auditorium
stories.script: The current Mokpo Shimsang Public Elementary School Auditorium is registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 30.  Mokpo Shimsang Public Elementary School is currently being used as Yudal Elementary School. The former Mokpo Shimsang Public Elementary School was established in 1929 and it was the first auditorium of the Shimsang Elementary School that was constructed for the first time in Mokpo for the education of Japanese children. It is the last remaining elementary school education facility from the Japanese Occupation still remaining in Mokpo. It has a reinforced concrete structure and the front and sides were finished with tiles of two colors, and on the second floor, there is a narrow arch window. It is the only remaining elementary school building from the Japanese Occupation in Mokpo, and it well represents the auditorium architectural features of the times.

stories.title: Mokpo Modern History Museum Hall 2 Information
stories.audioTitle: Mokpo Modern History Museum Hall 2 Information
stories.script: This place, which today is called Mokpo Modern History Museum  Hall 2, was first opened in June of 1920 with the objective of the Oriental Development Company gaining a monopoly on the Korean economy.  Because there is a strong impression as a vestige of Imperial Japan, its value as a cultural heritage was ignored. However, it was reevaluated for its historical and cultural value in light of the new century of culture, and was thus designated as ‘Jeollanam-do Regional Monument No. 174’ on November 20, 1999.   Oriental Development Company branch buildings currently still remain, but only in Mokpo and Busan, and the Busan building is smaller than the one in Mokpo. The former Oriental Development Company Mokpo Branch was not originally located here in Jungang-dong, Mokpo, but initially at Naju, and was promoted in 1908, and then moved here in 1920. In reality, this was an institution for plundering Korean farmers during the Japanese Occupation so that Imperial Japan could gain a monopoly on and exploit the Korean economy. The architectural mode of this building that was used by the Oriental Development Company is late Renaissance. This is a two-story stone building with a rectangular plane. It has patterns symbolizing Japan engraved in various areas, and the front gate has a sun pattern that represents Japan, cherry blossom patterns on the upper-left section, and sun patterns on the first floor wall inside the building.  Modern History Museum Hall 2, The first floor exhibit room 1 displays photos of the streets, buildings and lifestyles of Mokpo in the late 1920s.  Exhibit room 2 on the second floor is a special exhibit titled <Hero; Walking the Memories of That Day> and it offers the opportunity to learn the history of the efforts for national independence in the late 1920s, modern independence movements such as the April 8 Manse Movement, as well as the stories about various independence fighters who spent their lives facing off against the Japanese invasion.  There will be more detailed information provided once entering the history museum. Please enjoy your time here.

stories.title: Exhibits information
stories.script: When you enter the entrance to the museum, you will see a photo that compares the past and present of Mokpo. After passing the entrance, there is a safe used by the Oriental Development Company and photos from the Japanese Occupation period on display. At this time when the ports of Mokpo were opened, Japan developed Mokpo as a planned city, and pushed out the Koreans living there, threatening their very livelihoods. Urban development was carried out mainly for Japanese immigrants and the Japanese formed a village at the ‘former foreigner settlement.’ Koreans at the time were exploited twice through class discrimination and racial discrimination, and they formed a village in the ‘former area of Ssanggyo-ri, Bunae-myeon, Mokpo-bu.’ The Japanese residential area called ‘Namchon’ south of Yudalsan (Mt.) was lined with Japanese-style tile-roofed homes, and every home had running water. In ‘Bukchon,’ a residential area for Koreans known at the time as the slums, had water shortages and the water supply was frequently cut off. Koreans had to wait in line all day long just to get a bucket of water. Because of all the hardships during the Japanese Occupation, Koreans were very angry and hostile against the Japanese Empire.  Therefore, after liberation, there were strong claims to demolish, rather than preserve, the enemy property having traces of the Japanese. Many enemy homes concentrated in ‘Namchon’, the area reserved for Japanese and Japanese-style architecture, were demolished.   The second floor has a special exhibit on the independence movement called <Hero; Walking the Memories of That Day>. In the second half of the 19th century, the Japanese Empire had their eyes on Mokpo for its rich produce and favorable port from early on, and by installing the Japanese consulate, the Oriental Development Company, and other governing organizations, they exploited the rice and cotton, while completely suppressing any resistance or rebellion against this. But the people of Mokpo did not give up, and everyone ranging from students, youths, laborers, and women all kindled their desire for independence.

stories.title: Information on Mokpo Beonhwa-ro Japanese Style Mixed-use Building 1
stories.audioTitle: Information on Mokpo Beonhwa-ro Japanese Style Mixed-use Building 1
stories.script: This street that you are standing on is ‘Mokpo Modern History and Culture Space’ that was designated as the National Registered Cultural Heritage no. 718 on August 6, 2018. This space simultaneously holds on to the living history of the Korean Empire, Japanese Occupation, post-liberation, and today. When standing on this street that penetrates through modern history and current times, visitors will realize why exactly Mokpo is called a ‘roofless museum.’ With each step, you will find traces of history and feel the vestiges of life from the past in every alley. You can also see how the port city transformed through this.  The Japanese Style Mixed-use Building of Beonhwa-ro, Mokpo 1 is currently registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 718-7.  This is a commercial/residential building located at the corner of the Bonjeong (currently Beonhwa-ro) intersection, which was the central and main street of Mokpo, and it was built in 1935. This is a building in the traditional Japanese machiya style that combines stores and homes. In the past, the first floor was a store that sold traditional Japanese shoes called geta and the second floor was used as a home. The diagonal finish of the walls on the corners is unique.  Up until recently, it was used for the Saseum Supermarket and currently, it is being used as an exhibition area and place of rest for visitors through the urban regeneration project using vacant homes.

stories.title: Information on Mokpojin History Park
stories.script: Welcome to the Mokpojin History Park. The history of Mokpo starts with Mokpojin.  Mokpojin was installed in 1439, the 21st year of the reign of King Sejong, and it has been reported that it became a fortress in 1502 during the eighth year of the reign of Yeonsangun. Since then, Mokpojin served as a defensive post for the southwestern seas of the Korean Peninsula, but in 1895 (the 32nd year of King Gojong), it was abolished by the edict of King Gojong.  Mokpo has a long history related to naval posts, spanning back to over 500 years ago. Mokpojin has historical value as a defensive post for the southwestern seas of the Korean Peninsula, and it has significant meaning in that it is the first place to substantiate the history of Mokpo. The time when the name Mokpo mentioned in ancient literature became geographically identical with today’s Mokpo was because Mokpojin was installed here. From this aspect, it has important meaning in that it signals the start of the history of Mokpo. Also, as a naval post was established here, for about 500 years, called the first part of Mokpo history before opening its ports, it was a time that characterized Mokpo as performing its functions as a military stronghold that put enemies at a disadvantage and allies at an advantage.  Even at the time of opening the ports immediately following the closing of the base, some of its buildings were left in tact and were used by the Muan-Gamliseo, Japanese consulate, and Yeokguksagwan base. But it was damaged and only a monument for the remains of Mokpojin was left, but then it was restored to its current state in 2014. The military base that was removed during the Japanese Occupation was restored into a history park after 120 years, and it has three inner gates called naesammun, a red gate with spiked top (hongsalmun), and a traditional fence.  A hexagonal pavilion and bench were also installed. At the hexagonal observatory, visitors can get a bird’s-eye-view of downtown Mokpo. You are invited to make many fond memories at Mokpojin.

stories.title: Information on the Japanese Style Mixed-use Building of Haean-ro in Mokpo
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Japanese Style Mixed-use Building of Haean-ro in Mokpo
stories.script: The Japanese Style Mixed-use Building of Haean-ro in Mokpo is currently registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 718-9.   This is a symbolic commercial building that was constructed in 1939 at the intersection in front of the former Mokpo Police Station, which was the main street and center of Mokpo in modern history. It has a unique appearance that matches the multi-angle land of the intersection, and it is a two-story wooden commercial-residential building with an arch-type window on the corner wall and rooftop ornamentation. It exhibits the traces and history of the commercial street, and it is currently used as Jongil Supermarket.

stories.title: Information on the Former Mokpo Branch of Donga Women’s Store
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Former Mokpo Branch of Donga Women’s Store
stories.script: The former Mokpo Branch of Donga Women’s Store is currently registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 718-11.   This building was used by the ‘Donga Women’s Store’ that was first established in Jongno in Seoul in 1920 with the purpose of selling household goods and lifestyle items in demand by Korean women during the Japanese Occupation, and then subsequently opened in Mokpo, Gwangju, Daegu, Pyongyang and Hamheung. The Mokpo Branch of Donga Women’s Store offers a peek into life back then, together with the Hwasin Department Store at Beonhwa-ro, which was the representative main street and commercial center of Mokpo in modern history. It is currently a great example of being reused through the regeneration project after repairing the building.

stories.title: Information on Mokpo Beonhwa-ro Japanese Style Mixed-use Building 2, 3
stories.audioTitle: Information on Mokpo Beonhwa-ro Japanese Style Mixed-use Building 2, 3
stories.script: The Japanese Style Mixed-use Building of Beonhwa-ro, Mokpo 2 is currently registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 718-12. This is a commercial building located across the street from the Mokpo Branch of Donga Women’s Store at Beonhwa-ro, which was the representative main street and commercial center of Mokpo in modern history, and it is presumed to have been a confectionery store during the Japanese Occupation. This is a two-story wooden structure that looks narrow when seen from the street, but the inside is very long. Visitors can take a look at the traces and history of the representative commercial street of Mokpo in modern history.  The Japanese Style Mixed-use Building of Beonhwa-ro, Mokpo 3 is currently registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 718-13.  This is a commercial building that shows the traces and history of the commercial street constructed on the corner of the intersection at Beonhwa-ro, which was the representative main street and commercial center of Mokpo in modern history. This place was also famous as the Donga Pharmacy building that was operated by Ahn Cheol, a Christian leader in Mokpo at the time of the May 18 Democratization Movement, and the building has been preserved well even to this day.

stories.title: Information on the Red Brick Storehouse of Haean-ro in Mokpo
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Red Brick Storehouse of Haean-ro in Mokpo
stories.script: It is currently registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 718-14.  It is estimated to have been constructed in 1935 and due to its proximity to Mokpo Pier, it was used as a warehouse for cargo. There were many warehouses at Mokpo Pier and nearby locations back in modern history times. This red brick storehouse has well-preserved the appearance of the building, and it was constructed using red bricks, which was quite unusual at the time for a warehouse. Another unique feature is that three warehouses are connected as one building, and the wooden truss on the top and gable roof exemplifies the architectural styles in modern history.

stories.title: Information on Maningye Welcome Center (Jukdong 6-way Intersection)
stories.audioTitle: Information on Maningye Welcome Center (Jukdong 6-way Intersection)
stories.script: This place is called Jukdong 6-way Intersection and it is the old name of Mokpo that included the hilly area around today’s Juk-dong 6-way Intersection (Yukgeori) parking lot.  It was derived from ‘maningye’ that became popular after the opening of the ports of Mokpo in 1897. Maningye was a type of lottery gye (traditional private group funding in Korea) that sold gye tickets to people and shared the dividends by ranking through lotteries. Profits from sales were used to build public facilities of Korean villages, and it was therefore related to the development of downtown Mokpo at the time. Many people gathered on the day of the lottery, thus becoming a type of town festival. With this place name being spread orally, it was called ‘Maingye’ as it was easier to pronounce, and therefore, the current address name is registered as ‘Maingye-teo.’ Below the Maningye Culture Center is a pond where visitors can experience Okdani water-carrying yokes. Try it out

stories.title: Information on Okdani Road
stories.script: ‘Okdani Road’ is a historical alley exploration path in Mokwon-dong. It is a path where visitors can compare the lives of Koreans in modern history with that of the Japanese. Okdani is a real person who lived as a water merchant who traveled the alleys of the old downtown area of Mokpo and is the main character of the author Cha Beom-seok’s play, Okdaneo! After the opening of Mokpo ports, there were shortages of water due to geographical reasons. That is why there were merchants who carried water on A-frames and traveled to sell water. Okdani was one such water merchant in this play.   The small alleys at Okdani Road are interconnected like the vessels of a heart, and there are a number of modern history remains that can be found still to this day. When walking along Okdani-gil, you can feel the breath of Mokpo as a city in modern history that was built by Koreans since the opening of the ports in 1897.

stories.title: Nearby tourist attractions
stories.script: When passing the Maningye Welcome Center and going up, you will arrive at the Maningye-teo (site) and the Rainbow Overpass. When walking down the Rainbow Overpass, visitors can reach a number of streets and tourist attractions such as the Kim Woo-jin Street, Cha Beom-seok Street, and the Mokwon-dong Mural Alley. The Norano Museum is located toward the left of the Maningye Welcome Center.

stories.title: Information on Rainbow Overpass Street
stories.script: Rainbow Overpass is a street based on the theme of colors, and it is a Rainbow Overpass Street that is painted with rainbow colors. When walking along the colorful Rainbow Overpass, you will see some fun texts that use Mokpo dialects as well as wall paintings. Below the Rainbow Overpass there are words written on the wall talking about Lee Mae-bang, who is said to be a dancer from the heavens, and Cha Beom-seok, one of the most famous playwriters of Korea.   Lee Mae-bang was born in 1927 and passed away in 2015. She was a Korean dancer and her nom de plume was ‘Ubong.’ She was an art holder for Important Intangible Cultural Property no. 27 [Seungmu], and Important Intangible Cultural Property no. 97 [Salpuri-chum]. Lee Mae-bang was born in Daeseong-dong, Mokpo in 1927. Her given name was originally Gyu-tae, but she changed her name to Mae-bang after Mei Lanfang, a master of the Chinese opera. She learned traditional dance and song at Gweonbeon in Mokpo as a child. She learned seungmu (Buddhist dance), geommu (sword dance), and salpuri-chum (exorcism dance) from Lee Dae-jo, Lee Chang-jo, and Park Yong-gu, and after painstaking effort, she became a master that represents traditional dance of Korea. Starting with the [Seungmu] performance at the ‘Virtuoso and Master Singing Contest’ held in Mokpo in 1941, she traveled all across the world until her death in 2015, spreading the beauty of Korean dance. She also served as a professor at the Yongin University Department of Dance and received many awards including the Silver Certificate of Merit and the Order of Arts and Letters of France.  He was born in 1924 and passed away in 2006, and was a playwright from Mokpo that represented all of Korea. He also taught students as a teacher at Mokpo Bukgyo Elementary School and Mokpo Middle School. After enrolling at Yeonhee College in 1946, he began his theater work by founding the ‘Yeonhee Theater Art Research Club.’ In the 1950s, he began publishing works that mainly satirized and that were highly critical of social realities such as [Milju] and [Gwihyang]. [Bulmoji] and [Sanbul] are some of the most famous post-war literature that awakened rebellious awareness. He also worked as a playwriter for the MBC drama, Jeon Won Diary. Works related with Mokpo include [Crane, It is Love] and [Okdaneo!], as well as the essay collection [Memories of Slow Train for Mokpo]. He served as the chairman of the National Academy of Arts of the Republic of Korea and director of the Korea Culture and Arts Foundation, and received awards such as the Korea Culture and Arts Award, National Academic of Arts Award, Korean Literature Award, and the Seoul Culture Award. The Cha Beom-seok Play Award has been operating since 2007.

stories.title: Information on Cha Beom-seok Home & Cha Beom-seok Small Library
stories.audioTitle: Information on Cha Beom-seok Home & Cha Beom-seok Small Library
stories.script: This is the site where Cha Beom-seok was born and raised. The men’s quarter still remains as it was in the past. Next to the home of Cha Beom-seok is the Cha Beom-seok Small Library. It was originally a parking lot, but a library was built here.  Displayed inside the library are the Complete Works of Cha Beom-seok as well as 30 books donated by his eldest daughter, Cha Hye-young. Cha Beom-seok was the man who perfected Korean realism theater. He was a playwright born in Bukgyo-dong, Mokpo. He enrolled at the Mokpo Jeil Normal School in 1932 and graduated from the Gwangju Normal High School in five years. In 1945, he worked at Mokpo Bukgyo Elementary School, thus being a playwright who has deep relations with Mokpo. He was born in 1924 and was laid to rest in 2006.  He is assessed to be the representative playwright and producer who completed realism theater of Korea. In his 20s, as part of the post-war literature generation that lived through the Korean War, he published works that strongly satirized and criticized social realities. He was quite well known for his meticulous nature and being highly principled he continued to write until late into his life. He completed his new work [Okdaneo] when he was 80 and in late 2004, he also exhibited his energy by publishing ‘Small Theater History of Korea,’ that explained the history of the development of Korean small theater plays up until the current day since his new play. He is a playwright who can be categorized as a post-war writer, but he was not only fixated on the war. He also wrote works pursuing the psychology of common people of today through various themes based completely on realism. He is said to be a representative writer and producer of Korean realism theater following Lee Hae-rang and Yoo Chi-jin.

stories.title: Information the Kim Sisters Gallery
stories.script: Before entering the gallery, do you know who the Kim Sisters are? The Kim Sisters are Korea’s first female vocal group and was the first girl group from Asia to perform in the US. They began performing in the US in 1959 and appeared on popular American TV shows such as the ‘Ed Sullivan Show’ to achieve the American Dream. Their mother is the famous singer Lee Nan-young who sang ‘Tears of Mokpo.’ The Kim Sisters Gallery was opened on June 20, 2020. This gallery was hosted by being paid for completely by Jung Tae-gwan, a painter at the Painter’s House and was sponsored by the Tears of Mokpo Commemorative Association and the Alley People Bukgyogol community. The large painting in front was painted by a person who used to paint theater signs in the past.  The gallery includes three sets of clothes and one pair of shoes worn by Lee Nan-young and stored by the ‘Tears of Mokpo Commemorative Association,’ as well as three instruments, clothes, shoes, and photographs of the Kim Sisters. The gallery was built and is being managed and operating completely at the expense of Painter Jung Tae-gwan.

stories.title: Information on Bukgyo-dong Hanok Village
stories.script: This area was where the oldest village in Mokpo, 'Ssanggyochon’ was located. It was called ‘Ssanggyochon’ because it was a village with two bridges (gyo) called ‘Namgyo’ and ‘Bukgyo’ even before Mokpo opened her ports. The Bukgyo-dong area was an area where wealthy Koreans built modern hanok (traditional Korean homes) during the course of Mokpo being developed by being divided into Japanese villages and Korean villages. There are currently main buildings remaining that show how modern hanok transformed in the 20th century like the Shim Bok-ju home and Moon Jae-cheol home.

stories.title: Information on Mokwon-dong Mural Alley
stories.script: This is an alley village located below the former Dalseong Elementary School.  The Mokpo Mokwon-dong Mural Village is an alley village located below the former Dalseong Elementary School that is currently being used as the Yudal Art Town at the foot of Yudalsan (Mt.). It started to gain fame as local artists began painting the walls of the maze-like alleys.  Murals and experience facilities were added through the Mokpo Urban Regeneration Project, thus becoming what it is today.  The Mural Village has murals with a number of themes. Visitors can re-experience the alleys of their childhoods thanks to the murals filled with memories from the past.  Unlike the alleys of other villages, the entire village is filled with charming and bright colors. Enjoy the murals of the alleys and take some memorable photos.  Once you pass the Mural Alley and go up, you will arrive at the Yudal Art Town.

stories.title: Information on the Kim Woo-jin Street
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Kim Woo-jin Street
stories.script: The Kim Woo-jin Street was established in Mokpo to remember the genius playwright Kim Woo-jin. Kim Woo-jin was born in Jangseong of Jeollanam-do and moved to Mokpo when he was 14 when his father was appointed as the gamli (government administrator) of Muan. Kim Woo-jin Street is a street made around Bukgyo-dong Cathedral. His works are on display all around the walls of the street, so visitors can check out his works by simply walking along the street. His nom de plume is Choseong and Susan, and he was born as the eldest son of Kim Sung-gyu, who was the gamli of Muan at the time of the port opening of Muan. Kim Woo-jin is the only playwright who experimented with expressionism directly in the 1920s and he was a pioneer of modern theater that brought about the New Drama Movement first in Korea. He was a man who exhibited great talent across various genres. But unlike his literary aspirations, his father wanted him to continue the family business, which constantly brought the two at odds against each other.  Kim Woo-jin overflowed with passion for literature, and thus had conflicts with his father. He therefore moved to Tokyo, Japan. Here, he met Korea’s first soprano Yoon Shim-deok. In August of that year, the two boarded a ship sailing from Shimonoseki, Japan to Busan, Korea, where they ended their lives by jumping into the Korea Straits.

stories.title: Introduction of Kim Woo-jin
stories.script: Movements to reflect on and overcome the existing soap operas appeared in diverse ways in the 1920s, and at the center of such transition was the student theater focusing on students who studied abroad. Kim Woo-jin was a playwright in the midst of such student theater movement who tried to realize new types of drama different from the soap operas that were popular at the time. Kim Woo-jin was a representative playwright and theorist who revealed the problems and features of drama.  Kim Woo-jin’s plays exhibited two different directions such as deeply embracing the critical mind of domestic dramas that were mainstream in the 1920s, and to expand the intent for reforms contained in it toward a more socially realistic aspect.  While <Shipwreck> and <Disillusion of the Mole Poet> depicted the acute opposition between traditional ethics and western ethics and were more in the style of domestic dramas, <Noon> and <Lee Young-nyeo > shed light on the ghastly life of the poor at the brothels on the foot of Yudalsan (Mt.) in Mokpo and focused more on social issues. Furthermore, his most famous book <Mountain Boar> that was based on the Donhak Peasant Revolution combined both aspects.

stories.title: Information on Bukgyo-dong Cathedral
stories.script: Bukgyo-dong Cathedral is located on the site of Seongchwiwon, the home of Kim Woo-jin who was the first playwright that introduced modern drama to the Korean literary world. The area where Bukgyodong Cathedral currently stands at Bukgyo-dong 46-beonji in Mokpo was where Seongchwiwon, a huge mansion in this vast area, was located. There are no traces of Seongchwiwon remaining today, but there is a small monument that says playwright Kim Woo-jin Cradle of Literature.   Kim Woo-jin was the eldest son of Kim Sung-gyu and the first playwright in Korea to research modern western dramas and produce it on stage. Here, he wrote many works while staying at the ‘Baeksujae,’ a western-style building inside of Seongchwiwon. The Seongchwiwon site was donated to the Catholic diocese and became home to today’s Bukgyo-dong Cathedral in 1958. Inside the cathedral is a memorial stone that says ‘Cradle of Kim Woo-jin Literature.’

stories.title: Information on Buljongdae
stories.script: The height of Buljongdae seen here is 11m. The Buljongdae was a type of bell tower where a monitor would check for fires in the Korean village and when a fire broke out, that monitor would ring the bell. The location of Buljongdae is the intersection connecting to Namgyo-dong, Bukgyo-dong, Jukgyo-dong, and Yang-dong. In particular, the hill connecting to the Bukgyo-dong Cathedral on the left was a place where wealthy Koreans lived, thus forming a modern hanok (traditional Korean home) village.  The Buljongdae was preserved until 1970 and then removed, but was then restored across the street from where the Buljongdae used to be in 2017. The actual location of the bell tower is currently where the Bukgyo Shinhyup Credit Union is located, but due to land accommodation reasons, it was erected at the former volunteer fire station site to create the Buljongdae Specialized Park.  The Buljongdae Specialized Park includes the 11m high Buljongdae, and signs, water pumps, and a photo zone that records the history of Buljongdae and the activities of the volunteer firefighters.

stories.title: Information on the Former Mokpo Youth Center
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Former Mokpo Youth Center
stories.script: The former Mokpo Youth Center was designated as national registered cultural heritage no. 43.  The Mokpo Youth Center building still remains about 150m from the entrance of Kongnamul Neighborhood toward the former Shinan-gu Office.  This was a cultural hall for the youths of Mokpo during the Japanese Occupation, and it is a modern building that served as the first citizen’s hall of Mokpo. It was completed in 1925 through donations by the Mokpo Youth Assembly during the Japanese Occupation. This building, which was constructed in 1925, was the base for anti-Japanese movements among the youths of Mokpo during the Japanese Occupation, and it is a historical place that published the magazine titled ‘Joseon Youth.’ It was constructed with donations from various people of all classes, and therefore, each part was built focusing on functions over design elements.  It was a place that aimed at enhancing the knowledge and virtues of youths in Mokpo and as the center of national movements including the founding ceremony of the Mokpo Branch of the Shinganhoe, which was a bi-partisan anti-Japanese association. It is also the background for the short novel by Park Hwa-seong, ‘Crumbling Youth Center.’  The former Youth Center was the cradle for national movements among the youths of Mokpo during the Japanese Occupation, and it was a building constructed and operated autonomously by the Korean people, thus playing a central role for youth movements in Mokpo. In front of the building was where Heesung Kindergarten was located during the Japanese Occupation and where Wonjin Theater was after liberation, with the Muan Gamliseo site also located nearby.

stories.title: Information on Kongnamul Neighborhood
stories.script: The ‘Kongnamul Neighborhood’ alley is located about 50m right from the Koo Jong-myeong memorial stone.  There is a sad story related to Kongnamul Neighborhood. People slowly began gathering at Kongnamul Neighborhood after the Korean War. People began growing bean sprouts (kongnamul) and sold them at the nearby Namgyo Jungang Food Market to barely eke out a living. That is why people in Mokpo still call this alley Kongnamul Neighborhood or Kongnamul Factory. Compared to the other alleys, the roads of Kongnamul Neighborhood are quite wide. The reason why the alleys of Kongnamul Neighborhood is larger than that of others is because people had to push and pull hand carts filled with bean sprouts.

stories.title: Information on the Former Dongbongwonsa Temple Mokpo Branch
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Former Dongbongwonsa Temple Mokpo Branch
stories.script: Dongbongwonsa (Higashi-Honganji) is the first Japanese Buddhist temple.  It was designated as registered cultural heritage no. 340 in 2007, and it is currently used as the Ogeori Culture Center for the citizens of Mokpo. There is a monument in the building garden showing that this place is a historical site related to the May 18 Democratization Movement  Using Dongbonwonsa as the base, to the left was the Japanese settlement that was the new urban center and to the right was the Korean settlement that was the old urban center. The roads in the new urban center area where Japanese resided are orderly and well-organized. In comparison, when looking at the roads of the old urban center, which is also part of the Okdani Road, the alleys are winding and the houses seem to be built sporadically and not in any orderly fashion.  The Ogeori Culture Center building was constructed as the Mokpo branch of Dongbonwonsa, the first Japanese Buddhist temple to settle in Mokpo after the city opened its ports in 1897. Its official name is ‘Jinjong Daegokpa Dongbonwonsa.’ A missions office was installed near the Japanese consulate toward the opened port, but was then moved to its current location in 1904. This building is currently located is Ogeori (5-way street), which is the most bustling area in the old downtown area of Mokpo. This place has some distance from the open port area where the Japanese lived at the time, but it was an excellent location for a temple as it was set at the border area where Koreans met with the Japanese. After liberation, it was managed by Jeonggwangsa Temple, and then from 1957, it was used as the building for the Central Church. Literary critic Kim Hyun attended this church and his father was an elder of the church.

stories.title: Information on Yeonhee's Supermarket
stories.script: Yeonhee’s Supermarket became famous after being used as the set for the small store in the shantytown where ‘Yeonhee’ who was a class of ‘87 college freshman in the movie 1987, lived. The props used during the filming were recreated to remind visitors of Gang Dong-won, Yoo Hae-jin and Kim Tae-ri in this movie. Seosan-dong still has a building that was used as a licensed brothel for the Japanese, and it still keeps its look from 30 years ago, making visitors feel as if they are traveling back in time.  This entire town where Yeonhee’s Supermarket is located is a Modern History Museum Street. The Sihwa Village Alley near Yeonhee’s Supermarket still keeps in tact its appearance from the 1980s for visitors to feel the atmosphere from the past. The Seosan-dong area where there was a licensed Japanese brothel street still has buildings from then standing, and therefore, the entire village can be seen as a Modern History Museum Street.  Right behind Yonhee’s Supermarket is an air-raid shelter that was built by the Japanese by forcing Koreans into labor in order to shelter against air raids by the Allied Forces late into the Pacific War. It is 31m long with the largest width of 2.6m. It was used for evacuating the Japanese as a licensed brothel street during the Japanese Occupation was located here. It is historically meaningful in that it is the site of forcefully mobilizing Korean labor and that it is remains of the Pacific War.  Across the street from Yeonhee's Supermarket is Baekyang Laundry that is 50-years old. Various machines and bundles of thread used by laundry cleaners in the past still remain to remind people of the past. Just a little bit up from Yeonhee’s Supermarket is Sihwa Alley. There are murals of old sceneries and pretty poems hanging on the uphill narrow alleys, which were joined by local poets and artists of Mokpo, making it an alley with many attractions to see while walking.

stories.title: Information on Sihwa Alley
stories.script: Seosan-dong is a representative fishing village located on the foots of Yudalsan (Mt.) in Mokpo.  As you can see, it is a small shantytown with small houses lining the narrow alley. It is said to be a region that was mostly inhabited by fishermen. In different parts of Sihwa Alley the joys and sorrows of life, as well as its stories that stood fast against a long period of time, are contained in paintings and texts. There are poems written by residents and poems about Seosan-dong written by about a dozen poets who work in the Mokpo area. Visitors can take a look at the paintings depicting the lives of the residents of Seosan-dong and walk along the various wall paintings of fishing in the sea, sceneries, boats, etc. that go along perfectly with the fishing village to feel the beautiful sentiments and lingering images of the alley. There are three alleys at Sihwa Alley. The first alley on the left goes to ‘Babo Square,’ and to the right, the street continues on to the second and third alleys. When walking up along the first alley, you will be able to see Bori Square and it will continue to the second alley, and then go up toward Bori Square again along the third alley. This is the most typically used course. To the back of Sihwa Alley is the beautiful Yudalsan (Mt.) and at the very top is Bori Square, which is a large vacant lot used for threshing barley or rice after they are harvested. The Yugwak Street is located below. When viewing the entire area of Seosan-dong from here, you can see the outskirts of Yudalsan that has maintained its appearance from long ago, and the nightscape of Seosan-dong seen from Bori Square is another attraction worth experiencing. While walking along the Seosan-dong alleys, you will be able to remember memories from your childhood long ago. Yugwak Street is a street concentrated with lodging buildings built during the Japanese Occupation, and it is a street where visitors can remember the past history. There are also many houses built for the Japanese, thus showing the architectural mode of the time during the Japanese Occupation.

stories.title: Information on the Mokpo Literature Museum
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Mokpo Literature Museum
stories.script: This is Korea’s first four-person museum of literature where visitors can learn about Kim Woo-jin, a playwright who was the first to introduce modern drama to Korean theater; Park Hwa-seong, the first female novelist who wrote full-length novels; Cha Beom-seok, a playwright who perfected realism drama; and Kim Hyun, who was unrivaled in Korean criticism literature. On exhibit are relics used by the authors their entire lives, hand-written manuscripts on which they performed their creative activities, collections of works, etc., and the museum has a literature experience hall, a literature guestroom, a literary creation studio, and more. On the first floor of the Mokpo Literature Museum are the Park Hwa-seong and Cha Beom-seok Halls, and on the second floor are the Kim Woo-jin Hall and Kim Hyun Hall, making it Korea’s first four-person integrated museum of literature. The lives and literary worlds of Kim Woo-jin, Park Hwa-seong, Cha Beom-seok, and Kim Hyeon, who are masters and pioneers in their fields and are always included in Korean literary history, can be met through their relics that they used while they were still alive. Next to the Literature Museum are literary monuments of Park Hwa-seong and Kim Hyun, and also an outdoor gallery that displays poetry and paintings that can be appreciated. It is located in the Gatbawi Culture Town together with the Natural History Museum, Ceramic Livingware Museum, and the Maritime Museum.

stories.title: Information on the Home of Kim Woo-jin’s Butler
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Home of Kim Woo-jin’s Butler
stories.script: This site that is now a guesthouse used to be the home of Kim Woo-jin’s butler. There is not much known about Kim Woo-jin’s butler. On the right side toward the Bukgyo-dong Cathedral from the home where Kim Woo-jin’s butler lived is a house that is said to be the home of Kim Woo-jin’s daughter, Kim Jin-gil.  Kim Woo-jin’s nom de plume was Choseong and Susan and he is from the Andong Kim family. He was born in Yonggang-myeon, Jangseong-gun as the eldest son of Kim Seong-gyu, the governor of Jangseong who was also the gamli (government administrator) of Muan when the ports of Mokpo were opened, and Mrs. Park from the Suncheon Park family. At the age of 16, he wrote the short-story <Fantasy Literature> and could not let go of his dreams in literature. Despite his father’s opposition, he enrolled at the Waseda University Department of English in 1919 where he majored in drama. He was completely immersed in British social reform thinker Shaw, and the plays of the Swedish expressionist playwright, Strindberg, and was also interested in the works of Nietzsche. After graduating university, he returned to Mokpo and became the president of the farming business chain, Samseong Partnership Company, but he continued to have problems with his father. While working at the company, he left behind a total of 78 works including 50 poems, 5 plays, 3 novels, and 20 critiques. He fell in an artistic romantic relationship with soprano Yoon Shim-deok, who gained huge popularity both in Korea and abroad for singing Hymn of Death. But on August 4, 1926, while returning to Korea with Yoon Shim-deok on a Japanese government ferry, they threw themselves into the Korea Straits and died at the age of 29.

stories.title: Information on the Banditbul Small Library
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Banditbul Small Library
stories.script: The Banditbul (firefly) Small Library was initially called Kim Woo-jin Library. The site of the Banditbul Library used to be where the community office was located. In the front of the library is a sculpture engraved with the books and achievements of Kim Woo-jin. Kim Woo-jin is a writer who left behind 48 poems, 5 plays, 3 novels, and over 20 critiques, and his best known works includ ‘Mountain Boar,’ ‘Lee Young-nyeo,’ and ‘Shipwreck.’ Kim Woo-jin was born in Jangseong, Jeollanam-do as the eldest son of Kim Seong-gyu, who was the governor of Jangseong at the time. He moved to Bukgyo-dong 46-beonji in Mokpo in 1907 and graduated from the Mokpo National Normal School (currently Bukgyo Elementary School), and then studied in Japan at Kumamoto Agriculture School and graduated from the Waseda University Department of English in 1924. After graduating from college, he returned to Mokpo where he worked as the president of a farming business, leaving behind 50 poems, 5 plays, 3 novels, and 20 literary critiques.

stories.title: Information on the Home of Park Hwa-seong
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Home of Park Hwa-seong
stories.script: The place with the stone marker is where the home of novelist Park Hwa-seong used to be. Park Hwa-seong is the first Korean female novelist to write the full-length novel, ‘Baekhwa.’ She was born in Juk-dong, which is currently Mokwon-dong, in Mokpo in 1903. Mokwon-dong is also the background for her works, ‘Waterworks’ and ‘Crumbling Youth Center.’ The Park Hwa-seong Park was made at the Yongdang-dong Sehannu site where her studio used to be in Mokpo, and there is also the Park Hwa-seong Exhibit at the Mokpo Literature Museum in Yonghae-dong. As a novelist, Park Hwa-seong depicted the poor lives of farmers and laborers during the colonial period, and wrote works that have a realist tendency that searched for solutions. Park Hwa-seong’s birth name was Gyeong-soon and her nom de plume was Soyoung. She was born in Mokpo in 1904 and graduated from the Mokpo Jeongmyeong Girls’ School and Sookmyung Girls’ High School in Seoul. In 1922, while working as a teacher in Yeonggwang, she met with the sijo writer Cho Woon, who she studied literature under. In 1925, she published ‘Eve of Chuseok’ where she started her literary career and then in 1932, with the publication of ‘Waterworks,’ she focused on her works in earnest. She published works with realism tendencies containing hierarchal thoughts that searched for solutions to the reality of colonialism and the poor lives of farmers and laborers. She stopped writing for a while due to crackdowns by the Japanese Empire, but then picked up her pen once again after Korea gained independence. Since then, she continued publishing her works with popular appeal such as ‘Black Sandpaper,’ ‘Spring Fog,’ ‘In the Gale,’ ‘Over the Hill,’ ‘Flower Blooming on the Cliff,’ ‘Tomorrow’s Sun,’ and ‘Drawing in the Blue Sky.’  She also took part in various activities such as being a central member of the International PEN Korea Branch, and standing member of the Korea Writers Association. She received the Mokpo Culture Award, Korea Literature Award, National Academic of Arts Award, and the March 1 Culture Award, before being laid to rest in 1988.

stories.title: Information on the Park Hwa-seong Sehan-ru Small Park
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Park Hwa-seong Sehan-ru Small Park
stories.script: Located in Mokpo, Jeollanam-do is the restored ‘Sehan-ru’ at the old housing site of the studio where Soyoung Park Hwa-seong, Korea’s first female full-length novelist, spent her time in creative writing.  Sehan-ru was built at the Sehan-ru Small Park on a 454㎡ site, where there is a high concentration of homes behind the Dongmokpo Telephone Office in Yongdang-dong, in order to commemorate her literary achievements.  The old Sehan-ru house was where Soyoung Park Hwa-seong wrote her books from 1937 to 1962, and it was also where she held the publication event for her first short-story ‘People with No Hometowns’ in 1947. The city of Mokpo restored the symbolic Sehan-ru at this meaningful place.  At Sehan-ru Park is a bust statue, traditional hanok pavillion, simple door, traditional fence, and a monument that engraved her lifelong achievements and the words of ‘Anthem of Mokpo’ that she wrote.

stories.title: Information on the Residence of Kim Hyeon
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Residence of Kim Hyeon
stories.script: Bukgyobushik Supermarket is the site of Kim Hyeon’s home. Kim Hyeon was a literary critic who lived here. He was born in Jindo, Jeollanam-do in 1942, and then moved to Mokpo when he was 8.  His father and older brother ran the Guse Pharmacy at the Mokpo Quayside, and it was said that he grew up in an affluent environment. After graduating from Mokpo Middle School, he enrolled at the Mokpo Muntae High School, but soon transferred to Kyungbock High School in Seoul. He then went on to the Seoul National University College of Liberal Arts and Sciences where he earned his bachelor’s degree and then earned his master’s degree at the Seoul National University Graduate School of French Literature, and then studied at the University of Strasbourg in France.  While studying French literature at SNU in 1962, he made his debut in literature by publishing his literary critique ‘Essay of Narcissus - Issue of Poetry and Evil’ in ‘Free Literature.’  Based on his extensive reading, detailed yet sharp analysis of works, broad intellectual interest encompassing all of the humanities, and his clear and beautiful writing style, he has been evaluated as the first critic who raised the field of critiques from being parasitic on creative works to an independent literary genre. Poet Hwang Ji-woo said that Kim Hyeon was a ‘once-in-a-century critic,’ exemplifying just how much of a deep and broad impact Kim Hyeon had on Korean literature during his time. According to a survey by Yonsei University Graduate School in the late 90s, he took second place following Professor Rhee Young-hee as the most influential scholar in Korean academia in the 20th century.  Kim Hyeon wrote over 240 literary critiques and books and also authored the ‘Literary History of Korea’ together with Kim Yoon-shik. He also exhibited profound interest in other areas ranging from the classics to contemporary, thereby writing several books such as ‘Existence and Language,’ ‘Status of Korean Literature,’ and ‘Analysis and Interpretation.’ Furthermore, as a scholar of French literature, he also displayed a much interest in researching foreign literature in order to read between the lines of our literature and find meaning there through a more global and universal perspective. He received the Foreign Literature Thesis Award and the First Palbong Critical Literature Award (1989), among others.

stories.title: Information on Daeban-dong
stories.script: Yudal Recreation Area refers to the 300m beach between Shinan Beach Hotel and Mokpo National Maritime University, and the streets in its vicinity. Daeban-dong Coast offers a stunning scenery of perfect harmony between Mokpo Bridge and the sea. The view of the archipelago seen from here has been part of the Nine Sceneries of Mokpo even before Mokpo Bridge was built. Mokpo Bridge was erected in the shape of a crane in 2012. The beauty of Mokpo Bridge that illuminates like a crane in the night sky, the countless lights leading to Goha-do (Is.), and the stars sparkling between them were so beautiful that it was selected as a nighttime tourist destination by the Korea Tourism Organization.  The Skywalk offers thrilling excitements of walking over the sea 15m up in the sky. At night, you can enjoy the sparkling ocean that reflects the lights under your feet, the lights at the top of Yudalsan (Mt.), and the shining nightscape of Daeban-dong all at once.  Panoramic views of Mokpo Bridge and the seas of Mokpo can be enjoyed on the Skywalk. It is opened from 9 a.m. To 9 p.m. Between March and October and from 9 a.m. To 8 p.m. from November to February, and it is free of charge. Entry at night is restricted to prevent accidents.

stories.title: Information on Goha-do
stories.script: Goha-do is an island where you can enjoy pine trees while walking over the ocean. It is a beautiful island located at the foot of Yudalsan (Mt.) It is in the shape of a large crouching dragon. The Dragon Head and pine trees that embrace the front ocean of Mokpo were known as some of the best sceneries of Mokpo from long ago. Goha-do is close to Mokpo, just 1.2km away from the city. But before the construction of Mokpo Bridge in 2012, it was a remote island that could only be reached by boat.   There are many tourist attractions to enjoy the beautiful views of Goha-do. A 1,080m coastal desk was constructed from the Goha-do Observatory to the Goha-do Dragon Head. The coastal deck that was built over the sea offers a sensational feeling, as if walking on top of the sea while listening to the waves crashing over stones. You can also appreciate the pine trees that rise magnificently between the coastal caves, which is in itself beautiful natural scenery of Goha-do, as well as the coastal cliffs. There is a Yi Sun-shin photo zone to remember the feats of Admiral Yi who saved Korea by organizing the navy while staying 106 days here at the center of the deck, and there is also the Dragon Head photo zone at the end of the deck. Other attractions include Goha-do cable car, Goha-do black pine forest, cotton experience center, cotton garden, and the Honam National Institute of Biological Resources.

stories.title: Information on Samhak-do
stories.script: Samhak-do is an island of the legend of three cranes landing down. Legend has it that three women who loved one man passed away and became cranes. Those cranes fell and died, and at this place, the island of Samhak-do sprang up. This island is located in the front seas of Mokpo, Jeollanam-do, and it is one of the symbols of Mokpo.   Currently, Samhak-do connects Sosamhak-do, Jungsamhak-do, and Daesamhak-do with small bridges. Therefore, visitors can walk on the trail along Samhak-do Park or enjoy the beautiful nightscapes.  Samhak-do is home to the Mokpo Marine Science Museum for Children that offers various experiences related to the sea, Kim Dae-jung Nobel Peace Prize Memorial Hall that was built to commemorate the 15th president of the Republic of Korea, and Lee Nan-young Park for remembering the late Lee Nan-young who sang Tears of Mokpo.

stories.title: Information on Gatbawi Rock
stories.script: Gatbawi, which was designated as natural monument no. 500, is a rock in the shape of two people wearing satgat (traditional bamboo hat) standing next to each other. It is a welded tuff made when volcanic ashes hardened. Gatbawi is made up of two rocks. The larger one is 8m and the smaller one is about 6m.  The pair of rocks have a few legends. Long ago, a son who did not support his ill father well wanted to bury his dead father on a sunny grave site. But he made a mistake and dropped the coffin in the ocean. The son wearing a satgat stayed here thinking that he could not dare look up into the heavens because he dishonored his father, and ended up dying here. It was said that later two large stones rose up and the large rock was called ‘father rock,’ and the smaller rock was called ‘son rock.’ Thus, Gatbawi was given its name because it looks like a father and son wearing satgat are standing next to each other. Gatbawi is also called Satgatbawi. Another legend is that Buddha and his entourage were on their way to Yeongsangang (Riv.) and they stopped here and took of their satgat to take a rest. But they left their satgat here and left, and so it is also called Jungbawi (monk rock) or Seunimbawi (Buddhist priest rock). Gatbawi got its mysterious apperance because it is located right where seawater meets freshwater and it repeated the process of wetting and drying countless times with water containing salt when the waves crashed onto the stone surface or when there is fog. The silica melted in the water deposit there and then the parts that are dissolved causes the composition to soften and weaken, and that is why it has a hard part in the shape of a hat and there are weathering pits in the shape of a dented hive toward the bottom. In the past, Gatbawi could only be seen by taking a boat. But now, there is a pedestrian bridge that was constructed in the front ocean so that visitors can see the rock on top of the sea just by walking on the bridge, without having to take a boat.  The total length of the marine pedestrian bridge on top of the water is 298m and has a width of 3.6 to 4.6m. During high tide, it rises by about 1m, and at low tide, it drops with the water. The additional construction of a 118m wooden bridge, 40m walking bridge, and a 140m pontoon, together with the pedestrian bridge’s nightscape lighting offers a beautiful view at night that creates a romantic mood.

stories.title: Information on Peace Square
stories.script: Mokpo Peace Square is a representative tourist attraction of Mokpo where an ocean fountain puts on a spectacular performance.  This area was originally public waters, but was established through a reclamation project that lasted over 7 years and 5 months from February 1994 to July 2001. The park was first named Migwan Square, but it was renamed to the Peace Square in 2001 to commemorate President Kim Dae-jung winning the Nobel Peace Prize.  On top of the road that stretches out along the seas at Peace Square, many people enjoy the vigor of life riding inline skates, bicycles, etc.  There are also convenience facilities for families and couples, and it is a general cultural space used for sports culture, family culture, and outdoor performances. Many performances are held with the dancing ocean fountain in the background at this spacious and safe square. The ocean fountain show that unfolds in harmony with music puts on fantastic performances with lovely tunes having beautiful stories, brilliant lighting, and a massive gushing of water. There are also a number of programs such as accepting stories from visitors to introduce their story through the sea fountain, marriage proposals, etc.  The dancing water fountain puts on a total of three performances every day at 8 p.m., 8:30 p.m., and 9 p.m. in the summer from June to August, and also at 8 p.m., 8:30 p.m., and 9 p.m. in the spring from April to May and fall from September to November.  There are no fountain shows on Mondays. Also, shows are not performed during the cold winter season from December to March. For details, please check the below schedule or the dancing ocean fountain website.

stories.title: Information on the Mokpo National Maritime Museum
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Mokpo National Maritime Museum
stories.script: The Mokpo National Maritime Museum is the only national institute in Korea that finds, studies, exhibits and researches underwater cultural heritages in the sea.  Through deep-sea exploration, ships that were sunk in the past are being salvaged and preserved, which are then put on display. It also preserves the various artifacts including ceramics inside sunken ships to use for exhibition and research. Comprehensive research on literature related to marine cultures and on islands are conducted to study the marine cultures that connect the past and present. The museum is composed of four regular exhibit halls, one special exhibit hall, an outdoor exhibit, and a children’s marine culture experience hall. The outdoor exhibit hall has on display a number of actual ships and the children’s marine culture experience hall has various experience facilities for children, and it allows children to see, touch, enjoy and learn about marine culture. Furthermore, various social education programs are offered to spread the marine culture. When entering the exhibit hall, please turn your phones off or put them on silent mode.
