Also, using flash when taking photos is prohibited for the sake of protecting the cultural heritages and for the consideration of others. We also recommend visiting the various museums and exhibit halls such as the Jade Craft Gallery where you can see traditional jade craft works, Namnong Memorial Museum that has the works of Namnong, a painter of oriental paintings of the Republic of Korea on display, the Natural History Museum, the Ceramic Livingware Museum, and the Literary Arts History Hall.

stories.title: Information on the Mokpo Natural History Museum
stories.audioTitle: Information on the Mokpo Natural History Museum
stories.script: The Natural History Museum is composed of the natural history hall and culture and arts history hall. The natural history hall has a total of seven exhibition areas such as the Central Hall and Geology Hall, and it shows 4.6 billion years of natural history of the Earth. In particular, one of only two dinosaur fossils for the prenoceratops in the world and the world-class carnivorous dinosaur nest fossil that was found and restored at Aphae-do in Sinan-gun, Jeollanam-do are on display. It has the largest scale of dinosaur models, fossils, plants, insects, birds, and fish specimens in the nation, having about 40,000 pieces on display. Realistic content technologies are applied all around the museum. At the museum lobby, there is a photo zone with an AR photo booth where visitors can take photos with many different life forms. Also in the Central Hall, visitors can enjoy a media facade performance that tells the story of the birth of Earth, in addition to large dinosaur models such as the diplodocus. At the Land Life Hall on the second floor, using the tree of life as the anchor, various birds and mammals such as African lions and birds are depicted in a harmonious manner. Furthermore, media art that expresses the four seasons of Mokpo is on display, while also having an area for healing where you can take a break. The Regional Ecosystem Hall has an eco-pool providing exploratory content in which visitors can walk along a pond ecosystem where diverse aquatic organisms live, and interact with them. Visitors are also invited to enjoy experience-type AR services to interact with various exhibits at major spots. Also, at the Ceramic Livingware Museum that is located alongside the Natural History Museum, visitors can learn about the development of ceramics from everyday ceramics to high-tech ceramics, as well as enjoy the knot workshop and the outdoor workshop to experience spinning the wheel and crafting.

stories.title: Information on Japanese Style Houses of Beonhwa-ro, Mokpo 1, 2, and 3
stories.audioTitle: Information on Japanese Style Houses of Beonhwa-ro, Mokpo 1, 2, and 3
stories.script: The Japanese Style House of Beonhwa-ro, Mokpo 1 is currently registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 718-1.  It was company housing for Fukuda Agricultural Company, which was founded in Mokpo in 1920, that engaged in farming, forestry, and the reclamation and leasing of businesses during the Japanese Occupation. This is a two-story Japanese-style house constructed in 1935 and it shows traces of Japanese residences that were built around the Mokpo Shimsang Elementary School and the Oriental Development Company. After Korea gained independence, a Korean family lived in this building and installed ondol (floor heating system) and changed the interior. These aspects are also valuable as important historical materials in the history of residential architecture in Korea. It is currently being used by the owner.   The Japanese Style House of Beonhwa-ro, Mokpo 2 is currently registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 718-2.  It was company housing for Fukuda Agricultural Company, which was founded in Mokpo in 1920, that engaged in farming, forestry, and the reclamation and leasing of businesses during the Japanese Occupation. This is a one-story Japanese-style house constructed in 1935 and it shows traces of Japanese residences that were built around the Mokpo Shimsang Elementary School and the Oriental Development Company. After Korea gained independence, a Korean family lived in this building and installed ondol (floor heating system) and changed the interior interior. These aspects are also valuable as important historical materials in the history of residential architecture in Korea. It is currently being used by the owner.  The Japanese Style House of Beonhwa-ro, Mokpo 3 is currently registered as national registered cultural heritage no. 718-3.  It was company housing for Fukuda Agricultural Company, which was founded in Mokpo in 1920, that engaged in farming, forestry, and the reclamation and leasing of businesses during the Japanese Occupation. It shows traces of Japanese residences that were built around the Mokpo Shimsang Elementary School and the Oriental Development Company in the modern period. After Korea gained independence, a Korean family lived in this building and installed ondol (floor heating system) and changed the. These aspects are also valuable as important historical materials in the history of residential architecture in Korea.

stories.title: UNESCO World Heritage Figure (Road to Mundosa Temple)
stories.audioTitle: 7. UNESCO World Heritage Figure (Road to Mundosa Temple)

stories.title: Goyang Haengjusanseong Fortress
stories.script: Historic site of the Battle of Haengju, one of the three battles of the Imjin War The historic site of the Battle of Haengju, one of the three major battles of the Imjin War! It is none other than Haengjusanseong Fortress located in Goyang, Gyeonggi-do Province. This is the place where General Gwon Yul defeated an attacking force of 30,000 Japanese with less than 10,000 troops. It is widely known that women carried rocks in their aprons to fight against the Japanese invaders during the battle, and that this is the reason why the fortress was named after the word Haengju, meaning apron. However, this is not correct.  Shall we look around the Haengjusanseong Fortress? The braille and voice-type tourist information board is available by the gate. Once you get inside, the statue of General Kwon Yul and reliefs representing the Battle of Haengju will first come into your sight. If you touch a miniature relief for persons with visual impairments, you can feel the battle that took place 430 years ago at the tip of your fingers.  Unfortunately, most paths in the fortress are uphill, so it may be difficult for mobility disadvantaged persons to walk around the place. They can still take a ride on a cart, which is available at no charge, to look around the fortress. The first stop is the Memorial Hall. Advanced weapons including hwacha (multiple rocket launcher), singijeon (Korean fire arrow rocket), and suchaseokpo (stone canon), and various relics during the Joseon Dynasty are on display. Make sure wheelchair users accompany someone as the slope of entrance is quite steep.  The next stop is Chunguijeong Pavilion, which is currently used to play a video of the Haengju Battle. Sign language is also provided for those with audio disabilities. The access path to the building has a gentle slope, which is suitable for a wheelchair user and persons with disabilities. It has a barrier-free toilet inside the building as well. If you stand on the observatory deck located next to Chunguijeong Pavilion, an audio guide explaining the landscape will be played to help persons with visual impairments to imagine the view as well.  At the top of the fortress, you can see the Battle of Haengju Monument. It was constructed by the soldiers of General Gwon Yul after he passed away, which is around 420 years ago.  The final stop is a rest area. There is a wide pedestrian passage and a round table accessible by a wheelchair to catch your breath after a tour around the fortress. Let's wrap up this tour by looking at a 3D photo exhibition where you can see and feel all four seasons of the fortress.

stories.title: Goyang Haengjusanseong Fortress History Park
stories.script: Goyang Haengjusanseong Fortress History Park A riverside trail embracing the view of the mouth of Hangang River  Let's take a tour around the Haengjusanseong Fortress History Park, a treasure-like tourist spot to take a rest while looking at the Hangang River! Located between Banghwadaegyo Bridge and Haengjudaegyo Bridge, the park is flat and easily accessible by people of all ages to take a nice walk. It is also a barrier-free park equipped with facilities for mobility disadvantaged persons.  There is a parking space for persons with disabilities that can accommodate four vehicles. It also has a separate restroom exclusive for those with disabilities. For wheelchair users, the park removed steps from the parking lot to the toilet. In addition, there is a braille and voice-type tourist information board in front of the entrance, facilitating the visit of persons with visual impairments.  The first spot we will visit inside the park established along the Hangang River is the Ppallaeteo Observatory, where local women used to wash their laundry in the past. Ppallaeteo means a wash place in Korean. A wide wooden deck is installed so that everyone can get close to the riverside. And for their safety, a tempered glass fence surrounds the deck.  Walking along the deck from the observatory, a small fishing boat comes in the sight. The fishing boat sculpture was created based on the painting Haenghogwaneodo by the painter Jeong Seon from the Joseon Dynasty. A container-like building behind it is the Janghang Beodeul Eel Exhibition Center, where you can see species living at the mouth of the Hangang River, an environmentally protected area. 1.8-meter-wide wooden deck with rails add convenience to your entrance. The park provides a miniature of birds, such as grey heron, whooper swan, and Eurasian spoonbill, that can also be touched with hands for the tactile experience.  Last but not least, there is Haenghojeong Pavilion, an observatory made by repairing an actual military guard post. From the observatory, you can see the wide open mouth of the Hangang River at a glance. The access path was paved with precast pavers and equipped with a wheelchair lift, making it accessible for those with physical difficulties. From the observatory, a beautiful panoramic view from Banghwadaegyo Bridge to Haengjudaegyo Bridge unfolds before your eyes.

stories.title: Goyang Haengju Community Center
stories.script: A travel platform that plays the central role in the tourism of Haengju Village If you are planning to travel around the Haengjusanseong Fortress, how about visiting the Haengju Community Center first? Haengju Community Center, which plays the pivotal role in the tourism of Haengju Village, provides tourist information and allows visitors to have a variety of experiences and enjoy unique exhibitions related to Haengjusanseong Fortress.  First of all, you can get information about the customized programs and travel courses designed for the travel disadvantaged persons, such as persons with disabilities and the elderly. A braille and voice-type tourist information board at the wall provides tourist information for everyone.  Next is the Experience Zone. Various experiences from learning the history of Haengjusanseong Fortress and making an apron await you. Inside the Experience Zone, facilities for the travel disadvantaged such as a rapid-charger for electric wheelchairs and a nursing room are available so that visitors can conveniently look around the place. Multiple Haengjusanseong Fortress-related experience programs take place in other spaces as well.  Let's move on to the Haechan Songhak Laver Museum next to the Center. Here, you can see the process of making laver using seaweed harvested from the cleanest waters of the Western Sea of Korea. Machines used for making laver add to a vivid experience. You can taste 36 different types of laver and make gimbap with the laver as well. This experience is particularly popular among foreign tourists who are interested in Korean foods. There are other programs to experience Korean culture, such as wearing Korean traditional clothes Hanbok and experiencing Korean traditional culture.  This five-story building with a basement floor is a barrier-free building. The information desk is lowered to the eye level of wheelchair users and there is a toilet for persons with disabilities. An outdoor garden on the third floor is nicely decorated with sotdae (pillar with a carved bird on its top), jangseung (Korean traditional totem pole), dolhareubang (stone statue), and other ornaments representing the beauty of Korean tradition. The ramp slope and wooden deck are installed for the convenience of wheelchair users. It would be a great idea to take a rest here where you can see the surrounding panoramic view.

stories.title: Gangneung Heo Gyun and Heo Nanseolheon Memorial Park
stories.audioTitle: Gangneung Heo Gyun and Heo Nanseolheon Memorial Park
stories.script: The birthplace of the best female poet of Joseon Have you ever heard of Heo Nanseolheon and Heo Gyun, representative poets and writers of Gangneung in the Joseon Dynasty? Heo Gyun is the writer of the novel Hong Gil-dong jeon (The Tale of Hong Gil-dong), which is the first novel written in Korean, and Heo Nanseolheon is his older sister and a representative poet of the time. This place is established to commemorate them. The memorial park is harmonized with a graceful traditional Korea house and a pine forest. To support the travel disadvantaged persons, chargers for electric wheelchairs are placed by the entrance, and the wheelchair and stroller can be rented for free.  It is recommended to start your tour at the Heo Gyun and Heo Nanseolheon Memorial Hall, which is naturally connected with a wooden deck from the entrance. This is where detailed introductions about two authors and their literary works are on display. The five members of Heo’s family, including her father Heo Yeop, the eldest brother Heo Sung, second oldest brother Heo Bong, Heo Nanseolheon herself and her younger brother Heo Gyun, were known to be talented literary writers. Outside the Memorial Hall, you can see five memorial stones to praise them, each of which contains a poem wrote by each one of them.  Passing through the stone monuments, a historic house in Chodang-dong awaits you at the site of Heo Nanseolheon's birth home. The real birthplace of Heo Nanseolheon was demolished in the past. The one here is newly built. Upon entering through a tall gate, you can see a wide yard, sarangchae (men’s quarter) and main building behind it. The pine forest behind the house is said to have existed way before the birth of Heo Nanseolheon. Some say that it was planted by her father to celebrate her birth.  If you go into the pine forest along the trail, you can see a sign saying the “Site of Hoseojangseogak,” which was the library created by Heo Gyun for Confucian scholars and students. Only its site remains today.  Shall we go to the last spot, the Traditional Tea Experience Center across the Memorial Hall? Wheelchair users can enter the center easily by using the ramp behind the building. It is also recommended to take a cup of hot tea and walk into the pine tree forest to wrap up the tour of the Heo Gyun and Heo Nanseolheon Memorial Park.

stories.title: Gangneung Unification Park
stories.script: A park wishing for peaceful unification There is a unification park with the desire for the peaceful unification of Korea in Gangneung. Gangneung Unification Park is a war park exhibiting various war weapons, including combat planes, tanks, and armored cars, and exhibits related to wars in Korea and national security. The reason why the unification park was established in Gangneung is that Gangneung is the place where the North Korean forces landed during the Korean War and where North Korean submarine invaded the South on September 18, 1996.  The park is divided into the Unification Security Exhibition Hall and the Air Force Exhibition Hall. Let’s first go to the Air Force Exhibition Hall. It is connected to the parking lot and has a ramp for wheelchair users. At the exhibition hall, fighter jets that once defended South Korean airspace add dignity to the place. The War Monument of Gangneung District is built to honor the contribution of the Air Force and to commemorate the dead during the Korean War.  Next is the Unification Security Exhibition Hall. Since the two sites are fairly far apart, we recommend you drive there. At the exhibition hall, you can learn the history of the overcoming of national crisis along with the Korean War, as well as see various exhibits related to unification. In particular, items used during the battle, photos taken during wars, and diorama vividly describe the sorrow of one nation divided into North and South. The exhibition provides a charging service for an electric wheelchair, and the barrier-free design allows wheelchair users or visitors with strollers to enjoy the exhibition without any difficulty.  Now, shall we move on to the outdoor exhibition? You can see M48 Patton, armored tanks, howitzers, and other army armaments on display. There is a photo zone facing towards the East Sea in front of the exhibition hall. The safety guard is made out of tempered glass so that you can safely and clearly see the view of the East Sea.  The last place is the Imhae Natural Recreation Forest behind the Unification Security Exhibition Hall. This destination is the only place where you can see the mountains and sea at the same time. Some rooms are equipped with restroom, kitchen, and sink for those with disabilities. In addition, a parking space for persons with disabilities is located right in front of the building. Let's take a trip to the Unification Park and enjoy the travel from sightseeing to accommodation.

stories.title: Gangneung Solhyang Arboretum
stories.script: The one and only pine tree themed arboretum in Korea Did you know that there is the one and only pine tree themed arboretum in Korea? It's Gangneung Solhyang Arboretum. The primeval forest full of Korean red pines harmonized with various flowers and trees creates different landscape each season. Seomseokcheon Stream that runs across the arboretum adds picturesqueness to it.  The arboretum includes a wooden deck trail to the forest and a paved road to various exhibition halls. Even though all the paths are constructed to be barrier-free so that wheelchairs and baby strollers can move freely, it is recommended to accompany someone to go up and down slopes. There are also many facilities for the travel disadvantaged persons inside the arboretum. At the visitor shelter by the entrance of the arboretum, chargers for electric wheelchairs are placed; at the information center across the shelter, visitors can rent a wheelchair or a baby stroller free of charge. There are toilets for persons with disabilities inside the arboretum.  The first exhibition hall you meet after entering the arboretum is the Azalea Garden. In spring, the place looks as if red carpet is laid along the ridge. Along the path from the Azalea Garden to the Rock Garden, flower trees, which live on natural rocks, stones, and sands, create an ink landscape painting-like view. In the Medicinal Plant Garden, located upward from the Rock Garden, plants that have long been used to treat diseases and improve health can be found. In the Subtropical Garden, you can see siebold’s chinquapin, box-leaved hollies, and Hallasan juniperus chinensis, which can only be found in the southern coast of Korea and Jeju Island. Lastly, at the Greenhouse Exhibition Garden, warm-temperate and subtropical vegetation can be observed.  Exhibition halls, particularly the Azalea Garden, Rock Garden, Medicinal Plant Garden, and Greenhouse, are equipped with a tactile and voice assistant board. You can visualize the appearance of flowers by feeling the embossed plants in each hall with the tip of your fingers.  On your way down after looking around the Greenhouse Exhibition Garden, you will find a wooden deck leading to the forest. This path, passing through the Ecological Observation Trail and Pine Forest Plaza, will take you to the Dye Plant Garden, Healing Road, Sky Garden, and the Woodland Walks. Enjoying various forest experiences and breathing in the fresh air of the pine forest will take your tiredness away.

stories.title: Chungju World Martial Arts Park
stories.script: Gathering the martial arts of the world in one place! Do you know where is the home of Taekkyeon, a traditional Korean martial art which is inscribed on the list of UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity? The answer is Chungju. The World Martial Arts Festival is held in Chungju, Chungcheongbuk-do Province to globalize Taekkyeon. The major venue is the Chungju World Martial Arts Park, which is a beloved shelter by residents on regular days.  The park includes the Main Stage, World Martial Arts Museum, Outdoor Stage, Forest Playground, Stone Maze, and Floor Fountain. Suitable for a global festival, most paths do not have any raised steps and have a ramp so that wheelchair users can look around conveniently. The best course to look around the park is to start from the main gate parking lot. This is because all facilities including a parking space and a restroom for persons with disabilities, tourist information center where you can rent a stroller or a wheelchair, and nursing room are here at the parking lot. It is recommended to check the location of facilities and barrier-free route through the braille and voice-type tourist information board to avoid wandering around the park to find a place you need. If you need further assistance or audio guide, call the number written on the board.  How about planning your tour course centering around the Peace Road? The Peace Road connects the Main Stage, Peace Plaza where Aqua Ring Fountain is located, and the Forest Playground in a straight line. On the left side of the road, you can savor a quiet and secluded moment at the Outdoor Stage, Playground, and Tangeum Pond; on the right, there are many things to see and experience, such as Daecheongmaru Rest Area, Larva Land, World Martial Arts Museum and Water Playground. Chungju World Martial Arts Museum is another place to stop by to learn about the history of Korean martial arts including Taekkyeon. The interior of the museum is designed to be barrier-free and all floors are accessible by an elevator, allowing everyone to enjoy the place.  Chungju World Martial Arts Park has a barrier-free playground where all children, regardless of their disability status, can play together. For example, the swing in the Forest Playground has a large net as a chair, allowing both children with and without disabilities to ride on it. The Wheelchair Rotating Stage is a ride that can be used by wheelchair users. When a person sits on the ride, other person outside the ride can push and spin it.  In summer, family tourists with children come to the Water Playground. The park has a dedicated wheelchair to use in the pool as well. Chungju Martial Arts Park full of attractions is a must-visit tourist destination.

stories.title: Chungjuho Tourist Area
stories.script: Colorful and exciting tour Let's go to Chungjuho Tourist Area, a colorful and exciting destination full of hands-on experiences! If you want to travel around Chungjuho Tourist Area ranging from the Tangeum Lake International Boat Race Course to the Marina Center, you may want to stop by the Tourist Information Center first. This is because there is a tourist information board that provides voice guide as well as a braille map to identify the location of major facilities and barrier-free roads. It also provides free wheelchair and stroller rental service, as well as fast chargers for electric wheelchairs.  Let’s look at the Arts and Cultural House, which is located close to the Tourist Information Center. Although it is a classical and traditional Hanok building, it constructed a ramp so that everyone can enter easily. Visitors can try garments such as Hanbok, clothes from the time of enlightenment, and school uniforms, as well as adaptive clothes that anyone can wear without difficulty.  Walking along the Tangeumho Lake from the Arts and Cultural House, the Tangeum Lake International Boat Race Course awaits you. You can see the lovebird-themed mascots Tani and Geumi, which were named after Tangeumho Lake, standing at the entrance of the Boat Race Course. Constructed for the 2013 World Rowing Championships, there are Grandstand, Finish Tower, and Marina Center inside the race course.  The Grandstand is a place used as a viewing seat and a press box during rowing matches. As it faces the wide-open lake, it is the prime location to stare at the water and enjoy the surrounding view. The Finish Tower standing next to it embodied the shape of a national treasure Seven-Story Stone Pagoda in Tappyeong-ri, and the Marina Center behind the tower is built with the motif of boat and paddle in rowing.  The first floor of the Marina Center is the Chungju Experience Tourist Center, which provides various services for you to enjoy Chungju. What is noticeable is that it provides a rental service of an upcycled bicycle, as well as a hand-cycle and electric-assist bicycles for those with disabilities. Riding around the Chungjuho Tourist Area on a rented bicycle is a must. Feel the nice lake breeze and ride around the Tangeumho Lake!

stories.title: Chungju Jungangtap Park
stories.script: Be the leading actor at a historical site Do you know Seven-Story Stone Pagoda in Tappyeong-ri, Chungju, a towering national treasure set before the beautiful scenery of the Namhangang River? Standing 14.5 meters in height, the Seven-Story Stone Pagoda is the tallest of the extant stone pagodas built in the Unified Silla Period. It is also referred to as the Jungangtap, meaning the “central pagoda,” because it is located in the middle of the Korean Peninsula. A legend says the place where two people departing from the end of north and south met was marked as the center and a pagoda was built during the Unified Silla Period.  The rest area established around the Jungangtap Pagoda is the Jungangtap Park. The most effective way to walk around the park is to start off with the parking space for persons with disabilities in front of Chungju Museum or by the Chungju Tangeumho Water Park. This is because the path adjacent to the sidewalk is equipped with a gentle slope where wheelchairs can freely travel.  The distance from the braille information board marking facilities in the park to the Jungangtap Pagoda where a restroom for persons with disabilities is located is 100 meters long. As it is paved flat without any bumps, anyone can come and go without experiencing any difficulty. As the pagoda is placed on a tall two-story platform, you have to walk up the stairs. Even though there is no separate pathway for the travel disadvantaged persons, there is a miniature of the pagoda, which is 1/30th the size of the actual tower by the first stair. By referring to the information board, you can estimate the size and shape of the pagoda with your hands.  Behind the pagoda, there is Chungjuho Lake Sculpture Park neighboring the Namhangang River. Appreciating various sculptures placed across the park following a trail, you would see a filming site for the Korean TV series Crash Landing on You and Vincent. There is a low wooden bench for both persons with and without disabilities on the path towards the Namhangang River, making it a perfect place to enjoy a quiet mood while looking at the water.  If you want to savor the atmosphere of the Namhangang River closely, walk down onto Tangeumho Rainbow Road. Established to broadcast live the 2013 World Rowing Championships, it is accessible by a wheelchair along the ramp. A safety fence is installed for your safety as well. Rainbow lightings add a romantic mood at night.

stories.title: Gunsan Time Travel Village
stories.script: Time travel to the 1930s in Gunsan Do you know which Korean city still holds the sad history back in the 1930s? It's a harbor city, Gunsan. Gunsan had become a base of plundering crops cultivated and harvested from the Honam Plains by the Japanese. Buildings centering around the inner harbor of Gunsan built in the 1930s sill remain today, making Gunsan the city of modern history museum.  Gunsan Time Village encompasses the inner port of Gunsan port to Impi Station through the Honam Customs Museum, which was the former Gunsan Customs, and Modern Architecture Museum, which used to be the Gunsan branch of Josen Bank. Tourist attractions are all close to each other, 10 to 20 minutes in walking distance, making it convenient to travel on foot. 1-km-long tour course connecting the parking lot to the Jinpo Marine Park has barrier-free pedestrian passages for the convenience of wheelchair users. You can check your route in advance with the braille and voice-type tourist information board by this barrier-free pathway. Gunsan Time Travel Village provides free rental service of unique bicycles for persons with and without disabilities to ride together. You can call the Gunsan City Tourism Promotion Division for more details.  If you are ready, let's travel back in time. We will start off with the Gunsan Modern History Museum located at the end of the parking of the inner port of Gunsan. This museum features the Modern Life Hall, showing the life of Gunsan in the 1930s, Heroes of Independence Hall, and Marine Logistics History Hall. All entrances are barrier-free so that wheelchair users can enjoy the museum without any difficulty.  The red western-style building located next to the museum is the former customs office. Built in European architectural style, the edifice is a marvel to look at. It was designated as a state-designated cultural property for its high historical value. Following the wide and straight Haemang-ro, you can see the Former Japanese 18th Bank. It was the local branch of a Japanese bank and the Gunsan branch of Joseon Bank, which appears in the epic novel The Muddy Current by the writer Chae Man-sik.  We will end the tour after stopping by the Jinpo Marine Park, opened to commemorate the Jindodaecheop Battle, a victory of Jinpo in naval combat against Japanese forces led by General Choi Mu-seon during the Goryeo Dynasty. There are retired military crafts including landing vehicles tracked and F-86 jet fighter. Rest area in the park are equipped with chargers for electric wheelchairs and tables for wheelchair users for you to take a quick rest before ending the tour.

stories.title: Gunsan Gyeongam-dong Railroad Village
stories.script: The memory of the railroad village from the 70s and 80s Have you ever seen the view of the railroad crossing between old shacks? A defunct railroad track filled with old-school cafes and shops lined up on both sides creates a unique landscape. 300-meter-long area connecting the Yeonan Intersection of Gunsan to the Jinpo Intersection is called the Gyeongam-dong Railroad Village.  Since the tour course crosses the railroad tracks and sidewalks, it is better to get a brochure indicating the barrier-free route. You can get the brochure from the information center, which can be accessed by wheelchair users as the place replaced the threshold with an automatic door and has a restroom for persons with disabilities. Across the center, there is a tourism kiosk placed at the eye level of wheelchair users and a braille and voice-type tourist information board.  Let’s then start the journey to the Gyeongam-dong Railroad Village. After taking a nice picture in front of a large train model, we will walk along the old tracks. Houses lined up on both sides of the railway in the 1970s bring up the image of a filming site. In 1944, during the Japanese colonial area, this railroad was constructed to transport papers used for newspapers. Later on, people have begun to flock around along the railway and formed a village in the 1970s. Villagers would pull away their laundry near the railway when the train approached, listening to the whistle alarming them.  In the Gyeongam-dong Railroad Village, there are many barrier-free roads considering the mobility disadvantaged persons. First, the four sections connecting the pedestrian road in the north and south roads are paved flat so that wheelchair users can come and go comfortably. In addition, most stores located nearby have a gentle ramp and automatic doors. At the dalgona (Korean sugar and baking soda candy) experience place, even tables for wheelchair users are placed. In particular, on the north side of the railroad track, facilities that interfere with walking including manhole covers are removed and a safety fence is installed on the 300-meter-long roadside. These careful considerations make the trip more enjoyable.

stories.title: Iksan Prison Filming Set
stories.script: Chance to become the leading actor in Prison Playbook! Aren't you wondering where all the prison scenes from Korean movies and TV series are filmed at? They were all filmed here at the Iksan Prison Filming Set. Remodeled branch school of an abandoned elementary school, this is the only prison filming set in Korea. As many as 200 Korean movies and TV series including Miracle in Cell No.7, The War of Flowers, and Sunflower were all filmed here.  Many K-content fans and those who are curious about the inside of a prison visit here. Small court, jail, visiting room, and main set are connected centering around the wide field. Starting your tour from the parking lot for persons with disabilities by the small court would be the best. This is because there is a braille and voice-type tourist information board installed next to the parking lot, and this is the starting point of the barrier-free roads paved for the convenience of all people.  The small court is used to film trial scenes. The prosecutor’s seat and the lawyer’s seat face each other on the left and right sides of the judge’s seat at the front. From the costume shop across the small court, you can rent a prisoner’s uniform and a prison officer’s uniform. It would be more entertaining to look around with a costume on.  After passing through the small court, the real prison tour begins. On the way to jail, you can see a wide field. The lookout tower behind the field is the prime location to see a panoramic view of the filming set. However, you have to walk up many stairs, thus limiting the entrance of wheelchair users. The small court is connected with a gentle ramp with a safety rail to the jail. Both sides of the rail have directional signs in braille for the persons with visual impairments.  What’s noticeable is a rest area. In addition to a restroom for persons with disabilities, a nursing room is equipped with a toilet, a diaper deck, and a nursing couch. You can feel how scrupulous attention is paid to the convenience of visitors.  The highlight of this place is the route that connects jail, visiting room and the main set. Most jail scenes you saw in Korean TV series and films are all filmed here. This place is open for visitors as well. The visiting room is divided into security and the visiting space. The main prison set includes interrogation rooms and first and second-floor cells where prisoners are confined. Unfortunately, Cell 3-16 which appeared in the movie Miracle in Cell No.7 is located on the second floor, making it difficult for wheelchair users to look around.

stories.title: Iksan Kosrak
stories.script: Traditional paste fermented in 4,000 earthenware pots Can you picture a whopping 4,000 traditional Korean earthenware pots in the 99,173 m2-wideyard? You can smell doenjang (soybean paste) and gochujang (red chili paste) that fill the area. Kosrak is a pure Korean word meaning best of the best. It is a cultural experience center located in Iksan, Jeollabuk-do.  Kosrak can be largely divided into two spaces. Diving the place with the ramp at the center, there is Ewha Garden, which is a restaurant, in the upper area; there is cafe, an underground fermentation space, and Jangdok Garden in the lower area. All of them have parking lots for persons with disabilities, making it easy to go back and forth between the two spaces. In particular, in the parking lot on the lower area, a braille and voice-type tourist information board is installed. Inside the Management Office, there is a restroom for persons with disabilities as well as a nursing room.  Shall we look around the Jangdok Garden first? The garden has a whopping 4,000 Korean earthenware pots called hangari. It is a photogenic place harmonized with pine trees against the backdrop. How about taking a walk on the pine tree forest embracing pots outside the garden? As the roads are paved flat, even wheelchair users can look around and take pictures while savoring the mood and the moment.  In order to introduce the excellence of Korean fermented food to the world, there are various experience programs prepared for the visitors. At a cafe across the rest area, you can make onion-apple vinegar, ready-made gochujang, cheonggukjang cookie, and more. In particular, a customized sink for wheelchair users is installed so that you can use the sink and storage space while sitting in a wheelchair. Activities for hands-on experience to make fermented foods are only available on a reservation basis.  The last place to visit is the underground fermentation space to ferment organic soy sauce and vinegar. There is a gentle ramp at the entrance for convenient access. Inside the fermentation space, enormous pots are lined up after one another, all of which were baked in the old conventional way in a traditional kiln, creating a different mood under soft halogen lighting.

stories.title: Sunchang Gangcheonsan County Park
stories.script: Hidden secret forest in Sunchang Gangcheonsan County Park, located in Sunchang, Jeollabuk-do Province, is the first county park in Korea. Parks designated and managed by si (city) or gun (county) are referred to as county parks. Gangcheonsan County Park, featuring Gangcheonsan, Sanseongsan, and Gwangdeoksan Mountains, has the shape of two dragons waving their tails toward the sky and ascending to heaven.  There are three courses you can take to enjoy the park — barefoot trail along the valley, deck trail going around the mountainside, and hiking trail from Gangcheonsan Mountain to Gwangdeoksan Mountain passing Sanseongsan Mountain. A 5.5-km-long barefoot trail is a roundtrip course that passes through Byeongpung Falls and Gancheonsa Temple. It is also a barrier-free trail for everyone.  Let's walk the barefoot trail, shall we? A barrier-free path from the parking lot to the ticket booth and a gentle slope allows wheelchair users to move around conveniently. In addition, there is a braille and voice-type tourist information board next to the ticket booth. The park provides a free stroller and a wheelchair rental service. In consideration of dirt roads, offroad wheelchairs are available.  Once you get inside the park, you can listen to the clear sound of water running down, making you feel refreshed. You can see the Byeongpung Falls 200 meters away from the entrance, which is the starting point and the destination of the barefoot trail. Byeongpung Falls crashing against the rocks and stones from 40 meters high into two streams is picturesque. The valley under the falls has a rather shallow water level and slow-flowing current, which is a perfect place to enjoy water. The path down to the valley has a gentle slope with a safety rail to assist wheelchair users to get close to the valley easily. Instead of getting inside the water, you can enjoy foot-bathing instead. The place is safe for wheelchair users as the place has no bumps. There are safety rails and tables as well.  The scenery of the path connecting the falls and Gangcheonsa Temple is beautiful enough to attract painters who want to capture the splendid view of valley and dense forest on canvas. Woody fragrance wafting through the air and the sound of birds chirping will keep you company. Even wheelchair users can feel the atmosphere of Gangcheonsan Mountain following the forest path paved with decomposed granite soil.

stories.title: Sunchang Seomjingang Hyangga Auto Campground
stories.script: Time of healing amid the nature Let's get on a trip to a picturesque campground where the Seomjingang River flows and Okchulsan Mountain stands in the background. Located in Sunchang, Jeollabuk-do Province, it is the prime location to enjoy quiet camping as there are few residences and traffic jam. You can choose the camping type to your taste between auto camping, glamping and bungalow. What makes this place unique is that it is an open campground with barrier-free design.  The Campground No. 1 has 29 camping sites and 10 glamping facilities available for persons with and without disabilities. You may want to check out a guide brochure indicating barrier-free paths and facilities, as well as a braille and voice-type tourist information board at the Management Office.  Now, let’s start camping! The campground is spacious enough to accommodate a wooden deck, a large tent, and a tarpaulin. The area surrounding the campground is wide as well, and most slopes are gentle for convenient access for persons with disabilities. A parking space is located next to the camping site and a glamping space. The glamping space has a cot and a stand-up table to accommodate wheelchair users.  Convenience facilities, including a restroom, kitchen, and shower room, are clustered around the Management Office. From the restroom and the kitchen to the shower room, it is designed for wheelchair users to conveniently move around. Braille indicating hot and cold water is imprinted on the sink and faucet. If outdoor camping is overwhelming, a bungalow that has a restroom and kitchen inside can be an alternative. The sink, washstand, toilet and shower room are all wheelchair accessible. You can see considerations made for persons with disabilities as the power outlet, switch and hanger are installed at eye level of wheelchair users.  There are many things to enjoy on the campground. The ecological pond trail is suitable to feel the peaceful mood. You can even try out canoeing at the mooring next to it. With the wheelchair transfer system, wheelchair users can simply slide down the bench and use canoe safely.

stories.title: Suncheonman National Garden
stories.script: One-stop world garden tour Suncheonman National Garden is the first national garden of Korea. It has all the beautiful gardens from various countries around the world. Established on an area of 1,090,909 m2, it features the Lake Garden, KoreanGarden, World Traditional Garden, Theme Garden, etc.Dongcheon Stream running across the garden is connected by the Dream Bridge, which was made by putting 30 containers together.This bridge is also known as the “floating art museum” because it is decorated with the art work of KangIk-jung, and 140,000 works of children from all around the world.  Once you arrive at the Ticket Box following the barrier-free roads from the parking lot at East Gate and West Gate, you can check out the braille and voice-type tourist information board. There is a locker room and rental service for manual/electric wheelchair and stroller is available as well.  Let's go inside the garden. The most general course is to start at the East Gate where the Lake Garden, the landmark of Suncheonman National Garden, is located. Designed by the world-class garden designer Charles Jencks, the Lake Garden has the main hill at the center and five surrounding hills are connected to the spiral trail. Passing through the Lake Garden, the France Garden which is designed like the Versailles Palace comes into sight. It is the prime location to see the panoramic view of the Lake Garden. Anyone can easily walk up to the top using the elevator behind the building. In addition, there is a 3D tactile model of the garden by the entrance of the France Garden and the Floating Garden so that you can imagine the view with the tips of your finger.  Located next to the China Garden, Korean Traditional Medicine Experience Center is a must-visit place inside the garden. You can learn about your constitution with fingerprints or heat on your hands, and get health-related advice from a professional Korean medicine pharmacist. Once you are done looking around the Korean Traditional Medicine Experience Center, you would see Germany, Mexico, and Netherlands Garden. Do not miss the Netherlands Garden because it is so beautiful that it was even included in the Eight Scenic Views of Suncheonman National Garden. The southern exit of the Netherlands Garden naturally leads you to the metasequoia road, one of the representative photo spots of the Suncheonman National Garden. This 300-meter-long road is the prime location to take the best photo.  Looking at each country’s unique and distinctive gardens, such as the Mongolia Garden where Mongolian traditional dwelling Ger stands, as well as Italy, Spain, the U.K., and Turkey Gardens, you will feel like traveling around the world. As wheelchair-accessible shuttle is available, you can stop by all 35 spots conveniently.

stories.title: Suncheon Filming Location
stories.script: Time travel to the '60s to '80s in Seoul Bread, Love, and Dreams, which recorded the highest viewing rate of 49.3%, Love and Ambition, East of Eden, and Giant, which are all famous Korea TV series, were all filmed at the Suncheon Filming Location. As many as 70 TV series and movies against the backdrop of the '60s to '80s filming set were filmed here.  The place can be divided into three themes: downtown Suncheon in the '50s, Bongcheon-dong, Seoul in the '60s, and suburban Seoul in the '80s. Since they have been reproduced realistically through many background research, visitors would feel as if they are time traveling. Even the props and decorations used to reproduce Bongcheon-dong, Seoul, which was the background of the TV series Love and Ambition, were real waste from the shanty town.  Before we begin the tour, here are some of the information you need to know. At the Tourist Information Center by the main entrance, a brochure indicating the barrier-free routes and convenience facilities is placed. There are electronic wheelchairs that can be rented for free as well as a nursing room. The braille and voice-type tourist information board is installed at the main gate.  Shall we start looking around the filming set, thinking of the scenes from the movie or TV series that you enjoyed watching? Downtown Suncheon and Seoul suburbs are constructed on a flat field so they are accessible by everyone regardless of their physical challenges. The School Uniform Experience, the photo studio, the Gyeongseong hardware store, and other famous attractions are equipped with a gentle ramp to allow access for wheelchair tourists. Unfortunately, it is difficult for wheelchair users to access buildings with bumps and barriers.  Shall we go up to the shanty town of Bongcheon-dong located on a hill inside the filming set? Wheelchair-accessible electric carts provide a more safe and comfortable tour for family, friends, and the loved ones. Walking around the filming location will bring up the memories of the past.

stories.title: Naganeupseong Walled Town
stories.script: Traveling the past and present together Have you ever heard of the folk museum where people actually reside? The village is overall well preserved, becoming a museum itself and allowing visitors to observe houses and lifestyles that have all been passed down from the past. Among all the other walled towns, Naganeupseong preserves the lifestyle during the early days of the Joseon Dynasty far best. It was first constructed in the form of earthen fortifications to prevent the invasion from the Japanese raiders and later rebuilt into the stone fortress today.  You can notice many thoughtful considerations for persons with disabilities at the Naganeupseong Walled Town. The barrier-free pedestrian road is paved from the parking lot to the East Gate through a ticket booth and Tourist Information Center. The height of a ticket booth is lowered and a ramp is installed to allow access for wheelchair users. What's more, travel brochures and rental service of electric wheelchairs are available at the Tourist Information Center. Those who travel in an electric wheelchair can charge it for free at both the East and West Gate. The braille and voice-type tourist information board is located next to the Information Center as well. For further assistance, you can request the Tourist Information Center and get a voice guide and sign language video.  Shall we go inside to look around the Naganeupseong Walled Town? Once you get inside using the East Gate, you would be able to see that the main road divides the place into two sections: Management Office and Residential Area. At the Management Office area, there are Magistrate's office, Living Quarters, and Nangmillu Pavilion. Resource Center, located on the left of the Magistrate's office, tells the history of the Naganeupseong Walled Town with various displays. As most office buildings have gentle ramps, even wheelchair users can easily look around.  If you get a little hungry during the tour, you can visit Nanjeon. With a tavern-like interior design from the Joseon Dynasty, it sells pajeon (green onion pancake), gukbap (rice soup), and many other Korean foods. There are also tables specially designed for wheelchair users. Next to Nanjeon, there is a place where you can rent a wide range of Hanbok, or Korean traditional clothing, from traditional ones to modernized ones. Walking and looking around the town in a Hanbok will present you with a unique experience.  In the 600-year-old residential area, there are still 300 Korean traditional thatched-roof houses and 100 of them are inhabited by actual residents. You may create unforgettable memories by visiting filming sites for Korean TV series such as Dae Jang Geum and Love in the Moonlight as well as by traditional musical instrument-making experience and handicraft experience using straw and plants.

stories.title: Daegu Biseulsan County Park
stories.script: A paradise full of pink azalea There is a county park in Daegu as beautiful as a national park, which is managed by the state. Surrounding the south of Daegu like a folding screen, Biseulsan County Park is designated and managed by Dalseong-gun. This mountain was named after its figure of a spiritual one playing geomungo, a traditional Korean instrument. Every April, the field near the summit of Biseulsan Mountain blooms with azaleas. Azalea is also referred to as chamggot in Korean.  Shall we walk up to the Chamggot Habitat covering the mountain in reddish pink? It is good to start your tour from the Biseulsan Recreational Forest Parking Lot, which has a parking space for persons with disabilities, a ticket office, and an electric car stop. It takes about 30 minutes from the parking lot to the Daegyeonsa Temple by riding on a lightning bug electric cart. A small van with wheelchair lift is operated on a reservation basis.  Once you get off the station by the temple, what stands out is an observatory to look down the mountain. Block Stream, which is designated as a natural monument, is laid out along an uphill road. Block stream refers to the accumulation of gravel and rock flown down. When the sun goes down, the spectacular golden view between ridges comes into view. At the station by the temple, there is a rental station for wheelchairs and strollers, as well as chargers for an electronic wheelchair. You may find the restroom for persons with disabilities on the way to the Daegyeonsa Temple.  Wheelchair users can ride a minivan and get off at the sign stone of “Biseulsan Rainfall Radar Observatory.” The wooden barrier-free deck that stretches from the stone takes visitors to the Azalea Habitat. 990,200 ㎡-wide field nearby the Cheonwangbong Peak turns reddish pink with azaleas every spring. You can also look around the Daegyeonsa Temple, located under the rock, on your way back to the wooden deck.  Daegyeonsa Temple is a historic temple built in the Unified Silla Period. It is known that Buddhist monk Ilyeon, the author of Samguk Yusa (“Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms”), stayed as the first chief monk. The Dharma Hall and small halls next to it give a secluded atmosphere. Standing at the edge of the cliff of the yard, Daegyeonsaji Three-Story Stone Pagoda seems to look down the mountains and rivers, creating a magnificent landscape.

stories.title: Daegu Samunjin Jumakchon Village
stories.script: First place to introduce the Piano to Korea During the Joseon Dynasty, it was said that the transportation of goods in the Gyeongsang-do region took place in the Samunjin Quay. There is Samunjin Jumakchon Village that reproduced the village at the time where you can feel the mood of the area while enjoying nice food. Inside the village, there is a park and a ferry quay. All the paths are paved flat, allowing all tourists, including persons with disabilities, the elderly and families with young children, to enjoy their trip without difficulties.  Let's look around the Jumakchon Village first. Jumakchon Village with walls of red clay and a thatched roof sells delicious Korean food. The 500-year-old Japanese Hackberry enhances the elegance of the place. In particular, Jumakchon Village has a paging system for wheelchair users, facilitating all processes from ordering to returning empty tableware.  The most noticeable feature of the village is that there are many piano sculptures. One of them even says “here comes the haunted tube.” Back in the 1900s, when a missionary couple first introduced the piano through the Samunjin Quay, people were both surprised and scared at the hollow wood tub playing sounds, thereby calling it the “haunted tube.” Dalseong-gun has been hosting the “Dalseong Piano 100” since 2012. This concert is to gather 100 pianos and play at the site to commemorate the fact that the piano was first introduced to Korea through Samunjin Quay.  Now, let's go for a ferry ride. At Samunjin Quay, the very first ferry of the Nakdongang River is in operation. For around 40 minutes, the ferry sails between the Gangjeong Goryeongbo Reservoir and Samunjingyo Bridge. Visitors can take benefit of free wheelchairs and stroller rental service at the ticket booth and the fast-charging service for electric wheelchairs as well as tire pump service. With the help of the staff, wheelchair users can easily get on board. There is a wheelchair-marked area in the front row and a safety rail for safe travel. The view of Gangjeong Goryeongbo Reservoir is most beautiful. Why don't you make another unforgettable memory by looking the golden sunset on a ferry?

stories.title: Naepo Bobusang Village
stories.script: Located in Deoksan-myeon, Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do Province, this is the only bobusang (merchant) themed park in the country. It opened its doors in July 2020 on a 63,695㎡ site to remember the spirits and history of merchants of traditional societies such as the Joseon era. Called “bobusang,” they acted as middlemen between producers and consumers carrying merchandise on knapsacks or back carriers to sell in markets. This barrier-free tourist site welcomes all people, including those with strollers or wheelchairs, and houses facilities like the Yesan Bobusang Museum, a learning center, the Paeraengi Media Experience Center, a marketplace, an experience yard, and much more.  As a place for learning the traditions and culture of the Naepo merchants, and experiencing the history of distribution, the Yesan Bobusang Museum features the Yesan Promotion Hall, where visitors can learn about the region’s 1,100-year-old history and tradition; the Naepo Bobusang Story Hall, which tells the story of the merchants of Naepo and their distribution area; the Distribution Culture Experience Hall and the 4D Theater, which teaches about the distribution culture and changing history through virtual reality games; and the Special Exhibition Hall, where artifacts and materials of the merchants are displayed. Visitors can also enjoy the different aspects of the merchants through AR and VR experiences at the Paeraengi Media Experience Center.   The marketplace is a recreation of merchant activities of the past, while the experience yard offers programs for visitors to experience both traditional and modern cultures.    Also available are the Lawn Plaza, the Naepocheon Stream and the Outdoor Auditorium, as well as a media façade displaying the night travels of the merchants. And the colorful illuminations make it a great place to visit at night.   Admission fee is 11,000won for adults, 9,000won for teens, and 7,000won for children. Naepo Bobusang Village is open from 10 AM to 8 PM on weekdays, from 10 AM to 9 PM on weekends, and holidays, and is closed every Monday.  For a pleasant trip, be sure to check for latest updates prior to visiting.

stories.title: Site 1 Sudeoksa Temple
stories.script: Sudeoksa temple sits on Deoksungsan Mountain in Deoksan-myeon, Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do. Although no written records have been found to support this, it is thought by academia to have been built during the Baekje King Uideok's reign and rebuilt by Naonghwasang during the rule of Goryeo’s 31st ruler, King Gongmin. In 1865, the 2nd year of King Gojong, the 26th Joseon king, meditation master Mangong again reconstructed the temple, which continues to be the center of Korean Zen Buddhism to this day.  Sudeoksa Temple consists of a main hall and the Buddhist Art Museum, which is the first of its kind in Korea. The latter exhibits items that integrate Buddhist culture and the world of Goam Lee Ungno's art. Sudeok Inn is also nearby, where Goam Lee Ungno is said to have stayed after the Dongbaekrim Incident (known as the East Berlin Incident in English). The trail behind the main hall has 1,080 stairs and includes, among other famous sites with hidden stories, a grove cottage where master Mangong practiced asceticism.   The main hall of Sudeoksa Temple holds the Shakyamuni Buddha statue and was built in 1308, the 24th year of Goryeo’s King Chungnyeol, continuing the architectural style of Baekje. The oldest known wooden structure in the country, it is considered an important cultural asset due to the beauty of its decorative elements on the building’s sides. The gambrel roof is of a concise formation and only visible from the front and back, while it resembles a triangle from the side. This showcases the uniquely simple beauty in Buddhism. The structure was also built with entasis columns which appear thin in the middle, creating a sense of visual stability.   Rows of specialty restaurants for hungry visitors can be found at the entrance to the temple. Grilled deodeok in autumn, in particular, should not be missed.

stories.title: Site 2 Chunguisa Shrine and Yoon Bonggil Memorial
stories.audioTitle: Site 2 Chunguisa Shrine and Yoon Bonggil Memorial
stories.script: Chunguisa Shrine is located in Deoksan-myeon, Yesan-gun, and is embodied with the patriotic spirit of Yoon Bonggil, a patriot and independence activist from the Japanese occupation era. The 147,802㎡ site houses the Chunguisa Shrine where a portrait of Yoon Bonggil is kept, Gwanghyeondang where he lived for the first 4 years of his life, Jeohandang where he spent his youth, Buheungdang where he was active in the Rural Revivalism Movement, and the Yoon Bonggil Memorial where artifacts are displayed and guests can learn more and participate in a variety of experiences. The Yoon Bonggil Memorial displays 56 artifacts of the patriot Yoon Bonggil, who only lived a short but passionate life of 25 years. Magic vision screen and a variety of videos and dioramas about Yoon Bonggil's activities can also be viewed.  Active beginning in 1926 in rural social movements such as the Farmer Enlightenment and Reading Movement, Yoon Bonggil wrote educational materials to enlighten farmers and organized a night class association to teach disenfranchised adolescents in rural villages who weren't able to go to school. To improve the rural community, he established an organization called the “Revival Institute” in 1929 and pursued the Rural Revivalism Movement in earnest. With a conviction that he had to do something for his country, he went to Manchuria and resolved to join the independence movement. He later moved to Shanghai, the location of the Provisional Korean Government, where he vowed to devote his body and mind to the independence of his country, and joined the Korean Patriot Corps to resist the Japanese. On April 29, 1932, he threw a bomb into a ceremony marking the Japanese Emperor’s birthday, killing the commander of the Japanese Expeditionary Force in Shanghai. He was arrested at the scene, sentenced to death by a Japanese military court, and died for his country on December 19, 1932.   Every year from the 27th to 29th of April, the Maeheon Culture Festival is held at the Chunguisa Shrine in Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do. The theme of the festival is the youthful spirit and noble patriotism of Yoon Bonggil and the Independence Movement as a whole, and many performances, experiences, and exhibitions can be enjoyed together by couples and families. Guests can also visit the Deoksan Spa, Sudeoksa Temple, the Korea Traditional Architecture Museum, Gayasan Mountain, and the Tomb of Prince Namyeongun near Chunguisa Shrine.

stories.title: Site 3 House of Chusa
stories.script: The House of Chusa, located in Sinam-myeon, Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do, is an old structure where the late Joseon Silhak (Confucian social reform movement) scholar and calligrapher Chusa Kim Jeonghui was born. Known to be built by Chusa's great grandfather, Wolseongwi Kim Hanshin, and measuring at 266.11m² (80.5 pyeong), the house comprises the tall Munganchae (main gate), the Sarangchae (men's room) in the shape of a ㄱ (giyeok), the Anchae (main building) in the shape of a ㅁ (mieum), and the shrine where a portrait of Chusa is kept. The Sarangchae is comprised of a one-cell ondol room in the south and a two-cell ondol room to the east, while the rest is the wooden floored main hall. The Anchae has a six-cell hall and a two-cell main room along with another room across from it. The warmth and tidiness of hanok is felt in the house and the sweeping picturesque decor is cause for stopping visitors in their tracks. The House of Chusa also has the tomb of Chusa, the joint grave of his great grandfather Kim Hanshin and his wife, Princess Hwasun, and the red gate commemorating Princess Hwasun as a virtuous woman.  The Chusa Memorial features an exhibition hall where guests can view the great works of master calligrapher and epigraphist Chusa Kim Jeonghui, a theater and a souvenir shop. The permanent exhibition has 46 Chusa works throughout the year so guests can appreciate a highly-refined cultural legacy.  The Lacebark Pine Tree, a natural monument, can be seen about 600 meters north of the House of Chusa. This is a rare species of pine in Korea as it originates from northern China. The Lacebark Pine Tree of Yesan is at the entrance to the grave of his great-grandfather, Kim Heungkyung, and is said to have been planted by Chusa after he smuggled the seed inside a brush from Yanjing, Qing China when he was 25. The tree is 200 years old and about 10m tall.  A tip for guests is to look around the House of Chusa before visiting Chusa’s tomb, the Chusa Memorial, the Chusa Experience Center, Wolseongwi tomb, Lacebark Pine Tree park, and the Lacebark Pine Tree itself. Programs for kids and teenagers to experience the excellence of Chusa culture are provided at the Chusa Experience Center, while a Chusa Culture Festival is held every October to honor Chusa Kim Jeonghui. Entry and parking at the House of Chusa is free. The opening hours are from 9 AM to 5 PM in the winter, and from 9 AM to 6 PM in the summer.

stories.title: Site 4 Imjon Mountain Castle
stories.script: Also called Bongsusan Castle, Imjonsan Castle is located on Bongsusan Mountain, Daeheung-myeon, Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do. It served as the base for the Baekje Revival Movement and is a hilltop fortification from the Baekje period. The castle is at the midway point of Bongsusan Mountain with silver grass and azalea growing in the vicinity, and the Yedang reservoir can be seen below the castle.   The castle walls are 2.5-3.5m high and about 3.5m wide, with the outer layer of the southern wall made of stone and the inner layer consisting of mixed soil. A gutter 90cm deep and 60cm wide has been installed in the southern wall to transport water within the castle.   The large slab of stone covering the gutter is 70cm wide and 30cm high. This castle's four corners are 2m thicker than most places to stabilize the construction, while the castle itself is slightly taller.  The southern gate is thought to be the main gate, with a thick stone structure on either side thought to be part of the doorway. The same is thought to be the case at the northern gate. Within the castle are even slopes, and within the southern wall, pottery and roof tile shards can be seen, as well as the remains of a building with stairs. This castle is recorded in several documents as being the base for the Baekje Revival Army along with Geonjisan Castle in Seocheon-gun, Chungcheongnam-do.   A visit to Yedang Lake, Hyangcheonsa Temple, the House of Chusa, and Daelyeonsa Temple, all nearby, are also recommended.

stories.title: Site 5 Yedang Lake
stories.script: Yedang Lake is in Eungbong-myeon, Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do and was constructed in 1964. At 9.9 km2, it is the first reservoir in the country made for agricultural use. Yedang Lake is 40 km around and 2 km at its widest. Its name is taken from the first syllables of Yesan-gun and Dangjin-si as it supplied water for agricultural use to the Yedang Plain, the farmland for both localities. Designated a National Tourist Site in 1986 began its development as a popular vacation spot and is considered the best fishing site in the country with outdoor campsites, rest areas, hiking trails, and sculpture parks. It is also home to a variety of cultural events at the lakeside outdoor stage, and the recently-opened Yedang Lake Suspension Bridge, which is another popular tourist destination. Yedang Lake Suspension Bridge is the longest such bridge in the country, at 402m long, which, incidentally, is a representation of its circumference (40 km) and width (2 km). The gently swaying structure can give guests the feeling of walking on water, which, with the lake water visible through the tower floor, creates a thrilling memory. Given its Rank 1 seismic design, Yedang Lake Suspension Bridge is safe and strong, with a capacity of 3,150 adults at the same time. At 1.8 m wide, families can cross its span together. A variety of LED lights illuminate the bridge at night in a rainbow of color, making it a great place for a night visit. The Slow Lake Trail is a deck trail of about 7 km and stretches from Yedang Lakeshore Park to Central Ecological Park, providing visitors the opportunity to enjoy the beauty walking slowly. The course around the lake is approximately 20,000 steps—a great idea for a daily healthy activity. A music fountain in the lake is linked with landscape lights on the suspension bridge, measuring 96m long and 16m wide, shooting water up to 110m high. The resulting beauty has been officially recorded by the Korea Record Institute as the largest fountain in Korea. Please check the hours prior to your visit to view a musical fountain and laser show to make your trip even more special. Nearby sites include Gwangsi Hanwoo Village, Imjon Castle, and Uijoeunhyeongje Park. Yedang fish porridge is one of Yesan-gun’s “8 flavors,” and comes highly recommended. This delicacy consists of boiled freshwater fish (bones removed) mixed with hot pepper or soybean paste, rice, sujebi dumplings, and a variety of seasonings. Best eaten with kimchi.

stories.title: Site 6 Sapgyo Plain
stories.script: At 2,650ha, Sapgyo Plain stretches out along Sapgyocheon Stream through Sapgyo-eup Yongdong-ri, Seong-ri, Godeok-myeon Yong-ri, Guman-ri, Sangjang-ri, and Daecheon-ri in Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do. The view from the peak of Sapgyo Kkotsan Mountain in fall resembles a flow of golden waves with the vast plain reflecting the morning sunlight.  Sapgyo Plain is one of the 8 Sites of Yesan along with Sudeoksa Temple, Gayasan Mountain, Chusa Shrine, the House of Chusa, Yedang Lake, Imjon Castle, and Yesansa Temple. A traditional tourist destination, the plain is also the site of rice farming in the area due to the abundance of water. After completion of the Sapgyo Stream breakwater in 1979, flood damage decreased and agriculture grew.   Rice produced from the golden fields and clear water of Yedang Lake is processed in a nearby rice processing complex using state-of-the-art equipment, resulting in select high-quality, polished rice that is both fresh and delicious.  Sapgyo Plain produces 5,898 tons of rice annually, which is branded as golden rice and packaged in 4㎏, 8㎏, 10㎏, and 20㎏ bags at cooperative markets in the region.

stories.title: Site 7 Gayasan Mountain
stories.script: Located in Deoksan-myeon, Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do, Gayasan Mountain is part of the Charyeong Mountain Range and Deoksan Provincial Park. Many cultural remains are protected in the vicinity.   Gayasansa Temple was built during the Shilla Dynasty for ancestral rites, and even in the Joseon period, the governor of Deoksan performed rites in the spring and autumn. The azaleas and silver grass growing alongside the trail add to the joy of a hike. At 600m, the mountain boasts a surprising height as it is closer to the sea than inland mountains.   A varied but easy trail is open all along Gayasan Mountain, making it easy for the elderly, women, and children to hike. In spring, azaleas, royal azaleas and other wildflowers grow, providing a beautiful backdrop all year-round. Hikers usually start from or end at the valley holding the Tomb of Prince Namyeongun, the father of Joseon regent Heungseon, and the course up to Seokmunbong Peak. This peak has the most boulders on Gayasan and includes a ridge that leads to Okyangbong Peak.  These peaks appear to be far away, but it actually takes less than 1 hour to reach them. Signs and trails are well-kept so that families can hike together and take in the many cultural sites in the vicinity.  The view towards the west of Gayasan Mountain ridge includes Seosan, Taean, Cheonsu Bay, and the west coast, while the vast Yedang Plain can be seen when looking east.  The Janghang (train) Line and the Seohaean Expressway passes by Gayasan, making transportation easy. To access the mountain by car, take the Seohaean Expressway to Haeminadeulmok and National Route 45.   Deoksan Hot Springs and the Tomb of Prince Namyeongun can be visited in the area, or you can even take some apples home that you picked and purchased yourself at an orchard.

stories.title: Site 8 Yesan Apples
stories.script: Although Yesan was designated an apple export region as it produced the most in 1995 on 2,184ha, there are now 949 farms on 1,190ha. Since 2009, Envy and new red-fleshed varieties have been introduced and formed the apple region to keep the Yesan apple flourishing. About 50,000 kg of Envy apples, or 35,000 kg of red-fleshed varieties, are produced per hectare. They were supplied to the Pyeongchang Winter Olympics in the past and are also exported abroad to Taiwan, Vietnam and other countries.  Apple orchards in the area manufacture apple wines using Yesan red clay apples grown according to environmentally-friendly methods, while also providing guests with the opportunity to make their own apple pie and apple jam.  To promote Yesan apples—the best in the country—the Yesan Red Clay Apple Festival is held every year.

stories.title: Site 9 Yesan Stork Park
stories.script: Located in Gwangsi-myeon, Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do, Yesan Stork Park was the first such park to be built in the country in 2014, after the area was designated as part of the Stork Village Development Program by the Cultural Heritage Administration in 2009. This was part of efforts to restore the stork population (Natural Monument No. 199), almost extinct due to environmental destruction, as well as other forms of wildlife. Environmentally-friendly farming practices were introduced and habitats have been created so that storks can live in Yesan-gun again. Real storks can be seen showing off their graceful poses at Yesan Stork Park. Explanations from the ecological guide at the Stork Culture Center will inform guests of the value of this place.  Five villages around Stork Park were designated “Stork Area Villages” and began stork ecology farming in 2010. This involves creating a rich rice paddy ecology where storks can live and at the same time allow farmers to produce a safe, environmentally-friendly food source for our children. Many ecological programs are in development and currently being provided.

stories.title: Site 10 Deoksan Hot Springs
stories.script: Doeksan Hot Springs are located in Deoksan-myeon, Yesan-gun, Chungcheongnam-do, and have always been busy with visitors for their widely-known healing properties. First opened in 1917 as a location for bathing, Doeksan Hot Springs have natural alkalescent bicarbonate water with germanium—a mineral known for its healing properties—helping to treat muscle aches, arthritis and neuralgia, stimulate circulation and cell regeneration and even decrease subcutaneous fat, giving them the reputation as the best hot springs in the country, attracting over 2.5 million visitors each year. The hot springs area houses 7 hot springs and about 50 accommodation providers, including 2 tourist hotels and one regular hotel, along with restaurants and a variety of other services.   The history of Doeksan Hot Springs begins 500 to 600 years ago as they are recorded in the Augmented Survey of the Geography of Korea and Geographical Treatise in the Annals of King Sejong from the Joseon period.  According to Joseon Confucian scholar, Yi Yulgok, in his book Chungbo, villagers observed a stork standing in the middle of the rice paddy that did not fly away when they approached. As they got closer, they saw the stork had an injured wing and leg, scooping up the water with its beak and placing the water on its wounds. After 3 days of this, the stork's injuries healed and it was able to fly away, which the villagers found to be odd. They examined the spot the stork had been and found that the water there was warm. Later, they built a well there, and found that the water they drew up helped against skin disease and neuralgia. The village came to be called “Hot Spring Valley.”  Another legend that has been passed on is that of a busy farmer in the Sadong-ri region of Deoksan. He was poor and grew up with his single mother, becoming hardworking upon coming of age. He took care of his mother and his children, and lived a content life. But after 2 or 3 years of bad harvests, life became very hard as the only rice he saw was dried out when he went out with his hoe. However, he noticed one area where the grass was thriving among the withering rice and ran to it to strike the ground with his hoe where the plants were sprouting. After digging with all his might, the ground started to shine with water, which was unexpectedly warm. Believing that the heavens hadn’t abandoned this diligent man, the farmer later became the owner of the hot spring and lived in prosperity.   For the best effect from bathing in the hot springs, don’t go in within 1 hour after eating. Stay in the water only 10-15 minutes, resting 30-60 minutes afterwards. Soap should be used once a day and irritating the skin through excessive scrubbing with a coarse towel should be avoided. After bathing, the water from the hot springs should not be dried off with a towel but allowed to evaporate naturally. Avoid going into the spring quickly or drinking alcohol beforehand.

stories.title: Chuam Beach
stories.script: Chotdae Rock standing above the sea  Chuam Beach is a place crowded on the first day of the new year with people who come to see the sunrise. The word Chuam originated from unique-shaped rocks in a place once known as Yongchu, which means a swamp where a dragon lives.  Chotdae Rock, which is the symbol of this place, was named after how the rising sun seen at the tip of the rock resembles a candle that is lit. There is a painting of Kim Hong-do, a famous painter during King Jeongjo's reign of the Joseon Dynasty, near Chotdae Rock. Originally, Chotdae Rock consisted of two rocks standing side by side like a pair of chopsticks, but an earthquake in Gangwon-do region during the reign of King Sukjong caused a tsunami that ended up crushing one of the rocks, leaving just one rock. A legend has it that if you pray earnestly at Chuam Chotdae Rock, the rock will appear in the dream to make it come true, so if you have something in your mind that you really want to accomplish, consider visiting Chuam in Donghae.  Chuam Beach is shallow, which makes it a great place for family trips. It is the place where you can see an emerald-colored clear sea on a sunny day and rough waves crashing into the rocks on a windy day. Among many different rocks in the undulating seawater to the right of Chotdae Rock, you will find one that resembles a rabbit. An unknown tree, which seems as if it hadn't grown well due to sea wind, looks like the shape of a rabbit ear, making the rock look like a rabbit pricking up both of its ears and sitting down to nibble on a carrot. This rock and the one behind it are together called Hyeongje Rock. If you go around Chotdae Rock and walk down along the northern trail, you will find Geobuk Rock which looks like a good-looking turtle resting with its long neck protruded out on its way up a hill at the mid-slope of the mountain on your left.  Near the area, there is also a pavilion called Haeamjeong, which is known to have been constructed by Sim Dong-ro, the founder of the Samcheok Sim clan, for local residents in the late Goryeo period. It is a quiet and secluded pavilion where you can also check out a plaque made by Song Si-yeol, a famous scholar from Joseon Dynasty. Stop by this pavilion and hear the sound of waves from Chuam that sound like a bell before taking a stroll around a neighborhood park that also has a trail. This is Chuam Beach, a beach where anyone who visits once will be sure to visit again.

stories.title: Bukpyeong Fifth-Day Market
stories.script: Three times the generosity, eight times the happiness  Bukpyeong Market is the country's largest traditional fifth-day market full of joys and sorrows of the ordinary people which brings up the nostalgia of the good old days. Consisted of around 500 stores over a 13,223m2 land in Bukpyeong-dong, Donghae, Bukpyeong Fifth-Day Market is also called by its pure Korean words Dwittteureujang. It has a long history of over 200 years that started in the 20th year of King Jeongjo's reign in 1796.  It is held on days that end in 3 or 8 every month, which is why locals also like to call it the 38 Department Store. It is a humane, love-filled place full of discounts and giveaways. It is crowed with people shopping shoulder to shoulder with one another on a seemingly endless alley of shops.
