From the top, you can look down at downtown Chuncheon set against Uiamho Lake and Bukhangang River at a glance. The view from the top of this mountain is magnificent. Make sure to take souvenir pictures.

stories.title: Baegyang-ri Station (closed)
stories.audioTitle: Closed-down station that brings back old memories
stories.script: When willow flowers bloom by the Bukhangang River in spring, the area around Baegyang-ri Station turns white. Baegyang-ri Station, which started operating in 1939, was closed down when a new station opened on the Gyeongchun Line in 2010.   Having lost its function as a train station, Baegyang-ri Station was reborn as a celebrated spot to bring back old memories. So, it is famous as a date course for couples.   The old and rusty railroad tracks, wild flowers blooming in between them, and the old-fashioned signboard on the platform are great props for amazing photos. Don’t forget to take a picture in front of a public phone, which is no longer working, in front of the station building. Try using the Tortoise Mailbox, too. Write a letter and put it into this mail box. Then, the letter will be delivered in three weeks’ time.  Inside the station, where “Baegyang-ri Station Carrying Memories” is written, photos of the old days and office items used by the station staff are on display. There is also a photo zone where you can take a photo with Stationmaster Teddy Bear and an experience area to try on the station staff uniform.  Baegyang-ri Station is the starting point of the Bomnaegil 7 courses extending to Gangchon Station. Each of the seven courses span for approximately 2.1km. Why don’t you take a relaxing walk while enjoying the view along the Bukhangang River?

stories.title: Elysian Gangchon
stories.audioTitle: Full of excitement all year round
stories.script: Elysian Gangchon is Chuncheon’s most famous resort. After an hour-long drive from Seoul, you will reach this resort. Following the golf range in 1997, a condominium and a ski resort have also been opened.   The golf range measures 1.05 million ㎡, which is equivalent to the size of 150 football fields. Equipped with 27 holes, this golf range was designed according to the mountainous features of Gangchon to the greatest extent possible.  The official name of the condominium is Elsuite Condominium. Elsuite has 222 guest rooms.   The ski resort covers an area of 200,000 ㎡. Unlike other ski resorts, this resort has many slopes for novice skiers. Eight out of the ten slopes are for beginning and intermediate-level skiers.   Baengyang-ri Station for subway and rapid electronic railway trains is located near the ski resort. It takes only a two-minute shuttle ride from the station to the ski resort. So, you can travel conveniently by subway instead of driving yourself.

stories.title: D.Forest Theme Park
stories.audioTitle: Largest companion dog-themed park in Korea
stories.script: Another attraction of Chuncheon is D.Forest, the first companion dog theme park in Korea. With an area measuring as large as 12 football fields, D.Forest is equipped with a range of auxiliary facilities including walking trails, a playing field, a lawn garden, experience spaces, restaurants, cafes, and a pet shop in addition to a museum.   Exhibition Room 1 focuses on the history of dogs and humanity. In Exhibition Room 2, experts teach you how to care for your companion dogs. Exhibition Room 3 is a space for understanding the language, behavior, and psychology of companion dogs through monitors.   The walking trail and playing field outside are designed especially for companion dogs. These are the most important spaces in D.Forest. Walking on the trail through a birch forest, you will reach the playing field. This is where your companion dog can play freely without a leash. The playing field is divided into sections according to the size of dogs allowed to play inside.  If you are on a tour of Chuncheon with your companion dog, make sure to visit D.Forest.

stories.title: Story of Nami Island and the Surrounding Area_Nami Island and Tourist Attractions Nearby
stories.audioTitle: How to enjoy Nami Island and tourist attractions nearby
stories.script: Nami Island is one of Chuncheon’s most famous tourist destinations. This island is popular as a great picnic or dating location. Jade Garden and Uiam Ryu Inseok Memorial Hall near the island are also noted attractions. If you are planning a trip to Nami Island, it is recommended to visit Jade Garden and Uiam Ryu Inseok Memorial Hall one after another.  Nami Island shows off different landscapes each season. This is the reason many people come to visit this island. Nami Island is also famous as the filming site for Winter Sonata, which kicked off the K-drama frenzy. In addition to walking trails, Nami Island offers a variety of experience facilities including “Picture Book Playground,” as well as restaurants, cafes, and hotels.  Jade Garden is like a magical garden from a fairy tale book. This is a great place to take beautiful pictures. The concept of Jade Garden is “Little Europe in the Forest.” Jade Garden attracts many tourists because it is famous as a shooting site for a number of TV shows and films.   Uiam Ryu Inseok Memorial Hall tells you the story of how Uiam Ryu Inseok who had lived his entire life as a man of letters became the leader of loyal troops at the age of 54.

stories.title: Uiam Ryu In-seok Memorial Hall
stories.audioTitle: Great man who transformed himself from civil to military official
stories.script: A scholar who had lived his entire life surrounded by books suddenly became the leader of loyal troops at the age of 54. This man died at 74 after dedicating himself to the anti-Japanese struggle and the save-the-nation movement as the leader of loyal troops. Uiam Ryu In-seok Memorial Hall was built in commemoration of this man.  Born and raised in Chuncheon, Ryu In-seok decided to become a military person following the assassination of Empress Myeongseong, the wife of Emperor Gojong of the Korean Empire, in 1895 by the Japanese during the attack of Gyeongbokgung Palace, and Danballyeong, which is Japan’s decree banning topknots. In 1896, Ryu Inseok became the leader of loyal troops and started the anti-Japanese struggle in and around Jecheon and Chungju.  After his asylum in China, Ryu continued the struggle in China and the Hwanghae-do region. He broadened the stage of this activity all the way to Manchuria and the Littoral Province of Russia. Having dedicated himself solely to the anti-Japanese struggle and the save-the-nation movement, Ryu Inseok died in China in 1915. In 1935, Ryu’s body was carried to Chuncheon, his birthplace.   In Uiam Ryu In-seok Memorial Hall lies the Tomb of Uiam Ryu Inseok, which is Monument No. 74 of Gangwon-do, along with Uiyeolsa Shrine where the portrait and memorial tablet of Ryu In-seok are enshrined, and Uiam Memorial Center where Ryu Inseok’s legacy is on display. At Uiam Ryu Inseok Memorial Hall, take a look into the turbulent life of Ryu Inseok and also try various experience-type programs.

stories.title: Gangchon Station (closed)
stories.audioTitle: Station of the past that used to be full of excitement
stories.script: In the past, when a train from Cheongnyangni Station in Seoul stopped at Gangchon Station, numerous people poured out onto the platform. These were college students coming to Gangchon for workshops, couples on dates, and families out for picnics.   In 2010, however, Gangchon Station was closed down, leaving behind the memories of people carried through the Gyeongchun Line railroad alongside the Bukhangang River.  After being shut down in 2010, Gangchon Station was changed to a station for shuttle buses carrying people who came rail-biking from Gimyujeong Station. Graffiti paintings covering the walls of Piam Tunnel create a unique atmosphere. In 2016, Gangchon Station became the starting point of the Bomnaegil 7 courses extending all the way to Baegyang-ri Station, which was also closed. It is attracting an increasing number of tourists who come to enjoy the view of the Bukhangang River on foot.  A number of famous tourist destinations, such as Gugok Falls, Munbae Village, and Samaksan Mountain, are located nearby. The area around Gangchon Station is still full of things to enjoy, which include Gangchon Land and bicycle and four-wheel bike rental shops. If you plan to travel to Gugok Falls and Deungseon Falls, two of Chuncheon’s three waterfalls, in Gangchon, how about making time to pay a visit to Gangchon Station?

stories.title: Uirim Reservoir: Yongchu Falls
stories.script: Yongchu Falls  [Traveler] Looking down from the bridge above the waterfall, is a dazzling cliff about 30 meters in height, and a cool waterfall. Interestingly, on one side of this bridge there is a gentle flow of water and on the other there’s a dynamic waterfall.  A long time ago, people thought this waterfall resembled a dragon penetrating the valley before flying up into the sky. That’s why the word ‘Yong,’ which means ‘dragon’ in English, forms part of its name - Yongchu Falls. The high copper content in the water makes the waterfall look red, so the area is also called, the Red Dragon Valley. Look where the dragon left his mark, and listen to a folk tale. The story of <Five strong men and a python> has been passed down for generations here at Uirim Reservoir.  Once upon a time, there were five very strong brothers. Not only were they strong, but they also had scales on their bodies like dragons. One day, while the five brothers were playing around in Uirim Reservoir, a gigantic python came up behind the eldest brother. A python is an imaginary beast that frequently appears in Korean legends. It’s basically a baby dragon that has yet to acquire its mysterious powers. While the eldest brother fought with the creature under the water, his four brothers watched in shock, hoping for their brother to come back safe.   The brothers picked up wooden sticks from the waterside and started attacking the python. With help from his younger brothers, the eldest finally struggled back on land, while the angry beast whipped its tail at the five brothers.  The five brothers quickly dodged the attack, and the creature’s tail got stuck in a giant pine tree. The brothers beat down the evil beast with their bare hands and feet.   The beast’s scales broke off and were scattered all around, and its blood turned the waterfall red. The python was so big that when they hung it from the top of a giant tree, its tail reached all the way down to the ground. Thanks to the five brothers who defeated the python, the townspeople were able to go to Uirim Reservoir without fear.

stories.title: Japan Hard Porcelain Corporation
stories.script: A Scene of Hot and Fierce Life, Japan Hard Porcelain, Co. Ltd.  How did this road that we are standing on look like a hundred years ago? It was a time when rickshaws and trolleys were bustling, and people in Hanbok were staying strong to lead their lives. Let’s go back to Yeongdo of that time on this road. The first story that unfolds along the Modern History Trail is Japan Hard Porcelain Corporation, a pottery factory.   Japan Hard Porcelain Corporation was established in 1908 as the local company in the Kanazawa area of Japan. It expanded to Joseon in 1917 and established a factory right here where you are standing, at 17, 14beon-gil, Daegyo-ro, Yeongdo-gu. It was the biggest pottery factory in Joseon as well as in the Eastern world. They also had many employees, naturally. A total of 900 employees made Korean and Western dishes. The finished products were exported to various Southeast Asian countries, as it was very popular. After the Liberation, the factory changed its name to Daehan Pottery Corporation and continued to produce ceramics. Before they could fully rejoice in the Liberation, the company’s fate took another turn. With the Korean War breaking out, the famous artists at the time took refuge in Busan. The artists representing the era, including Lee Jung-seob, Kim Un-ho, and Pyon Kwan-sik, created hand-painted ceramics plates in Daehan Pottery. It served as the living foundation of the artists living in Busan, the refugee central. These ceramics garnered much attention as souvenirs. However, the stainless steel plates emerged, and ceramics gradually became less popular as time passed. In 1970, Daehan Ceramics faded into history as it failed to overcome the financial difficulties.    The site has changed into an apartment complex now. It used to be the place of life where the heat from the fierce lives rose from high chimneys. The part of the wall of Japan Hard Porcelain Corporation still remains at the back gate Blueport 2021 (138 Bongnaenaru-ro, Yeongdo-gu), keeping the factory's history.

stories.title: Mokdo Pleasure
stories.script: Mokdo Pleasure District of Fun and a Glass of Drink  Looking back on the place that we are standing now - the second story that unfolds along the Modern History Trail is about Mokdo Pleasure District.   People of Yeongdo 100 years ago would have been surprised if they saw the street you are walking now. Now an ordinary street, it once used to be the Mokdo Pleasure district. When Yeongdo was called Mokdo in 1932, there were 13 pleasure quarters in Yeongdo. Of those 13, 6 were here in Mokdo Pleasure District. Considering the concentrated entertainment facilities, you can tell that Daepyeong-ro used to be Yeongdo’s central adult entertainment district.   Pleasure quarters are associated with negative impressions these days, but you can get a glimpse of a different perception than now in the newspapers published back then. In the March 24th, 1925 issue of Busan Ilbo newspaper, there is an article that Kubushiro Kanichi, a councilman of Busan prefecture and an owner of a pleasure quarter, was elected the representative of the Mokjido Pleasure Quarter Business Union. To put this in modern terms, the article announced that a councilman of Busan city council is an owner of a pleasure quarter and elected as the pleasure quarter union operating in Yeongdo. It seems like pleasure quarters at the time were similar to pubs these days.   The street that used to be Yeongdo’s most popular pleasure district is now a quiet and peaceful street, making us feel the change in times.

stories.title: Mokdo Market
stories.script: Mokdo Market, Now Known as Bongrae Market  This is the third spot that traces back to modern history. Come! Look! Buy! This is Mokdo Market, where lively voices of the merchants filled the air.   Bongrae Market was created after the Liberation. Then, which market was here before then? Mokdo Market, established on June 1st, 1932, was located at the Daehwa Apartment complex spot that you see in the front. It was the 6th public market in Busan, along with Choryang Market. Built on about 0.59 acres of land, the market was 0.18 acres in size. Customers could buy anything from fresh seafood caught off the coast of Yeongdo to agricultural, industrial, and miscellaneous goods. The market was always packed with people. According to the census of Busan prefecture, Mokdo market recorded the highest sales among the major markets in Busan in 1941.   In the midst of rapidly changing contemporary history, the market now remains a page of modern history. We can now hear the sound of life from the merchants and customers from Bongrae Market.

stories.title: Streetcar terminal station
stories.script: Yeongdo Streetcar Terminal Station, a Rest Stop for Streetcars  The history of Yeongdo found while walking on the road – the fourth place is the Yeongdo Streetcar Terminal Station. This was where the last stop of the Yeongdo line was. You could get to the hot springs from here by train. What was the story behind the streetcar installation?  To explain the beginning of the Yeongdo line streetcar, we have to talk about the Yeongdo bridge. The only way to get to the land from Yeongdo was to take a ‘boat.’ As the ferry couldn’t handle all the passengers increasing every day, the Yeongdo bridge was built. After the completion of the bridge in 1934, the streetcar also started its operation as it was installed during the construction of the bridge. The Yeongdo Streetcar Terminal Station was also constructed around this time. The streetcar began to operate in February 1935, and it ran from the terminal and passed the Yeongdo bridge, arriving in front of the Busan Prefectural Office.  The streetcars became part of daily life at the time. They shared the happiness and sadness of Busan citizens until May 20th, 1967, when it stopped running after the operation of city streetcars was abolished. Yeongdo Streetcar Terminal Station, which was the trains’ last stop, also disappeared.  Even though the station disappeared, a monument that commemorates the Yeongdo Streetcar Terminal Station at 57, Jeolyeong-ro, Yeongdo-gu. Now, the monument remembers the now-gone station and welcomes the people on the street.

stories.title: Yeongdo's first theater
stories.script: There was a time when people watched motion pictures while focusing on the explanation of narrators. Let's meet Yeongdo of the time when people laughed and cried to the narrators' voices even though there was no music nor real voice from the actors. The fifth place that searches for modern history is the Ebisuza (Jiljajwa) Theater.   Around 98, Namhang-dong 1-ga you see in front of you now was Yeongdo's first theater, Ebisuza. Dedicated to plays, the Ebisuza theater opened in 1912 and operated for a short period of 6 years before it disappeared into history in 1918. After it closed, the Kotobukiza Theater opened nearby in February 1924. In April 1926, the theater's operational rights were transferred to the Saiwaiza Theater in Nampo-dong, and the theater was renamed the 2nd Saiwaiza. After changing its name back to Kotobukiza in April 1936, the theater continued to operate until the Liberation.   After the Liberation, the Kotobukiza theater abandoned its Japanese name and transformed into the 'Harbor Theater' to start anew. While it witnessed the turbulent contemporary history, the theater couldn't adapt to the world that changed as much as the years passed. The Harbor Theater was closed in 1990, with its 66 years of history at rest.   Busan, the city of films, may have started 100 years ago. The light from the black-and-white projector became the window of infinite possibilities, and Busan is the city built by those who dreamt of a shining future through movies.

stories.title: Shiraishi Saltern
stories.script: Shiraishi Saltern, Where White Salt was Made  An antique building stands out among the modern buildings. It has a Japanese-style wooden roof and red brick walls. When was this building built? The sixth modern history met on the road of Yeongdo is Shiraishi Saltern.   Modern Yeongdo had reached an industrial revival with large factories and shipyards. In May 1915, a salter, Shiraishi Umataro, established Shiraishi Saltern during the industrial revival. In 1937, there were 11 salt companies in Busan, and 8 of them were in Yeongdo. The salt industry was one of the leading industries in Yeongdo that was promising. After the Liberation, the Shiraishi Saltern changed its name to Namheung Saltern and continued to be in business. As time passed, the salt mills in Yeongdo began to close one by one. Namheung Saltern also closed its doors, and the saltern disappeared. However, parts of the saltern’s building still remain. The antique brick building you are seeing now proves that Shiraishi Saltern existed.   As 1950 Yeongseon-jeong, Busan prefecture changed to 128 Namhangseo-ro, Yeongdo-gu, Busan city, the salt industry has completely disappeared from Yeongdo. However, the building still remembers Yeongdo of 100 years ago when mountains of white salt were glistening.

stories.title: Daepungpo
stories.script: Daepungpo Reclamation Monument that Celebrates Reclamation  This is Daepungpo, where ships finished sailing and took a rest. The name means to wait for the wind. The seventh story we will tell you at the port waiting for the wind is about Daepungpo Reclamation Monument.   Daepungpo has long been a small port used by fishing boats as a shelter to avoid storms. It was also called Pungbalpo, meaning ‘a port where the wind powerfully rises.’ The port started to change when the Japanese fishing boats gathered in the early 1900s. The natural condition that the land surrounding the three sides made it great to anchor, and the Japanese office was close by, so it was easy to repair ships or get water supply. In 1916, Ozawa, a person of Japanese nationality, received the right to reclaim Daepugpo from the Japanese settlers in Busan and started the land reclamation. It was completed in June 1926, so it was a long-term construction of 10 years. Nearly 33 acres of land were reclaimed, changing the coastline of Daepungpo and Yeongdo. In February 1983, after the Liberation, the Daepungpo Reclamation Monument was erected by Busan city to commemorate the reclamation. The monument summarizes the schedule of the construction and the purpose of the monument.   Yeongdo had been quickly modernized with the shipyards and factories established on the land from the reclamation. Clang, clang, clang. The sounds of life made when red rust is removed ring with the reclamation of Daepungpo.  We are back again on the road. The last traces of modern history urges us to move on.

stories.title: Korea’s first modern shipbuilding company
stories.script: Tanaka Shipbuilding Ironworks, the Beginning of a Modern Shipyard  This is Daepyeong-ro, where the loud sound of industry booms. Here, shipbuilding-related industries such as shipyards and ship parts are concentrated, and it’s also famous as Kangkangee Culture Village. The last story along the Yeongdo Moden History Trail is about Tanaka Shipbuilding Ironworks, the matrix of modern shipyards.  Did you know that Korea’s first modern shipbuilding company was in Yeongdo? Tanaka Shipbuilding Ironworks was first established on Nampo-dong beach in 1887, and it was Korea’s first modern shipbuilding company. Later in 1912, Tanaka Kiyoshi took over the family business and established a shipyard that also served as an ironwork in 56 Daepyeong-ro, Yeongdo-gu of now. As Tanaka Shipbuilding Ironworks settled down in Yeongdo, the surrounding area became concentrated with the shipbuilding-related industry. There was a company that led Yeongdo’s shipbuilding industry with Tanaka. It’s Nakamura Shipbuilding Ironworks. It started as an ironworks in Nampo-dong in 1893, and it started shipbuilding as it moved the location to 62 Daepyeong-ro, Yeongdo-gu of now in 1902. Nakamura Shipbuilding Ironworks was managed by Nakamura Takatsugu after he took over the family business in 1913.  The location where the former Tanaka and Nakamura Shipbuilding Ironworks was still stand shipyards. The shipbuilding industry of Yeongdo continued over 100 years. We hope that the sparking flames and the sound of cutting iron will be heard 100 years later, too.  How was the trip to modern history on the road? Doesn’t Yeongdo look a bit different? We hope that this trip containing the turbulent times was a fun time where the past and the present meet.

stories.title: National Maritime Museum
stories.script: Shall we listen to the sea’s deep story?  [Child] Oh? Mom! What’s that big building over there? [Mom] It’s the National Maritime Museum. It looks very nice outside. [Child] It looks like the waves! What does the National Maritime Museum do? [Mom] It’s a place where you can hear many stories of the sea up close. Shall we visit together? [Child] Yes!  [Guide] Welcome to the National Maritime Museum! Opened in July 2012, this is Korea's first comprehensive maritime museum that presents a vision for the ocean's future to the public and aims to build a maritime cultural infrastructure. It's a leading museum in Korea that's visited by more than 1 million people per year, and it has a huge collection of more than 26,000 marine-related items.   [Mom] The building is so big. Where should we start looking? [Guide] The National Maritime Museum has 1st to 4th floors, and there is a sky park above it. If you enter the 1st floor, you will see the maritime library with more than 40,000 marine-related books. 2nd floor and on has various experience facilities that are filled with energy. Especially, families visit the children's museum a lot, making it always crowded. On the other side, there is a special exhibition room that holds exhibitions on various marine-related topics more than twice a year. It endlessly unravels the stories of the sea of Korea and around the world.   [Child] Oh, Mom! There's a fish! [Guide] The 3rd and 4th floors are the main floors of the museum and have exhibition rooms, an aquarium, and a video hall. Once you arrive on the 3rd floor, you can see the aquarium that's 5 meters deep with a tunnel in the middle, and it contains nearly 1,000 kinds of fish. After you pass the underwater tunnel, a video hall plays realistic video 360 degrees with '20,000 miles under the sea' as the topic. In the 3rd and 4th floor exhibition rooms, there are year-round exhibitions with various topics of the history of Korean sea, people, folklore, marine science, fishery, logistics, the polar regions, territory, and more.   A marine trip to the National Maritime Museum! Listen to the story of the sea at the National Maritime Museum, the hub of marine culture!

stories.title: Amir Park
stories.script: Would you like to take a walk in the attraction where you can meet the sea and hydrangeas together?  [Man] Shall we go to the sea during our vacation in July? [Woman] Yes! But I also want to see flowers, too…. [Man] Then, we should go to Amir Park! It’s where we can enjoy the sea with hydrangeas. [Woman] Really? That’s great! I can’t wait until summer!  [Woman] It's so beautiful! It's a great park for a walk. [Man] Amir Park looks like how it is now in 2012, thanks to the continuous interest and effort of the Dongsam Innovation District Development Committee, which longed for regional development. The walking trails on both sides of the wide lawn allow pets, so it's an excellent walking course for dogs, too.  [Woman] The name 'Amir' is peculiar. How did the park get its name? [Man] The name 'Amir' was selected through a contest in 2014. It's a combination of 'A' from a foal in Korean and 'mir,' which is a Korean word for dragon. It originated from Guryong-dong, the former name of Dongsam-dong.  [Woman] There is a statue of a horse in the square! What does it have to do with this park? [Man] Yeongdo had a long history with horses as it had a 'National Horse Stable' that raised excellent steeds since the Three Kingdoms period. 'Jeolyeongma' means a horse that runs so fast that its shadow would cut off. It's famously influenced by 'Jeolyeong-do,' the former name of Yeongdo. Afterward, Jeolyeongma became the symbol of Yeongdo-gu. That's why there is a statue of Jeolyeongma in the central square of Amir Park. The statue revived the history of the old national stable and established its identity, becoming the new tourist attraction of Dongsam Innovation District.  On a day you need fresh air and warm sunlight, how about taking a walk in Amir Park with your loved ones?

stories.title: Dongsam Seawater River
stories.script: Would you like to visit the eco-friendly ecological river that draws in seawater?  Flowers are one of the things that make you notice the change of season. Recently, in Dongsam Seawater River, the healing spot that changed into an eco-friendly ecological river, you can feel the change of seasons with cherry blossoms in the spring, hydrangeas in the summer, and cosmos in the fall. Did you know about such an eco-friendly ecological river? Dongsam Seawater River is a U-shaped, 1.6km-long artificial waterway built in 2006, and the seawater flows between the Dongsam Innovation District and the existing residential areas.   Recently, the floodgate that quickly circulates the seawater was completed, and people are looking forward to the improved water quality. The overturning floodgate that opens 90 degrees received a technological patent. The gate opens to lock in water during high tide, and it opens the floodgate on one side first and opens the other with a time difference during the lowest tide, guiding the water flow in one direction.   The two floodgates installed on both ends of the 1.2km seawater river function to increase the flowing speed of the seawater using the scientific principle of the difference between two tides. The gates became an opportunity to solve the chronic issue of water quality deterioration caused by stagnant seawater.   Dongsam Seawater River also has a small park, six bridges, and workout facilities and attracting the residents and tourists alike as a walking course and a place to view flowers. It’s also connected to the Korea Maritime University and the National Maritime Museum so that you can take longer walks.   You can also observe mullets and mallard ducks at Dongsam Seawater River. For it to become an eco-friendly ecological river, the continuous interest and love of the local residents played a significant role. We hope that it will be.

stories.title: Dongsam-dong Shell Midden Museum
stories.script: The Dongsam-dong Shell Midden Museum, the history seen through shell midden remains  Shell middens are the remains of shells collected as food and discarded after eating by prehistoric humans that accumulated for a long time. Near Yeongdo-gu Haeyangdae three-way intersection, the Dongsam-dong Shell Midden is famous for the remains from the Neolithic Age. It has been recognized as an important relic that shows the transition of the Neolithic culture of the South coast and was registered as National Historic Place No. 266 in 1979.   The Dongsam-dong Shell Midden Museum contains a history of the shell midden. It opened in April 2002 to introduce the achievements of the excavation of the Dongsam-dong shell midden and to preserve and research the remains. Now, as a museum specializing in the Neolithic period, it provides historical education and experiential learning related to the Neolithic period.   A Japanese teacher first discovered the Dongsam-dong Shell Midden during the Japanese colonial period in 1929. People from the Neolithic period lived for 4,000 years in this place. Fishing was an essential means of living for prehistoric humans. Vast amounts of seashells were discovered during the excavation, too. Therefore, it also has a reputation as the largest shell midden in Korea.   The Dongsam-dong Shell Midden was formed from 6,000 BC to 2,000 BC throughout the Neolithic period. It turned out to be a complex relic that contained the shell midden as well as various living facilities, including pottery midden, residences, and stove spots. It still provides crucial information in understanding the characteristics and changes of the Southern sea areas. It is said that the Neolithic people performed various living activities, including early farming, fishing, nut gathering, and hunting, and made earthenware and stone tools. Also, the excavated obsidian and Jomon earthenware imply that they performed primitive trading that exchanged regional products with other tribes through long-distance voyages.   Feel the history through the Dongsam-dong Shell Midden, where it’s known as Korea’s largest shell midden.

stories.title: Achi Island
stories.script: Achi Island with a trail where you can enjoy a magnificent view  Achi island is the gateway to Busan Port, and it is known as the place where the morning comes the earliest in Busan, so it is also known as 'Jodo,' the island of the morning. That is why many residents climb Mountain Bongrae and watch the sun rise over Achi Island. In addition, the Achi trail, a coastal walking path, is also popular.   Achi Island is a beautiful island that's 141 meters above sea level and looks like it's supporting a sharp peak. If you look east from Taejongdae, there is a small island that looks like it is supporting Cheongbong and may or may not look like an island. Until Korea Maritime University was established in 1974, more than 100 houses of residents lived on the island. The island's circumference is about 6km, which is a small island like a little brother to the big island of Yeongdo, hence the name Achi island.   Completed in April 2019, the Achi trail is where you can see the 'magnificent view of Achi Island' at a glance. This is the only place where you can see the entire Busan Port without getting on a boat, and you can enjoy the Busan Port at a glance while walking around the Korea Maritime University campus. There is also an observatory where you can look down on Busan's tourist attractions, such as Taejongdae and Oryukdo Island.   Achi trail is 656m long, and it is a decked road built on the coastal cliff facing Oryukdo Island. The trail is divided into three courses according to their characteristics. 'Achi Blue Road' with a wave prevention facility next to the grass field, 'Achi Sunrise Road' that leads to the gravel beach where you can enjoy a beautiful sunrise, and 'Achi Sunset Road' in the west where you can enjoy the sunset over Busan Port and Oryukdo Island.   When you walk along the Achi trail, you can see the wide-open sea with the harmony of the rock cliffs, and you will feel like your mind is washed away by the waves. Achi Island has been spotlighted as a marine-friendly healing spot. Please enjoy the magnificent scenery of the coast near the sea.

stories.title: Jangsa Rock
stories.script: Jangsa Rock, a legendary rock that guards Yeongdo  Mountain Bongrae was named after Im Ik-jun, one of the three military officers of Jeolyeongdojin, saying, The mountain looks like a phoenix flying in. The mountain is said to be one of the Three Gods Mountains in Chinese legends that miraculous hermits live according to Taoism.   Have you ever heard of the strange legend related to Mountain Bongrae, 395m above sea level? 'Jangsa Rock,' a famous shaking rock of Mt. Bongrae, is located on Arirang Pass between Bongrae-dong and Cheonghak-dong. As the name suggests, it is called Jangsa Rock because it is covered with stones like the shoes of a strong man, pronounced 'Jangsa' in Korean. There are two legends about this rock. One goes, once a giant who was nine feet tall, and this giant lived in Mountain Bongrae and came down to the village every day to eat 18 pounds of rice a meal. Then, one day, a monster appeared from the sea and kidnaped a village maiden, and the giant died while fighting the monster to repay the kindness of the village feeding him. After that, the giant's body turned into Jangsa Rock. It is said that the villagers made a tomb for the giant, and the tomb turned into a rock, and from then on, it was called Jangsa Rock.   Another legend is that a strong man of Mountain Bongrae ran across the sea from the Yeongdo shore toward Gamman-dong, and even though he crossed the sea safely, he lost a shoe, which became Jangsa Rock.   Because of this legend, Jangsa Rock is known to symbolize 'good luck' and grant wishes. It is said that when mothers pray for their children's future, their bodies and minds become strong, achieve success in entrance exams and employment, and live happy life.   Mountain Bongrae is a popular hiking spot in Yeongdo visited by many hikers. The slope is not that steep that even beginners or those with problems walking can climb. How about climbing Mountain Bongrae on a sunny day to meet the giant Jangsa Rock, the guardian of Yeongdo who protects the locals, and listen to the story of the legend?

stories.title: Bulocho Park
stories.script: Bulocho Park of longevity, where precious medicinal herbs are planted  Did you know that Busan is full of stories of Taoist hermit culture? Although it is difficult to verify its traces throughout the Busan area, it is naturally incorporated into the lives of the local residents. In particular, Mountain Bongrae in Yeongdo has much content related to the Taoist hermit culture. There are places where these cultures have been turned into tourism resources via storytelling. It's Bulocho Park, Yeongdo's leading ecological experience park.   The Yeongdo-gu Office used the old story of Qin Shi Huang and Seo Bok to create Bulocho Park. The park was built near the KBS transmission station of Mountain Bongrae and was completed in 2014. Yeongdo-gu has planted more than 30 medicinal plants, such as Korean Dendropanax, Cornelian cherry, Elm tree, bellflowers, Solomon's seal, and blue lilyturfs, fitting the name of the park. It has also earned the nickname 'Medical Plant Theme Park ' for planting precious medicinal herbs.' The fantastic idea turned an abandoned mountain area into a tourism resource by combining it with the legend of Bulocho, the elixir plant.   Bulocho Park is related to the legend of Qin Shi Huang in China. He sent Seo Bok to find a way to live forever, and Seo Bok visited the legendary Three Godly Mountains: Busan's Baekyang Mountain, Cheonma Mountain, and Bongrae Mountain. This legend was created into a cultural content. If you walk a bit after entering the park, you will see Bulromun. The shape of the gate is impressive, with two dragons climbing up and facing each other. There is also a theory that people will live a long life without disease if they pass through this gate in Bulohcho Park. Once you enter the park through the Bulromun Gate, you will see an observatory. The sunrise or the night views of Busan Port and Busan Port Bridge are magnificent.   In Yeongdo-gu and Bulocho Park, the heliport, the main base of Mountain Bongrae, was created as an outdoor garden with Yeongdo's unique theme. How about going up to Bulocho Park and the outdoor garden with different characteristics of Yeongdo and taking a pleasant rest gifted from nature?

stories.title: decked road
stories.script: The decked road at the top of Bongrae Mountain, the walking trail that will wash away your daily tiredness  Bongrae Mountain is the center of Yeongdo-gu and a famous spot where you can see the city center and the coast of Busan. It has a characteristic landscape where you can look down the thick forest and the blue sea at a glance in the middle of the city. There is a walking trail in Mountain Bongrae where you can get rid of the tiredness of everyday life. It is the decked road at the top of Mountain Bongrae, a path where you can see ‘the most Busan-like scenery.’   As a part of the project to turn Bongrae Mountain trail into a park, the walking trail has been improved, and the 741m-long deck road was completed and is attracting visitors. It’s a great place to see the whole of Busan and yet easily climb to the top, even for those who have difficulty walking.   Your daily stress would wash away when you look at the green forest and scenery with lush trees. You can enjoy a fantastic view all the way to the top of the mountain as you walk along the decked road. You can see Namhang Bridge and Busan Harbor Bridge from the decked road observatory on a clear day. The harmony between the huge bridge and the anchorage, known as the ships' home, creates a marvelous sight.   Also, among the many famous mountains in Busan, Mountain Bongrae allows trekking at night. The blazing red sunset transforms into a party of lights that dazzle the city center. The trail offers a different charm both day and night.   Walk the decked road at the top of Bongrae Mountain, where you can blow away your worries and anxieties in your daily life with nature’s care, and take a break gifted by nature.

stories.title: Halmae Rock
stories.script: Legendary Halmae Rock that protects the safety of the locals  Halmae Rock is the mountain god of Mountain Bongrae that sits at the top of the mountain. There is an interesting story about the rock. It is called 'Halmae Rock' because it resembles a crouched grandmother. The three grandmother gods are said to grow wild ginseng and the elixir plants in Mountain Bongrae and pray for the well-being of the people of Yeongdo so that they can overcome the difficult life on the island. Residents consider Halmae Rock as a sacred place, and when they are worried about their children who have left Yeongdo or when children visit or leave their hometown, they would pay a visit to Halmae Rock. As a result, Yeongdo's grandmother naturally became the mountain god of Mountain Bongrae and the local grandma god.   There is also a very different story on the other hand. It goes, Grandma Yeongdo protects people, but she likes people coming to Yeongdo but hates going out because she is jealous. So, there was even a story that you had to leave at night when the grandma was asleep to leave Yeongdo. The Japanese created this story to trick people. They misled the terrain of Yeongdo as the shape of a bird flying to Japan and spread the story that you will lose everything or die if you move to another place with your collected wealth. Galmae Yeongdo was not trying to be mean to those who left Yeongdo but instead trying to foresee the difficulties they would face in a different town.   Like in this story, the residents of Yeongdo consider Halmae Rock sacred and do not climb it recklessly. Everyone who comes up joins their hands together, bows, and sometimes offers food. Spanning the entire Yeongdo Island, Bongrae Mountain has the shape of a mother's arms. Like a mother's wide arms, it protects the safety of the residents of Yeongdo, and in the event of a national disaster, it protects the citizens of Busan and keeps them in peace. How about taking a hike in search of the legendary Halmae Rock, which protects the safety of the locals, and pray for the safety and well-being of everyone?

stories.title: first cultivation site of Korean sweet potatoes
stories.audioTitle: first cultivation site of Korean sweet potatoes
stories.script: ‘Yeongdo Jonaegi Sweet Potato’ History Museum, commemorating the first cultivation site of Korean sweet potatoes!  [Friend 1] Do you like sweet potatoes? [Friend 2] Sweet potato? Of course! It's rich in dietary fiber, and it keeps you feeling full for a long time! It was really helpful when I was on a diet a while ago! [Friend 1] You seem like you know your sweet potatoes well! Then, did you know that Yeongdo is the origin of sweet potatoes in Korea? [Friend 2] No, I didn't know that! [Friend 1] Then, let's hear more about sweet potatoes at the Yeongdo Jonaegi Sweet Potato History Museum! [Friend 2] Yeah, let's go!  [Guide] Welcome to the Yeongdo Jonaegi Sweet Potato History Museum. Opened in October 2020, this museum was completed in 2010 as a part of the historical park construction project, taking 10 years for the project to complete. During the reign of King Yeongjo of the Joseon Dynasty, Mun Ik-gong Jo Eom brought sweet potatoes from Daema Island and cultivated them for the first time in Yeongdo. The museum was built to commemorate the historical value and meaning of sweet potatoes that relieved the people's hunger and commemorate Yeongdo, the first site to cultivate sweet potatoes in Korea.  [Friend 1] There are a total of 3 floors in the building. What are there on each floor? [Guide] The first floor is the main exhibition hall, and there are various contents related to the history of sweet potatoes. This includes the propagation route of sweet potatoes, backgrounds, historical chronicles, fairy tales of sweet potatoes, sand art videos, puzzle kiosks, and sketch interactive. On the second floor, there are cooking experience room and education center, and you taste sweet potato latte and sweet potato bread in the sweet-potato-themed cafe. On the 3rd floor rooftop, you can look at the ocean view of the Busan Harbor Bridge and the North Port area at a glance to feel the coolness with your eyes and mind. There is a play area in the outdoor experience yard that children can enjoy, including an experiential sweet potato field, a large tree shelter, a jumping game, and a Hobbit house.  [Friend 2] I want to come with my family next time. What are the operating hours? [Guide] Our Yeongdo Jonaegi Sweet Potato History Museum is open from 10 AM to 6 PM and is closed on Mondays and on the day of Lunar New Year's Day and Chuseok. On Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM, you can listen to the commentary of a cultural tourism commentator, so don't miss out!   Oh, right! If you go out and go up the hill a little, there is also the Yeongdo Jonaegi Sweet Potato History Park. Why don't we visit there to enjoy various things, such as the sweet potato tunnel, a long slide, and the forest?

stories.title: Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Museum
stories.script: Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Museum, the only haenyeo museum inland except for Jeju  Hello, I am a haenyeo grandmother from Yeongdo. Thank you so much for coming to our Yeongdo and the Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Museum. Since it's where I belong, I'd like to introduce the Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Museum myself.   First of all, I should tell you about the origin of 'haenyeo,' right? During the Joseon period, there was a time when tax collection was severe on Jeju Island. The male catchers who worked at sea left to hide or go to land one by one. However, the court continued to force people to offer seafood such as abalone to the king, so women started to dive for seafood, which became the haenyeo of today. At that time, the female divers were called Jomnyeo, Jamnyeo, and Jamsu, but as the Jeju dialect merged, they were also called Chomnyeo. The term 'haenyeo' was coined during the Japanese colonial period. It is an expression that has been commonly used in Korea and Japan since then to mean a woman who works at the sea.   'Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Museum,' the only haenyeo museum inland except for Jeju Island, is created to improve the outdated seafood sales facilities of Yeongdo Jungni Beach and maintain the cultural asset value of Yeongdo Haenyeo. Under the theme of 'We dive because there are friends and there is the sea,' various exhibitions and experience spaces preserve and use the activities of us haenyeo as cultural tourism resources.   On the first floor, there is a haenyeo seafood market. The space is an improved version of the way seafood was sold on the deck in the past. Many customers come here and eat seafood. If you go up to the second floor, there is a haenyeo culture exhibition room, and you can see a lot of information related to haenyeo, such as haenyeo clothes, fishing tools, and seafood that can be collected from the sea of ​​Yeongdo. You can go up on the 3rd-floor rooftop to see the wide-open Yeongdo sea, which is yet another fun.   The museum is closed every Monday, January 1, and the day of Lunar New Year's Day and Chuseok. It's open from 9 AM to 6 PM from Tuesday to Sunday, so please come visit! The first floor's haenyeo seafood market doesn't have any days off, so you can come anytime!

stories.title: Cathedral
stories.script: Cheonghak Cathedral, the oldest cathedral in Yeongdo  Welcome to Cheonghak Cathedral. In 1890, it was called Jeolyeong-dong Catholic Church, and Father Moyse Jozeau (Korean name Jo Deok-ha) from France was appointed to the church. But the very next year, the parish moved to Choryang, and this location remained a community for the churchgoers. Then, in 1907, Yeongdo, which used to be void of religion, was changed with a small church and auditorium. Then, in 1932, Father Kim Seon-bae Apostle John was appointed as the first pastor of the church, and the parish was approved for establishment. Cheonghak Cathedral became the second oldest cathedral in Busan after Beomil Catholic Church and the oldest in Yeongdo. It also opened its own night school for residents for illiteracy eradication projects. It played a central role in Catholicism settling down in Yeongdo.   Cheonghak Cathedral is also attracting much attention for its eclectic style. The outside is decorated with red stone, and at the highest spot, there is an image of the Sacred Heart of Jesus with arms outstretched as if giving out his love to the world. A stained glass window is installed inside, creating a different atmosphere from the outside. The interior space structure is in the early Basilica style, the church architecture style created after the Edict of Milan in the ancient Roman period. The flat, rectangular space is divided into an altar, a hallway, and naves.   The old church also has great historical value. After the 625 war, the cathedral was also activated to accommodate the increased number of refugees and distributed relief supplies. From the port opening era to the Japanese colonial rule, the 625 war, and now with the development of the fishery and shipbuilding industries of Yeongdo, Cheonghak Cathedral shares the history of the modern and contemporary history of Yeongdo and the Busan parish.

stories.title: temple
stories.script: Bogcheonsa, a temple with a panoramic view of Yeongdo  Located high on Bongrae Mountain, Bogcheonsa is well-known for its panoramic view of the Yeongdo sea and South Port Bridge. It branched out from Beomeosa, the 14th parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. According to the oral tradition of Yeongdo, Zen master Na-ong built Bogcheonsa in the late Goryeo period under the name 'Haeunam'.  The name Bogcheonsa derives from 'Bokcheonam,' a name given by Yang Wan-ho, who was praised in the traditional Buddhist art world in Busan and Yeongnam, and is said to have stated about the area near the temple in 1921 that The water in the surrounding valley is good. Yang Wan-ho built a new Mahavira Hall while managing a Buddhist painting center for the succession and development of traditional Buddhist art.   In 1953, monk Im Yeong-ju became the abbot and partially renovated the Mahavira Hall and the temple. In 1973, Zen master Dohae of Wolgongdang became the abbot, and he changed the name from Bokcheonam to Bogcheonsa and expanded the temple. Myeongbujeon (hall of the judgment of the dead), Chilseonggak (shrine hall of the Big Dipper), Sansingak (shrine hall of the mountain spirits), Yongwangdan (shrine hall of the dragon king), three-storied Yosa (buildings for everyday lives of monks), a bell tower, and an abbot's hall were newly built. Bogcheonsa was designated as Traditional Temple No. 31 in 2008.  In the summer of 2011, heavy rains caused the mountain behind the temple to collapse, damaging Myeongbujeon, Sansingak, and Chilseonggak. All damage has been restored since, and it's re-decorated with new looks.  The most significant attraction of Bogcheonsa is the view. It shows with pride a sweeping panoramic view during the day, a fantastic sunset in the evening, and a night view full of lights, making it a place that anyone in Busan who is interested in photography should visit at least once. Looking down upon the wide-open Yeongdo sea and emptying your mind may lead to some unexpected and precious realization at Bogcheonsa.

stories.title: Lady Shrine
stories.script: Mountain Shrine and Lady Shrine, the places to pray for peace in Yeongdo  The hillside of Bongrae Mountain in Yeongdo has a legend from the Silla Dynasty. Here is the story of Mountain Shrine and Lady Shrine. Would you like to hear it?  It happened in Jeolyeongdo, the present-day Yeongdo, during the Joseon Dynasty. A military officer of Busan, who oversaw war horses, had a problem. When the horses traveled westward from Jeolyeongdo, the problem was that they kept falling ill and dying. The following story was circulating at that time: a celestial lady went into Jeolyeongdo with two old women. Two old women came back out, but no one saw the celestial lady coming back out. The horses kept dying. Around that time, a 180cm-tall new military officer named Jeongbal was newly appointed to be in charge of the horses. One day, he saw the very celestial lady in his dream.   “I am Chilwonseonggun, who presides over the life and death of human beings. Since the Jade Emperor ascended to the throne, I couldn't stay in heaven and instead, became the queen of Tamna. However, General Choi Young of Goryeo set fire to capture Tamna. I became the general's concubine and dedicated my body and soul, but the general left the island and has not reached out to me since. Shindon told me that the general was exiled to Jeolyeongdo, so I came here, but I later found out that it was all lies. With no one to trust, I became a solitary spirit. If you build a shrine for me and comfort my soul, I will prevent the horses from dying and keep the people here at peace. Also, those who serve me will prosper and fulfill their wishes.”  General Jeongbal shared this story with the court, and the king ordered the chief of Dongrae Song Sang-hyeon to build the Mountain Shrine and Lady Shrine and hold communal rituals every spring and fall. Since then, war horses have ceased to die from an illness.   This legend illustrates historical facts such as that Yeongdo has served as a national horse court for a long time and that Jeju residents migrated from the island. The ritual continues to be held, where people pray for fishers to return with full loads of fish and for Yeongdo residents' happiness and peace. The ceremony happens twice a year, on January 15 and September 15 of the lunar calendar. Residents participate once every three years.

stories.title: The 75 Square
stories.script: The 75 Square. an excellent view with relaxation  Walking along the coastal trails in Yeongdo may bring you to a small but wonderful plaza that protrudes toward the coast. Its completion in 1975 gave its name 75 Square. The square connects to the Huinnyeoul Cultural Village, making it a resting place with superb scenery. If you pause and turn towards the sea during your walk, you will see a spectacular view that‘s like a gift.   The sound of the waves crashing, the gentle breeze, and the sight of the clean and blue Yeongdo sea will embrace your body and make you feel as if you have become a scholar of the past. The ships on the faraway sea of Yeongdo remind us that this is indeed a port city. The square provides different charms day and night. The open view of the sea offers an immersive, multi-sensory experience in the daytime. At night, the moon looming over the sea presents a different type of beauty.   There is a small beacon fire station next to the square. It was used for a long time to communicate and inform the country of urgent news, such as foreign invasions or domestic uprisings. Smoke was lit during the day and torches at night.   How about looking at the scenic sea from 75 Square and refreshing your mind?

stories.title: X-SPORTS Square
stories.script: X-SPORTS Square, where you can work out with the sea  Did you know that Yeongdo has excellent sports facilities where you can work out with the wide-open sea in the background? South Port Breakwater X-SPORTS Square stretches under South Port Bridge. It is a space that can be used comfortably by all people of all ages and genders in Yeongdo-gu.  The square's construction started in May 2010, and a completion ceremony was held in November 2013. An 854m-long and 10m-tall breakwater and a sports facility were newly built for locals. The square's edge is connected to the Jeolyeong Coastal Trail and thus becomes an extension of the walk. Often hosting many cultural events, the square also functions as a tourist and leisure space.   The square features an area for skateboarding and inline skating. There are also simple courts for basketball, foot volleyball, badminton, and tennis, a multi-purpose field with artificial turf, and a jogging track. The trail near the field accommodates comfortable walks and light jogging.   Another way to enjoy this square is to take the elevator to South Port Bridge and look down upon the X-SPORTS Square. You can discover a beautiful view!

stories.title: Yeongdo Tourism Information Center
stories.script: The observatory at the Yeongdo Tourism Information Center, where Yeongdo gets closer to you  What do you look for when you're traveling? Some look for famous restaurants and good food, and some scenic routes for a nice walk. Like this, the theme of the travel is decided based on the goal or the means of the trip. This is a great place to plan and start your journey in Yeongdo. It is Yeongdo Tourism Information Center, inspired by the Yeongdo Bridge's appearance.   The Center that boasts a striking look consists of the ground floor to the third floor and an outdoor observatory. On the ground floor, you are greeted by intuitive touchscreens that introduce various legends and stories about Yeongdo, as well as renowned tourist attractions and the Eight Scenic Places of Yeongdo. The second floor is the Yeongdo modern history exhibition room. It invites you to learn about Yeongdo's modern history through comparative timelines between now and 1920. The third-floor houses Bongrae Lighters Wharf gallery, which exhibits unique artists active in Yeongdo.   The observatory on the top floor is the highlight of the Information Center! You can watch the famous bascule bridge of Yeongdo opening and closing. You can look down upon the busy pier of Busan with moored fishing boats through the framed photo zone. It is also a great spot to take memorable photographs.    Yeongdo Tourism Information Center is open all year round except for January 1st, the Lunar New Year's day, and the day of Chuseok to provide information to the tourists, so please make sure to stop by if you have planned for a Yeongdo trip!

stories.title: Sky Observatory
stories.script: Sky Observatory  What is your impression of Busan’s seascape? Usually, people think of a blue ocean, waves crashing under the sparkling sun and the blue sky. Yeongdo’s Sky Observatory, just like its name, invites you to enjoy the picturesque view of the open sky and sea. Here you can truly appreciate Busan’s marine landscapes.    The Sky Observatory features a semi-transparent floor from which everyone, even children, can observe the breathtaking view from above. A corner for couples allows them to attach padlocks as a romantic gesture. From the observatory, you can see many different islands. You can even see Daema Island using telescopes installed in the observatory on a clear day.    The Sky Observatory is located on the Jeoryeong Coastal Walk between Huinnyeoul Culture Village and Taejongdae. It’s also connected to the 75 Plaza. Enjoy the feeling of walking on clouds at the Sky Observatory, from which you can immerse yourself in the view of the open sea to the front and rich, green forests to the back, all enveloped in a cool marine breeze. Here you can start your day refreshed and clear your head at the end of the day.

stories.title: Taejongdae Observatory
stories.script: Taejongdae Observatory, where you can appreciate the gift of nature  The name 'Taejongdae' originates from King Taejong Muyeol of the Silla Dynasty. While touring the country, the king was captivated by the breathtaking coastal scenery and enjoyed practicing archery in the park area. Spanning about 440 acres, the Taejongdae Recreation Area centers around its highest peak, standing 250 meters above sea level, and boasts an array of approximately 120 tree species, including the sea pine. Along the coast, one can marvel at cliffs, uniquely shaped rocks, and views of the Korea Strait. On clear days, Japan's Tsushima Island, about 56 km away, is visible.  The Taejongdae Observatory was designated as a tourist attraction representing Busan in 1969, designated as National Cultural Heritage Site No. 17 in November 2005, and declared a National Geopark on November 27, 2013. It stands as the only destination in Busan to be selected five times consecutively as one of the '100 Best Korean Tourist Destinations' by the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism and the Korea Tourism Organization. The observatory offers convenient indoor tourist facilities, including picnic-themed cafes, Korean restaurants, and convenience stores. Visitors are greeted with panoramic views of the azure sea upon arrival.  However, before becoming a prominent tourist spot, Taejongdae Observatory witnessed tragic incidents. In the 1970s, despairing individuals jumped from the cliffs to commit suicide where the observatory now stands. It was once infamously known as 'Suicide Rock.' To address this social concern, Gumyeongsa Temple was built in 1976, serving as a poignant reminder of the value of life for visitors. Additionally, a statue portraying a mother embracing two children was installed at the entrance of Taejongdae Observatory, symbolizing profound maternal love and offering solace and hope to those contemplating suicide.  Immerse yourself in the beauty of nature at Taejongdae Observatory?leave behind life's daily hardships and adversities and relish the gift of serene moments bestowed by nature.

stories.title: Cheonghak Reservoir Observatory
stories.script: Cheonghak Reservoir Observatory, where the lights of the city and the port dance together  The port city of Busan has many attractions near piers. What comes to mind first when you think of Busan's night view? Recently, places with a panoramic view of Busan's harbor have emerged as new night view spots. They are called 'harbor view' spots.  The Yeongdo Cheonghak Reservoir Observatory is one of the most popular harbor view spots. It overlooks Yeongdo and its surrounding seas as well as the Busanhangdaegyo Bridge, which shines with different lights every minute. Lights from the city and docks harmonize together here, creating an admirable view. The scenery created by the high mountains, waterways, and the urban landscape of Busan is spectacular.  The way to the observatory features public exercise facilities in an ample open space. The facilities include exercise equipment and acupressure pebbles. The surrounding area of the observatory is also well-known as a filming location for famous TV shows and movies.  There are sculptures of Jeolyeong horses and a farmer carrying sweet potatoes at the observatory, all of which symbolize Yeongdo.  Jeolyeongdo, which was the original name of Yeongdo, was known for the farm that raised national horses.    Its production of many famous horses is recorded in historical documents, including Samguk Sagi, Goryeosa, and Dongguk Yeoji Seungram, and is now celebrated by statues that represent Jeolyeong horses. Yeongdo's sweet potatoes are also famous. Yeongdo was the first planting site for sweet potatoes, which were introduced by Chosun's diplomat Jo Eom. Raw sweet potatoes used to relieve hunger in the past. The gentle smile of the farmer carrying the sweet potato comes through.   Below the deck is a map that introduces Yeongdo's attractions. Check out the Busanhangdaegyo Bridge as well as downtown Yeongdo. The harmony of Busan's iconic pier and the splendid city center will forever stay in your memories.

stories.title: Sunrise Observatory
stories.script: Sunrise Observatory, where the sun rises with hope  The Sunrise Observatory is the first place to see the rising sun in Busan. Sunrise Village, which houses the Observatory, is located at the highest point in Yeongdo. The lush, crimson sunrise emerges from the eastern slopes of Bongrae mountain. It is said that the village’s name reflects the residents’ wish to prosper together with the rising sun.  Sunrise Village was originally a cemetery. During the Korean War, North Korean refugees wandered in search of a place to live. They built houses with stones and soil and established a village. Later, refugees living near Busan Station joined, expanding the town. The village stood upon the sorrows of life, buried along with the lives of refugees.  Sunrise Village stands where the top road of the village, a long walk down the steep alleyway between the narrow houses, and the Bongraesan trail meet. Its connection to the path makes the village part of a popular hiking course. During the day, you can enjoy the beautiful view of Bongrae Mountain, a pride of Yeongdo. The fantastic night view of Busan from the Sunrise Observatory is also worth checking out.   The Sunrise Observatory was built in 2016. Its terrace features a photo zone, a cafe where you can enjoy a cup of coffee and a view of the village, and an observation deck overlooking the village. The colorful houses of the village at sunrise add to the fun of looking at the scenery.  It is a place where the scenery is as incredible as the height of the tall town. How about greeting Busan’s morning at the Sunrise Observatory?

stories.title: Seobok Observatory
stories.script: Seobok Observatory, a wish for immortality in nature  Have you ever heard of a person named Seobok? Qinshihuang, the first emperor to unify mainland China, and his subject, Seobok, were inseparable. The story of their relationship continues to this day.  In Yeongdo, there is a park that thematizes Seobok’s story as a tourist attraction. At the ‘Bulocho Park,’ which is based on Qin Shi Huang’s long-lasted dream of immortality, you can see an observatory after passing the Bulomun, the door of eternal youth. The name of this observatory is ‘Seobok Observatory.’ The name comes from a legend that one of the places where Qinshihuang sent Seobok to find the elixir plant was Bongrae Mountain.  The legend goes, Bongrae Mountain that Seobok visited is located in the middle of the eastern sea and houses gods, elixir plants, and elixirs of eternal life. The Bulocho Park, completed in 2014 on Busan’s Bongrae Mountain, fosters various medicinal herbs and numerous ecological resources. Yeongdo residents, as well as visitors from all over the country, come to this place.  The Seobok Observatory stands on the other side of the Bulomun Gate of Bulocho Park. Bullomun is a gate that symbolizes longevity and contains the wish of Qinshihuang, who wanted to find elixir plants that promised eternal youth and immortality.   The scenery from the observatory here is just as spectacular as the folk tales handed down over the years. From here, you can see Busan Port and Busanhangdaegyo from sunrise to nightfall. Please enjoy the superb view that nature offers from the Seobok Observatory.

stories.title: Jungni Sunset Observatory
stories.script: Jungni Sunset Observatory, where you can enjoy a golden sunset  What do you think when you see a sunset that burns red and then sets? Busan has a lot of famous spots known for sunrise and sunset, and Dadaepo Beach is one of the best-known spots. But did you know that Yeongdo also has excellent places to watch the sunset?   You can safely and comfortably enjoy the sunset in the scenery that harmonizes a red lighthouse and blue waves at the Jungni Sunset Observatory on Jungni Beach, the starting and ending point of the Jeolyeong Coastal Trail in Yeongdo.  Yeongdo Jungni Beach, a gravel beach with a sunset observatory and Haenyeo Village, is also known as ‘Jungri Haenyeo Village.’ This is where the Jungni Sunset Observatory is. Unlike other beaches, the waves here are calm, and the coastal road is beautiful, making it one of the most scenic driving routes.  The Jungni Sunset Observatory features a square frame-shaped photo zone and a unique viewing facility with one end fixed and the other unsupported. It is also connected to Yeongdo Galmaetgil, which provides an opportunity to enjoy the fresh air, take a walk during the daytime, and wrap up a long day by watching a sunset in Jungni.

stories.title: Busan Bridge
stories.script: Busan Bridge, a symbolic bridge of Busan  There are a total of 7 coastal bridges in Busan that connect land and sea. Busan Bridge, built as a symbol of the development of Busan Port, broke its ground in 1976 and was completed in 1980. Before the bridge's opening, the current Yeongdo Bridge was called Busan Bridge. It has been connecting Jung-gu and Yeongdo-gu in Busan ever since its completion.  Busan Bridge has replaced the current Yeongdo Bridge, which was built under Japanese rule, as a representative structure of Busan. Its name comes from the fact that it represents Busan as the longest arch bridge in Korea. This gorgeous bridge celebrated the 100th anniversary of the opening of Busan Port and symbolizes Korea's industrial development.   Busan Bridge functions as an industrial road and a port road that easily handles the traffic volume of the Yeongdo district, a shipbuilding industrial complex, and a new port. Large trucks weighing 54 tons that cannot pass through the Yeongdo Bridge can pass Busan Bridge. The bridge also connects to Busan's urban expressway and thus directly links Busan Port and Gyeongbu Expressway.  Busan Bridge was designed and constructed by Korean engineers and is considered a turning point in developing domestic architectural engineering and construction technologies. Its size and complex structure make it meaningful that Korean engineers completed it with Korean materials.  The size is truly impressive. It is 260m long and 20m wide and has four-lane roadways and sidewalks 2m wide on each side.   Steel arches made of the tide arch method, a design method that connects the bridges at both ends of the arch with horizontal tension members, rise to a height of 31m, becoming a symbol of Busan. The original color of the bridge was orange, but it is now gray and white, reflecting modern beauty. Its new hues harmonize with the surrounding area, stabilizing the vibrant harbor nearby and downtown atmosphere.  Please take a closer look at the Busan Bridge, which shows the true nature of the port city of Busan and its value as a magnificent bridge.

stories.title: South Port Bridge
stories.script: South Port Bridge, connecting the South Port and Yeongdo with beautiful lights  Busan has many bridges that let you walk on the sea road. South Port Bridge is particularly famous for its landscape lighting in Yeongdo-gu, where four bridges are connected. Although it does not have remarkable sculptures or statues, the installed lighting gracefully harmonizes with the structural beauty of the bridge. South Port Bridge is a maritime bridge that connects Amnam-dong, Seo-gu, Busan and Yeongseon-dong, Yeongdo-gu. Its name comes from it linking the South Port to Yeongdo.   South Port Bridge has 3m wide sidewalks, allowing pedestrians to stroll and enjoy the scenery of the South Port area freely. Visitors can also enjoy views of Yongdusan Park, Jagalchi Market, Huinnyeoul Village, Jeolyeong Coastal Walk, and Songdo Beach.  South Port Bridge has unexpected charms. Its day and night are 180 degrees different. It provides a reliable walking trail during the day and presents a beautiful night view of the South Port adorned by a state-of-the-art LED lighting system. The visual feast of ships sleeping at the anchorage amidst the dazzling lights from sunset to midnight is also a sight to behold.  The 360m-long main route, where ships pass, decorates the night view with a dynamic colorful lighting spectacle every hour on Saturdays and public holidays. Enjoy the splendid display of lights on South Port Bridge.

stories.title: Busan Port Bridge
stories.script: Busan Port Bridge, the landmark of Busan  Busan Port Bridge, whose name comes from its function of connecting across Busan Port, was built on the North Port, the largest port in Busan. It is Korea's first steel-composite cable-stayed bridge and is rated as the world's fifth-largest steel-composite cable-stayed bridge. The bridge has received many external awards and honors, including the Grand Prize for Civil Structures by the Korean Society of Civil Engineers in 2015, the Grand Prize in Civil Engineering and Construction Technology in 2014, and the Best Artwork Award by the Concrete Society in 2014.  Busan Port Bridge connects Gamman-dong and Cheonghak-dong. This 3,331m-long bridge crosses the North Port and consists of a 1,114m-long cable-stayed section and a 2,217m-long connecting bridge. It forms the central axis of the coastal ring road connecting Gwangan Bridge, Yeongdo Highway Overpass, and South Port Bridge. The bridge has a reputation as a luxury bridge for providing a safe structure for transportation and beautiful scenery. Its diamond-shaped pylon offers an unforgettable spectacle and, at the same time, functions to resist wind more effectively.   Busan Port Bridge has a unique space—a camping ground in the city center. Yeongdo Marino Auto Camping Ground, a place where you can see the whole of Busan Port, represents the sea and the O-shaped circular path coming together in harmony. This eco-friendly campground has 52 sites (40 for cars, 12 for regular tents) where you can set up your tent and enjoy camping. There are also 7 fixed caravans where you can stay overnight, 107 parking lots, a walking trail, and an event plaza.  Please enjoy the leisure provided by Busan Port Bridge, the representative coastal bridge of Busan, and take memorable photographs, too.

stories.title: Cheong Wa Dae
stories.script: A Cultural Space of New Hope Cheong Wa Dae  The current site of Cheong Wa Dae addressed at 1(il), Cheongwadae-ro in Jongno-gu, Seoul, has been filled with the energy of the king since the Goryeo dynasty. The site served as a location of the royal palace of Namgyeong during the Goryeo dynasty and the back garden of Gyeongbokgung Palace in the Joseon dynasty. At the time of Goryeo, the capital city of Gaegyeong, Seogyeong, and Donggyeong were designated as “Samgyeong,” or three pivotal cities, based on the principles of feng shui. During the reign of King Sukjong of the Goryeo dynasty in 1104, a secondary palace was founded at this site, replacing Donggyeong as a pivotal city, and was renamed Namgyeong, meaning “Capital of the South.”  The site of Cheong Wa Dae reappears in history with the foundation of Joseon dynasty. Taejo Yi Sung-gye, the founder and first king of the Joseon dynasty, established a special organization to develop a new city plan for Seoul. He sent out his officers to seek an appropriate site for his new palace. The king’s people concluded that the site of the secondary palace in Namgyeong was too small and therefore the new palace should be built more to the south, which led to the establishment of Gyeongbokgung Palace at its current location. The secondary palace became the back garden of Gyeongbokgung Palace under the reign of King Sejong the Great in 1426.  Gyeongbokgung Palace was completely destroyed during the Imjin War of 1592. It was left abandoned for 270 years until towards the end of the Joseon dynasty, when Heungseondaewongun ordered to rebuild the palace, turning it into a garden named Gyeongmudae. During the Japanese colonial period, the residence of Japanese General-Governor was built on this site while the Japanese General Government Building was built right nearby, blocking the way to Gyeongbokgung Palace in an attempt to cut off people’s morale and spirit away from the Korean regime.    After the liberation of Korea in 1945, the general government building was used as an office for American General Hodge, then as the executive office and residential quarters by President Rhee Syngman until President Roh Tae-woo held office. The name Cheong Wa Dae, which means “a house with blue roof tiles,” was named by President Yun Posun.  Cheong Wa Dae consists of the Main Office Building, Yeongbingwan, Official Residence of the President, Sangchunjae, Nokjiwon Garden, Chunchugwan Press Center, and Yeomingwan. Although Cheong Wa Dae had been closed to the public until now, this was not always the case. During President Rhee’s time in office, Cheong Wa Dae was open to the public for two to three days during spring season as a cherry blossom attraction along with Changgyeonggung Palace.  But when the North Korean forces infiltrated into South Korean borders in 1968, Cheong Wa Dae strengthened its defense, shutting its doors to the public. Even the roads were closed, followed by prohibited entrance to Inwangsan and Bugaksan mountains. Twenty years later, President Roh Tae-woo reopened Cheong Wa Dae to the public, followed by an expansion of accessible premises to Cheong Wa Dae of today.  Cheong Wa Dae has served as the presidential office and residence to President Rhee Syngman, the first president of Korea, and the presidents that followed, up to President Moon Jae-in, the 19th president of Korea.  Today, Cheong Wa Dae is a cultural space, welcoming the public with its doors wide open.

stories.title: Main Office Building
stories.script: The Symbol of Cheong Wa Dae  The main office building stands as the iconic symbol of Cheong Wa Dae. Nestled against the backdrop of Bugaksan Mountain, it offers a breathtaking panoramic view. It is a place where the president carries out official duties, hosts foreign heads of state and diplomatic envoys. It is also the place that always appears in the media for all things related to Cheong Wa Dae.  Constructed on September 4, 1991, it was deemed inappropriate to continue using the former Governor-General of Joseon's building from the Japanese colonial era as the presidential office and residence. The new main office building was constructed on the basis of traditional woodwork and palace architectural style for its exterior, while featuring modern architectural amenities on the inside. Its majestic hip-and-gable-blue-tiled roof with emphasized curves serves as a striking exterior architecture. There are 11 Japsangs on the roof, a type of imperial roof decoration, signifying the elevated status of Cheong Wa Dae. Even the main hall of Gyeongbokgung Palace only displays nine Japsangs on its roof. The roof consists of a total of 150,000 carefully baked tiles designed to last for over a century.  The main office building comprises a two-story central structure with a single-floor wing on both sides. Upon entering the front door, a grand staircase adorned with a red carpet leads your way. Each room is graced with an elegant chandelier hanging from the ceiling, creating a resplendent interior throughout the building.

stories.title: Yeongbingwan
stories.script: The Official Banquet Venue for Diplomatic Guests  Yeongbingwan  Yeongbingwan is the first building that comes into view as you enter Cheong Wa Dae. With imposing pillars extending to the second floor, Yeongbingwan was used to hold large-scale meetings and official events for diplomatic guests. This state guest house was completed in December 1978 to accommodate the increasing number of diplomatic guests who visited Cheong Wa Dae in the 1970s.   Yeongbingwan has a total of eighteen stone pillars supporting the entire building, with four granite pillars in front seamlessly extending to the second floor. At glance, it looks like a Greek temple with a tiled roof, which was a popular architectural style for government buildings in the 1970s. The Sejong Center for the Performing Arts and the National Assembly Building are also designed in a similar style.  In the Joseon period, kings set up a personal farming ground and a shrine within the palace grounds to predict the harvest of the year. King Sejong set up his own in the back garden of Gyeongbokgung Palace, whereas King Seongjeong set up his farming land in Changgyeonggung Palace. The site of Yeongbingwan used to be where King Gojong set up his farming land and shrine, known as Gyeongnongjae. Gyeongongjae was built together with the reconstruction of Gyeongbokgung Palace. King Gojong had his farmland divided into eight sections to represent the eight regions of Korea. Each section was planted with grain seeds from its corresponding region. This farmland was called paldobaemi, meaning “rice paddies of the eight regions.”   In 2000, President Kim Dae-jung planted pine trees from Gyeongsang-do, Jeolla-do, Chungcheong-do and Gangwon-do with the purpose of reviving the meaning behind paldobaemi.
