Another interesting story name Mal Deung So is passed on and says that Gung Ye jumped into the river, struggled for his life in the rapids, and was saved by his own horse, which became a rock in the middle of the river. Do you see that the rock in front of you resembles a horse head? Whether or not these stories are true, they show that Gung Ye was in a lot of trouble when trying to cross this river. It is also noticeable that 30- to 40-meter-high cliffs of columnar joints have been well developed on the opposite side of the river. These particular cliffs were formed by a strong flow of water running along the bottom of the cliffs. The granite rocks blocked the water flow, which in turn pushed the columnar joints to the right and eventually as a result, the lower parts of the cliffs were deeply dented and their colors were darkened. The Neoreunbawi, or Spacious Rock, was a popular spot for picnics amongst the nearby middle & high school students back in the 1970s and 1980s. It is why it is also a place of nostalgic memories to some local mid-aged citizens.

stories.title: Minchulrang Observation Rest Area
stories.script: Arrival Announcement at Minchulrang Observation Rest Area You have reached Minchulrang Observation Rest Area.  Overview of Minchulrang Does the name Minchulrang sound friendly to you? It refers to a section of cliffs open to the steeply sloped rapids; it is actually a local dialect word meaning sheer cliff. Its origin is not clear, but the history of it doesn't seem to be very long. Do you feel overwhelmed by the lava plateau here at the top of a vertical cliff? I hope you're not intimidated, though. This particular section of the river is very narrow with a 30m to 40m width, and well-known for shallow and fast-flowing whitewater. Villagers moving to Cheorwon when a ceasefire agreement was made during the Korean War had to cross the Hantan River, and this Minchulrang area was one of the best options available to them. So, you can say that it is also a place where the sorrows of the Cheorwon settlers still stand resounding, associated with its calm and yet stunning scenery.  Would you like to listen to the astounding roars of the river rushing along the cliffs and rubbing against the river bed for a while? Another thing worth not missing is the waterfalls from the rice paddies on the top of the cliffs revealing themselves along the Columnar Joint Road down the river during the farming or rainy seasons.

stories.title: Maetdolrang Observation Rest Area
stories.script: Arrival Announcement at Maetdolrang Observation Rest Area You have arrived at Maetdolrang Observation Rest Area. This particular rest area is associated with a heart-breaking story.  Massive Flood in Cheorwon in 1996 From July 26 to 28, 1996, as much as 738 mm of torrential rain fell in the Cheorwon area, causing massive flooding damages. A landslide occurred in the mountainous area, which claimed a lot of casualties, and the collapse of the river banks destroyed dozens of houses and buried farming lands, resulting in 199.2 billion won in property damage.  Overview of Maetdolrang Observation Rest Area There used to be a large flat disk-shaped rock plate here in this area. A pair of disk-shaped stones, or millstones, were used to grind grains every day in Korea, and this is why the large flat round rock located here was called Maetdolrang locally in Korean. Unfortunately, the millstone-shaped rock was washed away during the 1996 Great Flood, and so is no longer in sight. The disk rock is long gone but still remains in the hearts of the villagers around here.  Overview of the Next Stop You need to walk up quite a steep staircase till the next stop, the Deureuni Rest Area from the Sundam direction or the Minchulrang Rest Area from the Deureuni direction. Please take your time and walk slowly with your earphones off.

stories.title: Deureuni Observation Rest Area
stories.script: Arrival Announcement at Deureuni Rest Area This rest area is one of the best locations to take a panoramic view of the Hantan River. Those of you coming all the way from the Sundam direction have worked really hard to get up here. For those of you who have just started your scenic journey from the Deureuni entrance, this is the first spot stop to view and experience the charming beauty of the river. Whichever direction you're coming from, I hope you will have a chance to appreciate the picturesque landscape presented and the calm blue-green river flowing below granite cliffs.  Overview of Deureuni Walking along this Columnar Joint Road is, to me personally, like watching a long-running soap opera with geological features as the main characters. Granite created 100 million years ago and basalt formed 540,000 years ago are lined up like brothers and sisters, and the plants growing close in harmony with the rocks will definitely add to the attractive elegance of the Hantan River Columnar Joints. The sights of harmonious and yet distinctive landscapes lead us to realize the way we are living alone or sometimes together with the people around us from birth till our parting moments. I hope the memories of walking along this road will help you through any difficult times by remembering the harmonies of the nature beyond any verbal descriptions for a long time after you visit our town.   Those of you coming from the Deureuni direction will continue to enjoy the dazzling scenery along the route till Sundam, and those of you from the Sundam direction will hopefully have one more look at this landscape and cherish the experience with the Hantan River in your memory. Thank you for your visit.

stories.title: Overview of Cheorwon
stories.script: Location of Cheorwon Welcome to Cheorwon County. I am Sunhee Kim, a geopark Interpreter of Cheorwon County. I am here to tell you about the attractions of our county while walking along the road today. I am glad to be of some assistance through these audio clips. Let me first introduce our county to you.    Intro When you hear the name Cheorwon, what first comes to mind? Many Korean men say Cheorwon reminds them of their military service days while Korean women associate our town with cold weather and delicious rice named Odae Rice. How about you?   Historic and Geographic Features of Cheorwon Located in the North-western part of Gangwon-do Province, Cheorwon is one of the northernmost areas in South Korea. When seen, however, from the strategically military viewpoints in terms of the whole peninsula including North Korea, Cheorwon is situated in the center of the Korean Peninsula, just like the belly button of a human body. A Korean historic figure, named Gung Ye, established Taebong State, and made Cheorwon its capital city in the late 9th century during the Later Three Kingdoms Period of Korea. This explains why there are so many legends related with King Gung Ye along with historic sites including the walls of the fortress surrounding the area. This town is also well-known as the area where Im Kkeokjeong, the leader of a peasant rebellion, was especially active in the mid-16th century during the Joseon Dynasty of Korea. If you visit Goseokjeong Pavilion, you will have more chances to hear many legends about this Korean version of Robin Hood. It was one of the most flourishing towns during the Japanese Colonial Era as it was connected with several major roads, with a major train station on the Gyeongwon Line from Seoul to Wonsan, and two department stores at the time. Many historic sites from the Korean War are located in Cheorwon, including the so-called Iron Triangle battle grounds such as White Horse Hill and Ice Cream Hill. The Second Tunnel of Aggression discovered here in Cheorwon back in 1975 is also a popular tourist site for South Korea's Peace Tours for peace-keeping efforts. These show the strategic, geo-political significance of this town serving as the base of various cultures throughout Korean history.   Geological Features of Cheorwon When traveling in Cheorwon, you are going to come across a lot of exotic rocks all over the area. These rocks are basalt with many pores on them, which are known to be commonly found in volcanic areas. Why then, are they here in Cheorwon? That's because this area was formed through lava activities. Cheorwon was created by lava eruptions between 540,000 to 120,000 years ago. Lava flowed from the crack between the 452-meter-high Orisan Mountain in Pyeonggang County, North Korea, and its neighboring 680m-high plateau to cover the whole Cheorwon in lava making it a lava plateau. When we think about a volcanic explosion, we usually imagine lava erupting from the tip of a volcano, but here in Cheorwon, lava as thin as honey water pierced through the crust and flowed here, creating a wide plain with rivers instead of gigantic, volcanic mountains such as Baekdusan Mountain or Hallasan Mountain in Korea. Over time, water started to flow in the deep dented areas to form the Hantan River, which is one of the best-known tourist attractions in Cheorwon. Numerous vertical cliffs and columnar joints from the cooled lava consist of the dazzling landscapes along the river. It is also important to note that Jeong Seon, an iconic Korean landscape painter living in the mid-18th century, chose this particular river and its surrounding scenes as the main themes of his true-view Korean landscape paintings. Wouldn't you like to feel the way the famed Korean painter depicted in his masterpieces? The Hantan River Columnar Joint Road and other trails along the water way are here for you to get the most from your visit here.  Specialty Products of Cheorwon The lava plateau surface in Cheorwon makes up a wide plain, so growing rice is one of the most popular farming activities with many water-supply facilities around. The local rice produced here in Cheorwon is sold as Cheorwon Odae Rice, which is a signature brand of rice in this town. The Cheorwon Basin has fertile soil due to the decomposed basalt and is well equipped with irrigation facilities. In the surrounding farmlands, fallen grains after the harvest season provide a rich source of food for migratory birds, making the plains a popular habitat for cranes and geese, where you can enjoy winter bird tours. Cranes are also a symbol of Cheorwon County. In winter, there is a crane birding tour program that departs from the DMZ peace town, so please don't forget to come again to check out the mysterious migratory birds with your family in winter.  Closing Remarks They say we can enjoy certain things better when we take our time. The slogan Slower is better is really recommended when you're traveling through our town, Cheorwon. That's the way you can get a better experience of the nature and the hospitality of the local people in our beautiful town. Shall we get started now?

stories.title: Goseokjeong Pavilion
stories.script: Overview of the name Goseokjeong Pavilion, listed as Number One of the Nine Scenic Spots of the Cheorwon, is an iconic symbol of Cheorwon Tourism, with the great harmony of the Hantan River and odd-looking cliffs, and is also a national tourist site as well. The view-point pavilion, together with a 15-meter-tall granite rock standing in the middle of the Hantan River and a pine forest growing on it, has been named Goseokjeong since King Jinpyeong of Silla Dynasty in the early 7th century. Many more kings during the Goryeo and Joseon Dynasties are also recorded to have visited this acclaimed scenic spot. Legend also has it that Im Kkeokjeong, a Korean version of Robin Hood, hid himself within the caves of the Goseok Rock while fleeing from government soldiers in the mid-16th century during the Joseon Dynasty.  Geological Features around Goseokjeong Pavilion This area is also worth citing for its geological values. The Hantan River, flowing below the Goseokjeong Pavilion, is the only volcanic river in the whole Korean Peninsula and has unique and high geological values such as curious harmonies between basalt and granite. Basalt gorges stand in symmetry on both sides of the deeply dented river in the lava plain. All the dark-colored basalt rocks are washed away and distinctively light-colored granite rocks are revealed in the river bed where rapid currents have winding turns and faster flow. Goseokjeong Pavilion is in a location where you can also view rather contrary and asymmetric scenes.  Tourist Attractions near Goseokjeong Pavilion Now, let me give you a few more tips about how to better enjoy your visit here. King Sejong's Gangmu Pavilion on the right of the entrance of the downhill staircase was named after the historic record that King Sejong of the Joseon Dynasty visited Cheorwon 19 times for military trainings called Gangmu and hunting. The pavilion is a good place to view the breath-taking scenery of the gorge. The pavilion down the staircase is called Goseokjeong Pavilion, which was restored back in 1971 after it was burnt down to ashes during the Korean War.   Now, would you like to go down to view the Goseok Rock? You can appreciate the solid style of the rock standing alone in the middle of the Hantan River. It looks classy at any time of the year, and each season has a different style to appreciate. The pine forest growing from the cracks at the top of the rock without soil show an atmosphere of integrity. At the bottom of the massive rock, you can see the interesting layers of rocks piled up one after another. Its spectacular settings were the reason why this area was used as a filming location for Korean movies such as The Fatal Encounter and Kundo: Age of the Rampant and for Korean TV series such as The Slave Hunters and Hur Jun. From spring to autumn, you can hire a motor-powered boat and view the odd-looking rock cliffs from aboard the boat; when looked up at from the level of the flowing water, the 15-meter-high rock looks like a massive work of sculpture. It goes without saying that the boat-ride is definitely worth trying at least once.  How to Enjoy Your Visit Better at Goseokjeong Pavilion It would be a good idea to visit the Hantan River UNESCO Geopark Visitor Center to get a better chance to learn more about the geology of Cheorwon on your way back home after your visit to the pavilion. It's also worth visiting a local food market called Today's Farmers where local specialty products such as fresh produce grown by local farmers and processed foods are sold. You can also get more information at Tourist Information Centers about the DMZ Peace Tours including Cheorwon Peace Observatory and Woljeong-ri Station, which is an abandoned train station on the northernmost end of Korail's Gyeongwon Line, located within the Civilian Control Zone.

stories.title: Sambuyeon Falls
stories.script: Overview of Sambuyeon Falls Sambuyeon Falls, listed as No. 2 of the Nine Scenic Spots in Cheorwon, is a 1-meter-wide, 20-meter-tall waterfall flowing down the cliffs at Myeongseongsan Mountain. This scenic waterfall was named by a Confucian scholar named Kim Chang Heup with a pen name of Sam Yeon in the early 18th century and its true landscape was painted by the famed painter Jeong Seon. It was also listed as one of the 50 beautiful places to visit in South Korea by CNN Travel in 2013. The name literally means three cauldron waterfalls in Korean as the waterfall streams are bent three times and looks like three cauldrons.   A Legend of Sambuyeon Falls According to a legend, four imaginary pythons lived in these waterfalls a long time ago and only three of them were able to transform themselves into dragons. When these dragons flew up to the sky, they wiggled their tails to leave the rocky cliffs on either side of the waterfall smooth with large holes. When the other failed python becomes bad-tempered, a drought occurs in Cheorwon and local residents have to set up an altar and hold a ritual for rain.  Geological Characteristics of Sambuyeon Falls Do you see a big dent cut off on the left-hand side of the waterfall where water does not flow down? It is where the waterfall flowed before the current waterfall flows. Several traces of the water stream can be observed at Sambuyeon Falls. These show that the erosion was concentrated on the spots where the stream flowed for a long time or where its direction is bent along the joints. Not only is the downpouring water fascinating at this water fall, it is also a place with so many secrets kept hidden.  How to Enjoy Your Sightseeing at Sambuyeon Falls The small opening on the right is called Oryonggul. It was dug by soldiers back in 1973 and was actually used until Yonghwa Tunnel was opened in 2016. It is currently used only for tourism. When looked at from a distance, the water falls are gorgeous, but you can also feel great awe when hearing the roars of the falling water. Why don't you close your eyes and focus only on the sounds here for a while?

stories.title: Jiktang Falls
stories.script: Origin of Jiktang Falls Welcome to Jiktang Falls after crossing the cute, little bridge. This is where you can view water falling like a curtain over the 80-meter-wide columnar joints across the Hantan River. The name Jiktang was changed over time from Jiktan, meaning rapids where the water falls vertically.”    Columnar Joints If you take a closer look inside the falling water, you can observe basalt. Jiktang Falls is unique in that water flowed for a long time on the basalt lava which was cooled and hardened layer by layer, weathering and cutting into the rock to form the cascading waterfall. It is just 3 meters tall but as wide as over 80 meters. This waterfall, made up of naturally straight-lined rocks between the much higher cliffs on either side of the Hantan River, is also listed as one of the Nine Scenic Spots in Cheorwon for its magnificence, uniqueness, and beauty.  Features of Jiktang Falls When we think of a waterfall, we usually imagine a water stream falling from a very high location. In that sense, you might find this waterfall rather disappointing with its short stature. The appeal here is the impressive width of as much as 80 meters. You might find it even calming while looking at this draped cooling water over the whole width of the river. The waterfall may look not intimidating but friendly to you just like your neighbors who don't stand out but look familiar. Jiktang Falls are also nicknamed as live, moving waterfalls because the on-going erosion is taking place with the continuously falling forces of the water, which collapse the basalt columns and in turn move the location of the waterfalls little by little upstream. This phenomenon is called headward erosion in geology, which is also found in Bidulginang Falls nearby and Jaein Falls in Yeoncheon County.  How to Enjoy Your Visit Better at Jiktang Falls Jiktang Falls look very different from various view points, and so you may want to move around from location to location to look at them from different directions from left to right and from top to bottom. The western bottom corner is regarded as the best location to view the water fall in the most fascinating and loudest way. To not miss the chance to take cool pictures, we recommend walking a litter further upstream of the water fall where you will find a basalt bridge, which is photogenic.

stories.title: Songdaeso Columnar Joints
stories.script: Overview of Songdaeso Cheorwon was formed along the Hantan River, so a lot of names are related with the river. The river means big rapids in Korean. The water here does not flow as fast as water drops are splashed, but flows as fast as the sound of water flowing. On the other hand, the place where the flow of water stops for a while is called yeon, and the place where the water is deep among such places is called so as in the suffix of Songdaeso. Songdaeso is one of the deepest with a depth of 15 to 20 meters, which is actually among the deepest in the Hantan River.  Overview of Songdaeso Columnar Joints Upon arriving at Songdaeso, please take a look around first. The columnar joints with breathtaking scenery seem to make you forget where you are for a while. Songdaeso Columnar Joints are where the characteristics of the Hantan River are best showed  shown together, where you can see the best view of the columnar joints where the basalt cliffs have fallen off by the grain. The columnar joints at Songdaeso were created by vertical splitting as the hot lava cooled, reducing its volume and generally remaining in the form of pentagonal or hexagonal columns. Watching the river flowing through the gaps with autumn leaves flowing on may give you a sense of awe towards nature.  The shape of the upper and lower parts of the cliffs forming a harmonious stairway, piles of basalt stones piled under the cliff, a sandy beach formed by sedimentation next to them, and a flock of ducks leisurely floating there may lead you to have an imagination of looking at a watercolor landscape. Above all, the harmony between the 30meter-tall vertical cliff and the jade-colored river water that looks deeper than the cliff height might make you excited with admiration.  How to Enjoy Your Sightseeing at Songdaeso Columnar Joints The columnar joints here look different with distinctive features depending on where you view them from, so you can appreciate the scenery wherever you are looking from. From every November till the following March, a trekking course called the Hantan River Mulwitgil is available, where you can view the columnar joints from the water level. If you visit Cheorwon in winter, it is recommended that you take a walk along the Mulwitgil.

stories.title: Hantangang Milky Way Bridge
stories.script: Overview of Hantangang Milky Way Bridge Welcome to the Hantangang Milky Way Bridge, Landmark of Cheorwon. The river that flows below you is called the Hantan River. The prefix han of the name has the meaning of big, wide, or clear, but it also means the Milky Way, long-lined group of stars. The name of this bridge originated from the Hantan River.  Construction Background of the Hantangang Milky Way Bridge The Hantan River areas were designated as the UNESCO Global Geopark in July, 2020. As the deep gorges along the river are not easily accessible for tourists to appreciate the fascinating scenery around the Hantan River, Cheorwon County opened the Hantangang Milky Way Bridge in October, 2020 so that the tourists, domestic and overseas as well, can enjoy sightseeing following the natural routes along the columnar joint valleys.  Design Overview of the Hantangang Milky Way Bridge Red-crowned cranes migrate to the Cheorwon Plains after the harvest season to survive the winter every year. Designated as Natural Monument 202 and a first-class endangered species, red-crowned cranes are considered a symbol of luck, longevity, and fidelity and live near the Hantan River during the winter season. Cheorwon provides a lot of food and good habitats for the migratory birds that more and more of them come here every winter. That's why these big birds are a symbol of Cheorwon County and the Hantangang Milky Way Bridge has been constructed with the design of a red-crowned crane.  Characteristics of the Hantangang Milky Way Bridge The Hantangang Milky Way Bridge is 180 meters long, 3 meters wide, and 54 meters high. This single-pylon asymmetric bridge has a maximum capacity of approximately 2,311 people. The 100-meter section of the whole 180-meter-length is equipped with a transparent glass bottom. The suspension bridge gives you a thrilling feeling as it moves slowly from one side to another when crossing it. You can take great photographs through the bridge handrails against the backgrounds of the Hantan River and the columnar joint cliffs. Cheorwon is definitely one of the places where you can take once in a lifetime” picture.

stories.title: Soisan Mountain
stories.script: Overview of Soisan Mountain Soisan Mountain is a 362-meter-high mountain standing in a plain, where you can experience unspoiled nature and view the widespread Cheorwon Plains from the peak. A considerable part has been restricted as the Civilian Control Zone since the cease-fire agreement during the Korean War and so the whole mountain is considered a symbol of peace where you can experience the natural environment kept well in the demilitarized zone, which has been visited by people for decades.   Overview of Cheorwon Plains The Cheorwon Plains, when seen from the top of Soisan Mountain, were formed by the thin lava that rose through the cracks in the crust from 540,000 years ago till 120,000 years ago and spread to cover each and every valley in Cheorwon with lava, forming plateau-shaped areas. The Cheorwon Lava Plateau, covered with fertile basalt weathered soil, has developed into the largest food basket in Gangwon-do Province with the expansion of irrigation facilities. This, in turn, is one of the main reasons that attract a lot of migratory birds to our town during winter.  The Korean War Soisan Mountain is where the sad history between the two Koreas is kept. The so-called Iron Triangle located between Cheorwon and Gimhwa-eup in the south and Pyeonggang County in the north was the scene of heavy fighting resulting in numerous casualties. At the top of Soisan Mountain, you can see places related to the Korean War, such as Kim Il-sung Hill, where highland battles took place, White Horse Hill, which saw its owner changed 24 times in ten days, and Ice Cream Hill, where the hill top was said to look like ice cream when it collapsed with bombings. The mountain is where a laser base for the US military was located until the 1990s and US army barracks and heliports still remain on the mountain. The low-lying Soisan Mountain, which has now been turned into Pyeonghwamaru Park, meaning literally Peace Ridge Park, serve as a place to remind tourists of the significance of peace with such a heartbreaking history.  How to Enjoy Your Visit Better at Soisan Mountain A monorail has been opened on Soisan Mountain since July, 2022 so more and more tourists can enjoy their visits more easily. Soisan Monorail runs a 1.8km round trip from the platform of Cheorwon Station installed inside the Cheorwon History and Culture Park to the top of the Soisan Mountain, where you can have an overall look at the splendid sceneries of the Cheorwon Plains, the DMZ, and the Pyeonggang Plateau in the North.   Cheorwon History and Culture Park, opened in July 2022, is a historical park that replicates the appearance of the city of Cheorwon in its prosperity in the early 1900s before the areas were destroyed during the Korean War. We also recommend the Cheorwon History and Culture Park, where you can experience the old atmosphere and lifestyle of Cheorwon with all your heart.

stories.title: Amidong Tombstone Culture Village
stories.script: Amidong Tombstone Culture Village  A historical space where the living and the dead coexist, along with the joys and sorrows of refugees  When the Korean War broke out in 1950, Busan became the temporary capital and refugees from all over the country flocked here, creating several refugee villages. One of them, Amidong Tombstone Culture Village, was the site of a cemetery and crematorium for Japanese people who lived in Busan during the Japanese colonial period.   After liberation, the Amidong cemetery area became land without an owner, but it was an ideal place for refugees to build houses because unlike other mountainous villages, it was flat land. Moreover, at a time when building materials for houses were scarce, the tombstones and headstones were useful for embankments and steps for stairs. The refugees continued their fierce lives by using the rectangular boundary stones surrounding the cemetery for the walls of their houses and setting up tents, and they built shacks with fish boxes from the Jagalchi Fish Market and packaging material for aid supplies.  In fact, even now, you can see the remains of tombstones and headstones with the names of the deceased Japanese on the stairs and walls around the houses. In addition, the recently opened Refugee Life Museum displays daily items from the 1950s and 1960s with six themes to vividly show the lives of refugees.   Amidong Tombstone Culture Village is a place with a painful history where the “houses of the living” and the “cemetery of the dead” coexist. As an urban space that preserves the residential changes of the Busan area in modern and contemporary history, it is a place with high historical and architectural value. Busan Amidong Tombstone Village Refugee Residence, which was recently listed as Busan Metropolitan City’s first registered cultural property in recognition of its value, is being reborn as a village that is finding hope and happiness through various urban regeneration projects.

stories.title: Train House Artistic Cultural Experience Ground
stories.audioTitle: Train House Artistic Cultural Experience Ground
stories.script: Train House Artistic Cultural Experience Ground  Culture and Art Complex that guards Cheonmasan-ro   This culture and art complex at the entrance of Cheonmasan-ro overlooking the city of Busan is named the Train House Artistic Cultural Experience Ground, and is reminiscent of the time of poverty when people lived in single rooms divided into several sections like train cars.   The abandoned houses were remodeled into a cafe that looks like a small station with stylish decorations where coffee and other drinks and homemade desserts are sold.   The Train House Artistic Cultural Experience Ground operated by “Ami Moms”, a village community company founded by local young mothers, operates a variety of programs with artist studios and cultural experience groups. Residents and tourists alike can experience  activities such as making cookies, bracelets, and soap.  The Train House Artistic Cultural Experience Ground is a place for the people of Armidong to share their lives. It also attracts attention from tourists as a unique healing space where you can experience the warm atmosphere of the hillside village, as well as try delicious drinks, and participate in various art programs.

stories.title: Hanmaeum Happy Center
stories.script: Hanmaeum Happy Center  A beautiful framed view cafe that represents Cheonmasan-ro  The Hanmaeum Happy Center, located on the eastern side of the original downtown of ​​Busan, at the foot of Mt. Cheonmasan, was created by local residents and immigrant women from multicultural families, and it is the representative cafe of Cheonmasan-ro with a wonderful view. Because you can see the original downtown of Busan, the hillside village, and the scenery of Yeongdo’s southern port at a glance, it is called “Scenery (pungyeong) of Chunma,” and is also called “Pung Chun Cafe” for short.  When you enter the cafe, the beautiful scenery of Busan unfolds like a picture framed by the open glass window. You can fully enjoy the fantastic ocean view of Busan Port and the shipyard, which was the center of Busan industry until the present day.  The Hanmaeum Happy Center has been designated as a business that sets the price at an affordable range, so you can drink delicious tea at a low price. It is a good resting place for those visiting Cheonmasan-ro due to the good price and luxurious taste. In addition, it is establishing itself as a popular tourist spot in Cheonmasan-ro where the visits of residents do not stop because people can read various humanities books in the library and purchase products made in local workshops at low prices.

stories.title: Cheonmasan Sky Trail
stories.script: Cheonmasan Sky Trail  A hidden spot to appreciate the past and present of Busan Port  Cheonmasan Sky Trail, a scenic road that runs from Ami-dong to Chojang-dong along Cheonmasan-ro, boasts such an excellent view that it is included in the 10 Views of Busan. It is a scenic spot where you can see the entire original downtown area of Busan as well as Busan Port and Namhang Port at a glance.  In particular, works by the first-generation Korean documentary photographer Choi Min-sik and trick art murals have been installed in various places along the 300-meter-long wooden deck from the Ami Cultural Learning Center to Cheonmasan Eco House, providing a unique sight. In addition, the outdoor gallery exhibits photos and records of the original downtown area of Busan from the 1960s to the 1980s, making it feel as if you have traveled back in time to Busan's past.  On Cheonmasan Sky Trail you can see the present Busan Port spread out like a panorama, and look back on the past through photos as well! If you visit here, you will be able to capture the beauty and history of Seo-gu in Busan, as well as the memories of the past and the beautiful scenery at the same time.

stories.title: Cheonmasan Eco House
stories.script: Cheonmasan Eco House  Eco-friendly housing experience center and romantic night view spot  Cheonmasan Eco House is an eco-friendly housing experience center in the city center operated with eco-friendly facilities. It is divided into four experience halls: Deoki-dong, Songi-dong, Mokryun-dong, and Haesong-dong. You can visit directly or make a reservation by phone.  In particular, the view from Cheonmasan Eco House, where you can see Yeongdo, Namhangdaegyo Bridge, Nampo-dong, Yongdusan Park and Busanhangdaegyo Bridge, is beautiful during the day, but it becomes more charming at night. This is because the sparkling lights of the city embroider the night sea and romanticize the night of Busan.  Cheonmasan Eco House is praised for its cost-effectiveness and high satisfaction level, and the visits of Busan citizens as well as tourists continue without stopping.

stories.title: Cheonmasan-ro Observatory
stories.script: Cheonmasan-ro Observatory (Observatory where Clouds Rest, Cheonmasan Sky Observatory, Nuribaragi Observatory, Busan Port Photo Observatory)  The pride of Cheonmasan-ro, observation decks with a night view that shines like jewels   Cheonmasan-ro, which boasts the best hillside view, was selected as one of the 10 most scenic spots in Busan and has four observatories that capture the eye with various characteristics.  The first one is the Observatory where Clouds Rest, which is in the Tombstone Culture Village. It is a place where you can have a good time with children, as cloud sculptures and humorous characters are hung to represent the clouds resting. When you sit on the bench with an open view, you can see the lives of Busan citizens from the farthest Busan Harbor Bridge to the original downtown around Yongdusan, as well as apartments and villages built on mountain slopes.  The Cheonmasan Sky Observatory  in the middle of Cheonmasan-ro was built by using abandoned houses. When you go up to the rooftop of the observatory, you can see a full view of Yeongdo in front of you. In fact, this observatory offers a unique sight, as there is a sculpture modeled after the elderly couple looking at the city of Busan in the ending scene of the movie Ode to My Father, which had 14 million viewers. In particular, it is popular as a beautiful photo zone where you can take wonderful photos while looking at the night view of Yongdusan Park Busan Tower and Yeongdodaegyo Bridge, which transform splendidly at night.  The third observatory on Cheonmasan-ro is the Nuribaragi Observatory. “Nuri” is a Korean word that means “world,” so the name of the observatory has the meaning of looking at the mountains, sea and sky of Busan. As its name suggests, it is a place where you can enjoy a panoramic view of the city, and it was selected as a “Small but Certain Happiness, Top 1% Busan Travel Destination for Me” by the Busan Tourism Organization. In the center of the observatory there is a sculpture called “Sori Tree,” which looks like a tree with a cloud hanging on it. Dozens of bells are hung on this tree, so when the wind blows, the pure sound of nature soothes the weary spirits of visitors.  The fourth observatory on Cheonmasan-ro is the Busan Port Photo Observatory, which boasts a panoramic view that will even open your heart. When the weather is good, you can see Daemado across the sea in the distance, and it is a photo spot where you can capture the colorful and dynamic scenery of Busan. When you stand here, you can see the four representative bridges of the city surrounding Yeongdo at a glance. You can see Yeongdo Bridge and Busan Bridge on the left side of Yeongdo, and Busan Harbor Bridge with a towering bridge tower behind it, and even Namhang Bridge that connects Yeongdo and Songdo. Recently, it is known as a driving course with a beautiful night view, so it is visited by many tourists.

stories.title: Flower Village
stories.script: Flower Village  A village where flowers bloom transformed into an art village where art blooms  Located on a mountain pass that connects Mt. Gudeok and Mt. Eomgwang, this was a place where refugees lived and formed a village during the Korean War. At that time, refugees cut wild flowers growing at the foot of the mountain and sold them and made their living by cultivating flowers such as chrysanthemums and carnations. It’s been called the Flower Village since that time.   In the 1970s, there were large flower complexes that suited the reputation of the Flower Village. Most of the residents who grew flowers have disappeared, but hikers continue to visit Mt. Gudeok and Mt. Eomgwang. It has become popular for restaurants selling dried radish leaf haejangguk to hikers to soothe their hungry stomachs after hiking.  In particular, through the recent urban regeneration project called Flower Village Provence, buildings and signboards throughout the Flower Village are being transformed into bright pink pastel tones. When you walk around the village, you will see colorful murals painted on the walls in the alleys.  The Flower Village has various cultural facilities and experience spaces such as Gudeok Culture Park and Traditional Culture Experience Center, providing cultural attractions to villagers and visitors

stories.title: Gudeok Culture Park
stories.script: Gudeok Culture Park  A natural eco-cultural space where you can experience nature and culture together  In the beautiful Gudeok Mountain Forest, Gudeok Cultural Park has both nature where you can take a walk and rest and experience cultural sites. It is a natural ecological and cultural space with about 20,000 plants of about 100 species throughout the park.  The forest full of cool, tall cypress trees provides a good walking trail to meditate, allowing visitors to fully enjoy the atmosphere of nature. If you enter the Mokseok Gardening Hall, which is filled with well-managed greenhouse plants like a rainforest, you can see unusually shaped stones and various plants that you would not commonly see. In addition, in the Education History Museum you encounter on the walking path, you can see books that were used at Seodang in the Joseon Dynasty and Japanese textbooks made during the Japanese colonial period. As you enter the classroom that reproduces the 1970s and 1980s, it will be reminiscent of your old school days.  In the Folklore Hall, you can see various folk items such as traditional musical instruments, toys, hanbok, and tableware.  In addition, the Seo-gu Forest Playground, the first multicultural space for children in Seo-gu, Busan, which children and parents can use together safely, has been in pilot operation since the end of July in the multipurpose hall of Gudeok Cultural Park. The Seo-gu Forest Playground is a healing cultural space in the city equipped with an immersive content experience center and a new concept children’s library, and it is scheduled to officially open in early September.

stories.title: Traditional Culture Experience Cente
stories.script: Traditional Culture Experience Center  Learning about our culture and filling our hearts.  Located at the foot of beautiful Mt. Gudeoksan, the Busan Traditional Culture Experience Center is a place where you can learn the etiquette and culture necessary for living in the world and cultivate the right character and morality through various traditional cultural experiences of our ancestors. Opened in April 2017, this three-story building has a food experience room and office on the first floor, a tea ceremony etiquette room, life etiquette room and exhibition room on the second floor, and a multipurpose event space, a traditional tea room and Haneul Park on the third floor.  Various education and experiential activities are free of charge with reservations, but in some cases, there may be separate material costs. The programs run as regular quarterly classes and include temple food class, tea ceremony class and gayageum class and one-day experience activities such as traditional games, hanbok experience, traditional food making, and filial piety and etiquette activities. In addition, many people participate in family programs every Saturday, such as making traditional rice cakes, making crafts such as hanbok keyrings, experiencing hanbok and playing traditional Korean music.  Through various programs such as attending traditional etiquette classes with beloved children and grandchildren, learning pansori or taekgyeon with close friends, and enjoying healthy food by making temple food with respected parents, visitors can create special memories that will be remembered for a long time.

stories.title: Naewonjeongsa Temple Stay
stories.script: Naewonjeongsa Temple Stay  A trip to meet the true “me” at a temple in the city  If you go to Naewonjeongsa Temple at the foot of Mt. Gudeoksan, which is close to the city, you can experience a temple stay program where you can examine your inner self that you haven’t seen before. Temple Stay is a cultural experience program where you can experience the daily life of a monk at a mountain temple where the history and culture of Korean Buddhism are still active. It is a time for modern people who need a rest in their lives to get away from their busy daily life and empty their body, mind and thoughts to face their real self. Naewonjeongsa Temple Stay Hall is a cultural space where you can experience various cultures of Korea along with nature. It is a healing culture center that informs Korean and foreign visitors of traditional Korean culture and connects them. In particular, people who are looking for a place to rest their minds continue to visit because they can feel the life of the forest here and participate in forest therapy by breathing and listening to the sounds of water, wind, and birds.  Your mind that is fatigued by daily life can be relieved a little by participating in the main programs of Temple Stay such as tea time, where you chat with a monk while drinking warm, comforting tea, balwoo gongyang, where you can experience a meal with the wisdom of a monk, Zen meditation, which is a quiet meditation session that calms the five senses that are over-excited in the city, prayer time for peace and enlightenment at the beginning and end of the day, and 108 bows that fill up the heart and teach you humility by lowering your body. Staying at the temple, experiencing Korean Buddhist culture, and recovering the body and mind, is attracting attention as a healing trip.

stories.title: Gudeok Stadium
stories.script: Announcement: A trip on the old streetcar rail in Seo-gu, Busan. This stop is Gudeok Stadium.  Student: 	 Grandma! It just looks like a stadium, were there really streetcars here?  Grandma:  Of course! You can’t see it now, 	but when I was young, there were streetcars here.  Student: 	 Since when?  Grandma:  They say that the first streetcar in Busan ran in 1915. Then, in 1928, the last stop of the streetcar was extended to Gudeok Stadium.  Student:	 Did you take the streetcar often, grandma?  Grandma:	 Of course. I took it many times to go to school. The streetcars disappeared in Busan in 1968....  Student: 	 I can’t really imagine it now, but that means there were streetcar rails in old Busan for more than 50 years.   Grandma:	 That’s right. This was the last stop of the streetcar. There should be a monument for the last streetcar stop over there....  Student:	 Found it! It’s really here. It says “Stone Monument for the Last Stop of the Streetcar in Daesin-dong.” I feel like I can hear the sound of a streetcar. Grandma, what did Gudeok Station look like back then?  Grandma:	 It was very big. It was called Busan Public Stadium at the time. Before Sajik Stadium was built in 1985, this was the 	only public sports complex in Busan....	It was amazing because it had a track and field, a baseball field, an indoor gym and a swimming pool.  You know Busan’s famous baseball player Choi Dong-won, right? The place where Choi played in his high school days was Gudeok Baseball Stadium.   Student: 	 That’s right! I heard that Choi Dong-won is the legend of Gudeok Baseball Stadium. That’s why there is a statue of Choi and a glove and a baseball in front of the stadium. 		 And it says the words “Choi Dong-won, the great pitcher who made Seo-gu shine!”Grandma! Let’s go to the next streetcar rail spot….   Grandma: Sure, let’s do that!

stories.title: Busan Streetcar
stories.script: The last streetcar of Busan that disappeared into history  Announcement: 	A trip on the old streetcar rail in Seo-gu, Busan. This stop is Dong-A University Bumin Campus.  Student:	Grandma! There’s the last streetcar that ran across old Busan….  Grandma: Ah, I thought all of it had disappeared…It’s really here.   Student:	Is it the same as the streetcar you used to ride?  Grandma: It looks cleaner than the streetcar in my memory.   Student:	That’s true. It looks like it can even start running right now. If the last stop of the streetcar was Gudeok Stadium, where did it start from?   Grandma: Do you know where Oncheonjang is? It ran from there and went through Dongnae, Seomyeon, Beomil-dong, Choryang and Busan Station and passed through the City Hall and Nampo-dong to Gudeok Station. There was also a line that went from Busan City Hall to Yeongdo.  Student: 	I heard that on October 31, 1915, the Busan Station and Oncheonjang section were opened, and the era of the Busan streetcars began, and about 50 streetcars were running in the city. It operated well for 53 years. So, why did it disappear?  Grandma:	It was because of the buses.  Student:	Since buses are fast, many people took the bus instead of the slow streetcars,		and as the financial loss accumulated, the Busan streetcars disappeared into history....   Grandma:	That’s right. The number of cars also increased and people preferred fast things....So streetcars that ran slowly along the rails were gradually neglected. But it’s very nice to reminisce about the old days like this by looking at this streetcar.

stories.title: Provisional Capital Memorial Hall
stories.script: Provisional Capital Memorial Hall  From the capital of refugees of the Korean War to modern Busan  Announcement: A trip on the old streetcar rail in Seo-gu, Busan.  This stop is the Provisional Capital Memorial Hall.  Student: Grandma, this is the Provisional Capital Memorial Hall where former President Syngman Rhee lived when Busan was the provisional capital of Korea during the Korean War.  Grandma: That was when I was a baby, so I don’t remember it at all. But I heard about it from my mother growing up.  In August of 1950, the summer I was born, Busan was the provisional capital.   Student:	That’s right. I heard that this was the presidential residence until the armistice agreement was signed on July 27, 1953. So, President Syngman Rhee lived and worked here, and now it is being used as a memorial hall.		 This building was built in August 1926 to serve as the residence of the governor of Gyeongsangnam-do, so it has a mix of Japanese and Western architectural styles. The reception room is Western style, while the residential space is Japanese style.   Grandma:	It must have historical value.  Student: Yes, its historical value was recognized as a modern architecture building and was designated as National Cultural Heritage Site No. 546 in 2018. The garden here is also quiet and beautiful, so you can take great pictures. Let's take pictures later after we look around the exhibition hall.  	 Grandma:	Are we able to go inside the building?   Student: Of course, since it’s a memorial hall. It is divided into the presidential residence and exhibition hall, and the rooms where President Rhee and his wife resided, worked and received major state guests, such as the reception room, study, inner room, and office, were reproduced in the presidential residence. The exhibition hall, which was built as the office of the prosecutor of the former Busan High Public Prosecutor's Office, is organized into two themes: war and life, and 1,000 days of the provisional capital of Busan. First, in the War and Life Exhibition Hall, objects used in the war and models such as a shack and refugee school are displayed. In the 1,000 Days of the Provisional Capital of Busan Exhibition Hall, various relics focusing on major political events and administrative and economic changes in Busan at that time are exhibited, so you can take a careful look at the role of the city as the provisional capital.   Grandma:	Then let’s hurry and go inside.   Student: Yes, let’s look at the retro goods collection and time travel to modern Busan!

stories.title: Seokdang Museum of Dong-A University
stories.script: Seokdang Museum of Dong-A University  A museum that preserves the political and social changes of modern and contemporary history   Announcement: A trip on the old streetcar rail in Seo-gu, Busan. This stop is Seokdang Museum of Dong-A University.  Grandma:	I heard that this was where the Busan Provisional Capital Government Building used to be, but it has become a museum!  Student: 	Yes, this building was completed in 1925 as the Gyeongsangnam-do provincial government building during the Japanese colonial period. So, it is a historic modern cultural heritage that combines Western classicism and Japanese wooden style. During the Korean War, it was used as a government building for the provisional capital Busan, and after that, it was the Gyeongnam Provincial Office and the Busan District Prosecutors' Office. Since 2009, it has been used as the Seokdang Museum of Dong-A University.   Grandma:	This building has so many stories!    Student:	It’s a historical building that preserves the political and social changes of our country’s modern history. So it’s designated as National Registered Cultural Property No. 41.  Grandma:	Are there many cultural assets inside?   Student: 	There are more than 25,000 artifacts, including two national treasures and 131 pieces of 17 treasures. From the Paleolithic era to modern times, there are many archaeological relics and folklore-related items collected from Busan, Gyeongnam, and Jeju-do, and there are also many Joseon Dynasty art history materials collected from all over the country.   Grandma:	I see there is also pottery here!   Student:	Yes, isn’t it elegant? Not only celadon from the Goryeo Dynasty and white porcelain from the Joseon Dynasty, but also Buddhist sculptures and crafts from the Unified Silla period to the Joseon Dynasty are on display. If you go to the calligraphy room over there, you can see paintings and calligraphy works of the Joseon Dynasty as well. In the exhibition room on the third floor, the history of the Busan Provisional Capital Government Building is displayed as a model. Should we go see it together?   Grandma:	Let’s do that. It’s so nice to see the cultural assets of Busan at a glance.

stories.title: Songdo Beach
stories.script: Songdo Beach  Korea's first public beach  Teacher: 	 Welcome to the Songdo Beach Trip!   Student:	 Wow, it’s the ocean! Why is this place called Songdo?   Teacher:	 This place was named Songdo because it has had many pine forests since old times, and it was the first public beach in Korea that opened in 1913. It was the No. 1 tourist spot in Busan and was called the Naples of the East. It was a great beach that was selected as the best tourist destination in the country from the 1960s to the 1970s because of its clean white sandy beach and clear water.  Student:	 I heard this from my grandma. She said she came to Songdo Beach for her honeymoon, hehe.  Teacher: 	 At that time, there were many things to enjoy, including the cable car, and the surrounding scenery of nature was also very good, so many tourists came to visit. It is a place that holds the memories and romance of lovers and newlyweds of that time.  Student:	 There are not that many people here now compared to Haeundae or Gwangalli Beach.   Teacher:	 As development accelerated in the 1980s, a lot of sand was lost, and the cable car and surrounding facilities were damaged by Tropical Storm Selma in 1987 and Typhoon Maemi in 2003, so the number of visitors to the beach significantly decreased.  However, with the restoration of old Songdo landmarks such as the Busan Air Cruise, marine diving platform, and Yonggung Suspension Bridge, tourists are coming back again. Now, shall we go together to see the famous Busan superstar Songdo Beach?

stories.title: Busan Air Cruise
stories.script: Busan Air Cruise  The thrill of crossing 1.62 km over the ocean  Teacher: 	The Busan Air Cruise you will be boarding opened in June 2017 by restoring the old cable cars of Songdo that were discontinued in 1988.  Student:	It was restored after almost 30 years.  It’s really high and quite thrilling.  Teacher: 	It goes up to 86 m high. It runs 1.62 km from Songnim Park on the east side of Songdo Beach to Amnam Park on the west side, so you can feel the thrill as you go across the ocean. You can take in the beautiful scenery of Songdo Beach, Busan Yeongdo and Namhang Bridge, Songdo Coast Walk, and the waves crashing against unique rocks and cliffs.  Student:	The floor of the cable car over there looks clear It looks a little scary.  Teacher:	It’s the crystal cabin with a transparent floor. It is a little more expensive than a regular cabin with a closed floor, but you can experience the fantastic feeling of standing on the mysterious boundary between the sea and the sky. All cabins of Busan Air Cruise are made of glass, so you can enjoy a panoramic view of the open blue sea.   Student:	I think it will relieve stress and make me feel like I’m flying over the sea. I’m excited to see how magnificent the view from the cable car will be.  Teacher:	You can have a superb view of the sky and the sea that change every hour. It is also a good place to take in the unique night view of Songdo while watching the tranquil sunset and the night sea colored with glamorous lights. Let's check out what Songdo Beach looks like from the sky in the cable car….

stories.title: Songdo Cloud Trail (Geobukseom Island)
stories.script: Songdo Cloud Trail in Seo-gu, Busan is a 365-meter long seatrail. It’s installed at a height of 5.5 to 9 meters above the sea near Geobukseom Island on the east side of Songdo Beach. Unlike most of the other sea trails, it is impressively curved. It’s because the bridge was designed in the flowing shape of a dragon navigating through the sea. It’s based on a Geobukseom Island’s legend of a young fisherman and the dragon king’s daughter.  Once upon a time, a young fisherman lived in Songdo with his single mother. One day, he fell in love with Princess Inryoung, the daughter of the dragon king. Inryoung, who was also a dragon, wanted to marry the fisherman. She decided to pray for a thousand days in the dragon cave to become a human. However, on the last day of her prayer, Inryoung was attacked by a sea monster. The fisherman bravely fought with the monster. After a deadly fight, he did save the princess and defeated the sea monster, but he lost his own life and became a spirit of the sea. Princess Inryoung didn’t become a human, either. Instead, she turned into a half-human half-dragon. The dragon king, who took pity on this, turned the fisherman into Geobuksom Island, so he could be with Princess Inryoung forever. It’s said that the island gives longevity and wealth to those who visit. If a man and a woman who are in love with each other visit, the island blesses their love.  Visiting the trail is a fulfilling experience in multiple ways. Part of the floor of the skywalk is made of tempered glass. It’s a thrilling experience to see the waves through the glass. You may even feel like you are walking on the ocean. The trail is open from 6 am to 11 pm every day. In the daytime, if you look up to the sky, you can see the colorful Busan Air Cruise cable cars. You can also enjoy the beautiful view of Songdo Beach as you walk along the trail. At night, the suspension bridge reflected in the night sea and the lights around Songdo Beach create a romantic scene.

stories.title: Songdo Marine Diving Platform
stories.script: Songdo Marine Diving Platform  A unique summer leisure sport to enjoy the dynamism of the sea  Student:	 Teacher! What’s that over the ocean?   Teacher:	 It’s the Songdo Marine Diving Platform that was lost in a typhoon, but was restored in 2013.   Student:	 The shape looks quite unique. It looks a bit like a turtle.    Teacher:  With the motif of Geobukseom Island near Songdo Beach, it’s shaped like a mother turtle and her baby.  The high diving board area in the front is the mother turtle, where you can dive from a height of 5 m. And the baby turtle diving board in the back is 3 m high.    Student:	 I think many people would use it. Can people dive at any time?  Teacher:	 It’s popular because it’s a unique summer leisure sport that can only be used when Songdo Beach is open. In fact, many tourists who want to feel the dynamic movement of the sea and test their hidden courage come visit. When you dive, you must follow the guide and instructions of the safety personnel to prevent accidents.

stories.title: Hyeon In Plaza
stories.script: Hyeon In Plaza  Fall in love with the songs and memories of the national singer Hyeon In  Student:	 I hear music from somewhere…A snowstorm blowing …♫   Teacher: 	 It’s “Be Strong, Geum-soon” by Hyeon In!  It’s because this is the Hyeon In Plaza, which was established to commemorate the national singer Hyeon In, who is from Busan.  Student:	 He must have been a very famous singer if there is a plaza named after him. not know Hyeon In.  Born in Yeongdo, Busan in 1919, Hyeon In is a first-generation popular singer and representative singer of Korea in the 1950s. He released more than 160 popular songs, including his debut <The Moonlight Night in Shilla>, <Rainy Gomoryeong>, and <Be Strong, Geum-soon>.  Hyeon In's songs reflect the ups and downs of our modern history and has been loved by many as it soothes the hearts of the people who had to live through hard times from the Japanese colonial period to the Korean War.  Teacher:	 Hyeon In spent a lot of time at Songdo Beach in his childhood and dreamed of becoming a singer. When he grew older, he visited from time to time to rest and worked on his songs.   Since the death of Hyeon In in 2002, the Songdo Festival has been held at Songdo Beach every summer since 2005 to commemorate the singer and discover talented new singers.  Hyeon In Plaza was built in August 2007 by the Seo-gu Office to reflect the wishes of Busan citizens for the Hyeon In Song Festival to develop into a global music festival beyond a domestic one.    Student: 	 I hope the next national singer that follows Hyeon In will be discovered at the Hyeon In Song Festival that represents Busan.

stories.title: Songdo Ocean Park
stories.script: Songdo Ocean Park  A marine resort complex where you can enjoy the four seasons of Songdo Beach  Teacher:	 Songdo Ocean Park, on the west side of Songdo Beach, was completed in 2017 by reclaiming 19022.5 square meters of shared water surface.    Student:	 This huge plaza used to be the ocean?  Teacher:	 That’s right. So it took a very long time to complete. This huge plaza is divided into three themes with a festival plaza, youth plaza, and healing plaza. There is a wide coast walkway around the plaza, and it is loved by residents as a place where you can take a walk with your family, lovers, and pets.   Student: 	 Are festivals held in the festival plaza?   Teacher:	Right. As the name suggests, it is used for various festivals and events, or as a waterfront in normal times. And in the Youth Plaza, you can play various sports such as badminton and inline skating.  The Healing Plaza, recently opened to the public, has decks and benches where families and couples can relax, making it a perfect place for tourists who want to unwind and enjoy the sea.   Student:	 Songdo Ocean Park must have a great night view.     Teahcher:	 You’re right…When the moon and rabbit sculptures installed in the plaza light up at sunset, you can take beautiful pictures there. You can feel the cool ocean breeze and listen to the sound of waves as a bonus.  Student:	 It’s a space for healing in the city.  If you prefer to enjoy the ocean quietly, rather than at a crowded beach, then taking a break at Songdo Ocean Park might be a good idea.

stories.title: Songdo Yonggung Suspension Bridge
stories.script: Songdo Yonggung Suspension Bridge  Feel the thrill of walking on the sea while admiring the natural scenery  Teacher:	 Songdo Yonggung Suspension Bridge is 127 m long and 2 m wide and connects Amnam Park and the upper part of Dongseom Island, a small uninhabited island across the sea. It is a restoration of the old Songdo Cloud Bridge, a popular Songdo landmark.  Student:	 What happened to the old Songdo Cloud Bridge?  Teacher:	 The old Songdo Cloud Bridge, also known as the Suspension Bridge, was a 150 m long and 1.8 m wide bridge that connected Songrim Park and Geobukseom Island.   It was installed in 1965 and was popular in Songdo Beach along with the cable cars. But it was demolished in 2002 when it was damaged by Tropical Storm Selma.   Then, the Songdo Yonggung Suspension Bridge was restored in Amnam Park and opened in June 2020 as part of a project for the restoration ’of four major landmarks in Songdo.   It is rapidly emerging as a representative tourist destination in Busan.  Student:	 It is 25 m above the sea, so you can feel the thrill of walking on the sea. The view of the sea that refreshingly stretches along the horizon and the scenery created by the uniquely shaped cliffs are very impressive.  Teacher:	 So it is rapidly emerging as a representative tourist destination in Busan. Like me, citizens of Seo-gu, Busan, have free admission, but there is a separate admission fee (KRW 1,000), except for children under the age of 7, the disabled, and people of national merit. If you cross the Yonggung Suspension Bridge and arrive at Dongseom Island and enjoy the 360-degree view of beautiful Songdo beach in Busan, you will feel that the admission fee was not wasted.  Student:	 I’m curious why it’s called Yonggung Suspension Bridge… Is it because we’re walking on the ocean?  Teacher:  This is because, in the legend of Geobukseom Island, this was the middle point to meet to enter the Dragon Palace, which was the wedding venue for the fisherman and Inryong, the dragon king’s daughter. It’s a bridge that connects the people to the dragon king.  So, there is a saying that people who cross this bridge and go to meet the dragon king will be blessed with either good fortune, success in life, or good health, and that love will come true for young men and women.   Student:	 Really? Dragon king… I will come visit often, so please give me good fortune, success in life, and good health!

stories.title: Daeshin Park
stories.script: Daeshin Park  A healing space in the city where you can breathe in the heart of nature  Daeshin Park in Seo-gu, Busan, is a natural park in the city where you can soak in the forest as you walk along a trail among the tall cypress trees.  Entry to Daeshin Park, which started as forests formed by the creation of two water sources in the valleys of Mt. Gudeoksan and Mt. Eomgwangsan, was prohibited to the public for a long time to protect the water sources. Thanks to this, it became a dense forest with trees over 70 years old including cedar, cypress and cherry trees. After the Nakdong River became Busan's water supply source in 1968, Daeshin Park was opened to the public as a neighborhood park. In 1986, it was integrated with Daecheong Park and called Jungang Park, but Busan citizens still call it Daeshin Park.  Daeshin Park's cypress forest, which won the Beautiful Forest Nuri Award at the 18th National Beautiful Forest Contest Awards Ceremony, has well-made trails for walking. If you walk along the trail with the sound of leaves rustling in the wind and bird songs, you will come across a water source from the valley and a mineral spring with tasty water. Also, there is a monument with the verses of poets engraved on it, so you can have a time of contemplation.  On one side of the park is the Gudeok Folk Art Museum, which was established for the purpose of handing down and distributing intangible cultural assets and inheriting good customs. It is the hall of traditional culture in the Seobusan region, and the Gudeokgol Traditional Folk Art Festival is held here to provide a venue to continue the original form of traditional Korean games.

stories.title: Busan Cooperative Fish Market
stories.script: The largest seafood wholesale market in Korea that greets the dawn in Busan  As soon as the auctioneer's bell rings, dozens of wholesalers quickly rush to the wooden crates full of fish. The Busan Cooperative Fish Market is filled with the passionate shouts of the auctioneers who are bargaining, the busy gestures of wholesalers, and the excitement of auctions. It’s a vibrant scene that greets the dawn of Busan.   The Busan Cooperative Fish Market is Korea's first modern fish market, established in 1963 to control prices with the quick and hygienic treatment of catches, to promote the welfare of fisherman and to improve people's diets. At that time, it was located on the site of the current International Passenger Wharf Terminal with the name Busan General Fish Market, and was renamed the Busan Cooperative Fish Market based on the amendment of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act in 1971, and was moved to the current location in Nambumin-dong in 1973.]  The Busan Cooperative Fish Market is a mecca for the distribution of coastal seafood, and is the largest wholesale seafood market in Korea, selling about 30% of the seafood caught in the coastal waters of Korea. About 100 kinds of fish are handled here. Among them, mackerel is a popular fish that accounts for 70-80% of the sales volume of the market and 90% of the nationwide distribution. Thanks to this, there are many restaurants that serve mackerel near the Busan Cooperative Fish Market.  In addition, the Seo-gu District Office of Busan selected mackerel as the symbol of Seo-gu in 2007 and has held the Busan Mackerel Festival since 2008 to revitalize the local economy, and it has established itself as a famous and popular festival of Busan.

stories.title: Amnam Park
stories.script: Amnam Park  A pristine natural park with mysteries from 100 million years ago   This is Amnam Park, where the ocean that can be seen through the pine forest and the uniquely shaped cliffs carved by the waves harmonize to create a picture-perfect view. It is located by the coast and at the foot of a mountain toward the sea at the southern end of Mt. Jinjeongsan on the Songdo Peninsula. It was designated as a park in December 1972, but was closed to the public because it was part of a military reserve. For this reason, nature is well preserved compared to other places, and when it was fully opened to the public in 1997, it was surrounded by dense forest.  Amnam Park is a pristine natural park where marine plants grow wild and where there are areas of natural ecology that are hard to see in the city, such as 370 species of plants and trees including black pine, alder tree, and platycarya trees growing on top of sedimentary rock formed about 100 million years ago, as well as 100 species of wild flowers such as corydalis and false-starwort. In addition, there are distinctive cliffs made by the waves along the coast with the bands of each stratum clearly visible that harmonize with the ocean in an impressive way. Dinosaur footprints and Neolithic traces remain throughout the park's shoreline.  In the park, there is a walking path that anyone can easily take with convenient facilities such as an overpass and a plaza. It also has high-quality sculptures by world-class artists who exhibited at the 2002 Busan Biennale in various locations. Recently, the four-course healing forest path in Amnam Park has been redeveloped and is loved as a healing and resting park for the whole family.

stories.title: Father Lee Tae-seok Memorial Hall (birthplace)
stories.script: Father Lee Tae-seok Memorial Hall (birthplace)  Commemorating the Schweitzer of Sudan, who practiced sharing and love throughout his life.  In January 2010, the death of a priest who passed away at the young age of 48 brought sorrow to many people in the distant land of Tonj in Sudan, Africa. This is because the priest shared his love with the people of Tonj by volunteering there for 10 years before his death.  This story is about Father Lee Tae-seok, who is the main character of the documentary film Don't Cry For Me Sudan, and who was called the Schweitzer of Sudan. Born in Nambumin-dong, Seo-gu, Busan in September 1962, Father Lee became a doctor and was discharged as a military doctor in 1991. Then he suddenly left the guaranteed path of a doctor and joined the Salesians of Don Bosco Order to live the life of a priest.  As soon as he was ordained a priest in 2001, he moved to Tonj, South Sudan, Africa, established a school, formed a band, and actively volunteered in all fields including missions, medical care, education, and culture. He gave dreams and hopes to the children in the poor village of Tonj.  However, he was diagnosed with stage 4 colorectal cancer in 2008, and while he was fighting the disease without losing his will to live, he died of colorectal cancer in January 2010 at the age of 48.  Father Lee Tae-seok Memorial Hall and birthplace were built to commemorate his noble life as a priest, doctor, and musician who lived a life of love and service and practiced the true spirit of sharing. The birthplace of Father Lee and Tonj Culture Park are on the first basement floor, a cafeteria and offices are on the first and second floors, an exhibition hall and multipurpose room with stories and mementos of Father Lee are on the third and fourth floors, and there is an outdoor terrace and observation deck on the fifth floor.  Father Lee Tae-seok Memorial Hall and his birthplace, which many people still visit, is where you can hear the story of Father Lee, who showed through his life that true happiness exists through sharing.

stories.title: HiKR Ground
stories.script: Walking along the Cheonggyecheon Stream, where freshwater flows all year round and all sorts of cultural and arts performance are available, one will easily come across a noticeable building with a beautiful facade. That is HiKR Ground, a Korean tourism promotion center launched by the Korea Tourism Organization Seoul Center. This tourism center made for hands-on experience by renovating the existing promotion center features popular Korean tourism content associated with smart technology, Korean culture, art, and more, offering a different perspective for enjoying content. Collaborations with various private companies, such as Netflix Korea and SM Entertainment, are also attracting the attention of younger generations. Visitors can create short videos for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok, and experience augmented reality and virtual reality that makes Korean celebrities appear as if they are standing right in front.  HiKR Ground takes its name by combining “Hi” and “Korea” (KR), greeting international tourists visiting Korea, and “Ground” as a playground for young generations to interact and enjoy K-pop and content together.  Once you enter HiKR Ground, you will first notice a large media wall called the HiKR Wall that screens media artwork with visual content that feature Korean tourism, such as tourist attractions with magnificent landscapes, K-pop and K-drama. Screened on the media wall are Millennial Parade, which features hanbok as haute couture, and New Cityscape by media artist Lee Yi-nam to commemorate the launching of HiKR Ground.  Lee Yi-nam is a leading new media artist of Korea who gives life to traditional cultural heritage by converging digital technology. New Citiscape features beautiful sceneries of five main tourism cities, including Mokpo, Busan, Jeonju, Andong, and Gangneung, and proposes the future image of cities. The image of the marine cable car that starts from Yudalsan Mountain in Mokpo and all the way to Busan fills the large media wall, proving the potential of Korean art.

stories.title: K-pop Ground
stories.script: Beautiful beach with undulating waves, fairy tale-like scenery with floating candies and cookies, spaceship of the future... These are some images visitors of K-pop Ground can select along with music and lighting to make their own magnificent work.  K-pop Ground features spaces designed like settings that often appear in K-pop music videos, such as the subway, laundry, spaceship, and color rooms. Visitors can choose lightings and music the way they want to create their own music video or take pictures to post on social media. My Stage, the only extended reality studio of the nation, allows visitors to enjoy over 100 virtual backgrounds created with extended reality to create their very own music video. Three cameras are installed in different angles for visitors to use. A lot of props are also available, so visitors just need to bring a USB flash drive to store their outcome.  At K-pop Ground, visitors can learn K-pop dances from the 1990s to the 2020s. This is available at K-pop Dance Evolution, a game-like dance corner. Visitors can pick a song they like and follow the choreography of the displayed dancer to score points.  Anyone can become a K-pop music video star at K-pop Ground. This playground is filled with excitement beyond your imagination.

stories.title: HiKR Art Museum
stories.script: HiKR Art Museum is a space where visitors can appreciate and experience Korean art through special exhibitions that feature Korea’s main tourism content reinterpreted by leading artists of Korea. Gwon Osang's exhibition Homo Ludens is currently ongoing to celebrate the opening of the museum. Gwon, a pioneer of the photo piece genre, is showcasing his Deodorant Type series that cut and paste pieces of photographs. This work is well-known to have used pictures of Korean celebrities, including G-Dragon and Yoo Ah-in.  At HiKR Art Museum, three busts of actor Yoo Ah-in is displayed as part of the Deodorant Type series. Gwon has mentioned that he took 300 to 400 photographs of Yoo’s face from different angles to create this piece. Another piece called Festival portrays five regional festivals of Korea from the artist’s perspective. The work was inspired by Jinju Namgang Yudeung Festival, Gimje Horizon Festival, Hwacheon Sancheoneo Ice Festival, Andong Mask Dance Festival, and Boryeong Mud Festival.  Dramatic Trip displayed on the same floor visualizes Korean cultural content that have received significant attention recently. Visitors can try to look for tourist attractions that appear in the video. K-drama series include Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha and Secret Royal Inspector & Joy. With a pair of wearable glasses, visitors will feel as if they are on set through AR and VR technologies. As for Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha, actor Lee Sang-yi personally introduces a shooting episode at Guryongpo, a shooting location of the series. The actor will appear as if speaking right before visitors by the beautiful blue ocean of Guryongpo.  Northwall by the famous artist Seo Do-ho hangs by the stairway to the third floor. This is a series piece of Fabric Architecture that replicated the studio and old and current houses of the artist with a translucent cloth. This piece connected doors, windows, roof tiles, and bricks as if a quilt to show the beauty of hanok architecture. HiKR Tower, a vertical media tower that connects the third and fourth floor, features various Korean tourism content.  HiKR Art Museum, a venue to appreciate Korean art of various genres. This K-culture spot can be enjoyed by everyone, regardless of age.

stories.title: HiKR Cave & Festival Experience Center
stories.script: HiKR Cave for experiencing Korean tourism located at the fourth floor of HiKR Ground enables visitors to learn tourism information of various themes, such as tourism hubs, local festivals, and wellness, through videos, music, lighting, and scent. Suncheonman Bay with large fields of reeds are currently exhibited to celebrate the opening of HiKR Cave. Different scents that remind Suncheonman Bay are mildly diffused in the area, and noises of birds and reeds shaking in the wind are also played through the speaker. Sitting surrounded by reeds makes one feel as if they have teleported to Suncheonman Bay.  The Festival Experience Center is decorated with different themes of interactive exhibitions quarterly. The current exhibition is about Jinju Namgang Yudeung Festival. Visitors can color a card with a drawing of a lantern and scan it to make it appear on the main screen of the festival. It is a virtual experience, but visitors will feel the excitement.  An information center for medical tourism is also available at the fourth floor. Medical Wellness Zone is where visitors can check their skin condition and stress level. They will be offered with tea most suitable for their condition. Visitors can have fun and stay healthy at HiKR Ground!

stories.title: Gwanghwamun Square
stories.script: Even after Gwanghwamun was left in ruins during the Imjin War, the main thoroughfare in front continued to serve as the main artery of Hanyang (now Seoul), the capital of Joseon (now the Republic of Korea), where various government offices were headquartered, including Samgunbu, Yejo, Saheonbu, Uijeongbu, Jungchubu, Byeongjo, and Hyeongjo.  Gwanghwamun was constructed in 1395, right after the establishment of the Joseon dynasty, serving as the main gate of Gyeongbokgung Palace, the royal palace of the dynasty. Sajeongmun was the original name of the gate, but was renamed as Gwanghwamun in 1425 (7th year of King Sejong's reign), conveying a message that the king shines the nation with his great virtue. As the gate which the king passed through, Gwanghwamun had a painting of jujak, a mythical creature of Joseon, on the ceiling, and statues of haetae, also a mythical creature, on both sides in front of the gate.  Gwanghwamun that held great historical significance was unfortunately burnt down during the Imjin war, left in ruins for over 270 years, until it was reconstructed along with the rest of Gyeongbokgung Palace by the order of Heungseon Daewongun, in 1864. However, after the forced annexation of Korea to Japan in 1910, the gate was forcefully moved to the east of the palace to make way for the Japanese Governor–General Building.  This is not the end of the story. Gwanghwamun was once again destroyed during the Korean War. It was restored in 1968 as a reinforced concrete structure, but was moved backwards to expand roads and was the subject of controversy in relation to construction materials. Eventually in December 2006, Gwanghwamun underwent a restoration and relocation project which was completed in August 2010 to become what it is today.
