To dwell as an artist was to focus on himself defining his own identity and communicate with the changing world by expanding his world. According to the artist, when he expanded, he wished to extend his world of evolving art.

stories.title: Untitled -Artist  Park Choong-Heum
stories.script: This metal work titled “Untitled” by the artist Park Choong-Heum, was completed in 2008. The artist aimed to capture his deep respect for nature. The organic shape, which stands on the ground, was made by repeatedly welding together small net-like copperplate units in regular sizes. Doesn’t it evoke an enormous vessel, mountain peak, or giant mushroom, or perhaps a UFO? Copperplates form a slow curve and bloom towards the sky, while the light emanating through the crevices creates fantastic new patterns that are reflected back on the ground. According to the artist, the light that crawls on the ground symbolizes the vitality of nature, while the crevices capture void and generosity allowed by nature. To embrace light in the artwork and disperse it to the environment was his grand wish, with which he adapted himself to nature embracing infinite vitality and communicated with nature.

stories.title: Old Pine 09-1 - Artist Lee Gil-Rae
stories.script: “Old Pine 09-1” was created by the artist Lee Gil-Rae in 2009, and you might have noticed, the sculptor was inspired by the strong vitality of pine trees found all over Korea. As if touched by each brushstroke in Oriental ink paintings, the sculpture features pine barks and branches, which were created by delicately welding together regularly cut copper pipes. The repetitive organic cellular growths express both dynamic vitality of life and the culmination of Asian aesthetics through a sculptural work. The artist Lee Gil-Rae said, “Just as a living organism or an object loses its function when it decomposes, cells or fragments assemble in condense matter and can maintain organic vitality.” This pine tree, pieced together like a puzzle, metaphors the strong vitality and infinite force of life, as the sculptor pays tribute to the great nature.

stories.title: Long-Cherished Wish - Artist Woo Moo-Gil
stories.script: The artwork “Long-Cherished Wish” was created by the artist Woo Moo-Gil in 2008, and the form of a house made of ferroconcrete mass reveals its skeletal-like structure, making it look like a rudimentary house discovered, perhaps, in piles of discarded concrete. The artist intentionally made the structure bare and basic as possible. That way, the focus lied in the symbolism of the form, clearly revealing the essence that had existed behind the façade. He meant to depict a house as being commonplace, yet a unique, enclosed place where someone expresses his or her identity. Such a house trapped inside the concrete beam also represents the psychological state of individuals isolated in modern society. His hope to be make relationships with others was represented with ferroconcrete that looks like a skein of yarn

stories.title: Pillar of Perception - Artist Ryu In
stories.audioTitle: Pillar of Perception - Artist Ryu In
stories.script: Now, this bronze artwork is titled “Pillar of Perception” by the artist Ryu In, who created the series in 1988. The late artist aimed to represent isolation, solitude, anxiety, and fear of man in a desolate modern society. This work realistically captures the dramatic moment of a young man bursting out of a pillar. With his lower half of the body still trapped, the young man put his chest forward but his head and arms dropped backwards. To some viewers, he might appear pathetic and sad, while to others, relieved or even joyous having busted out of a dark tunnel of life. According to the late artist, the series represented the desire and consciousness of man in crisis who wanted to escape from an oppressed reality, such as a pathetic reality or irrational social circumstances. The work allows viewers to contemplate on the dignity of man through the writhing existence bound by human bondage and oppression.

stories.title: Cheeky Buggers - Artist Yang Tae-Geun
stories.script: Look! Doesn’t it look like a comical animal? This artwork is called “Cheeky Buggers” by the artist Yang Tae-Geun, and was completed in 2007. Taking up the porous form of an animal figure, this sculpture was made by welding together steel washers. The head features a green face. Standing upright with its arms crossed and looking out onto the world, the animal can be said to look funny or ostentatious with the point of having a hollow body. Thus, it’s as though the artist is mocking the authority-centric attitude of materialistic society, a tacit message to those who display shameful behaviors. The artist aimed to satirize his belief that communication and coexistence between man and between man & animals in the man-dominated world would be realized through not the head used for one-way self-justification but the heart and body.

stories.title: Don Quixote - Artist Sung Dong-Hun
stories.script: This artwork is titled “Don Quixote” by the artist Sung Dong-hun, who created it in 2011. Composed of assorted machine parts and cement, it is rather funny-looking man riding on a horse. This piece dynamically captures the moment when the man figure and his horse are about to have a bad fall. The sculpture satirizes the legendary delusional dreamer Don Quixote and his horse Rosinante from its namesake Spanish novel by Miguel de Cervantes. Whereas the quixotic knight was in impractical pursuit of idealistic goals with his horse who revived tradition and served his country, this Don Quixote serves as a self-portrait of the artist who tried to challenge the older generation in modern society. The artist pities his kind of people thrown into this world, and this also is a metaphor of such people who are surrounded by fantasy and cannot see reality for what it is.

stories.title: Door of Wisdom - Artist Shin Ok-Joo
stories.audioTitle: Door of Wisdom - Artist Shin Ok-Joo
stories.script: This sculpture is called “Door of Wisdom” by the artist Shin Ok-Joo, who completed it in 2012, and combines the heaviness from steel plates and lightness from rhythmic forms. The artist heated thick square-shaped steel plates to cut into long strips, which were then bent in multiple directions and angles, before securing the work on the ground. The cold and heavy steel plate represents modern civilizations as well as numerous walls that we are faced with in urban life in which we endure despair and alienation. So, the artist said the production process to create doors using walls was “a gesture of resistance in search of an exit from reality.” As the artist intended to bring in the surroundings into the space between the cut and bent plates, viewers can explore the creator’s world of art where contrasting elements can coexist, such as hardness vs. lightness, immobility vs. liveliness, unbalance vs. balance, civilization vs. nature.

stories.title: Self-Portrait - Artist Kang Dae-Young
stories.script: This giant mosquito is titled “Self-Portrait” by the sculptor Kang Dae-young, and was created in 2012. The sculptor breathed a life into the insect on the green lawn by bending thick wires and minimizing volume. With his deep interest in various inclinations of modern people in modern society, the artist focused on collective selfish aggressions or hatred and man’s infinite desires, while thinking that man’s self-centeredness and collective immoderate aggressions were similar to mosquitos that sucked blood to survive and procreate its species. The sculptor created a work that pointed out man’s attitude that insensitively hurts other people or beings for self-interest. As a result, the work was not about the mosquito but rather our own “self-portrait.”

stories.title: Nail and Love  - Artist Park Jong-Bae
stories.audioTitle: Nail and Love  - Artist Park Jong-Bae
stories.script: This work is titled “Nail and Love” by the sculptor Park Jong-bae who created it in 2012. Made of bronze, this work features a simple semi-spherical form with a square-shaped column being nailed into it. The contrast made between the round organic form and cold straight lines creates a dramatic, almost explosive moment as the cold, hard object firmly and perfectly presses against the round full object, yet there is a strong, almost inseparable attraction between the opposing elements. The expanding round form exuding inner energy and the hard-square form diving into it create both a stark contrast and a high tension. Such a sense of tension stirs the viewer’s inner peace and invites them to the inner world. Through the artwork that would guide viewers to the mysterious inner world, the creator intended to imply a conception of a being.

stories.title: Contact, My Heart’s Radio Wave Telescope - Artist Lee Sang-Gill
stories.audioTitle: Contact, My Heart’s Radio Wave Telescope - Artist Lee Sang-Gill
stories.script: Here, we are looking at a giant steel cone with a hollow middle called “Contact, My Heart’s Radio Wave Telescope” that was created by the sculptor Lee Sang-Gill in 2006. Finished with stainless steel, the smooth outer surface reflects light and surroundings, making the work part of a harmonizing scene. The interior wall displays thin, tightly welded stainless lines that create the look of a torpedo as it darkens towards the inner vanishing point. Viewers feel as if they’re being sucked into a black hole that absorbs messages of a parallel world. As the title suggests, this work can be like a telescope to look out onto the world, or an ear trumpet to capture its sounds, or an antenna to detect its sensitivities. The sculptor aimed to capture the theme of “encounter” and “communication” through this work that served as a means of communication, by which the lively exterior and delicate interior combine in perfect harmony.

stories.title: Pebble-Echo - Artist Park Eun-Saeng
stories.script: Here, we have what looks like a large pebble called “Pebble-Echo” that was created by the sculptor Park Eun-Saeng in 2012. By welding small triangles made of artificial materials such as steel plates and stainless steel, the sculptor captures a form evocative of a pebble. The partially sparkling reflective light made by stainless steel can make viewers lose the feel of weight they normally get from steel. The steel on the exterior surface was left to naturally rust, so that it would resemble life, during which people endure changes through organic relationships. According to the artist, rust embodied the irony of life, because to live means to approach death. It seems that through the openings, the pebble could tell stories from within. The artist said the organic shape of the exterior represents the ever-expandable field of nature as well as possibilities of nature that produced varied forms.

stories.title: Paju Samneung (Gongneung, Sulleung, Yeongneung)
stories.script: Paju Samneung are the tombs of three queens of Joseon, with Queen Jangsun buried in Gongneung, Queen Gonghye in Sulleung, and Queen Hyosun in Yeongneung.   Gongneung is the single tomb of the Han Queen Jangsun (1445~1461), the first wife of King Yejong, the 8th King of Joseon. Sunbin Jang, the third daughter of Han Myunghoi, married Crown Prince Yejong in 1460 and became Crown Princess, giving birth to Grand Prince Inseong the following year, but died from postpartum infection at the young age of 17. Gongneung is made in the form of a crown prince's tomb, with a large burial mound. Paju Samneung was registered as a World Heritage Site on June 10, 2009.  Sulleung is the single tomb of Han Queen Gonghye, the first wife of King Seongjong, the 9th King of Joseon. Queen Gonghye, the fourth daughter of Han Myunghoi, married the second son of Deokjong in 1467, and when he ascended to the throne, she became queen. She died childless at the young age of 19. It is the only one of the three tombs that has the form of a royal tomb, because Queen Gonghye passed away as a queen. Stone warriors with helmets and swords gripped in two hands wear the armor of officers with crouched necks. The lines of the armor are clear, and their faces strained.  Yeongneung is the tomb of Jinjong and Crown Princess Hyosun. The son of Yeongjo and Queen Jeongseong, Jinjong died at 10 years of age and was posthumously received the title “Crown Prince Hyojang.” In 1728, when Jinjong died, his tomb was placed in the hill left of Sulleung. Because Jinjong died before ascending to the throne as king and emperor, three tombstones were placed in Yeongneung.  The mounds of the king and queen are side by side on the same hill in Yeongneung, and, when viewed in front of the burial house, the tomb of the king is on the left, and the tomb of the queen is on the right. The decorative stone officials are wearing hats that represent their position, both hands hold scepters, and their bodies are small in proportion to their faces, while their uniforms have long, stretched-out sleeves. Their elbows also have three lines of wrinkles.

stories.title: Yongmili Standing Stone Buddha Pair
stories.script: Paju's Yongmili Standing Stone Buddha Pair was made during the Goryeo period and is Korea's oldest standing stone Buddha. The impressive Yongamsa, located on the eastern foot of Jangji Mountain, is designated as National Treasure No. 93. At a total height of 17.4 m, the face alone is 2.3m, and it is Korea's largest stone Buddha, together with the Stone Statue of Mireuk Buddha of Nonsan Gwanchoksa. The standing stone Buddha pair, made of 2 carved natural boulders that have been moved to the temple, consist of separately made heads, necks, and hats, making them unique Buddhas with wide shoulders that give them a feeling of grandeur.  The left Buddha sitting on top of a natural stone wall is wearing a hat and holds a lotus flower; it has a rounded neck, a proud-looking chest, and the body is clothed in a way that represents Buddha. On both sides, the skirt is expressed in great detail. The rectangular face also has a gentle smile.  The Buddha on the right wears a square hat and is similar to the Buddha on the left, except its hands are clasped together in piety. Both Buddhas have their eyes peacefully closed and face Yongmili Cemetery. According to legend, Prince Hansan was said to have been born in answer to a prayer offered here by the royal court.

stories.title: Majang Lake
stories.script: Majang Lake is a travel destination with a suspension bridge, kayaks, canoes, and water bikes. An urban theme park sits next to the lake and is surrounded by mountains coming together in harmony with the trees and the green of nature.   Along Majang Lake is a beautiful path, a trekking route, a walking trail and a camping trail, as well as water activities, a suspension bridge, an observatory, and cafés. This is Paju's main natural attraction, and offers an escape from busy life and an entry into peaceful rest in the calm of nature.  The ideal place for mental rejuvenation, the tidy park has a water fountain, benches, wildflowers, and photo zones to create memories. The beautiful sky stairway near the reservoir is full of silver grass. Touch the sky at the top of the 148 stairs!  The suspension bridge that crosses Majang Lake is 220m long and 1.5m wide, and is designed to safely withstand gusts of wind and even earthquakes. The moment their feet land on the suspension bridge, visitors express excitement and slowly walk across the bridge.  Reinforced glass (strong enough to withstand bullets) is installed in the middle of the bridge so people crossing can see the lake below, adding to the thrill. With a water walkway, this is a well-loved, romantic lake made into an eco-friendly park that is accessible to all.

stories.title: Bogwangsa Temple
stories.script: Bogwangsa in Goryeong Mountain, Paju is imbued with the love that King Yeongjo, the longest-living Joseon King, had for his parents, and is known for being a mystical temple with lots to see. Bogwangsa Temple is designated as Gyeonggi-do Cultural Asset No. 158.  This is a thousand-year-old temple built during the reign of Unified Silla’s Queen Jinseong. It is also the resting place of Sukbin Choi, and received offerings from the royal family until the late Joseon period.   Built during the Silla period and burned down during the Imjin Wars, the sanctuary and monastery was restored in 1622 by two monks, Seolmi and Deogin. It is also recorded that they established the Dosolam Buddha.  Engravings that depict Daeungbojeon remain with the traces of the royal family. Yeongjo's filial love can be seen in Eosil Hall and the juniper tree in front of it. Eosil Hall is a cozy shrine that houses the portrait and ancestral tablet of Sukbin Choi. A four-corner roof raised in the middle is placed at the front and side. The imposing juniper tree in front of Eosil Hall is more than 300 years old, and is said to have been planted by Yeongjo when he built the hall.  Yeongjo extensively repaired Bogwangsa’s Daeungbojeon and Manseru, and engraved his writing on one side of Daeungbojeon. The current signboard at Daeungbojeon is known to contain Yeongjo's handwriting. After being renovated by Yeongjo, Daeungbojeon and Manseru survived—even the ravages of the Korean War—as a special trace personally left by Yeongjo.

stories.title: Paju Historic Site of Yi I
stories.audioTitle: Paju Historic Site of Yi I
stories.script: The site of Yulgok Yi I, National Monument No. 15, is the location of the ancestral tablet and family tomb of Yulgok Yi I, a scholar and politician of the mid-Joseon Dynasty, and is also the site of Jaeun Academy of Classic Studies where the spirit of Sin Saimdang still lives and breathes.  Yulgok Yi I's pen name was Yulgok; his father was Lee Won-su, and his mother was Sin Saimdang. At the age of 6, he moved to Seoul with his mother to study. At the age of 29, he was first appointed to the Hojojwarang and was a representative political reformer, serving as governor of Hwanghae, Daesaheon, Daejehak, Hojo, Byeongjo, and Leejo Panseo.  In the family tomb area, the tombs of Yulgok and his wife Goksan Roh, the joint tombs of parents Lee Won-soo and Sin Saimdang, and the tombs of his older brother and son form the central tomb. There are 14 other family tombs in total.  Paju has an exceptionally large number of cemeteries, which serve as comfortable resting places for the dead and where the longing of the living pierces.  Currently, the statues of Yulgok Yi I and Sin Saimdang have been restored and are magnificently enshrined here. There are five bullet marks on the marble front of the memorial stone to Yi I, so it is currently protected by a monument.  Yulgok Memorial Hall, which exhibits Yulgok's mementos and biography, is also located here. His books include Seongriseol, Seonghak Seongyo, Gyeoggyeol Yogyeol and others.  In 1973, Jaeun Academy, Yulgok Yi I's tomb, and Sin Saimdang's tomb were each designated Gyeonggi-do Cultural Assets. In February 2013, the site was promoted to National Historic Site No. 525 “Paju Yi I Site” in recognition of its sense of place where artifacts related to Yulgok Yi I are gathered in one place.

stories.title: Hwangpo Sailboat
stories.script: It is said that the Imjin River's hwangpo sailboat was a major means of transportation in the Joseon Dynasty, spreading its wide yellow sails and leisurely passing through, following the wind.  Nowadays, tourists can enjoy 45 minutes of the majestic views of the Imjin River between Duji-ri and Jajang-ri, on a hwangpo sailboat that looks just as it did during the Joseon period. The cruise starts from the Duji-ri dock and travels 3 km while looking at the stone walls of Jajang-ri. At Gorangpo where the water is ankle-deep, the boat turns and makes its way back to Duji-ri for a round trip of 6 km.  With the Vertical Cliffs Tour, see up close the 10-40 meter-high rock cliffs forming a vertical wall of deep red along the Imjin River. Known locally as “Jeokbyeok,” the rock is solid basalt, which can otherwise only be found on Jeju Island. It is said that the cliffs were formed by lava flowing from a volcanic eruption in the Cheorwon area.  Of the 11 red cliffs along the Imjin River, the Jajang-ri Red Cliff seen from the cruise ship is relatively short, but the cruise itself is pleasant. Get on the Hwangpo Sailboat to see the beautiful scenery of the Imjin River, including Wondang-ri red cliff, Horogoru Fortress, and Gorangpo.  Jeokbyeok Boating is one of the 8 scenic spots on the Imjin. For reference, the “Eight Scenes of the Imjin at Paju” are Hwaseokjeongchun (1st view), which is called the Spring of Hwaseongjeong; Jangamsujo (2nd view), which is called Fishing in Jangam; Songamcheongun (3rd view), which is called the Clear Cloud of Songam; Jangposaewoo (4th view), which is called Jangpo's Drizzling Rain; Dongpawanwol (5th view), the Moon of Dongpa Station; Jeokbyeokbeomjoo (6th view), Boating in Jeokbyeok; Dongwonmoseol (7th view), the Evening Snow in Dongwon; and finally Jinsahyojong (8th view), the Bell of the Dawn in Jinsa.  The 8 scenic spots of Imjin are reproduced in works such as Gyeomjae Jeong Seon's Yeongang Imsulcheop and Imjin Jeokbyeokdo, making it possible to realize that they are the essence of an Imjin River cruise. Be sure to visit the Paju Hwangpo Sailboat experience site, where you can take a cruise of the Imjin River, see the columnar joint cliff and listen to the historical commentary.

stories.title: Gamak Mountain
stories.script: Located in Gamgol-gil, Jeokseong-myeon, Paju-si, Gamak Mountain is where nature and history come alive. “Gamak Mountain” means “Dark Blue Rock Mountain,” because it is said that black and blue light came out at the same time between the rocks.  Since ancient times, Gamak Mountain has been known as one of the five peaks of Gyeonggi, along with Hwaak Mountain in Gapyeong, Songak Mountain in Gaeseong, Gwanak Mountain in Gwacheon, and Unak Mountain in Pocheon. Beneath Janggunbong Peak is Imgeokjeong Cave, where the bandit Im Kkeokjeong hid from government forces during the reign of Joseon’s King Myeongjong. In Seolma-ri Valley are monuments commemorating the battles of the British Army and the Daehan Heroic Corps during the Korean War.  Located at the starting point of Gamak Mountain walking road is a suspension bridge that connects the two sides of Seolmari Valley, divided by a road, and makes it whole. The 150m span is suspended in harmony with nature and leads to a trail to Ungye Waterfall, making it the best 1-day hiking course.  A charming valley with Seolma Stream, Ungye Falls is the pride of Gamak Mountain. The nearly vertical waterfall is said to be used for ice climbing in winter.  At the top of Gamak Mountain is Local Relic No. 8, which is a stele 170cm high, and the Im Kkeokjeong Cave, where Im Kkeokjeong is said to have sought refuge from pursuing government forces, just below Janggunbong Peak.  Gamak Mountain is close to the Military Demarcation Line. Once you climb to the top, you can see the Imjin River and Songak Mountain in Gaeseong. Many hikers seek out the trail where the fragrance of pine trees and fresh earth wafts through.

stories.title: Yulgok Arboretum
stories.script: Yulgok Arboretum was created for the preservation, proliferation, and exhibition of plant resources. It was selected as one of the 24 best scenic spots nationwide and offers a variety of forest experience programs.   Yulgok Arboretum was officially opened in June 2021 as a place where dense forest had been transformed through the forest recovery project in the 1960s.  Within the Yulgok Arboretum is a botanical garden with 21 themes, including 70 trees of 15 species donated by citizens, 80,000 trees of 700 species, and 220,000 plants of 500 species, totaling 300,000 plants of 1,300 species.  Yulgok Arboretum operates two representative types of forest experience programs. First is a forest experience program for infants, and forest healing programs such as Healing Forest, Family Forest, Mom's Vitality Forest, and Silver Forest.  The 5 km path around the arboretum includes an observatory overlooking the Imjin River, a pine fragrance trail, and Munbawi Rock, all of which give the site a rich and colorful charm. See the Imjin River to the north and Papyeong Mountain and Gamak Mountain to the east at a glance. It is also close to the historical sites of Yulgok Yi I and Hwang Hee, making for a well-rounded tour of the whole area.  Yulgok Arboretum is a proud forest complex and cultural space of Paju, both in name and reality, providing a variety of forest culture and recreational tourism services.

stories.title: Imjingak Tourist Attractions (Mangbaedan, Peace Bell, Steam Locomotive)
stories.audioTitle: Imjingak Tourist Attractions (Mangbaedan, Peace Bell, Steam Locomotive)
stories.script: Imjingak Tourist Site is a place engraved with sadness over the tragedy of the Korean War that broke out on June 25, 1950, and the subsequent national confrontation.  There are a number of war memorials, such as the Imjin River Region War Monument and the US Army Participation Monument here, as well as the actual train that stopped here on its way to Sinuiju, the northern tip of the unified nation before the Korean Peninsula was split in two in 1945.  Imjin Railway Bridge was originally two bridges side by side. One was destroyed during the war, and only the structure of the steel bridge remains.  Korean nationals must bring their ID, and foreign nationals must bring their passports.  Mangbaedan is where displaced people from families north of the Demarcation Line pay their respects to their parents and grandparents living in North Korea, from as close as possible to their hometown every Lunar New Year's Day, Chuseok, and whenever they miss their family. Mangbaedan is where people wish to know whether their separated family members are alive or dead, as no news comes from the North. Millions of Koreans and foreigners visit each year as tourists to a unification and security destination of yearning for the reunification of Korea.  The Peace Bell, which rang in the new millennium with a reverberating sound from a high place overlooking the northern land of Imjingak, was built in reflection of the desire of 9 million Gyeonggi-do residents for a lasting peace and the reunification of Korea. Weighing 21 tons, the Peace Bell is 3.4m high, and 2.2m in diameter, and symbolizes the 21st century. It was rung 21 times at midnight on January 1, 2000. The bell house is a magnificent wooden structure with a Samo roof, 12.2m high and a floor area of 70m2.  The steam locomotive kept in the Imjingak tourist area went up from Gaesong Station to Hanpo Station in Hwanghae-do to transport military supplies to the Allied Forces during the Korean War. While on one of its return trips south, it was attacked from the air at Jangdan Station on the Gyeongui Line late at night on December 31, 1950 and was derailed there. The Cultural Heritage Administration registered it as Cultural Property No. 78 in order to protect and manage it as a painful historical symbol of the division between the two Koreas. It was mainly operated for cargo and passenger transportation in North Korea, and was evaluated as one of the most outstanding steam locomotives in the history of Korean railways, as it was used for cargo and passenger transportation in South Korea as well. On June 25, 2009, the Gyeonggi Tourism Organization put a roof over it to protect it from sun and rain, cleaned it up, gave it anti-corrosion treatment and provided permanent protection against rust. It has been relocated to its current location and is on display to the public.

stories.title: Imjingak Tourist Site (Peace Gondola)
stories.script: The Peace Gondola is listed as one of the ‘100 Must-Visit Tourist Spots’. It stands as the first gondola to traverse the Civilian Control Line, crossing the Imjingang River from the tourist sites area of Imjingak.  The Peace Gondola building located in Imjingak on the south side consists of three floors. The first floor houses the ticket office, a restaurant, convenience store and the Paju Agricultural Specialty Products Promotion Center. On the second floor, there are a bakery store and a restaurant, while the third floor serves as the boarding area.  Covering a total length of 850 meters, the Peace Gondola travels from the Imjingang River tourist site to the U.S. Military Camp Greaves, taking approximately 5 minutes to complete the journey. Each gondola can accommodate up to 10 passengers and operates in red, green, or white. Notably, the white gondola features a transparent glass bottom, providing exceptional visibility. This particular gondola is the most sought after, as passengers can observe unique views through the glass bottom, offering a 360-degree perspective of the Imjingang River and the rice field within the Civilian Control Line during the ride. Due to its location within the Civilian Control Zone, warning signs indicating potential from mines and unidentified bombs are prevalent. Consequently, the boarding area is surrounded by metal fences to ensure visitor safety. Being the only place in the world where tourists can witness the site of a divided country, it annually attracts numerous foreign tourists.  Visitors usually spend an hour at the northern boarding area of the DMZ region before returning to the southern boarding area at Imjingak. Through the Peace Gondola, visitors can easily traverse the Civilian Control Zone as regular civilians. Korean nationals are required to present their identity cards, while foreign nationals must carry their passports for identity verification upon entering the Civilian Control Zone.

stories.title: Imjingak Tourist Site (Freedom Bridge)
stories.script: The Bridge of Freedom is located behind the Mangbaedan Memorial Altar in the Imjingak Pavilion. It stands as a commemoration to honor the souls of displaced individuals who yearned for their hometowns and families but passed away in North Korea.   Originally, the Gyeongui Line Railroad had both upper and lower bridges. However, the bridges were destroyed by bombing and only the piers remained. The restoration of the western railway bridge was undertaken for the purpose of exchanging prisoners of war, and a temporary bridge was erected at the southern end.  The bridge was previously known as Dokgaedari Bridge, named after the Jayeonmaeul Village in Nosang-ri. It acquired its current name in 1953 when 12,773 South Korean and UN soldiers who had been prisoners of war returned by crossing the bridge. On closer inspection of the structure, it becomes evident that it is not completely made of wood but areas crucial for bearing weight are reinforced with steel. The bridge consists of squared wood beams and I-shaped steel beams arranged in a well-like formation atop the piers, with four logs in four rows and a wooden top plate laid over them. Its total length is 83 meters, with a width of 4.5-7meters and a height of around 8 meters.  The significance of the Bridge of Freedom lies in symbolizing hope amid the tragedy of Korean War. Despite not being architecturally exceptional and being a temporary structure, it stands as a modern heritage piece, evoking memories of the Cold War and representing the return to freedom. The bridge was designated as Gyeonggi-do Monument No. 162 on December 24, 1996.

stories.title: DMZ Peace Tour - Dora Observatory
stories.script: Have you heard of the DMZ Peace Tour? It offers three courses, including the visits to Dora Observatory, the 3rd Tunnel, and Unification Village. Travelers can easily explore these notable attractions with the tour. Let’s take a closer look of the Dora Observatory.  Dora Observatory was built in 1986 to monitor the northernmost part of the Western Front. It was first opened to the public in January 1987. Equipped with dozens of telescopes, it provides visitors with glimpses of North’s scenery. Views include Gaesong City, Songak Mountain, Jangdan Station, and Gijeong-dong Village, offering an almost tangible insight into life in North Korea. The observatory also features auxiliary facilities such as 500 spectator seats, a V.I.P. room, a control office, and a parking for up to 40 vehicles.  However, due to its location within the Civilian Control Zone, regular vehicles are restricted to access. Therefore, the best way to visit the observatory is by joining the DMZ tour program operated by Paju City. Also, visitors must present valid ID at Imjingang Station for access. Korean nationals should bring their ID, while foreign nationals need their passports.

stories.title: Historic Site of Hwang Hee
stories.script: Five kilometers from Imjingak Pyeonghwa Nuri Park can be found the historic site of Hwang Hee in Bangujeong, and both are popular tourist destinations in Paju. This is the place where Hwang Hee spent the rest of his life after resigning from his government post. It offers a great view of the Imjin River.  Hwang Hee assisted the king from the end of Goryeo to the reign of King Sejong of the Joseon Dynasty, and in particular, helped King Sejong lay the foundation for Joseon. He is known to have been an honest official and a great asset to Joseon.  Inside the Hwang Hee Historic Site are Bangujeong Pavilion, Angjidae, Bangchon Yeongdang, Gyeongmojae, Wolheonsa Temple, and Bangchon Statue. Monument No. 29 stands in the middle of the Historic Site, and is so named for Hwang Hee’s pen name.  Hwang Hee's tomb is enshrined in Tanhyeon, not far from Bangujeong. The name “Bangchon Yeongdang” is hung here, and is where his descendants hold ancestral rites in honor of his achievements.  He practiced principled politics based on tolerance and conviction, and was also the longest-serving high-ranking civil servant in Joseon. When he retired from a long career in government and returned to his hometown, he spent the rest of his life in Bangujeong, along the Imjin River. The name, “Bangujeong,” suggests that there were many seagulls here a long time ago.  The annexes include the unpainted Gyeongmojae and Gojiksa buildings, which are spaces for visiting guests and ancestral rites. Bangujeong, Gyeonggi-do Cultural Heritage Material No. 12, was burned down during the Korean War and reconstructed in 1967.

stories.title: Jangdankong Wellbeing Maru
stories.script: The Jangdankong Wellbeing Maru building was completed on August 31, 2021. Rice, Jangdan beans, and ginseng produced in the clear and clean Jangdan area have been called Jangdan sambaek since ancient times, and were gifted to the king because of their excellent quality. Jangdan soybeans are unrivaled for their deep flavor thanks to the soil, good drainage from the Imjin River, clean air, and climate with a large daily temperature difference.  Since ancient times, Paju has been blessed with excellent soil quality and climate for five crops, including rice, beans, barley, and millet. Various local products, including rice, have been offered to the government in the past, due to their excellent reputation for flavor and nutrition—a legacy which continues to this day. In addition, Jangdankong Wellbeing Maru is Korea's best domestic soybean power brand, with processing facilities that produce meju, soy sauce, and bean curd (tofu).  In addition, this is a special experience space where you can see, create, and enjoy a coexistence with Paju farmhouses. Here, through the modernization and scientification of traditional sauces, hygienic, quality paste products are produced without sacrificing traditional flavors. Such products continue to contribute to increasing farm household incomes and revitalizing the local economy. Research and development of safe premium soybeans has resulted in HACCP certification and aided in production of other agricultural products by Paju farmers. Businesses here have gained a competitive edge with specialized products and promotion of a “well-being” food culture, providing high-quality food products to residents and tourists alike as they flexibly respond to consumer trends.  Products using fermented Paju Jangdan soybeans, rich in organic matter and high in cancer-fighting isoflavones, are characterized by their savory, light flavor. These products are from the brand called Haeseumillae that you can trust and eat because they are produced in hygienic facilities using tofu and pastes that are full of nutrition and flavor.  In addition, at local grocery store, Paju Jangdan Beans directly shipped from farms are always available.

stories.title: Odu Unification Observatory
stories.script: Odu Unification Observatory is a representative unification education site. On a clear day, you can see Songak Mountain in Gaeseong and North Korean villages. On September 28, 1992, this observatory opened as a five above-ground and 1 basement floor building to ease the longing of separated families in the South and to educate the unification with the Korean people's desire for unifying.  The observatory is located on the summit of Odusan Mountain, 118m above sea level, where the Han River, the lifeline of Seoul, and the Imjin River flowing down from the North meet. Currently, you can enter the Unification Observatory by private vehicle.  This is the location of the Odu Castle Site (Historic Site No. 351) from the old Samguksagi or Goryeosa, which was a strategic military point in ancient times. It is now the northernmost point of the western front, and is also where the two Koreas have not been able to cross the short distance of 2 km over the Imjin River for more than half a century.  Propaganda Village in Jeonggot-ri, Imhan-myeon, Panmun District, Gaesong City, North Korea, is the closest North Korean settlement to Seoul. In a straight line, it is about 24 km from the edge of the Seoul and about 38 km to Seoul City Hall. Inside Propaganda Village are houses, facilities such as the Kim Il-sung Historic Tower, a threshing center, and an elementary school, as well as farmland, and you can see a military post. On a clear day, you can see Mt. Songak to the north of Gaesong City and about 3 km from the Odu Unification Observatory. If you look to the right, there are places where the river narrows to only about 650m.  Looking toward South Korea, a hanok (traditional Korean house) structure comes into view. The name of the building is “Goryeo Reunification Center,” and it is an exhibition hall displaying the shrines of Goryeo Dynasty figures and related cultural assets. The stadiums below it make up the Paju NFC training facility for the national soccer team.  From Odu Unification Observatory, you can see Songak Mountain in Gaeseong to the north and the 63 Building in Seoul to the south. It is the best unification and national security tourist destination connected to Imjingak, the 3rd Tunnel, and Panmunjom to the northeast direction along the freely opened Jayu-ro.

stories.title: Provence Art Village (Matgoeul)
stories.script: Paju Provence is a small European-style village, famous for its light festival and for its picturesque buildings as if located in the south of France. There are many things to see and experience such as small shops, workshops, a miniature Eiffel Tower, pretty cafes, and good spots to take pictures.  The Provence Art Village has a colorful and charming atmosphere. It is also a popular place for reunions, dates, drives, healing, filming of dramas and movies, and has been recognized as a notable shopping area. It is also home to Heyri Art Village.  The motif is buildings in Provence, France, but there are many that are colorfully pastel-toned or have exotic wall murals or sculptures, so it reminds us of a fairytale land more than the actual Provence region. From around sunset to closing time, a colorful starlight festival occurs around a variety of sculptures in the complex.  Starting with a high-class French restaurant in 1996, it began to become a place to try food from all over the world at European-style bakeries and cafes and Italian restaurants, as well as Korean establishments, in harmony with beautiful gardens, story murals, and night lighting. Come to enjoy some leisure in life, take in trend-setting fashion, household items, and experience facilities.  In Provence Art Village, each shop runs its own respective concept but is organically connected in independent buildings with warm colors. A greenhouse and outdoor garden provide rest areas of flowers and water and a popular tourist stops. A variety of festivals feature cultural performances, new experiences, and beautiful events throughout the four seasons.  Dishes at Matgoeul, a restaurant in Provence Art Village, use only domestically grown Paju Jangdan beans and include Jangdan Bean Cheongukjang, Jangdan Kongbijjigae, Jangdan Soybean Doenjang-jjigae, Tofu Mushroom Hotpot, Tofu Seafood Hotpot, Tofu Bossam, Bean Bijijjigae, Cheonggukjang Stew, Stir-fried Beans, and Soft Tofu.

stories.title: Heyri Art Village
stories.script: Heyri Art Village is on the “Top 100 Korean Tourist Sites” list. Established in 1998, it is the largest art village and cultural district in Korea and lies within the Unification Park Special Tourist Zone. It is a work of art itself, with studios of artists from a variety of fields, art galleries, and performance halls. About 380 artists, sculptors, musicians, writers, architects, and craftsmen participate, building houses and galleries, roads and bridges to create this community of art.  Heyri Art Village was the third location in Korea to be designated a cultural district, following Insadong Culture Street in 2002 and Daehangno in 2004. At that time, there were a total of 380 members here from various artistic fields, including prominent figures in culture and arts, such as Yoon Dohyun (singer), Park Bumshin (novelist), Hwang Inyong (broadcaster), Kang Jegyu (film director), and Kang Woo-seok.   Here in Heyri, commercial and entertainment facilities unrelated to cultural facilities are prohibited. Admission to the village itself is free, but most of the experience facilities charge admission fees. Commercial facilities include bookstores, theaters, museums, art galleries, and restaurants. When searching for a map of the area around a certain building, enter the building number on Heyrimaeul-gil, Tanhyeon-myeon, Paju-si, Gyeonggi-do.  Bus number 2200 runs from Hongik University entrance to Heyri Paju. If you don’t have enough time to wander around the whole of Heyri Art Village, Area F is the must-see core.  Area A is marked by a purple road on the map, which includes Gate 1, the General Information Center and Parking Lot 8, a public parking lot. Area B is marked by a black road and includes private houses, workshops, and hostels. Area C is marked by a maroon-colored road. Like Area B, it includes private houses, workshops, and hostels. Area D is marked by a turquoise road. Accessible through Gates 8 and 9, Parking Lot 12 is also located here. Area E is marked by a brown road on the map. Area F is marked by a yellow road and is the core area in Heyri Art Village. It can be accessed through gates 4 to 7. Public Parking Lot 10 is also here. In addition, the three large buildings located in Areas H and F are collectively referred to as Area H.

stories.title: Jangneung
stories.script: Jangneung is located in Jangneung-ro, Tanhyeon-myeon, Paju, and refers to the joint tomb of Injo, the 16th king of the Joseon Dynasty, and Queen Inyeol, its first queen. Jangneung here was built in Bukuncheon-ri, Paju, after Queen Inyeol passed away. Later, when King Injo passed away, it was made into a twin tomb for a king and his queen to be buried together.  However, as snakes and scorpions frequently made their homes in the crevices between stones, it was moved to its current location and rebuilt into a joint tomb. The stone folding screen of Jangneung is the first Joseon royal tomb to have peony and lotus patterns engraved on it, rather than the traditional zodiac statue or cloud pattern.  The tomb is surrounded by a stone folding screen and a banister stone, and inside are stone statues of warriors, horses, lagoons, sunsets, and jangmyeong lanterns. In addition, two Honyu stones were placed to connect the two tombs into one.   The stone figures of Jangneung include those from before and after the move, so you can see the stone figures of royal tombs in the 17th and 18th centuries in the same place. Jangneung was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site on May 26, 1970.

stories.title: DMZ Peace Tour - The 3rd Tunnel
stories.script: After visiting the Dora Observatory, we proceeded to the second course of the DMZ Peace Tour. It is the 3rd Tunnel, located in Gunnae-myeon, Paju City.  The 3rd Tunnel is an infiltration tunnel constructed by North Korea and discovered in 1978. Extending over 1.6 kilometers with a height and width of 2 meters, it was designed to mobilize 30,000 troops in an hour. Despite being similar in scale to the 2nd Tunnel, it is considered a more significant threat as an invasion tool, being only 52 kilometers away from Seoul, approximately 45 minute drive by car.  Inside the tunnel, visitors may observe blast marks from the excavating process facing south. Currently, facilities such as the DMZ cinema, symbolic sculptures, and souvenir stores offer tourists unique and unforgettable experiences. Visitors can explore the tunnel by walking or riding the monorail.  To visit the 3rd Tunnel and other national security destinations like Dorasan Station and Imgin-gak, joining DMZ tour program of Paju is highly recommended. Remember to bring your identity card and foreign visitors should carry their passports.

stories.title: DMZ Peace Tour - Unification Village
stories.script: The Unification Village, known as Tongilchon in Korean, marks the final stop of the DMZ Peace Tour. Its administrative district is located in Policy Resident Village, only 4.5 kilometers south of the Military Demarcation Line.  The village is established in August 1973 following a special directive from the President to ‘build a strategic pilot farming village that addressed the deficiencies of the reconstructive village’. At that time, it comprised a total of 84 households, including 40 households from the original inhabitants of that area, 40 households from the 1st Division reserve officers and non-commissioned officers, and 4 households consisting of families working at the school, pumping station, and church. Over 30 years, the population has increased, and it currently houses 102 households.  Additionally, during the early 1970s, the previously neglected land underwent cultivation to produce food and crops. Since the village has been maintained as a privately controlled area, there have been no factories or pollutants in the vicinity for 50 years. The clean natural environment, combined with fertile soil, allows the village to produce Korean Ginseng, rice, and soybean, renowned as the special products of Paju and known as ‘Jangdan Sam Baek’, three white food produced in Jangdan Province of Paju. Notably, a Soybean Festival is even held in the village in every November.  For those interested in experiencing the taste of ‘Jangdan Sam Baek’, products can be purchased by visiting the ‘Paju Jangdan-myeon Tongilchon Agricultural Products Market’. Please note that access is only granted after joining the DMZ Peace Tour or Paju City Tour. Hope you enjoy exploring the DMZ area during the tour.

stories.title: Paju City Tour Nature and Wellness
stories.audioTitle: Paju City Tour Nature and Wellness
stories.script: Welcome to Paju City Tour’s Nature and Wellness course! Join us in the British Military Seolmari Battle Memorial Park, Gamaksan Suspension Bridge, and Yulgok Arboretum where, you can relish nature’s beauty.  Established in 1957, the British Military Seolmari Battle Memorial Park honors the fallen British soldiers of the Korean War. They fought valiantly against Chinese armies in Seolmari, Jeokseong-myeon, Paju. Pass through the Peace Gate at the entrance of the park, and you’d be greeted by historic sculptures. There is a giant beret, which is a symbol of the British Armed Forces, statues of British soldiers, and battle monuments. Look to the lush trees and the stream trickling beneath the Gloucestershire Bridge, and you can feel the nature within.  The Gamaksan Suspension Bridge reconnects the Seolmari Valley, which was once cut off by roads, and is around 150m long. The bridge is located in Gamaksan Mountain, where there is everything from quaint valleys to the dramatic Ungyepokpo Falls and Imkkeokjeongbong Peak. Due to its beautiful natural environment, tourists flock to the bridge on weekends and holidays.  Yulgok Arboretum is a place of endless possibilities! In addition to preserving, propagating, and showcasing plant genetic resources, they also offer a variety of forest-related cultural and recreational services. At the arboretum, you can see beautiful exhibition halls, such as Four Seasons Garden, Coniferous Garden, Rock Garden, Fruit Tree Garden, Saimdang Forest, and many more. There are also forest experience programs where you can observe nature from up close. From the Forest Healing Program to the Children’s Forest Experience, there are programs for all ages! Come and try!

stories.title: Paju City Tour Nature and History
stories.audioTitle: Paju City Tour Nature and History
stories.script: Welcome everyone to Paju City Tour’s Nature and History course! This course takes you to the most beautiful nature locations in Paju City as well as its precious historic sites such as Bogwangsa Temple, Hyeeumwon Inn Site, and the Two Rock-carved Standing Buddhas.  Our first stop is the Majanghosu Suspension Bridge. It is 220m long and is built on the eco-friendly park, Majanghosu Lake. As you cross the bridge, you can see the beauty of the mountains and lake in harmony. The tree colony coupled with the cool green mountain make the whole view look like a painting. On top of that, bulletproof glass is partially installed in the middle of Majanghosu Suspension Bridge. There, you can feel the thrill of floating above the water.  Our next stop is Bogwangsa Temple, a thousand-year-old temple made in the year 894. By the order of the king, the United Silla monk Doseon had it made. The temple was a bit damaged during the Japanese invasion and the Korean War, but the grand building is preserved well thanks to the efforts of Korean ancestors. Bogwangsa Temple is also where the Joseon King Yeongjo honored his mother. Here, there are pavilions dedicated to the portrait of Sukbin Choi, the mother of King Yeongjo and a juniper tree that protects it. You can truly feel the heartfelt love King Yeongjo had for his mother.  Established in 1122 during the reign of King Yejong of the Goryeo Dynasty, the Hyeeumwon Inn Site was a national housing facility. It was created to protect and aid the people who traveled between Namkyeong and Gaeseong. Not only did it house ordinary people, it also had a separate palace for government officials and the king himself to stay. As such, its scale is estimated to have been very large. Traces of ancient civil engineering, including 27 building structures, pond sites, and drainage channels were discovered so far. These are in the architectural style of the early Goryeo Dynasty. This is a rare find in South Korea, so the site is considered significant data for architectural history.  Finally, there are the Two Rock-carved Standing Buddhas. The Buddha statues are carved into the side of a natural cliff and were made under either King Seonjong of the Goryeo Dynasty or King Sejo of the Joseon Dynasty. Two Buddhas are standing together in harmony with the surrounding rock cliff. The sight is truly a wonder and was recognized as a national treasure. The statue stands at 17.4m tall and the face alone is 2.4m. When you see it in person, you can’t help but marvel at its sheer scale.

stories.title: Paju City Tour Special Tourist Zone
stories.audioTitle: Paju City Tour Special Tourist Zone
stories.script: Welcome one and all to the Paju City Tour Special Tourist Zone course! Did you know- in the evaluation of Gyeonggi-do’s special tourist zones- Paju City’s Unification Dongsan Special Tourist Zone won first place for two consecutive years? In this course, you can enjoy Paju City’s pride and joy: the Unification Dongsan Special Tourist Zone and all it has to offer!  The first place to visit is the Odusan Unification Observatory. As the Hangang River flows from the south and the Imjingang River flows from the north, they meet near the Unification Observatory and flow into the Yellow Sea. The sight is truly breathtaking. It is also a historical location. The ancient kingdoms Goguryeo and Baekje fought for this very territory and built the 118m long Odusan Mountain Castle Grounds. If you’re interested in history or beautiful nature, Odusan Unification Observatory is the place for you!  The next destination is Provence Village, a charming spot where European-style buildings in every corner create a distinctive atmosphere. Visitors can enjoy not only delicious restaurants but also cafes, bakeries, accessory shops, and clothing stores, offering a wide variety of things to see, eat, and experience.  The next place to be is Gyeonggi-do’s shopping tourist landmark: the Shinsegae Premium Outlet. From exotic-looking sights to countless categories of brands, concerts, and convenience facilities await you here. The outlet is a mere 30 minutes away from Seoul, making it very accessible. Being a true cultural complex, there are lots to enjoy nearby such as the Heyri Art Valley, the Nuri Peace Park, and more!  Located in Paju City, the Heyri Art Valley is Korea’s biggest art village. Established in 1998, its foundational inaugural meeting started it all. Around 380 artists, musicians, authors, and architects are members in the community. Heyri is a place by the artists, for the artists. Numerous galleries, museums, exhibits, concert halls, and cafes call the valley home. The homes and studios of the artists are alongside them, making for a unique atmosphere. On top of it all, each building is made to amplify the natural environment around them. Whether it is mountains, clouds, swamps, or streams, Heyri Art Valley’s design is yet another reason to visit the marvelous village.  Finally, we come to Paju City’s bean themed tourist locations: Jangdankong Well-being Maru. Jangdankong Well-being Maru opened in 2021, and their main attraction is the Hangari Yard that displays over 1400 jangdok crock pots. Here you can try making your own jang through the Jangdok Distribution Program. Their Haeseumilrae Café also has a ton of creative menu items using beans. Jangdankong Well-being Maru is packed with sights to see, stuff to eat, and lots to enjoy! Come on over and experience their diversely welcoming space.

stories.title: Paju City Tour Popular Course
stories.script: Welcome everyone to the Paju City Popular Course! This course goes through Paju City’s most popular tourist attractions. From Majanghosu Suspension Bridge, Bogwangsa Temple, and all the way to Odusan Unification Observatory, you can see them all in this course!  The first place we visit is the Majanghosu Suspension Bridge. Located just above the surface of Majanghosu Lake, the suspension bridge is 220m long. Here you can enjoy the mountains and the lake in harmony with the foliage and the setting sun. These sights make the bridge one of Paju City’s top tourist attractions. Near the bridge there is a Sky Stairway surrounded by wildflowers, some benches here and there, and a trail going around the lake. You can leave the busy city, immerse yourself in nature, and relax your soul.  We stop next at Bogwangsa Temple. It was built under the order of Queen Jinsung and at the hands of the United Silla monk Doseon. The temple survived both the Japanese Invasion and the Korean War. It is also known as the place King Yeongjo of the Joseon honored his mother: Sukbin Choi. Bogwangsa Temple is also recognized for its high historical value. The temple’s Daeeungbojeon Hall and the Wooden Bodhisattva Statue were both registered as tangible cultural heritage in Gyeonggi-do.  For our last stop, we go to the Odusan Unification Observatory. The observatory was established in 1992 and aims to soothe the homesickness of the war-separated families as well as educate citizens on unification. Odusan Unification Observatory is built on the truce line and is where the lifeline of Seoul Hangang River and Imjingang River from the north come together. Here, you can physically see the division between the two Koreas yet still appreciate the beauty of Korea’s scenery.

stories.title: Paju City Tour Main Sightseeing
stories.script: Welcome to Paju City Tour’s Main Sightseeing course! This course takes two days from Saturday to Sunday, and throughout we will look at Paju City’s main attractions. We’ll visit the Imjingang Hwangpo Sailboat, Gamaksan Suspension Bridge, Historic Site related to Yi I, and the National Folk Museum of Korea together.  The first course is the Imjingang Hwangpo Sailboat experience. Located near the Imjingang Riverside, the program is Paju City’s sole boat riding tourist experience. Here, you can try getting on a Hwangpo sailboat: the main mode of transportation in the Joseon Dynasty. We can ride along the river and look at the sights around Imjingang River. Imjingang River was once off-limits to civilians for 50 years. But now, you can enjoy its scenery at gaze upon the 8 Sights of Imjingang, Duji Pier, and experience the history and culture of Gorangpo-gu.  Next, we go to the Gamaksan Suspension Bridge. The bridge connects the valleys of Gamaksan Mountain: one of the five famous mountains in Gyeonggi-do. It is 150m long and in the style of a Mujutap Hyeosu bridge. You can feel the thrill of the bouncing bridge along with the mountain’s beautiful scenery.  The next destination is the Historic Site related to Yi I. It was built to honor the scholarship and virtue of Yulgok Yi I: an important figure of the Joseon Dynasty. Inside the site, there are the family graves: including the graves of Yulgok Yi I and his mother Shin Saimdang. The site is also home to Jawunseowon, Yulgok Yi I's congregation stone, and Yulgok Memorial Hall. Here, you can get a good glimpse into Yulgok Yi I's inner thoughts and life.  We will end the first day’s schedule at the National Folk Museum of Korea. Its Paju branch houses folk relics and materials and was built to both store and exhibit their artifacts. The National Folk Museum of Korea has a near total of ten thousand books and you can freely use their folk archive materials. You can also see small exhibits and realistic hologram videos. Come and truly experience historic moments in person.  We’ll start off the second day with the DMZ Peace Tour and its main attractions: The 3rd Infiltration Tunnel and Dora Observatory. Discovered in 1978 inside the DMZ, it is 1,635m long and made up of arches 2m long and wide. Visitors can use the monorails to go inside the tunnel. It takes only 15 minutes and allows for comfortable viewing. Inside, there is much to see like the DMZ clip theater, exhibits, and symbolistic installations. Our next stop Dora Observatory is right next to the tunnel. Located on the far north of the Military Demarcation Line, it is a security tourism location installed by the Ministry of National Defense in 1986. There are tens of telescopes, around 500 seats in their theater, VIP rooms, and a situation room in the observatory. You can also see North Korean life through the Gaeseong Industrial Complex and the periphery of Gaeseong City.  Finally, the Imjingak Tourist Site is where we end the course. It is a place of longing for unification and thus is closest to North Korea. It also historically commemorates the pains of the Korean War. The site was established by people coming down from the north and who had just lost their homes. Now it is used as the Gyeonggi Peace Center where you can see life in North Korea through various materials. You can also use the telescope on the third floor of the observatory to see North Korean lands.

stories.title: Paju City Tour Peace Sightseeing
stories.script: Welcome one and all to the Paju City Tour’s Peace Sightseeing course! On this course, we visit locations that tell the pain of North and South separation. We’ll be visiting the National Memorial for Abductees during the Korean War, Imjingak Tourist Site, and the DMZ Peace Tour. Through these places, we hope you can feel just how precious peace is.  First, we go to the National Memorial for Abductees during the Korean War. Many were kidnapped by North Korea during the Korean War in 1950. The space is a reminder of that painful history and aims to comfort the missing victims and their families. Each abductee was someone’s friend and neighbor. The memorial is there to remember them and wish for their safe return. You can look to the abductees and their families, their sadness, and begin to understand the need and meaning of peace and unification.  Next, we head to the Imjingak Tourist Site. It is located 7km south of the Military Demarcation Line. Imjingak still holds the tragic memories of war and was established in 1972. Now it is used as the Gyeonggi Peace Center. Here you can see life in North Korea through various materials and videos, but you can also actually see North Korean land through a telescope on the third floor of the observatory.  Concluding the course, let us go to the DMZ Peace Tour’s main attractions: The 3rd Infiltration Tunnel and Dora Observatory. The 3rd Infiltration Tunnel was an underground tunnel for infiltration and was discovered at the Panmunjom 4km southwards. Discovered in 1978 inside the DMZ, it is 1,635m long and only 265m of it is available to the public for their safety. Inside there is the DMZ clip theater, exhibits, and symbolistic installations. Using the monorails, venturing inside the tunnel takes only 15 minutes and allows for comfortable viewing. Dora Observatory is a security tourism location and was installed by the Ministry of National Defense in 1986. It is located on the far north of the Military Demarcation Line. There are tens of telescopes, around 500 seats in their theater, VIP rooms, and a situation room in the observatory. You can also see the Gaeseong Industrial Complex, Songaksan Mountain, and the Peace Village with your own eyes.

stories.title: Museum of the Japanese Invasion of Joseon at Jinnamgwan (Yeosu Jinnamgwan Museum)
stories.audioTitle: Museum of the Japanese Invasion of Joseon at Jinnamgwan (Yeosu Jinnamgwan Museum)
stories.script: Yeosu's Jinnamgwan Hall, a guesthouse for the Joseon navy at Jeolla Jwasuyeong (naval base in Jeolla province), is a place of historic import. The Joseon navy won battles in the second Japanese Invasion of Korea (1592-1598).   To widen the space inside the building, two pillars on either side were moved back, and simple, robust materials were used to maintain its grand structure.   Although built in the early 18th century, the building has historical implications, as well as holding great academic and artistic value.  In the Museum of the Japanese Invasion of Joseon, visitors can see a miniature of Jeolla Jwasuyeongseong (Jeolla Naval Fortress), which comprised a stronghold from the early Joseon period, a fortress wall, a south gate, an east gate, a government office inside the fortress, civilian housing, an artillery pavilion, a moat, a lake and other features.  There’s also a miniature of Jinnamgwan Hall, a map indicating Yeosu's historical sites related to Admiral Chungmugong Yi Sun-sin, and a miniature ship to show off the inside of Geobukseon (Turtle Ship). You can see what life was like on a ship, from rowing and shooting to eating and sleeping.   Rare photos showing old Jinnamgwan Hall and a miniature of a steel chain defense system recorded in Nan-jung-il-gi (War Diary of Admiral Yi Sun-sin), and Nan-jung-il-gi itself, which is a national treasure. Copies of the Admiral's letters are always on display.

stories.title: Maritime & Fisheries Science Museum
stories.script: The Maritime & Fisheries Science Museum opened in May 1998 to spark teenage interest in maritime exploration, fisheries, and the importance of the ocean.   There’s lots to see, including rare local aquarium fish from the South Sea and different marine organisms that can practically be touched. The museum preserves and passes on the legacy of the maritime and fisheries culture and serves as a living education center.   Of particular interest to high school students are the exhibition of seasonal local aquarium fish and colorful subtropical fish, as well as experiential programs where participants can touch marine organisms living in tidal flats.  Observe the colors and shapes of big and small fish swimming freely inside the massive live fish tank, while froinm the robot tank, you can take a look at the agile movement of AI fish.  See the past, present and future of the fishing industry at the Fisheries Industry section in one go. Gain an overview of the development and evolution of traditional fishing and the equipment used in modern fishing. A miniature vessel reveals the structure of a fishing trawler and how fishing works in reality.   The Fishing Reef Learning Center is an apartment-like ecosystem with a variety of artificial fishing reefs installed in the ocean to enable fish, seaweed, kelp, abalone, conch, and other forms of marine life to live in harmony. A life-size fishing reef is currently on display here as well.

stories.title: Hyangiram Hermitage
stories.script: Hyangiram Hermitage in Dolsan-eup, Yeosu, is located at the tip of a rock. Directly overlooking a cliff, it is the perfect place to see the sunrise from the east-facing stairs.  Because of the rugged precipice with rocks of fantastic shapes populated by Camellia trees and subtropical plants and the surrounding turtle shell-shaped and hexagonal rocks, the hermitage was called Geumoam Hermitage and Yeongguam Hermitage in the past.  With its reputation of being the best place to watch the sunrise, the Hermitage is the location of the Hyangiram Hermitage Sunrise Festival between December 31 and January 1 every year. As one of Korea's four Avalokitesvara prayer sites, legend has it that if a person making a wish here passes through seven rock gates, Avalokitesvara Guan Yin (the Buddhist goddess of mercy) will make one wish come true.   The rock itself looks like a turtle heading to the underwater palace of the Dragon King with Hyangiram Hermitage on its back. Legend also has it that an underwater palace exists somewhere in the imaginary triangle connecting Hyangiram Hermitage, Boriam Hermitage in Namhae and Sejondo Island.  One folk story says that one of the rocks facing the front yard of Daeungbojeon Hall was formed when Wonhyo, a Korean Buddhist philosopher, threw away the Tripitaka as he was leaving the Hermitage because the woven sack he had was too heavy. After the Tripitaka fell into the ocean, it soared out and turned into a rock. Inside Daeungbojeon Hall, Avalokitesvara Guan Yin and Ksitigarbha stand on the right and left side of the Buddha.  You can see the tree of love, the entangled roots of Machilus thunbergii S. et Z. and a Camellia tree, which legend tells us that couples who vow their love while looking at Gwaneumjeon Hall and the Sea Avalokitesvara Guan Yin will be together forever.   Take in the marvelous views of the ocean while looking around Wonhyo's Jwaseondae (where he used to sit in meditation), Cheonsugwaneumjeon Hall and Samseonggak Pavilion.

stories.title: Fisheries Market
stories.script: Yeosu Fisheries Market in Gyo-dong, Yeosu opened as a concrete two-story building in 1968. Modernization in 2011 resulted in a cleaner location that is both a traditional and modern market.   Besides live, fresh and dried fish and shellfish, the market also sells other marine products, fresh produce and local delicacies from Yeosu, such as kimchi and salted seafood. Fish not easily found at fish markets in Seoul and its surrounding can be found here, such as cubed snailfish, rockfish and raw Spanish mackerel.   The market is largely divided into live marine produce and dried marine produce sections and food stalls. To ensure freshness and safety, a 400-meter aquatic pipe running from the ocean towards Janggundo Island supplies purified, clean ocean water to every tenant in the live fish section.  The dried fish sold here is processed and dried in the sun and sea breezes at a rooftop processing center. Fishery products available for customers to taste include raw fish, octopus, sea squirt and blue crab, among others, on the first floor. Those products chosen can be eaten in the restaurant on the second floor.

stories.title: Dolsan Daegyo Bridge
stories.script: Dolsan Daegyo Bridge, running between Namsan-dong, Yeosu and Udu-ri, is a cable-stayed bridge 450m long, 11.7m wide and 62m high. Completed on December 15, 1984, it connects Dolsando Island and Yeosu Peninsula, just as Geobukseon Daegyo Bridge does.  Installed on either side are 62m tall piers to accommodate large ships entering Yeosu Port. Twenty-eight steel cables specially constructed and 56~58mm in diameter support the weight of the bridge.    Dolsan Daegyo Bridge has made it possible to increase the distribution of local agricultural products from Dolsando Island, such as got-gimchi which has become Yeosu's leading local product.  The Bridge also made Dolsando Island part of the mainland, resulting in the appearance of many tourist attractions, as well as hotels, cafes and cable cars, making Dolsando a popular tourist destination.   On Janggundo Island, which you will see while crossing Dolsan Daegyo Bridge, there used to be a stone fortress built by Joseon General Yi Ryang with piles of stones from Dolsando Island and Janggundo Island to defend the area from Japanese pirate raids. The huge stones that used to make up the fortress can still be seen there.   Dolsan Park overlooks the beautiful port of Yeosu, while at sunset, one can see Dolsan Daegyo Bridge overlooking the night sea, and Janggundo Island.

stories.title: Yeosu City Hall
stories.script: Yeosu City Hall in Hakdong, Yeosu, was established to promote democratic principles and efficiency in administration and provide public services to promote regional growth and public welfare.   The Administrative Support Division is responsible for general affairs, accounting, sports, tax administration, tax collection and handling of public complaints; the Planning & Economic Affairs Division is responsible for planning, industrial assistance, information & communications, investment expos, census and job creation; the Tourism & Cultural Education Division is responsible for tourism, culture, education and the city library; the Environment & Welfare Division is responsible for social welfare, the elderly and those with disabilities, women & family, climate & ecosystems and city sanitation; the Green Marine Division handles fishing production, marine management, marine port leisure, exploration of island resources and forestry; the Construction & Traffic Division is responsible for urban planning, construction, roads and traffic.  Other organizations within the City Hall handle administrative work for healthcare and agriculture.    On April 1, 1998, Yeosu merged with Yeocheon-si and Yeocheon-gun, which was the first such merger in the nation after a resident proposal. The city and its residents hosted a welcome event for a BIE feasibility study group for the World Expo in April 2007. Then in 2012, the Yeosu International Expo took place, topping off efforts to raise international awareness of the city, which included inviting staff from foreign embassies and foreign press to hosting international symposiums.    Yeosu’s administrative district is comprised of 1 eup, 6 myeon and 20 dong while the organizational structure consists of a mayor, a vice mayor, 6 divisions in the headquarters, the city council secretariat, 2 organizations affiliated with the city hall, the main office and branches.      Yeosu is currently implementing its key strategy, which includes shifting its tourism policy towards people, expanding its high-level sustainable marine tourism infrastructure, creating a city regeneration ecosystem that involves revitalizing areas far from the city center, etc.

stories.title: Hwayang Jobal Daegyo Bridge
stories.script: Hwayang Jobal Daegyo Bridge in Hwayangmyeon and Hwajeongmyeon, Yeosu is a cable-stayed bridge connecting Jangsu-ri, Hwayangmyeon to Jobal-do, Hwajeongmyeon and is the first large bridge from Hwayangmyeon to Goheung.   This concrete bridge has two diamond-shaped bridge towers and is a world-class structure built with Korean technology. The bridge is 170m tall, 854m long and 11.5 m wide, while the longest span width is 500 m. Construction began on November 12, 2011 and the bridge officially opened on February 28, 2020. The bridge was built according to the vision, Opening the way to the island’s future to build friendship with good people.  Jobaldo Island, the first island you will see coming off of the Bridge is so named because the sun shines over the village as it rises early in the morning. The island was originally called “Bbidduli,” meaning “uneven” or “crooked,” as no flat ground could be found on its horseback-like shape, and its patches of paddies and houses located on the slopes. On Jeongwol Daeboreum (first full moon of the new year), the Island holds Dangsanje (a village ritual to worship the village gods and pray for peace and prosperity), where the host of the ritual should abide by difficult rules, including avoiding all pork and other meat, not attending funerals or weddings, avoiding places with fires and places where people fight. The host is also not to intervene in village affairs or the personal matters of others. A shrine can be found in the upper part of the village and keeps the ancestral tablets.  There is a fire beacon communication system reportedly built by Admiral Yi Sun-Sin at Yomaksan Mountain on the island. Residents engage in both agriculture and fishing, with marine products in the region including anchovy, eel, and octopus.

stories.title: Jobal Haeoreum Hill
stories.script: Jobal Haeoreum Hill, 2,314m2 of land located at the center of Jobaldo Island, has four land-to-island and island-to-island bridges between Yeosu and Goheung.   Haeoreum Tower, a symbolic structure on the hill, is an embodiment of the sun rising over Jobaldo Island and the sunset at Yeojaman, Yeosu's blue sea. Here, a rooftop observatory and barrier-free decked paths welcome visitors.    “Seomseom Yeosu Healing Center The Seom” has a rest area and tourist information center. The Seom, made up of multi-purpose tourism facilities, is visited by many tourists for its agri-fishery stores, souvenir shop, cafeteria, and VR Experience Zone.   Natural brown rock seaweed from Geomundo Island, cutlassfish, Japanese Spanish mackerel, mussel and marine plants are sold in the Fisheries Corner, while pesticide-free barley grass grown under Yeosu's sea breezes and makgeolli (Korean rice wine) from Nangdo Island and Geumodo Island are sold in the Agri-products Corner.    Try some seasonal food, such as seafood-flavored ramen, sausage with rice cake, or a dessert such as handmade oranda snack and sweet pumpkin sikhye (sweet rice drink). At The Seom VR Experiencel Zone, view 10 awesome beautiful locations of Yeosu in virtual reality. Five-minute panoramic videos from a hot-air balloon, a rollercoaster, and a drone can also be seen. Reservations can be made for individual activities through the OK Integrated Reservation System on the Yeosu City Hall website.

stories.title: Dunbyeong Daegyo Bridge
stories.script: Dunbyeong Daegyo Bridge connects Jobaldo and Dunbyeongdo in Hwajeongmyeon, Yeosu. The bridge is a regional symbol where travelers can see the islands in Yeojaman and the rising sun in Jobal. It also showcases the beauty of its curves, magnificent exterior and impressive structure with creative and harmonious asymmetric line angles that make up a cable-stayed bridge.   With two lanes, the bridge is 990m tall and has a breadth and width of 12.05m and 11.5m, respectively. Officially opened in February of 2020, it is the first bridge in the world that includes a three-dimensional tower that curves back like a bow.   Some say that the island is called “Dunbyeongdo” because naval forces temporarily stayed on the island during the Imjin War, while others believe that it is named after a deep puddle in the sea in front of the island.  The largest number of clam remains from Korea’s Three Kingdoms period is found here. The 300m tall costal hill on the southwest coast is a popular view.  The highest peak on the island is 114m high, while the village and farming areas are evenly distributed across the region thanks to gradual sloping on the four sides of the northwest area. The coast runs 7.13 km while the island itself is 0.8 km2. The main occupational activities are farming and fishing.

stories.title: Nangdo Deagyo Bridge
stories.script: Officially opened in February 2020, the bridge connects the islands of Dunbyeongdo and Nangdo in Hwajeongmyeon, Yeosu. The distance between each bridge pillar is 170m, the widest in the nation, while the two-lane bridge itself, with a PSC box girder structure, runs 640m and is 12.5m wide. With its rhythmical scenery, the bridge’s open views ensure that magnificent views of Dadohae can be seen from the driver's side.   Nangdo Island, the top tourist destination in South Jeolla Province, is named “Nangdo” after the Chinese character pronounced nang, thanks to its wolf-shaped geographical features. On the east side is 280m-tall Sangsan Mountain, but most of the island is low-lying flat plain. Along its 19.5-km-long coast are small bays and capes. The island itself is 5.02 km2 in area.   Nangdo Island’s tourism resources include a dinosaur fossil site, amazing views from its coast, and intangible cultural heritages, such as Dangje (village ritual held to pray for good health and prosperity). Typical natural landscapes found in this area include sea cliffs and sandy beaches, fossilized dinosaur footprints, columnar joints, and stratified sedimentary rocks.  More than half of the residents of a large village on the central southern coast work in farming. Major agricultural products include potatoes, sweet potatoes, barley, rice, radish and garlic. The main fishery products include gray mullet, anchovy and eel. Every January 15th on the lunar calendar, the island hosts the Dangsanje ritual.

stories.title: Jeokgeum Daegyo Bridge
stories.script: Jeokgeum Daegyo Bridge connects Nangdo and Jeokgeumdo in Hwajeongmyeon. Made up of 6 sections, an orange metal arch spans both sides of the third and fourth sections. The two-lane bridge is 470m long, 12.5m wide and has, at most, 130m between its bridge pillars. Construction was completed in December 2019 and it officially opened on February 28, 2020.   In consideration of the harmony of the islands in Dadohae and the surrounding panorama, it was built with a half-through arch, which supports plates in the center of its span. Other arch bridges include upper-through and bottom-through.   Due to their aesthetics, arch bridges have been appreciated throughout history and built with stone since the ancient Roman Empire.   Jeokgeumdo Island, which appears once you’ve passed through the bridge, was known as “Jeokho” in the Joseon period, but was renamed with the Chinese characters “Jeok” and “Geum,” meaning “piles of gold” because gold deposits were found here and a mine built.
