Pebbles on the beach form Mongdol (pebble) Beach. The island has quite a bit of arable land considering its size because the entire island is a flat plain. The major sources of income for the village are from marine plants, short-necked clams and fishery products. Nangdo, Dunbyeongdo, Sanggwado, Hagwado, Odo, Maeseom, Sodangdo and other islands are also located in close proximity.

stories.title: Palyeong Daegyo Bridge
stories.script: Palyeong Daegyo Bridge connects Hwajeongmyeon, Yeosu with Yeongnammyeon, Goheung County and is the 11th and final bridge in the island-to-mainland construction project between Yeosu and Goheung. It is the first gateway to Yeosu from Goheung and given its symbolic value as such, it is an earth-anchored suspension bridge connecting the two regions.   The two-laned bridge is 1,340m long and 13m wide, with 850m between the pillars—the longest in Korea at the time of construction.   The bridge tower is 138m tall and is designed as a suspension bridge. Construction began in November 2004 and took 12 years before its official opening on December 27, 2016.   The bridge is dubbed steel-made harp because it is harp-shaped. Suspension bridges require technological prowess, and Korea became the 6th country in the world to build its own suspension bridges.  First and foremost, a bridge should be durable enough to withstand typhoons and earthquakes. Second, since a bridge can shorten by 2~3m with changing temperatures, the elasticity of the steel should be exceptional. Third, the steel should not easily corrode in salt air. Fourth, since the steel should not corrode easily in the salt air, high carbon steel should be used and the surface should be coated with special paint. Fifth, the most appropriate location must be decided in the design stage, and details on the millions of rivets and parts as well.

stories.title: Jeokgeum Park
stories.script: Jeokgeum Park in Jeokgeum-ri, Hwajeong-myeon, Yeosu has been developed as a tourism project to publicize 65 beautiful islands in Yeosu. It is the sea dotted with islands stretching the 39 km-distance between Yeosu and Goheung.    “100-ri seom-gil” (39 km island path) refers to the area comprised of Hwatae Daegyo Bridge in Shinbok-ri, Dolsan-eup, Yeosu, South Jeolla Province, and Wolho Daegyo Bridge connecting Hwataedo and Wolhodo, Gaedo Daegyo Bridge connecting Wolhodo and Gaedo, Jedo Daegyo Bridge connecting Gaedo and Jedo, Hwajeong Daegyo Bridge connecting Jedo and Baekyado, Baekya Daegyo Bridge connecting Baekyado and Hwayangmyeon, Hwayang Jobal Daegyo Bridge connecting Hwayangmyeon and Jobaldo, Dunbyeong Daegyo Bridge connecting Jobaldo and Dunbyeongdo, Nangdo Daegyo Bridge connecting Dunbyeongdo and Nangdo, Jeokgeum Daegyo Bridge connecting Nangdo and Jeokgeumdo, and Palyeong Daegyo Bridge connecting Jeokgeumdo and Yeongnammyeon, Goheung County.   There is a Dangjip (shrine house) where a guardian tree for the village and deity are kept in the center of the park, which leads to the beginning of the 39 km-long island path. “Dangsan” refers to a village ritual held to ask the village gods for peace and prosperity.   Time-honored folk religions can be found on the islands, which have to do with the sea. Twelve dangje (village rituals), Jeokgeumdo folk festivals, are unique in that villagers pick a place for worship and play traditional Korean percussion music in different melodies for grand dangsan, small dangsan and festivals in huge spaces around a bridge, in barley fields, on large roads, at lands’ end, nal-dang-san, stand-alone island, and for rituals to the underwater king.   Jeokgeum Park has photo zones where visitors can take pictures of the beautiful scenery of Yeosu during their tour of Dadohaehaesang National Park and the 39 km-long island path.

stories.title: Gasari Eco Park
stories.script: Gwangi Dyke Reservoir in Gasari Eco Park is an ecological treasure. Located in the south part of Hwayang Peninsula, the reservoir leads to Yeojaman. Tidal flats in Yeojaman remain intact, serving as a habitat for a variety of living things and the place is especially known for the beauty of the sunrise reflecting on the flats themselves.   “Ga” and “Sa” in the “Gasari” refer to “beauty” and “sand,” respectively. With the establishment of a Japanese company, Gorwae Farm, during Japanese colonial rule, a 764m-long dyke was built in 1922 to protect 24.8 million m2 of rice paddies.   Enjoy the views of a quiet, peaceful fishing village and the islands which seem to be floating in the blue ocean of Dadohae beyond the stretch of tidal flats. This is the point where the sea meets the sky and spacious wetland is formed.    Looking at Yeojaman from the dyke, you can see Undudo nearby and Soyeojado and Daeyeojado further away. Take a stroll along the center of a reed “forest” even in the evening, thanks to the lighted decks and hear the sounds of migratory birds.  Rent a bicycle at nearby Gasari Eco Learning Center and enjoy the view of the sun going down as you cycle.   Gasari Eco Park Wetlands have been designated “Level 1,” which means they are of great value and must be preserved in accordance with the findings of district research conducted by the National Wetland Center in 2015. The wetlands are packed with reeds and are homme to many different wetland plants, amphibians, and birds.

stories.title: Seoteulleo Succulent Botanical Garden
stories.script: Seoteulleo Succulent Botanical Garden in Soramyeon, Yeosu, is located on the way to Gasari Eco Park. Currently designated as Yeosu’s farming education center, it provides many unique educational programs that enable independent study linked to any school curriculum.    “Succulent” refers to a plant which stores water in its leaves to adapt to dry or sandy environments. This Garden is touted as the world’s best of its kind because it showcases 60,000 succulent plant species and Korean orostachys japonicus against the backdrop of Yeosu’s golden fields, living up to its theme of “Communication between Soil, People and Nature.” A popular destination for “relaxation tourism,” visitors can also try some anion-therapy all year-round as the Garden is in a greenhouse complex.     In the Pottery Center, visitors can make their own flowerpots and other clayware and plant succulent plants after learning about the Center’s theme of “Soil and Nature.”      Traditional cultural activities, such as straw bag-weaving, rice threshing and sweet potato picking are also available.    As a social enterprise, Seoteulleo Succulent Botanical Garden provides jobs for the vulnerable and works to accomplish other social objectives.

stories.title: Chungminsa Temple
stories.script: Chungmansa is a shrine built by Yi Si-eon, naval commander of the three provinces, to commemorate Admiral Yi Sun-sin in accordance with the King’s order to do so following Chief State Councillor, Yi Hang-bok's proposal submitted in 1601. It was Korea's first shrine to receive a plaque from the King and precedes Hyeongchungsa Temple in Asan and Chungryeolsa Temple in Tongyeong.   The shrine puts the Admiral in the middle while Uimingong Yi Eok-gi and Jwachanseong Ahn Hong-guk are placed on the right and left, respectively. In 1709, the 35th year of King Sukjong’s reign, Yi Bong-Sang, a 5th-generation descendant of the Admiral, overhauled the site to look more like a shrine, which was inherited by Yi Myeong-Sang in 1732, the 8th year of King Yeongjo’s reign.     In 1870, the 7th year of King Gojong’s reign, all but the Chungmindang building was demolished and after that, ancestral rites to the Admiral were held at Seokcheonsa Temple, which was located next to the shrine. A shrine reconstruction project begun by a group of Confucian scholars in Yeosu in 1971, under the Five-year Purification Project, was completed in 1978 to look as it does now.   The small shrine faces south and its low walls are enclosed by other low walls. On the southwest side of the front yard are cornerstones for the old building while on the south, a new monument has been set up. It is built in the iikgong style (double-wing bracket) with 3 closed sections on the front and 2 closed sections on the side, while the roof is paljak (hip and gabled). The stylobate is 3 sets of foundation stones on top of each other. At the center front are some wide stairs flanked on either side by narrow stairs. The central stairs lead to the shinmun, the entrance gate, and the path is paved with granite stones. The façade has ttisal-mun (belted grid door) surrounded by walls. The entire building is decorated with traditional Korean multi-colored paintwork.

stories.title: Old House of Chungmugong's Mother
stories.script: The Old House of Chungmugong's Mother in Ungcheon-dong, Yeosu, was where Admiral Yi Sun-Sin's mother, his wife, surnamed Bang, and relatives stayed during the Imjin War.   It is in today’s Songhyeon Village, Ungcheon-dong, within Jeolla Jwasuyeong (naval base in Jeolla Province). It was originally the house where General Chungjeonggong Jeong Dae-su lived with his widowed mother during the earlier Japanese Invasion of Joseon. Upon his appointment as Sugunjeoldosa (naval commander) Admiral Yi moved his mother here due to its proximity to Jeolla Jwasuyeong, and visited her here. The Admiral’s mother is reported to have stayed here between 1593 and 1597.   During the Imjim War, the house served as a command center for the Admiral, and also served as the place where Admiral Yi could practice filial piety toward his mother.   Yeosu’s city government turned the place into a historic site and designated it as a Yeosu monument. The city also rebuilt the rooms for the Admiral’s mother and wife, and the kitchen showcasing a chest, sabangtakja (tall three- or four-tiered shelf open on all four sides), iron, mirror, samtaegi (a straw basket) and other items used in those days to show visitors today what the times were like. There is also a miniature of the Admiral holding his mother’s hand when he came to visit and see how she was doing.    Around the house are memorial stones for his mother, Ms. Byeon from the Chogye Byeon clan, and the Admiral and historic items used there, including sot (traditional Korean cauldron), stone mortar and a millstone.

stories.title: Heungguksa Temple
stories.script: Heungguksa Temple is a hidden place of Hwaeomsa, which is built on the lotus-shaped mountain peak on the southwest of Yeongchwisan Mountain.   As a place dedicated to praying for the nation's stability and prosperity, the temple notably places patriotism ahead of Buddhist rules.   A bowstring-shaped rainbow bridge built by Monk Gyeteuk in 1693, the 17th year of King Injo's reign, is intricate work, created by stacking up 86 neatly cut foundation stones which stand over the valley on either side, forming a semi-circle. The stones fit tightly together and can sustain the weight of the bridge by themselves.     Around the bridge, small stones seem to have naturally stacked up, but they were placed there to form a column, improving the strength of the rainbow-shaped structure and causing the bridge to stand out. On the handrails on either side, a dragon glares, wishing health for people crossing the bridge. Construction of the rainbow-shaped bridge required very intricate techniques, and the harmony of hand-shaped and naturally shaped stones show off the beauty of traditional Korean construction.      As of 2022, there are a total of 1021 cultural heritage items divided into 227 types in the temple. In addition to these, Heungguksa Temple houses 10 national treasures: Rainbow Bridge, Daeungjeon Hall (main hall of the Buddhist temple), Hubultaeng (Buddhist painting behind the Buddha statue) and wall painting of the Buddhist Goddess of Mercy in Daeungjeon Hall, wooden trinities of the Buddha (Yeorae samjon), 16 Arhat, Nosana Buddhist deities and Suwol-Gwaneum-Do (Avalokitesvara with Water and Moon).

stories.title: Yeosun Incident Memorial Hall
stories.script: Yeosun Incident Memorial Hall, located on Odongdo Island, Yeosu, gives visitors an overview of the incident through indoor exhibitions.   The Memorial Hall was built to propagate the truth of the incident, and allows visitors to easily understand the developments and the public-private endeavors and activities to enact a special act. There are six archives, videos presented in sand art, Remembering the Yeosun Incident in 1948, a photo zone decorated with finger guns by the artist Kim Gyu-hee, a summary of the incident, timelines, related materials and photos, and a masterful painting of the incident, which took the artist, Gang Jong-ryeol, 3 years to complete.   The Yeosun Incident, which followed the Jeju April 3 Incident, was a massacre of civilians that occurred during the process of establishing the Korean government amid the chaos after independence.  The Memorial Hall delivers a message of peace and human rights through reconciliation and harmony to visitors from home and abroad, and serves as a place for our future generations to understand some of Yeosu’s painful history, in stark contrast to the backdrop of camellia flowers on Odongdo Island.

stories.title: Seo Market
stories.script: Seo Market, located in Seogyo-dong, Yeosu, opened in 1934 as a market for Yeosu-eup. It obtained a permanent market license in May 1982.   Begun as a place for barter, where people exchanged rice, barley, beans, grains and firewood for pants, shirts, socks and fish from nearby farming and fishing villages in the 1930s, during Japanese colonial rule. Seo Market later became a traditional five-day market (opening every 5 days).   As Seojeong, the name of the place during Japanese colonial rule changed to Seogyo-dong upon independence and administrative district restructuring, the place became known as Seo Market. As of 2022, 560 shops and street stalls call this place—Yeosu's largest traditional market—home.   Among the popular locations in the market is an alley where deokyang gopchang-jeongol (beef tripe hot pot), meorigogi (slices of head meat) and jokbal (pig's trotters) are sold. This is indeed a place of delicacies, with restaurants serving traditional dishes such as raw chicken, dakttongjip (chicken gizzard), chicken feet, old-style fried chicken, gopchang (beef tripe), meorigogi (slices of head meat), jokbal (pig's trotters) and rice cake. Other shops sell snack foods such as sweet breads, fried food, gimbap, red bean porridge with small rice cakes, pat-kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup with sweetened red beans), desserts and tteokbokki.  The food prices here are very affordable.       A variety of clothing, agricultural and fishery products are also available in the market, and small pojang macha (vendor tents) wait to sell you alcohol and food and a place to enjoy it. The five-day market held every 4th and 9th day of the month is especially charming, with the typical hustle and bustle of a traditional market.

stories.title: Post of the 14th Regiment
stories.script: The Post of 14th Regiment in Sinwol-dong, Yeosu, is where the camp for the 14th army regiment used to be.   Originally, there were three villages called Bongyang, Mulgimi and Shingeunjeong which were formed by the Japanese Navy when they forced people to move here to manufacture military supplies and build Navy 202 barracks due to the geographical features of Gamakman in front of Gubongsan Mountain in 1942, when the Pacific War was in full swing.   The Japanese mobilized civilians and students in the eastern part of South Jeolla Province and named their unit “Geunro Bogukdae” (National Unit) and forced them to work in shifts. Construction of the necessary structures was 90% complete by the time Korea gained independence. However, with the defeat of Japan, the U.S. military government took over the camp with its empty barracks and hangars.   On May 4, 1948, the National Police formed the 14th Regiment with recruits and a battalion it detached from Gwangju's 4th Regiment. The Yeosun Incident began when staff sergeants defied orders to crack down on the civilians during the Jeju April 3 incident and killed some commissioned officers on October 19, 1948.   A couple years later, the Korean War broke out in 1950, and the armed forces completely withdrew on July 25. The 15th Military Hospital was here from December 31, 1952 to July 27, 1953 while from June 26, 1962 to February 20, 1976, the place was designated a rehabilitation center for tuberculosis patients. Since September 23, 1976, Hanhwa's Yeosu Plant has been operating here. The place is etched with the great pain and suffering of Korea's modern history.

stories.title: Site where Reverend Son Yang-won was martyred
stories.audioTitle: Site where Reverend Son Yang-won was martyred
stories.script: This is the site of a former orchard where Reverend Son Yang-won of Yeosu's Aeyangwon (shelter for lepers) was shot and killed on September 28, 1950, the year the Korean War broke out, after being arrested by the North Korean communists.   Born in Haman, South Gyeongsang Province in 1902, Reverend Son graduated from Pyeongyang School of Theology. In 1939, he was appointed reverend in charge of Yeosu's Aeyangwon to take care of the lepers and continued his missionary work there.   Reverend Son stayed in Aeyangwon until the end, insisting that he could not abandon the patients, even at a time when everyone was fleeing from the North Korean army marching into Jeolla Province, after the Korean War began in 1950.  The patients begged the Reverend to leave them behind because the Communists wouldn’t kill them, but he stayed and was arrested by the occupying North Koreans for being a Christian missionary. Even while detained with others, he would choose the smallest riceball for himself and share it with the person in the room who needed it most, saying that it was his habit to eat very little. After brutal torture, he was shot and killed with other inmates at the age of 49 on September 28, 1950.   His tomb is near the Memorial Hall, which also has a small garden built in his memory. He received the Aejokjang (Independence Medal) posthumously in 1995.

stories.title: Site of the Manseong-ri Massacre
stories.script: This site, located in Manheung-dong, Yeosu, is where hundreds of civilians, detained in the former Jongsan Elementary School, now called Jungang Elementary School, were sentenced to death for alleged collaboration with the Communists. The killings of many of those sentenced to death occurred in mid-November 1948, and the bodies were buried in valleys under mud, sand and stones.  The military stayed at Yeosu’s Jongsan Elementary School while the police helped them identify those civilians accused of aiding the Communists.   According to eyewitness accounts, for two days (November 13-14, 1948), after the 5th military tribunal sentenced 280 of the 506 arrested to death, 88 in all were killed.  Shootings and screaming lingered from continued massacre in the valley, which was filled with people transported from Jongsan Elementary School with their hands tied in rope. For this reason, residents in Manseong and Ocheon traveling to the city center detoured around Maraesan Mountain, rather than taking the shortcut, as it had become the land of horror.  Following the Yeosun Incident, people passing by threw small pebbles into the valley to pay tribute to the innocent, or piled up a stone tower to pay their respects. Currently, there is a commemorative tower built in 2009 for the victims of the incident.

stories.title: Night View of the National Industrial Complex
stories.audioTitle: Night View of the National Industrial Complex
stories.script: Yeosu National Industrial Complex, in Jungheung-dong, Yeosu, was established in 1967 as the nation's largest heavy and chemical industrial complex for refined oil, fertilizer and petrochemicals.   The complex continues to contribute to national economic growth through industrial development and is laying the foundation for continued growth of the national and regional economies.   Home to around 300 businesses as of 2022, Yeosu National Industrial Complex is the nation's largest heavy and chemical industrial complex.   As of 2022, GS Caltex produces 26% of the nation’s refined oil and 47% of its ethylene for petrochemical use, while Namhae Chemical Corp. manufactures 33% of the total domestic output of fertilizer.   The Complex also accommodates shipping at 36 berths at 18 port points. Because products manufactured at the Complex need to be maintained at high pressures and temperatures at all times, the plants run 24/7 all year-round except during complex-wide maintenance periods.  Tens of thousands of lights installed for safety and operation of huge machinery create a golden hue of little diamonds, making for amazing night views.

stories.title: Dolsan Park
stories.script: Facing Dolsandaegyo Bridge, Dolsan Park was built in 1987.   At Dolsan Park, you can see Yeosu Port, Ria coast, Dadohae, meaning “sea with many islands,” and South Gyeongsang Province’s portion of Namhae (“South Sea”).   In 2000, a tower depicting the dynamic movement of fishermen pulling a fishnet was erected to mark completion of the construction while in 2002, a park for the fishing village and a commemorative tower were built to pay tribute to the fishermen who died working in rough seas.   At the top of the park center, a time capsule was placed of a variety of items related to integration of Yeosu, Yeocheon and Dolsan counties in 1994. The capsule will be opened on April 1, 2098, marking the centenary of the integration.    Take a ride on a cable car at the Yeosu Marine Cable Car Station in Dolsan Park for magnificent night views of Dolsandaegyo Bridge and Janggundo Island.   The lights over Dolsandaegyo Bridge shine in multiple colors at night and in harmony with the beautiful light over Janggundo Island, together brightening Yeosu's night sea.

stories.title: Dolsangat Kimchi Street
stories.script: Dolsangat Kimchi Street is where visitors can experience the flavor of Yeosu dolsangat kimchi from ingredients cultivated in the warm oceanic climate and alkaline soil.   In Yeosu, where it's rare for the temperature to fall below zero in winter, the nutrient-rich sea breeze and warm sun soften the fiber of mustard greens and give dolsangat kimchi a crispy texture that sets it apart from other kimchi. The mustard greens grown in the salty sea breeze, red clay, and mild climate are sometimes referred to as bomdonggat in spring, kimchigat in summer, and gimjanggat in winter.  Unlike red mustard, there are no fine hairs on soft and tender dolsangat. It is a green vegetable that can slow down aging with the antioxidant properties of vitamins A and C, beta-carotene, phenolic compound, and chlorophyll.   The main ingredient of dolsangat kimchi is mustard greens, which are mixed with a seasoning of chili powder, garlic, ginger, anchovy sauce, and shrimp ground up together. The hotness of the mustard and the pungency of the fermented fish sauce stimulates the appetite—once you’ve tried some, you’ll find yourself coming back for more!  It is also said that dolsangat kimchi supports bone growth, improves vision, stops coughing, regulates energy, warms the body, and prevents palsy of the head and face.  As a chemical-free natural food full of calcium and iron, this Yeosu specialty is known to prevent chronic disease and pernicious anemia while also improving constitution. Order this pride of Yeosu online from anywhere in the world.

stories.title: Guk-dong Fishing Port Complex
stories.script: Guk-dong Port enjoys the natural topography of several islands that block the waves and winds—ideal for a fishing port.   Designated a National Port in January 1979, Guk-dong Port is surrounded by fish processing plants and ship repair shops, and has the ice manufacturing, freezing, and refrigeration facilities you would expect from a well-equipped port. In January 2013, it became a multipurpose fishing port.   As a multipurpose fishing port, the Guk-dong Port Complex serves as a base for fishing and fish farming industries. Its status as a National Fishing Port means it’s a nationwide base for the fishing industry. To be designated a National Fishing Port, the port or harbor must be able to accommodate 80 fishing vessels with a total tonnage of at least 200 tons. It must also be accessible to at least 100 foreign fishing vessels a year and located in topographical conditions that allow for evacuation in the event of hazardous weather conditions. The port must also facilitate the hauling of at least 1,000 tons of catch a year.     National Fishing Ports are designated by the Minister of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, and there are 115 nationwide. By region, Jeollanam-do has the most with 126, followed by Gyeongsangnam-do, Gyeongsangbuk-do, and Incheon. Ulsan has the least, with 8 ports.   Trading centers for marine products and key players in regional development, multipurpose fishing ports are contributing to the improvement of fishing incomes through the fishing industry and related tourism.

stories.title: Gyeongdo
stories.script: Gyeongdo, located in Gyeongho-dong, Yeosu, consists of the 3 populated islands of Daegyeongdo, Sogyeongdo, and Yado, and 11 uninhabited islands.   Meaning Whale Island, it is said that Gyeongdo was so named because the island as a whole resembles a whale, but that has changed to mean “Seoul” for one of the king’s concubines who lived there during the late Goryeo period.   Remains of clam piles and patterned earthenware were discovered on Daegyeongdo, which tells us that people have been living there since the Neolithic Era. Dolmen, the main tombs of the bronze period, are scattered here and there, and cave paintings symbolizing fertility and abundance have also been discovered.  Korea's first seaside pension is in business in Gyeongdo, guests of which can take in some sea fishing from a barge.   Another attraction is the Daegyeongdo Golf Course with 27 holes and fantastic views of the beautiful ocean beside Yeosu.   Restaurants at the entrance of the Daegyeongdo wharf sell pike eel shabu-shabu. In the past, pike eels were exported to Japan in their entirety, desired as they were for their flavor and nutrition, but now tourists and Yeosu residents together consume them in the summer as healthy food.   Currently in Gyeongdo, construction on a plot of 2.14 ㎢ is currently underway for a 6-star hotel and resort, a golf course and commercial facilities, and a marine cable car.

stories.title: Turtle Ship Bridge
stories.script: Turtle Ship Bridge connects Jonghwa-dong, Yeosu-si, Jeollanam-do, known as Sujeong-dong today, with Udu-ri, Dolsan-eup. A bridge that connects the venue with Dolsando for the successful hosting of the 2012 Yeosu World Expo and a 17 km-long road from Udu-ri, Dolsan-eup to Jusam-dong in the form of a concrete cable-stayed bridge together make up one section of the National Highway Detour Project.  Turtle Ship Bridge is a first-class bridge with a 90m tower, a 230m span, a 744m bridge extension, a 490m tunnel, and a 706m approach, together running a total of 1.94 ㎞ and supporting 43.2 ton for maximum load.   In particular, it is the ocean where Admiral Yi Sun-sin loaded his Turtle Ships with cannons and test-fired them the day before the Imjin Wars began. Once a place with iron-clad fortifications, it was tentatively named “Dolsan 2 Bridge” but was renamed “Turtle Ship Bridge” to mark the area’s historical significance.   Under Turtle Ship Bridge sits the Hamel Lighthouse, the Hamel Museum, and a marine park. Light fixtures show off the beauty of the nightscape that matches with the night sea.

stories.title: Jongpo Marine Park
stories.script: Located in Jungang-dong, Yeosu city, Jongpo Marine Park was begun in 2001 by the Yeosu Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries and took 5 years to complete. Built as part of Stage 1 of Yeosu Kuhang Maintenance, it was established to both improve the aesthetics of the lighters wharf in Jonghwa-dong Port to the Yeosu Kuhang breakwater where the Hamel Lighthouse is, and to transform Yeosu into a futuristic port city.   Jongpo Marine Park was designed to connect with Yi Sun-sin Square for the 2012 Yeosu World Expo, and city functions were added to its port facilities and surrounding waterfront space to serve as a rest area and cultural center for residents and visitors.   Within the park, a shipyard has been built with a breakwater, a lighters wharf and pier for small boats, and a repair station, along with a bronze statue of Hendrick Hamel (1630-1692) for his connection with Yeosu, the red Hamel Lighthouse, a man-made green space, and an outdoor theater.   In 2016, a romantic pocha street was established within Jongpo Marine Park, but it was moved under Turtle Ship Bridge in 2019 as the number of tourists increased.  Today, many visitors are attracted to the area for its Jongpo Marine Park, which serves as a jewel in the nightscape of Yeosu, Dolsan Bridge, the marine cable car, and Hamel Lighthouse.

stories.title: Aqua Planet
stories.script: Aqua planet is a marine eco-center where a plethora of marine animals can be seen up close.   This eco-center is an environmentally-friendly aquarium run on solar power, with Ocean Life, Marine Life, Aqua Forest and other exhibitions to be experienced on each floor.   Visitors can see large fish that inhabit the Amazon River. The 40 m tunnel tank allows visitors to see the main tank in tunnel form and marine life through a transparent floor underneath them. A total of 55,000 marine animals of 300 different species live here, and research is ongoing on the beluga, green sea turtle and other endangered species.    There has been evidence that the green sea turtle, designated “protected marine wildlife” by the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, has not spawned in Korean waters since 2002 due to a drastic reduction of its spawning grounds and habitats as a result of climate change. As a result of securing a number of these endangered sea turtles and conducting preservation research, Aqua Planet Yeosu was the first to successfully artificially spawn a sea turtle in Korea, and has been releasing sea turtles into the wild since 2016.  Furthermore, having been designated a “habitat conservation and marine wildlife rescue and treatment agency” by the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, Aqua Planet is leading the way in protecting marine wildlife through research on breeding and raising marine animals that are losing their natural habitat.

stories.title: Yeosu Marine Cable Car
stories.script: Connecting Dolsando and Jasan Park over the ocean, Yeosu Marine Cable Car is Korea's first marine cable car, and the fourth in Asia after Hong Kong, Singapore, and Vietnam.   With operations that began in December, 2014, it shuttles back and forth over the 1.5 ㎞ distance between Jasan Park and Dolsan Park. Fifteen “crystal cabins” with transparent floors and 35 regular cabins mean that Yeosu Marine Cable Car has 50 cabins to offer visitors. The crystal cabin is a favorite as riders can take advantage of its reinforced glass cabin for a truly panoramic view of the beautiful sea below.   Islands in the maritime national park, centered around the exhibition venue and Odongdo Island, can be seen from Yeosu Marine Cable Car, along with a view of Turtle Ship Bridge, ocean-going vessels, islands, Yeosu’s cityscape, Hamel Lighthouse, Jasan Park Observatory, and Odongdo. At night, enjoy a different view of the ocean surrounding Yeosu.   Nora Station in Dolsan Park has an observatory from where a 360-degree view of Yeosu and the whole of Dolsando can be seen. Boarding a cable car shortly before dusk means visitors can take in the sunset from the air and enjoy the romantic nightscape of Yeosu.  The cable cars can be boarded from Nora Station at Dolsan Park or Haeya Station at Jasan Park.

stories.title: Yeosu Expo Venue
stories.script: Located in Deokchung-dong, Yeosu, Yeosu Expo Venue is where the 2012 Yeosu World Expo took place over the 93 days from May 12 to August 12, 2012, themed as The Living Ocean and Coast.   The 2012 Yeosu Expo Memorial Hall exhibits content regarding the history of the world expo, commemoration of the 2012 Expo, stop motion shows, tidal and wind power, and marine technology.  The Big-O Show is a special facility in the Expo venue that involves water fountains, fog and pyrotechnics, lasers, and lights. The marine fountain show, dancing to the mellow tunes of classical music and jazz, is the world's largest.   The Hana Show teaches us, through a boy named “Hana” who lives in the island archipelago in the blue ocean around Yeosu, that we can choose to preserve and live in harmony with the beautiful living ocean. The Monkey Show also shows visitors the playful talents of Monkey through octopuses, which are important products of Yeosu.  The Yeosu Expo Venue is a great place for a walk through the waterfront park, and also houses the Convention Center and Aqua Planet. A variety of experiences are also available at the Eye Museum, which utilizes the venue facilities, along with restaurants and cafés.

stories.title: Hamel Exhibition Hall
stories.script: The Hamel Exhibition Hall located within Jongpo Marine Park in Yeosu, was built to commemorate the Dutch merchant, Hendrick Hamel.   Known for Hamel's Journal, the Dutchman Hendrick Hamel and his companions recorded their 13 years in Joseon (the previous name for Korea) from when they arrived in 1653 to how some of them left in 1666. The traces they left behind were collected and a related exhibition hall opened on October 4, 2012 on the site where they departed the country.   Hamel's Journal was written to the East India Company to explain that he had drifted to Jejudo during a storm and was detained, but was able to escape to his home country after being sent to Yeosu. His Journal had been written as proof of his experience and to ask for the wages he had not received while detained in Joseon.  Exhibition Hall 1, “Remembrance,” shows Hamel's life and his Journal entries during his 13 years in Joseon.    In Exhibition Hall 2, “Return,” the difference between 17th-century Joseon and the Netherlands can be seen. It shows the historical background of Joseon, which was working to better defend itself after enduring the Japanese invasion and crisis, and of the Netherlands, which was in its golden age of maritime trade. A miniature model of the Sperwer (“Sparrowhawk”), the Dutch merchant ship Hamel and his crew worked on, is also exhibited.   Exhibition Hall 3, “Realization,” introduces Hamel's Journal. Exhibition Hall 4, “Vision” shows the past, present, and future of Yeosu.

stories.title: A brief introduction to the island tour of Geomundo, Geumodo, Sanghwado, and Hahwado from Yeosu Passenger Terminal
stories.audioTitle: A brief introduction to the island tour of Geomundo, Geumodo, Sanghwado, and Hahwado from Yeosu Passenger Terminal
stories.script: Yeosu Passenger Terminal is the gateway to safe transport of passengers and cargo to the coastal islands, and also runs passenger ferries to Geomundo, Geumodo, Sanghwado, Hahwado, Sado, Nangdo, Gaedo, Yeondo, and Sonjukdo.   Geomundo, part of Samsan-myeon, Yeosu, is the southernmost island between Yeosu and Jejudo. Geumodo, Nam-myeon, Yeosu is part of the Geumodo district of Dadohae Maritime National Park, comprised of 32 districts, and is also named “Golden Turtle” for its resemblance to a turtle. The Geumodo Cliff Walk currently consists of 5 routes totaling 18.5 km and takes place in nature along a seashore cliff.   Sado and Chudo are located within Nangdo-ri, Hwajeong-myeon. Sado is the site where fossilized dinosaur footprints from the Cretaceous period of the Mesozoic Era were discovered in December 2000 and designated as natural monuments. Chudo holds the remains of an 85m trail of dinosaur footprints.   Gaedo, part of Hwajeong-myeon, was attached to Jeolla Jwasuyeong during the Joseon period and played an important part in war as war horses were raised here.   Yeondo, part of Nam-myeon, is so named for its resemblance to a kite. Sonjukdo, Samsan-myeon, is where Joseon General Lee Daewon was killed in battle. The island was called Sondaedo after his death in reference to the loss of an important figure. It was later renamed Sonjukdo.

stories.title: Hyangiram Trail
stories.script: The Romance Bus of Yeosu, Hyangiram Trail is a city tour that goes through Odongdo, Jinnamgwan, Hyangiram, and the fish market, making for a comfortable view of the beauty of Yeosu.   In Odongdo, follow the breakwater with a guide to Barefoot Park, Bamboo Tunnel, and go to the observatory to view the dark blue ocean. The whole island is a habitat for royal foxglove, green bamboo, silver magnolia and other trees.   Jinnamgwan is a National Treasure and the largest single-story wooden government office still surviving to this day. Together with Jeolla Jwasuyeong and the Navy Headquarters of the Three Provinces during the Imjin Wars, it helped lead the way to victory. Namhae (the South Sea) can be seen from Museulmok Beach, and makes for a great photo background.  On the trail to Hyangiram, fields of green mustard and farms create a warm background. The boulders of Hyangiram look like statues of turtles and create a peculiar sight.     Fishery products of all kinds can be seen at the Yeosu fish market. Separated by a road between them, Yeosu Fish Market and Fishery Specialty Market is where fresh live fish, dolsangat kimchi, and Yeosu specialties can be purchased.

stories.title: Bridge Route
stories.script: Eleven bridges will soon connect Yeosu and Goheung. The Romance Bus Bridge Tour takes visitors on a safe, comfortable trip to 5 of them opened on February 28, 2020—Hwayangjobal Bridge, Dunbyeong Bridge, Nangdo Bridge, Jeokgeum Bridge, and Palyeong Bridge.   Beginning from Expo Station in the morning, the tour takes you through Soho Dongdong Bridge, the 5 bridges, and Gasa-ri Ecological Park before returning to Expo Station.   If all completed by 2028 as planned, the 11 bridges will connect Hwatae to Baegya, Dolsan-eup, Yeosu all the way to Yeongnam-myeon, Goheung, as part of a world-class maritime tourism belt that resembles a bridge museum through majestic spans and sparkling islands.    Soho Dongdong Bridge is a 742m trail above the sea. The coastal scenery of Gamak Bay, camellia flowers and guitar photo zones make for beautiful pictures.     Hwayangjobal Bridge is a land bridge that connects Jangsu-ri, Hwayang-myeon to Jobaldo, Hwajeong-myeon. Dunbyeong Bridge connects Jobaldo to Dunbyeongdo, Hwajeong-myeon. Nangdo Bridge is a PSC box girder bridge that connects Dunbyeongdo, Hwajeong-myeon, to Nangdo. Jeokgeum Bridge connects Nangdo to Jeokgeum-ri, Hwajeong-myeon, and is a half-through, orange arch bridge that connects Pier 3 and 4 (of 6 piers).   A tranquil fishing village and the Dadohae islands on the vast indigo sea can be seen from Gasa-ri Ecological Park. A large field of reeds and an observation deck make it perfect for memorable sunsets.

stories.title: Yi Sun-sin Culture Tour of Historical Sites
stories.audioTitle: Yi Sun-sin Culture Tour of Historical Sites
stories.script: The Historical Culture City Tour starts from Expo Station and visits Chungminsa, Jinnamgwan, Gosodae, Yi Sun-sin Square, the house where the admiral's mother lived, Yeosu Seonso, and Heungguksa, before returning to Expo Station.   In Yeosu, traces of Yi Sun-sin, who led the way to victory during the Imjin Wars, have been gathered together as cultural sites.   Chungminsa, Korea's first shrine to honor Admiral Yi Sun-sin, consists of an artifact exhibition and shrines for holding rites in the spring and autumn.   Jinnamgwan is a National Treasure, and Jinhaeru, Jeolla Jwasuyeong headquarters, was where Japanese forces from the south were defeated, bringing peace to the nation. It is now Korea's largest wooden structure and serves as an inn.   The Monument for the Naval Victories of Yi Sun-sin in Gosodae is the largest monuments in Korea. There is also Tarubi Monument (taru meaning tears) was built by the Admiral's men to commemorate the victories of this great military leader in 1603, 6 years after his death.   The house where the admiral's mother and wife lived is in Songhyeon village (within Jeolla Jwasuyeong) where her relatives also lived. They were moved there in 1593 to escape the fighting.  Heungguksa, a holy site for the patriotic Buddhism of Admiral Yi, was built in 1195 by the national priest Jinul during the 25th year of the reign of Goryeo’s King Myeongjong. Preserved in the exhibition are the blood-stained robes of the monks who went into battle without armor, along with their weapons.

stories.title: Yeosun Incident Dark Tourism
stories.script: Yeosun Incident Dark Tourism, designated by the Yeosun Incident special law in 2021, is a tour where one can pay their respects at the sites of the incident and hear the explanations of the guide.   The tour goes through Expo Station, Odongdo, Yeosun Incident Memorial Hall, Yi Sun-sin Square, Seo Market, Seo Elementary School, the Camp of the 14th Regiment, the site of Reverend Son Yangwon’s Martyrdom, and the Manseong-ri Massacre Memorial and Hyeongjemyo.  The Yeosun Incident began on October 19th, 1948, when soldiers of the 14th Regiment of the National Defense Guard, based in Sinwol-dong, refused orders to help suppress the Jeju uprising. Numerous civilians were killed in the ensuring uprising and its suppression.   The visit starts from Yeosun Incident Memorial in Odongdo, where private efforts to legislate a special law on the incident, and the law’s progress, are shown through 6 archives, photo zones depicting finger guns, VR panorama, and the Yeosun Incident theater.   Visitors will visit the base of the 14th Regiment to see the air-raid shelter that was used as an armory and the smokestack that was used by the Regiment.   Lastly, the martyrdom site of Reverend Son Yang-won will be visited to tell the story of the reverend's death. Reverend Son had earlier adopted Ahn Jaeseon, the man who killed his two sons, as an act of forgiving his enemy as God commanded. The tour ends with silence at the Manseong-ri Massacre Memorial, giving visitors the opportunity to pay their respects to the numerous unknown victims.

stories.title: Night Tour
stories.script: The Romance Bus Night Tour starts from Expo Station and passes by Odongdo Music Fountain, the Yeosu Industrial Complex, Dolsan Park, Jongpo Marine Park, and Romance Pocha Street, before returning to Expo Station.   Odongdo has night lights on its 768m breakwater for visitors to view the Expo venue from across the bay.   The Yeosu Industrial Complex was built in 1967 and is the country's largest chemical industry complex for refining oil, and the manufacture of fertilizer, petrochemicals, nonmetallic materials, machinery and electronics, as well as housing some non-manufacturing businesses. At night, a grand view of the lights installed at the facilities can be seen.   In 1984, Dolsan Bridge, connecting Namsan-dong and Dolsando, was completed along with a memorial. At the top of the park sits the Yeosu Marine Cable Car Station, and Dolsan Bridge, Yeosu Port of Janggundo, and a vantage point from which to enjoy the scenery of Gamak Bay.   The Hamel Lighthouse was built along with a statue to introduce the history of a Dutchman named Hendrick Hamel and his record of living in Yeosu for 3 1/2 years.   Turtle Ship Bridge and Cable Car has as a backdrop the beautiful Yeosu night sea, and memories can be made at Romance Pocha Street in front of Hamel Exhibition Hall.

stories.title: Day Double-decker
stories.script: The daytime double-decker operated by Yeosu City is a popular choice for visitors looking for a convenient connection to the city’s key attractions. It runs 6 times a day, and a day pass allows up to 6 re-boardings.   The course starts at Expo Station and goes through Aqua Planet, the cable car parking lot, Odongdo, Hamel Exhibition Hall, Yi Sun-sin Square, the Fishery Specialty Market, and the entrance to Dolsan Park.   Aqua Planet, located at the Yeosu Expo venue, shows visitors the value of marine creatures and ecosystems and offers a variety of shows.   Odongdo is connected by a 768m long breakwater on which visitors can stroll and view the bright camellia flowers along with 190 species of plants. The large ships anchored in front of Odongdo add to the scenery of Yeosu Bay and the blue seas.   Hamel Exhibition Hall showcases a collection of items from Hamel's last three of the 13 years he spent in Joseon after his crew washed up on Jejudo. During those final years, he stayed in Yeosu. In addition to Hamel's Journal, which depicts a westerner’s view of the Joseon people, visitors can also see the Hamel Statue and Hamel Lighthouse.  Yi Sun-sin Square was built to honor Admiral Yi who led the way to victory during the Imjin Wars. The Square is comprised of a bronze statue of the admiral, a model of a Turtle Ship, and stories of the Imjin Wars and Admiral Yi Sun-sin.   The Yeosu Passenger Terminal operates ferries and safely transports cargo to the inhabited islands among the 365 islands around Yeosu.   Yeosu Fish Market and Fishery Specialty Market sell fish caught or harvested near the coast of Yeosu, sold in live form or semi-fried. Anchovies and dolsangat kimchi are also on offer.   Dolsan Park was created in 1984 and is the location of a monument marking the completion of Dolsan Bridge, which connects Namsan-dong and Dolsando, in 1988. At the top of the park sits Nora Station for the Yeosu Marine Cable Car system.

stories.title: Night Double-decker
stories.script: The Yeosu Romance Bus, Night Double-decker, starts at Expo Station and goes through Turtle Ship Bridge, Dolsan Park, Dolsan Bridge, Seonso, Soho Dongdong Bridge, City Hall, and Jongpo Marine Park before returning to Expo Station.   Turtle Ship Bridge connects Jonghwa-dong and Udu-ri, Dolsan-eup. Constructed to connect to Dolsando for the 2012 Yeosu World Expo, it overlooks the ocean where Admiral Yi Sun-sin loaded his Turtle Ships with cannons and test-fired them the day before the Imjin Wars began. Once a place with iron-clad fortifications, it was tentatively named “Dolsan 2 Bridge” but was renamed “Turtle Ship Bridge” to mark the area’s historical significance.   Under Turtle Ship Bridge sit Hamel Lighthouse, Hamel Museum, and Jongpo Marine Park, and at night, the colorful light fixtures show off the beauty of the nightscape that matches the night sea.  Walk around Dolsan Park and take in the historical stories of Dolsan Bridge and Janggundo while viewing the beautiful Yeosu night sea. Then head off to enjoy some marinated crab and eel stew in one of the many restaurants of Bongsan-dong. Pass by Sinwol-dong and Guk-dong, where the 14th Regiment used to be and the Yeosun Incident occurred. Along the way, you will come upon the site of the past Yeosu Shipyard, where ships were made beginning in the Goryeo period.   Yeosu Shipyard was a place where vessels were built during the Goryeo period, and during the Joseon period and the Imjin Wars, it served as a naval base for Suncheon defense forces. Panokseon and turtle ships were built here.   The 742m tech walkway on Soho Dongdong Bridge is where the night scenery of Gamak Bay can be enjoyed, along with camellia flowers and guitar photo zones. Soho-dong was called “Jangsaengpo” in the past, and was where General Yootak led his men to victory against the Japanese invaders during the reign of Goryeo’s King Gongmin,. To celebrate their victory, the soldiers made a song which was titled “Dongdong.” Soho Dongdong Bridge is so named for the area’s historical significance.

stories.title: Buskers through Time
stories.script: Buskers of the Romance Bus through Time is a musical city tour that combines a musical, romantic busking, cultural tour narration, and events on a double-decker bus.   Buskers of the Romance Bus through Time is a two-hour themed tour that starts from Yi Sun-sin Square and goes through Soho Dongdong Bridge, Seonso, Dolsan Bridge, Turtle Ship Bridge, and Jongpo Marine Park before returning to Yi Sun-sin Square.    From Yi Sun-sin Square, there is a sand art exhibition that helps people understand the musical performance of the love of Camel and Lia, which begins in the Goryeo period, weaves its way through the Joseon period and ends in modern times.   Arrive at Soho Dongdong Bridge with the help of a wizard to walk the 742m deck path. Afterwards, on the bus back to Yi Sun-sin Square from Soho Dongdong Bridge, a busker performance, romantic letter writing, Yeosu quiz, and serenade of love can be enjoyed.    The love story of the Buskers of the Romance Bus through Time starts with pike eels, the main natural food of Yeosu. On Yeongchwisan Mountain with its blooming azaleas, Camel falls in love with Lia, and their love grows as they share pike eels on the Yeosu coast, but Camel ends up volunteering in Yi Sun-sin's forces during the Imjin Wars. Lia waits for her love, Camel, seemingly to no end. What will the fate of these two be? Come hear the love story of Yeosu to find out!

stories.title: Taehwagang National Garden– Taehwagang Observatory
stories.script: The Taehwagang River at a glance  From the Taehwa River Observatory, you can see all sides of the Taehwa River, which flows through Ulsan's downtown. It is a popular place to take photos because of the beautiful red sunset.  The Taehwa River Observatory was constructed as a water intake tower for the Ulsan National Industrial Complex. It was no longer used due to a change in industrial water policy in 1995. But it was remodeled in 2004 as a river observatory.  You can see fish native to the Taehwa River on the first floor. And you can explore “Samho Bamboo Grove” and “Simni Bamboo Grove,” the two ecological spaces, at the 360-degree revolving cafe on the third floor and the observatory on the fourth floor, respectively.  About 6,000 to 7,000 white herons migrate to Samho Bamboo Grove in the summer, and about 100,000 jackdaws and rooks from the north perform their dances in the winter. Blue lily-turfs and yellow ginkgo trees are beautiful in autumn, between August and mid-September. There are many things you can do: such as going for a walk, riding your bike, having a picnic, enjoying Chimaeg (fried chicken and beer), or even going camping.  You will find the Milky Way Bridge about 700 meters west of Taehwagang Observatory. You can cross the Taehwa River through the Milky Way Bridge, which allows you to walk on a transparent floor. However, children are prohibited for safety reasons.

stories.title: Sipni Forest & Milky Way Road
stories.script: The Taehwagang River National Garden Sipridae Forest is the first of the 12 scenic views in Ulsan. The long blue bamboo forest along the Taehwagang River is long enough to hide the end, and the Taehwagang Sipridae Forest is an eco-friendly natural bamboo forest that allows people to enter. It is a forest that can be enjoyed comfortably and freely regardless of gender, the disabled, and non-patriotic, and it is a garden in the city center where you can feel the negative ions from the green bamboo forest all year round.  The Taehwagang Sipni Forest has a long history because it has been around since the Joseon Dynasty. In 1749, there is a record that there was a large field in Hakseongji, the first town chronicle in Ulsan, and in the poem Taehwaru by Kim Geuk-ki, a writer during the reign of King Myeongjong of Goryeo in the 12th century.  The trail in the Sipni Forest is attractive. Listen to the sound of the wind created by the bamboo forest that has grown here for a long time. The night forest turns into a Milky Way. The moment you light up about 600 LED tricolor laser beams and small light fixtures, it creates an illusion that you are in space.  In late July or early August, the Taehwagang Grand Forest Horror Festival will be held inside the Taehwagang River Sipni Forest. If you like experiences such as House of Ghosts, participate. You may encounter ghosts hiding in the bamboo forest.

stories.title: Taehwagang National Garden – Migratory Bird Center
stories.audioTitle: Taehwagang National Garden – Migratory Bird Center
stories.script: Coexistence between humans and migratory birds  Taehwagang River is the first place on the East Coast, 17th place in Korea, and 150th place in the whole world to have been designated as a migratory bird flying route. It is the only route for migratory birds in the city. Samho Bamboo Grove is the most important place for migratory birds on the Taehwagang River. Despite it being located in the center of the city, people are not permitted to enter to preserve migratory birds. You can visit the Migratory Bird Center if you are curious about Samho Bamboo Grove.  If you look around the education center and observatory of the Migratory Bird Center, you can see that Ulsan is making efforts to transform itself from an industrial city to a green, smart, eco-friendly city. As well as discovering information about the herons and rooks living in Samho Bamboo Grove, you can also watch migratory birds' daily lives through the telescope installed on the 5th floor.   The Migratory Birds Center was built out of consideration for coexistence between humans and migratory birds. At one time, the Samho Bamboo Grove was in danger of being reduced in size as plowland increased. With the residents' help, more bamboos were planted and the ecology now resembles that of a virgin forest.

stories.title: Taehwagang National Garden – Donggulpia
stories.script: Explore the Mysterious Cave   Located west of Taehwa Rotary, caves with gorgeous artificial waterfalls can be found. These are four artificial caves used as supply rooms in the past, originally called Namsangul Caves.  In 2017, this historical space was transformed into a unique cultural experience space that combines history, culture, and nature. An underground plaza was created by connecting three of the four caves, and it was reorganized as a waterfront space for sightseeing and exploration. The Taehwagang River is also connected underground.  In the first cave is the Namsan Cave History Museum.  The second cave has many adventure-themed attractions, including Mirror Cave, animal-shaped lights, and the legendary whale habitat.  The third cave is a place where you can experience digital sketching by projecting a picture drawn in the aquarium or a sketch of the cave onto the screen.  The fourth cave is where a variety of events are held every season. It turns into a flower garden with LED lights in spring, a haunted house in summer, a gallery where you can admire artworks in autumn, and a frozen kingdom of light and ice in winter.  Donggulpia is a tourist attraction located near Taehwagang Observatory, the artificial waterfall, Ulsan Crane Park, and Migratory Bird Park. A hiking trail behind the Donggulpia parking lot leads to Namsanlu Pavilion, where you can see the Taehwagang River at a glance. From Namsanlu Pavilion, you can reach Ulsan Grand Park by strolling along the Solmalu road.

stories.title: Ulsan_Kyeongnam Bus Ulsan Office
stories.script: Kyeongnam Bus Ulsan Office   Ulsan and automobiles are inseparable.  In Ulsan, the city of automobiles, the history of public transportation began in Seongnam-dong, Jung-gu. The first automobile was introduced to Korea in 1903. It was imported from the United States to commemorate the 40th anniversary of King Gojong's accession. Those who first saw the four-wheeled object called it the rolling iron foal and the rolling lightning.” At first, only kings and nobles rode iron foals, but they soon spread throughout the country. Eventually, automobiles were introduced to Ulsan too. The Gyeongnam Passenger Ulsan Office was built on the site of the Dong-a Pharmacy in Seongnam-dong, Jung-gu, where now stands a convenience store. There was a waiting room on the site of the convenience store. Next to it was an office and a residence for Kyeongnam Bus.  The bus operating at that time had about 30 seats, about two-thirds the size of modern buses. Something is interesting about the fuel of the bus at that time. They used charcoal because gasoline was expensive.  In the pictures of the old charcoal bus, you can see a large barrel attached to the back for burning charcoal.  As charcoal is less efficient than gasoline, it had to be set on fire two hours before operation, and passengers often had to get off the bus to push it on hilly roads.   In 1960, a pharmacy opened on the site of the Kyeongnam Bus Ulsan Office. Dong-a Pharmacy is the first pharmacy in Ulsan, according to its registration certificate.  Many politicians and local officials in Ulsan visited Myung Teahouse at the time, located at a nearby intersection. People had to pass the pharmacy to reach there, which made the pharmacy a center of public opinion in Ulsan.  The Dong-A Pharmacy operated until 2021 and was then converted into a convenience store. Having been the origin of Ulsan’s public transportation and the center of public opinion at one time, Kyeongnam Bus Ulsan Office still plays an important role in Ulsan’s history.

stories.title: Ulsan_Reservoir with a Water Tower at Ulsan Station on the Gyeongdong Line
stories.audioTitle: Ulsan_Reservoir with a Water Tower at Ulsan Station on the Gyeongdong Line
stories.script: First Train Station in Ulsan   The first railroad built in Ulsan opened on October 25, 1921.  During that year, as Chosun Central Railway Gyeongdong Line opened, Ulsan station was built at the old site of the 119 Safety Center on the Street of Youth in Seongnam-dong   The Gyeongdong Line was a narrow-gauge railway with a track gauge narrower than standard, and it ran from Daegu to Ulsan. Steam locomotives fueled by coal were operating at that time. The fare from Ulsan to Daegu was 4.83 won for 1st class, and 3.95 won for 2nd class. In those days, taking the train was considered a symbol of wealth because the average daily wage was 0.5 won.  For your information, the value of 1 won in the 1920s is about 50,000 won in 2022.   There were water towers around the train station to supply the water for locomotives before diesel locomotives were introduced in the 1950s.  Although the water towers have long since disappeared, the suction well still remains in Seongnam-dong, where the first Ulsan Station stood. After the relocation of Ulsan Station, the suction well provided water to the residents of Ulsan but was buried during road replanning of the area. However, it is currently being restored as a well.  Ulsan Station moved to Hakseong-dong in 1935, and railroad worker residences remained at the old station. As part of the redevelopment plan, the Ulsan Tax Office, Ulsan Public Hall, and Ulsan Fire Station were built in the rest of the area.  As part of the rebuilding plan, Ulsan's Clock Tower intersection, fire station, and KT office complex are located in the original downtown area of the city. It formed the basis of Seongnam-dong, Ulsan's central commercial district.  There were many changes in Ulsan at the time due to the opening of the Ulsan Railway and the relocation of Ulsan Station.   A newspaper article from February 2, 1936, reported that Ulsan's land values soared during  two or three years, and its population increased by 2,000 in one year. The relocation of Ulsan's railway station from Seongnam-dong to Hakseong-dong expanded the city to the south and east. Furthermore, having a rail network led Ulsan to be selected for the Yuya-Ulsan Liaison Base project aimed at connecting Ulsan Port and Yuya Port in Japan. Consequently, the Ulsan Industrial Center was built in 1962, establishing Ulsan as an industrial city.

stories.title: Ulsan_Ttokttak Street
stories.script: The road that offers consolation, Ttokttak Street  In Jungang-dong and Seongnam-dong, Ulsan's old downtown, you can find many alleyways of memories where time seems to stand still. High-rise buildings pushed them out during the industrialization period of the 1970s and 1980s. For example, on your way to the Goboksu Music Center through Seongnam-dong Culture Street, you'll come across a narrow alley named Ttokttak Street.  Ttokttak Street was the busiest street in front of the Ulsaneupseong Walled Town and served as the marketplace. It is similar to the newly paved road near Gwanghwamun in Seoul. Houses were built densely due to the area's high property value at the time, thus forming narrow alleys.  Ttokttak Street was named after the ticking sound of a clock to comfort the young people in Ulsan who both suffered frustration and experienced success during the turbulent industrialization in the 1970s and 1980s and to help them look back once more on the past.   You can see the garden through the brick holes at the entrance of Ttokttak Street. Hakseong Inn was located here in the past, and there was a garden behind the inn. Here, you can see an old well from the Joseon Dynasty, one of eight wells in Ulsaneupseong Walled Town, and it feels like going back a hundred years in a time machine.  It's fun to look at the drawings all over the alley. Drawings of a wedding couple, a young girl who jumps to receive a bouquet, and a dog all look familiar and can make you smile. It's as if the small flowerpots along the road and the flower garden are telling an old story.

stories.title: Ulsan_Barefoot Youth Street
stories.script: Memories of the 70s and 80s~ Barefooted Youth Street  During the 1970s and 1980s, Barefooted Youth Street was where industrial workers who worked all day at Ulsan Industrial Complex walked while humming after getting off the bus in Seongnam-dong, Ulsan's busiest downtown area.  As part of an urban regeneration project in Jungang-dong, the Barefoot Youth Street alley project was initiated to preserve the memories of these alleys. It was divided into three zones based on their characteristics: music, movies, and fashion. Murals and sculptures were installed accordingly. When a person passes the music zone, music from the 70s and 80s is automatically played to make you feel nostalgic.  The “Barefooted Youth Street” is decorated with characters symbolizing the 70s and 80s. Ajiya will take you back to the 1970s with his long hair, flared trousers, and funny face. For your information, Ajiya refers to a middle-aged male in the Ulsan dialect.   Neon signs light up the street at night and portray a different scene from what can be seen during the day. Why don’t you discover Ulsan's history and culture along Barefooted Youth Street, where old restaurants, clothing stores, karaoke rooms, and unique pubs line every alley.

stories.title: Ulsan_Seongnam Market
stories.script: A bustling five-day interval village market   Every five days, a market was held in a large vacant lot where children now play hide and seek.  In the past, there was a pond where the present-day Seongnam Plaza is located. However, the pond has been filled, and the Seongnam Market has been constructed in its place.  Initially, the market wasn't large, but cattle markets and pottery shops were set up, food stall alleyways formed around it, and it became a popular destination for young people.  Small business owners from Gyeongju, Miryang, Busan, and Daegu filled the bars on market days and gambled. Among the five-day markets in general, Seongnam Market modernized more rapidly by installing arcades on the site. During market days, musical troupes performed to add to the fun.  As time passed, Seongnam Market became a permanent market in 1969. However, the present building has been built as a result of the mid-1980s fire. A market has developed around Seongnam Plaza, but the bustle of the five-day market has gone.  Although the old market has disappeared, you can hear musicians busking in Cubic Square, and you can also find small but special restaurants.

stories.title: Ulsan_Ulsan Financial Association
stories.script: The bank that even fed cows  Nowadays, everything can be done on a smartphone, from remittances to transactions. There was, however, a business in the distant past that could never be replaced by a smartphone: feeding the cows.  The Ulsan Financial Association was founded in 1907 in Seongnam-dong, Jung-gu, on the site of the present NH Nonghyup. Financial associations were mainly financial institutions for the working class, such as farmers and small business owners. As of today, they are very similar to credit associations. The jobs were mostly similar to those of a bank today, with one exception: caring for cows.   Farmers used to sell cows on market days. Farmers who couldn't sell cows used them as collateral and borrowed money from the bank. As soon as the cows were sold, the farmers would come to the bank to pay back the borrowed money and take them back. Instead, the bank charged a fee for feeding cows. Accordingly, the bank even had staff to feed and care for the cows. Can you imagine a bank where cows moo?

stories.title: Ulsan_Sim Won-gwon, The diary king of Ulsan
stories.audioTitle: Ulsan_Sim Won-gwon, The diary king of Ulsan
stories.script: A man who kept a diary every day for 64 years   Even though keeping a record of your daily activities and weather might seem meaningless, if you record these things steadily over a long period, it becomes an important source of big data. Long before the Internet existed, Ulsan had a king of big data: Sim Won-gwon. He was born in 1850, during the reign of King Cheoljong of the Joseon Dynasty.  At first, the yangban Sim Won-gwon was interested in civil service examinations but soon gave up and moved to his hometown to farm. For 64 years, from 1870, when he was 20, until his death in 1933, he kept a diary almost every day.  Unlike other diaries, Shim Won-gwon's diary contains not only the impressions and feelings of the day but also information about the weather, the direction and strength of the wind, and the visiting of graves and ancestral rites observed during rural life. Its most distinguishing feature is that it consistently tracked rice price changes for a long time. Rice prices were recorded every ten days from July 1876 to November 1933, and it is probably difficult to find any other data that shows the flow of price fluctuations over the past 60 years.  For these reasons, Sim Won-gwon's diary was designated as a tangible cultural property of Gyeongsangnam-do.  The greatest king of big data in the late Joseon Dynasty, Sim Won-gwon! His name should be saved in Ulsan Tour Big Data.

stories.title: Ulsan_ Jangteogeol
stories.script: The street where markets open, Jangteogeol  Whenever you think of the market, you probably imagine women walking around with pots on their heads like they are doing tricks, the elders carrying their burdens on their carriers and shouting loudly, and the grandmothers selling vegetables and grains in big bowls. The streets around Okgyo-dong, Jung-gu, now called Culture Street, once served as a marketplace for Ulsaneupseong Walled Town. This place was once called Jangteogeol, which means the street where markets open.  The Jangteogeol market was held on the 5th and 10th of every month. In the early 1900’s, markets were held on the road between Ulsan Elementary School and the Clock Tower intersection in Seongnam-dong. After liberation, markets were opened from east to west along the road in front of the Ulsan-gun Office, the Magistrate's office, and the old Ulsan Elementary School.  The road was crowded with people and goods on market days. The Ulsan Gun Office, the post office, the myon office, the financial association, and various shops were built at that time and became the center of modern administration and commerce.  It is also a good example of the history of urbanization that shows administration and commerce develop as people gather and money flows. So a cup of tea or a bowl of soup at the market today will also become history in the future, right?

stories.title: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Youth Ko Bok-soo Jazz Street
stories.audioTitle: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Youth Ko Bok-soo Jazz Street
stories.script: Theme Alley in the Old Downtown, “Listening to music from the 1930s”   “Living away from home, how many years? I finger counted to see. A decade plus years away from home, just turned my youth to an old one.” Living away from home is a song sung by Ko Bok-soo, whose sad voice brings tears to many people's eyes just hearing the first verse. He was born into a poor merchant family in Ulsan in 1911. A dream of becoming a singer led him to Seoul. And in 1934, at the age of 23, he won the 2nd prize in a music competition hosted by Columbia Records. He gained huge popularity after releasing the song “Living away from home.” Living away from home is a nostalgic song that compatriots who lost their country and moved to Manchuria sang whenever they missed their hometown. The sentimental and mournful voice of Koh Bok-soo soothed people's pain. When it was performed for compatriots in North Gando, Yanbian, and Harbin, it received 33 encores. In Ulsan’s old downtown area, there is Youth Go Bok-soo Jazz Road and Go Bok-soo Music Hall, a music space commemorating Go Bok-soo. Youth Go Bok-Soo Jazz Path is a themed alley built in a place where Ko Bok-Soo might have walked when he was young. In an alley full of modern houses, you'll find attractions with modern viewpoints and photo spots with benches, so it's worth strolling through. The Goboksu Music Hall, which was remodeled from a Western-style building, has an exhibition space on the first floor and a retro cafe on the second floor decorated with the concept of a stage from the 1930s. Here you can listen to songs including Unrequited Love, Living Away from Home, as well as songs by popular singers from the 1930's music scene with the sound of vinyl records.

stories.title: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Cohabitation of inshore hagfish and chicken
stories.audioTitle: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Cohabitation of inshore hagfish and chicken
stories.script: Foil-wrapped Seasoned Inshore Hagfish and old-fashioned Fried Chicken Mukbang   Whale meat and Eonyang bulgogi are often viewed as Ulsan's signature dishes. Inshore hagfish and chicken, however, are Ulsan's most famous dishes. There used to be a factory in Ulsan that produced inshore hagfish skins. Because inshore hagfish skin is soft and water-resistant, it was used for belts and wallets. These products were exported to Japan. The inshore hagfish alley was formed in Ulsan Central Market as people began eating leftover meat after selling their skins. Ulsan's inshore hagfish alley was the most lively in the 1980s and 1990s. This is because Ulsan has become an industrial city and has developed a culture of company dinners for workers. Low prices and generous market merchants made inshore hagfish a popular dish. As a place for gatherings, the alley was popular among both college students and workers. In Ulsan, seasoned inshore hagfish is wrapped in silver foil and grilled. With the prevalence of company dinners, chicken also became a favorite dish, and Ulsan Central Market became a food district filled with the delicious smell of inshore hagfish and chicken. Although the number of restaurants has decreased compared to the past, there are still some old restaurants that are still open. If you visit the old downtown, you should try the 80's and 90's style grilled whole chicken and inshore hagfish at Ulsan Central Market.

stories.title: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Maduhee Festival
stories.audioTitle: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Maduhee Festival
stories.script: “Giant tug of war festival,” a traditional game called Maduhee   Maduhee is Ulsan's tug-of-war festival with a history of 320 years. It is a combination of Chinese characters meaning horse (ma), head (du), and play (hee), and it refers to the game of playing with the head of a horse. The tug-of-war competition has been held in Ulsan since the Joseon Dynasty to pray for unity and a good harvest. Because the horsehead-shaped Dongdaesan Mountain range faces the southern sea, it was held every year to prevent good energy from escaping into the sea. There is a record of Ma Du-hee in the customs section of Hakseongji, a town chronicle published in the 29th year of King Yeongjo (1749 AD). The game was interrupted during the Korean War, but was rediscovered and handed down again from 2012.  Over two weeks before the Maduhee Festival, bundles of straw are twisted into ropes as thick as a human body, each of which is 100 meters long. Every September, a tug-of-war with a 160-meter-long rope is held at the Clock Tower intersection in Ulsan’s old downtown during the “Maduhee Festival.” The Madujeon currency, which is issued for Maduhee, can be used in the shopping malls around the old downtown during the festival.

stories.title: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Teahouses that blossomed with romance and literature
stories.audioTitle: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Teahouses that blossomed with romance and literature
stories.script: Teahouses of literature and romance that sold morning coffee  Enjoy a cup of coffee while walking along Memories Street on Ulsan Keunaegi Street in the old downtown. The theme of Memories Street is coffee. There was a time when cool people gathered to enjoy morning coffee on the teahouse street in Ulsan's original downtown. There was a trend in the 1960s and 1970s of white-collar and blue-collar workers in search of romance and literature stopping by teahouses on their way to work to have a morning coffee. Morning coffee was made with coffee, sugar and cream in the right ratio, then egg yolk was floated with a drop of sesame oil, At that time, the Cheongja Teahouse and Sinhwa Teahouse served as meeting places for young people and college students in Ulsan, an industrial city. It was a place where you could go on a blind date or ask the DJ for music that fit your story. Marronnier Coffee Shop, which was Hakseong Inn in the past, was a gathering place for college students and youth in Ulsan. Garosu Teahouse and Myeong Teahouse were popular spots among gentlemen, writers and artists. Take a walk along Ulsan's memories street and have a cup of morning coffee that was once the ultimate luxury. There are now galleries and cafes instead of the famous teahouses of the time.

stories.title: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Seongnam-dong Tailor Shop Street
stories.audioTitle: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Seongnam-dong Tailor Shop Street
stories.script: Originally a street of tailor shops, now a street of secondhand clothing  Everyone was striving for a quick economic recovery in the mid-1960s. Under the slogan advancing without interruption, Ulsan rapidly developed into a base for industrialization. This led to an increase in population from 270,000 in the 1970s to 1 million in the 1990s. During the 1970s, Ulsan became a land of opportunity and a city of youth. As money and people flowed into the city, restaurants and bars were built in the old downtown area known as Okgyo-dong and Seongnam-dong. In response to the growing importance of dating, tailors for dandies started to flourish on the street. Back then, many people in Ulsan, where wages were high, bought customized clothes on Tailor Shop Street. A tailor-made suit cost the equivalent of five months' salary for a teacher, but the tailor shop was always busy. When the Tailor Shop Street was created, many tailors from Seoul and Busan moved to Ulsan. Tailor Shop Street in the old downtown lasted until the 1990s, but declined as ready-made clothing replaced it. Nowadays, there are sculptures of tailor shops and tailors on Tailor Shop Street near Memories Street.

stories.title: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Okgolsaem Spring
stories.audioTitle: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Okgolsaem Spring
stories.script: A living well covered with a lid  The Okgolsaem Spring is located in an alley near Okgol Market. This well was like the water of life for the residents of Okgyo-dong. The water tasted good and did not dry out in a drought, so people from various towns came there to fetch water. During the Joseon Dynasty, this well was primarily used for a prison in Ulsaneupseong Walled Town. However, Okgolsaem Spring had to be covered with a lid due to rapid modernization. For safety and hygiene reasons, the residents debated whether the well should be completely filled, but decided to leave it covered with a lid. Residents who live nearby have voluntarily drained and cleaned the well since then.  Okgolsaem (Oksam) has a story to be told. It is said that a beggar found a mute at a well in this village. Villagers tried to drive the beggar out, but the mute brought him some water. After thanking him, the beggar said that he would be able to speak if he drank Okgol spring water for three years. And it is said that the mute could actually speak clearly. Isn't it likely that people would love and take pride in the well? Next to the well covered with a wooden lid, there are sculptures of a mother pouring water and naked babies about to bathe. Enjoy the scenery that reminds you of memories at Okgolsaem Spring, where you can take photos with sculptures.

stories.title: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Hakseong Inn
stories.audioTitle: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Hakseong Inn
stories.script: Hakseong Inn with its secret garden  Built in 1911, the Hakseong Inn used to have the size of today’s mid-range hotel. Hakseong Ryokan was advertised in the Ulsan Guide magazine in 1917 as a Government Office Designated Inn providing luxurious interiors and delicious cuisine. As the opening ceremony for Ulsan Airfield, Korea's first international private airport, was held in 1928, Hakseong Inn served as a venue for preparations and offered lodgings to distinguished guests. Even after liberation, the Hakseong Inn remained popular. This inn was at its peak in 1958, during the fourth general election. Since Hakseong Inn was designated as election headquarters, the inn was packed with campaign members. In 1950, it served as a shelter for refugees from the Korean War. And in the 1960s and 1970s, it was crowded with young people undergoing physical examinations at the Gyeongnam Military manpower Administration. In the 1980s, the inn was closed and converted into a supermarket and shoe store. Later on, it was converted into Marronnier Coffee Park and became a rendezvous in 1987. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism restored its old appearance in 2016, and now it is a tourist attraction in Ulsan's downtown area, which has been maintained for more than a century. Although the signboard and its exterior have changed, the original framework of the Hakseong Inn has been preserved. You can see the traces of the old building from the front of the cafe and the internal structure of the roof. Be sure to stop by the Ulsaneupseong Walled Town's well and the secret garden in the garden at the back, which were built in the Joseon Dynasty.

stories.title: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Ulsan Magistrate's Office and Living Quarters
stories.audioTitle: Old Downtown – Keunaegi Street – Ulsan Magistrate's Office and Living Quarters
stories.script: Ulsan Magistrate's Office, a local government office of the Joseon Period  Ulsan Magistrate's Office is Ulsan's Tangible Cultural Property No. 1. This was a government office in Ulsaneupseong Walled Town to protect residents during the Joseon Dynasty. Built in 1681, the Ulsan Magistrate's Office served as the administrative and judiciary for the region and is the same as the current city hall.
