Ulsan’s Daewangam Park, a place that captures the love of the queen over her people,  is today a tourist spot chosen as one of the 100 Must-Visit Tourist Spots and night spots in Korea. The people of Ulsan host an annual rite for fisheries on the rock. The size of the rock has led to the people calling the rock “Daewangbawi Rock” or “Daengbawi Rock”, “Yongbawi” from its dragon-like form, or “Yongchuam” for its semblance to a dragon that fell on the sea.   Daewangam Park is one of the favorite picnic spots in Ulsan, and one of the 12 Sights of Ulsan. Along with Ganjeolgot Cape, it is a popular destination for sunrise-watching. The literati in Joseon period called this area the Haegeumgang, or the Geumgangsan Mountain of the sea, thanks to its beautiful view of the sea and the rock formations.   The area is also home to a lush forest of 15,000 pine trees, and a white lighthouse that was the first of its kind in the eastern shore of Korea.

stories.title: City Tour - Daewangam Course - Car Field / Car Loading Dock
stories.audioTitle: City Tour - Daewangam Course - Car Field / Car Loading Dock
stories.script: When one passes the Yeomposan Mountain and the Ulsandaegyo Bridge, one finds oneself in the coastal road of Asan-ro. The scenery to the left-hand side here is a very unique one: The Car Field of Ulsan, or the export loading dock for Korea’s automobile industry, where nearly six thousand to ten thousand cars wait to be loaded onto ships.   The ten thousand cars that wait here were all produced to order for export, in their final stages before being loaded onto the vessel. You can see the cars being loaded into massive ships, which make the cars look like toy cars from sheer size. Hyundai Motor Company’s Ulsan Plant is capable of producing 1.4 million cars per year in a single plant, and the cars produced to order from the plant are lined up here in the “Car Field”.   The people who load the vehicles onto the ship are the best of the best in driving. Their specialty is parking, which they make use to park the cars inside the ship in narrow, yet secure formations.  The coastal road that the “Car Field” is located on is called Asan-ro. The name of the road comes from the courtesy name used by the late founder of Hyundai Heavy Industries, Chung Ju-yung. Originally the site of a manufacturing plant belonging to the company, it was developed into a coastal road and donated to the City of Ulsan. The city in turn recognized Mr. Chung’s contribution to the Korean and Ulsan economy and his generosity to the citizens of Ulsan by naming the road after his courtesy name, Asan. Thanks to Asan-ro, the traffic between Bangeojin and the city center area has improved dramatically.

stories.title: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary – Samsan-dong
stories.audioTitle: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary – Samsan-dong
stories.script: Ulsan is the seventh metropolitan city of South Korea, and it’s 1.7 times bigger than Seoul. Despite its size, the mountains, rivers, and sea are all within an hour’s drive from anywhere in the city. The city was named Ulsan in 1413 under the reign of King Taejong because there are many mountains and dense forests in the area. As such, Ulsan has always been known for its beautiful natural landscape.   However, Ulsan has never been the same since the modernization. The part of the city that has changed the most is Samsan-dong, which is the district we’re passing through right now. It’s a planned town constructed in the 1980’s as the population grew in the area. It was a sea bed up until the middle of the Joseon period.   Story has it that the town was named Samsan, which means “three mountains” in Korean, because there are three mountain peaks in the area. When there is a fog over the mountains, it makes them appear as though they are floating in the air like islands.   There were salt farms during the Joseon period, but all of them had to give way to airstrips since it was where the first private international airport was built. Today, it’s the busiest part of the city.

stories.title: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary – Taehwagang River and Ulsan
stories.audioTitle: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary – Taehwagang River and Ulsan
stories.script: A river flows east-west through Ulsan called the Taehwagang River. It is named after the Taehwasa temple, which was built by Jajang, a monk in the Silla Dynasty, in the 12th year of Queen Seondeok (643 AD). Using 100 pieces of Buddha's ashes brought from the Tang dynasty, Jajang built three major temples to overcome Silla's national crisis. Back then, Tongdosa Temple, Hwangnyongsa Temple Site's nine-story stone pagoda, and Taehwasa Temple were built as patriotic temples.  The Taehwagang River has long been the center of Ulsan's development, but pollution worsened in the 1970s as the city's economy developed. Mass fish deaths were reported five times in 1992 on the Taehwagang River, which has become a river of death. The situation is illustrated very well by a picture of a child looking sadly at a dead fish in a newspaper on August 15, 1992. A once uncontaminated area where corbiculas and clams lived has become water of grades 5 and 6, where even tubifexes cannot survive.  As part of the Taehwagang River Restoration Master Plan, Ulsan, citizens, and businesses announced the Eco-Police Ulsan Declaration in June 2004. There was then a movement to save the Taehwagang River, which included cleaning, river maintenance, and improving its water quality. After a Korean rose blitterling fish first appeared in the Taehwagang River, daces, sweetfishes, and salmons began returning each season. Ulsan has become an eco-city where migratory birds visit in the summer and winter. There are also endangered species like the long-billed plovers and black-faced spoonbills along the Taehwagang River, which is now the first migration route for migratory birds on the east coast.  Taehwagang River has become an exemplary case in ecological history across the globe. In Ulsan, residents are more proud of the Taehwagang River restoration than of the history that fueled Korea's economic growth. People often ride their bikes along the Taehwagang River, or have picnics with their families.

stories.title: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary – Information on Taehwagang Donggulpia
stories.audioTitle: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary – Information on Taehwagang Donggulpia
stories.script: Taehwagang Donggulpia    There is Donggulpia on the left. This artificial cave was originally used as a military depot before it was transformed into a tourist attraction. The entrance is adorned with an artificial waterfall and a fountain.  There is a tower-like building on the right bank of the river after passing Donggulpia. It is the Taehwagang Observatory where you can observe the bamboo grove. You can walk across the river by crossing the Milkyway Bridge, a footbridge under the National Garden Bridge.

stories.title: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary– Information on Migratory Birds Center (After passing Taehwagang Observatory)
stories.audioTitle: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary– Information on Migratory Birds Center (After passing Taehwagang Observatory)
stories.script: The Migratory Bird Center on the left is where you can see Samho Bamboo Grove. Among nine scenic spots in Nam-gu, Samho Bamboo Grove is the seventh. Since it is a nesting site for migratory birds, people are not allowed to enter. You can visit the Migratory Bird Center instead to learn more about migratory birds. A telescope is available on the roof of the 5th floor for observing migratory birds. Heron herds can be seen in the summer, and jackdaws and rooks can be seen in the winter.

stories.title: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary– Information on Taehwagang National Garden
stories.audioTitle: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary– Information on Taehwagang National Garden
stories.script: Taehwagang National Garden is South Korea's second national garden. It is becoming one of the most attractive travel destinations for many people currently. The Taehwagang National Garden has more than 20 themed gardens. Being Korea's largest waterfront space in the city, the garden includes ecological gardens, bamboo gardens, seasonal gardens, aquatic gardens, participation gardens, mugunghwa gardens, and ginkgo trees. In every season, you'll find different attractions. The trail from Osan Plaza to Simni Bamboo Grove is something that cannot be missed in the Taehwagang National Garden. The willows in Zelkova Plaza are also very attractive.  Taehwagang National Garden offers a variety of ways to enjoy it. You can ride a bicycle or a convertible, or set up a tent and have a picnic while camping. On hot summer days or rainy days, umbrellas and parasols can be rented for free at the Taehwagang Information Center.

stories.title: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary– Information on Taehwalu Pavilion
stories.audioTitle: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary– Information on Taehwalu Pavilion
stories.script: A symbol of Ulsan, Taehwalu, can be seen on the hill facing Dongkang Medical Center along the Taehwagang River. Along with Chokseongnu Pavilion in Jinju and Yeongnamnu Pavilion in Miryang, It is an architecture of traditional tiles, one of three major pavilions in Yeongnam.   An Ulsan Eupji published in 1902 contains a record that was lost before and after the Imjin War. Following repeated failures over 45 years, Ulsan citizens were able to build a new one in 400 years. You can enjoy sunrises, sunsets and the beauty of the Taehwagang River all year long here.  The signboards are in Chinese and Korean. It was written in Hangeul, which symbolizes Choi Hyeon-bae, the language scholar from Ulsan who established the Korean Language Society and enacted the draft for a unified spelling system.   Cultural and artistic activities are often held in front of the Taehwalu Pavilion. Also, Taehwa Market is held on the 5th and 10th of every month.

stories.title: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary– Information on Clock Tower and Ulsan Central Market (After passing Taehwalu Pavilion)
stories.audioTitle: City Tour – Taehwagang National Garden Itinerary– Information on Clock Tower and Ulsan Central Market (After passing Taehwalu Pavilion)
stories.script: In Ulsan's old downtown, the Clock Tower Intersection and Ulsan Central Market are located. There are various foods available at Ulsan Central Market, such as inshore hagfish and chicken. Located at the intersection is the newly built Clock Tower, a dome-shaped building. This building served as a rendezvous in 1966 when it was first built. Six trains at the top of the tower used to run every hour with the woo woo! sound of a train whistle, but now it has stopped operating.  The alleys and streets of Ulsan's old downtown, where the Ulsan Magistrate's Office and the guest house used to be located, are full of local artists' art galleries and cafes. Like Montmartre in Paris, it hosts various street performances and exhibitions during the weekends.  Additionally, there are a variety of themed streets. Take a stroll along Gamseong Course, Ulsan Keunaegi Street, Memories Street, and Eupseong Walled Town Street, where history and stories from the past and present coexist. They are full of artistic spaces and attractions such as Dream Garden, Taehwaseowon Confucian Academy, Ulsan Keunaegi's House, and Go Bok-Soo Music Hall.  The character Ulsan Keunaegi is often seen in the old downtown. The newly created character who wears a red skirt and a big head as a representation of Ulsan was inspired by the lyrics of the 1969 song Ulsan Keunaegi. The character was recognized for its success and received many awards at home and abroad. The official who made Ulsan Keunaegi got a promotion too. And there is a real character who actually appears in television programs like Pengsoo.  Also popular is the Ulsan Art Museum, which opened in January 2022. Enjoy a variety of experimental and adventurous exhibitions at a reasonable price at the Media Art Theatre.

stories.title: Taehwagang River Area – Taehwagang Silver Grass Habitat in Myeongchon
stories.audioTitle: Taehwagang River Area – Taehwagang Silver Grass Habitat in Myeongchon
stories.script: Sand islands and the wetland stretching for miles A silver grass habitat near the Myeongchongyo Bridge on the Taehwagang River There are many bridges on the Taehwagang River that flows through the middle of Ulsan into the East Sea. Among them, the silver grass habitat near Myeongchon Bridge on the Taehwagang River is one of 12 scenic spots in Buk-gu. There are wetlands and sand islands under Myeongchon Bridge. Silver grass can be found abundantly. You can still enjoy the waves of silver grass in the middle of the city on the banks of the Taehwagang River. The largest area is in Myeongchon-dong on the northern end.  The silver grass of Myeongchongyo Bridge has a legend. According to the legend, the silver grass originally lived with the reed in Ganwoljae Pass in Sinbulsan Mountain. On a full moon night, the reed said, “I'll follow the moon and see what's under the mountain, so let's go together, silver grass. But the silver grass replied, “No! I will not leave Ganwoljae and the mountain!” The reed did not return because it fell in love with the Taehwagang River and the sea view. It is said that the lonely silver grass eventually moved to the Taehwagang River to live with the reed, and thus became a common reed. The silver grass that became a common reed would have no regrets because it reunited with their loved one. Now, common reeds grow much taller than humans and can be seen endlessly along the Taehwagang Tiver. This beautiful scenery is loved by many people.  Myeongchongyo Bridge's riverside deck offers a view of silver grass and migratory birds. Around 2 o’clock in the afternoon, you can also see Hyundai Motors workers who work in shifts riding motorcycles and bicycles to work at the northern end of Myeongchongyo Bridge.

stories.title: Taehwagang River Area – Samhoseom Island (Migratory Bird Park)
stories.audioTitle: Taehwagang River Area – Samhoseom Island (Migratory Bird Park)
stories.script: The mystery of the bamboo grove in the wetland, “Samhoseom Island” Samhoseom Island is a bamboo grove that spreads beneath the newly built Sinsamhogyo Bridge at the end of Namsan-ro, which can reached by driving along the Taehwagang River. It is closer to the lower stream than the middle stream of the Taehwagang River. As a wetland, it enjoys a unique ecological environment.  Samhoseom Island (11,500 square meters), created in the 1910s, was originally called Samtan. This area is significant because it is a well-formed biotope and sandbank, a site that provides habitat for creatures. It used to be an isolated island-like terrain with a wetland filled with bamboo and reeds, but it has now been connected to the mainland and is easily accessible.  You can walk quietly through the bamboo grove trail on Samhoseom Island thanks to the wooden deck laid along the wetlands and ecological waterways. You can also watch migratory birds swimming or eating in the Taehwagang River at the bird observatory. In addition, you can see dace in spring, sweetfish in summer, and salmon returning to the mother stream in winter.  If you walk along the deck road in the dense bamboo forest and wetland, there are stepping stones upstream of the Taehwagang River. When you cross the river on the stepping stones, you will find Dajeon Village, a tea plantation in Ulsan, and a rock with the legend of Belikkeut on Baekni-gil. According to legend, there was once a big flood during the rainy season. When an elder brother saved his wife before his sister, the sister sang a song of sorrow. The song was passed down in Ulsan as a rice-planting song.  There is a mysterious feeling when it rains in Samho grove. You can take a walk there if you want to feel the mystique of bamboo groves.

stories.title: Taehwagang River Area – Sogeumpo History Museum
stories.audioTitle: Taehwagang River Area – Sogeumpo History Museum
stories.script: Is there salt from the river? “Ulsan Sogeumpo History Museum” In the Joseon Dynasty, Ulsan was famous for salt because it had many salterns. There were four major salterns in Ulsan, three of which were located downstream of the Taehwagang River. They all made “Jayeom,” which is salt made differently from sea salt. Jayeom is salt made by boiling cast-iron pots filled with seawater in a hut called sogeummak in Korean. All salt made from the Taehwagang River was Jayeom. Ulsan's Jayeom was a very famous product in the Joseon Dynasty. As a result, it was sold all over Korea through Jukryeong to Wonju's Sibiryeong Pass. Salt was the payment for Jwasuyeong soldiers (naval soldiers) during the Joseon Dynasty. Located downstream of the Taehwagang River, Yeompo-dong was once a port for trading Jayeom. It is now occupied by automobile shipping carriers. “Yeompo” means a port that trades salt. There is a Sogeumpo History Museum in Yeompo-dong.  At the Sogeumpo History Museum, you can learn about the history of salt in Ulsan. Also, you can learn about the history of salterns and the port before the automobile factory was built. There is also information about Sam-cheol Yoon, the last salt vendor in Ulsan, the location of the old saltern, the geography and environment of Ulsan, and how Jayeom is made. Sogeumpo History Museum also won a prize at the Ulsan Architecture Award in 2021. It is fun to look for architectural elements that relate to salt. Every Saturday, you can also do salt painting or make bath salts.

stories.title: Other Areas – Ulsan Local Confucian School
stories.audioTitle: Other Areas – Ulsan Local Confucian School
stories.script: “Ulsan Local Confucian School,” a school in the Joseon Dynasty The Local Confucian school is a tangible cultural property. It was the public education institution in the Joseon dynasty. At that time, each village had a local Confucian school. People revered Kongzi as an old sage and learned about his character and studies here.  Ulsan Local Confucian school is estimated to have been built around the 15th century. Originally, it was located in Gugyo Village, which is now Bangu-dong. During the Imjin War, the building was destroyed and moved to its present location in 1652. During the relocation, the main facilities of the Hyanggyo, including the Daeseongjeon Shrine, were built, and five rooms over the gateway were built in 1711 (the 37th year of King Sukjong). The present structure was developed in 1796 (the 20th year of King Jeongjo). Although it was rebuilt 26 times after 1800, the main buildings were arranged at right angles to the north-south and east-west axes, preserving the typical characteristics of its architecture. Local Confucian schools are typically divided into Confucian shrines and Hakdang academies. After passing Changwonru Pavilion, the entrance to Ulsan Local Confucian school, there is Myeongnyundang Lecture Hall, a Hakdang academy where students studied, in front of the entrance. If you go down the road between Myeongnyundang Lecture Hall and the library, there is a gate to Jeonsacheong Hall. The low stone walls and old wooden side gates are quaint features that you might see in historical dramas. There is a large cypress that seems to have lived since the Joseon Dynasty in the yard. This is a great place for photos along with the tiled roof and stone walls. You can also rent hanbok costumes and experience what it is like to be a Confucian scholar in Sung Kyun Kwan.

stories.title: Other Areas – Dalcheon Iron Mine and Soeburi Festival
stories.audioTitle: Other Areas – Dalcheon Iron Mine and Soeburi Festival
stories.script: Digging into the history of iron in the Samhan  “Dalcheon Iron Mine and Soeburi Festival” Dalcheon Iron Mine is an iron ore mine that dates back to the Samhan period. It is also believed to have been the largest iron producer in Yeongnam since the ancient Samhan period. Here we can see the origins of Ulsan's industrial history as far back as ancient times. Iron mines are places where iron ore or soil mixed with iron was mined. Like the remains of iron manufacture in Hwangseong-dong, Gyeongju, the iron excavated from the Dalcheon Iron Mine was confirmed to contain arsenic, making it a historically important site. In addition, it is believed that Seok Talhae was the first blacksmith at Dalcheon Iron Mine before he became the 4th king of Silla. It is also said that the Dalcheon Iron Mine, associated with Seok Talhae, is where the Korean goblin legend began. According to the ancient Chinese books Book of the Later Han, Records of the Three Kingdoms, Book of Wei, and Biographies of Wuhan, Xianbei, and Dongyui, it is stated that iron from the Dalcheon Iron Mine in Ulsan was also used in Japan during the Samhan Period. In the literature, the first record about the Dalcheon Iron Mine can be found in the Geography Section of the Annals of King Sejong recorded in 1452, which states that 12,500 geun of iron were stored in Dalcheon. It is said that large amount of iron was mined to produce weapon at the Dalcheon Iron Mine in Ulsan after the Imjin War and Manchu War of 1636.  The mine produced iron ore and serpentine until the late 1990s, but now it is closed. The Soeburi Festival is held at the Dalcheon Iron Mine for three days every May. The term Soeburi refers to the process of mining, melting, and pounding. Plus, you can always experience Soeburi culture at Dalcheon Iron Mine Exhibition Hall and Dalcheon Iron Mine History Park.

stories.title: Other Areas – Ihyujeong Pavilion+ Yongyeon Seowon Confucian Academy
stories.audioTitle: Other Areas – Ihyujeong Pavilion+ Yongyeon Seowon Confucian Academy
stories.script: Cultural assets preserved by descendants, “Ihyujeong Pavilion+ Yongyeon seowon Confucian Academy” Ihyujeong pavilion is a hanok designated as cultural heritage material of Ulsan in 1997. This is the gatehouse (a house with a gate) above the south entrance of Hakseonggwan Guesthouse, which was the guesthouse (where officials on business trips and foreign envoys stayed) of Ulsan's local government. This gatehouse has existed since the Joseon Dynasty, but it was converted and used as a library for some time until it was demolished in 1940 when Ulsan Elementary School expanded its campus. The house of Hakseong Yi in Ulsan purchased it and converted it into a house with an ondol room. The building was then destroyed by a fire in 2003, but was restored in June 2005 and completed in November 2007. The building still preserves the shape of the gatehouse of the late Joseon Dynasty. Next to Ihyujeong pavilion, there is a hanok called Yongyeon Seowon Confucian Academy and its annexes. Yongyeon Seowon Confucian Academy is a place to commemorate Yi Ye, who served as the first envoy to Japan during the reign of King Sejong. He was an envoy to Japan who saved 667 Koreans by travelling back and forth 40 times on the sea road between Korea and Japan, which is difficult to do even today. Yongyeon Seowon Confucian Academy was built in the 13th year of King Yeongjo (1737 AD), and was demolished in the 5th year of King Gojong (1868) by an abolition order issued by Daewongun. It was restored in 2001 at a cost of about 1 billion won. If you visit Donggulpia, you should stop by the Ihyujeong pavilion and the Yongyeon Seowon Confucian Academy, which are located in nearby residential areas, and feel the quiet atmosphere of a Joseon Dynasty hanok.

stories.title: Sanneomi Farm
stories.script: Boasting as one of the finest mountain view in Korea, Sanneomi Farm is a black goat farm and a spot where numerous campers come to enjoy nature and unwind, located in the wild at 700-900 meters high above sea level.  The location was once a farmland for slash-and-burn agriculture, and opened Sanneomi Black Goat Farm in 1983. Now, the farm owner Lim Seong-nam grazes black goats based on eco-friendly natural circulation following in his father’s footsteps. It is said this farm is the second largest black goat farm in Korea. It feels blissfully peaceful to see the black goats leisurely grazing here and there on the foot of the mountain.  The landscape is stunning as the farm with karst topography of the Alps. The farm owner Lim Seong-nam first had the idea of turning his farm into a large farm for tourism as more and more people came to enjoy the scenery. However, after camping was prohibited at Yukbaek Majigi, a tourist spot across the mountain, Lim decided to open his farm as a camping site.  Here, you can not only camp, but also enjoy experiences like collecting wild edible greens, trekking, and feeding black goats. If you go up to the TV series filming site, you can look down the panoramic view of Sanneomi Farm at a glance. Looking up, you will see a clean, cloudless sky. The strong wind of Daegwallyeong pushes all clouds away. Lower your head again to stare ahead to see the ridges of the mountain of Gangwon-do dancing like waves.  You can see Yukbaek Majigi, a former site of old slash-and-burn farming, right ahead across the mountain. The wind power generators line up along the ridge creating a fascinating landscape.  Open up your ears, nose, and eyes to the sound, fragrance, and sights that you have not experienced at Swiss-style Sanneomi Farm. Here, you will discover what true healing is all about under the high and clear sky, in fresh wind, and listening to the pleasant humming of birds.

stories.title: Yukbaek Majigi
stories.script: Pyeongchang is very short of farming lands as 80% of its area is mountainous. Thus, slash-and-burn farmers had to climb the mountain to cultivate their fields. Yukbaek Majigi, a plain as large as six soccer fields combined that was formed on the top of Cheongoksan Mountain, was created in the same way. At first, in the 1960s, the slash-and-burn farmers settled on the top of the mountain and cultivated the wasteland, making Korea’s first highland vegetable farms.   Meaning a plain large enough to sow 10,800 kg of rice seeds, Yukbaek Majigi is not only a farm, but also has wild flower beds in some section, which invites a number of tourists. Driving a car along the meandering mountain road, you will see the wind power generators along the ridge of the mountain. The landscape you will see while going up will the make your heart already beat fast.  The most beautiful season of Yukbaek Majigi is between June and July. Around this time, Shasta daisies are in full bloom in the wide field making the space a snow white flower garden. Shasta daisy is not colorful but blooms wide and full throughout the meadow, creating a spectacular view just like the Alps.  .  In summer, a cool wind will blow from the summit of the Cheongoksan Mountain to cool you off; in autumn, the endlessly spreading field of napa cabbage creates yet another amazing scenery. In winter, the blanket of snow warmly covers the frozen land. There are perfect photo spots here and there, such as a mini castle-shaped structure and a rainbow chair where you can take photos against the mountain ranges.  Offering gorgeous sights throughout the year, Yukbaek Majigi is like a flower that has come into bloom on the soil made by the slash-and-burn farmers. The land earned from the sweat of their brow will let you feel the landscape, fragrance, and energy gifted by nature, free from pressures and worries of life. Every moment and scenery of Yukbaek Majigi is a gift.

stories.title: Bongpyeong Traditional Market
stories.script: “The hillside is fully covered with buckwheat fields, and the flowers beginning to bloom like scattered grains of salt make a breathtaking scenery in graceful moonlight.”  The buckwheat fields that embroider all around in pure white even without moonlight presents us with a breathtaking landscape. Thanks to When Buckwheat Flowers Bloom, a representative short story of Yi Hyoseok, Bongpyeong, once just a small rural village, has now become a place representing the Korean Literature.  The Bongpyeong Traditional Market is a 5-day traditional market held at the center of the village. In Yi’s short story, Bongpyeong is the place revisited by a peddler because he cannot forget the woman he poignantly loved there. The market takes places on dates ending in the number 2 or 7. On a market day, the place is crowded with more than 100 stores, stalls, and visitors and tourists who come to look around.  The highland vegetables and wild greens produced in Pyeongchang along with other diverse foods are abundant. However, among all the best title belongs to buckwheat. If you miss buckwheat flowers due to an early season, don’t be disappointed. Memilmuk (buckwheat jelly), memil guksu (buckwheat noodles), memil jijim (pan-fried buckwheat pancake), and memil jeonbyeon (buckwheat crepe) will welcome you from anywhere in the market, making up for the flowers. The generous memil jijim is pan-fried by hands of an old lady sitting at the stall tastes exceptional.  Buckwheat is highly nutritious, rich in protein and vitamins. According to Boncho gangmok (General List of Herbal Medicine), buckwheat is good for intestine and stomach and makes your mind refreshed by energizing your body. The taste is not fancy but simple and earthy, taste of hominess.  In the short story, Mr. Heo, the peddler, didn’t sell much in the market, but that is no longer true at the Bongpyeong Traditional Market flocked by people from all over the country.

stories.title: Odaesan National Park
stories.script: Odaesan National Park  Odaesan National Park, designated as the 11th national park in Korea, is renowned for its vibrant autumn foliage. With gorgeous scenery comparable to Geumgangsan Mountain, it has earned the nickname “Little Geumgangsan Mountain” (小金剛). Starting with Birobong Peak at 1,563 meters above sea level, the range includes Dongdaesan Peak, Durobong Peak, Sangwangbong Peak, and Horyeongbong Peaks, lined up like a natural backdrop, creating a magnificent view.  The entrance features an accessible 2-km fir tree forest path that people of all ages can enjoy. Walking along this refreshing trail lined with towering fir trees, you’ll feel invigorated by the pure, fresh air.  As you continue along the forest path, you’ll reach the Iljumun Gate of Woljeongsa Temple, the head temple of the 14th diocese of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. Founded in the 12th year of Queen Seondeok’s reign during the Silla Dynasty, Woljeongsa Temple boasts a thousand-year history and houses numerous cultural treasures, including the Octagonal Nine-story Stone Pagoda and the Wooden Seated Child Manjusrī statue. Odaesan Mountain has long been regarded as a center of Buddhist culture, preserving historic Buddhist sites such as Sangwonsa Temple, Jeokmyeolbogung Hall, Bukdaesa Temple, Jungdaesa Temple, and Seodaesa Temple, along with significant sites like the Odaesansago National History Archives.  Odaesan National Park is a sacred site for Korean Manjusri worship and a historic place that once housed the Odaesansago National History Archives, where the “Annals of the Joseon Dynasty” were stored. This weekend, why not spend some time at Odaesan National Park, where you can experience the beauty of nature and the spirit of history?

stories.title: Odaesan Healing Village (Byeolmaru)
stories.script: Odaesan Healing Village is a village company that is operated by local residents of Jinbu-myeon, who developed the brand, Byeolmaru.  All residents of the Odaesan Healing Village are forest experts who took the forest commentary course and earned a certificate. They are proud of their programs where visitors can star watch and enjoy pure nature of Pyeongchang at an altitude of 700 meters above sea level in a Nordic walking program for first hand appreciation of the forest. In particular, the Nordic walking program is unique in that it lets you walk even on the snow using gears like snow shoes.  The residents also sell salted highland napa cabbages, onions, and more, and in winter, they offer a kimchi-making program as a seasonal experience program. In the program, you can make delicious kimchi with fresh highland napa cabbages grown in clean nature.  The sound of first-class water in Odaecheon Stream, the source of Hangang River, the sound of refreshing wind, the green pine forest, and fragrant wild flowers. A day at Odaesang Healing Village is all about nature.

stories.title: Balwangsan Cable Car and Gi Skywalk
stories.audioTitle: Balwangsan Cable Car and Gi Skywalk
stories.script: Balwangsan Mountain is a mountain as high as 1,458 meters above sea level located in Gangwon-do. In winter, it snows a lot so many skiers visit this place. It is the 12th highest mountain in Korea, but people can go to the top easily by a cable car.  The cable car, operated by Yong Pyong Resort, is as long as 7.4 kilometers. It goes up and down along the ridge of Balwangsan Mountain, allowing you to enjoy not only the landscape but thrills. You can feast your eyes for all seasons with colorful flowers in spring, lush greenery in summer, multi-hued fall foliage in autumn, and white snowflakes in winter.  To feel the nature of Pyeongchang, it is enough to look around the landscape of Balwangsan Mountain on a cable car, however, if you want to feel the energy of Balwangsan Mountain, walk on the Gi Skywalk where you can get fresh energy. After you get off the cable car, you can conveniently move to the Gi Skywalk through the elevator. It is a tourist facility least restrictive for the vulnerable such as persons with disabilities and the elderly.  The center of the Gi Skywalk, there is a turn table that turns 360 degrees, which lets visitors appreciate the breathtaking view of Baekdudaegan Mountain Range from all directions just in one spot. If the weather is clear, you can even see out to the sea of Gangneung. It is also the point from which you can enjoy not only the sunrise from the east sea but also the sunset to the west mountain.  When you stand on the Gi Skywalk, it feels as if you are filled with healthy energy from the mountain stretching beneath your feet and from the sky above you.  After filling yourself with energy, follow the forest trail to the top of Balwangsan Mountain. There are three major Gi Trails, such as Baraemgil Trail, Balwangsu Garden Deck Road, and Jumok Healing Forest Trail, all neat with wooden decks. Walk slowly along the landscape and enjoy nature. On the way, you will see the rest area where you can rest and drink Balwangsu, cool mineral water, to quench your thirst.  When you buy the cable car ticket, present your digital tourist identification card to get 30% discount.

stories.title: Samyang Farm
stories.script: You will spot sheep leisurely grazing on a stretched open meadow. Fleecy clouds in the blue sky seem so close as if you can reach out and catch them. With a postcard-like landscape, it is not the Alps in the Switzerland but a group of farms in Daegwallyeong, Pyeongchang, Gangwon-do.  The biggest charm of Samyang Farm is that you can closely see and touch animals. It is thus popular not only among children but also adults from the city.  Samyang Farm, one of the oldest farms in Daegwallyeong, was created in 1972. At that time, when foods were scarce, Jeong Yun-jung, the late chairman of Samyang Foods, was determined to supply high-quality protein to people by raising cows. With this willingness, he cultivated the land as large as 7.5 times of Yeouido in Daegwallyeong into a grassland. It was previously called Samyang Farm, but in 2011, it was renamed Eco Green Campus as it started to graze cows in nature following organic stockbreeding.  Eco Green Campus is divided into sections 1-5 of 4.5 km trail along the wooden fence from the entrance to the highest point of the farm, Dong Hae Observatory. Each section has its own story: Hill of Wind, a section for taking a tour around the observatory; Relaxation in the Forest, a section for walking down the meadow that is in harmony with more than 50 wind power generators; Memory of Love, a section for visiting the filming site of Lovers’ Concerto and the famous tree in the film, A Stroll on Meadow, a section to say hello to grazing sheep, cows, and ostriches, and Rest for Your Heart, a section that detours the sheep herding performance stage and connects back to the entrance.  Eco Green Campus lets you enjoy not only the scenic landscapes but also various experience programs. The most popular one is the shepherding performance. It is amazing and exciting to watch the agile shepherd dog galloping to lead a herd of sheep this way and that way skillfully. After the performance, you can go beyond the fence in the meadow to feed the sheep or take pictures with the flock of sheep as a background.  If you slightly walk down from the shepherding performance stage, you will see the animal experience center where you can feed milk to lambs. The farm market sells milk manju made from organic milk produced at Samyang Farm, handmade burger, and Samyang Ramen.  Daegwallyeong Yangtte Ranch opened in 1988 as Pungjeon Ranch exclusively for shepherding. In 2000, it changed its identity as a tourist farm and was renamed. Daegwallyeong Yangtte Ranch is smaller than Eco Green Campus or Sky Ranch, but it is small and charming.  In the middle of the farm, you can experience feeding sheep with hay. Sheep are not afraid of human and watching them stick out their head to eat hay is simply adorable. Both sheep grazing in the meadow and sheep eating hay from tourists are plump, so you can probably presume that they are happily thriving in the farm.  Sky Ranch, established in the similar period to Samyang Farm, became open to the public only in 2014. Not only has it preserved pure nature as it is located on Seonjaryeong Pass, the highest pass in Daegwallyeong, but also it has kept its eco-system intact as little to none had access to it for 40 years. As the farm grazes sheep and horses during winter as well, you will be able see animals romping around in the snow field.  Unlike other farms, you can also have various experiences in the farm, in particular, it offers horseback riding and horseback trekking. You can also feed hay and milk to baby animals at the baby animal zoo in front of the straw and plants yard.  Sky Ranch tractor carriage tour will grab your attention. They made a special wooden carriage usually seen in a cowboy movie and connected it to the rear of a tractor. Riding the carriage, you can go up to the Haneulmaru Overlook that is at a 3 km distance away. It is about 15 minutes to the overlook. You can enjoy the surrounding landscape at the overlook and ride the carriage back down again, or walk down yourself feeling the refreshing breeze of Seonjaryeong Pass. You will be led by walkable and beautiful walking trails, such as Broad Landscape Trail, Border Forest Trail, and Forest Rapids Trail.

stories.title: Pyeongchang Olympic Market
stories.script: Pyeongchang Olympic Market, located in a town in Pyeongchang-gun, has a long history as it was registered as a regular marketplace with a market building in 1955. It was originally called Pyeongchang Traditional Market, but in 2018, when Pyeongchang was selected as the host city of the Winter Olympic, it was renamed Pyeongchang Olympic Market.  This market has more than 40 stores. The market is open all year round, but the fifth-day market opens on dates ending with 5 or 10. The market that takes place on dates ending with 5 is especially famous, providing various experiences.  If you visit Pyeongchang Olympic Market, there are foods must try. They are made of buckwheat and corns, representative ingredients produced in Pyeongchang.  You will find buckwheat related foods here like memil buchigi (buckwheat pancake), kotdeungchigi guksu (buckwheat noodles), and memil cha (buckwheat tea) which are the best. Among others, the memil buchigi (buckwheat pancake), a symbol of Gangwon-do, was first sold at Pyeongchang Traditional Market since the 1970s.  Olchaengi guksu (tadpole noodles) and kotdeungchigi guksu (buckwheat noodles), only found in Gangwon-do, is traditional dishes of the province made of corns. Olcghaengi guksu (tadpole noodles) was named after olchangi, a Korean word for tadpole due to the shape resemblance. Kotdeungchigi guksu (buckwheat noodles) was named after the image where the noodles hit the tip of your nose when you slurp and eat them. The taste of noodles is simple but kimchi and seasoned toppings will add more flavors to the dish.  Lastly, there are susu bukkumi (millet pancake) and corn makgeoli (corn rice wine). If you pair mashed pat (red bean) wrapped susu bukkumi (millet pancake) together with corn makgeoli (corn rice wine) will make your day perfect.  Another special thing about Pyeongchang Olympic Market is that various wall paintings liven up the mood. There are other numerous things to see as well. What about having fun of a marketplace at Pyeongchang Olympic Market which is filled with things to eat and enjoy?

stories.title: Dutasan Recreational Forest
stories.script: Dutasan Recreational Forest is a mountainous recreational forest located at the foot of Dutasan Mountain on 1,394 meters above sea level on the border of Jinbu-myeon and Jeongseon-gun, Pyeongchang-gun, Gangwon-do. Located on the west of Taebaek Mountain Range, where clear water falls from the source of Odaesan Mountain through the clean valley to where the leisure industry blooms.  The west part of Taebaek Mountain Range has a well-developed mountainous valley and a thick pine forest. The campsite is in the valley across the management office of the recreational forest. The deck established in the dense pine forest beside the valley has lots of shadowy grounds, which make it cool to rest there. In particular, the autumn foliage is famous for its beauty. If you walk a little up the valley from the campsite, you can see a rocky slopes beside the debris dam and a small waterfall in the upper side of the area.  You can see the healthy and robust forest as home to wild animals, such as Asian badgers, raccoons, boars, and hares, medicinal herbs, and large trees like firs, birches, nut pines, and liden trees. There are also Seonnyeotang Valley in Achagol that is located in a serene area along with a well for rabbits, which are unique to watch.  As a typical mountainous recreational forest, Dutasan Recreational Forest has well paved forest trails: Dutasan Dulle Trail, a 13.3 km course for professional hikers that goes through Chilseongdae Peak, the high peak of Dutasan Mountain, and other main peaks, Recreational Forest Dulle Trail, a 8.4 km course for going through nation-owned trails   for hiking lovers, Hiking Trail, a 5.9 km course for climbing the high peak, and the 3.2 km course for looking around the surroundings of the recreational forest.  To help you enjoy the courses, they also offer Dutasan Recreational Forest Trail Senior School on weekdays and in off-season. Besides from that, from March to November, there are programs for families, such as forest education, forest play, forest commentary and three-day event for celebrating the family month in May.

stories.title: Mill Bridge
stories.script: Near the Bangadari Mineral Spring, which has been famous since the Joseon dynasty, a unique cultural complex was established. It feels as if you are at a forest in North Europe with the white buildings that are in harmony with green firs. It is Mill Bridge, an English name of Bangadari Mineral Spring.  The surroundings of the Bangadari Mineral Spring became a wasteland after the Korean War. In the 1950s, the late Kim Ik-ro started to create a forest which has been transformed into what it is today through more than 60 years of cultivation. With the total of 100,000 trees, including firs and larches, have been artificially planted. From the entrance of Mill Bridge to the mineral spring, there is a 300 meter long fir forest, which is the main result of the cultivation.  However, the deteriorated facilities have been abandoned in the national park in Odaesan Mountain, and has damaged the natural landscape and threatened the safety of visitors. Thus, the existing facilities were renovated and improved centering around the Bangadari Mineral Spring, newly turning into a natural education center of Odaesan Moutain.  Mill Bridge, designed by Seung H-Sang, the top architecture of Korea, has a forest trail that uses the environment of fir forest to the fullest, wild flower garden, wetland park, meditation garden, gallery, coffee shop, accommodation, and a space for education and culture in line with the forest.  The small and large buildings surrounded by the firs standing straight toward the sky look like a part of forest. The space is not fancy, but it is a cozy rest area providing oneness with nature where you can forget the complicated life in the city for a while.  The accommodation has 18 rooms. The wide window that takes in the forest landscape, white walls, and wooden furniture will naturally draw your attention back to the forest even when inside.  Mill Bridge, where you can spend a peaceful time free from the busy routines, is not only perfect as a recreational forest but also a place for education where children can experience nature. Even without spending a night there, you can experience forest through day experience programs.  Visitors will be greeted with various experience programs, such taking part in the forest commentary with a guide, making bread board with hinoki cypress, making dream catcher, meditating in a hammock, singing ball meditation, and treeplaying as part of the forest sports.  While you stay at Mill Bridge, time will go slowly and quietly. Walk down the trail filled with firs and larches in light clothes and feel the energy from the forest. You don’t have to have a set destination as you will feel your day enriched with the forest and nature.

stories.title: Farm Herbnara
stories.script: Lee Ho-sun and Lee Du-i, a married couple, decided to live a farm life at the year when their ages added up hit 100. They looked for a suitable land all around Korea and found perfect one for them in Pyeongchang. It was first stony land and they had to pick countless stones out and cultivate the soil to make the field. Then, they started to plant herbs and grow them. In 1996, three years after, they opened Korea’s first herb-themed tourist farm, Farm Herbnara.  Starting from the area of 990 ㎡, the farm is now 33,000 ㎡, becoming a renowned tourist spot in Pyeongchang and the birthplace of herb industry in Korea. As a successful model of the 6th industry through herb cultivation, psroduct development, and sales, the Farm Herbnara has earned New Knowledge Farm Award in 2008 and was selected one of the 20 Ecological Tourist Destination by the Ministry of Environment in 2009.  Farm Herbnara consists of more than 10 themed gardens, in which more than 150 herbs, such as lavender, sage, and buckwheat, are growing in different sections. Each garden has distinct characteristics: Palette Garden with colorful herbs and flowers, Shakespeare Garden with herbs mentioned in works of Shakespeare, Butterfly Garden with honey plants loved by bees and butterflies and more.  There is also a Medieval Garden where you can find statues of goddess of four seasons. There is a woman holding a flower symbolizing spring, a woman holding the grape symbolizing summer, a woman holding oats symbolizing autumn, and a woman holding a tree symbolizing winter. Right beside them, the fountain in the middle is surrounded by baby musicians with tambourine, mandolin, cymbals, and pipe. If there is a land where Greek and Roman gods dwell, it might be Farm Herbnara.  The Starlight Stage specially named by singer Lee Moon-sae, holds concerts by famous singers. The herb experience class offers programs such as making natural soap and scented candles. Aroma Fountain, the herb gallery, is the place to learn about the history of herbs, herbs around the world, how to use herbs, and aroma therapy in detail. Han teo wul, the Turkish gallery the owners made to introduce Turkey, a country that feels close yet is far to display Turkish culture.  Farm Herbnara that delights all your five senses did not forget about your appetite. At Birch House, a restaurant operated by Lees, you can taste dishes topped by herbs produced from the farm.  From the days as new and humble farmers, Lees plowed the land and planted seeds. Those seeds now bloomed into flowers and grew into trees to form a fragrant garden. Come to this fairytale-like garden with flowers that bloom all four seasons and be enraptured in its beautiful fragrance.

stories.title: Citizen's Forest
stories.script: Citizen's Forest is a national forest open to the public to enjoy various experiences in the forest. It is located near the (former) Daegwallyeong Service Area on the 700 meters above sea level, an altitude that is believed to be most healthy for human biorhythms. It has a hiking course of 3.95 kilometers for which it takes about 1.5 hours to finish.  At the entrance of the forest, there is a board that reads the Forest Hiking Course of Citizen's Forest. When you climb the stairs to the forest, larches will greet you first. Tall larches form a dense forest with sunlight shining through the branches, give off mysterious mood. When the larch forest ends, the fir forest starts. Green all year round, firs are full of integrity even in winter. When it snows, you don’t have to envy North European snow fields.  Walk along the dirt path that goes around the mountainside and you will feel oneness with nature as you see firs, taxus, Norway spruces, nut pines, larix kaempferi, and a birch forest as well as wild flowers blooming here and there. As the forest is mainly filled with coniferous trees that are rich in phytoncide, your body and mind will be healed fully simply by walking.  Daegwallyeong was once forest turned into fields through slash-and-burn farming, but the farmers moved out in 1968 and the place was abandoned for years. In 1975, Yeongdong Expressway opened and the plan for afforestation of nearby land was implemented for 11 years where trees were planted continuously during that period. However, Daegwallyeong had harsh climate for trees with strong wind, cold temperature, and heavy snow. Thus, trees couldn’t grow well.  The residents installed fish nets and windbreak nets made from bush clover to protect young trees from the wind. They also installed wood poles so that the roots of the trees won’t be damaged by wind and wood fencing with 50 m intervals so that the trees can resist against the wind. They kept making strenuous efforts to make the forest healthy, carrying fertilizer on jige (Korean A-frame) to manure the land to prevent the land from becoming barren and also pruned the branches.  Through their perseverance, the wasteland of Daegwallyeong became today’s luxuriant forest. It was designated as Korean Forest Culture Property in 2014 and Masterpiece National Forest in 2022. It became a forest full dream and hope of children, a beautiful forest presenting leisure and healthy to people when they are exhausted. Citizen's Forest, after bearing hardship and adversity, is now encouraging healthy and happy life of citizens.

stories.title: Okcheon Catholic Church
stories.script: Okcheon Catholic Church is an one of a kind cathedral with the light gray, pastel-tone exterior. Similar to the buildings in Santorini Island, Greece, Okcheon Catholic Church was constructed in 1955. It is the only cathedral of that age in Chungcheongbuk-do.  Catholicism was first introduced in Okcheon around 1900. After that moment, the number of Catholics steadily increased until the first parish church was established in Imun-dong, Okcheon-eup with Rev. Hong Byeong-cheol (Luca) as appointed provost. Rev. Hong Byeong-cheol performed his missionary for the farmers who cultivated the land owned by the parish church, and it led to a great increase in the number of Catholics. The current Okcheon Catholic Church is a western architecture building that was built when Father Roy D. Petipren, who belonged to the American Maryknoll Society, was appointed as the eighth provost of the Okcheon region after the Korean War.  The bell hanging in the bell tower was brought from France in 1955. The church was used in an oblong shape for about 40 years, and in 1991, it was extended into a long cross shape. The antechapel in the front has a gable roof and an arch-shaped gate with the bell tower at the center, which forms the interior of the church today.  The Cultural Heritage Administration evaluates the Okcheon Catholic Church as not only is it the only Catholic church in Chungcheongbuk-do that was built in the 1950s, but also it holds a profound significance for the study of the changes in church architecture as it retains the typical form of a local cathedral built after the national liberation. In 2002, the Okcheon Catholic Church was designated as a National Registered Cultural Heritage.  The Okcheon Catholic Church is a rising star as a tourist spot on social media with not only its architectural value but also in its unique exterior. The pastel-tone church is of course beautiful during the day, but it has another charm during sunset that goes in harmony with the ruddy sky. Standing imposingly on a hill, the Okcheon Catholic Church is a beautiful petite church where the fragrance of faith softly emanates with the clear sound of its bell.

stories.title: Hyangsu Baengni Bike Road
stories.script: Toward the eastern end of great grand plains. Meanders the streamlet babbling its antique stories, where pigment-stained bull unrestrainably sustains the golden moos in his idle cries. That place, how could I ever forget even in dream?  Okcheon, the hometown of Poet Jeong Ji-yong who imagificated nostalgia and longing for his hometown into poetic words. His poem Hyangsu (Nostalgia) made his hometown Okcheon a hometown for everyone. In Okcheon, a friendly and nostalgic village like your own hometown, has Hyangsu Baengni Bike Road, a cozy bike road. It is a nice rural road with a beautiful landscape of the Daecheongho Lake and the literary feeling of Hyangsu.  The beginning of the bike road is the Jeong Jiyong Literature Gallery and Birthplace, where you can look into the life of the poet. Jeong Ji-yong, who used a highly trained astonishing words in his poems, is the first modern poet of Korea. His literature gallery and birthplace shows a peek inside the world of his poems. The birthplace where he grew up is equipped with a thatched roof, a twig gate, a well and crocks. Outside the stone wall, you can see the memorial stone for his poem and a streamlet. Jeong Jiyong Literature Gallery is behind the house.  From the birthplace, you can continuously ride a bicycle along the road side 37 of the national route, famously known beotkkot-gil (cherry blossom walkway), to Janggye Tourist Area.  At Janggye Tourist Area, there is a Brave New World which is made under the theme of literary world of the poet Jeong Ji-yong. It is the core space of the poetry art belt that serves as a place for rest.  You can catch your breath here to once again ride strong toward the golden ripples of Daecheongho Lake. You can also appreciate the shape of Korean Peninsula that is made by the curving Geumgang River from the Dunjubong Peak in Annam-myeon, and vigorously ride the bicycle along the scenic riverside of the Geumgang River. After a while, you will be able to see Geumgang Service Area and Geumgang Recreation Area where you can find the finest scenery in Korea.  Hyangsu Baengni Bike Road is good for beginners. It is about 50 km long and it takes about 4 hours to go from one end to the other. Hyangsu Baengni Bike Road in Okcheon, the village where Geumgang River comes in and goes out. You can ride a bicycle enjoying the poetry and the beauty of nature, a place you could never forget even in a dream.

stories.title: Okcheon Traditional Culture Center
stories.script: Located deep inside the inland, Okcheon has rich soil due to the clean water from Geumgang River with scenic natural environment, and a long history of culture and tradition. In Okcheon, people began to live dating back to the prehistoric age. The prehistoric remains were excavated in Daecheon-ri and the Anteo Dolmen Site was discovered in Seoktan-ri.  Okcheon Traditional Culture Center is where you can look into such history of Okcheon. Here, you can observe not only archaeological remains but also the traditional culture of Okcheon that goes long back from the Three Kingdoms Period to the present surrounded by rich natural environment.  The permanent exhibition hall displays the education history that has cultivated the spirit of Okcheon residents through the documents on Okcheon Hyanggyo Confucian School, Village School, and Jukhyang Elementary School. The special exhibition hall displays the craft works of transmitters of intangible cultural heritage that represent the Korean traditional craft and the creative works of local artists of Okcheon.  The Okcheon Traditional Culture Center is a cultural complex equipped with exhibition and performance halls, a coffee shop, restaurant, and an accommodation. All buildings are hanok-shaped with graceful elegance. Not only can you stay nights here, but also you can have various experience, such as taking the Korean etiquette and tea ceremony classes, making traditional foods, and making craft works. The large yard is good for enjoying Korean traditional games, including geune (swinging), jegichagi (kicking a jegi), and tuho (throwing arrow).

stories.title: Ijidang Hall in Okcheon
stories.script: Ijidang Hall in Okcheon is a village school that was jointly built by Kim, Lee, Jo, and An families who lived in Okgak-ri, Okcheon-eup in the mid Joseon dynasty. It was once called Gaksin Village School as it was located in front of a village called Gaksin-dong. Here, Jo Heon, a Neo-Confucian scholar of the mid Joseon dynasty, cultivated his pupils. His calligraphy that reads Gaksin Seodang (Village School) is shown on the hanging board of the building.  Ijidang Hall is a pavilion-like building with accommodation that was built to commemorate the accomplishment of Jo Heon. It was renamed Ijidang with the last letter “Ji” from a phrase from Uam Song Si-yeol’s Book of Poetry: “If a mountain is high, one keeping looking up. If one does something great, he keeps doing it.” There are large rocks right beside the path to Ijidang Hall on which Ijidang in Chinese letters is engraved.  Showing the neat and elegant traits of the late Joseon dynasty, Ijidang Hall has the main hall that is 6 kan (distance between pillars) wide and 1 kan deep. It is connected to the annexes, 3 kan on its left and 2 kan on its right. The annexes on the left and right sides have a dual structure. The fact that it has a pavilion on the second floor means it contains a very rare shape compared to the typical architecture style of the time. For this reason, it is viewed to have a high historical, artistic, academic and architectural value.  It preserves the value in architectural history as it was built on the small territory between the Seohwacheon Stream in front of it and the mountain behind of it to limit the damage to the landscape with almost intact original locational values. Thus, it was raised to be designated as a Treasure in 2020.  Ijidang Hall, where you can not only enjoy the style of architecture from the late Joseon dynasty but also appreciate the scenic landscape for all four seasons, is the must-visit spot when you travel in Okcheon.

stories.title: Dunjubong Peak Mini Korean Peninsula
stories.script: The Mini Korean Peninsula in Seonam Village, Yeongwol, Gangwon-do is famously known. However, the fact that Okcheon-gun also has the similar mini Korean Peninsula is not widely known. The Mini Korean Peninsula viewed from Dunjubong Peak located in Yeonju-ri, Annam-myeon, Okcheon-gun is famous among local residents as it is one of best out of the nine scenic sites in Okcheon.  Before you reach the top of Dunjubong Peak, you can see from the observatory the mini Korean Peninsula, which is a magnificent view that is formed by the course of Geumgang River. The geographical feature is 1.45 km long, 1:980 scale of the real size of the Korean Peninsula. It looks like the Korean Peninsula that is flipped left to right. You can bring a small mirror and check how it really resembles the Korean Peninsula.  Many photographers visit the Dunjubong Peak Mini Korean Peninsula for its mysterious landscape, but it is also famous for its hiking course where you can take a walk. The course is good for a forest therapy as you walk between dense pine forest on a gentle slope.  The courses from the Dunjubong Peak are mainly divided into three courses. Course 1 is walk from Dunjubong Peak down to Goseong, then along Geumgang River, and return to the start point; course 2 is walk from the peak down to Geumjeong-gol, then along Geumgang River to pass Geumjeonggol; course 3 is walk from the peak down to Pisil, then following the uphill path to the start point. According to their preferences and conditions, hikers can enjoy various courses.  The Dunjubong Peak is shaped like a pile of stones. It is because it was used as a saddle-shaped earthen ramparts in the Three Kingdoms Period. Look over the flipped Korean Peninsula shape and enjoy a scenic site of Okcheon while hiking.

stories.title: Daecheongho Lake
stories.script: Okcheon first reminds us of Hyangsu (Nostalgia), the poem of Jeong Ji-yong, but it is also a region of Daecheongho Lake. When Daecheong Dam was established in December 1980, a great-sized Daecheongho Lake was created at the same time. It is large enough to be called an inland sea. Daecheongho Lake is a lifeline that supplies not only drinking water but also living water and industrial water for Daejeon and Cheongju regions. It also transformed how the landscape of Okcheon looks. Even without the sea, Okcheon now has a landscape of an archipelago.  With the creation of Daecheongho Lake, numerous mountains and villages had to be submerged under water, but ironically, the rare and precious landscape made by its waterway pleases our eyes. In the landscape, you can find Dunjubong Peak from which you can see the flipped mini Korean Peninsula, Busodamak that resembles Sogeumganggyegok Valley, the beotkkot-gil (cherry blossom walkway) beside the old national route 37 where cherry blossoms blooms splendidly in spring, and Geumgang Recreation Area with a stunning scenery of Geumgang River.  The Hyangsu Hosu-gil Trail that leads from Subuk-ri to Janggye-ri, Annae-myeon, is a trail where you can enjoy the view of the peaceful and scenic waterway. Enjoy hiking in nature to make friends with birds and squirrels and become one with nature by looking down at the wide and blue Daecheongho Lake from the observatory that was once used as an intake tower.  In the early morning, Daecheongho Lake in thick water fog is serene. In the sunset, the lake has a feel of solitary with the silhouette of faraway mountains reflecting off its golden ripples. How does unwinding from your busy schedules by the calm and quiet Daecheongho Lake?

stories.title: Busodamak (Chusojeong)
stories.script: There is a magnificent spectacle formed by mountain peaks that unfolds like a folding screen for about 700 meters in Daecheongho Lake. It is Busodamak. Uam Song Si-yeol called it “Sogeumgang (small Geumgangsan Mountain)” due to its similar resemblance to a miniature of Geumgangsan Mountain.  Busodamak was once a mountain, but the construction of Daecheong Dam made its lower part submerged under water, seemingly making the mountain ridge float on the water. Before the submergence, there were three villages, Chudong, Buso, and Jeolgol Village. Now, only Jeolgol Village remains and the other two villages are under water. The commune “Chuso-ri” was named after the two submerged villages. “Chu” is from Chudong Village and “so” is from Buso Village.  Busodamak was named because it is a mountain floating on water in front of Busomuni Village in Chuso-ri, Gunbuk-myeon, Okcheon-gun. Due to the submergence, the villagers lost their hometown but instead earned beautiful rocks with bizarre shape.  The shape of Busodamak is made up of the bizarre-looking cliff that goes from the north to the southeast of the village for about 700 meters. It looks mesmerizing yet mysterious like a dragon fluttering by on the water.  The trail leads you along the spine of Busodamak, and its gentle slope allows people of all ages to enjoy a walk comfortably. When you pass Jangseong Park at the entrance and climb the hill, you can the a small pavilion Chusojeong. It was named after the village in Chuso-ri. From the pavilion, you can see a panoramic view of the wide open Daecheongho Lake and the bizarre-looking rocks of Busodamak, which forms a breathtaking landscape.  Busodamak is not a single piece of rock, but joints. You can discover the joints on its edge where its inclining shape even looks marvelous. You may be awed by pointed rocks and old pines growing through the crevices, feeling the natural force of Busodamak. It is not surprising that it was selected as one of the most beautiful riversides in Korea in 2008.

stories.title: Yongamsa Temple
stories.script: Yongamsa Temple was built in the 13th year under the reign of King Jinheung of the Silla dynasty. This temple of thousand years of history boasts stunning landscape and was selected by CNN Travel as one of the 50 beautiful places to visit in South Korea.  Don't miss out watching the East and West Three-story Stone Pagodas and Standing Rock-carved Buddha that were created during the Goryeo dynasty. The East and West Three-story Stone Pagodas face each other according to the idea called sancheon-bibo, which means to build pagodas or structures to raise spirit of mountains and streams.  The two pagodas has the same form, even they differ in appearance near the top. The style of each part and the construction method of stone show simplicity. What is remarkable is that the stone pagodas are set up not in front of Daeungjeon Hall but on a low tip of the hill on the northern side of the temple. The location follows the idea of sancheon-bibo, which encourages in forming an ideal site by supplementing natural geographical features and promoting harmony and balance against strong forces. The East and West Three-story Stone Pagodas are the only twin pagodas established according to the teaching of sancheon-bibo.  It is maybe for this reason that Yongamsa Temple looks most beautiful when viewed from the location of the East and West Three-story Stone Pagodas. The temple dormitory for Buddhist monks, Jubuljeon Hall, and Cheonbuljeon Hall beyond them form a spectacular scene that is different from that of any other temples.  The Standing Rock-carved Buddha behind Daeungjeon Hall in Yongamsa Temple shows the beauty of space like an Oriental painting. The upper part of the imposing rock was only carved out for embossed eaves. Water flows out from the narrow clefts on the foot of the rock and the Buddha is engraved in the middle of the tall rock, looking as if wafting in the air.  It is said that Yongamsa Temple was built by Great Master Uishin as he marveled at the graceful shape of the mountain. It was ruined during the Japanese Invasion in 1592, and only maintained its existence, but recently was rebuilt with new Daeungjeon Hall and temple dormitory, restoring its original form.  There is a legend that the last prince of the Silla dynasty stayed here for a while on his way to Geumgangsan Mountain when parted from his father, King Gyeongsun, who was about to surrender to Wang Geon, the founder of the Goryeo dynasty, and would bitterly mourn on Yongbawi Rockface looking at the southern sky.  Many photographers visit this place in early spring or late autumn, the in-between seasons with a large temperature gap between day and night, as it is a perfect spot to see the exquisite harmony of a sea of clouds and the rising sun. You will be marveled watching Okcheon from Yongamsa Temple at the break of the clear day as you will be able to see the red sun rise through the thick clouds covering the world with its hue.

stories.title: Jangnyeongsan Recreational Forest
stories.script: Jangnyeongsan Mountain, 656 meters high above sea level, is a healing spot famous for its stunning and beautiful landscapes. Pines, maples, and broadleaf trees are growing wild, showing off wondrous charm of each season. In particular, the fall leaves form a majestic view. Inside the mountain, there is the Jangnyeongsan Recreational Forest, a favored spot of campers for its beautiful scenery.  The water of Geumcheongyegok Valley never runs dry all year around, flowing through center of the Jangnyeongsan Recreational Forest, makes the place even more outstanding as a refreshing resting place. Not far from the campsite are abundant things to look at and enjoy, such as Seodaesan Dream Resort, Cheonsudonggyegok Valley, and Yongamsa Temple.  The Jangnyeongsan Recreational Forest consists of not only large facilities like multi-purpose playground and outdoor concert garden but also other outdoor facilities, such as large parasols, decks, pavilions, and camping grounds. It also has the accommodation called the House in Forest of various sizes tailored to the conditions of guests, considering whether they are a family, a couple, or a group.  One of the reasons that the Jangnyeongsan Recreational Forest is recognized as a healing spot would be its various programs. There are free programs you can take part in, including a stroll through the forest with commentary, meditation, and forest therapy. The water therapy room where you can enjoy foot bath, and the thermal therapy room where you can enjoy dry sauna, are open as well. Visit the Jangnyeongsan Recreational Forest, the best place for healing in Okcheon, for relaxation in nature.

stories.title: Sangchunjeong Pavilion
stories.script: “Where are you? What are you doing? Do you not want to see the stars with me? I don't want to go somewhere far. But I do want to hold your hand tightly.”  It is part of a lyric from Let’s Go See the Stars, a song by singer Jukjae that became famous when actor Park Bo-gum sang his song. Just like the lyrics, you can go and see the stars at Sangchunjeong Pavilion in Okcheon.  In winter, Sangchunjeong Pavilion is a spot to go where you can see the sky with the Milky Way sprinkled all over. Many people visit this place to take photos during the season when the Milky Way spreads in the night sky. Sangchunjeong Pavilion is a good spot for taking the photos of the Milky Way, but you can take a better picture across with the Sangchunjeong Pavilion as the center.  In the middle of Bocheongcheon Stream that meanders in the east of Okcheon, there is Doksan Mountain. Doksan Mountain has a limestone peak, like Dodamsambong Peaks, a scenic spot that is located in Danyang-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, with a similar shape erected among the waterway. Sangchunjeong Pavilion is on such top of Doksan Mountain in Okcheon established in the 1970s as a modern architectural structure. It is considered as a representative scenic point of Okcheon with a fantastic view.  “Sangchun” means the surrounding landscape is always as beautiful as in spring. For this name, Sangchunjeong Pavilion is famous as the place for photography. As Doksan Mountain stands with its back towards the east, photographers can capture the reflection of the Sangchunjeong Pavilion on the surface of water during sunrise.  Beneath the Sangchunjeong Pavilion, you can see a river as large as a great lake formed by a reservoir keeping the water in Sangye-ri. Across the river, there spread spacious sand beach and the largest field in Okcheon. Looking around from the Sangchunjeong Pavilion, which is the highest spot in the area, you can see the open view of the river and the field.  During the time when water reduces in the river, you can cross the Sanseongbo Reservoir to climb to the pavilion. In summer, when its rains heavily, you should be careful because the reservoir can overflow. On the Sangchunjeong Pavilion that embodies the ancient sages’ idea of harmony between nature and human, take a once-in-a-lifetime photo with the Milky Way in the background.

stories.title: Geumgang Recreation Area (Geumgang Service Area)
stories.script: The Geumgang Recreation Area is a tourist spot of Okcheon that became renowned when the Geumgang Service Area was established after the opening of Gyeongbu (Seoul to Busan) Expressway in 1970.  The headwaters of the Geumgang River is Tteunbongsaem Spring in Jangsu, Jeollabuk-do. The river enriches the land of Muju and Jinan, Geumsan in Chungcheongnam-do, and the northwestern part of Yeongdong, Chungcheongbuk-do to flow into Okcheon-gun. The water goes through Geumsan-gun and Yeongdong-eup before reaching Dongi-myeon, Okcheon-gun, where the Geumgang Recreation Area was established.  Here, the Geumgang Service Area was also constructed so that more people could enjoy themselves while appreciating the scenic view. The design of the Geumgang Service Area focused on using the surrounding landscape of mountains and the connected river to the fullest. The building was set to stand facing the river with the parking lot located at the back. The wide window allows visitors to admire the beautiful landscape.  Each service area in Korea serves different special menu, and the Geumgang Recreation Area is famous for doribaengbaengi (glazed deep-fried fish). The deep-fried fish are boiled in gochujang (red chili paste) and served to eat. The menu is common in villages along the Geumgang River, such as Geumsan, Okcheon, Yeongdong, and Muju.  If you have time, stop by Joryeong-ri Village that is linked through an underpass to the Geumgang Service Area to taste local foods of Okcheon such as saengseon guksu (fish noodles) and doribaengbaengi (glazed deep-fried fish). Saengseon guksu (fish noodles) are delicious spicy noodles made by boiling whole fish that are just caught with gochujang (red chili paste), gochugaru (red chili powder), doenjang (soybean paste), and deulkkae (perilla seed powder).  Geumgang Service Area and the Geumgang Recreation Area sure are full of things to watch and such a captivating landscape for an expressway service area.

stories.title: Dalgusan Mountain
stories.script: An old woman who turned into a stone at Dalgusan Mountain  There is a sharp mountain rising to the left of the entrance to a tea house on the main road from Namhae-eup. A very long time ago, there lived an old couple on the foot of the mountain. The old man was a bad-tempered, greedy man who did not know how to be sorry for what he had done. The old woman, however, was warm-hearted and always kind.  One day outside the gate, a monk knocked on the door while chanting Buddhist prayers for alms. There was no way that the greedy old man would open the door. Instead of giving alms, he replied that there was no owner inside. However, the monk was no ordinary monk. “I can't pass by a wealthy family like this without receiving alms. Save us, merciful Buddha, Bodhisattva of compassion. Save us, merciful Buddha.” The monk kept chanting Buddhist scriptures and asking for alms. Then the old men yelled at him to go away that he had nothing to give.  The monk did not give up. He kept chanting and waited for alms. The old man couldn’t help it, so he donated a sack full of something. However, the sack was filled with cow dungs from the stable. Having finished chanting, the monk calmly accepted the sack, thanked the man, and quietly departed.  The old woman's heart broke seeing all what happened. Then, without her husband's knowledge, she took out grain, followed the monk and donated it to him.  “I am deeply sorry, sir. My husband has a bad temper, so please do not be too upset. Please take this and leave with a good heart.”  Feeling grateful for her sincerity, the monk said in a quiet voice and disappeared. “You will have water coming out of your yard in a few days. Without telling anyone, save yourself at the mountain behind your house. You must not look back while climbing the mountain. Something bad will happen if you talk to anyone or look back.”  Indeed, water gushed out in the middle of the yard a few days later. The old woman panicked and hurriedly ran up the mountain behind the house. As she climbed the mountain, she reached a rock shaped like a chicken and caught her breath. She would often climb up to the rock since she liked chickens.  Unaware of what she was doing, she looked back to see what had happened to her house. After shouting “ugh,” she suddenly turned into a rock. The greedy old man vanished as if the water had washed him away.  After that, people called it Daksan Mountain, meaning the chicken mountain, because the old woman turned into a stone in front of the chicken-shaped rock that she liked. As time passed by, it was named Dalgusan Mountain.

stories.title: Sangsabawi Rock
stories.script: The lovers who turned into serpents and the Sangsabawi Rock  Rocks in Korea are the subject of many legends. In Namhae-gun, there is Sangsangbawi Rock located at the entrance of the hiking trail on the Geumyang side of Geumsan Mountain holding two stories about serpent. It must be because it is the largest and most impressive rock in Geumsan Mountain.  There was a rich man living in a village in Namhae, Gyeongsangnam-do. He had a lot of money and many servants, but he had only one daughter. He raised his daughter with great care. She grew up to become a beautiful woman. She was very popular not only among men in her neighborhood, but in her neighboring villages. Many bachelors snooped around the walls of the rich man's house just to catch a glimpse of the woman.  As for Dolsoe, the servant of the house, he was no different. He loved her so much, but his low social status prevented him from expressing his love or getting close to her. With time, Dolsoe became lovesick, couldn't eat anything and withered away.  A few days after Dolsoe's death, Dolsoe's spirit, which wandered around, turned into a serpent. In the middle of one night, he went into the room where the woman was sleeping and wrapped his body around her. The rich man who saw it the next morning was terrified. He tried his best to get the serpent off his daughter, but it wouldn't budge. He even called a shaman to perform an exorcism, but it didn't work. As the day passed and came the next morning, an old man with a long beard came to the rich man and said,  “If you take your daughter and the serpent to a high cliff on Geumsan Mountain and perform an exorcism, you will avoid disaster.”  After the old man disappeared, the rich man took his daughter to the top of the highest cliff on the mountain. As the exorcism reached its climax, the snake's body began to unravel around the daughter. After it was all unwrapped, it fell down a cliff and died. After that, the villagers called the cliff Sangsabawi Rock, meaning that the lovesick heart was resolved there.  There is also a serpent in the second story about Sangsabawi Rock. A young man from the Shilla Dynasty visited a hermitage in Geumsan Mountain to practice asceticism. He loved a woman in his hometown, but he put her out of his mind and devoted himself to the asceticism. She eagerly awaited the young man's return.
