This unique rock is filled with the holy spirit, showing Jesus praying on Gethsemane if looked at from the graveside and the Blessed Mary standing toward the cross if looked at from the other side.  Montmartre in Paris, a hill of hungry artists, means the hill of pilgrims. Mont means a “hill or a mountain,” and Martre means “pilgrim” in French. Chimyeongjasan Sanctuary, the primary spot for pilgrimage in the Honam area, is the home of faith for pilgrims who admire martyrs; it is Korea’s Montmartre hill.

stories.title: Samcheon-dong Makgeolli Alley
stories.script: Makgeolli is more of a soul food than an alcoholic drink for Koreans. It satisfies your hunger with a little buzz and comforts you when you feel low. It unleashes emotional barriers when you drink with many people. It is just like the warm heart of Korean people.  Jeonju makgeolli is one of the best makgeollis in Korea and it is one of the representative foods of tasty Jeonju along with bibimbap, Korean Table D'hote (hanjeongsik in Korean), and bean sprout and rice soup (kongnamul gukbap in Korean). When you drink makgeolli in Jeonju, you will get drunk with four things. You get drunk with joy, taste, generous snacks, and reasonable price and affection.  The Samcheon-dong Makgeolli Alley is a place to get drunk with the taste and warmth of Jeonju makgeolli. There are a few makgeolli alleys in Jeonju but Samcheon-dong is the original. It is fun to just look around the alley filled with about 20 makgeolli pubs.  The best thing about the Samcheon-dong Makgeolli Alley is generous snack. When you order a kettle of makgeolli, about 20 dishes are served with makgeolli. The snacks alone will fill your stomach.  It is common to see foreigners in the Samcheon-dong Makgeolli Alley. The Samcheon-dong Makgeolli Alley is also designated as the future heritage of Jeonju. If you get hungry when you are in Jeonju, visit the Samcheon-dong Makgeolli Alley and enjoy the taste and warmth of Jeonju.

stories.title: Seohak-dong Art Village
stories.script: Seohak-dong Art Village, also known as the “Teacher’s Village” because many teachers and students attending the Jeonju National University of Education live here, can be found across the Namcheongyo Bridge from Jeonju Hanok Village. The village, which was experiencing a decline with the old downtown, slowly began to change when a married couple who plays music and writes settled down here. Artists like painters, Jasujang (embroidery), and photographers moved here one by one and created galleries, studios, coffee shops, and bookstores, which eventually became an art village. Artists live and perform art in this charming village where art is woven into everyday life.  Past and present, old and new, and natives and artists live in Seohak-dong Art Village in harmony. Take a look at murals and gardens decorated by artists as you walk slowly and enjoy old shops like rice shops, tailor shops, and rice cake shops as well as unique studios, cafes, and galleries. The scent of art will enrich your journey in Jeonju.

stories.title: A Returned Korean-German Nurse in Namhae
stories.audioTitle: A Returned Korean-German Nurse in Namhae
stories.script: The story of Suk Sook-ja who returned to Korea after working as a nurse in Germany  A Korean angle left for Germany One of the main guests of the “Delivery Mudo,” a special episode of a well-known Korean entertainment show Muhandojeon (Infinite Challenge) on MBC, is Suk Sook-ja. In 1973, she left for Germany as a nurse and settled down in a small city called Leichlingen. She was the first Asian woman in the town. Overcoming all sorts of challenges and difficulties, she was dubbed the “Korean angel” since she never lost her smile even during difficult times. At that time, her salary was KRW 15,000 per month, which was 10 times higher than the salary for a nurse in Korea. She sent the money back to Korea, saving KRW 30,000 to KRW 40,000 as spending money in Germany. Sending money back to Korea was recognized as a way to show dedication to the nation and contribute to Korea’s economic growth. After 30 years in the foreign country, she settled down in Namhae, Korea, Suk leads a busy life there, just like in her 20s in Germany. In 2002, she built a house in the German Village in Namhae and named it the “Rosen House.” Her German husband, Joseph, moved to Korea with her but passed away 2 years after. Just like the quiet snow that fell between yellow daffodils bloomed on her first day in Germany in March. “Beautiful Youth, and the Last Stop of Life.” She is putting a great amount of effort into this village as if this is the last stop of her life. Beginning with a German language camp, she contributed to promoting the German Village as the head and held the famous Oktoberfest as well.   <This guide was recorded by Lee Sae-bom of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Hadong Local Poet
stories.script: The story of the Hadong Local Poet Choi Yeong-uk  Poet Choi Yeong-uk is a Hadong local who lives in Pyeongsa-ri, the village that appeared in Toji (“The Land”) written by Park Kyong-ni as well as the setting of a TV series House of Choi Champan. Poet Choi is the prime mover who made this village the mecca of the Toji literature. Started as a big fan of author Park, he became a literary person and built a literature museum dedicated to Park, bringing her novel Toji to life. He designed the House of Choi Champan and built the Toji Literature Road. He truly lived in the world of Park Kyong-ni. At a very young age, Choi decided to be a writer after reading Park's article To the Youth Who Want to Write. Being immersed in the works of Park during his youth, he became a poet in his 40s. After several attempts to gain approval from the author Park, he was finally able to build the Pyeongsari Literature Museum as well as the Toji Literature Road. Poet Choi has solely taken care of the Literature Museum for 15 years.  <This guide was recorded by Lee Sae-bom of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Jinhae Gunhangje Festival
stories.script: [Photo Credit (Kim Ji-ho), Korea Tourism Organization] A big festival in the Naval Town  The mecca of the Korean cherry blossom festival, beginning with the first festival on April 19, 1953, is by far the largest festival in Jinhae. Its origin dates back to time when the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-shin was set up at Bukwon Rotary and a memorial service was held. Jinhae Gunhangje Festival started as a local ceremony. However, as cherry blossoms always bloom at the time and the military marching band and cultural art event are held together, it has positioned itself as an international festival. When 360,000 cherry blossoms begin to bloom in the downtown of Jinhae, residents start cleaning roads and setting up tents. Tourists flock from all over the nation and take pictures of cherry blossoms that fill the city. Now that it has become famous to international visitors, many tourists from Thailand, China, Japan, and the U.S. come to Jinhae to see the fully bloomed cherry blossom in Jinhae.  If you are going to Gunhangje Festival, you may not want to miss out on the Korea Naval Academy and the Command of Naval Base in Jinhae. They are usually not open to the public but they are accessible only during the festival. Along with breathtaking cherry blossoms, this must-visit spring festival offers plenty of activities, such as the exhibition of Turtle Ship and trying out naval uniform. Cherry blossoms in the main road are 100 years old or older, adding splendor to the festival. When you take a photo here, be careful not to capture the building of the Naval Base. The second tip is to find a way around the rotary. There are three rotaries, Jungwon, Bukwon, and Namwon, taking you to any tourist destinations. These rotaries are against the backdrop of efforts to make Jinhae into military town during the Japanese colonial era. Visitors can feel as if they are in the 20th century by looking at Jinhae Post Office, Heukbaek Cafe, Yeonghaeru Pavilion and Gunhang Village History Hall. During the festival, the roads around the rotary become no-car zones, enabling visitors to walk around freely. The third tip is to enjoy cherry blossoms anywhere. Of course, you can enjoy them in the downtown. But since Jinhae is quite a big city, you can enjoy your ride and see the cherry blossoms lined up on the side of the road along the coastal roads. If you don’t like to be in a crowded downtown, how about going on a drive to the Marine Park along the coast?

stories.title: Jinhae NFRDI Environment Eco Park
stories.script: A park that looks like an impressionist painting Where Route 2 from Masan to Jinhae and Yeojwacheon Stream meet, there is Jinhae NFRDI Environment Eco Park. Constructed as the Jinhae Fishery in 1929, it serves as a research center for studying freshwater ecosystems and the aquaculture environment by the National Institute of Fisheries Science after the independence of Korea. In 2008, it became the official site of the 10th Ramsar General Assembly, serving as a habitat for conserving the wetland ecosystem. This paves the way for the park to be open to the public as a favorite nature experience center as well as a place for a retreat by building the wetland observatory trail.  Even today, this place is a space for testing and researching inland water fishery as well as a beautiful outing spot for citizens throughout the year. You can either choose to go to the reservoir observation trail or the wetland observation trail from the entrance. The reservoir observation trail is equipped with an artificial island and an observatory. Visitors can take a look at freshwater fish and other lives living in the reservoir. Cherry blossom trees, red leaf willows, and other trees along the trail provide shade for you to take a rest. In the wetland observatory trail, there is a wooden bridge, a small stream, and a wetland centering around the red leaf willow. The forest behind the wetland is home to many animals and plants. The sound of birds and leaves rustling will refresh your mind. This place is open to the public throughout the year except for the holiday seasons. The opening hour varies by season, so you have to check the hours before visiting. In addition, you should not cause harm to animals and plants within the park conserved for the purpose of actual research. Eating and drinking in the park are strictly prohibited, so please refrain from eating foods except for water.

stories.title: Yeojwacheon Stream (Romance Bridge)
stories.script: Blooming romance Do not miss out on one of the best cherry blossom attractions in Jinhae, a 1.5-kilometer-long Yeojwacheon Stream. Trees alongside the stream naturally form a tunnel of cherry blossom. Additional lightings and sculptures installed during the festival add to the beautiful cherry blossom even at night.  All 15 bridges over the Yeojwacheon Stream have a different name. The most well-known bridge is the “Romance Bridge” located across from the Jinhae Girl's High School. Widely known as the filming location for the popular Korean TV series called “Romance” that was aired in 2002, it is a photo spot for couples until today. If you take a photo on the bridge, it captures the moment as if two of you are the only people in the place. Here are some tips to enjoy the cherry blossoms along the stream. First, walk down the stone stairs below the bridge. You can find a perfect photo spot to shoot cherry blossoms blowing in the wind. But be careful during rainy days as the level of the stream may rise. Second, be careful not to bump your head on the big and thick cherry blossom branches. And do not cause damage to the trees by breaking or shaking branches. Your cooperation will contribute to beautiful scenery next year.  Third, enjoy the unique charm of cherry blossoms at night! As numerous people come to enjoy the night view, pay extra attention not to get hurt. Make sure to carry your camera or smartphone with a necklace or a wrist strap, and keep your eyes on your smartphone not to fall off the selfie stick.

stories.title: Jungwon Rotary
stories.script: Central plaza of the Jinhae Gunhangje Festival In 1929, during the Japanese colonial era, the Japanese built the Navy Headquarters in Jinhae, surveyed the land, and constructed roads by dividing rice paddies and fields under the name of modernization. Jungwon Rotary was one of the results of the colonial era. Today, it plays a pivotal role of crossing the downtown of Jinhae in eight directions. If you walk down the Jinhae Modern Culture & History Trail nearby the rotary, you can see buildings explaining why Jinhae was once called the “Gunhang (naval port) Village.” Jinhae Post Office, the Historic Site No. 291; Chinese restaurant named Wonhaeru visited by the first president of Korea, Rhee Seung-man; Gunhang Village History Hall where you can see the history of Jinhae at a glance; Gunhang Village Theme Park; Gunhang Village Street and many other places will help you feel the modern history of Jinhae. Most of them are within five minutes of walking distance, so you look around the Jungwon rotary within a day. The area is restricted for the Gunhangje Festival every year and transformed into roads for the festival. The place is filled with various performances on the stage in the central plaza along with many things to enjoy such as parades and delicious food. Many good restaurants are clustered around the rotary. From affordable yet plentiful restaurants especially famous among taxi drivers to cherry blossom bread and ice cream, do not miss out on a single thing!

stories.title: Jehwangsan Park
stories.script: Enjoy cherry blossoms on a monorail  If you look at the Jinhae Post Office from the Jungwon Rotary, you can see the Jinhae Tower on top of the Jehwangsan Mountain. Jehwangsan Mountain is often called the Jinhae Tower Mountain. It was originally named the Bueongsan Mountain, meaning that it looks like an owl on top of the mountain. Its name was changed to Jehwangsan Mountain after the liberation of Korea. It is by far the best place you can see the city of Jinhae at 360 degrees.  You can either walk or ride on a monorail to go to the tower located on the top of the mountain. By choosing a round trip or one-way ticket, you can comfortably enjoy the view of the downtown of Jinhae. The stair next to the monorail is called the 1-Year Stairs because it consists of 365 steps. Many people walk up to the top as an exercise. On the top where the Jinhae Tower stands used to be the site for the Memorial Tower of the Russian-Japanese War during the Japanese colonial era. In 1967, it was demolished and the nine-story tower was constructed to symbolize the warship of the ROK navy. Recently, it was designated as the Modern Building of Changwon-si No.3. If you take an elevator or walk up the stairs, you can see the entire city at a glance. The view of the city colored in cherry blossom pink during the Gunhangje Festival creates a jaw-dropping scenery. You can also look at the history, culture, and relics of Jinhae at the Jinhae Museum of Changwon City located on the second floor of the Tower. At the museum, you can get to know more about Jinhae by looking at the exhibition including Jinhae during the Japanese colonial era and the letter left by Baekbeom Kim Gu during his visit.

stories.title: Jinhae Central Market
stories.script: Jinhae daily market Jinhae Central Market is the largest market in the city which was opened in 1946 as a private market. Many people who returned home after liberation together with refugees during the Korean War settled down here and established the market. As it obtained permission as a public market in 1958, it grew into today’s market. The large market is divided into the ground and underground floors. In the 1980s, a new apartment building with stores on the ground floor was newly built. There are stores on the first floor, and the second to fourth floors are general residential spaces. It is packed with stores that sell all kinds of daily necessities. There is a raw fish center underground where you can enjoy fresh sea foods. Jinhae Central Market is the first to issue its own vouchers to revitalize the traditional market. Visitors can still purchase products and foods with these vouchers. During the Gunhangje Festival, you can see various performances at the Meeting Plaza located behind the market.

stories.title: Jinhaeru Beach Park
stories.script: Let’s have fun by the ocean! Jinhaeru Beach Park is the starting point of the 29-kilometer-long Jinhae sea trail. It is located between the Jinhae Sea and the Naval Base. There are various things to see and experience in the park that stretches along the sea. We will introduce them to you one by one. As you walk into the park, the first thing you would see is none other than a fishermen. Since it is not illegal to fish here, you can see many fishermen grabbing a nice spot and enjoying fishing. At the center of the park, you can see a huge Jinhaeru Pavilion. There is a signboard hanging on the pavilion written in Korean. On the second floor of the pavilion, you can enjoy the vast blue sea that would refresh your mind. In front of the pavilion, there is a wide wooden stage which is made for outdoor cultural performances. As long as you make a reservation on the Changwon-si website, anyone can perform busking at a scheduled time. The audience would be everyone passing by the park. Next to the Jinhaeru Pavilion, there are two Turtle Ships: one for a snack bar & cafe and another for a playground. It used to be a regular playground with a slide. However, after it was renovated into the Turtle Ship playground, the number of visitors increased with more children. Next to the snack bar, you can see Marine Adventures where you can take a boat. From pedal boats, fun boats, and catamarans (power boats) to water bikes, you can enjoy a variety of water leisure activities at a cost.

stories.title: Gyeonghwa Market (Fifth-Day Market)
stories.script: Do you smell something delicious?   Gyeonghwa Market is held every five days in front of the Gyeonghwa station. Although it is held throughout the Gunhangje Festival, it is a normal road where cars pass by on regular days. The market takes place on days ending in a 3 or an 8. There are so many people and stores gathered that you may forget this is a regular car road. As the market is held regularly, there are a variety of good eats ranging from puffed rice cakes that pop with a loud sound to freshly extracted perilla oil with a nice nutty smell, hotteock, which is the griddlecake with sugar filling, hot rice soup, and even crispy fried chicken! The market is full of delicious smell that it makes you crave more food. In addition to delicious gourmets, you can also buy horticultural plants, agricultural equipment, pottery, handicraft accessories, and every other daily necessity at a relatively low price. Another thing to see is mid-aged women shopping with a basket and their bargaining skills. Why don’t you look around the Gyeonghwa Market with food in one hand?

stories.title: Gyeonghwa Station
stories.script: [Photo Credit (Park Seong-geun), Korea Tourism Organization)  Cherry blossom by the railroad  Another spot for Jinhae Cherry Blossom Festival! Here you can see the train passing through the cherry blossom tunnel. As railway service of Gyeonghwa Station has been discontinued as of 2006, it turned into a flag station for freight trains passing by. What makes this place famous is that you can see rows of cherry blossom trees forming a tunnel of flowers. This magnificent spring scenery of the cherry blossom tunnel and a freight train passing by makes people reminisce about the past. During the festival, all trains are stationed at the Gyeonghwa Station, becoming one of the top three cherry blossom photo spots in Jinhae. Make sure you take a photo in an orderly manner as this place is crowded with people. Another unique point of this place is that you can walk on the track freely. But be careful not to trip over the track. Benches and rest areas cannot be used during the Gunhangjae Festival, so bringing your own mat would be a great idea!   <This guide was recorded by Kim Hak-rae of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Jinhae Marine Park
stories.script: [Photo Credit (Lee Bum-soo), Korea Tourism Organization] The sea embracing the sun  If you drive 20 minutes along the coastal road from the downtown of Jinhae, you can see a huge shipyard and a marine park located in Myeong-dong, Jinhae. Jinhae Marine Park was formed by transforming the entire Umjido Island into a park. On the island, there are Marine Solar Park, Solar Tower, Fish Ecology Learning Center, Marine Life Theme Park, and Maritime History Hall.  The Solar Tower is the most famous one as it is the nation’s largest and tallest solar power plant. It has 1,949 solar panels installed on one side of a 28-story high tower, generating an average of 1,300 kW of electricity daily, which is the amount that allows 200 households to use electricity at the same time.  You can also go up to the observatory on the 27th floor by purchasing an admission ticket. You will find more detailed explanations on solar energy, an eco-friendly renewable energy. One side of the floor, where you can see Udo Island, is transparent, enabling visitors to see the ground 120 meter below. It explains why its name is “dizzy floor.” This dizzy floor is made of solid materials, which can withstand the weight of 70 people at once, so there is no risk of falling.  Coming down from the Solar Park, you can either head to the Udo Island by crossing a bridge or head to the Marine Life Theme Park and Fish Ecology Learning Center to explore a mysterious underwater ecosystem. The Naval Battle History Experience Hall allows visitors to experience naval battle, letting them understand the importance of the navy.  It is not well known to the visitors, but the entire island turns pink in spring covered by blooming cherry blossom trees. If you look down from the observatory of the Solar Tower, you can enjoy the panoramic view of blue sea, pink-colored island, and red sun. Have a wonderful time enjoying this beautiful scenery created by nature.

stories.title: Hwawangsan Mountain in Changnyeong
stories.script: Hwawangsan Mountain in Changnyeong Fortress surrounded by azalea and silver grass  Hwawangsan Mountain is a famous mountain of Changnyeong-gun. Its old name is “Bulmoe,” meaning a mountain blowing out the fire. The current name Hwawang originated from the meaning of the old name. There are many tourist spots in Hwawang Mountain, including Hwawangsanseong Fortress and Eoksae Plain which can be reached only when you climb up the mountain as it is located at the top of the mountain.  You need to choose the most suitable course to get to the peak. The most common course is from Jahagok Ticket Booth close to the downtown of Changnyeong and the Okcheon Ticket Booth nearby the Okcheon Reservoir. Since each course has a different level of difficulty, it is recommended you start climbing with hiking equipment. However, if you just want a casual hike with sneakers on, taking the Jahagok Course 3 that passes the Doseongam Hermitage to the West Gate of the Hwawangsangseong Fortress would be a good choice.  If you go up to the top along the hiking trail, you can see the view of winding mountain ranges and Changnyeong. Inside the fortress, you can see the beautiful silver grass waves at the Eoksae Plain. The fortress was built for the purpose of defense by using the cliffs and ridges at the top, but it is unknown when it was built. Still, the story of the General Gwak Jae-u, dubbed the Red Robe General, defeating the Japanese army led by Kato Giyomasa here at Hwawangsanseong Fortress is well-known.  Landscape around Hwawangsanseong Fortress changes every season. In spring, the place is filled with pink-colored azalea along the trail. During fall, a vast silver grass field creates a splendid view of golden silver grass waving in the wind. Due to these beautiful sceneries, many Korean TV series including Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace), Sangdo, Wangcho, and Mr. Sunshine were filmed here. Nearby the East Gate, you can visit an actual filming site of the legendary series Hur Jun.  When enjoying the view, watch your step at all times as there are many cliffs at the top. Since no safety fence is installed here, walking the inner road of the fortress is highly recommended.  <This guide was recorded by Kim Ha-rim of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Haegeumgang Islets
stories.script: As one of the best sights of Geojedo Island, Haegeumgang Islets are called the Geumgangsan Mountain of the sea.  If you take a ferry from the Haegeumgang Islets or Jangseungpo, you can enjoy another sightseeing course to the Oedo Island. Haegeumgang Islets look like a cross when viewed from the sky. If you go on the ferry tour, you will be fascinated by the height of the rock walls and the inside of the Sipjadonggul Cave.  Its original name was Galdo as it is shaped like the spreading roots of an arrowroot. These days it is better known as the Haegeumgang Islets. If you go on the tour, you will be fascinated by the mysterious scenery created by Chotdaebawi Rock that looks like a candlestick and the Sajabawi Rock that resembles a lion facing each other along with the Sipjadonggul Cave. For your information, you cannot land on the Islets and you can only enjoy it on a ferry to look around the islets. The guide will stand on the bow and give you a detailed explanation, giving you plenty of time to savor the view.

stories.title: Hakdong Pebblehaebyeon Beach
stories.script: Hakdong Pebblehaebyeon Beach, located in the southern area of Geoje-si, is famous for its exotic view created by pebbles resembling black pearls. The beautiful sunrise that can be enjoyed in the camellia habitat next to the beach contributes to its popularity. It is also known for fairy pittas stopping by this place in summer. At the entrance to the beach, the first thing you would see is this alphabet sculpture of “Hakdong.” Depending on the angle of view, the dispersion of light varies, making it a perfect photo spot. Turning to the pine forest, you would see many couples as there is a sculpture shaped like a heart.  It is well equipped with parking lots and accommodations thanks to its long length.  Tourists come to the beach to see the sunrise at dawn. Some are here to look for pretty pebbles on the beach. Please note that taking pebbles out of the beach is strictly prohibited. How about visiting the Hakdong Pebblehaebyeon Beach before going to the Windy Hill and Haegeumgang Islets?

stories.title: Windy Hill
stories.script: A place where the windmill adds an exotic feel This is the windy hill. As one of the Eight Scenic Views of Geoje, it is the most unique tourist attraction in the southern area of the region. Walking up on a hill by the sea after purchasing a ticket at the ticket booth, you will feel the breeze that will make your walk more pleasant. It seems like a nice place to read as there is grass and bench.  Stretch your arms wide and feel the peacefulness of the sea as if embracing the vast sea. The fishing boats on the sea add to the peaceful view to make visitors feel relaxed and understand the true aesthetic of slowness.  The windmill, which is the symbol of this place, was built in 2009. Since it is difficult to spot windmills in Korea, they were used as a filming sites for popular TV series and films. It used to be called “Tthebatneul,” which means a hill covered with strap, but its name changed to “Windy Hill” in 2002.

stories.title: Yeocha Hongpo Observatory
stories.script: At the Yeocha Hongpo Observatory, you can see many islands and islets including Daebyeongdaedo and Sobyeongdaedo Island of Geoje. There is an open area at the back of the right side where you can see Mamuldo Island. The wooden two-story observatory is well maintained. Depending on the region, people call the observatory differently, such as Byeongdaedo Observatory and Yeocha Hongpo Coastal Road Observatory. When you use a GPS, you may have to try several times to find the exact location. Please be informed that you would have to go up the unpaved and rough road. However, once you reach the observatory, the view that unfolds before you pays off every drop of sweat. Please note that the observatory is connected to three narrow forest paths, so you can enjoy the archipelago from different locations.

stories.title: Gujora Beach
stories.script: Against the backdrop of the beautiful landscape, Gujora Beach is known for its natural beauty and crystal clear water. Another merit of this beach is that it can be reached easily. It was initially used by the U.S. soldiers when a prisoner-of-war camp was established in Geoje in the aftermath of the Korean War.  The beach is relatively shallow with warm water. It stretches 1.1 kilometers long and has a width of 30 meters, which is the perfect condition for sea-bathing. It has many nearby attractions such as Anseom Island to the front, Mangsan Mountain to the east, and Sujeongbong Peak and Yundolseom Island to the west, creating a beautiful view. Situated farther inland, partially encircled by the coastline, the water at Gujora Beach is calm and serene. You can also enjoy fresh sea foods and purchase famous local produce such as anchovies. Visitors can enjoy the nearby tourist sites such as the Gujorajinseong Fortress as well as the Haegeumgang Islets, Naedo and Oedo Islands by taking a cruise tour.

stories.title: Oedo Botania
stories.script: The official name of this place is Oedo Natural Farm, which opened in 1995. It is a popular attraction welcoming more than a million tourists annually. Unlike other islands, Oedo Island, located 4km away from Geojeodo Island, has plentiful water and warm weather. On a clear day, you can see far to Haeguemgang Islets, Hongdo Island, and Tsushima Island.  Oedo Botania is only accessible via a ferry from seven docks on Geojedo Island. Once you arrive, the 90-minute-long tour will start with an exotic lighthouse at the dock. If you want to take a photo at the entrance of the Oedo Botania, you have to be patient because you are not the only person wanting to take a scenic photo. You might wonder how such a beautiful place was made as you look around the Oedo Botania. What draws the attention of visitors is the 870 types of plants that have been cultivated over the past four decades, especially subtropical plants which are difficult to see in Korea. At the Oedo Botania, where the popular Korean TV series Winter Sonata was filmed, you would leave with lots of good memories.

stories.title: Wahyeon Beach
stories.script: Wahyeon Village and Wahyeon Beach are located at the southeastern tip of Geoje. 510-meter-long beach has a gentle slope and fine dust, which is good to walk barefoot. Clear water and the tide that comes in the beach makes visitors feel safe to enjoy their vacation here at the Wahyeon Beach. And Wahyeon Village right next to the beach serves as a good place to find accommodation. There is a changing room, shower place, and other basic facilities. You can easily see anglers enjoying fishing at many fishing points. Wahyeon Beach underwent renovation to recover from severe damage by typhoon Maemi and is renamed Wahyeon Moraesup Beach. A newly built park nearby the beach is named the “Maemi Park” to commemorate the loss and damage of the typhoon.

stories.title: Geoje P.O.W. Camp Historic Park
stories.script: Geoje P.O.W. Camp Historic Park was built to accommodate the prisoners of the Korean War.  It remains preserved after being designated as Gyeongsangnam-do Cultural Property No. 99. Some of the buildings are preserved intact and the lifestyle of the war prisoners can be seen so that the visitors can have a bit of understanding of how they lived back then.  It consists of a War Zone, Prisoner Zone, Recovery Zone, and Peace Zone, all of which are spaces to remember the tragedy. In particular, the “1950 Experience Hall” is a maze to find the freedom, at which you are given a task to complete five missions in search of freedom. During a short time, visitors can understand the precious value of freedom and enjoy virtual shooting at the optical illusion hall and shooting hall.  The historic park, which needs an admission fee, is equipped with a large pay parking lot. There is a ticket booth for a monorail to reach the top of the Gyeryongsan Mountain nearby. It would be more meaningful to see historical relics at the historic park and enjoy the view of Geojedo Island to embrace the meaning of the place. As visiting both attractions take quite a lot of time, it is recommended to plan your trip wisely.

stories.title: Geojedo Island
stories.script: Geojedo Island is the largest island and the only si (city) among the countless in the southern coast. It is the second largest island in Korea after Jeju Island. Unlike Jeju Island and Ulleungdo Island, it is located closer to the Korean peninsula. You can rarely feel that it is an isolated land as it is connected to Tongyeong with Geojedaegyo Bridge and Shingeojedaegyo Bridge and to Busan with Geogadaegyo Bridge. Thanks to the development of transportation, far more tourists are visiting Geojedo Island. People from all over the country come to see the astonishing scenery that is ever-changing created by the surrounding islands and cliffs. Entering Geojedo Island from Busan and Tongyeong gives you a completely different feeling. If you come from the western part of Gyeongsangnam-do Province, you may depart at Goseong, stop by Tongyeong and enter Geojedo Island. If you are coming from the east, it would be smart to start your journey from Busan to Gimhae and then Geojedo Island through the Geogadaegyo Bridge. The construction of the Geogadaegyo Bridge, which connects Busan and Geojedo Island, has greatly shortened the time. The 8.2-km-long bridge going through undersea tunnels and above the sea makes your trip more unforgettable.

stories.title: Geoje Maengjongjuk Park
stories.script: Maengjongjuk, also called the Honamjuk, Juksoonjuk, Ilbonjuk, or Mojuk, is a type of thick bamboo that grows up to 20 meters in height and 20 centimeters in diameter. Geoje Maengjongjuk Park uses maengjonjuk bamboos to create a therapy theme park that is both nature-friendly and relaxing. The trees are preserved and used to provide forest bathing experience as well as a splendid scenery by blending environmental art and ocean views.  As the forest blocks sunlight, it is about 4 to 7 degrees cooler than the outside. A bamboo forest bathing helps to ease stress, cools off your mind and body, and is efficient in preventing diseases due to the higher amount of oxygen generation. Thick bamboo forest, which generates 10 times more anion, promotes blood circulation and makes the body supply more oxygen.  In addition, the adventure forest and survival experience are great courses for children to have thrilling and fun experiences.

stories.title: Maemiseong Fortress
stories.script: Baek Soon-sam lost an arable land of about 2,000m2 in Geojedo Island due to Typhoon Maemi in 2003. To restore the land, he repeatedly stacked square stones near the beach, which has now become a castle known as Maemiseong Fortress. For 15 years, along the rocks on the seashore, Baek alone has been constructing the wall, which is 120 to 130 meters long.  What is worthy of attention is that he has no architectural training. He just stacked the stone and it eventually became a big castle, which has gone viral to the general public. In 2011, it became popular nationwide as it was aired on TV. It is also an ideal place for a wedding photo shoot. You have to walk in since this place is inaccessible by car. Maemiseong Fortress with more than 10,000 stones piled up at the end of a small pebble beach creates a perfect harmony with the blue sea.

stories.title: Sinseondae Observatory
stories.script: Sinseondae Observatory, located on the beach across the Windy Hill of Dojangpo Village, offers picturesque views of the southern coast of Korea.  The white and red colored sculpture meaning Sinseondae in Korean creates a nice photo spot with a sea background. Some are here to make wishes while looking at the Sinseondae Terrace with two hands closed. There are parking lot and convenient facilities that would make your long-staying comfortable. Sinseondae Terrace is said to be the place where Taoist hermits used to stay. The beauty of this spot supports the legend. Along with the neighboring islands, the sea, and rocks that form a harmony, the white waves crashing on rock creates a picturesque view.

stories.title: Gohyeon Market
stories.script: Gohyeon Market, located in Gohyeon-dong, the central place of Geoje, is the largest market in the city forming a cross shape. It is conveniently accessible by car as there is a public parking building. In the first basement floor there is a seafood marketplace, and the ground floor sells agricultural products and vegetables just like a typical Korean traditional market. However, what is unique is that children’s paintings are decorated as tiles on the wall from the entrance to the basement. It forms a friendly atmosphere reminiscent of childhood.  At the seafood sections, you can purchase seafood and eat them right away at the place. In the agricultural product section, local specialties are well arranged for sale. The market rotary, where four alleys intersect, has a place that sells street foods, attracting the most people.

stories.title: Deokpo Beach
stories.script: Deokpo Beach is a white sandy beach with fine sand, clear waters, and a gentle slope, which is a perfect place for a family vacation. Many retusa fringe trees are planted along the coast and the Okpo Great Victory Commemorative Park is located nearby.   Thanks to the thick pine grove, you can feel the exotic mood. Accommodations and convenience facilities make your visit more pleasant and comfortable. In addition, there is a penguin statue symbolizing the Geojedo International Penguin Swimming Festival for you to take a photo with. This place also serves as an observatory to enjoy the view of the sea.  The global milestones marking the distance between Mexico City and Colombo are installed to attract the interest of visitors. On the right side of Deokpo Beach, there is a zipline called the Sea Line, where you can enjoy thrilling and exciting experience.

stories.title: Jeoguhang Port
stories.script: At Jeoguhang Port, many ferries are running back and forth to and from Somaemuldo Island.  Unlike other passenger terminals which have routes to several islands and tourist destinations, Daemamuldo and Someamuldo Islands are the only destinations one can arrive from the Passenger Terminal at the Jeoguhang Port. The ticket office is on the first floor and the waiting room and the restaurant is on the second floor. It runs about four times a day during weekdays. You can get on board more easily and conveniently if you book a ticket online. Just so you know, there is no returning ferry if you ride the last one. After a 40-minute ride to Daemaemuldo Island, a huge female statue welcomes visitors at the dock. Many come here for trekking. If you walk along the blue line, you can look around the island more conveniently. From the Janggunbong Peak (210m), you can choose a hiking course among the 90-minute, 2-hour, and 4-hour course for a round trip. On the island, there is a closed-down school, which allows visitors to camp out in the playground. The view of the sea looking from the school is remarkable.  To Somaemuldo Island, it takes around an hour. From the dock to the Mangtaebong Peak (152m), there is a 90-minute course and a 2-hour course. Somaemuldo Island was said to be called the “Mamido” due to the shape of an island that resembles a general riding a horse. The path to Deungdae Island is another attractive point of this place. To go to Deungdae Island, you have to pass Yeolmokgae, the mysterious sea path. If you are here at the right time, you can cross the sea, stepping pebbles. You can also see the panoramic view of the archipelago from Deungdae Island covered with waving reeds.

stories.title: Tongyeong Central Traditional Market
stories.script: Tongyeong Central Traditional Market   Tongyeong Central Traditional Market, with 400 years old history, is a must-visit destination in Tongyeong. On the hill behind the market, there is a Dongpirang, known as Montmartre in the East, and a Turtle Ship with other fishing boats right next to the market. A spacious cultural plaza reminds of the yard for warships occupied with soldiers from the Joseon Dynasty. Numerous merchants together with crowded visitors make the traditional market energetic and dynamic every day. You can not only purchase fresh fruits, vegetables, and seafood but also experience the joy and excitement of the place. Looking at stores, products, and foods, you can feel time goes faster than you think.

stories.title: Tongyeong Seopirang Village
stories.script: Even though there is a well-known photo spot such as Seoporu in Seopirang, it was less known than Donpirang. In the past, Seopirang was one of the most underdeveloped areas along with Dongpirang, but it has risen rapidly as a tourist destination after undergoing a transformation. There are small and large artworks made by the residents in every nook and cranny, and there are many places to visit including Seopirang Story Tunnel, Monument to Baekseok, and the Birth Home of Lady Gong Deok-gwi. Artists drawing a painting with a brush in hand can easily be spotted at Seopirang.  The lower village of Seopirang is the birthplace of Park Kyong-ni who wrote the famous novel Toji (“The Land”), as well as the main background for Kim’s Daughters, another famous novel wrote by Park. Seomungogae, Ganchangol, and Myeongjeongsaem, which are places described in the novel, are located here, making Seopirang the village of literature. The village is still developing as a literature village by hosting the “Park Gyeog-ni Literature Village, Seopirang Alley Tour,” thereby attracting many visitors across the nation.

stories.title: Tongyeong International Music Festival, Coastal Trail
stories.audioTitle: Tongyeong International Music Festival, Coastal Trail
stories.script: Since 2002, Tongyeong hosts the Tongyeong International Music Festival (TIMF) to honor the Korean composer Yun I-sang every year in his hometown, Tongyeong. It is hosted every spring and fall, and the Isangyun Competition is held in every fall. Every other summer, the city provides a music learning opportunity through the TIMF Academy. The Tongyeong Concert Hall, opened in 2014, is the main stage.  Rooted in classical music, Tongyeong International Music Festival presents various musics such as modern music, symphonies, chamber music, opera, and musical theater. Although TIMF pursues diversity in genres, it is known to have strengths in modern music generally. Tongyeong Coastal Trail is one of the 52 Korean Coastal Trails selected by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the Korea Ocean Foundation. The name Korean Coastal Trail is given to trails that preserve nature as it is or a beautiful spot where visitors can experience the marine culture, history, and industry among the developed sea trails. The trail is 6.6km long that stretches from Yeongun Village to Donam-dong, where Chungmu Marina Resort is located. As you walk along the trail with the beautiful nature and peaceful sound of waves, you would encounter Bokbawi Rock standing in the middle of the sea. The legend says that a fairy who was caught making love with one of the soldiers of Great Jade Emperor was struck by lightning and turned into a rock. This is also the site of the Battle of Hansando where Admiral Yi Sun-shin defeated the Japanese naval force with his well-known Hakikjin (crane wing, a semicircular formation) strategy and took over the sea. On Hasando Island, Jeseungdang Hall, the headquarters of the Navy Headquarters of Three Provinces during the Joseon Dynasty, is located.

stories.title: Hallyeosudo Viewing Ropeway, Skyline Luge Tongyeong
stories.audioTitle: Hallyeosudo Viewing Ropeway, Skyline Luge Tongyeong
stories.script: Built on the Mireuksan Mountain, known as one of the 100 scenic mountains in Korea, is the longest (1,975m) tourist cable car and the first mono cable car circulating gondola ropeway to be built in Korea. Once you reach the top of Mireuksan Mountain, you are guaranteed a breathtaking view in every direction you look. The sea off Hansando Island is also the place where Admiral Yi Sun-shin led the Battle of Hansan to victory with his sweat and blood.  Selected as one of Korea’s 100 Must-Visit Tourist Spots by the Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism and the Korea Tourism Organization, it was also selected as the 2015 Open Tourist Site. On your way down with a cable car ride, you can find a long track under your feet. It is a ride called the Skyline Luge Tongyeong. Luge is a unique wheeled gravity ride that provides riders full control over their descent on a purpose-built track. Since there are only six places to ride this luge in the world, Skyline Luge Tongyeong is filled with visitors wanting to feel the excitement every weekend.  Since it runs without an engine, in order to speed up, you have to drive without braking on the first straight course. Once it accelerates, try out the S-course, U-course, and 360-degree rotation course as well. Once is never enough! Skyline Luge Tongyeong is the only place with a 360-degree rotation course in the world, attracting second-timers to try out a new course.  Skyline Luge Tongyeong sits directly below the Hallyeosudo Cable Car which takes visitors to Mireuksan Mountain and offers stunning views across Tongyeong city, the sea, and surrounding islands.

stories.title: Saryangdo Island
stories.script: Saryangdo Island, which is 50 minutes away from the Gaochi Port in Tongyeong by ferry, is where you can enjoy various outdoor activities including hiking, fishing, and water leisure. Saryangdo Terminal is crowded with people in colorful climbing suits or with MTB. Most visitors come to Saryangdo Island for the Jirisan Mountain trekking. Due to the relatively lower elevation of Jirisan Mountain on Saryangdo Island, you may not be able to enjoy all scenes, but it is still a popular trekking course that is beautifully harmonized with cliffs and forests. The best part is that you can enjoy the view of the sea and mountains at the same time. Even now, a ferry cruising to Saryangdo Island is passing through the sea with many passengers and vehicles loaded. Saryangdo Island consists of Sangdo and Hado and the Saryangdaegyo Bridge that connects the two. Saryangdaegyo Bridge allows visitors to enjoy forest paths in both Sangdo and Hado.  There is a Sangdo Coastal Trail, giving another option for a visitor who feels the burden to climb the mountain. Ongnyeobong Peak and Suspension Bridge are other tourist spots when walking on a forest path of Jirisan Mountain. The wonderful panorama of the blue sky and sea from the Ongnyeobong Peak is eye-catching. But make sure to watch out if you are not an experienced hiker as the mountain has rough and irregular sides.

stories.title: Tongyong Pak Kyongni Memorial Hall
stories.script: Pak Kyongni Memorial Hall was established to honor the author Park who marked a milestone in Korean literature history with her epic novel Toji (“The Land”) and to raise awareness and understanding of the literature by introducing Tongyeong, which constantly inspired her literature.  The building is intentionally built with a whole glass window to see the view of the sea of Tongyeong. You can see Par's photo at a glance from the entrance. Her round chignon hairstyle and modest outfit describe her youth. well. There are paintings of her high school graduation and wedding to give you an understanding of how she lived.  The keepsakes of Park such as the handwritten script of Toji, passports, and letters attract the literature lovers. The video explaining her life and a collection of papers about her works are displayed as well. Park's writing room is recreated and it makes you feel like you can meet her any time soon.  Park Kyeongni Park, located behind the hall, is where she is buried, so you can pay a silent tribute at her grave. In fact, many fruits and flowers before her grave are evidence proving many people are still respecting her life and works.

stories.title: Tongyeong Navy Headquarters of Three Provinces, Sebyeonggwan Government Office
stories.audioTitle: Tongyeong Navy Headquarters of Three Provinces, Sebyeonggwan Government Office
stories.script: For over 200 years since its establishment, the building served as the naval force headquarters of three provinces: Gyeongsang-do, Jeolla-do, and Chungcheong-do. It is deemed as today’s Naval Command. Sebyeonggwan Government Office is the main building of the Navy Headquarters of Three Provinces. It was established in 1605 by the 6th generation commander-in-chief Lee Kyung-jun and upgraded to a National Treasure in 2002. This is the first Navy Headquarters in the Hansando camp that contributed to the promotion of Admiral Yi Sun-shin to the Commander of the Navy Headquarters of Three Provinces. This was constructed to manufacture military supplies amid the ongoing fierce war.  After several renovations works, it still commands its old-time majesty as one of the most grandiose local government buildings overlooking the South Sea. It features hipped-and-gable roof whose curved eaves lead to corners going upwards. It is fun to see fancy and decorative patterns on the ceiling.  Sebyeonggwan is named after Man (pulling), Ha (water), Seh (washing) and Byeong (soldiers), meaning “cleaning the weapon with the milky way.”

stories.title: Tongyeong Dara Park
stories.script: Located in the southern part of Mireukdo Island, it is at the center of the Sanyangiljur-ro. Dara Park was originally named for its resemblance to the tusk of an elephant. The name also means “a vista point for a view of the moon.”  This place is actually more famous for sunset. The top of the park is a prime location to see the broad view of the archipelago. A large guide map lets you get to know the park better while waiting to see the sunset. To just give you a little insider tip, you should check the sunset time in advance.  On the path to the park is Gwanghaejeong Pavilion, which is well-known for its night view of the Dara Village. However, the camellia surrounding the Village makes it difficult to enjoy the view.  Looking at the blue sky and sea and resting under the shade of a tall tree at the observatory will refresh your mind. This small park will offer its visitors relaxation amidst pristine nature.

stories.title: Tongyeong Yi Sun-sin Park
stories.script: Yi Sun-sin Park is located where the Great Battle of Hansan took place in a quintessential tourist destination in Tongyeong. Constructed to honor the patriotism of General Yi Sun-sin, the park features a statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, pointing his finger to the sea, and Cheonja Chongtong Gun, which played a significant role in defeating the Japanese navy during the Japanese Invasion of Korea in 1592.  There are many things to enjoy in addition to the sculpture of the Turtle Ship and topiary (the art of clipping and shaping the foliage of plants). You can clear up your mind while looking at the waves that cause white bubbles. You can also swim and rest at the nearby sandy beach in summer. In addition, there is an outdoor stage where performances take place.  If you are looking for a trail where you can walk next to the open sea and green forest at the same time, how about stopping by Yi Sun-sin Park?

stories.title: Tongyeong Undersea Tunnel
stories.script: This is an undersea tunnel built to connect Tongyeong and Mireukdo Island. Constructed over a 16-month period from 1931 to 1932, the undersea tunnel in Tongyeong is Asia’s first submarine tunnel. The 483-meter-long concrete-paved road is a good place for a walk or a ride.  The tunnel served as a convenient pass-through for Japanese fishermen during the colonial period. Despite its construction period, it is designated as a Modern Cultural Heritage of Korea, meaning that it is the result of the work of our ancestors. The word “Yongmundaryang” engraved at the entrance means “the entrance of an undersea tunnel that connects the island to land.” If you walk up the tunnel, you can see information board on the right, showing the history filled with joys and sorrows of Korea at the time. Though it was a tunnel connecting Mireukdo Island to Tongyeong, it is rarely in use ever since the opening of Chungmugyo Bridge and Tongeyongdaekyo Bridge. This place is accessible 24/7 free of charge.

stories.title: Maemuldo Island, Yokjido Island, and Hansando Island
stories.audioTitle: Maemuldo Island, Yokjido Island, and Hansando Island
stories.script: Maemuldo Island was called the “Mamido Island” after Ma (Chinese character meaning horse) and Mi (Chinese character meaning tail) due to its horse-like shape. It became “Maemuldo” today as the pronunciation changed. A huge buckwheat (maemil in Korean) is another theory behind the name of the Island. Although it was a lesser-known place than Hansando Island, which has become famous through the media and TV shows, Janggunbong Peak, at the top of Maemuldo Island, is a beloved hiking course for many hikers across the nation.  If you want to travel to a rather quieter place, going to Yokjido Island is highly recommended. Yokjido is well known for sweet potato and mackerel farming. It is the prime location to enjoy the sea, fishing, hiking, and sea-bathing at once. You do not want to miss the cool suspension bridge along with the seaway of beautiful Hallyeosudo.  If you are for a day’s trip, Hansando Island would be a perfect place to visit. Hansando Island is the biggest island of Hansan-myeon which consists of 65 islands. It is more well-known for its historical importance related to Admiral Yi Sun-sin and the battle of Hansando . It is accessible in 20 minutes by boat from Tongyeong and the ferry comes every hour. There are five different courses on the Island. Whichever you are taking, visiting the Jeseungdang Hall as the last spot is highly recommended. This is a place for people to pay their tributes to Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Since it is located nearby the port, you can stop by before going back to the land.

stories.title: The Jeon Hyuck Lim Museum of Art
stories.audioTitle: The Jeon Hyuck Lim Museum of Art
stories.script: A magician of colors, a painter of archipelago, the master of color-field abstract, and the founder of Korean abstract painting. These are nicknames calling the late painter Jeon Hyuck-lim. There is a museum permanently exhibiting his works in Tongyeong. This is the Jeon Hyuck Lim Museum of Art, located at the foot of Mireuksan Mountain. The outer walls of the building are decorated with the master painter's paintings and his son Jeon Yeong-geun's paintings which were selected from among their works and reproduced by utilizing a massive amount of ceramic tiles. The front wall on the third floor is a reproduction of the great artist's work titled Window painted in 1998. As the both inside and outside of the museum are art itself, it can be said that this place is open all year round, even on closed days. In the exibition halls, 80 paintings and related 50 materials are displayed and changed every three months.  Managed by painter Jeon Yeong-geun, the son of Jeon Hyuck-lim, it has become a place where families and the loved ones come to enjoy art, take pictures, and spend valuable time together.

stories.title: Dangposeong Fortress Site
stories.script: Dangposeong Fortress is a stone fortress built on top of the hill and the slope of the hill in Samdeok-ri, Sanyang-eup, Tongyeong-si, Gyeongsangnam-do. This fortress is said to be constructed by General Choi Young, together with a number of his soldiers and residents, to prevent the Japanese invasions during the reign of King Gongmin from the Goryeo Dynasty. Though this region was occupied by the Japanese troops in 1592 during the Imjin War, Admiral Yi Sun-shin regained control during the Battle of Dangpo.  It is a typical stone fortress founded in the Goryeo and Joseon periods where most of the fortresses were built by stacking stones in important areas for the national defense such as borders and coastal areas. It was designed to have a gate in the north and south and ramparts protruded to fire cannons.  From Dangposeong Fortress Site, you can see the coast of Samdeokhang Port. The panoramic view of the winding fortress makes you feel another beauty.

stories.title: Dongpirang Mural Village
stories.script: A well-known mural village, located behind the Tongyeong Central Market, is Dongpirang, meaning the east birang. The word “birang” means hill in the Tongyeong dialect. The name shows the unique color of Tongyeong. On a winding uphill, you can find painted murals. In October 2007, a contest led by a civic organization was held to paint the walls of Dongpirang Village, and 18 teams throughout the nation came to paint murals here. Thanks to beautiful and unique paintings, this hillside village on the sea became a new tourist site.  This village also offers a beautiful seascape. The Gangguan Port, which can be seen from the top of the village, gives you a feeling of taking a walk with the sea. Coffee and honey buns are the perfect mate for a stroll. Why don't you walk along the alleys of Dongpirang Village and enjoy mural paintings?

stories.title: Nammangsan Sculpture Park
stories.script: Nammangsan Sculpture Park was established to display the works of 15 famous sculptors from 10 countries. Established in 1997, the place exhibits a dignified world of artworks against the backdrop of the beautiful natural view of the 16,528m2-wide park. As there are various artworks, some come to feel inspired and others to enjoy the open space.  Well-equipped with landscape gardening, it delivers an amazing view during the day and night. During the day, you can walk quietly through the sculptures with the indigo sea in the background; at night, you can spend some romantic time on a slightly high hill with beautiful night view.  How about walking through sculptures in the park, guessing the title of each work during day and night?

stories.title: Tongyeong Chungnyeolsa Shrine
stories.script: Chungnyeolsa Shrine was built to commemorate Admiral Yi Sun-sin's loyalty and brilliant exploits. In 1606, this divine place was constructed following the order of the king during the 39th year of King Seonjo's reign (1606) by the 7th commander-in-chief Lee Woon-yong. In 1663, the 4th year of King Hyeonjong's reign, a plaque was bestowed along with Chungnyeolsa Temple in Namhae.  Hongsalmun, or the Spiked Red Gate, to commemorate the shrine of only second-class or higher officials, is located within the place, showing its authority. There is a hall and relic exhibition hall housing a memorial tablet of General Yi inside. Eight Gifts from Ming Emperor, which are national treasures of Korea, and other cultural assets are displayed here.  The shrine regularly holds ancestral rites in February and August of the lunar calendar as well as during the birthday of General Yi and the Hansan Battle Festival. Goyuje, meaning the rite to report an event to gods, is held to notice the beginning of the festival to the spirit of General Yi Sun-sin. Seungjeonmu (Victory Dance), a local dance of Tongyeong, is performed as well during the rite. It contains the meaning of commemorating the victory of Admiral Yi and praising his virtues and loyalty.

stories.title: Danghangpo Tourist Area
stories.script: Danghangpo Tourist Area is an optimal place for tourists who want to enjoy various experiences in one big place. This place was constructed by the residents to pass on General Yi Sun-sin's spirit and sacrifice to the country to the next generations in 1981. It was designated as a national tourist destination in 1984 and opened in November 1987. In the area, there are two attractions — “Sea Gate,” an area themed to General Yi, and “Dinosaur Gate” to the fantasy world. If you pass the Dinosaur Gate, you will be greeted by the Dinosaur Land which is the most popular among various themed attractions especially for children. This is because the actual-size dinosaurs are in the wide park so that visitors can have vivid experiences and take memorable photos. In addition, at the Botanical Garden where you can see rare species that lived in the dinosaur era, you can feel as if you have time traveled to the distant past when nature, dinosaurs, and people coexisted. Passing through the dinosaur-themed attractions, let’s move on to meet the “Yi Sun-sin-themed attractions.” Once you pass the Sea Gate, diorama video about Yi's life is presented before your eyes. This is to commemorate the area where he led the victory of the Battle of Danghanpo. You will also encounter Danghanpo Exhibition Hall as well. If your interest lies in a warship, you can see the turtle ship and the landing ship tank (LST) up close. As Danghangpo Tourist Area is equipped with a natural art center, recreational facilities, and various themed parks, it is loved by family tourists.

stories.title: Sangjogam County Park
stories.script: Sangjogam County Park is where most dinosaurs' footprints can be found in Goseong. People who come here to see the dinosaur footprints, however, are often fascinated by the landscape of the unique rock cliff. The scenery of the sedimentary layers along the coast is quite unique. Cliffs created by the sea and wind for many years and legends about the caves created by waves attract visitors’ eyes and interest. The most famous cave is the “Sangjokgul Cave.” A legend says that fairies from heaven came down to the Sangjokgul Cave to weave clothes out of brocade for the Great Jade Emperor. Many people call a pond inside the cave the “Seonnyoetang Pond” which is believed to be a place where fairies took bath. A rock shaped like a loom and a puddle shaped like a bathing tub still exist inside. In addition to the Sangjokgul Cave, many oddly shaped rocks inside the caves have their own stories behind them. It is recommended to visit and see them in person.  Passing the unique rock cliffs, let's take a look at dinosaur fossils around Sangjogam in detail. This site was first discovered by professor Yang Seung-yeong at Kyungpook National University and Professor Kim Hang-muk at Pusan National University in 1982 while they were investigating dinosaur fossils in Korea. It is recognized as one of the three major dinosaur sites in the world, along with those in Brazil and Canada. Clear footprints of dinosaurs that lived during the Cretaceous Period of the Mesozoic Era remain to extend over the coast of Sangjogam region. Professor Yang stated his happiness of discovering the footprints later in his book, saying that “I can envision a herd of dinosaurs wandering around.” It has been designated as the Natural Monument No. 411 as dinosaur footprints are valuable resources in discovering the uncovered mysteries of life before the appearance of mankind.

stories.title: Manhawhangcho
stories.script: Another mystical area in Goseong in the land of dinosaur is “Manhawhangcho” filled with flowery fragrance. Manhawhangcho, which has a rough and natural charm, means a botanical garden with 10,000 types of flowers and plants. Due to the lavender gray-colored hydrangea, it is also called the sea in the forest. Although you can encounter ever-changing nature, it is not a good path for a walk due to many slopes and gravel on the roads. This is because this place is meant to be inconvenient. The owner of this garden who has managed and operated it for over 20 years by himself wanted to keep this place as intact as possible. Therefore, it is recommended to wear sneakers to walk on the rather rough trails. In addition, be aware that there is an entrance fee as this is a private garden. Make sure to also check the opening hours before your visit. Inside the Manhawhangcho, you can walk the hydrangea path and the forest of cypress trees, and the resting areas with hammocks offer another pleasure. The first Hydrangea Festival was held in the summer of 2018. Why don't you come to enjoy the leafy shade of the forest and the fragrance of hydrangea?

stories.title: Sodam Botanical Garden
stories.script: Sodam Botanical Garden is located on the way to the dinosaur tracksite of Jangjwa-ri, Donghae-myeon from Danghangpo Tourist Site, the venue for the “Gyeongnam Goseong Dinosaur World Expo.” It is a popular driving course since it is connected to Route 77, which was selected as one of the Beautiful Roads of Korea.  Surrounding flowers and trees nearby coffee shops on a hill greets visitors. Don't be disappointed by its small size. If you look carefully and closely, you can see a variety of flowers. The owner, Sung Man-gi, has managed this place for over three decades with the goal of creating this place like a Heidelberg in Germany. The inspiration he received from tourist destinations overseas when he traveled around the world 700 times as a cabin crew of an airline together with props that go well with the place demonstrates his sincerity to this place.  You may take a rest with a cup of fruity herb tea, a representative menu of the garden's coffee shop, and be immersed in the landscape of this place. Those who came up the uneven path would be fascinated by the breathtaking view of the archipelago.

stories.title: Goseong Yeonhwasan Mountain
stories.script: Yeonhwasan was named because its shape resembles a lotus flower with overlapping petals. Although Yeonhwasan Mountain is called a mountain consisting of 10 peaks including Seonyubong,Ongnyeobong and Tangeumbong, the gentle slopes and ridges are more like a hill, creating a hiker-friendly route. From the summit of the mountain, visitors will be able to see the Okcheonsa Temple nestled in the mountain and the deep Danghangpo Sea to the mountain's south. It is also fun to find dinosaur footprints at the entrance of the trail. It is difficult to see the sunlight, let alone the view, due to the soaring trunk of trees and leaves in the dense forest. However, it adds a mood to the secluded hiking. Walking through the lust forest, you will encounter Jeongolmot Pond. Some people fish in the calm water, allowing visitors to find peace of mind. Walking straight up along the valley, there stands Okcheonsa Temple. Yeonhwasan Mountain creates magnificent view along with the valley surrounding Okcheonsa Temple.  Voted as one of the 100 scenic sites by the Korea Forest Service, Yeonhwasan Mountain is the most popular tourist destination in Goseong. Why don't you plan to rest and find peace of mind in the secluded Yeonhwasan Mountain?

stories.title: Goseong Okcheonsa Temple
stories.script: Okcheonsa Temple is a historic temple located in Yeonhwasan Mountain. It was built in the 16th year of King Munmu's reign (676) during the Silla Dynasty by Great Master Uisang to preach the Science of Huayan and is being referred to as one of 10 Huayan Temples. After walking up the stone stairs, there is a yard in front of the temple. It was the training ground for monk army during the Imjin War.  This was the place where Great Monk Cheongdam, who tried to follow and live by the words of Buddha by reorganizing the Buddhist order after the liberation, first lived as a monk in 1927. On September 27th of the lunar calendar, the Nirvana rite for the Great Master Uisang and Great Monk Cheongdam is held every year.  Maybe because of the spirit of patriotic Buddhism for the country, the scenery of the temple gives a quiet yet robust feeling like a stone tablet located at the entrance of the temple. The name Okcheon, which means “jade spring,” was derived from the mineral spring located next to the main hall. Okcheonsam Spring has long been famous for its water, which is believed to cure diseases, and is selected as one of the top 100 water in Korea.

stories.title: Goseong Namsan Park
stories.script: No. 1 landscape of Goseong, Goseong Namsan Park is the only county park in the area. Centering around Bogwangsa Temple, there is a memorial stone to pay respects to the souls of all the fallen heroes who died protecting Korea during the Korea War and a rest area on the ridge, allowing visitors to take rest and enjoy the view of Hallyeosudo. In particular, the trail is well-built with a thinning-out cypress tree to provide comfort for a walk. It attracts professional athletes for winter training due to the comfortable trail bringing about less joint pain. The trails take visitors to the peak of the mountain. From the top, you can see a panoramic view of Goseong. The real charm of Namsan Park comes from the auto camping site. Visitors can enjoy a romantic evening with the sunset over the South Sea in a caravan or tent. In addition, this place is filled with sweet scent of red chrysanthemum in fall, and a magnificent view and colorful autumn colors add splendor to the view. Furthermore, there are outdoor exercise equipments for physical training for the health of locals. Goseong Namsan Park is a perfect place for physical training and forest bathing at the same time.

stories.title: Sangjogam Rock
stories.script: Sangjogam is a rock in the sea located in Deongmyeong-ri, Hai-meyon, Goseong-gun. It was named after its shape of table legs. It is also called “Ssangbari” due to its odd shape of multiple table legs.   Overall, it is a towering cliff. Its precipitous wall of stratified cliffs creates harmony with the wide, open coastal scenery. What makes this place even more famous is the dinosaur footprints from the Cretaceous Period together with the beautiful landscape. Looking at the remains of dinosaur nearby the steep coastal cliffs, you can naturally imagine dinosaurs romping in nature. It is a perfect place for a family outing with children. The white sandy beach next to Sangjogam Rock is shallow and has a gentle slope, creating a nice ground for children to play. Come and make unforgettable memories with your family in a picturesque Sangjogam Rock away from hard concrete walls.

stories.title: Goseong Dinosaur Museum
stories.script: Founded to study dinosaur footprint fossils and understand the Earth's environment better, this place exhibits four genuine dinosaur fossils and other replicas. Its other name is the Korean Jurassic Park due to its mega size unlike other dinosaur museums. Silicone was used to realize the actual leather of dinosaurs and moving models add graphicness as if dinosaurs came back to life.  In the indoor exhibition hall, you can feel the traces of dinosaurs at that time, such as fossils and footprints, and also see the diorama video of the life of dinosaurs in the Cretaceous Era. As a so-called fossil excavation experience, there is an experience center to excavate dinosaur fossils buried in the sand. For children fascinated by dinosaurs, this experience center will make them feel like a paleontologist for a moment. To top it off, there is an outdoor playground with dinosaur models displayed and a trail of dinosaur footprints along the Sangjogam Beach. Feel the joy of exploring the world of dinosaur.

stories.title: Donghwa Fishing Village
stories.script: Donghwa Fishing Village was constructed in March 2005 by local fishermen to transform the village into a tourist area providing a special memory to visitors. You can see Getbeol (mud) Village unfolding before your eyes if you go east from Sangjogam Rock for about 5 minutes. From digging out clams, which requires to be on time for the low tide, the place provides various programs such as the torch experience that catches octopus by lighting up the torch. (It is now changed to lanterns due to sea pollution). You have to make reservation online for the experience.  In addition, there is Soeulbiposeong Fortress, which served as a military base when Admiral Yi Sun-sin set up a camp to train his soldiers during the Imjin War in 1592. Back then, it was a restricted area. Along with the fortress site, enjoy the fairy-like moments at Donghwa Fishing Village.

stories.title: Old Walls of Hakdong Village, Goseong
stories.audioTitle: Old Walls of Hakdong Village, Goseong
stories.script: One day, a crane appeared in a dream. The crane flew down to a place and laid its eggs. Visiting the place from the dream the next day, an area with a stunning view shaped similar to a crane appeared. The place was since then named Hakdong (Hak meaning crane in Korean). This is the fable of Hakdong Village.  These old walls are modern cultural heritage recognized by the Cultural Heritage Administration of Korea. Constructed with flat stones from Sutaesan Mountain located behind the village and red clay layered on top of one another, it retains the locality of stone wall, which rarely can be found these days.  The first house built against the backdrop of this landscape is none other than the Head House of the Choe Clan. Built by Choe Hyeong-tae, a great-great-grandson of General Choe Gyun of the Righteous Army during the Imjin War, it features unique buildings and vegetable garden, creating genteel atmosphere. Next to the head house is the Historic House of Choe Yeong-deok sharing the wall with the head house. This is currently operated as a Hanok guest house and a place to experience the Korean traditional Hanok house.  If you walk into the village following the path along the wall, you will find a cauldron lid hanging at a teahouse. Inside the teahouse, there is Hakdong Gallery where a large garden and bamboo forests greet you. You can appreciate arts made with juniper and drink tea by sitting on the toenmaru (“wooden-floored veranda”). The old walls of the historic Hakdong Village are considered the most beautiful among the 14 wall heritage sites in Korea. Feel the historical mood in this traditional village.

stories.title: Byeongpung Rock
stories.script: Spotted after 10 minutes of walking from Ibap Village, Byeongpung Rock is columnar joints that resemble a long column of cross-section, just like its name. It was named as Byeongpung because the columnar joints in the distance look like a folding screen. At the end of the well-polished wooden deck, there is a small observatory where you can see the scenery that will take your breath away. There is clear glass installed on the bottom of the observatory to see the sea and cliffs under your feet which will add to the excitement.  You can see the sea cave known as the Groom Rock and the Bride Rock located at the bottom of Byeongpung Rock on your way to the sea from the Ibap Port. Don't you think there is a legend behind the cave just listening to its name? Long time ago there was a kind couple who lived in a fishing village. One day, they saved the Dragon King’s son and, in return, he turned the shelter into a cave so that the couple can be safe amid the war. Another legend says that two dragons ascended to heaven in this place. Due to these interesting stories that have been passed down from mouth to mouth, many visitors come to the sea cave to make a wish.

stories.title: Munsuam Hermitage
stories.script: Munsuam Hermitage was established in 688 A.D. by the famed monk Uisang-daesa (625–702 A.D.) in the 5th year of King Seongdeok's reign of Silla. It was known as a training site for elite youth corps called Hwarang during the Silla Dynasty. However, as the current Munsuam Hermitage was reconstructed to be recovered from the damage by typhoon Sara, it may be difficult to find the traces from 1,000 years ago. Nevertheless, the hermitage has long been referred to as the “Haedong Scenic Area” since the Three Kingdoms of Korea. The hermitage is located on the top of Muisan Mountain. However, as it is accessible by car, people visit to see the amazing view comfortably. The views of the archipelago from Munsuam Hermitage are simply breathtaking.  This place is also known as one of the three major prayer places in the southern area of Korea. When the college entrance exam is around the corner or at the end of the year, the place is crowded with visitors making a wish. At the Munsubosal (the Bodhisattva of Wisdom) Cave, located behind the hermitage, numerous people are gathered before the cave to see the face of Munsubosal and to make a wish.

stories.title: Ancient Tombs in Songhak-dong
stories.script: This is a place where ancient tombs, or Gobun in Korean, in the Gaya Era are gathered. Gobun is a tomb of the ruling class in a certain form. All the tombs, including the tomb No. 1, which is located on the highest location, are drum-shaped tumuli with a rectangular stone room inside. They serve as the sources of important historical data of Gaya culture. The reason why people of Gaya built tombs in the wide open field was to boast its powerful force to other neighboring countries. As there is a convenient path in between the tombs, you can take a look around the whole area.  Since they are ancient tombs, various relics and remains were discovered here. As many as 1,000 relics including vessels were excavated and are now being displayed at the nearby Goseong Museum. You can also see the dolmens, a representative tomb of the Bronze Age, which can be rarely seen in the country. If you connect holes on the dolmen, you would be able to spot the Big Dipper.

stories.title: Jangboksan Mountain
stories.script: Jangboksan Mountain, located in Yeojwa-dong, Jinhae-gu, Changwon-si, is 585.2 meters above sea level surrounding Jinhae-gu like a folding screen. Since General Janbok from the Three Hans period is believed to have learned how to ride a horse and martial arts here, this mountain was named “Janboksan Mountain.” At the foot of the mountain, Jangboksan Park stands on a 2.9 million m2-wide green lawn. A mermaid statue, a lion statue of the Janbokgyo Bridge, and a monument can be found in the rest area within the park. In addition, there are Daegwangsa and Jinheungsa Temples around the mountain. If you walk along the cherry blossom path of the park, there is a memorial monument to eight navy military police officers who died in preventing the collapse of the tunnel in 1979 on the west side of the entrance to the Majin Tunnel. At the top of the park, it offers a panoramic view of beautiful Geojedo, Jamdo, Jeodo, Samduck, and Gagdeokdo Islands. In particular, it is a must-visit spot in spring as thick cherry blossoms in full bloom will present unforgettable memory. Climb up Jangboksan Mountain and encounter a romantic city Jinhae in all four seasons.

stories.title: Gunhang Culture Exploration Trail & Modern Culture and History Street
stories.audioTitle: Gunhang Culture Exploration Trail & Modern Culture and History Street
stories.script: If it is your first time visiting Jinhae, how about going on a “Jinhae Modern Culture Tour,” allowing you to explore Jinhae with fun stories told by a tour guide? The Modern Culture Tour consists of two courses: Course 1 is “Gunhang Culture Exploration Trail” to explore the history of Jinhae centered on historic sites, and Course 2 “Modern Culture and History Trail” to feel the modern culture of Jinhae.  Gunhang Culture Exploration Trail allows you to visit a military base using the feature of a military port. Accompanied by a volunteer, it provides a tour with historical and cultural stories related to the site.
