You get to explore historic sites, such as the shooting location of the first Battle of Yeonpyeong, Monument with the Autograph of Patriotic Martyr Ahn Jung-geun, Tonghae Station, the Turtle Ship, the statue of General Yi Sun-sin holding a bow, and the hexagon pavilion.  After exploring beautiful landscape and military port of Jinhae through the Gunhang Culture Exploration Trail, shall we begin the Modern Culture and History Trail to feel the breath of modern history in Jinhae?  The Jinhae Modern Culture and History Trail tour program was developed as a guided tour course. Starting from the House of the Navy, the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, the cultural space Heukbaek, the Gunhang Village History Museum, the Gunhang Village Theme Park, the Jinhae Gunhang Village Street, and other tourist destinations to feel the history of Jinae, it ends at Japanese-style Jangok Street, Jinhae Post Office, Central Market, and Jinhae Station to feel the modern culture of Jinhae. If you go on a modern culture tour while listening to a guide's explanation, you would be able to realize the saying “you can see as much as you know.”  Feel the atmosphere of Jinhae's modern cultural heritage along the Modern Culture and History Trail.

stories.title: Jinhae Tower
stories.script: Jinhae Tower is an observatory and a museum located on top of Jehwangsan Mountain. It is designated as the Modern Building of Changwon-si No.3. On the top of the mountain, there used to be a memorial monument made after the mast (a long pole rising from the deck of a ship) of the Mikasa battleship, which served as the flagship (a vessel used by the commanding officer) of the Battle of Korea Strait, to commemorate Japan’s victory from the Russia-Japan War by defeating the Baltic Fleet. However, it was demolished and replaced with a new nine-story concrete tower, symbolizing Korean Navy on September 20, 1967 following the public opinion to destroy the emblem of the national disgrace after the liberation in 1945. The first floor is dedicated to the Jinhae City Museum and the second floor is to the reference library, which features artifacts excavated around the Jinhae area. From the 3rd to the 8th floor, you can either walk stairs or use an elevator to go up and down. You can overlook the whole city of Jinhae and its surrounding coast on every floor through a large clear window.

stories.title: Jinhae Station
stories.script: Jinhae Station is a railway station of the Jinhae Line in Yeojwa-dong, Jinhae-gu, Changwon-si, Gyeongsangnam-do Province. As Tonghae Station, the last station of the Jinhae Line, is located in a military reservation area, Jinhae Station is considered to be the final destination of the line. This building was designated as a Registered Cultural Heritage No. 192 on September 14, 2005. KORAIL and Changwon-si agreed to stop its operation in February 1, 2015 and only run a tourist train in every April for Jinhae Gunhangje Festival. Only freight trains run on Hangamseon line of the Jinhae branch line in the normal days.  Jinhae Station still preserves the form and scale of the regional train station in the year 1926 when it was founded. The platform is in a unique form of combining island platform and terminal platform. In April, visitors fill the station to enjoy the Jinhae Gunhangje Festival. Jinhae is home to a large number of navy forces. The station used to have Traffic Management Office (TMO), but it transferred to Changwon Jungang Station when the Jinhae Station closed down due to the suspension of passenger service.

stories.title: Dongseom Island
stories.script: Dongseom is an island located 100 meters away to the southeast from the Sinmyeong Village of Myeong-dong. Originally known as Ai (child) seom, the island was written in Dongseom borrowing the Chinese characters. It is assumed that the place used to be called the “Au (little brother) seom” for its small size and changed to “Aiseom” later, which eventually became Dongseom. Many tourists visit the island to walk on a sea path formed by a sand bank appearing two times a day at the low tide. Changwon Marine Park located nearby together with Dongseom Island are a nice travel destination to visit in one day. The deck surrounding the entire seashore creates a nice trail.  Following the beautiful coastline of Jinhae, friendly port villages will come into sight. Amazing landscape and marvelous nature would make your jaw drop. Dongseom Island with a mysterious sea path becomes a popular filming site at night. How about a special night out on the beautiful island?

stories.title: Jinhae Dream Park
stories.script: Opened in March 2009, Jinhae Dream Park is a large forest recreation facility named after a public contest. It has Jinhaeman Ecological Forest (126 ha), Timber Culture Experience Center, Gwangseokgol Shelter, and Youth Center.  Jinhaeman Ecological Forest, which restored a warm-temperate forest utilizing the warm southern coastal region to the fullest, has around 90 subtropical rare plants and a total of 145 species, along with approximately 70,000 warm-temperate forest trees.  At the Timber Culture Experience Center, you can see and experience all about tree at a glance, ranging from the generation and growth of the tree. Gwangseokgol Shelter is a resting area built in a natural valley, which flows throughout the year, with a lawn plaza and 25 types of trees, including maple trees. Natural Ecological Learning Wetland provides a learning space to explore lotus, calamus, aquatic plants, fish and more.  You can visit one place at a time by car, but if you park your car in the parking lot of the Jinhae Community Center for the Differently Abled next to the gu (district) office, you can feel the fragrance of nature and the surrounding views while walking from Gwangseokgol Shelter to Jinhaeman Ecological Forest and Timber Culture Experience Center.  How about a “healing picnic” at Jinhae Dream Park to experience both forest and sea?

stories.title: Anmingogae Pass
stories.script: Anmingogae Pass is a 9-kilometer-long pass that stretches from Taebaek-dong, Jindae-gu to Anmin-dong, Seongsan-gu. The pass is also known for its scenic view of Jinhaeman Bay, Jinhaegu Port, Sirubong Peak and Cheonjabong Peak. Particularly known for its beautiful sunrise, sunset, and night view, cherry blossom trees are lined up on both sides of the two-lane road for 5.6 kilometers to Jinhae, making up the famous cherry blossom tunnel in spring.  There are benches placed about 100 meters apart, offering visitors a rest to catch their breath while enjoying the view and cherry blossom trees. Another name for this destination is “Mannaljae.” The name originated from the fact that women who came to Changwon to marry from Jinhae met their families on the third day of the national holiday. Enjoy the beauty of Jinhae all year round at Anmingogae Pass, which is famous for sunrise, sunset, night view, and cherry blossom.

stories.title: Jinhae Marine Leports Center
stories.script: Built to expand the base of ocean leisure, Jinhae Marine Leports Center is well equipped with excellent facilities, various sports equipment, and a marine training center with instructors who are all former national athletes available at low fee. The center provides classes for marine sports, which are difficult to experience, such as cruising, dinghy yacht, and windsurfing. After completing the course, you can enjoy it anytime with an equipment rental service. Simple try-out programs are also provided for kayaks, rafting boats, and banana boats. As you can even ride a cruise yacht, feel the breeze of sea wind, and enjoy the splendid landscape of the sea, more and more family tourists are coming for it.  Anyone can easily learn how to ride a dinghy yacht and windsurfing here at the Jinhae Marine Leports Center. More and more children are visiting with their parents to experience the excitement of driving a yacht. Feel the thrilling experience of leisure sports here at the Jinhae Marine Leports Center!

stories.title: Ungcheon Ceramic Kiln Site Museum
stories.script: Founded on the Ungcheon Ceramic Kiln Site, designated as Gyeongsangnam-do Monument No. 160, the Ungcheon Ceramic Kiln Site Museum opened its doors to the public on November 23, 2011. Ungcheon Ceramic Kiln Site is where Buncheong jars and white porcelains were produced during the early days of the Joseon Dynasty. Bowl, which takes up the largest proportion of the excavated artifacts here, has received attention for its simple yet natural beauty. In addition, excavated kilns are used as valuable research materials for the study of kiln structure in the early days of the Joseon Dynasty.  In addition to the exhibition hall, where 80 artifacts excavated from the site are displayed, the museum operates a workshop where visitors can actually gain hands-on experience in making ceramic ware. It is an open cultural space where people can take a look around the kiln site from the observation deck as well as a tour around the historic site, view the exhibits, and take part in the ceramic ware-making program.

stories.title: Minister Ju Gicheol Memorial Hall
stories.script: The life of Minister Ju Gicheol, who kept his faith until the end against the shrine worship that the Japanese forced on Korean people, is a pride of Presbyterian churches in the Gyeongsangnam-do Province. The Minister Ju Gicheol Memorial Hall, located in Ungcheon, Jinhae, is dedicated to Reverend Ju Gi-cheol, one of the patriotic martyrs during the Japanese colonial period. He died in prison after being arrested for refusing to worship at Shinto shrines and for his involvement in the anti-Japanese movement. This place allows a visitor to look back upon the footprints of the minister. Honoring the anti-Japanese independence activist Ju Gi-cheol and his spirit who died at the Pyongyang Prison in 1944, it is a place of education where people can better understand the modern history of Korea. There is an exhibition hall, with more than 100 of his personal items on display, as well as a multimedia room and an archive.  In addition, there is a trail called “Pilgrimage route of Minister Ju Gi-cheol.” Departing at the Minister Ju Gicheol Memorial Hall in Nammun-dong, Jinhae-gu, it is a 64-km-long course that looks around Ungcheon elementary school, Ungcheon Church, the Memorial Hall of Gyeongnam Mission 120 Years, Masan Moonchang Church, Memorial Hall of Martyr Rev. Son Yang-won and his birthplace. Have a special pilgrimage to Jinhae, following the footprints of martyr Ju Gi-cheol.

stories.title: Sokuri Island
stories.script: Sokuri Island is an uninhabited small island, named after sokuri (“basket”) due to its shape. It is 1.5km away from the southwest of Myeong-dong, Jinhae-gu. There are two mountaintops on both sides of the east and west of the Island. Crossing the uphill path in between, the northeastern seashore and Ungdo (bear) Island come into sight. Every summer, dried anchovies provide a unique experience for tourists to visit the place. At low tide, a mysterious sea path called the “Moses Miracle” opens between the south of the island and Ungdo Island so that you can walk through it. In addition, the island is famous for clean water, shallow water levels, and soft beach sand. Family tourists visit the island to enjoy the good scenery of the natural environment during summer days. The number goes up to 300 people on the weekend. Recently, people come here to spend time for boat-fishing or camping. If you want to make your summer vacation special, Sokuri Island would be perfect for you.

stories.title: Kim Daljin Literary Museum and Birth Home of Kim Daljin
stories.audioTitle: Kim Daljin Literary Museum and Birth Home of Kim Daljin
stories.script: Kim Daljin Literary Museum was constructed by his disciple to pass down the passion for Buddhism and literature of Kim Daljin who lived as a scholar of the Chinese classics, teacher, monk, and poet by restoring his private house in Jinhae. This hall is highly appreciated as the “Best Literature Hall in 2016” by the Korean Literature House Association. The museum consists of an underground and a ground floor. The birth home of Kim is located nearby. The appearance of the museum gives off a benevolent feeling like an old country school. Before entering the museum, visitors can appreciate the creative artwork of children. The actual size of his photo greets the visitors at the entrance. Visitors can see actual items used by Kim as well as his research documents to look back on his life and literature work. Art Street near the museum reenacts scenes from daily life in the 1930s. The birth home of Kim Daljin has a wide yard as well as a vegetable and flower garden, giving off a homely atmosphere that well demonstrates his warm and soft personality. If you want to learn about Korea's past and literature of Kim, how about visiting Kim Daljin Literary Museum in Changwon?

stories.title: Sosa Village (Kim’s Museum)
stories.script: Sosa Village filled with a unique atmosphere allows visitors to feel the 60s and 70s. It was once a reservoir for water supply when the Japanese built Jinhae Gunghang Port in 1905. At that time, there were seven villages in the area, and Sosa Village was the place where they were forcibly relocated. Therefore, Sosa Village, which was established in the modern period, can be said to have opened up Jinhae today. Still, there are many traces of Japanese heritage remaining in this village. In particular, Ungdong Reservoir, located in the west of the village which is still in use as a naval water source, is a good example of the trace. It is currently stretched with barbed wire to prohibit the access of civilians. During spring and summer, the water levels rise due to heavy rain, passing the floodgate and forming a seven-step waterfall, creating a spectacular view. The narrow path from the village to the floodgate of the reservoir is called the “Lover’s Road.” Kim’s Museum and Sosa Tavern are private museums built by Kim Hyun-cheol to demonstrate the modern and contemporary history of Korea with the family history of Kim. If you look thoroughly as if you are exploring your grandmother’s house rather than studying the exhibits displayed, you may feel the memories and history of the village that stood the test of time.  How about going on a time-travel by walking the old path of Sosa Village, which itself is a museum?

stories.title: House of Choe Champan, Hadong
stories.script: The setting of the famous TV series Toji (“The Land”) and the family house of Kim Hee-sung from the Mr. Sunshine was filmed in the House of Choe Champan in Pyeongsa-ri, Hadong.  Originally, this place was used as a filming site to reenact the scene of Toji. As the major background of Toji is Pyeongsa-ri, Agyang-myeon, Hadong-gun, houses and villages were reconstructed here. Starting as the filming site for the TV series, the house has not only made its appearance in more than 10 films but is also a valuable cultural asset that many tourists visit even on weekdays.  Walking up the path following the signpost after paying an entrance fee, the statue of Choe Champan reading a book under the big tree comes into sight. Take a memorable photo here as it is a famous photo spot.  If you go inside, you can see the location where Kim Hee-sung received a watch on his way to studying abroad in Mr. Sunshine. You are allowed to get inside by taking your shoes off. You can reenact the famous scene by stepping on the wooden floor.  A detached quarter where Seohee, the main character of Toji, lived has a pond, so it is very easy to recognize the place. Fans of Toji, either novel or drama, cannot pass the place without taking a photo. If you get close to the stone wall after finishing looking around the house, a golden rice field and a big mountain capture your attention. If you visit right before harvesting rice, you can see the splendid view of golden field that sways with the wind. Make sure you take another photo here as it will leave you an unforgettable memory.  <This guide was recorded by Kwon Ah-hyun of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Historic House of Ildu, Hamyang
stories.script: Walking briskly hiding the bouquet behind with a pounding heart. This is the place where Hee-sung went to see Ae-sin in Mr. Sunshine: the Historic House of Ildu. When you walk along the walls, you can see arch-stone laid, which can be only found at a palace. The arch-stone served as a doorbell so that servants inside could recognize the owner returning on a horse.  This house was owned by Jeong Yeo-chang, a great scholar during the Joseon Dynasty, and his descendants. It is designated as a Important Folklore Cultural Heritage No. 186. Because it has all the features of a noble family during the Joseon Dynasty, it often appeared as a house for rich or noble family in the historical drama. This house was named the “Historic House of Ildu” by reflecting the pen name of Jeong Yeo-chang.  The tall gate which is so high that you can pass through riding on a horse has five doorplates to commemorate loyalty and filial piety, showing the power of the family. There are a total of 12 buildings in the house. If you are running out of time, sarangchae (men’s quarters) and gotganchae (storage quarter) are the must-see.  The sarangchae with a cool upper floor appeared in Mr. Sunshine as the house of Ae-shin. There are two big tablets hung on the building; the black one says “Munheonsega (scholarly families)” and the wooden one says “Chunghyojeorui (loyalty, filial affection, and fidelity).” Underneath the upper floor is called Gwang, which was used as a warehouse. It was said that a phallic rock was buried there, helping to carry on a family line.  The storage quarter shows the economic power of the household. Built with wood and soil, it is in a different structure from the general Hanok style. As it was used to store grains for a long time, ventilation and humidity were critical. To keep away harmful insects, a window was designed upward, assisting the repeated contraction and relaxation of wood and soil according to temperature and humidity.  This place provides Hanok-stay program as well. If you make a reservation online or by phone and settle the payment, you can experience staying at a cultural property How about a unique experience of staying in an ondol (Korean traditional floor heating system) room in the cold winter?  <This guide was recorded by Kwon Ah-hyun of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Hamgyang Yongyudam Valley
stories.script: Hamgyang Yongyudam valley was used as a filming site for the TV series Mr. Sunshine for a scene in which Ae-shin, the leading female character, practices her gunnery exercise. When you look at the large rocks and water flowing down, you may immediately notice the scene from Mr. Sunshine. It is famous for spiritual energy coming down from the Jirisan Mountain, maybe because it was said to be a place where nine dragons used to stay.  A legend says that there once were nine dragons and Taoist Majuk that lived in the Yongyudam valley. One day, when the Taoist was focused on playing his favorite game, janggi, nine dragons got into a fight. It began as a small fight but ended up as a mess that the entire valley was shaken. However, as Taoist Majuk was so immersed in playing janggi, he didn’t hear a sound. The beloved donkey of Majuk called him loudly, but he got caught into a fight, turning into a rock as a result.  When the game was over and he looked around, the donkey had already turned into a rock. The Taoist was so angry that he broke the janggi board into pieces and threw them to the nine dragons and eventually expelled them from the valley. It is said that the broken pieces of the board are the rocks of Yongyudam Valley today.  It once used to be a state-designated scenic spot. After the construction of a dam nearby, it is no longer referred to as the scenic spot. The valley is not for swimming, and it is prohibited to swim or camp out in the valley. Pay extra caution during the rainy season as the water rises. Instead, you can appreciate the marvelous view of the valley by walking on Jirisan Dulle-gil along the valley.  <This guide was recorded by Kwon Ah-hyun of Korea Tourism Organization

stories.title: Changnyeong Uponeup Marsh (1988)
stories.script: In Changnyeong, which has been long referred to as the “Fire Village” from the Gaya Era, there is a large marsh. Uponeup Marsh, located about 10 minutes by bus from downtown Changnyeong, is the second marsh designated as the Ramsar Wetland in Korea. It is the largest of the wetlands in the country.  Uponeup Marsh is so large that, depending on where you depart from, you can see and experience whole different things. In general, visitors start at the Ecological Center. This route is suitable for a walking trip or bicycle trip, which is recommended to those who want to take a slow stroll. If you want to see migratory birds, start at the parking lot of Somok Village.  Uponeup Marsh includes Upo, Sajipo and Mokpo sections, as well as Jjokjibeol and sanbakbeol wetlands.These are the names made during the Japanese colonial period, and their original Korean names are Sobeol, Namubeol, and Moraeboel. People who lived here for a long time prefer to call them by their old Korean name. The marsh was created by Topyeongcheon Stream and Nakdonggang River nearby. It is assumed that the bank was piled up following the flow of the river and stagnated water, thereby creating the Uponeup Marsh today. It used to play the role of the reservoir in the past. It was also a fishing spot to catch freshwater fish by riding a boat or throwing a net. Now is the home to migratory birds, freshwater fish, and wild plants. Ecological Wetland School and Ecological Experience Center provide both educational and scientific opportunities to see and learn about the ecosystem of the wetland and experience dugout canoe riding, loach fishing, and aquatic insect hunting. Come and see the famous Uponeup Marsh.   <This guide was recorded by Kwon So-hyun of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Healing Forest Entrance
stories.script: Healing Forest Entrance This is the Healing Forest located in Jongcheon-myeon, Seocheon-gun, Chungcheongnam-do.  The place was named “Jongcheon-meyon” because you can hear the sound of bell (or jong in Korean) ringing from the flowing stream. Unlike other places, Jongcheon-ri is famous for having many propitious spots. There is also a legend about the famous Lee Ji-Ham who wrote the Secret Divinatory Art of Tojeong. Healing Forest provides visitors a chance to enjoy peaceful nature with a relaxing walk along the forest.  Located at the skirt of Huirisan and Mususan Mountains, the destination provides various experiential programs for visitors from singing-ball experience, log meditation, and aroma therapy, to detox yoga. Full of cypress, pine, oak, and bamboo trees, take a breath of fresh air away from the hustle and bustle of busy city life.

stories.title: Nakgang Waterway Park
stories.script: Nakgang Waterway Park, located on the left side of the entrance of Andong Dam Hydroelectric Power Plant, is a park that was created by additionally constructing the pond, metasequoia forests, fountain, and walking trails in the existing waterfall park.  This park was inspired by the image of the great Korean scholar, Toegye Lee Hwang, but it somewhat reminds us of one of Monet's paintings.  Monet is 19th century's representative pioneer of impressionism, who is also well known as the “artist of water,” or the “magician of light.”  His life was full of water and garden, and his drawings are full of waterscapes.  The scenery of this Nakgang Waterway Park looks very similar to Monet's Garden at Giverny, where he spent half of his life, creating a fantastic atmosphere as if having walked into a masterpiece.  That's why this park is also known as the “Giverny of Korea.”  The water in the waterfall and fountain comes from the reservoir of Andong Dam,  which works by the system that uses the natural head drop caused by the difference in water level. The pond filled with water lilies slightly bends by the rainbow bridge, leads to the narrow wetland, and then spreads wide over the shallow waterway across the stepping stones. By the side of the pond, evergreen fir trees and metasequoias are beautifully lined up, making the walking trail look more refreshing.  After walking through the path lined with fir trees and metasequoias, it continues to the woodland path going upward to Andongnu Pavilion. From the pavilion, located at the highest spot in the park, Andong Dam reveals itself at a stone's throw away, and in the distance, Woryeonggyo Bridge and the waterway of Nakdonggang River flowing into the city creates a picturesque view.  If you walk up the woodland path a little further from Andongnu Pavilion, you can reach the top of Andong Dam. In the past, it was not allowed for the public to access because it was designated as a national security facility. Nowadays, the top of the dam is open to the public, allowing people to use this place for rest and picnics. When you stand on the top of the dam, the panoramic view of the Nakdonggnag River and the fresh breeze will make you feel refreshed.  But do you know why this place is called Nakgang Waterway Park instead of Nakdongdonggang Waterway Park? It's because the people of Andong call the waterway that leads to Andongho Lake Nakgang, and called Nakdonggang River when the waterway joins Banbyeoncheon Stream by downtown Andong. Nakgang Waterway Park is a “secret forest” to the people of Andong where they can enjoy their time relaxing and taking photos.

stories.title: Andong Folk Museum
stories.script: Andong, dubbed the “Capital of the Korean Spirit and Culture,” is a place where Korean traditional culture is alive and the Confucian culture is deeply rooted. In particular, the buildings and folk crafts from the Joseon Dynasty are well preserved in this city. In addition, this is where many Confucian scholars came from, including Toegye Lee Hwang. Since people can experience the traditions and cultures of the Joseon Dynasty while staying in the old houses that are hundreds of years old, Andong became a popular tourist site visited by many tourists all year round. Among those many places where you can see traditional cultural heritage, there is this one place you should never miss. It is Andong Folk Museum.  Andong Folk Museum is one of the museums of the northern region of Gyeongsangbuk-do Province, built back in 1992. This place mainly exhibits Confucian culture, the distinct culture of the Andong region, especially the Four Ceremonial Occasions. In addition, visitors can see various folk games made in this region in miniature models. The museum also has an audio-visual room and theater where you can watch videos.  Andong Folk Museum consists of an indoor and outdoor museum with a total area of 171,630㎡. The indoor museum mainly exhibits materials related to life-long rituals based on the Confucian culture of Andong and its unique living culture. On the first floor of the exhibition room, the timeline from the pray for offspring to the growth of children is displayed. On the second floor, the customs from the coming-of-age ceremony to the ritual ceremony are displayed. In the case of the living culture, the living culture of the ordinary people is displayed on the first floor exhibition room, while the living culture of Yangban (nobleman) is displayed on the second floor.  The outdoor museum holds important living cultural materials of traditional houses built across the submerged district during the construction of Andong Dam, such as Seokbinggo, Woryeongdae, Stonewall House, and Thatched-Roof House. Since the displayed materials are more vivid than the small miniature models displayed in the indoor museum, this is a perfect place for taking commemorative photos.  If you are interested in traditional culture and want to learn more about Andong, we highly recommend visiting the Andong Folk Museum.

stories.title: Woryeonggyo Bridge
stories.script: This is a city of classical scholars full of fidelity, but it seems like there were also many couples full of love  because this bridge was made to commemorate the beautiful and sublime love of a couple who lived 400 years ago.  The bridge is called Woryeonggyo, and it is the longest wooden bridge in Korea, measuring 6 meters wide and 387 meters long.  Back in 1998, during the relocation of an Andong citizen, Lee Eung-tae's grave, a pair of shoes made of hair, a baby's swaddling clothes, and a “letter from Woni's mother” were found. Woni's mother, the wife of the scholar Lee Eung-tae, cut her own hair and made it into a pair of shoes, praying for the recovery of her sick husband.  However, despite her devotion, her husband passed away at age 31.  A letter written by Woni's mother, who grieved her husband's death, is the “Letter from Woni's Mother.”  You can feel the mournful heart of a wife who lost her husband in this letter that starts with the sentence, “Dear. Woni's father.”  Since this letter has such a high archaeological value, it has even been featured on the cover of the international archaeological jorrnal ANTIQUITY, as well as the global documentary magazine NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC.  Based on this story spread all over Andong, Woryeonggyo Bridge was built to praise the affectionate love of Woni's mother by making the overall shape of the bridge resemble the shoes of Woni's mother. Maybe this is why there is a myth among many couples that if you walk over Woryeonggyo Bridge by holding hands with your loved one, the love will last forever.  Another thing to notice is the Woryeongjeong Pavilion in the middle of the bridge, built with an octagonal shape.  The beautiful shape of the Woryeongjeong Pavilion even makes Woryeonggyo Bridge look more classic. The beautiful mountainscape surrounding the Nakdonggang River and the subtly rising water mist by the Woryeonggyo Bridge create a dreamy atmosphere. In particular, this place is famous for its beautiful nightscape harmonized with colorful lights and fountain shows. The fountain show is held every day at Woryeonggyo Bridge. Looking at the colorful lights under the moonlit night, you will be able to feel the charm of the Woryeonggyo Bridge more deeply.  When the sun goes down in the evening, hold your loved one's hand and stroll over the Woryeonggyo Bridge. You would be able to feel the affectionate love from 400 years ago with beautiful night scenery.

stories.title: Imcheonggak House and Seven-Story Brick Pagoda at Beopheungsa Temple Site
stories.audioTitle: Imcheonggak House and Seven-Story Brick Pagoda at Beopheungsa Temple Site
stories.script: Imcheonggak House and Seven-Story Brick Pagoda at Beopheungsa Temple Site are the places that have both the glorious and tragic history of Korea.  The famous writer Yoo Hong-jun, who served as the Administrator of the Cultural Heritage Administration, mentioned the story of Imcheonggak House and Seven-Story Brick Pagoda Beopheungsa Temple Site in his book My Exploration of Cultural Heritage. The detail of the story is as follows.  “Over the bank of Nakdonggang River that surrounds the east side of downtown Andong, a railway was built during the Japanese colonial period. The bank passed by the side of the Seven-Story Brick Pagoda Beopheungsa Temple Site very closely. The servants' quarters at the Goseong Yi clan's head house had to be broken down, as well as Gunjajeong Pavilion, of Imcheonggak House located in the mountain with a beautiful Nakdonggang River view. Even today, every time the train passes, these places must endure the vibration and noise that even shakes the ground. This is such a tragedy that the national assets and treasures still suffer in the poor surrounding.”  Let's first look at the Imcheonggak House. This oldest residential house in Korea is also the birthplace of Seokju Lee Sang-ryong, the independence activist and the first Prime Minister of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea. This house was built in 1515 by Lee Rak, who served as assistant section chief of the Ministry of Justice. It is a mansion designated as a treasure of Korea, where 500 years of history remained intact.  It was originally larger in size, but during the Japanese colonial period, it was considered a house where many disobedient and delinquent Koreans were born. For that reason, the Japanese demolished the servants' quarters and pavilions during the construction of the centerline railway. Since it still boasts great dignity, you can imagine how magnificent this place would have been if the original form had remained intact. Currently, it is constantly visited by tourists who want to try out various experience programs and stay overnight.  Imcheonggak House is also special in that it is located near the National Treasure of Korea, Seven-Story Brick Pagoda at Beopheungsa Temple Site. It is a brick pagoda stacked with bricks made from soil,  presumed to be built around the 8th century, during the Unified Silla Period. It is called the Seven-Story Brick Pagoda at Beopheungsa Temple Site because it is presumed to be built in a temple called Beopheungsa.  Seven-Story Brick Pagoda at Beopheungsa Temple Site is the tallest brick pagoda in Korea, measuring 17 meters high with a 7.75-meter-wide stylobate. The stylobate of the pagoda has a square-shaped single layer. Currently, six granite plates carved into the statue of Eight Devas and Four Heavenly Kings are placed on each surface, and a staircase is installed in the center of the south.  Currently, the railroad next to the Seven-Story Brick Pagoda at Beopheungsa Temple Site has been relocated, and this brick pagoda will be repaired through the complete dismantlement method. Since it is planned to go through a total repair after the restoration project of Imcheonggak House is over by 2025, we will soon be able to meet the Seven-Story Brick Pagoda at Beopheungsa Temple Site that resembles its original shape.

stories.title: Nagcheon Park (Nagcheongyo Bridge)
stories.script: Nakdonggang River, also referred to as Nakdong River, is a compound word for “Nakgang,” the waterway flowing to Andongho Lake, and “Donggang,” which flows from the east side of Andong, currently called the Banbyeoncheon Stream.  By this confluence, where two rivers meet, there is Nagcheongyo Bridge and Nagcheon Park.  Nagcheongyo Bridge connects Andong's original city center and Yongsang-dong. In order to create a distinctive bridge, Andong selected a wave pattern design for the sidewalk handrail on the bridge and installed lighting that goes well with the image of the bridge and its surroundings at night. Accordingly, the lighting of Nagcheongyo Bridge creates a distinctively modernized atmosphere. In particular, the colorful lights glimmering on the structure resembling a wave mark express the dynamic movement that cannot be seen on other bridges. On the right side of this bridge, there is a walking trail where many citizens can take a walk or exercise.  On Nagcheongyo Bridge, you can observe remarkable sights that cannot easily be seen elsewhere. It is the herons and cormorants living in large flocks. From a long time ago, about a dozen of herons and cormorants living in flocks were often observed in the Banbyeoncheon Stream and riverside areas.  Near Dongcheonbo, located at the eastern end of Nagcheongyo Bridge, there is Nakcheon Park. This park, which opened in May 2022, has a natural mooring (stream) facility, observatory pavilion, rest area, and walking trail. This place is especially loved by the citizens of Andong, since it is beautifully created with children's playgrounds, grass square for the whole family to enjoy, and themed gardens where you can explore seasonal flowers, such as the flower garden, peony garden, and hydrangea garden.  Nagcheongyo Bridge and Nagcheon Park are indeed the best places to enjoy modern walking trails in Andong, a city full of history and tradition.

stories.title: Gwiraejeong Pavilion & Woni’s Mother Theme Park
stories.audioTitle: Gwiraejeong Pavilion & Woni’s Mother Theme Park
stories.script: Nearby Yeonggadaegyo Bridge, which crosses the Nakdonggang River, there are Gwiraejeong Pavilion and Woni’s Mother Theme Park, where you can peek into the history of the Joseon Dynasty in the 1500s.  Gwiraejeong is a pavilion built by Nakpo Lee Goeng after he resigned from the government position in 1513, which is now designated as the Cultural Heritage Material of Gyeongsangbuk-do No. 17. Gwiraejeong Pavilion is a T-shape building with two kans in width and four kans in depth. Kan is a traditional measurement unit of Korea, one kan meaning the length between two supporting pillars. It has a hipped and gable roof, which features a triangular shape from the side. Except around the wooden floor, all pillars are angular, and the windows have wedge pillars.  Lee Goeng named this place Gwiraejeong because he was inspired by the meaning of the poem Gwigeoraesa (Homeward Bound I Go) written by Tao Yuanming. At the age of 25, Lee Goeng passed the state examination and worked in many government positions. However, he was suddenly exiled as he was involved in the Literati Purge of 1504 and appointed as one of an official of the Jungjong Coup. He had lived such a turbulent life.  Gwigeoraesa was a poem that recited the feelings of Tao Yuanming, who was on the way back home after he resigned from his position as governor of Pengze County in China. It was a declaration that stated he would be isolated from the secular world. It is surely no coincidence that Lee Goeng recalled Tao Yuanming's poem while he was building the pavilion.  In Taengniji, Korea's first human geography book, the writer Yi Chung-hwan selected Gwiraejeong as the best pavilion among many pavilions built in the Andong region. Gwiraejeong Pavilion boasts incredible scenery because it has secured the site widely opened towards the confluence of Nakgang River and Banbyeoncheon Stream, and it is always the place where the changes of nature and the river flow can be observed. The signboard of Gwiraejeong was written by the master calligrapher Hwang Gi-ro. In the rooms, poems written by the family's nine eldest sons, including Lee Goeng, and 30 poem plates written by Lee Hyeon-bo, Lee Sik, Lee Woo, and Kim Ryeong, are displayed.  Right next to Gwiraejeong Pavilion, there is Woni's Mother Theme Park. It was created near the tomb where the “Letter from Woni's Mother” and Korean affectionate love story were discovered. On the signboard that guides the park entrance, there is a beautiful trumpet creeper drawing, meaning yearning and waiting. In one corner of the park, a memorial stone engraved with the Letter from Woni's Mother stands still as a symbol of love. In the center of the park, sculptures that embody the image of a woman who made a pair of shoes with her hair by wishing for her husband's recovery, and the finger ring — a sign of their love — catch visitors' eyes. The statue of Woni's Mother looking at the slowly flowing Nakdonggang River is also an impressive feature of this park.

stories.title: Talchum Park
stories.script: One of the representative images of Andong is traditional Korean mask called Tal and Talchum, meaning Mask Dance. In particular, Andong Hahoe Mask and Hahoe Byeolsingut Talnori are considered important historical materials that they were even designated as the National Treasure and Important Intangible Cultural Heritage. The Andong International Mask Dance Festival, made under the theme of Korean mask and mask dance, is held in the whole district of the Talchum Park as Korea's representative festival.  Talchum Park, located in Unheung-dong, Andong-si, was opened on April 21, 2004, by Andong city to hold the Andong International Mask Dance Festival. Normally, this is a park that citizens can conveniently use, but it is used as a festival venue during the festival period. In the evenings during the festival, Daedong Nanjang takes its place to open the world of various types of mask dance.  Talchum Park was created with unique features from the front entrance. It was built with Korea's traditional tiled roof that expresses the vibe of the city of nobles, Andong. Once you enter the park, various sculptures related to masks and mask dances will catch your eyes. Thanks to the unique sculptures, this will become a photo zone where you can take a lot of fun and memorable pictures. This park not only has masks;  it has many movie and cartoon characters such as Batman, The Little Prince, and Shrek on display in realistic statues, which will be a place loved particularly by children.  Talchum Park not only takes its place as a park but also plays a role in promoting Korean Mask Dance. In the building on the right, there is Exhibition Hall that introduces and promotes the Korean mask dance, Main and Auxiliary Concert Hall with 2,500 seats, Chajeon Nori (Chariot Game) Training Center, Andong Tourism Information Center, and Andong Festival & Tourism Organizing Committee. Moreover, in the building on the left, there is Andong World Mask Culture Exhibition Hall.

stories.title: Former Andong Station (Modi 684)
stories.script: Andong is indeed a cultural city full of history and tradition.  It is also called the repository of Korean history and culture, as it preserves various historical and cultural properties for each era. However, we cannot only stay in the past. There is a place where it changes the cultural life of citizens and promotes sustainable development as a city of civic culture. It is Modi 684.  Located in the former Andong Station, Modi 684 is a newly created cultural platform as part of the specialized cultural zone development project. Modi is a word of Gyeongsang-do dialect that means “all together,” and it was named to preserve the regional identity and reflect the will of people who gather together. 684 is the street number of Gyeongdong-ro, which it used to be the Andong Station.  Modi 684 is a space full of vitality of the city and communication where all citizens can freely talk about the city, and it is the center of communication where citizens' public meetings are held to solve urban problems, issues, and agendas. In addition, this also becomes a complex cultural space where various cultural events and activities can be held, such as concerts, exhibitions, conferences, performance practices, pop-up stores, and media studios. Even today, various performances are held every day in this place.  Modi 684 has many facilities, such as the Modi Gallery, where exhibitions of artworks opens; Cultural Hall and Modi Plaza, where performances and events related to culture and art are held; Modi Studio, where local creators operate creative activities and pod casts; club practice rooms and small meeting room D&T; and Modi Store, where cultural product exhibitions and short-term market events are held.  Everyone can use these facilities if they apply for the rental at least a week or a month in advance.  Lastly, at the Andong Station 100 Years History Exhibition Hall, a permanent exhibition is held under the theme of Station Scenery. It is a permanent exhibition room that shows the past of Andong Station, which has vanished into history, and changes in the original city center, the meaning of spaces in the formal Andong Station, and its related records. This exhibition consists of photos of Andong Station taken in the modern and present age, landscapes of the original city center and its storytelling video records, and the Station Staff Photo Zone, where you can peek into the history of Andong Station at a glance.

stories.title: Sinse-dong Mural Village
stories.script: The charm of murals is infinite. Murals can transform an empty alley into a lively street and transform undeveloped districts into art galleries. Graffiti artists such as Banksy, a famous faceless artist, use murals to convey messages of social satire or consolation.  Sinse-dong Mural Village, located nearby Andong Dongbu Elementary School and Seongjingol, is a rising tourist attraction in Andong. The village is also an area where residents live together through community participation instead of just accepting public art. Since the Village Art Project began in 2009, the Urban Regeneration Project and the Creative Community Project were implemented in Sinse-dong. It used to be a slum, but now it has transformed into one of the must-visit tourist attractions in Andong.  At the entrance of the Mural Village, you will see the adorable moon and rabbit sculptures that let you know the beginning of the culture village.  In this village, you will find many rabbit sculptures. They symbolize this slum so-called moon village, the place closest to the moon.  In the main building of Andong Donbu Elementary School, you can find a mural of a black girl wearing a Hanbok, which was drawn by the artist Shim Chan-yang. This is the work of a world-class artist who was highly praised for the graffiti arts.  As you walk up to the mural village, you will also encounter Seongjaejeong, a 1000-year-old well. Seongjaejeong is famous for the water level that constantly maintains the same even during drought or rainy season. In addition, there has been a myth handed down that if you wash your hands in the water from this well, you will meet your destiny.  Sinse-dong Mural Village is indeed a photography destination where you can take the best photos anywhere just by pressing the shutter. How about strolling along the alleys of the Mural Village with your beloved ones?

stories.title: The History of Pride, Jeonju Hanok Village
stories.audioTitle: The History of Pride, Jeonju Hanok Village
stories.script: You are at Hanok Village of an international slow city, Jeonju. What is the first thing that comes to your mind when you think of Hanok Village? Most people would think about the street crowded with many snack stands. In fact, there is a far more important history of Korea hidden in this place. It dates back to when Korea was under the colonial rule of imperial Japan. Back then, a number of Japanese built Japanese-style houses and took over the commercial supremacy of the region. Did Koreans just stand by the oppression? The answer is no. Around 1930, Jeonju residents began to form Hanok communities villages in Pungnam-dong and Gyo-dong areas. This came from the consciousness of conflict against the expansion of Japanese-style houses and their power in Korea and from pride of being Korean. The communities remained as ordinary villages until the 2002 World Cup when there was a public opinion that Hanok Village should be used as a tourist resource in Jeonju. And that's how the Hanok Village of today, full of good eats and restaurants, has been created.  Near the Hanok Village, there is Gyeonggijeon Shrine where you can trace the footprints of Kings of Joseon Dynasty as well as Historical Archives, also known as Jeonju Sago, housing the Annals of the 500-year-long Joseon Dynasty. How about, just for today, searching for the hidden history across the Hanok Village and feeling the pride of Koreans who united to protect the country from Japan?

stories.title: The Last Prince Yi Seok Who Lives in Jeonju
stories.audioTitle: The Last Prince Yi Seok Who Lives in Jeonju
stories.script: Yi Seok, the 11th son of the Prince Yi Kang, lived a life of adversity hidden in the shadow of extravagance. He is also a grandson of Emperor Gojong and a great-grandson of Heungseon Daewongun. If the Korean Empire had continued, he would have lived a wealthy and prosperous life. However, even though he was a member of the royal family, his life was full of ups and downs. He was a singer who sang Pigeon House, a soldier who served in the Vietnam War and returned as a wounded veteran, and an exile who stayed in the United States and returned Korea to live in a rooftop house.  He dreams of restoring the imperial family for their symbolic value. Yi founded an organization called the Korean Imperial Family Cultural Foundation and is constantly on the move to restore the royal culture. What he wants to restore is not the old glory or authority but the root of Korean culture and history, as well as its symbolic value, which was once distorted and damaged by Japan during the colonial period. Yi Seok himself is the “last root of the Joseon Dynasty,” from which he wants to restore the historical value and its meaning.  <This guide was recorded by Lee Sae-bom of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Geumgang Estuary Embankment
stories.script: Completed in 1990, Geumgang Estuary Embankment was constructed with 20 floodgates and a 1,127m high embankment. It connects Gunsan in Jeollabuk-do with Seocheon in Chungcheongnam-do. The estuary embankment can hold up to 130 million tonnes of water. Geumgang Wetland Eco Park, established close to the estuary embankment, has a nice path to walk around the reed forest and ecological pond, serving as a perfect place to have a family outing. At the Geumgang Migratory Bird Observatory on the other side, you can observe migratory birds. Inside the Migratory Bird Observatory, you can get information on migratory birds from the Permanent Exhibition Hall, 3D Hall, Aquarium, Animal Specimens Exhibition Hall, and Insects Diorama Hall. On the 11th floor, there is an observatory so that you can enjoy the beautiful landscape of the Geumgang River for free. For external facilities, there are Exploration Center, Plants Ecological Center, Geumgang Bird Park, Hatching Experience Center, and Predatory Bird Center, which are also very good places for family trips for children's educational benefits as well. Geumgang Park located nearby is a perfect place for local residents to take a rest and work out, not to mention to observe migratory birds.

stories.title: Gunsan Daeya Market
stories.script: Daeya Traditional Market is a fifth-day market with a 100-year-long history, the one-and-only market in Gunsan. It is held on days that end in 1 or 6 every month. When the market opens, the place that was once quiet becomes crowded with visitors. Starting from the three-way intersection at the entrance, the market continues 300 meters long until the parking lot. When the market is held, you can see all kinds of agricultural products and foods from Gunsan, Iksan, and Gimje. Although it was famous as a cattle market until the 90s, it is now known as the tree market.  Daeya Market creates a dynamic and lively mood, particularly due to large-sized parasols and colorful tents. Once you take a step inside, you can see many seedlings, including ornamental trees and fruit trees. There is a mill near the parking lot. The savory smell of extracting sesame oil and the steam of making tteok (rice cake) stimulate the appetite of visitors.  Daeya Market is becoming a popular tourist destination among tourists, with increasing number of visitors. Make sure to visit the Impi Station, which is an abandoned railway station not far from the market, after visiting the market.

stories.title: Saemangeum Embankment
stories.script: The 33-kilometer-long Saemangeum Embankment is the world's longest man-made seawall, which took 19 years to complete. Tremendous amount of soil and stone was used for its construction that took long years to complete. It was even listed in the Guinness Book of Records as the longest seawall in the world.  A memorial tower was built to commemorate the completion of the Saemangeum Embankment in 2012 and named it “The Promised Ground,” representing Korea’s rising stature in the world.  Saemangeum 33 Center, built in the shape of a ship, is 33m tall from the ground to the top, symbolizing the 33-kilometer-long Saemangeum Embankment.  Equipped with exhibition halls, theater, observatory, conference room, and rest areas, Saemangeum Project Office is a place of education to understand the history and structure of Saemangeum Embankment.  There are six rest areas, parking lots, cafeterias, and restrooms so that visitors can enjoy the place conveniently and comfortably. Please note that many visitors take the course of going to the Gogunsan Islands after visiting Saemangeum Embankment.

stories.title: Jinpo Maritime Theme Park
stories.script: The purpose of this park is to establish the right view of history and promote self-esteem. This is because this place, located in the inner harbor of Gunsan, was a fierce battlefield of the Jinpodaecheop War.  Jinpodaecheop War was the battle that defeated Japan who invaded Jinpo, the mouth of Geumgang River, in 1380 (the 6th year of King Uwang's reign of Goryeo). History says that the Japanese raiders plundered and pillaged villages so badly that it was impossible to calculate the damage. During the time of difficulty, Choe Mu-seon invented gunpowder-based weapons and played a critical role in defeating the Japanese warships. Naval firepower was first used in the Battle of Jinpo, where the first fire maneuver tactics and naval firefight took place.  At the park, there is the Wibongham Ship exhibition hall. Built in 1945 in the U.S., Wibongham is the name of a warship that served in World War II. Taking it over from the U.S. in 1959, the ship carried out landing and transport operations and even served in Vietnam War. After serving a significant role on the sea for 48 years, it retired on the last day of the year 2006 with great honor. The exhibition hall inside the Wibongham Ship showcases weapons used during the Jinpodaecheop War, artillery made by General Choe Mu-seon, and the typical life inside the warship. The exhibition hall is a must-visit place to stop by if you visit Jinpo Maritime Theme Park.  In addition, 13 types of 16 decommissioned equipment from the Army, Navy, and Air Force are on display. So if you a big fan of military and weapons, be sure to visit Jinpo Maritime Theme Park.

stories.title: Time Travel Village
stories.script: Modern Architecture Museum (formerly the Joseon Bank Gunsan Branch), which was established for the economic exploitation of Korea during the Japanese colonial era, was the only grand building outside of Seoul. As described in the novel The Muddy Current, Joseon Bank, which was built to plunder lands of the Jeollabuk-do region, changed its name to the Bank of Korea and relocated to Jeonju. Later it was burnt down while in use as a branch of the Hanil Bank. After restoration, it has become the Modern Architecture Museum where modern building figures and bank-related documents are on display.  Gunsan Modern History Museum exhibits the old Gunsan, which was the hub for maritime logistics as a trading port, with largest modern cultural assets in the country. The unique feature of this museum is that it is an experience-type museum equipped with digital technology. In addition, by displaying the relics from the Japanese colonial era, it vividly shows the situation at the time. The museum has a Gyujanggak Library for the Modern Period,* which comprehensively manages documents, videos, books, and academic papers related to Korean modern history and culture. It plays a pivotal role for experts trying to find related data.  Honam Customs Museum (formerly the main building of the Gunsan Customs), one of the three remaining Western classical buildings in Korea, the Japanese-style house of Sinheung-dong, which is the largest and the most well-built building from the colonial era, and other historic buildings await you.

stories.title: March First Movement Historic Park
stories.script: March First Movement Historic Park is the place of missionary activity and medical education by American missionaries who established Guam Church, Guam Jesus Hospital, Gunsan Guam Kindergarten, Gunsan Allak Elementary School, Gunsan Yeongmyeong School, and Gunsan Mary Baldwin School for Girls in the Gungmeol Village. On Mar 5, 1919, teachers and students from Gunsan Yeongmyeong School and Gunsan Mary Baldwin School for Girls, staff from Guam Jesus Hospital, and people from the Guam Church played a key role in the Independence Movement.  In 2018, the Centennial Memorial Museum of the March First Movement opened inside the March First Movement Historic Park. As exhibits related to the March Fifth Independence Movement, the first March First movement in the south of the Hangang River, are displayed, you can feel the day of the independence movement 100 years ago.  There were a total of 28 independence movements that took place in Gunsan. Around 31,500 citizens joined the demonstrations, leaving an indelible scar of 53 casualties, 72 injuries, and 195 imprisonments. Nevertheless, the Gunsan March Fifth Independence Movement, the first of its kind in the south of the Hangang River, triggered the nationwide March First Movement. It shows the firm will of independence of the city where the Japanese military was stationed.  The sculpture with hands raised represents the earnest cry for love and independence of the country, fighting spirit, and indomitable spirit of independence. The Memorial Museum consists of the space to commemorate patriots (1F), space to feel the cry of the day (2F), and space to experience patriotism (3F).

stories.title: Seonyudo Beach
stories.script: Seonyudo Island, one of the most popular tourist destinations in Gunsan, lies in the heart of the Gogunsan Islands. Gogunsan Islands are composed of 63 large and small islands about 50km southwest away from Gunsan.  There are Eight Scenic Views of Seonyudo Island: Myeongsasimni Beach, a natural coastal dune with clear and fine white sand; Mangjupokpo Falls, where 7 to 8 streams of water pour down from the Mangjubong Peak when heavy rain falls in summer; Pyeongsanagan, a sandy hill in the shape of a wild goose landed on top; Musan Twelve Peaks, showing the picturesque beauty of nature; Jangjaeohwa, meaning beautiful lights of hundreds of fishing boats; autumn foliage of Woryeongbong Peak; Samdogwibeom, the three islands of seabirds; and last but not least, the Seonyu Sunset Point where fine sandy beach and Mangjubong peak form perfect harmony with breathtaking view of sunset.  It would be nice to try out the zipline, which allows you to fly over a 700-meter-long distance between the Myeongsasimnihaebyeon Beach and Solseom Island.

stories.title: Chowon Photo Studio
stories.script: Chowon Photo Studio is a well-known filming site of the Korean movie Christmas in August starring Han Suk-kyu and Shim Eun-ha. As a matter of fact, it was used as the background for most scenes of the movie.  This place was not originally a photo studio. There is a fateful story behind this special place. After searching for the right studio throughout the nation for the movie, the camera crew was discouraged that they couldn't find the one they liked. After days of disappointment, they came across a shaded garage and renovated it into a photo studio after getting permission to do so from the owner. According to the agreement, the staff tore down the place and restored it to as it was. Later, however, Gunsan city government restored the photo studio to be used as a tourist attraction.  Props from the movie are displayed inside the studio, and the manager sends a photo taken inside the studio to its visitors by e-mail. The studio is only closed on New Year's day and every Monday.

stories.title: Strife Museum in Gunsan
stories.script: Strife Museum in Gunsan is built to show the struggle that Koreans went through during the Japanese colonial era and the independence movements to reclaim the country. On the first floor of the museum, the history of strife in Gunsan and photos of the independence activities are on display. On the second floor, there is a torture room, where you can experience how the torture went, and an exhibition hall showing the names and stories of each independence activist. Thanks to the detailed explanation of the anti-Japanese movement, this place helps visitors to clearly understand and learn about the past. There are rubbings of patriotic martyrs including Yoo Gwan-sun, so you can get a copy of their faces. Feel the sorrow, agony, and strong will for independence of our ancestors.

stories.title: Gunsan Okdol Beach
stories.script: Okdol Beach located on Seonyudo Island is full of pebbles instead of sandy beach. Whereas regular beach is made up of sand, Okdol Beach consists of gem-like pebbles. Unique rock formation in harmony with pebbles on the beach create an amazing beach view.  You can enjoy a tranquil trip at Okdol Beach. While sitting on the beach, enjoy the view of a small fishing boat and cruise ships sailing across the sea or enjoy sea fishing on a seawall. Inside the port, you can take a picture against the backdrop of Samdo Gwi Beom, the three islands of seabirds, which is one of the Eight Scenic Views of Seonyudo Island.

stories.title: Jangjadaegyo Bridge
stories.script: Jangjadaegyo Bridge is a pedestrian overpass connecting Seonyudo Island with Jangjado Island. The 268m long, 67m high, and 3m wide suspension bridge is not accessible by car; you can only cross the bridge by foot. And only fishing boats can pass under the bridge. Constructed in 1986, it aimed to assist residents to come in and out of islands freely.  Jangjadaegyo Bridge, which is a symbol of Seonyudo Island along with Seonyudaegyo Bridge, is built with four steel pipe trusses. The steel pipe truss structure is assembled by welding or with bolts to assemble triangular materials posts. It is different from the Seonyudaegyo Bridge built of concrete.  Jangjadaegyo Bridge is the prime location to see the beautiful landscape of Seonyudo Island. If you look around slowly walking over the bridge, you can see the sea embracing the surrounding views along with the Eight Scenic Views of Seonyudo Island. You can also see Manjubong Peak, Jangjabong Peak, and Seonyubong Peak clearly. The sunrise from the Jangjadaegyo Bridge in the morning is so picturesque that you might think you are looking at an artwork. Enjoy Gunsan on the Jangjadaegyo Bridge and take memorable photos.

stories.title: Eunpa Recreation Area
stories.script: It's not easy to see forest in Gunsan, which is surrounded by plains and sea. But there is one place where you can enjoy green woods in Gunsan: the Eunpa Recreation Area. The road from downtown to the Eunpa Recreation Area located in Naun-dong is like a forest funnel, making you feel as if you are in a forest. Eunpa Recreation Area is a national tourist destination built on a vast land of about 2,314,000 m² with dense forest and Mije Reservoir, which is indicated on Daedongyeojido (“The Great Map of Korea”), a revered document developed by geographer Kim Jeong-ho.  Eupa Lake Park inside the recreation area is full of natural beauty. It was once a reservoir built for agriculture but was designated as a national tourist site in 1985. Cherry blossoms bloom in Spring, creating a breathtaking tunnel of pink flowers, and there is an outdoor stage, waterside stage, and lotus flower deck you can enjoy as well. Eunpa fable and love-themed Mulbit Bridge together with the Music Fountain in the shape of a petal add to the beauty of the park. There is the “Legend of Jungbau” in Eunpa Reservoir; on the Mulbit Bridge, the sculpture of Aegibau, Jungbau, and Gaebau from the legend stands in harmony. During the day, you can enjoy the beautiful scenery reflected by the lake on the bridge, which passes through Eunpa, meaning silvery moonlit waves. At night, you can enjoy the spectacular nightscape created by lights.  Next to the lake, there is a boat racing course, which is used for a rowing course for the National Sports Festival. 76,033 m²-wide Meeting Plaza with Chunghontap Tower built for independence patriots from Ok-gu, Gunsan forms a large forest with approximately 100 zelkovas.

stories.title: Gunsan Railroad Village
stories.script: Gyeongam-dong in Gunsan was in fact a sea in the past. During the Japanese colonial period, it was reclaimed by Japan to build textile factories. It was in 1944 when the railroad was completed to transport products and raw materials of a newsprint manufacturing company called Paper Korea located in Jochon-dong. The railroad connecting Gunsan Station and Paper Korea is 2.5km long and its official name is Paper Korea Line. After liberation, those who lost their home gathered in Gyeongam-dong and formed a village.  Buildings in the railroad village still have the traces of the 70s and 80s since they did not go through reconstruction. Trains crossed the village until 2008. The scene of train passing through the village was unique enough to draw attention from people. As the village fulfilled the necessary conditions to be a tourist destination, it began to change little by little. There used to be conflicts between the traditional village and contemporary stores. But as it was reborn into a “Memory Trail” under the theme of reminiscence, it successfully attracted visitors from all over the nation.  On the wall nearby the railroad, flowers and cargoes are painted to remember the past. It is actually fun to look at doors with various patterns. Since there is a costume rental store, why don't you rent an outfit from the 70s and make unforgettable memories with your family, friends and the loved ones?

stories.title: Gunsan Wolmyeong Park
stories.script: Wolmyeong Park is a popular tourist destination in Gunsa. It has five mountains — Wolmyeongsan, Janggyesan, Seollimsan, Jeombangsan, and Seokchisan Mountains — in its vicinity. The park has 12 kilometers of walking trails and the total size of the area is 2,545,454 m2. The path that goes up to the Wolmyeong Park is a thick forest; forsythia and cherry blossoms emit a sweet fragrance every spring. In addition, you view the downtown of Gunsan, the sea to the south of Gunsan, the mouth of the Geumgang River, and the large Janghang smelting factory.  At the top of the park, there is an observatory, sculpture park, Susi Tower, March First Independence Movement Monument, 35th Anniversary Monument of Port Opening, The Thinking Citizen, Chae Man-sik Literature Monument, and Beacon Fire Station at the top of the park. In the Sculpture Park, you can see many artistic sculptures related to the sea. Chae Man-sik, the author of the novel The Muddy Current is an iconic writer of Gunsan. At the Chae Man-sik Literature Monument, you can see a glimpse of his life story. Passing the monument, a wide west coast unfolds before your eyes at the Beacon Fire Station. The scene of the sun sinking behind the Gogunsan Islands elicits exclamation from visitors.  Once you reach the foot of the Seollimsan Mountain at the west side of the park, there is Eunjeoksa Temple. And the First Water Source, built by blocking the gap between Jeombangsan and Seollimsan Mountain, is located nearby. In 1912, the first water source built to provide drinking water to people has become a mountain lake, which also became a place where mountain birds and animals come to quench their thirst.  The park has well-arranged gardens and 30-year-old wisteria and cherry blossoms. A cherry blossom photo contest is held every April when the park is covered with cherry blossoms. There are three tourist courses: Course A (1.5km), Course B (3.7km), and Course C (3km). Depending on the course, it may take 1 to 2 hours.

stories.title: Namwon Seodo Station
stories.script: Did you know that the “Jemulpo Station” where Ae-shin in mourning dress was waiting for Dong-mae from the TV series Mr.Sunshine was actually the Seodo Station in Namwon?  Seodo Station, currently abandoned, is better known as the background of the novel Honbul (“The Ghost Fire”) by writer Choi Myeong-hee. The original Seodo Station was built in 1931 for Jeolla Line and was closed in 2008. It is currently used as a filming location for many films and dramas. Today it is widely referred to as the Old Seodo Station Set. The wooden building once used as a train station is the first thing you see. It is actually the oldest train station in Korea.  Passing the old wooden building, you can see the scene from Mr. Sunshine. This railway is where Dong-mae sat in the series. Take a look at Seodo Station from the railway and take a memorable picture of yourself.  Choi Myeong-hee, the writer of the novel Honbul, who made the station a popular tourist destination, spent her childhood in this village. Since it was a clan village where all of her family and relatives lived together, she said it was the most comfortable space for her to work on her writing.  Within 5 minutes of driving from the Seodo Station, there is Honbul Literary Museum. Hope you experience the neighborhood where Choi Myeong-hee lived and her literary world.  <This guide was recorded by Kwon Ah-hyun of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Buan Cinema Theme Park
stories.script: Buan Cinema Theme Park is a famous filming site for battle scenes against the backdrop of the Joseon Dynasty. You can easily recognize the place as the big fortress and gate are quite noticeable.  Once you get inside after paying a fee, pond, pavilion, and village from the Joseon Dynasty come into sight. Films such as The King and the Clown, The Throne, and Masquerade, and TV series such as Immortal Admiral Yi Sun-sin, The Emperor: Owner of the Mask, and Mr. Sunshine were filmed here. Because it reenacted the village and palace of the Joseon Dynasty, it often appears in historical movies and series of the Joseon Dynasty.  Passing through the towns, you can see a palace with a wide yard. It is so large that most of the fighting scenes by the gate to the palace were filmed here.  Don't be surprised as you would find all or part of walls ruined. This is because camera crews have to remove them to secure space for cameras, audio equipments, and lightings for a movie.  If you step on the fortress by the entrance on your way out from the filming site, you can see a panoramic view of the park. Looking down the village, imagine how real villages back then would have looked like!  <This guide was recorded by Kwon Ah-hyun of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Gochang and Buan Tidal Flats (2010)
stories.script: Gochang and Buan Tidal Flats, designated as the Ramsar Wetlands, is located within Gomsoman Bay and Byeonsanbando, or Byeonsan Peninsula. “Man” is a Korean word referring to a broad inlet of the sea where the land curves inward. In English, it means a bay. In this sense, Gomsoman means a bay called “Gomso.”  There are two origins for Gomso. One is that the name of the Island on the Bay is “Gom Island” and another is that salt was referred to as “Gomso” in the past. In Chinese characters, the place was written as Ungyeon (ung, meaning bear in English; yeon, meaning water in English).  Then why was it called the peninsula? As Hanbando means the Korean Peninsula, the term Bando sounds quite familiar. Bando originates from the Chinese characters meaning peninsula, which refers to a land of which the three sides are surrounded by the sea and one side is connected to the mainland. The west coast of Korea is famous for its complicated shoreline and many peninsulas are developed in this region. Among all, Buan is called the Byeonsan Peninsula, which was a filming site for the movie Byeonsan and the TV series Lovers in Prague.  The name Byeonsanbando first appeared in the Baekje Period. In the Samguk Yusa (“Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms”), the following phrase was written: “It was called Byeonhan because another place is already called as ‘Byeonsan’ in the land of Baekje.” By looking at history, we can see that the name “Byeonsan” was used way before the Three Hans (Mahan, Byeonhan, and Jinhan) period.  Tidal flats in Gochang and Buan are the least developed, which are closest to a natural mudflat. There are still plentiful resources and biodiversity in these tidal flats. It has long been famous for salt and jeotgal, or salted seafood. Gomso Salt Farm and Gomso Jeotgal are well-known local specialties across the nation. During the kimchi-making season, people are literally rushing here to buy its local salt and jeotgal.  The landscape of the Byeonsan Peninsula is another thing to notice. Famous sea cliffs such as the Chaeseokgang and Jeokbyeokgang Cliffs along with a tidal flat are a pride of Buan. In particular, people visit here to see a sunset, which creates a breathtaking view of the sun falling into the sea and land, so make sure to come here on time for the sundown.  <This guide was recorded by Kwon So-hyun of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Ungok Ramsar Wetland (2011)
stories.script: Gochang is famous for dolmens, which was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Jeon Bong-jun, dubbed as the General Mung Bean. Within a 30-minute distance from the Dolmen Site, there is Ungok Ramsar Wetland.  This wetland is rather new.  In 1981, a reservoir was built in Ungok Village to provide coolant to the Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant. Residents were relocated to another area and the surrounding was put up with barbed wire.  As the access of people was limited, and water permeates behind the reservoir, the wetland was naturally created. The plants began to grow and it has become home to endangered migratory birds. As time passed by, the species living here became more diverse and it became a wild wetland where yellow-throated martens, leopard cats, and Korean ratsnakes were observed.  The park and playground to help you understand the wetland better is a good place to visit. However, if you want to experience a real wild wetland, it is recommended to take the trekking course from Ungok Ramsar Wetland to Gochang Dolmen Site. The path is well-arranged with wooden deck. You can observe migratory birds at observatory decks and habitat of wetland plants at a place once lived by humans.  Since it is an easy trekking course, anyone can feel the vibe of a wild wetland by taking a light walk. If you get too close to the wetland, you may sink in or pose a threat to animals, so observing them at a designated location using a telescope or camera is recommended.  <This guide was recorded by Kwon So-hyun of Korea Tourism Organization through talent donation.>

stories.title: Dalgusan Mountain
stories.script: An old woman who turned into a stone at Dalgusan Mountain  There is a sharp mountain rising to the left of the entrance to a tea house on the main road from Namhae-eup. A very long time ago, there lived an old couple on the foot of the mountain. The old man was a bad-tempered, greedy man who did not know how to be sorry for what he had done. The old woman, however, was warm-hearted and always kind.  One day outside the gate, a monk knocked on the door while chanting Buddhist prayers for alms. There was no way that the greedy old man would open the door. Instead of giving alms, he replied that there was no owner inside. However, the monk was no ordinary monk. “I can't pass by a wealthy family like this without receiving alms. Save us, merciful Buddha, Bodhisattva of compassion. Save us, merciful Buddha.” The monk kept chanting Buddhist scriptures and asking for alms. Then the old men yelled at him to go away that he had nothing to give.  The monk did not give up. He kept chanting and waited for alms. The old man couldn’t help it, so he donated a sack full of something. However, the sack was filled with cow dungs from the stable. Having finished chanting, the monk calmly accepted the sack, thanked the man, and quietly departed.  The old woman's heart broke seeing all what happened. Then, without her husband's knowledge, she took out grain, followed the monk and donated it to him.  “I am deeply sorry, sir. My husband has a bad temper, so please do not be too upset. Please take this and leave with a good heart.”  Feeling grateful for her sincerity, the monk said in a quiet voice and disappeared. “You will have water coming out of your yard in a few days. Without telling anyone, save yourself at the mountain behind your house. You must not look back while climbing the mountain. Something bad will happen if you talk to anyone or look back.”  Indeed, water gushed out in the middle of the yard a few days later. The old woman panicked and hurriedly ran up the mountain behind the house. As she climbed the mountain, she reached a rock shaped like a chicken and caught her breath. She would often climb up to the rock since she liked chickens.  Unaware of what she was doing, she looked back to see what had happened to her house. After shouting “ugh,” she suddenly turned into a rock. The greedy old man vanished as if the water had washed him away.  After that, people called it Daksan Mountain, meaning the chicken mountain, because the old woman turned into a stone in front of the chicken-shaped rock that she liked. As time passed by, it was named Dalgusan Mountain.

stories.title: Sangsabawi Rock
stories.script: The lovers who turned into serpents and the Sangsabawi Rock  Rocks in Korea are the subject of many legends. In Namhae-gun, there is Sangsangbawi Rock located at the entrance of the hiking trail on the Geumyang side of Geumsan Mountain holding two stories about serpent. It must be because it is the largest and most impressive rock in Geumsan Mountain.  There was a rich man living in a village in Namhae, Gyeongsangnam-do. He had a lot of money and many servants, but he had only one daughter. He raised his daughter with great care. She grew up to become a beautiful woman. She was very popular not only among men in her neighborhood, but in her neighboring villages. Many bachelors snooped around the walls of the rich man's house just to catch a glimpse of the woman.  As for Dolsoe, the servant of the house, he was no different. He loved her so much, but his low social status prevented him from expressing his love or getting close to her. With time, Dolsoe became lovesick, couldn't eat anything and withered away.  A few days after Dolsoe's death, Dolsoe's spirit, which wandered around, turned into a serpent. In the middle of one night, he went into the room where the woman was sleeping and wrapped his body around her. The rich man who saw it the next morning was terrified. He tried his best to get the serpent off his daughter, but it wouldn't budge. He even called a shaman to perform an exorcism, but it didn't work. As the day passed and came the next morning, an old man with a long beard came to the rich man and said,  “If you take your daughter and the serpent to a high cliff on Geumsan Mountain and perform an exorcism, you will avoid disaster.”  After the old man disappeared, the rich man took his daughter to the top of the highest cliff on the mountain. As the exorcism reached its climax, the snake's body began to unravel around the daughter. After it was all unwrapped, it fell down a cliff and died. After that, the villagers called the cliff Sangsabawi Rock, meaning that the lovesick heart was resolved there.  There is also a serpent in the second story about Sangsabawi Rock. A young man from the Shilla Dynasty visited a hermitage in Geumsan Mountain to practice asceticism. He loved a woman in his hometown, but he put her out of his mind and devoted himself to the asceticism. She eagerly awaited the young man's return. After several years, there was no news that he would come back, and eventually she got sick of longing. She eventually fell ill with love-sickness and died, having suffering for long days.  The soul of the dead woman turned into a serpent and came to the hermitage in Geumsan Mountain to find the man she waited for.
