Despite establishing the school with his entire fortune, Yi refused to take a high position in the school, choosing instead to be a teacher.  When you are in the area, check out the Exhibition Hall next to the house. This is the first public museum in Seocheon, home to an exhibition dedicated to Yi Ha-bok, special exhibition hall, and VR experiences. The collection includes 1,500 items, including the Korean flag, Taegeukgi, hailing from the 1940s and 1950s. So drop by and trace the humility of Yi Ha-bok in the Yi Ha-bok's Historic House.

stories.title: Seocheon-gun Bird Eco Exhibition Hall
stories.script: Seocheon-gun’s Bird Eco Exhibition Hall opened its doors once again in 2023 after renovations. The exhibition hall preserves the ecosystem of the Geum River Estuary, Korea's largest migratory bird sanctuary, and offers a variety of hands-on education programs.  The exhibition hall is made up of four floors. The first floor, COEX-topia, is the place where experience and educational programs like wooden bird brooch-making, marine life pencil holder-making, and folk painting picture frame coloring are offered.   Bird Philia on the second floor offers a vivid look at Seocheon's natural environment and bird life through dioramas, panoramic videos, and taxidermy exhibits of migratory birds. The third floor, Enjoy U-topia, is a fun ecology experience and playground that brings bird ecology alive for children. It has a photo area with Kkami the Eurasian oystercatcher and Ttoyo the spoon-billed sandpiper, a VR experience center, and a 4D experience center.   The 4th floor’s Eco Observatory is a place where you can get a view of the Geumgangho Lake and Geum River Estuary. In winter, you can see migratory birds like Baikal teals, mallards, Northern pintails, tundra bean geese, and greater white-fronted geese.  Seocheon-gun Bird Eco Exhibition Hall also offers a variety of outdoor experience programs, such as a program where you can experience the tidal flats where sandpiper and plovers live and do some bird-watching for yourself. So get to know the migratory birds and find some interesting experiences in the Bird Eco Exhibition Hall.

stories.title: Hongwon Port
stories.script: Hongwon Port is a small port located below the Chunjangdae Beach. The port sits on the northwestern beach, which juts out toward the sea like a small peninsula. Across the port to the south lies Maryang Port.  A 40m-high hill touches the beach to the west of the port, and when seen from the lighthouse, the view of the sun going down beyond the hill is absolutely beautiful. There’s plenty of other things to do in Hongwon Port, though. You can watch the fishing boats moving between the red and white lighthouses, and fishers casting their rods on the embankment.  You can even climb onto seaside rocks or the quay to enjoy some fishing in Hongwon Port, or opt to take a fishing boat to the sea and try your hand in catching black sea bream, Korean rockfish, spotty-bellied greenling, webfoot octopus, and cuttlefish.   Every early fall, Hongwon Port hosts the Jeoneo & Crab Festival. Along with Gwangyang Port, Hongwon Port is the place that the largest amount of jeoneo, or gizzard shad, are caught in Korea. The festival features hand-catching gizzard shad, gizzard shad cooking contest, and plenty of things to eat. In fact, you can get good food in many of the shops and restaurants that handle seafood near the port. Drop by this small, yet charming port to make fond memories.

stories.title: Five-story Stone Pagoda in Seongbuk-ri, Seocheon
stories.audioTitle: Five-story Stone Pagoda in Seongbuk-ri, Seocheon
stories.script: The Five-story Stone Pagoda in Seongbuk-ri, Seocheon is Treasure No. 224 of Korea, from Goryeo Period. Just like other stone pagodas discovered in the former territory of Baekje, it follows the format established by the Five-story Stone Pagoda at Jeongnimsa Temple Site. But it is said to have a much larger roof stone than the base, and the upper tier stones are said to shrink excessively in size, which create imbalances in its form. Nevertheless, it remains as a highly valuable historical reference for the path of transmission for Baekje-style stone pagodas.  In 2007, Seocheon County undertook an excavation of the areas surrounding the Five-story Stone Pagoda in Seongbuk-ri. Generally speaking, such pagodas are built near temples, so the goal of this excavation effort was to confirm whether there was a temple site in this area. Indeed, a temple site was found in the area near the stone pagoda.  The survey revealed that there were foundations for pillars laid to the west and southwest of the stone pagoda, and stone piles used as foundations for wall or buildings. The area west of the stone pagoda revealed flags and sculptures bearing herringbone patterns, as well as celadon fragments printed with patterns. These findings put the estimated date of the temple’s construction as mid-11th Century to mid-12th Century.

stories.title: Culture Factory
stories.script: Did you know that Cheongju Culture Factory used to be a tobacco factory? From 1946 to 1999, the building was used as a tobacco factory where some 3,000 workers produced upwards of 10 billion cigarettes a year. These were exported to 17 countries, contributing to the growth of the modern Korean economy. When the tobacco factory closed, the building was left abandoned for a long time, until it was given new life as a cultural space. Although it still retains the appearance of a factory, the smoke in the air has been replaced with culture and the arts. Performances, exhibitions, events and seminars related to arts and culture take place all year round in this factory of culture for the city of Cheongju. It houses the Chungbuk Community Media Center, a shop for craft products, an open library and performance hall. Cheongju Culture Factory is also the stage of the Cheongju Craft Biennale. Cheongju Craft Biennale began in 1999 as a culture and arts festival for traditional and modern crafts to showcase the 5,000 years old tradition of Korean crafts to the world.  As a formerly abandoned space transformed into a place for culture and the arts, Cheongju Culture Factory is also compared to world famous art museums such as the Tate Modern converted from a power plant, and Musée d’Orsay which was once a train station.

stories.title: Korean Craft Museum
stories.script: The Korean Craft Museum is a public museum dedicated to crafts located in Cheongju, the host city of the Craft Biennale. As Korea’s only art museum dedicated to crafts, it has been promoting crafts to the public and opening new horizons in the world of crafts. It was established in 2001 and is currently located in the main building of Cheongju Culture Factory.  The Korean Craft Museum not only hosts exhibitions of outstanding works of craft in various genres, but also runs a craft academy and craft classes for the general public. The museum shop in the first floor sells items such as teaware, vases and wallets made by local craftspeople.

stories.title: Dongbu Changko
stories.script: Dongbu Changko consists of the seven buildings currently remaining of the old Cheongju Tobacco Factory’s tobacco leaf storage facility. The buildings have retained their original features as factory warehouses built in the 1960s, with red brick walls and wooden trusses which make them valuable modern cultural heritage.  The bigger significance of Dongbu Changko lies in its rebirth from abandoned warehouse to an art playground for the people of Cheongju. After 8 years of renovation, the 7 buildings of Dongbu Changko have been reopened as public culture spaces and art education facilities, each preserving its unique charm. They currently house the Community Platform, performing arts practice rooms, the Community Cultural Center, an event hall, a cafe, the Dream Arts Center, and the Creative Arts Education Space.

stories.title: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
stories.audioTitle: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
stories.script: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art is a public art museum established to collect, preserve, and exhibit contemporary art, as well as conduct research and promote international exchange and art creation. The main museum is located in Makgye-dong, Gwacheon-si, Gyeonggi-do, with the Seoul branch in Sogye-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul, and Deoksugung branch in Deoksugung Palace. The Cheongju branch was opened in 2018 as its first branch outside of the Seoul metropolitan area. The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Cheongju was built in the annex to the main building of the Korea Tobacco and Ginseng Corporation’s former Cheongju Tobacco Factory. This place where cigarettes were once produced and stored has been renovated and transformed into a cultural hub. The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Cheongju is a museum specializing in the storage and restoration of Korean art. It’s even home to Korea’s first open storage, allowing visitors to see the museum's main collection and how it is preserved through the windows. It also has Korea’s only conservation science lab, preserving and systematically managing the 8,700 pieces in its collection. It also operates various programs such as exhibitions and classes.

stories.title: Cheongju University
stories.script: “For independence, we need to build strength. This strength comes from learning.”  At the height of the exploitation and oppression of Japanese colonial rule in 1924, the brothers Kim Youngwon and Kim Wongeun held up the torch of education. Donating everything they had, they established the Daeseong Primary School, and then Cheongju University in 1946. Cheongju University was the first private university to be established south of the Han River. Its spacious campus at the foot of Uamsan Mountain boasts beautiful sights all year round. It’s more than just a place of learning for the community, being a regional landmark with attractions such as the school museum. Many movies and drama series were also filmed on this historical campus.

stories.title: Daeseong High School
stories.script: Daesung High School, which neighbors Cheongju University, has its roots in Daeseong Primary School founded in 1935. It operated as a commercial high school for many decades, then was renamed Daeseong High School. On its grounds is a red Japanese colonial era building which was formerly a classroom, and is now a memorial hall registered as modern cultural heritage. The school has produced many notable figures including Han Un-sa, Korea’s first radio playwright who wrote The Red Scarf, Captain Ko Sang-don, the first Korean to climb Mount Everest, and football legends Choi Soon-ho and Lee Woon-jae.

stories.title: Cheongju Agriculture High School
stories.script: Cheongju Agriculture High School was established in June 1911 as an institution to produce skilled farmers. However, students also served the country and society with patriotic spirit, taking the lead in anti-Japanese national movements such as the March 1st Movement. The school consists of several large and small buildings for practical training and coursework, spanning an area of 550,000 square meters. It also has a beautiful garden which houses the Centennial Memorial Hall and Baekchu Park. It trains skilled professionals in a wide range of fields including agriculture, sericulture and forestry in Chungcheongbuk-do, as well as livestock, agricultural machinery, horticulture, agricultural distribution, food processing, and bio-beauty.

stories.title: Naedeok-dong Cathedral
stories.script: A cathedral is the throne on which a bishop sits, symbolizing the duty and authority of the position. Naedeok-dong Cathedral, located in Cheongwon-gu, Cheongju-si, is the cathedral of the Catholic Diocese of Cheongju, where the bishop resides and holds mass services. Construction on the building which combines Eastern and Western architectural styles began in August 1960 and was completed in November 1961. The church was upgraded to a cathedral in March 1962. While most cathedrals have bell towers in the center of the building, this one has the bell tower on the side, influenced by the Maryknoll Catholic Foreign Mission Society. The sounding of the bells in this beautiful cathedral has a calming power over the distracted mind.

stories.title: Cheongju Hyanggyo
stories.script: A hyanggyo was an official educational institution established to educate students on Confucian etiquette and scriptures, as well as serve as a ceremonial site where the ancestral tablets were housed and memorial rites for Confucian scholars were held. Cheongju Hyanggyo, Tangible Cultural Property of Chungcheongbuk-do No. 39, was founded during the reign of King Taejo of the Joseon Dynasty. King Sejong bestowed books to the hyanggyo in 1444, and King Sejo visited to worship at its Confucian shrine in 1464. Passing through Hongsalmun Gate, the name meaning to defeat bad luck, and the stairs where ancestral spirits are said to enter, you will find Myeongnyundang Hall and Daeseongjeon Hall. A Seokjeonje ritual is held in Daesungjeon Hall each spring and autumn.

stories.title: Chungbuk Cultural Center
stories.script: In 1937, when the Chungbuk Provincial Office was relocated from Jungang Park to its current location, the governor's official residence was established near the provincial office in 1939. The building was built in Western style in the front and Japanese style in the back, differentiating its public and private spaces. It was used as the governor's official residence for a long time, and then opened to Chungbuk residents in September 2012 as a new cultural space.  Now, the House of Culture, a book cafe, the Forest Gallery, and an outdoor concert hall are operated under the Chungbuk Cultural Center. The floral landscaping alongside the unique building creates a welcoming atmosphere. The site has been designated as National Registered Cultural Heritage No. 353.

stories.title: Woo-ri Art Institute
stories.script: The building of Woo-ri Art Institute was built in 1924 as company housing for the Chungbuk Financial Association and was later used as the Cheongju YMCA building from 1954. It was famous at the time for its tin roof with sharp edges constructed at a 45-degree-angle. Being a hip-roofed house with roof tiles from all four sides converging at the top of the roof, it has a unique bungalow-style exterior which is rarely seen in Japanese houses in the era.  It was once selected as Cheongju’s most beautiful house, and also used as a kindergarten. Currently, it is an art institute where musicians learn to play the marimba. The site has been designated as National Registered Cultural Heritage No. 9.

stories.title: Garamsinjak
stories.script: Garamsinjak is a multi-purpose cultural space located to the left of the back gate of Chungbuk Provincial Office. The building used to be a restaurant named Garam Hanjeongsik, which the Chungbuk Cultural Foundation purchased and transformed into a cultural space.  Garamsinjak is a space where cultural products are exhibited, loaned and enjoyed through exhibitions, performances, and talk shows. “Sinjak” in Garamsinjak means everything new and the space was created to develop new cultural programs for the community. It is open to everyone, from content creators to members of the public.

stories.title: Chungbuk Provincial Office Main Building & Former Chungbuk Industrial Promotion Center
stories.audioTitle: Chungbuk Provincial Office Main Building & Former Chungbuk Industrial Promotion Center
stories.script: The main building of the Chungbuk Provincial Office was built in April 1937 with two stories, and then expanded to three stories in 1959. The building has been constructed symmetrically around the main entrance, and finished with brown scratch tiles popular at the time. It still houses the office of the governor and plays a central role in the administration of Chungcheongbuk-do to this day. The site has been designated as National Registered Cultural Heritage No. 55. Right opposite the Chungbuk Provincial Office building is the Chungbuk Industrial Promotion Center, designated National Registered Cultural Heritage No. 352. It was built in 1936 and used as a promotion and exhibition space for businessmen in Chungcheongbuk-do Province. The entire facade has been geometrically designed using modernist architectural techniques.

stories.title: Anglican Church
stories.script: The Anglican Church of Cheongju has its roots in British missionary priest George Hewlett’s house church in Daeseong-dong. The current Anglican Church building was built in 1935 by Bishop Cecile Cooper, and has been well-maintained over its ninety years of history. The paljak roof, Korean roof tiles, and rafters from traditional Korean hanok architecture, have been incorporated into the Western basilica structure, harmonizing architectural elements from the East and West. Walk up a small flight of stairs at the main gate to reach “Anna’s Garden”, a small sanctuary for rest and contemplation. The site has been designated Tangible Cultural Property of Chungcheongbuk-do No. 149.

stories.title: East Reservoir
stories.script: The Water Quality Control Facility at the East Reservoir is a bell tower-type concrete structure built to monitor water quality. It is topped with a hexagonal dome measuring 16.24㎡ wide and 3.5m tall. Each corner has a protruding prism-shaped pillar, and the eaves are finished with stringcourse. The top of the dome is decorated with a pointed spire-shaped structure. Completed in April 1923, the structure reflects the characteristics of Korea's water supply facilities of the era. The floor plan which has been preserved to date shows that the East Reservoir consisted of four drainage tanks and one building. The building is now a landmark for visitors to Dangsan Park.

stories.title: Jeil Church
stories.script: Jeil Church is Cheongju's first church, first established as Cheongju-eup Church in 1904. It not only spread the gospel, but also acted as the bastion of modernization, championing activism for independence, enlightenment, social and cultural development and women's rights.  The church also founded Cheongnam School, Cheongju's first modern education institution. It played a key role in the education of the community over the course of its history, with the establishment of Cheongsin Girls' School in 1909, Sangdang Kindergarten in 1926, the Cheongju YMCA in 1945, Segwang Middle School in 1949, and Segwang High School in 1953. During the Japanese colonial era, the Japanese government tried to demolish Mangseonnu Pavilion, a wooden building from the Goryeo Dynasty. Jeil Church led a campaign to save the pavillion, reconstructing it in its grounds. The church building, constructed in October 1939 as a central spire-type Gothic brick building and expanded in 1950, is also noted for its significance to modern Korean architecture.

stories.title: Western Halls of Tap-dong
stories.script: The Western Halls of Tap-dong, located in the vicinity of Ilshin Girls' High School, were built in 1904 as housing for missionaries by Pastor F.S. Miller. The land was purchased in 1904, and the houses were built slowly over time, with two buildings completed in 1906, three from 1911 to 1913, and one in 1932. The walls are built according to Western construction standards, but the roof is a Korean hapgak-style. The introduction of fireplaces, steam boilers, flush toilets, and other hardware used in indoor spaces not found in traditional wooden houses document the process by which modern architecture was adopted in Korea, making these buildings modern heritage sites. They have been designated Tangible Cultural Property of Chungcheongbuk-do No. 133.

stories.title: Five-Storied Pagoda of Tap-dong
stories.script: The name Tap-dong comes from this ancient stone pagoda. The original stone pagoda is thought to have been five stories tall with a two-tiered base, with a height of at least 6 meters. However, the lower tier of of the base is now missing, and just three stories of the body remain, making the entire structure about 3.26 meters tall. It is estimated to be from the Unified Silla Period from the 9th to the early 10th century, based on the Buddhist bas-relief on the first story, the five-tier support of the roof stone, and the style of the stylobate. It is the only stone pagoda from the Unified Silla Period in Cheongju, and has been designated Tangible Cultural Property of Chungcheongbuk-do No. 25.

stories.title: Suamgol Village
stories.script: Suamgol Village is the intersection between Su-song and Uam-dong in Sangdang-gu, Cheongju. Formed by refugees in the Korean War, the village has been home to people of humble backgrounds familiar with hardship.  However, when local artists started painting its walls, Suamgol transformed into an attractive destination. Its steps and walls filled up with stories from its residents, bringing light into this old and overlooked corner of the city. Hit drama series such as ‘Bread, Love and Dreams’, ‘Cain and Abel ’, ‘Glory Jane’ were filmed here, and the crowds followed. Many cafes and restaurants have since opened in the neighborhood, and young people now know Suamgol as the cafe street.

stories.title: Suamgol Observatory
stories.script: Suamgol Observatory is the best spot to get a bird’s eye view of Cheongju. Come at night to see the city lights shine brilliantly in the darkness. The observatory is spacious with heart-shaped structures to frame the perfect shot. Its location on the Uamsan Mountain Ring Road makes it an ideal stop on a scenic drive through the cherry blossoms in spring or colorful leaves in autumn. It is also a great spot to include in a walking tour of Suamgol Village.

stories.title: Uamsan Mountain
stories.script: This mountain in Cheongju offers scenic beauty all year round. Being close to the city and just 353 meters above sea level, it is an accessible climb for all. One always feels welcome on Uamsan Mountain’s gentle trails. Its old name is Wausan, given for its form resembling a cow laying on the ground. Near the peak, one can find traces of the ancient Wausanseong Fortress dating back to the three kingdoms era. There are multiple trails up the mountain starting from all directions and the Uamsan Circumference Hiking Trail. Uamsan is also home to the flying squirrel, natural monument of Korea no. 328.

stories.title: Pyochungsa Shrine
stories.script: The Musin Rebellion of 1728, in the 4th year of the reign of King Yeongjo, was an uprising led by Yi In-jwa and Jeong Hee-ryang of the Soron faction to drive out King Yeongjo and establish Tan of Milpung-gun as king. The rebels hid weapons in biers and entered the gates Cheongju to launch a surprise attack on the barracks. The rebellion cost the lives of many soldiers and military officials Lee Bongsang, Hong Lim and Nam Yeonnyeon. Pyochungsa Shrine was built to honor these three loyalists who laid down their lives to protect Cheongju. It was originally built near the North Gate of Cheongju Eupseong Fortress, but was moved to the current location in 1939 due to an expansion of the urban center. To the east of the shrine is a memorial stone for the three loyalists erected in 1731. It has been designated Monument of Chungcheongbuk-do Province No. 17.

stories.title: Samil Park
stories.script: Samil Park was opened in August 1980 to honor patriotic martyrs who worked to regain the nation’s independence. In the park were erected statues of 6 patriots from Chungcheongbuk-do Province among the 33 leaders of the March 1st movement- Son Byunghee, Gwon dongjin, Gwon Byungdeok, Shin Hongshik, Shin Seokgu, and Jeong Chunsu. However, Jeong Chunsu was later discovered to have collaborated with the Japanese and his statue was taken down by members of the public in 1990, leaving just its base.  The park was refurbished in 2010 to its current form.

stories.title: Kim Soohyun Drama Art Hall
stories.script: “I believe that life consists of the choices we make at every moment. As a writer, I try to look into how people live their given lives as individual human beings.” This is a quote from screenwriter Kim Soohyun. Hailing from Cheongju, Kim Soohyun is a legendary writer who penned numerous hit series such as Trap of Youth, Love and Ambition, Love and Truth, and Men of the Bathhouse. Kim Soohyun Drama Art Hall is a gallery showcasing a collection of the writers scripts, published collections, photographs and videos. It presents an overview of the life’s work of a writer whose legacy will remain in the history of Korean dramas.

stories.title: Yukgeori Traditional Market
stories.script: This is Cheongju's most famous traditional market formed in the 1950s, considered one of the top five traditional markets in Korea. With fresh agricultural and marine products, fashion items, and a sumptuous spread of food, the market is full of life all year round. The sellers are usually happy to throw in extras for a sweet-talking customer. The street is covered by a shelter that stretches over one kilometer, protecting visitors from rain and snow. Yukgeori market is full of things to see, eat and buy, a place for shopping with the human touch.

stories.title: Seomun Traditional Market Sampgyeopsal Street
stories.script: Cheongju-style pork belly, marinated in a special soy sauce and grilled golden brown, then eaten with spicy, sweet and sour scallion salad, has become a nationwide hit. Samgyeopsal Street in Seomun Market was created to promote this delicious pork belly dish. The street is lined with small samgyeopsal restaurants, each with its own unique take on the recipe.  The street also holds a Samgyeopsal Festival each year on March 3rd, with tasting events and discounts at restaurants.

stories.title: Jungang-dong Car-free Street
stories.script: A stretch of Jungang-ro street from the former Suasa yarn shop to Cheongju City Hall has been designated a car-free street. The street is also called Pine Tree Street for the pine trees that line both sides. The formerly quiet area has become the meeting spot for young people, with the introduction of a Youth Square, unique dessert cafes and restaurnts, and cultural spaces. Performances, exhibitions, and interesting events are held here all year round. There is also an artist’s market where visitors can buy unique handicrafts.

stories.title: Hanbok and Wedding Street
stories.script: The Namju-dong market area became famous for shops selling furnishings for newlyweds shortly after the Korean War, and has been transformed into a Hanbok and Wedding Street after urban regeneration. It is now a shopping street specializing in weddings. There are about 30 hanbok shops in a 200 meter stretch along the main road south of Jungang Park, together with shops for wedding dresses, traditional wedding food, wedding gifts, and photo studios. The street is popular not only among couples preparing for weddings, but also young people who appreciate the beauty of hanbok.

stories.title: Former Cheongju Station Building Park and Urban Regeneration Hub Center
stories.audioTitle: Former Cheongju Station Building Park and Urban Regeneration Hub Center
stories.script: Cheongju Station opened in 1921 and operated for 47 years in before moving to its current location in Jeongbong-dong. On January 7th 2019, a park was opened on the site of the former Cheongju Station Building. The old station has been recreated faithfully with even a short track. There is also a museum where visitors can undertand the history of the station through dioramas, artifacts, digital photos and a recreated platform. It is located near the Pine Tree Street next to the Urban Regeneration Hub Center.

stories.title: Cafe Mokgan (Hakcheontang)
stories.script: Hakcheontang was a famous public bathhouse in Cheongju designed by leading Korean architect Kim Soo-geun. After it closed, the building was transformed into a themed cafe where visitors can relive the nostalgia of the old bathhouse. Parts of the bathhouse have been ingeniously preserved to create a unique experience. Drink coffee while sitting in an empty bath or a row of showers, and eat the boiled egg that comes with every drink to soak up the bathhouse cafe atmosphere.

stories.title: Cheongju Eupseong Walled City
stories.script: The history of Cheongju-eupseong dates back to the establishment of Seowon Sogyeong in the 5th year of King Sinmun of Silla. After unifying the three kingdoms, Silla reorganized the administrative structure of the country, and established Bukwonsogyeong in Wonju, Geumgwansogyeong in Gimhae, Jungwonsogyeong in Chungju, and Seowonsogyeong in Cheongju. Subsequently, a large-scale civil engineering project was carried out to establish a system of cities. Thus, Seowon Gyeongseong, or Cheongju Eupseong, was built in the 9th year of King Sinmun. Cheongju Eupseong played a central role in the history of Korea, in education, culture, and trade. The area where the old city once stood is now called Seongan-gil. The walls of Cheongju Eupseong were 4 meters high and 1,640 meters long. The town was rectangular in shape, longer in the north-south direction, with four gates in the north, south, east and west.  Unfortunately, Cheongju Eupseong was demolished without a trace under Japanese colonial rule in the guise of “urban reform”, and its stones were used to build a sewer. Perhaps due to its history as the site of Korea’s major victory on land in the Imjin War, the Japanese colonial government demolished Cheongju Eupseong before any other town wall in the country.

stories.title: Iron Flagpole at Yongdusa Temple Site
stories.audioTitle: Iron Flagpole at Yongdusa Temple Site
stories.script: This iron flagpole is Korea’s National Treasure No. 41, erected in 962, the 3rd year of King Gwangjong of Goryeo. There was a plague circulating in Cheongju at the time, which was blamed on the shape of Cheongju resembling a sailing ship without a mast. Thus the flagpole was erected to act as a mast. Unused tools and wartime weapons were collected from households around the city to build a pole 18 meters high, topped with a dragon’s head. The dragon’s head has since been lost along with 10 tiers in the stylobate, reducing the pole’s height to 13 meters. Nevertheless, the flagpole is still an impressive presence.  About 60 flagpole sites dating to the Unified Silla and Goryeo periods have been found, but only the supporting pillars remain in most of these sites. The iron flagpole at the Yongdusa Temple Site in Cheongju is the only Goryeo-era flagpole site with the original pole.

stories.title: Cheongnyeonggak
stories.script: Cheongju Dongheon is a Joseon-era government building located behind the former Cheongwon-gun Office and the current temporary building of Cheongju City Hall. It was established in 1731, the 7th year of King Yeongjo, by Lee Byeong-jeong, the prefectural governor of Seowon, under the name of Geunminheon. It was renovated twice, once in the 25th year of King Sunjo and once in the 5th year of King Gojong. The building was renamed Cheongnyeonggak in the second renovation.  The building has 28 sections, 7 in the front and 4 in the side. It was where all matters of local administration were handled. Next to it was Gangseonru Pavilion, which served as a guest house for visiting officials and a banquet hall, but it was demolished under the Japanese policy to erase Korean culture.

stories.title: Namseokgyo Bridge
stories.script: Namseokgyo Bridge was the oldest stone bridge in Korea, built in the year that Hyeokgeose of Silla ascended the throne. It was 64 meters long and 4 meters wide.  In 1723, there was a big flood in the Cheongju area. Before then, Musimcheon Stream was close to the current Yukgeori Market and Seongan-gil, but the water was diverted away from Namseokgyo Bridge due to flooding. Namseokgyo Bridge was no longer on the waterway and the ground rose gradually below it. In 1932, it was completely buried underground. It is currently buried underground on the main road from Seongan-gil to the Yukgeori traditional market, and can only be seen in old photographs.

stories.title: Mangseonnu Pavilion
stories.script: Mangseonnu Pavilion is a Goryeo-era wooden building used as an annext to the Cheongjumok government office. It was also called Chwigyeongnu for the breathtaking view of the entire town it gave.  In the 10th year of King Gongmin, the capital fell to the Red Turban Rebellion, and the king fled to Cheongju Eupseong. He continued ruling from Cheongju and even presided over a court examination during the war. Mangseonnu Pavilion was demolished for a road expansion project under Japanese rule, but was reconstructed next to Cheongju Jeil Church through a fundraising campaign by the Jeil Church Youth Association. The young people of Jeil Church opened a night school in Mangseonnu, studying the Korean language through old books when the Japanese government banned reading and writing in Korean.  The Pavilion was later moved to Cheongju Jungang Park where it currently stands.

stories.title: Apgaksu Tree
stories.script: This ancient ginkgo tree has stood in its place in Jungang Park for over a thousand years, and has been designated Monument of Chungcheongbuk-do Province No. 5. It was named apgaksu, meaning “duck foot tree”, for the shape of its leaves and trunk that resemble duck flippers.  The tree also comes with an interesting legend. In the second year of King Gongyang of Goryeo, many scholars and politicians, including Yi Saek, Kwon Geun, Yi rim, Byun An-ryeol, Yi In-min, Jeong Ji, Yi Soong-in, Yi Jong-hak, and Yi Gwi-saeng, were accused of opposing Yi Seong-gye and imprisoned in Cheongju prison. Then one day, a sudden thunderstorm caused the flooding of Musimcheon Stream and water rushed into Cheongju Eupseong. The entire town and all its buildings filled with water. The prison guards fled to the trees, and the prisoners also escaped and climbed up the apgaksu tree. When this was reported to the court, the flood was deemed a sign from heaven proving their innocence and the prisoners were pardoned.

stories.title: Jungang Park
stories.script: Seowon Sogyeong was established in March of the 5th year of King Sinmun of Unified Silla, and the walls of Cheongju Eupseong were built in the 9th year of King Sinmun. During the Goryeo Dynasty, the site of Jungang Park was the center of Cheongju Eupseong. In 1651, the second year of King Hyojong of Joseon, the Chungcheong barracks were moved from Haemi, Chungcheongnam-do to the location of Jungang Park in Cheongju. The grounds were occupied by the provincial government office in 1908, which became a park when the government moved to a new building in 1937.  In addition to the Cheongju Cultural Center, Jungang Park is home to several monuments such as Apgaksu, Mangseonnu Pavillion, the main entrance to the Provincial military headquarters in Cheongju and monument honoring the victory of Jo Heon, Tangible Cultural Property of Chungcheongbuk-do Province No. 15 and 136 respectively, making it the most important heritage site in Cheongju.

stories.title: Cheongju Early Printing Museum
stories.script: This is Korea’s only museum dedicated to early printing technology, established in 1992 at the site of Heungdeoksa Temple where Jikji, the oldest existing book in the world printed with movable metal type, was made. It is the “Mecca” of printing culture, where pioneers of the metal type toiled to invent groundbreaking technology and put it to practical use.   Follow the flow of the exhibition to experience the emotions of the day that opened a new chapter for humanity. Augmented reality, 3D holograms and video presentations bring the history to life.

stories.title: Heungdeoksa Temple Site
stories.script: The Heungdeoksa Temple site, where Jikji, the world’s oldest book printed with metal type was made in 1377, was designated a historic site on May 7th, 1986. The site of Heungdeoksa Temple had remained unidentified, its only trace being the mention of “Heungdeoksa Temple of Cheongjumok”  in ancient literature. Then, in 1985, a piece of a drum engraved with the words Seowonbu Heungdeoksa and a bronze Buddhist bowl engraved with the words “10th year of Hwangtong Heungdeoksa were excavated here, confirming it as the site of the ancient temple.

stories.title: Cheongju Metal Type Education Center
stories.script: The Cheongju Metal Type Education Center located opposite the Cheongju Early Printing Museum is where visitors can learn all about the production of the Jikji. There are also demonstrations by artisan Lim In-ho, bearer of the craft of metal type casting, important intangible cultural property of Korea No. 101, so be sure to check the schedule before visiting. Watch as the craftsman toils at the furnace and shapes the molten iron into words with solemn dedication. Also make a reservation in advance if you want to try making your own book using metal type.

stories.title: Modern and Contemporary Printing Museum
stories.script: This is a museum of modern and contemporary printing technology located in the “Mecca” of printing culture. Printing presses and publications from the end of the 19th century to the present day are on display, showing the development of printing in Korea and the latest printing technologies. There are also lead type printing, letterpress printing, transfer printing, and 3D printing facilities where visitors can try out the printing technologies.

stories.title: Unridan-gil
stories.script: Unridan-gil is the nickname of a stretch of road about 600 meters long, from the Modern and Contemporary Printing Museum to the Uncheon Sinbong-dong Community Center. Cozy cafes, workshops, bakeries, and restaurants are nestled between the gingko trees that line the street. Next to the Early Printing Museum, Metal Type Education Center, and Modern and Contemporary Printing Culture Center, amidst the new and trendy storefronts are old school corner stores and barber shops. The stationery shop next to the elementary school is alive with the chatter of children.  Take a stroll through Unridan-gil taking in these sights and sounds to open your heart to the joy of an unhurried day.

stories.title: Cheongju Arts Center
stories.script: Cheongju Arts Center is Cheongju’s leading cultural space. High-quality performances and exhibitions have been held here each year since its opening in 1995, bringing the arts to Cheongju all year round.   The Cheongju Arts Troupe, consisting of the Cheongju Philharmonic Orchestra, Cheongju Civic Chorale, Cheongju Korean Music Orchestra, and Cheongju City Dance Company, are based here and hold frequent performances. The tiled roof-shaped building exudes classic grandeur, while the Jikji Pavilion which is shaped like the Jikji, is a popular photo spot in Cheongju Arts Center Square. Cheongju Arts Center is connected to the Early Printing Museum by an overhead bridge.

stories.title: Cheongju Museum of Art
stories.script: Cheongju Museum of Art is a dynamic and inviting cultural space that promotes Cheongju as a Cultural City. The museum recently opened a Smart Museum program, providing users with lifelike digital images, virtual reality experiences, and access to digital archives. The museum was opened in 2016 at the former KBS Cheongju Broadcasting Station building to meet the community’s demand for culture and the arts.

stories.title: Cheongju Historic Museum of Baekje
stories.script: Cheongju Historic Museum of Baekje is a museum specializing in artifacts from Baekje, with about 900 items excavated from a tomb in Sinbong-dong. Even the exterior of the building is in the form of an ancient tomb. The exhibition hall contains various artifacts, including armor, helmets, round-ring swords, arrowheads, and other weapons, as well as earthenware such as pots and mugs with handles, dated to the 5th century. There is also an outdoor exhibition of an earthen tomb in the yard.  The museum was designated as Historic Site No. 319 in 1987 as a window to life in Cheongju during the Baekje period.

stories.title: Sangdang Sanseong Fortress
stories.script: It is unclear when Historic Site No. 212, Cheongju Sangdang Sanseong Fortress was first built, the name Sangdang is believed to be from Sangdanghyeon, which was the name of Cheongju during the Three Kingdoms period. The walls measure 4.2 kilometeres in circumference and 4 to 5 meters in height, enclosing an area of 72 hectares. The current structure was partially repaired during the Imjin War and rebuilt in the 42nd year of King Sukjong. About 3,500 troops and monks participated in the maintenance and repair of the fortress at the time. Cheongju Sangdang Sanseong Fortress is one of the few remaining fortresses used in the frequent territorial disputes of the Three Kingdoms era, and is also recognized for its architectural beauty, with curves that create harmony with nature.

stories.title: Sangdang Sanseong Fortress Nature Recreation Forest
stories.audioTitle: Sangdang Sanseong Fortress Nature Recreation Forest
stories.script: Cheongju Sangdang Sanseong Nature Recreation Forest is located to the north of Cheongju Sangdang Sanseong Fortress. Visitors are treated to the view of the mountain ridge from the fortress to the forest, with a variety of trees that change their colors with the season. There is a trail to Sangdang Sanseong Fortress, which is a two hour-walk or hike through the refreshing air of the forest. The facilities include accommodations, a children’s forest experience center, a woodworking experience center, a family playground, a sports field, a wild flower garden, and a camp site for groups.

stories.title: Geotdaesan Mountain
stories.script: Geotdaesan Mountain is an accessible peak at 484 meters with a view over the entire city of Cheongju. It is also a historic site with five beacon fire stations used to send signals with smoke during the day and fire at night in times of trouble. Use of the beacon fire stations ended in 1895, but they were reconstructed by the people of Cheongju in 2009. Geotdaesan is also famous as a night view spot. The city of Cheongju seen from the peak of Geotdaesan Mountain at night glitters like a giant christmas tree.

stories.title: Bosalsa Temple
stories.script: Bosalsa Temple is the oldest temple in Cheongju located in Yongam-dong, Sandang-du, Cheongju. It was established by an official who established the Beopjusa Temple in Songnisan under King Jingheung of Silla. The historic temple is full of precious cultural artifacts, such as the Hanging Painting of Bosalsa Temple designated as National Treasure no. 1258, Geungnakbojeon Hall, designated Tangible Cultural Property of Chungcheongbuk-do no. 56, the Relief of Two Standing Buddhas in Geungnakbojeon Hall, designated Tangible Cultural Property of Chungcheongbuk-do no. 24, and the five story pagoda, designated Tangible Cultural Property of Chungcheongbuk-do no. 65. The temple is also famous for its tranquil beauty, nestled in the foothills of Nakgasan Mountain.

stories.title: Uamsan Hiking Trail
stories.script: Uamsan Mountain has a low peak at just 350 meters, but expands generously around the city of Cheongju. It is also called Wausan for its form resembling a laying cow.  The mountain gets covered with cherry blossoms in spring, lush greenery in summer, colorful leaves in autumn, and pristine snow in winter. With many courses to the summit, choosing the trail is part of the fun. A new Uamsan Circumference Trail is also being created from Samil Park in Cheongju to the Children's Center. It will be a 4.2 kilometer-long walking trail accessible from the city all year round.

stories.title: Cheongju Fortress Village
stories.script: Turn right from the East Gate of Sangdang Sanseong Fortress and you will find a Hanok Village. There are some 20 restaurants selling local fare, attracting hikers with the scent of pancakes frying and other delights. There is also a small reservoir with a walking path right by the restaurants, perfect for a stroll after the meal. The village is always bustling not just with hikers but also those who come for the scenic drive and quaint ambience. The Sangdang Sanseong Fortress Natural Garden, an eco-park converted from farmland, recently opened here as yet another attraction to enjoy.

stories.title: Myeongam Reservoir
stories.script: Water flowing from the valley of Sangdangsanseong Fortress in Cheongju collects in Myeongam Reservoir. The reservoir was first created to supply water for agriculture, but it has now become a popular spot for Cheongju citizens with beautiful scenery and good food. The walking path with its scenic beauty in every season attracts crowds year round. Many restaurants and cafes have opened to serve these crowds, making it a dining destination for people looking for a good meal with scenic views. There are also pedal boats in the reservoir. Take a ride, feeling the gentle breeze, to experience tranquility in nature like time has stopped.

stories.title: Cheongju National Museum
stories.script: Cheongju National Museum, built in 1987, was designed by Kim Soo-geun, Korea’s leading architect who called architecture “poetry built with light and bricks”. The museum buildings set against the backdrop of Uamsan Mountain blends beautifully in natural harmony with the scenery, like a well written poem. A spring culture festival is held under blooming trees in spring, while lush green leaves sparkle under the hot sun in summer. Autumn brings sumptuous colors to the maple leaves, while pristine snow covers its rooftops in winter.

stories.title: Cheongju Land
stories.script: Cheongju Land consists of a small amusement park, a zoo, and the Children's Center. The Children's Center has an exhibition hall where you can see fossils of dinosaurs, shellfish, and minerals, a play experience center full of adventure and imagination, and a butterfly ecology experience center. The children's eyes light up at just the sight of the dinosaur model outside the building. The zoo is well loved by young and old alike. It has a sky deck, where visitors can observe the animals from up high.

stories.title: Cheongnamdae
stories.script: Cheongnamdae was the presidential vacation villa with grounds stretching over 180 hectares near Daecheongho Lake. The name Cheongnamdae, means the Cheongwadae of the south. Cheongnamdae remained veiled in secrecy until 2003 when it was opened to the public. With such outstanding scenic beauty, it’s clear  to see why it was selected for the presidential villa.  Cheongnamdae consists of the Main Building, Annex, Presidential Memorial Hall, Ogakjeong Pavilion, golf course, fish farm, Chogajeong Pavilion, Sky Garden, music fountain, and walking trail. The main building and annex offering a peek into the lives of former presidents is unexpectedly ordinary, but step into the garden and there is plenty to see. Well-kept garden trees and wildflower plots delight the eyes all year round. The statues of past presidents are also an interesting feature. Cheongnamdae becomes even more popular in autumn with a chrysanthemum festival and jazz festival.

stories.title: Daecheong Dam
stories.script: Daecheongho Lake is like the sea of Cheongju, an inland city far from the coast. Created when Daecheong Dam was constructed, it is the third largest manmade lake in Korea after Soyangho Lake and Chungjuho Lake.  The drive to Daecheong Dam is one of the most scenic routes in Cheongju. The ride on the forest road along the beautiful Daecheongho Lake fills the spirit with joy. The floodgates are sometimes opened to control the water level in Daecheong Dam. The massive waterfall that results is spectacle to behold in itself. Daecheong Dam is lit up at night, drawing people to its mesmerizing night view.

stories.title: Munui Cultural Heritage Complex
stories.script: Munui Cultural Heritage Complex near Daecheongho Lake was built to preserve local heritage sites in danger of becoming submerged with the construction of Daecheong Dam. Tangible and Intangible heritage native to the Cheongju region are collected and exhibited in this heritage conservation site. Dolmen, old houses, and Munsangwan, the ancient government office of Munuihyeon were moved and restored, while other structures such as a nobleman’s house, a tavern, a mud-walled hut, a blacksmith’s shop and town walls were recreated based on historical research. Being in this space, one feels as though they have travelled back in time. At the end of the complex is Daecheongho Museum of Art with three exhibition halls and an outdoor sculpture park.

stories.title: Beollat Hanji Village
stories.script: Beollat Hanji Village is where visitors can learn about hanji and experience the craft of hanji making. This is a mountain village so remote that when the Korean War broke out, its residents remained blissfully unaware. It still retains this rustic charm today. It is said that residents of the village have been making hanji from mulberry trees for generations. However, this tradition had almost died out before Hanji artist Lee Jong-guk settled here 20 years ago, continuing the history of hanji in the village. Lee and the villagers grow mulberry trees and make hanji from the pulp using traditional methods, and also run hanji experience programs for visitors.

stories.title: Madong Creator’s Village
stories.script: Madong Creator’s Village is a great example of the transformation of an abandoned space through art. The village used to be an abandoned school building until painter Lee Hong-won moved here and turned it into a studio and exhibition space for his playful creations. Over time, the artist breathed life into its nooks and crannies with imagination. Now it has become a place for the residents of Cheongju to enjoy art and unwind. Facilities include the gallery, an outdoor sculpture display, an unmanned cafe, and a guest room.

stories.title: Dumori Village
stories.script: A 600 year-old protected zelkova tree stands guard at Dumori Village, located in the foothills of Yangseongsan Mountain north of Munui-myeon, Sangdang-gu, Cheongju,   Here, old houses have retained their original structures with the gate, main house, men's quarters, and barn, as if time had stopped. The wild flowers blooming along the road are all the more endearing for their simplicity. Even the small insects floating through the air add to the rustic charm.  The village is also where “Country Diaries”, a well-loved long running drama series in the 1980s, was filmed.

stories.title: Daecheongho Lake Walking Trail
stories.script: Daecheongho Lake Walking Trail was created to share the beauty of the lake with even more people. Around Daecheongho Lake a mountain rises 300 meters from sea level, covered by trees like a folding screen. Such scenic beauty has made it one of Korea’s most popular hiking trails. The trail has 21 sections, passing through Cheongju, Boeun, Okcheon and Daejeon. Picking one is part of the fun, each has its own character and story. The trail also contains a location featured in the drama “Sad Love Story”.

stories.title: Hyeonamsa Temple
stories.script: Hyeonamsa Temple is the branch temple of Beopjusa Temple, the headquarters of the 5th parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, and is said to have been founded by the Goguryeo monk Seongyeong.  In the past, one had to climb a long path of narrow stairs to reach the temple. However, with the huge influx of visitors, a mini monorail has been recently installed. Nevertheless, one might still walk up the stairs as a form of meditation, shaking off worldly woes with each step. Walking up one step at a time, one finally reaches the peak to a view of Daecheongho Lake, spreading out like a gift. This is why Hyeonamsa Temple is a popular destination, even among non-Buddhists.

stories.title: Wollisa Temple
stories.script: Wollisa Temple is the branch temple of Beopjusa Temple, the headquarters of the 5th parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, established by monk Euisang of Silla. It is known as the oldest temple in Chungcheongbuk-do province.  According to the Memorial Stone of Wollisa Temple erected in 1665, the 6th year of Hyeonjong, it was named Wollisa or Temple in the Moon for its proximity to the moon. Daewoongjeon Hall, a well preserved example of Joseon-era architecture with a paljak-style roof, and its mural are worthy of attention. The Saembongsan Hiking Trail which begins from Wollisa Temple is popular for its gentle inclines and view of Daecheongho Lake.

stories.title: Ansimsa Temple
stories.script: Ansimsa was built by monk Jinpyo in the 11th year of King Hyegong of Silla. It was given the name “Ansimsa” which means the “Temple of Relief” as a place that brings peace of mind to his many disciples. The temple stores many valuable treasures. Daewoongjeon Hall of Ansimsa which houses the clay Buddha Triad and painting of Buddha is Treasure no. 664. The Storage Chest for Hanging Painting in Yeongshinjeon Hall holds National Treasure no. 297, the Painting of the Vulture Peak Assembly. The painting was created in 1652, the 3rd year of Hyojong, depicting buddhist saints, disciples, the four devas and guardians assembled around a Sakyamuni Buddha Statue in symmetry. It measures 462 cm wide and 627 cm high, and the height of the central buddha statue is 372 cm.

stories.title: Yangseongsan Mountain
stories.script: Yangseongsan Mountain located in Munui-myeon, Sangdang-gu, Cheongju is popular among hikers as an accessible peak at 300 meters which provides a sweeping view of Daecheong Dam and Cheongnamdae. It is also part of the Daecheongho Lake Walking Trail.  Midway to the peak is the Eagle Rock, shaped like an eagle soaring into the sky. Climb up to the Palgakjeong Pagoda at the peak and you can take a picture with Daecheongho Lake in the background. Add a visit to the nearby Munui Cultural Heritage Complex to wrap up a perfect day trip.

stories.title: Yebburi Folk Museum
stories.script: Yebburi Folk Museum is a private museum opened by handicrafts collector Lee Youngjun. The museum focuses on shamanistic art from the primitive Bronze Age to the modern era. There are also works of art incorporating ideas from Buddhism, Taoism, and Confucianism into animal spirit worship and shamanism.  Another part of the museum displays everyday items from the Joseon era to the present, such as wardrobes, cupboards, braziers and chamberpots.

stories.title: Soro-ri Rice Seed Village
stories.script: Do you know where the world’s earliest rice farming site is? It’s actually right here in Cheongju, in Soro-ri, Oksan-myeon, Heungdeok-gu. An excavation team from Chungbuk National University found the world's oldest rice seed here in 1997 and 1998 during the development of the Ochang Industrial Complex. Previously, the world's oldest rice seeds had been those found in Hunan Province, China, from about 11,000 years ago. Soro-ri’s rice seeds were found to be 15,000 years old, making Korea home of the world's earliest rice farming site. Soro-ri Rice Seed Village is now trying to promote the history of Soro-ri Rice Seeds. Plans are underway to build a museum and a cultural center, to transform the village into a global cultural heritage site.

stories.title: Chojeong Mineral Spring
stories.script: Chojeong Mineral Spring is a natural mineral spring that has continued to flow for more than 600 years. It is recorded in Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam, a Joseon-era Survey of the Geography of Korea, that “Chosu spring is located 39-ri east of the village, with water that tastes peppery and cold, and bathing in the water heals disease. King Sejong and King Sejo have previously visited the spring.” The name Chojeong means a well where water as pungent as pepper flows. Chojeong mineral water is naturally carbonated and rich in magnesium and calcium, which promotes metabolism and gastrointestinal activity. It is also said to help skin elasticity and alleviate some skin diseases. With such incredible properties, it is even known around the world as Mysterious Water of the East.

stories.title: King Sejong and the Chojeong Haenggung Palace
stories.audioTitle: King Sejong and the Chojeong Haenggung Palace
stories.script: King Sejong built a temporary palace in Chojeong-ri in the spring and fall of 1444, and stayed for 121 days to recuperate. King Sejong rode a modest carriage for the five-day trip from Seoul to Chojeong, and compensated farmers with grain for any damage to crop caused by the royal procession. While getting his eye disease treated at Chojeonghaenggung Palace, King Sejong worked to improve the Hangeul system and taught it to his young son Yeongeung Daegun, as well as his ministers. He also worked with Park Yeon to develop a musical instrument called Pyeongyeong. Chojeong Haenggung Palace is a tourist destination with a story- the 121-day trip of King Sejong. Visitors can tour the mineral water bath, sleeping quarters, prince’s room, reading hall and exhibition hall, as well as use the cafe and accommodation facilities.

stories.title: House of Unbo
stories.script: When Unbo Kim Kichang was young, his father wanted him to be a carpenter. He believed that was the only way his son, who could neither hear nor speak, could make a living. However, he became an artist thanks to his mother. Woohyang Park Raehyeon was his wife, fellow artist, and lifelong friend. His works were a silent letter of gratitude to the two women for their love and devotion. House of Unbo is located in Hyeongdong-ri, his mother’s hometown. It comprises an art museum, a sculpture park and workshop as well as a collection of the artist’s items that offer a peek into his life and creative spirit.

stories.title: Gurasanseong Fortress
stories.script: There is an old tale behind Gurasanseong Fortress, built in the forest on the border between Chojeong and Miwon. Once upon a time, there lived a single mother with one son and nine daughters. All her children possessed great strength, but did not get along. One day, a dispute led to a bet on their lives. The daughters were to build a fort on the top of the mountain, while the son was to make a trip to Seoul and back in clogs. Whoever finished their mission first would win. When the fortress was almost finished and the son did not return, the mother, fearing for her son's life, cooked red bean porridge for her daughters, asking them to take a break and eat. The son returned while they were still eating and having lost the bet, the nine daughters jumped from the fortress to their deaths. Shocked by the death of his nine sisters, the son repented and left their home, never to be seen again. It is said that the collapsed walls of Gurasanseong Fortress is the incomplete fortress built by the nine daughters.

stories.title: Jeogok-ri
stories.script: The protected pagoda tree stands majestic at the entrance to the village. The pagoda tree symbolizing integrity, abundance and good fortune, was planted to commemorate someone passing the official exam or being appointed to an important post.  Jeogok-ri was once a valley full of mulberry trees, with the name itself meaning Mulberry Valley. The atmosphere is relaxed and leisurely. A hundred year-old mill has been converted to a village cafe and meeting place. The past lives on here bringing peace to our hearts in the present.

stories.title: Stone Buddha Triad
stories.script: The Stone Buddha triad at the entrance of Bijoong-ri about 2 km from Chojeong Mineral Spring is Treasure no. 1941. The relief carved from a narrow and long pillar-shaped granite rock measures 144 cm tall. With characteristics typical of Buddhist sculpture from the Three Kingdoms period such as the oval shaped folds in the clothing flowing from the chest and large hands, its estimated production period is the early 6th century, around the end of the Three Kingdoms period. As the oldest of the large stone buddha statues from the three kingdoms period remaining today, it is a valuable resource on the history and culture of the region.

stories.title: Hongyangsa Shrine and Samse Chunghyomun Gate
stories.audioTitle: Hongyangsa Shrine and Samse Chunghyomun Gate
stories.script: Hongyangsa Shrine is a shrine dedicated to the ancestors of the Na family of Anjeong. The clan village of the Nas produced numerous scholars and faithful officials of the court. Samse Chunghyomun Gate was built to remember the loyalty of Na Sajong’s family over three generations. Na Sajong died in battle fighting against the five thousand strong Jurchen army with just 50 men in the 22nd year of Seongjong. His son Ungeol followed his fathers footsteps in excursions against the Jurchen failed to avenge his father, and committed honorable suicide on the 3rd anniversary of his death. The sons of Ungeol, Bin and Lin also led several excursions against the Jurchen that failed, also joining their father in honorable suicide on the 3rd anniversary of his death. Thus the three generations of warriors are all commemorated on the same date of death.

stories.title: House of Son Byunghee
stories.script: Man is heaven, said Uiam Son Byeong-hee, the leader of the March 1st Movement and the Donghak Peasant Movement. The commemorative House of Son Byunghee in his birthplace of Geumam-ri, Naesu-eup comprises an exhibition hall, shrine, statue, pavilion, his former home and a pine forest.  Uiam changed the name of the Donghak Movement to Cheondogyo and became the religious movement’s third leader. He devoted himself to propagating the faith as well as educational and cultural projects. He was one of 33 national representatives of the March 1st Movement in 1919, for which he was arrested and imprisoned in Seodaemun Prison. He died during treatment after being released from prison on medical bail.

stories.title: Historic Site of General Han Bongsu
stories.audioTitle: Historic Site of General Han Bongsu
stories.script: General Han Bong-soo was born in 1884 in Segyo-ri, Naesu-eup, Cheongju.  Han joined the anti-Japanese movement when Emperor Gojong was forced to abdicate by the Japanese in 1907 and the Korean Imperial Army was disbanded. He organized a righteous army unit of some 100 disbanded soldiers which won many victories in the Chungcheong-do and Gangwon-do regions. He was famous as an artilleryman when young, and became known as an invincible general with only one loss in 33 attacks. The government awarded him Order of Merit for National Foundation poshumously in 1963 to honor his service. A shrine and a grave were built in Cheongam-ro near the site of his birthplace.

stories.title: Choi Myeong-gil and the Jeonju Choi Clan Village
stories.audioTitle: Choi Myeong-gil and the Jeonju Choi Clan Village
stories.script: The history books refer to Choi Myung-gil as a pacifist. He wrote the surrender document when the Qing invasion of Joseon began 1636. Kim Sang-heon tore up the document, berating Choi for writing such humiliating words. Choi Myung-gil picked up the torn document and made a tearful appeal. Facing reality and saving the country is more important than loyalty. We surrender now, but we will build a strong country to make them pay for the bloodshed. Choi Myung-gil called for normalization of relations with the newly emerging Qing instead of keeping loyal to the declining Ming. His grave is located in Daeyul-ri, Buk-myeon, Cheongwon-gun, Cheongju. This is the village of the Jeonju Choi clan, and his grandson was Choi Seok-jeong, a prime minister of Joseon known for his politics of tolerance amid the chaos of the faction disputes during King Sukjong’s reign.

stories.title: Ochang Lake Park
stories.script: Ochang Lake Park is located in Yangcheong-ri, Ochang-eup, Cheongwon-gu, Cheongju covering an area of about 16.5 hectares around the manmade lake of Hoam Reservoir. There is a 1 km walking path along the lake, and a wide lawn, making it a popular spot for a light walk and recreation. The lake is lit up at night, creating a beautiful atmosphere, and frequent performances and events are held here. Ochang Lake Library and Yangcheong Park are also conveniently located nearby.

stories.title: Ochang Songdae Park
stories.script: Ochang Songdae Park is a small park built along the Songdaeje Reservoir. It is a great place for a simple picnic, with a short walking trail and a lawn. The reflection of the scenery in the lake is beautiful all four seasons, especially in spring, when the walking trail is covered with cherry blossoms. There is a playground right next to the park, making it great for families with children as well. Chungbuk National University's Ochang Campus is also nearby for a visit if time permits.

stories.title: Ochang Miraeji Agriculture Theme Park
stories.script: Ochang Miraeji Agriculture Theme Park is where the annual Cheongwon Life Festival is held. The large site houses an ecological playground, a lotus wetland, a rice exhibition experience center, a promotional exhibition of agricultural products, a local farmer’s market, a multi-purpose field, and the Ochang Miraeji Hanok Village. The theme park operates a cauldron rice experience center and a woodworking experience space. The walking paths are well maintained, making it ideal for family outings. The campsite has been growing in popularity as well.

stories.title: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 1- Cheongseokgul Cave
stories.audioTitle: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 1- Cheongseokgul Cave
stories.script: The first of the Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa is Cheongseokgul Cave, a natural cave where a dragon was seen according to legend. It is also thought to be a paleolithic dwelling site, based on archaeological discoveries such as choppers and planes. The total length of the cave is about 60 meters. Although the entrance is wide, the inside is very narrow and dark. More than 20 species of creatures live in the cave, including the golden bat, a natural monument of Korea. Climb up to the Cheongseokgul Artificial Waterfall Observatory for a sweeping view of the grain fields of Miwon-myeon.

stories.title: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 2- Yongso Pond
stories.audioTitle: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 2- Yongso Pond
stories.script: Second of the Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa is Yongso Pond, located between Cheongseokgul Cave and Okhwadae. Yongso Pond is the deepest part of Dalcheon Stream, with a steep cliff and trees creating an impressive view. The patterns of the cliff’s rocks and the reflection of the trees on the water are also a sight to behold. Legend has it that a dragon once lived here. It was spotted by a woman while ascending to heaven, lost its power and fell back into the water, turning into a serpent monster. Yongso Pond was also called Odam or Turtle Pond for the turtles that live in it.

stories.title: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 3- Cheongyeongdae
stories.audioTitle: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 3- Cheongyeongdae
stories.script: Third of the Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa is Cheongyeongdae, named after its clear water that reflects the tall cliffs and moonlit sky like a mirror. Facing the cliff and looking at the waves flowing in the direction of the wind, worldly woes seem to get washed away. Vehicles are not allowed to enter the area, making it less accessible, however it also means that there is more tranquility to enjoy, with fewer people. Pass through Okhwagyo Bridge to find Cheongyeongdae to the right and Okhwadae to the left.

stories.title: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 4- Okhwadae
stories.audioTitle: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 4- Okhwadae
stories.script: Fourth of the Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa, Okhwadae was named for its beauty resembling a piece of jade shining in the wilderness. Long ago, Seogye Lee Deuk-yoon and his disciples built several pavilions here, where they spread their teachings. The surrounding scenery together with these clifftop pavillions created a breathtaking sight. In the present, Chuwoljeong Pavilion, named after the clear autumn moon, Mangyeongjeong Pavilion, containing all the sights of the world, and Sesimjeong Pavilion, a place to cleanse the mind, have been restored. The legacy of Okhwaseowon Confucian Academy continues in the form of Sunghyeonsa Shrine.

stories.title: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 5- Geumbong Peak
stories.audioTitle: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 5- Geumbong Peak
stories.script: Fifth among the Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa is Geumbong, a mountain south of Bangchukgol Valley, located in Wolyong-ri, Miwon-myeon, Sangdang-gu, Cheongju. Its name means ‘peak wrapped in silk’. One can’t help but marvel at the poetic expression, likening the sublime harmony of Geumbong’s forests and Dalcheon Stream to silk. The silken peak mesmerizes with colorful flowers in spring, lush greenery in summer, shining autumn colors in the fall, and pristine white snow in winter.

stories.title: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 6- Geungwan Forest
stories.audioTitle: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 6- Geungwan Forest
stories.script: Sixth of the Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa, Geumgwan Forest is the forest by Dalcheon Stream in Geumgwan-ri. Oak trees soaring 30 meters high cover an area of 7900 square meters, covering the sky with a thick canopy. This makes it the perfect summer vacation spot in the shade, and cooling waters of Dalcheon Stream. It has recently gained popularity as a camping site for families. With well-equipped facilities for camping and beautiful views all around, the only thing to do is relax and create memories.

stories.title: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 7- Gamasoppul Hill
stories.audioTitle: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 7- Gamasoppul Hill
stories.script: Gamasoppul Hill is the seventh of the Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa located below the cliffs of Dalcheon stream, which comes with a sad legend. Once upon a time, a newlywed couple was passing this area. Perhaps the bearers were too distracted by the view, they dropped the bride’s palanquin into the water, causing her to drown. The groom, in his grief, followed her into the water and drowned as well. Did the lovers continue their love story in the afterlife? Knowledge of the legend adds poignancy to sound of the flowing water.

stories.title: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 8- Shinseonbong Peak
stories.audioTitle: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 8- Shinseonbong Peak
stories.script: Eighth of the Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa is Shinseonbong Peak, located at the border of three administrative districts- Miwon-myeon, in Sangdang-gu, Cheongcheon-myeon in Goesan-gun, and Sanoe-myeon in Boeun-gun. The view from the Miwon-myeon side is so famous for its beauty, legend has it that deities came down to play. Listening to the babbling of water below the rocks of Shinseonbong Peak amidst such surreal beauty, one might daydream that they too were deities lost in paradise.

stories.title: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 9- Bakdaeso Pond
stories.audioTitle: Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa 9- Bakdaeso Pond
stories.script: Last of the Nine Scenic Views of Okhwa is Bakdaeso Pond, earning its name from the blue rocks and greenery enclosing the deep pond like a screen. It is about 1 kilometer northwest from Shinseonbong Peak. Trees growing in the cracks of mountain rocks cast shade over the water, creating a mystic ambience. People come to Bakdaeso Pond to heal in the embrace of unspoiled nature.

stories.title: Shrine of Shin Chaeho
stories.script: This shrine was built to honor Danjae Shin Chae-ho, an independence activist, historian, and journalist during the Japanese colonial era. Facilities include the Shin Chae-ho Memorial Hall, shrine, statue and grave of Shin Chae-ho, where visitors can learn about the life of this well-respected man of integrity. Shin was born in Daejeon, but moved to Nangseong, clan village of the Goryeong Shins, at age seven when his father passed away. After his death in February 1936 in Lushun Prison, Manchuria, his remains were secretly moved and buried here.  Shin is also remembered for the famous story that he remained standing with a straight back when washing his face at the basin, refusing to bow down to the Japanese even under colonial rule.

stories.title: Midongsan Arboretum
stories.script: Midongsan Arboretum is the only public arboretum in Chungcheongbuk-do Province. A visit to this forest restores the mind and body of from the fatigue of everyday life. Known as the largest arboretum in the central region with 900 species of plants planted over 250 hectares of land. Walking paths, hiking trails, and red clay paths are well maintained, making every part the forest accessible in every season. Visitors are treated to the sight of the metasequoia forest stretching high into the sky, as well as a rich variety of trees, birds and flowers. Visitors can also experience and learn at the Forest Science Museum, Nandae Botanical Garden, Succulent Botanical Garden, and Wood Culture Experience Center.

stories.title: Gwaneumsa Temple
stories.script: Located in the middle of Uamsan Mountain behind Cheongju University, Gwaneumsa is a temple under the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. It is a well-loved temple in Cheongju frequented not only by Buddhists but also hikers, as it captures the beauty of Uamsan Mountain in all four seasons. The view of downtown Cheongju is another charm of Gwaneumsa Temple. Passing by Cheonbuljeon Hall to the stairs that lead to Geungnakbojeon Hall, you will see a statue of Monk Budai. Budai was a monk from Tang Dynasty who used to carry alms received in a sack, passing them out to the needy. His good-natured smile is a gift of good energy to passers-by even today.

stories.title: Jeongbukdong Toseong Fortress
stories.script: The earthen fortifications of Jeongbuk-dong have been built in a square shape in the middle of the plain where Mihogang River and Musimcheon Stream merge. The fortress is the oldest of its kind in Korea along with Pungnap Toseong Fortress in Seoul and the only one maintained almost in its original form. Thus it is considered a valuable resource for the study of earthen fortifications in early Korean history. It was designated a Monument of Chungcheongbuk-do on December 14, 1990, then promoted to Korean Historic Site No. 415 in 1999 when its importance was recognized. The Jeongbukdong Toseong Fortress becomes the best sunset watching spot in the evening. People flock to photograph the brilliant sunset and the trees atop the earthen fortifications each day.

stories.title: Munam Ecological Park
stories.script: Munam Ecological Park is loved by Cheongju citizens for its beauty that reveals a different side each season. Interestingly, the park used to be a landfill up to the year 2000. It went through an amazing transformation through the efforts of many, becoming a well loved eco-friendly landmark.  Munam Ecological Park is equipped with an ecological wetland, arboretum, ecological trail, health forest experience center, a wellness themed forest, basketball court, jogging course, camping site, and dog playground, attracting an unending stream of visitors on weekends.

stories.title: Mihogang River
stories.script: Mihogang River is the largest tributary river of the Geumgang River, which originates from Mangisanseong Fortress in Eumseong, Chungcheongbuk-do. From there it passes through Jincheon and Cheongju, to reach Hapgang-ri (Dumulmeori) in Sejong, stretching over 89.3 kilometers. Its name was changed from Mihocheon Stream to Mihogang River in July 2022. When the sun sets, the river is colored a beautiful crimson. It is the main habitat of the Miho spiny loach, a natural monument and endangered species. It is also a winter habitat for shelducks.

stories.title: Seated Buddha Rock Carving in Jeongha-dong
stories.audioTitle: Seated Buddha Rock Carving in Jeongha-dong
stories.script: The Seated Buddha's Rock Carving of Jeongha-dong is engraved on a roadside rock at the entrance to Jeongha-dong Village in Sangdang-gu, Cheongju. It measures 323cm high in total, with the lotus pedestal measuring 45 cm high and 214 cm wide. The Buddha carving is well balanced in form, the wrinkles on the clothes flow naturally, and the left index finger is held in the right hand. It has a clean and elegant style, and is characterized by a crown on the Buddha’s head, a rare feature in Korea. It is thought to be from the early Goryeo era, with features typical of the Unified Silla Period.

stories.title: Baekhwasan Mountain
stories.script: Baekhwasan Mountain is a gentle mountain in Juseong-dong, Cheongwon-gu, Cheongju, suitable place for light hiking. It is all the more popular due to its proximity to Sangdangsanseong Fortress. The name Baekhwasan Mountain was given because of its geology. Formed from white rocks and sand, it looks like a white flower from afar. There are many pine trees on the mountain, and its peak is Suribong Peak, also known as the Eagle Peak. Halfway up the hill you will find Seogisa Temple, famous for the Seated Stone Buddha of Seogisa Temple, designated as Tangible Cultural Property of Chungcheongbuk-do No. 174.

stories.title: Bumosan Hill
stories.script: Bumosan Mountain is a 232 meters-high peak located on the border of Biha-dong and Jidong-dong, Heungdeok-gu, Cheongju. The Mihogang River flows around this mountain. It went by several names in the past, Ayangsan, Agyangsan, and Amisan. However, during the Mongol invasion of Goryeo Dynasty, people in the area were able to evacuate to its fortress where they remained unharmed. Thus, the name Bumosan or “Parents Mountain” was given, expressing the debt of gratitude they owed the mountain. At its peak are the Bumo Sanseong Fortress, designated Monument of Chungcheong No. 121, and Yeonhwasa Temple.

stories.title: Tropical Botanical Garden
stories.script: The Tropical Botanical Garden is located inside the Cheongju Agricultural Technology Center, a sanctuary that remains lush and green even in winter. There are four themed halls - temperate, tropical, subtropical, and mediterranean, arranged around the Central Square. Each themed hall houses more than 250 species of tropical plants. An indoor fountain and small waterfall add to the tropical atmosphere. Outside the building is a lawn and kids’ park, making it a perfect outing location for families.

stories.title: Korea Silk Museum
stories.script: The Korean Silk Museum located in Hakcheon-ri, Gangnae-myeon, Heungdeok-gu, Cheongju showcases the history and future of sericulture in Korea. It offers a rare look into the process of making silk from cocoons. Visitors can also see live silkworms and try out activities such as making necklaces from silkworm cocoons.  Alongside special seasonal events such as sweet potato digging, facilities such as the sheep garden, sledding slope, and digital play area makes it a fun attraction for families with young children.

stories.title: History of DMZ
stories.script: Hello, everyone. This is your DMZ Live audio curator, Saengsaengi DMZ stands for the (Korean) Demilitarized Zone.  The DMZ is an area where South and North Korea agreed not to deploy military forces 2 km from each Military Demarcation Line (MDL), which was mutually decided upon during the armistice negotiations of the Korean War. As a result of the area being restricted to civilian access for over 70 years, the DMZ has been preserved, and the scars of war have healed naturally. The DMZ has now become the repository for the ecosystem of the Korean Peninsula. It has a total area of 903.3 km2, accounting for 0.41% of the entire Korean Peninsula, or is a similar area to about half the size of Jeju Island, and is home to 101 out of 267 endangered species (38% of the total endangered species) and the estimated total species is about 6,000. However, considering the challenges of conducting an ecological examination in the DMZ, the actual number of species is believed to be higher than what is known.
