Deogyusan Mountain is considered as one of Korea’s most beautiful and beloved mountains among hikers after Jirisan Mountain and Seoraksan Mountain. The northern valley of Muju Gucheondong is particularly famous, attracting visitors year-round. The park is also renowned for other valleys such as Chilyeon Valley, Tooakdong Valley, and Wolseong Valley.  In Deogyusan National Park, you can also enjoy a special camping experience under a starry sky. The park has the largest national park campground, Deogyudae Campground, which is nestled in a forest with a valley nearby, making it a popular spot for regular visitors.   Camping here and surrounding by the beauty of nature feels like you have the whole Deogyusan Mountain to yourself!

stories.title: Four Seasons of Deogyusan Mountain
stories.script: Four Seasons of Deogyusan Mountain  Watching a mountain change its clothes with each season is another way to appreciate the beauty of nature. Deogyusan National Park interprets this idea well as each season offers its own unique charm.  In spring, Deogyusan National Park is covered with all sorts of colorful wildflowers, such as mountain azaleas and rhododendrons. The azaleas of Deokyupyeongjeon Hall, where the Gucheon-dong valleys meet the ridge, are often referred to as “heavenly flower garden.”  On a hot summer’s day, there’s nothing better than cooling your feet in a refreshing valley stream. Gucheondong Valley in Deogyusan National Park is known for its striking cliffs and meandering rapids that the ancestor named it 33 Picturesque Sceneries along its course. Gucheondong Valley is named for its 9,000 twists and turns that begin on the northern slopes of Deogyusan Mountain and make up the 33 Picturesque Sceneries including Haksodae, Chuwoldam, and Gucheon Fall. The 24-km-long valley road starts with Najetongmun Gate, which used to be the border between Baekje and Silla and runs through the summit of Sinpungryeong Pass to Geochang-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do. The valley road was selected as one of the top 100 beautiful roads to drive in Korea by the Korea Road Traffic Association, and it crosses through National Route 37.  Autumn in Deogyusan National Park is a breathtaking sight as the mountains are covered in colorful fall foliage, particularly around Hyangjeokbong Peak and Jungbong Peaks area .  Many hikers visit each year to walk the maple road under the clear autumn sky.  When winter arrives, many people come to Deogyusan National Park to admire the snow-covered forests. Muju Deogyusan Resort has a gondola ride that provides a shorter and easier hiking trail, making it accessible for the less-experienced winter hikers. When you reach the top of Hyangjeokbong Peak, you can see the entire snow-covered land in a single glance. This alone makes for a special experience, but for an even better experience, spend a night at the Hyangjeokbong Shelter, where you can enjoy the serene beauty of Deogyusan Mountain snowy landscape and countless stars sparkling above the snowy ground. If you make a reservation first, you can experience both the snow-covered natural scenery and the starry night of Deogyusan Mountain.

stories.title: Dadohaehaesang National Park
stories.script: Dadohaehaesang National Park  Do you know which national park in Korea is the largest? It is Dadohaehaesang National Park designated as the 14th national park in Korea. Dadohaehaesang National Park, which spans the coastal areas and islands from Hongdo Island in Jeollanam-do through Sinan-gun, Jindo-gun, Wando-gun, and Goheung-gun, all the way to Yeosu-si. In total, the park stretches approximately 23,000m².  In Dadohaehaesang National Park, there are around 1,700 islands, along with uniquely shaped rocks and caves that create a mystical landscape. Besides, the wide blue sky and cobalt-blue ocean beneath it from a breathtaking view allow visitors to immerse themselves in the beauty of nature.  Dadohaehaesang National Park holds as much rich history as its large space. During the Silla Dynasty, it was where Jang Bogo established his maritime kingdom, and in the Goryeo Dynasty, it served as a major maritime trade route with neighboring nations like Song Dynasty and Yuan Dynasty. In the Joseon Dynasty, it became the battlefield where Admiral Yi Sun-sin defeated Japanese invaders, and even untill now, people can still explore the historical relics scattered throughout this significant area.   Dadohaehaesang National Park is divided into six areas. Among them, Hongdo Island and Heuksando Island are the most famous, and Heuksando Island in particular, being the most renowned fishing round in Korea for skate and croaker. Now, why don’t we get a closer look at the six representative areas of Dadohaehaesang National Park?  First, Hongdo Island and Heuksando Island, is a beautiful region with stunning scenery known as a place where scholar Jeong Yak-jeon wrote the “Jasaneobo” during his exile in the late Joseon Dynasty. Next, Jodo Island area gets its name from the abundant islands that said to resemble a gathering of birds. This area is also known for its fine sand and pristine beach. Bigeum and Docho area has the largest dune in the East, and it is home to a salt pond that produce 70% of Korea’s salt supply.  The Soan and Cheongsan area is home to Jeongdo-ri Gugyedeung, a place known for its beautiful pebble beach as well as the filming location of the movie “Seopyeonje”. Not only does this beach features white sand, creating a harmonious landscape, but also holds historical significance as it preserves the trace of Yun Seon-do. The Geumodo Island area is known for its dense camellia trees and the rocky formations around Geumosan Mountain, which create a breathtaking sunrise view over the horizon. The annual Hyangilam Sunrise Festival is held here to celebrate its beauty. Finally, Narodo Island area located at the southernmost part of Dadohaehaesang National Park features unique and mysterious rock formations created by wind and sea erosion. These formations enhance the scenic beauty of the sea.

stories.title: Cheongsando Slowgil Street
stories.script: Cheongsando Slowgil Street  If you step onto Cheongsando Island surrounded by beautiful seas, barley field canola flower and rice terraces, everyone will choose to pause their hurried steps and walk slowly to appreciate the natural beauty. Cheongsando Island is a village that preserves the value and charm of slow living, earning global recognition when it was selected as Asia's first Slow City in December 2007.  Cheongsando Island derives its name from the Chinese characters of Cheong (靑) and San (山), as it is known for its mountains, sea, and sky, all appearing in blue. Its eminent natural scenery has earned it a designation as part of Dadohaehaesang National Park. Cheongsando Island has also been recognized as the fourth most beautiful island in Korea by CNN and has been selected as one of the Top 100 Must-Visit Tourist Destinations in Korea, making it one of the country's representative island travel spots.  When you step onto Cheongsando Island, you can find the Slow-gil Street, which spans about 42km and divided into eleven courses and seventeen trails. The Slow-gil Street is a themed walking path designed for leisurely walk, allowing visitors to fully embrace the art of slowing down and enjoy the island’s beauty. Along the way, you can enjoy photo spots, stunning views of the blue sea and mountains, and charming stone wall paths. With so many diverse attractions, walking the trail never feels boring.   If you are worried about feeling lonely while walking, we recommend you join the Cheongsando Slow Walking Festival held in Cheongsando Island. This festival held every spring when the island is covered in blooming canola flowers. Participants can enjoy the Slow-gil Street while fully immersing themselves in the beauty of nature. Come and enjoy the art of slowing down at Cheongsando Island, a part of Dadohaehaesang National Park where both day and night interpret beauty well.

stories.title: Taeanhaean National Park
stories.script: Taeanhaean National Park  There is a national park famous for its beautiful scenery where numerous beaches, uniquely shaped rocks, and mountain peaks. It is Taeanhaean National Park.  Taeanhaean National Park was originally designated as Seosanhaean National Park in October 1978, before its name was changed to Taeanhaean National Park in March 1990. The geographical features in the park was shaped by wave and tidal erosion along the coastline, giving it not only stunning scenery but also a number of beautiful beaches. Also, with an average temperature of 4°C in January, the park features unique natural characteristics, including the distribution of distinctive plant species.  The biggest feature of natural topography in Taeanhaean National Park is dune, which is the vast sand hills stretches out there. Along with the sandy beaches spread across the Taean Peninsula and Anmyeondo Island, new sand dunes form every winter due to the rise of strong northwest monsoon. These unique landscapes, made of soft sand, can be seen throughout the park, offering an exotic view of nature.  In the past, tourists had rarely visited here because of inconvenient transportation, but after the 2000s when the construction of Seohaedaegyo Bridge and Seohaean Expressway were completed, access to the land has become much easier. Why not visit Taeanhaean National Park, where you can enjoy the beautiful dunes, refreshing breezes, and the surrounding blue sea?

stories.title: Wolchulsan National Park
stories.script: Wolchulsan National Park  Have you heard of  Wolchulsan National Park, the southernmost mountainous national park on the Korean Peninsula? Wolchulsan National Park located in the Wolchulsan Mountain region, spanning Yeongnam-gun and Gangjin-gun in Jeollanam-do. It is a place where beautiful scenery, prominent cultural heritage, and local charms come together in harmony.   Wolchulsan Mountain gets its name from its position facing the West Sea, meaning it is the first to greet the moon. The name derives from the Chinese characters for moon (月) and to rise (出). During the Goryeo Dynasty, it was also called Wolsaengsan (月生山), using the Chinese character for birth (生), meaning the place where the moon is born”. Also, as the Sobaeksan Mountain Range splits from the Taebaeksan Mountain Range and stands tall at the southwest coast, it is often referred to as the Sogeumgangsan Mountain of Honam.”  Wolchulsan Mountain is considered one of the five famous mountains of the Honam region. It is often called a strange rock exhibition because of its stone peak and sea cliffs made up of uniquely shaped rock that stands tall like a towering backdrop in the middle of the plains. When you reach the summit, you can look down and enjoy a view in all directions. From rugged rock formations along the ridges, to the rural landscapes of Yeongam-gun and Gangjin-gun, and even a panoramic view of the Dadohae.  From the sunrise over the mountain ridges to the moonrise, the countless islands and river tanks that scattered across the South and West Sea, and the sunset that paints the West Sea in scarlet are unique to Wolchulsan Mountain.   Why not take a trip to Wolchulsan National Park and experience its beauty from sunrise to sunset?

stories.title: Temples of Wolchulsan Mountain
stories.script: Temples of Wolchulsan Mountain  Wolchulsan Mountain, named for being the first to greet the moon, may not be a particular tall mountain, but its landscape is composed of uniquely shaped rocks and cliffs, giving it a majestic and grand appearance. From its summit, where steep rocky cliffs dominate, you can capture the view of the Dadohae archipelago at a glance. Wolchulsan Mountain is not only renowned for its stunning mountain ranges but also for its significant historical and cultural value. It is home to some remarkable Buddhist cultural heritage sites, including Dogapsa Temple, Cheonhwangsa Temple, and Muwisa Temple. Shall we explore the significant temples of Wolchulsan Mountain?  First, Dogapsa Temple located in Yeongam, Jeollanam-do, with a thousand-year history is said to have been built by the Monk Doseon during the reign of King Munmu of the Unified Silla period to capture the spirit of national prosperity. This temple is known for its beautiful scenery, and at the entrance, you will find an ancient hackberry tree that stood for over five hundred years was once designated as a nurse-tree. Though it is now a dead tree, it still creates a unique atmosphere. If you are visiting Dogapsa Temple, you can’t miss the national treasure Haetalmun Gate. This gate was built in the Joseon Dynasty and symbolizes the passage of leaving the worldly realm behind to the pure realm where Buddha resides. Dogapsa Temple suffered from three fires during the Jeongyujaeran and the Korean War, but legend has it that the Haetalmun Gate survived each time, remaining untouched by the flames.  Moving on to Cheonhwangsa Temple in Yeongnam, Jeollanam-do, it is estimated to have been founded between the late Silla Dynasty to the early Goryeo Dynasty. The temple was lost in the Jeongyujaeran during the reign of King Seonjo but was rebuilt in 1646 during King Injo’s reign. Cheonhwangsa Temple has maintained its status as a small but historically significant temple ever since. It’s located at the hiking trail entrance that leads to Cheonhwangbong Peak, the summit of Wolchulsan Mountain, making Cheonhwangsa Temple the perfect place to visit before climbing up to the summit of Wolchulsan Mountain.  Finally, Muwisa Temple that was founded by the Buddhist Monk Wonhyo during the Silla Dynasty, and it is in Gangjin-gun of Jeollanam-do. To reach the temple, you will pass through a green tea field that spread across Wolchulsan Mountain, making the journey itself a heartwarming destination. Muwisa Temple is also home to cultural heritage that brings history to life. In the temple courtyard, a memorial stone records the detailed story of Monk Seongak, who was executed by Gungye for supporting Wang Geon, the first king of the Goryeo Dynasty. Inside the temple, you will find the Painting of Amitabha Buddha Triad, a masterpiece of early Joseon Buddhist art.   With beautiful sights stretch from sunrise to sunset and even moonrise, come experience the landscapes together with the deep history at the temples of Wolchulsan Mountain!

stories.title: Gayasan National Park
stories.script: Gayasan National Park  Gayasan National Park spans from Geochang-gun and Hapcheon-gun in Gyeongsangnam-do to Seongju-gun in Gyeongsangbuk-do, and it was the ninth national park to be designated in Korea. Gayasan Mountain was also called Udusan Mountain meaning cow head mountain which derives from the Chinese characters, “牛” means cow and “頭” means head because its shape is said to resemble a cow's head.  Inside Gayasan National Park is Haeinsa Temple, home to the Tripitaka Koreana, a proud cultural heritage created to overcome the national crisis during the Mongol invasions of the Goryeo Dynasty. This ancient temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site, was built during the Silla Dynasty with the full dedication of the nation. In addition to housing the Tripitaka Koreana, Haeinsa Temple also preserves over 200 national treasures and various other cultural relics, making it a culturally significant site.   When visiting Gayasan National Park, you should also stop by the Hongryudonggyegok Valley, which stretches about 4 km from the park entrance to Haeinsa Temple. The valley gets its name from the Chinese character for red (紅), as it turns red in spring with azaleas and rhododendrons, and in autumn with vibrant foliage. Also, the forest path surrounded by ancient pine trees, which have stood for a thousand years, creates a breathtaking scene.  Namsan Jeilbong Peak in Gayasan National Park is also called Cheonbulsan Mountain. The name comes from the unique rock formations along the ridges, which resemble a thousand Buddha statues covering the mountain. At Namsan Jeilbong Peak, there lies Cheongnyangsa Temple, an ancient temple dated back to the Silla Dynasty. It is said that Choe Chiwon, a prominent scholar of late Silla Dynasty, embraced Buddhism and practiced asceticism on this mountain. Along with Odaesan Mountain and Sobaeksan Mountain, Namsan Jeilbong Peak is known as one of the regions that were spared from destruction during the Japanese invasions of Korea, earning it the reputation of being protected from disaster.   This coming weekend, why not take a trip to Gayasan National Park to enjoy its beautiful landscapes and rich Buddhist history?

stories.title: Gayasan Sorigil Trail
stories.script: Gayasan Sorigil Trail  The Gayasan Sorigil Trail is the most famous pathway in the Gayasan National Park. It spans a 6 km section from the Daejanggyeong Theme Park in Hapcheon-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, to Yeongsangyo Bridge at Haeinsa Temple. This trail follows the restored and refined old Hongryudong path, allowing visitors to walk along the Hongryudonggyegok Valley on an easily accessible route. Notably, it has a barrier-free trail making it an excellent option for visitors with limited mobility that everyone can have an inclusive and enjoyable experience.  The Gayasan Sorigil Trail can be divided into three sections including the 2 km “Maeul-gil” leading to the Exploration Support Center, the 4 km “Hongryudonggyegok Valley Trail” from the center to Yeongsangyo Bridge, and the 1.2 km “Haeinsa-gil Trail”. On the Maeul-gil, you can experience the rustic atmosphere of a rural village, while the Hongryudonggyegok Valley Trail offers views of the majestic valley and pristine nature. As you pass through the village, forest, and get closer to Haeinsa Temple, you begin to feel as if you are walking back through history.  The Gayasan Mountain Sorigil is particularly suitable for all ages and genders as it has little to no uphill or downhill tracks on steep slopes. The trail is divided into five segments with exits along the way, making it a good path for beginners to walk without having to finish the entire course.   Come enjoy the harmonious combination of nature, history, and scenery along the Gayasan Sorigil Trail, where the sounds of birds and the breeze accompany the stunning views.

stories.title: Jirisan National Park
stories.script: Jirisan National Park  Do you know which place was designated as Korea’s first national park? It’s Jirisan Mountain, a mountain that has long been regarded as one of the nation's most sacred peaks, alongside Geumgangsan Mountain and Hallasan Mountain. With its majestic yet serene ridges, Jirisan Mountain is known as the roof of Yeongnam and Honam regions. It has also served as a vital site for local communities and remains the Mountain of Life, continuing to maintain its presence.   Jirisan National Park is home to over eighty-five big and small peaks. The ten roughest peaks including Cheonhwangbong Peak, Banyabong Peak, and Tokkibong Peak. Nestled between these ridges, several valleys and falls stretches like a natural backdrop, creating breathtaking landscapes throughout the park.  There are ten must-see places in Jirisan National Park known as the “Ten Scenic Views of Jirisan Mountain”. They are the landscape covered by Nogodan Sea of Clouds, the Piagol Autumn Leaves, the evening glow of Banyabong Peak, the clear flowing waters of the Seomjingang River, the bright moon over Byeoksoryeong Mountain, Buril Fall, the royal azalea between Seseok, the mystical beauty of Yeonha, and the sunrise from Cheonwangbong Peak. With such a large area and deep history, Jirisan Mountain offers a variety of things to see, making it a year-round destination for countless visitors.  Jirisan National Park has sixteen different hiking courses, including the Guyronggyegok Valley Course, Samsinbong Peak Course, and Baemsagol Valley Course, each with varying difficulty levels and themes. This variety attracts many repeat visitors who return to explore different trails. Also, with improved accessibility through highways such as the Tongyeong-Daejeon Expressway, the Suncheon-Wanju Expressway, and the 88 Olympic Expressway has led to an increase in visitors.   Jirisan National Park has been the site of the Korean people for a very long time. Spanning across three provinces from Gurye-gun in Jeollanam-do, Namwon-gun in Jeollabuk-do, to Hadong-gun, Sancheong-gun, and Hamyang-gun in Gyeongsangnam-do. As such, Jirisan National Park is a place where three diverse cultures meet in harmony, making it an excellent place to explore Korea’s rich history and culture.

stories.title: Jirisan Asiatic Black Bear
stories.script: Jirisan Asiatic Black Bear  Asiatic Black Bear, with their round faces, fluffy ears, black fur, and a cute V-shaped white patch on their chest, are so adorable that just seeing them makes you feel their “cuteness.” Wondering where these charming bears live? It’s right here in Korea's Jirisan Mountain.  Since a wild Asiatic black bear was first spotted in the Jirisan Mountain in November 2000, efforts have been made to restore the species through breeding and release. The Jirisan Asiatic Black Bear Restoration Project is significant as it marks the beginning of efforts to restore endangered wildlife in Korea.  During the Japanese colonial period, the population of Asiatic black bears plummeted due to excessive hunting. Misbeliefs about the medicinal benefits of bear bile, known as “woongdam,” led to widespread and indiscriminate hunting. Hence, Asiatic black bears were thought to have disappeared from Korea. However, the Korea National Park Service was the first in the world to artificial inseminated the endangered Asiatic black bear species and trained the bears to adapt to the wild successfully. They then released it in Jirisan National Park for the first time in 2004. As of 2024, 89 Asiatic black bears now live in Jirisan National Park, and it is predicted that their population will soon exceed 100.  At this point, you might be worried. What if I bumped into an adorable yet very scary Asiatic black bear at Jirisan National Park? Well, if you do happen to encounter an Asiatic black bear, playing dead like the fairytale taught won’t be very effective. Instead, let the bear know your presence naturally and gradually move out of the bear's sight. The Asiatic black bear is generally gentler than you might think and tend to avoid humans, simply staying out of its sight and moving slowly will keep you safe.   While they are cute, they can be dangerous, so let's learn to coexist with them peacefully!

stories.title: Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region in Jirisan Mountain
stories.audioTitle: Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region in Jirisan Mountain
stories.script: Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region in Jirisan Mountain  Have you ever been to the Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region in Jirisan Mountain, which is the beginning of the Jirisan Jongju traverse? Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region is the starting point to the trail where you can walk along the ridges of Jirisan Mountain, one of the most spiritual mountains for the Korean people.   The Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region in Jirisan Mountain is a 7km exploration trail that takes around four hours to complete. It starts at Hwaeomsa Temple, a thousand-year-old temple at the foot of Jirisan Mountain and ends at “Munenggi”, a Jeolla dialect term meaning a riverbank made to let remaining water overflow.  The Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region in Jirisan Mountain is best known as the classic route leading to Nogodan, a site where rituals were traditionally made to honor the mountain spirit of Jirisan. This course is also available during the forest fire prevention period, making it an ideal spot to visit year-round. Particularly, for the starting point of the Jirisan Mountain Jongju course, if you begin the trekking at dawn, you can walk a quiet trail while listening to the resounding bell of Hwaeomsa Temple echoing through the mountain. This is a charming experience unique to Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region. If a four-hour one-way journey feels a bit overwhelming, it is recommended to go as far as Yeongiam Hermitage from the starting point. The trail from the entrance of Hwaeomgyegok Valley to Yeongiam Hermitage is well-maintained and accessible to everyone. It is an hour-long trek and along the way, you will pass by a bamboo shelter rest area at the 200 m section and a gum tree shelter rest area at the 1 km section too. You can visit Yongso, a spot where legend says a dragon ascended to the heavens, making this a fun and interesting route.  However, if your heart is set on conquering Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region, you might want to try the Munenggi trail at Yeongiam Hermitage. The distance between Yeongiam Hermitage to Munenggi trail is about 5 km and takes about three hours. You can refill your water along the way and the first 2 km from Yeongiam Hermitage has relatively gentle slopes, making it less challenging. However, after that point, you will encounter a more rugged and steep rocky path with several sharp inclines, so if you are aiming to conquer the Hwaeomgyegok Valley Region, it is better to be mentally prepared.

stories.title: Byeonsanbando National Park
stories.script: Byeonsanbando National Park  Byeonsanbando National Park is the one and only national park in Korea that has both mountains and seas. It is broadly divided into two areas including Oebyeonsan Mountain, the coastal areas, and Naebyeonsan Mountain, the inland mountainous areas.  Byeonsanbando National Park located in Buan-gun, Jeollabuk-do, was designated as a national park in 1988. One of its main features is the unique rock formations that make up peaks such as Uisangbong Peak, Sinseonbong Peak, and Ssangseonbong Peak. Between these peaks, you will find stunning natural attractions like Jikso Falls, Bongnaegugok Valley, and Nakjodae. The park is not only known for its breathtaking landscapes but also for its historical and cultural significance, with heritage sites like the Kiln Site in Yucheon-ri and Guam-ri Dolmens nearby.  Byeonsanbando National Park is not only home to natural treasures like Chaeseokgang Cliff and Jeokbyeokgang Cliff but also features cultural sites such as the Sibi (poetry monument) of poet Shin Seok-jeong and Korea's first sculpture park. In addition, it boasts three beaches, making it one of Eight Scenic Jeon of Korea. It is also a perfect place for children to experience nature as well as history.  Naebyeonsan Mountain, the inland mountainous area of Byeonsanbando National Park is home to the Buan Dam built in 1995. With its completion, what was once a valley transformed into the Buanho Lake as water filled the dam. This area creates a breathtaking landscape, as the beautiful lake combines with uniquely shaped rocks and cliffs that appear to be carved.  Byeonsanbando National Park, where coastal and inland mountainous areas coexist, is home to a diverse range of flora and fauna. It features groves of Ilex cornuta, Machilus thunbergii, Japanese holly, and Abeliophyllum, many of which are designated as natural monuments and protected by law. The park offers a unique experience where visitors can enjoy not only the beach but also hiking and forest exploration, making it a popular destination year-round for countless tourists.

stories.title: Jiksopokpo Falls of Buan
stories.script: Jiksopokpo Falls of Buan  Located in Buan-gun, Jeollabuk-do, Jiksopokpo Falls is the largest waterfall in Byeonsanbando National Park, the only national park in Korea where the sea and mountain meet. The waterfall thundering down 30 meters and its name “Jikso”, comes from the fact that the water falls directly into a pool underneath, which was derived from Chinese characters meaning straight (直) and pond (沼).  According to legend, a dragon was enchanted by the beauty of Jiksopokpo Falls in Buan-gun that it once lived in the pond beneath the falls. In the past, people believed that the dragon was the God of rain and agriculture. During droughts, they would perform a ritual by sacrificing a pig into the waters to pray for rain. Because of these traditions, Jiksopokpo Falls has been considered a sacred place for a long time.  Jiksopokpo Falls in Buan has been designated as a national geopark attraction in Korea’s West Coast region. This is because Jiksopokpo Falls is made of tuff, a type of rock formed from volcanic ash and debris during eruptions. Also, the waterfall gives a view of the formation process of columnar joints, which are created when magma cools and solidifies.  The area around Jiksopokpo Falls is also easy to access with its gentle slopes, making it a representative trail in Byeonsanbando National Park. Since this 2.3 km course only takes about fifty minutes to complete, it is also a good place for families with children. As you gaze at the waterfall with your children, you can discuss geological features like columnar joints and explore the natural beauty, history, and cultural significance of the region. This makes great experience for their educational and emotional growth.

stories.title: Hallyeohaesang National Park
stories.script: Hallyeohaesang National Park  Do you know that Hallyeohaesang National Park is the first national marine park in Korea? Stretching from Hansando Island in Tongyeong-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, all the way to Yeosu-si in Jeollanam-do, Hallyeohaesang National Park covers parts of Hallyeosudo, Namhaedo Island, and the coastal areas of Geojedo Island. It is also the second-largest national park after Dadohaehaesang National Park in Korea.  Hallyeohaesang National Park, with 76% of its area made up of marine zones, is known as the most beautiful sea route. It consists of seventy-one uninhabited islands and twenty-nine inhabited islands. Along the 300-ri (120km) waterway, the park features a stunning harmony of small and large islands, making it a treasure trove of marine ecosystems. This beautiful scenery attracts over 3 million visitors every year.  Hallyeohaesang National Park is highly valued as a geological field site where you can observe the effects of volcanic activity on the Korean Peninsula, weathering by strong waves and water, and features of dinosaur habitats. Famous attractions for observing geological features of Hallyeohansang National Park includes Sochido Island and Geumsan Mountain in Namhae-gun, and Aduseom Island in Sacheon-si.  Hallyeohaesang National Park, with its diverse charm, can be divided into six distinct areas. As its scale and location vary, you can enjoy and experience the diverse charms of the park to the fullest!  If it is your first time visiting Hallyeohaesang National Park surrounded by beautiful ocean, it is recommended to start from Hallyeohaesang Bada Bangnigil Street in Tongyeong-si. This trail consists of themed paths spread across six islands in Hallyeohaesang Island. From the Hansando Historic Trail with Admiral Yi Sun-sin to the nature-friendly Yeondaedo Jigetgil trail, each route provides a unique experience. It would be a pleasant trip where you can be surprised at the beautiful nature and engaging themes.

stories.title: Daeson Daedo Island
stories.script: Daeson Daedo Island  In Korea, there are some islands with limited access all year-round to preserve its high natural value. These islands are called “Uninhabited Islands under Absolute Conservation”, and Daeson Daedo Island located in Hallyeohaesang National Park belongs to one of these islands with restricted access because of its high conservation value.  Daeson Daedo Island located in Geoje-si, Gyeongsangnam-do looks like a traditional conical hat rising above the sea. Near Daeson Daedo Island, there are about fifteen large  and small islands, and the two largest islands together are known as either “Daeson Daedo” or “Daebyeong Daedo”.  Daeson Daedo Island composed of rocky coast features a variety of geological formations shaped by wave erosion such as sea cliffs, sea caves, and vertical joints. There are also populations of Machilus and Pinus Thunbergii on the island. In the surrounding waters, various marine invertebrates, such as Halichondria japonica and Anthopleura japonica, as well as diverse seaweed species, inhabit the area.   Hallyeosudo, one of the eight sights of Geoje, is made of beautiful islands. Most of all, Daeson Daedo Island makes its landscape more magnificent with the nearby inhabited or uninhabited islands such as Maemuldo Island, Somaemuldo Island, and Deungdaeseom Island. You can view the beauty of Daeson Daedo Island and island nearby the Yeocha Hongpo Observatory located at southern tip of Geojedo Island.

stories.title: Bada Bangnigil Street
stories.script: Bada Bangnigil Street  Hallyeohaesang National Park, which embraces the southern sea of the Korean Peninsula, is home to the Bada Bangnigil Street that stretching across six islands. This trail is not newly constructed but long been served as a path where island residents would gather firewood from the mountains or naturally use it to support their family livelihoods from the old times. If you leisurely walk along the trail and taking in the scent of the island, you will be drawn into the story of the islander, making Bada Bangnigil Street an attractive trail.   Bada Bangnigil Street stretches across six islands from Mireukdo Island, Hansando Island, Bijindo Island, Yeondaedo Island, Maemuldo Island, and Somaemuldo Island. Why don’t we explore the attractive trails on each of these islands together?   First, on Mireukdo Island, you will find “Dara-gil Street” with a gentle slope combining three scenic elements of the ocean, a cypress forest, and a scenic trail. Next, Hansando Island features the “History Trail” which steeped in the story of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. This trail offers a special experience that combines history and walking themes of both history and walking. Through this trail, you can walk in the footsteps of the Admiral Yi Sun-sin. On Bijindo Island, there is “Sanho-gil Street” named after a coralline ocean covering the island. As you walk, you will be amazed by the stunning ocean view.  On Yeondaedo Island, you will find the “Jiget-gil Trail”, a path created with a pain and sorrow of the island residents. In every season and section of the trail, it offers something different and new, making it an interesting and attractive walk, In Maemuldo Island, there is “Haepum-gil Trail” along the ocean with camellia grove and seashore cliff. Along the way, you will encounter public artwork installation reflecting the lifestyle and culture of Maemuldo Island .  Finally, on Somaemuldo Island, there is “Deungdae-gil Trail” filled with attractions such as greenwood, Maemuldo Customs Museum, breathtaking views, and Sighting of Finless Porpoise. One of the highlights of this trail is the “Mongdol-gil”, which appears between Somaemuldo Island and Deungdaeseom Island during low tide, just like the miracle of Moses from ancient time. This transformation allows you to enjoy a special experience by walking across to the lighthouse in the right time.

stories.title: Gyeryongsan National Park
stories.script: Gyeryongsan National Park  Do you know the second place in Korea to be designated as a national park, following Jirisan National Park? It’s Gyeryongsan National Park located in Gongju-si, Chungcheongnam-do.  Gyeryongsan Mountain got its name because its ridges resemble the shape of a dragon wearing a rooster’s comb. The Chinese characters for rooster (鷄) and dragon (龍) were used to form its name, as it suggests a place of ever-changing mountains. Coupled with its great accessibility, the park is full of visitors all year-round. Gyeryongsan National Park is a great place to enjoy the changing beauty of nature across four seasons. Its breathtaking nature shifts with spring, summer, fall, and winter; so much so that there are names for each seasonal sight. In spring, the whole mountain is covered with blooming flowers, earning it the name “Chunsan Baekhwa.” In summer, the lush greenery is so abundant that it is named “Noeum Bangcho.” In fall, the entire mountain turns red, known as “Mansan Hongyeop,” and in winter, snow blankets the deep valleys, giving it the name “Simgae Baeksul.” With such unique scenery each season, it is fun to discover new sights every time you visit. Gyeryongsan National Park is home to numerous attractions, including Baekje cultural heritage sites, ancient temples, and scenic spots, making it an ideal tourist destination. In particular, large temples are placed across the mountain. With Donghaksa Temple to the east, Gapsa Temple to the northwest, and Shinwonsa Temple to the southwest, creating a balanced layout within the mountain.   Gyeryongsan National Park has long been known not only for its stunning landscapes but also for its positive energy. Yi Chung-hwan's Taekliji, written during the Joseon Dynasty, mentioned that there are four greatly energizing places in Joseon, and Gyeryongsan Mountain is one of them. Shall we set off to Gyeryongsan National Park to experience this beautiful natural setting and receive its good energy together?

stories.title: Gapsa Temple of Gyerongsan Mountain
stories.script: Gapsa Temple of Gyerongsan Mountain  Gyeryongsan Mountain, named for its ridges that resemble a dragon wearing a rooster’s comb, stretches from Cheonhwangbong Peak, its main peak, to Yeoncheonbong Peak and Sambulbong Peak. Renowned since ancient times as a place of positive energy, Gyeryongsan Mountain is home to historic temples such as Donghaksa Temple and Gapsa Temple.  Among the temples located within Gyeryongsan National Park, Gapsa Temple sits in the northwestern part of the mountain. Built in the year 420 by the Goguryeo monk Adohwasang, it is a temple that holds great historical significance.  There is an old saying, Chun Magok Chu Gapsa. which uses the Chinese characters for spring (春) and autumn (秋) to mean that Magoksa Temple is best visited in spring, while Gapsa Temple is most the beautiful in fall. Just like the saying, if you visit Gapsa Temple in the fall, the entire landscape is painted red with fall foliage, creating a breathtaking view. Even when it isn’t fall, the lush forest surrounding Gapsa Temple is so serene and beautiful that it leaves visitors in awe.   With its long history, Gapsa Temple is home to a variety of cultural heritage treasures. From Stupa of Gapsa Temple, designated as a national treasure, to the Printing Woodblocks of Worin seokbo and the Daeungjeon Hall, there are numerous relics, making it an excellent destination for exploring and learning about history.  Among the many relics at Gapsa Temple, one must-see is the flagpole named Dangganjiju. This Buddhist relic, typically found at larger temples, is a type of flagpole support used to hold flags during major temple events, guiding visitors to the temple. Only three iron dangganjijus remain in Korea, one at Chiljangsa Temple in Anseong-si, Gyeonggi-do; one at Yongdusa Temple Site in Cheongju-si, Chungcheongbuk-do; and one at Gapsa Temple in Gongju-si, Chungcheongnam-do. This weekend, why don't you come and experience the essence of Buddhism at the beautiful Gapsa Temple?

stories.title: Bukhansan National Park
stories.script: Bukhansan National Park  Since ancient times, the five major mountains representing the north, west, east, south, and central region were called the “Ohak”. These mountains were considered sacred, believed to be home to guardian deities, and were sites for ceremonial rites. Of the Five major mountains, the one representing the central region of South Korea is none other than Bukhansan Mountain.  Designated as Korea’s 15th national park, Bukhansan Mountain has many names. “Hwasan” meaning “shining mountain” and “Samgaksan” meaning “triangle mountain,” are named as its three peaks forming a triangular shape. Located in Seoul and Gyeonggi-do, the heart of the country, it is a rare example of an urban natural park on a global scale. With Uiryeong as the border, the northern area is known as the Dobongsan region, while the southern area is referred to as the Bukhansan region.  Bukhansan National Park is composed of a granite foundation offering a variety of geological attractions formed through centuries of weathering and erosion. Insubong Peak, Samobawi Rock, and Gucheongyegok Valley are some great examples.  Bukhansan National Park serves as the green lungs of the metropolitan area. It is easily accessible from anywhere in the city. It even holds a Guinness World Record as the most visited national park per unit area.  When city life feels overwhelming, why not visit Bukhansan National Park, rising between the city’s tall buildings, to refresh your mind and body?

stories.title: Songchugyegok Valley of Bukhansan Mountain
stories.script: Songchugyegok Valley of Bukhansan Mountain  In the heat of summer, people often seek out beaches, valleys, and other refreshing spots to escape the heat. Immersing yourself in the cool waters of a valley surrounded by dense forest can make the summer heat feel miles away. There’s a valley accessible within an hour by subway from Seoul and Gyeonggi-do. This is Songchugyegok Valley, located in Bukhansan National Park.  Songchugyegok Valley is located in the northwestern gorge of Bukhansan Mountain. Its name derives from the Chinese characters for pine (松) and Manchurian walnut (楸), reflecting the abundance of pine and walnut trees in the area. Stretching about 4 km, the valley is flanked by a lush forest of various trees, including pines and walnuts, creating a stunning landscape where the three-tier waterfall harmonizes beautifully with the surrounding scenery.   Thanks to the excellent accessibility and beautiful scenery of Songchugyegok Valley, restaurants began to spring up nearby, eventually leading to the development of a recreational area. This area now features a swimming pool, arcade, fishing spots, and even pottery-making experiences, along with a variety of entertainment options and amenities, making it a perfect place to cool off and spend a summer day.  Songchugyegok Valley, located within Bukhansan National Park, connects to hiking trails as you move up along the valley. Among them, the “Sapaesan Course” that leads from Songchugyegok Valley to Wongaksa Temple and the “Obong Course” that takes you from Songchugyegok Valley to Obong Peak are the most famous. These courses each take about 3 hours back and forth. Both trails have wonderful sights of trees and rocks in harmony, making them ideal to visit in all four seasons.

stories.title: Bukhansan Dulle-gil
stories.script: Bukhansan Dulle-gil  Welcome to Bukhansan National Park, a nature park within the city. Not sure where to start exploring? In that case, I recommend taking a walk along the Bukhansan Dulle-gil.  The Bukhansan Dulle-gil is a horizontal trail created by connecting and refining existing side paths, allowing for a leisurely walk along the slopes of Bukhansan Mountain. Stretching 71.5 km and divided into twenty-one sections, each segment has its own unique charm. Highlights include Section 1, the Pine Forest Trail, lined with dense pine trees, and Section 2, the Sullye-gil, which honors independence activists with a cemetery that inspires a sense of resilience. Section 3, the Huingureum-gil Trail, features a 12-meter-high viewing platform offering sweeping views of downtown Seoul, while Section 4, the Solsaem-gil, showcases various wildflowers. Each of the twenty-one sections offers its own distinct characteristics.  The Bukhansan Dulle-gil is captivating on its own, but there are also various attractions to enjoy along the way. At the meeting point of Section 1 and 2, you’ll find Ui-dong Solbat Neighborhood Park. Just off Section 2 is the Peach Blossom Tunnel at Baengnyeonsa Temple, while Section 9, known as Masil-gil, starts at Eunpyeong Hanok Village. You’ll also encounter Wondangsaem Park along the Royal Tombs Path in Section 20. Walking the Bukhansan Dulle-gil provides an opportunity to discover these and other scenic spots.  The Bukhansan Dulle-gil invites people and nature to come together harmoniously. Please note, however, that “Uiryeong-gil” in Section 21 requires an advance reservation if you wish to visit.  This coming weekend, why not take a walk along the Bukhansan Dulle-gil, where history, culture, and nature’s beauty await?

stories.title: Odaesan National Park
stories.script: Odaesan National Park  Odaesan National Park, designated as the 11th national park in Korea, is renowned for its vibrant autumn foliage. With gorgeous scenery comparable to Geumgangsan Mountain, it has earned the nickname “Little Geumgangsan Mountain” (小金剛). Starting with Birobong Peak at 1,563 meters above sea level, the range includes Dongdaesan Peak, Durobong Peak, Sangwangbong Peak, and Horyeongbong Peaks, lined up like a natural backdrop, creating a magnificent view.  The entrance features an accessible 2-km fir tree forest path that people of all ages can enjoy. Walking along this refreshing trail lined with towering fir trees, you’ll feel invigorated by the pure, fresh air.  As you continue along the forest path, you’ll reach the Iljumun Gate of Woljeongsa Temple, the head temple of the 14th diocese of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. Founded in the 12th year of Queen Seondeok’s reign during the Silla Dynasty, Woljeongsa Temple boasts a thousand-year history and houses numerous cultural treasures, including the Octagonal Nine-story Stone Pagoda and the Wooden Seated Child Manjusrī statue. Odaesan Mountain has long been regarded as a center of Buddhist culture, preserving historic Buddhist sites such as Sangwonsa Temple, Jeokmyeolbogung Hall, Bukdaesa Temple, Jungdaesa Temple, and Seodaesa Temple, along with significant sites like the Odaesansago National History Archives.  Odaesan National Park is a sacred site for Korean Manjusri worship and a historic place that once housed the Odaesansago National History Archives, where the “Annals of the Joseon Dynasty” were stored. This weekend, why not spend some time at Odaesan National Park, where you can experience the beauty of nature and the spirit of history?

stories.title: Temples of Odaesan Mountain
stories.script: Temples of Odaesan Mountain  Odaesan Mountain has long been considered a sacred site in Buddhism, believed to be the residence of Manjushri, the Bodhisattva symbolizing the perfection of wisdom. Revered as a holy place for Buddhist practice since the Silla Dynasty, Odaesan Mountain is home to several representative temples. Shall we explore some of them within Odaesan National Park?  Woljeongsa Temple and Sangwonsa Temple are the main temples in Odaesan National Park, housing much of the park’s cultural heritage and underscoring their importance. Connecting Woljeongsa Temple to Sangwonsa Temple is the Seonjae-gil, or “Path of Enlightenment.” Let’s walk along Seonjae-gil together, taking time for reflection and healing within Odaesan’s serene forest.  Located at the entrance of Seonjae-gil, Woljeongsa Temple was founded during the reign of Queen Seondeok in the Silla Dynasty. The temple features heritage treasures such as the Octagonal Nine-story Stone Pagoda from the early Goryeo Dynasty and the Stone Seated Bodhisattva that is facing the pagoda. The fir tree forest road in front of Woljeongsa Temple is also renowned as one of Korea’s most beautiful forest trails.   Starting from Woljeongsa Temple at the beginning of Seonjae-gil, we reach Sangwonsa Temple at the trail’s end. Sangwonsa Temple is the most famous among the smaller temples associated with Woljeongsa Temple. While its exact founding date is unknown, it is believed to have been established during the Silla Dynasty. Comparable in scale to Woljeongsa Temple and rich in legends, Sangwonsa Temple attracts visitors year-round.  The Seonjae-gil trail connecting Woljeongsa Temple and Sangwonsa Temple spans 8.1 km. This decked path through dense forest, accompanied by the soothing sound of clear valley streams throughout the walk, healing the mind as you walk. With parking areas, entry and exit points, and bus stops throughout the trail, Seonjae-gil trail is accessible and welcoming, even for visitors who are not experienced hikers.

stories.title: Naejangsan National Park
stories.script: Naejangsan National Park  Designated as the 8th national park in Korea, Naejangsan National Park connects the lower part of the Honam Jeongmaek Mountain Range, which stretches across Jeollanam-do from east to west. Known as one of the four famous mountains of Honam(the southwestern part of South Korea, encompassing Jeollanam-do), alongside Jirisan Mountain and Wolchulsan Mountain, Naejangsan’s name reflects the hidden beauty within. Derived from the Chinese characters “Nae (內)” meaning “in” and “Jang (藏)” meaning “to hide.” Shall we explore the beauty it holds?  Naejangsan Mountain has distinct beauty across the seasons; its autumn foliage is particularly stunning, drawing many tourists and hikers. The dense forest transforms into a breathtaking scene of vibrant colors, making the mountain appear as if it’s ablaze. Each fall, Jeongeup in Jeonllabuk-do, where Naejangsan National Park is located, hosts an annual maple festival to celebrate the fall foliage season.   Naejangsan National Park is home to Baegyangsa Temple, nestled within the Bijarim Forest. The temple boasts a 1,300-year history and houses various heritages, including Daeungjeon Hall, designated as a Jeollanam-do Tangible Cultural Heritage, the Sacheonwangmun Gate, and the Stupa of Buddhist Monk Soyo. Visitors can also explore the lush Bijarim Forest, a designated natural monument with over five thousands trees.  Beneath Seoraebong Peak in Naejangsan National Park, there are several attractions like Gonejang, Janggunsu, and Seokranjeongteo. At 1.9 km from Naejangsa Temple, beneath Bulchulbong Peak, lies a large stone cave with a legend that Buddha emerged from it, giving it the name Bulchulam Rock. This name combines the Chinese characters “bul (佛)” meaning “Buddha” and “chul (出)” meaning “to appear”  Located in Jeongeup, Jeollabuk-do, Naejangsan National Park provides excellent accessibility from Seoul, Daejeon, and even the Gyeongsang region via expressways and trains. Why not spend some time at Naejangsan National Park this fall?

stories.title: Naejangsan Cable Cars
stories.script: Naejangsan Cable Cars  Naejangsan Mountain is one of the five most famous mountains in Honam, alongside Jirisan Mountain and Wolchulsan Mountain. Naejangsan Mountain is known for its vibrant red glow in the fall. Although the main hiking trail spans 11.7 km and takes about 7 hours, which may be challenging for beginners, there’s an easy way to enjoy the views, the Naejangsan cable cars.  Shall we go ride the Naejangsan Cable Car together? First, we’ll enjoy the beautiful Uhwajeong Pavilion. According to legend, this pavilion was so beautiful that it sprouted wings and ascended into heaven. As we continue along the path, we arrive at the Naejangsan Cable Car Station. Once on board, you’ll be able to see Naejangsan Mountain sprawling beneath you, a view especially stunning in autumn when red and gold foliage showcase their vibrant beauty. After about a five-minute ride, we reach the top. From here, trails lead to Yeonjabong Peak and Sinseonbong Peaks, offering further exploration. A short, ten-minute walk along the path will take you to the Observatory.   Naejangsan Mountain attracts over one million visitors every year, with around 35%, mostly 350,000 people, visiting during the fall alone. To accommodate demand, Naejangsan Cable Cars operate every 20 minutes during the off-peak season and more frequently in the autumn peak. Please be aware that wait times may be longer during the fall, as many come to view Naejangsan Mountain’s famous foliage. Vehicle access is restricted in the park during the autumn season, so we suggest taking a shuttle bus or walking from the parking lot to the cable car station.

stories.title: Seoraksan National Park
stories.script: Seoraksan National Park  Do you know the third-highest mountain in South Korea after Hallasan Mountain and Jirisan Mountain? It’s Seoraksan Mountain, located within Seoraksan National Park. The “Seol” (雪) in Seoraksan means “snow,” and it’s said that snow falling around Chuseok (Korean Thanksgiving) doesn’t melt until June. Another explanation is that the mountain’s white rocks resemble snow.  Jirisan Mountain is praised for its majestic, earthy ridges; Juwangsan Mountain for its dramatic rock formations and sheer cliffs. Odaesan’s Sogeumgang River for its beautiful valleys with flowing streams. Seoraksan Mountain is said to be a renowned mountain that embodies the distinct features of all these three mountains. For this reason, people often refer to Seoraksan Mountain as the most scenic among mountains.  Designated as the fifth national park in Korea, Seoraksan Mountain is beloved for its beauty in all four seasons. In spring, azaleas and royal azaleas are in full bloom, painting the entire mountain pink. In summer, the lush green foliage and the cool canyons create a breathtaking view. In autumn, fiery red fall foliage glows between the boulders, in winter, snow covers the mountain, creating a fairytale-like scene.  In addition to its vibrant flora, Seoraksan National Park features numerous valleys like Cheonbuldong Valley and Baekdamgyegok Valley, along with twenty-eight waterfalls, including Biryong Falls and Daeseung Falls. The park also features uniquely shaped rock formations such as Ulsanbawi Rock and Gongnyong Ridge as well as cultural and historical sites like Sinheungsa Temple and Baekdamsa Temple. These elements give Seoraksan Mountain both geographic and cultural significance.

stories.title: Ulsanbawi Rock of Seoraksan Mountain
stories.script: Ulsanbawi Rock of Seoraksan Mountain  Seoraksan Mountain is known as the “beauty among mountains” for its stunning views, featuring the famous Ulsanbawi Rock formation.  Seoraksan Ulsanbawi Rock showcases uniquely shaped stones arranged like a natural stone backdrop along the mountain slopes. With six peaks and a circumference of about 4 km, Ulsanbawi Rock is a magnificent sight. If you come and see Seoraksan Ulsanbawi Rock, you’ll be amazed by the variety in shape and scale of each rock formation.  Ulsanbawi Rock is also famous for its scenery, wrapping around Sokcho like a natural screen and facing Seoraksan Mountain. From the summit, you can enjoy breathtaking views of Daecheongbong Peak, Hwachaen Ridge, and the surrounding landscapes, including the East Sea and Sokcho city at a glance.  Seoraksan Ulsanbawi Rock is steeped in legend. One story tells that the Heavenly God gathered mountain peaks at Geumgangsan Mountain to create the most scenic place. However, the large and heavy Ulsanbawi Rock arrived late. Instead of returning to its hometown in Ulsan, it chose to settle on Seoraksan Mountain, where it remains to this day as Ulsanbawi Rock.  The hike to Seoraksan Ulsanbawi Rock begins at Sokcho’s Sogongwon Park, passing by Sinheungsa Temple and Heundeulbawi Rock. The round trip takes about four hours and is relatively challenging, so it may be difficult for children or the elderly.

stories.title: Seoraksan Cable Cars
stories.script: Seoraksan Cable Cars  In the past, large mountains in Korea were referred to as “Aksan.” Representative examples include Gwanaksan Mountain in Seoul, Wolaksan Mountain in Chungju, and Seoraksan Mountain in Sokcho. Seoraksan Mountain has relatively challenging trails, making it difficult for children and the elderly to hike. Fortunately, there is an ideal way for everyone to enjoy the scenic beauty of Seoraksan Mountain, and it is the Seoraksan cable cars.  From the Seoraksan Cable Car station at Sogongwon Park in Seoraksan National Park, you can reach Gwongeumseong Fortress, located 700 meters above sea level, in just about ten minutes. While the cable cars provide a faster alternative to climbing the mountain, only round-trip tickets are available; one-way tickets are not offered.  Shall we take the Seoraksan Cable Car up to Gwongeumseong Fortress? After purchasing your round-trip ticket, join the line and board the cable car. Once inside, the scenic views of Seoraksan Mountain unfold before you. Enjoy the harmony of the mountains and rocks, the massive Ulsanbawi Rock with its six peaks, the clear sky, and even the sea in the distance. Time flies as you take in the breathtaking scenery, and before you know it, the cable car comes to a stop. After exiting, head up the stairs toward Gwongeumseong Fortress, where the beacon platform comes into view. At the summit, be amazed by grand ridges and uniquely shaped rock formations on Seoraksan Mountain.  The Seoraksan Cable Car offers a convenient way to enjoy the beauty of Seoraksan Mountain, making it popular among visitors. Due to this convenience, many visitors come on weekends, holidays, and especially during the autumn foliage season. It’s a good idea to arrive early during these times, as there may be long queues and waiting times.

stories.title: Chiaksan National Park
stories.script: Chiaksan National Park  Chiaksan Mountain extends southward from Korea’s Taebaeksan Mountain Range into Wonju-si. Known as the symbol of Wonju-si, Chiaksan Mountain was originally called Jeokaksan Mountain (赤嶽山) because its foliage turns the entire mountain red in autumn. The current name, Chiaksan Mountain (雉岳山), originates from a legend in which a scholar traveling to take his civil service exam saved a pheasant from a snake. Later, the pheasant returned to repay the scholar’s kindness, and the mountain was named Chiak, with Chi (雉) meaning “pheasant.”  Chiaksan Mountain offers much more than its legends and autumn colors. It’s home to temples like Sangwonsa Temple, associated with the grateful pheasant legend, and Guryongsa Temple, which houses the Bogwangru Pavilion, a designated cultural heritage of Gangwon-do There is also striking natural sights, such as Sadari Byeongchang, a ladder-like cliff, streams cascading from Yeongwon Falls and Seryeom Falls, and the towering peaks of Hyangrobong, Tugubong, and Birobong Peak. Each season interprets beauty in its own way, spring offers azaleas, summer brings lush pine forests and cool streams, autumn paints the mountain in vibrant foliage, and winter’s snowscape is breathtaking.  Chiaksan National Park provides various hiking trails, each starting at an information center where visitors can check weather updates and essential safety information. The trail from the Geumdae Branch Office (Visit Support Center) to Namdaebong Course is the closest to downtown Wonju. It is highly recommended for first time visitors to Chiaksan Mountain because they can climb the Namdaebong Peak, the highest peak at the southern end of Chiaksan Mountain, while stopping by Sangwonsa Temple.

stories.title: Juwangsan National Park
stories.script: Juwangsan National Park  Korea has three majors Rocky Mountains, namely Seoraksan Mountain, Wolchulsan Mountain, and Juwangsan Mountain, which was designated as the 12th national park. Located in Cheongsong-gun and Yeongdeok-gun, Gyeongsangbuk-do, Juwangsan National Park spans a unique area rich in history and natural beauty.  Formed by lava flows that solidified around seventy million years ago, Juwangsan National Park offers a unique landscape. Its natural attractions include valleys like Jubanggyegok Valley, Jeolgolgyegok Valley, waterfalls such as Yongchu Falls, Jenggu Falls, Dalgi Falls, and caves including Yeonhwagul Cave, Mujanggul Cave, and Juwanggul Cave. Besides, the mountain features many uniquely shaped rock formations and peaks, making the hike up both scenic and enjoyable.  Giam Cliff, an iconic symbol of Juwangsan Mountain, rises majestically at the park’s entrance, resembling a tall monument. According to legend, during the Silla Dynasty, a man named Zhu Do fled from the Tang Dynasty after a failed rebellion and claimed to be Zhu Wang. When his deception was uncovered, the Tang Dynasty requested Silla’s help to capture him. General Mailseong of Silla apprehended Zhu Do in the Juwanggul Cave and marked the victory by planting a flag on the most visible boulder, now known as Giam Cliff, the symbol of Juwangsan Mountain.  Juwangsan National Park, with its majestic Giam Cliff and accessible trails, is especially popular in autumn, drawing around 70% of its annual visitors during the fall foliage season. With 70% of visitors coming in the fall, Juwangsan's autumn beauty is widely renowned. There are various trails to enjoy, including the 6.8 km Jubangcheon course that takes about three hours, the 12.5 km Jeolgol course taking six hours, and the 9.4 km Janggunbong course taking five hours. Choose a trail that suits your pace and immerse yourself in the stunning autumn beauty of Juwangsan Mountain!

stories.title: Balwangsan Cable Car and Gi Skywalk
stories.audioTitle: Balwangsan Cable Car and Gi Skywalk
stories.script: Balwangsan Mountain is a mountain as high as 1,458 meters above sea level located in Gangwon-do. In winter, it snows a lot so many skiers visit this place. It is the 12th highest mountain in Korea, but people can go to the top easily by a cable car.  The cable car, operated by Yong Pyong Resort, is as long as 7.4 kilometers. It goes up and down along the ridge of Balwangsan Mountain, allowing you to enjoy not only the landscape but thrills. You can feast your eyes for all seasons with colorful flowers in spring, lush greenery in summer, multi-hued fall foliage in autumn, and white snowflakes in winter.  To feel the nature of Pyeongchang, it is enough to look around the landscape of Balwangsan Mountain on a cable car, however, if you want to feel the energy of Balwangsan Mountain, walk on the Gi Skywalk where you can get fresh energy. After you get off the cable car, you can conveniently move to the Gi Skywalk through the elevator. It is a tourist facility least restrictive for the vulnerable such as persons with disabilities and the elderly.  The center of the Gi Skywalk, there is a turn table that turns 360 degrees, which lets visitors appreciate the breathtaking view of Baekdudaegan Mountain Range from all directions just in one spot. If the weather is clear, you can even see out to the sea of Gangneung. It is also the point from which you can enjoy not only the sunrise from the east sea but also the sunset to the west mountain.  When you stand on the Gi Skywalk, it feels as if you are filled with healthy energy from the mountain stretching beneath your feet and from the sky above you.  After filling yourself with energy, follow the forest trail to the top of Balwangsan Mountain. There are three major Gi Trails, such as Baraemgil Trail, Balwangsu Garden Deck Road, and Jumok Healing Forest Trail, all neat with wooden decks. Walk slowly along the landscape and enjoy nature. On the way, you will see the rest area where you can rest and drink Balwangsu, cool mineral water, to quench your thirst.  When you buy the cable car ticket, present your digital tourist identification card to get 30% discount.

stories.title: The National Museum of Korea
stories.script: The National Museum of Korea is located in Yongsan Family Park, Seoul, and it is the museum that represents the Korea. Since moving to Yongsan in 2005, it has been receiving great attention and love from many people, with high-quality exhibitions spanning both the past and the present, and a collection of 420,000 artifacts. The museum continues to grow day by day. The National Museum of Korea consists of six permanent exhibition halls, each presenting exhibits organized by era and theme. In addition, the museum features special exhibition halls showcasing a variety of topics, as well as exhibition commentary programs designed to help visitors better understand the displays. The Children's Museum offers a hands-on learning experience, allowing young visitors to engage with the exhibits in an interactive way. The museum also includes an outdoor exhibition space, where various stone relics, such as stone pagodas, are displayed in the museum's garden. To create high-quality exhibitions, the museum is committed to several key areas, including the collection and preservation of artifacts, academic research, and educational programs. Furthermore, with a strong foundation in Korean cultural identity, the museum actively participates in international exchanges with countries around the world.

stories.title: Ttukseom Hangang Park
stories.script: Ttukseom Hangang Park, located in Gwangjin-gu, Seoul, is one of the city's most iconic spots for relaxation. The park offers a variety of spaces, including a riverside plaza, a rose garden, and a children's playground. However, the first thing that catches your eye as you enter the park is Jabeolle, a unique and multifunctional cultural space that resembles a caterpillar.   The “Jabeolle” is a 243-meter-long structure that is cylindrical in shape, inspired by the form of a caterpillar. It is conveniently connected to Jayang Station on Subway Line 7, providing easy access to Ttukseom Hangang Park. Inside the park, you can find a café, a gift shop, and exhibitions showcasing works by media artists, creating a leisurely atmosphere to enjoy the view of the Hangang River.   From the riverside plaza, you can take in stunning views of the Han River and the Seoul cityscape. It's the perfect place for a relaxing walk with friends, family, or loved ones while enjoying the cool breeze from the river. In the summer, the area is also popular for water sports like windsurfing and water skiing.   Ttukseom Hangang Park offers a range of attractions and activities throughout the year. Every summer, it opens an outdoor swimming pool, and in winter, there’s a sledding hill. There is also a bike rental station, allowing visitors to enjoy a refreshing ride along the river’s bike paths.   In addition, the park features various facilities, such as an X-Games park, an artificial rock-climbing wall, and a ferry dock. With its distinct charm throughout the seasons, Ttukseom Hangang Park offers a special urban retreat. Why not experience this wonderful space and take a break from the hustle and bustle of the city?

stories.title: Nanji Hangang Park
stories.script: Nanji Han River Park is located in Mapo-gu, Seoul. It is a newly revitalized and attractive waterfront park that created through the Hangang River Renaissance Project. The park has become even more accessible and convenient for visitors, thanks to the central connecting bridge and the Peace Park bridge, which link it to Noeul Park and Sky Park.   At Nanji Hangang River Park, visitors can enjoy a harmonious blend of nature and leisure, with a variety of experiences to explore. One of the park’s most notable features is the Mirror Fountain, located in the front of the Peace Park bridge. When the water jets shoot into the sky, they create a beautiful scene like a rainbow with seven colors, offering a special sight to those who visit the park.  If you want to feel the breath of nature, head to the Wetland Eco-Park. At the Wetland Eco-Park, you can walk along the pedestrian bridge and encounter natural meadows, plant colonies, and a variety of animals living near the water's edge. In the summer, a safe riverfront water play area with a depth of 80cm opens up, allowing families to create unforgettable and refreshing memories together. If you enjoy camping, be sure to visit the Nanji Campground. You can enjoy a barbecue while camping, which is why it is loved by many locals.   If you want to ride a bike, try using the park's bicycle paths. To the east, the path leads all the way to Ttukseom Park, and to the west, it stretches to the southern end of Haengju Bridge in Goyang City, making it a great route to enjoy the scenic views of the Hangang River while cycling.

stories.title: Banpo Hangang Park
stories.script: Banpo Hangang Park, located in Seocho-gu, Seoul, stretches along the Hangang River between Banpo Bridge, Hannam Bridge, and Dongjak Bridge. The park is one of the iconic waterfront parks in Seoul, newly revitalized through the Hangang River Renaissance Project. Banpo Hangang River Park is known for its beautiful landmarks, including the famous Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, along with a variety of playgrounds and sports facilities. Let’s explore more about Banpo Hangang River Park!   The Moonlight Rainbow Fountain at Banpo Hangang River Park is the longest bridge fountain in the world. It is installed on both sides of Banpo Bridge which stretches a total length of 1,140 meters, and was even listed in the Guinness World Records in 2008 as the longest bridge fountain globally. Especially at night, over 200 lights illuminate the fountain, creating a fantastic spectacle with a rainbow of colors. From the Moonlight Plaza at the center of the park, visitors can enjoy both the beautiful fountain and the night views of the Hangang River.   Another must-see in the area is the artificial islands surrounding the park: Some Sevit and Seoraeseom Island. Some Sevit is the world’s first set of floating artificial islands which designed to stay afloat on the water. It serves as a complex cultural space with an outdoor stage and other facilities. Seoraeseom Island, connected to Banpo Hangang River Park, is particularly scenic in every season, with fields of canola flowers and buckwheat flowers creating a breathtaking view. In spring and fall, the island hosts the Canola Flower Festival and Buckwheat Flower Festival, attracting many visitors.   The diversity of attractions at Banpo Hangang River Park is endless. In addition to its well-maintained bike paths and walking trails, the park offers various sports facilities, including football fields and basketball courts. Whether it’s enjoying the enchanting night view of the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, the beautiful scenery of Seoraeseom Island, or taking part in various activities with the cool river breeze, Banpo Hangang River Park offers a perfect opportunity to fully experience the charm of the Han River.

stories.title: Olympic Park
stories.script: Olympic Park, located in Songpa-gu, Seoul, is a space where the spirit of the 1988 Seoul Olympics lives on, offering a place for sports, culture, and leisure for Seoul's citizens. Olympic Park was built and completed on a vast area of about 430,000 square meters in 1986 to host the Asian Games and the 1988 Seoul Olympics.  At the heart of the park is Mongchontoseong Earthen Fortification, an ancient Baekje-era fortress. Here, visitors can explore historical sites such as pit houses and dolmen tombs. The nearby Seoul Baekje Museum displays artifacts excavated from Mongchontoseong Earthen Fortification, offering a deeper dive into the region's history. Around this fortress, six sports venues are arranged in a semicircular shape, beautifully blending the past and present.  Some of the Olympic venues from the 1988 Seoul Olympics have been transformed into new spaces. The gymnastics venue has been converted into the KSPO Dome, the fencing venue into the SK Handball Arena, and the weightlifting venue into the Woori Financial Art Hall. These venues have been remodeled to accommodate various events. Not only the sports, but also concerts and exhibitions, making them multi-functional spaces loved by citizens for cultural activities.  The charm of Olympic Park doesn't end there. It also houses a Sculpture Park, featuring works from 191 artists across 98 countries. Walking through the park, visitors can encounter famous sculptures from around the world. It’s also a great place to appreciate various sculptures that commemorate the Olympics. In addition, the park has spacious green lawns, the 88 Plaza, and picnic areas, providing the perfect setting for a relaxed family outing.  Moreover, due to its stunning scenery, Olympic Park is frequently used as a filming location for commercials and movies. How about embarking on a special journey through time at Seoul Olympic Park, which is conveniently located in the city center and easily accessible by subway or public transportation?

stories.title: Yetteo Folk Museum
stories.script: The Yetteo Folk Museum, located in Daejeon, was established to rediscover and preserve Korea’s precious traditional culture while contributing to the cultural and artistic development of the Daejeon area. The museum was opened in 2001, designated as Daejeon's fourth private museum. As a folk museum, it aims to collect, preserve, and exhibit Korea's rapidly disappearing traditional culture.   The museum displays a variety of artifacts that showcase the lives and culture of our ancestors. Visitors can see everything from jewelry, old paintings, and rare books to folk crafts, earthenware, ceramics, stone carvings, and antique furniture. It offers a comprehensive view of traditional Korean life in one place and operates year-round. Therefore, visitors can visit at any time.   Stepping into the outdoor exhibition area, you’ll find traditional tools like stone statues, grinding stones, stone mills, and other old daily implements. This space serves as a living learning experience for children, allowing them to see and learn about historical tools firsthand.   One of the museum's highlights is its variety of traditional culture experience programs. Visitors can directly engage with practices such as natural dyeing, hanji (Korean paper) crafts, knotting, and domestic crafts. These hands-on activities help visitors develop a deeper connection with Korea’s traditional culture. The museum also holds an annual special exhibition, presenting its collection from new perspectives to raise the cultural awareness of its audience. Additionally, the museum offers various educational programs, fulfilling its role as a lifelong education space for the citizens of Daejeon.   After visiting the museum, you may take a break at the “Courtyard with a Campfire and the Full Moon in the Sky” lounge, where you can enjoy traditional Korean tea, Korean meals, or Western dishes while experiencing the charm of a traditional hanok (Korean house).   Why not visit the Yetteo Folk Museum to learn, experience, and rediscover the beauty and value of Korea’s traditional culture?

stories.title: Daejeon Observatory
stories.script: Daejeon Observatory is located within the Daedeok Research Complex in Daejeon. It opened in 2001 as the first municipal astronomy center in Korea, welcoming over 100,000 visitors annually. It captivates guests with its diverse facilities and programs related to space and astronomy.   On the third floor, you'll find the observatory, where you can observe both the daytime and nighttime skies using a telescope. During the day, you can observe solar flares and sunspots, while at night, you can view planets, stars, nebulae, and star clusters. Whether you visit during the day or at night, you can observe the captivating view of the universe. Even if you can't do any stargazing, there's no need to be disappointed. On the first floor, the planetarium offers explanations about the constellations of the four seasons, and astronomy-related videos are also shown. Especially in the first-floor hallway, the 'Astro Gallery' art exhibition is taking place, which is something you definitely shouldn’t miss!   The Daejeon Observatory is not just a place for science, but also a hub for culture and the arts. Programs like the “Star Concerts” and “Starlight Poetry Readings” are held weekly. Therefore, make sure to plan your visit to catch one of these events. Additionally, the observatory offers Astronomy Classes for both children and adults. These classes are split into two sessions each year, where participants can learn about astronomy and observe the sky through telescopes.   The observatory is dedicated to sharing the wonders of astronomy and space science with everyone. The Children's Choir of Daejeon Observatory participates in volunteer activities at events in Daejeon and the Daedeok Research Complex. The observatory’s official supporting group, “Starry Sky Playground”, also volunteers at various events. In 2017, the observatory made its facilities more inclusive by installing a ramp in the observatory hall, making it accessible for people with disabilities to enjoy stargazing as well.   How about experiencing the mysteries of the universe at the Daejeon Observatory, where science and art meet in the most brilliant way?

stories.title: KOMSCO Currency Museum of Korea
stories.script: The Korea Minting and Security Printing Corporation (KOMSCO) Currency Museum, located in Daejeon, opened in 1988 as Korea's first museum dedicated to currency. The museum works to preserve and pass on the culture of money by collecting, researching, and displaying materials related to currency, which plays a crucial role in economic activities.   The museum features four permanent exhibition halls, one special exhibition hall, and an educational experience room. Among the collection of approximately 140,000 items, around 4,000 exhibits are displayed by era and type.   In the first exhibition hall, the History of Coins Gallery, visitors can view a thousand years of coin history, from the Goryeo Dynasty's Geonwon Jungbo, Goryeo coin, to the modern coins in circulation today. In the second exhibition hall, the History of Banknotes Gallery, you can explore the evolution of Korean banknotes, along with special exhibits such as a 100 trillion-dollar bill issued by Zimbabwe. The third exhibition hall, the Anti-Counterfeit and Security Features Gallery, offers a unique space where visitors can learn about the advanced techniques used by KOMSCO to combat the increasing sophistication of counterfeit banknotes. The visitors can also discover anti-counterfeiting measures used in currencies from around the world. The fourth exhibition hall, the KOMSCO Gallery, displays various items such as stamps, Christmas seals, commemorative medals, and decorations. Additionally, currency from over 70 countries is exhibited in this space.   The museum also offers a range of educational programs, particularly designed for children to learn about money in a fun and engaging way through various hands-on activities. If you're interested in understanding the history and culture of money, which has shared in both the joys and struggles of our lives, a visit to the KOMSCO Currency Museum would be a great way to explore this fascinating subject.

stories.title: National Science Museum
stories.script: The National Science Museum is located in the Daedeok Research Complex in Daejeon. Serving as a cultural hub for science and technology, the museum is built around the theme of Harmony between Nature, Humanity, and Science. Originally opened in the 1940s in Seoul as the National Museum of Science, it moved to Daejeon in the 1990s and was transformed into its current form.   The National Science Museum offers an exciting and engaging experience of science in everyday life, while also providing a space for in-depth scientific learning. In addition to its diverse exhibitions, the museum offers educational programs, various science-related events, and interactive experiences, giving visitors the chance to immerse themselves in science and technology culture.   Let’s explore the museum in more detail! One of its main attractions is the Science Alive Discovery Center, where visitors can interact with cutting-edge scientific instruments in a theme park-like setting. It’s a fun, hands-on science playground for children and teenagers, while also serving as a place for adults to spend quality time with their families and enjoy new ways of learning together.   Next, the Planetarium features a large hemispherical dome screen where visitors can watch 3D dome movies on a variety of topics.
