It’s an exciting opportunity to explore the stars and the mysteries of the universe in Korea’s first 3D planetarium!   In addition to these attractions, the museum also features the Science and Technology Hall, where you can learn about the history of Korea’s scientific advancements and the Industrial Revolution. The Botanical Garden offers a chance to observe the diverse plants and animals found throughout Korea, while the Natural History Hall allows visitors to discover the evolution of life on Earth.   The National Science Museum also has well-equipped spaces for children. The KkumAty Hall, designed for children under six, allows them to learn science naturally through play. Meanwhile, the Children's Science Museum serves as a science playground centered on the theme of the coexistence of nature, humans, and machines.   Why not visit the National Science Museum, a place where everyone can enjoy learning about science and experience the joy and creativity it offers?

stories.title: Gosangol Dinosaur Park
stories.script: In the Gosangol of Dalseo District, Daegu, there’s a unique park called Gosangol Dinosaur Park. In 2006, fossilized footprints of a herbivorous dinosaur, believed to be from the early Cretaceous period around 100 million years ago, were discovered in the area. The discovery of dinosaur footprints sparked the creation of Gosangol Dinosaur Park is fascinating.  The dinosaur footprints found in Gosangol are approximately 20 to 30 cm in size, with 4 to 5 distinct tracks. These footprints are thought to belong to a herbivorous dinosaur, as evidenced by the three-toed prints. Notably, the discovery also includes ripple marks, a type of fossil typically found along shallow lake shores, as well as mud cracks that form in dry and arid environments. These fossils provide important clues about the natural environment of that time.   After exploring the fossilized dinosaur footprints, you can visit the Dinosaur Park, where life-size models of various dinosaurs await. Among them, the Tyrannosaurus rex, Stegosaurus, and Brachiosaurus are particularly popular and loved by visitors of all ages, so be sure to check them out. Additionally, you’ll find dinosaur eggs and baby dinosaurs scattered throughout the park, offering great photo opportunities at the designated photo zones. For an even more immersive experience, you can use the augmented reality app available through the information boards to watch a vivid video that demonstrates how dinosaur fossils are formed.   Since its opening in 2017, Gosangol Dinosaur Park has quickly become a popular tourist attraction, drawing over a million visitors in just its first year. Why not make a special memory at Gosangol Dinosaur Park, a place full of fun and learning?

stories.title: Daegu National Museum
stories.script: The Daegu National Museum first opened its doors in 1994. It is established to preserve, research, and exhibit the cultural heritage of Daegu and Gyeongsangbuk-do. In 2006, the museum expanded with the addition of a storage facility to the south and the construction of Haesol Hall and a special exhibition hall to the north. Additionally, in 2010, the museum was revamped with new exhibits, including the Ancient Culture Hall, the Medieval Culture Hall, and the Textiles and Clothing Hall, making it a continuously evolving museum.   Now, let’s take a closer look at the museum’s highlights. First, in the Ancient Culture and Medieval Culture halls, you can explore the cultural heritage of different eras. The museum showcases artifacts from the Paleolithic period to the Joseon Dynasty. You can learn about the earliest human cultures in the Paleolithic era, the cultures of Silla and Gaya during the Three Kingdoms period, and the culture of the Joseon Dynasty, which was based on Confucian ideals. The exhibits offer a fascinating journey through the diverse cultures that shaped Korea’s history.   Next, let’s explore the newly opened Textiles and Clothing Hall, which replaces the former Folk Hall. This exhibition offers a unique focus on Daegu’s history, highlighting how the city's rise as a modern industrial center was largely driven by its textile and clothing industry. In this hall, you can learn about the evolution of clothing, a fundamental part of our daily lives. It is regularly updated, incorporating both domestic and international materials to create a richer and more diverse display.   The outdoor exhibition area is also filled with fascinating sights. As you walk around the grounds, you’ll encounter Bronze Age dolmens and house sites, pottery kilns from the Three Kingdoms period, and stone pagodas from Unified Silla, among other historical artifacts. In addition, the museum hosts a variety of special and themed exhibitions in its planned exhibition halls, and educational programs are offered at Haesol Hall, making it an enriching experience for all visitors.   Visit the National Daegu Museum and immerse yourself in the vibrant culture and history of Daegu and Gyeongsangbuk-do!

stories.title: Daejeo Eco Park
stories.script: Daejeo Eco Park, located in Gangseo District, Busan, is an ecological park where visitors can enjoy the beauty of nature, which changes with each season. The park stretches along the floodplain from the Nakdong River’s Daejeo Weir to the Gimhae Airport ramp and is part of the Nakdong River Lower Wetland, a designated natural monument near Geupo Bridge.   Daejeo Eco Park is well-developed, featuring a variety of wetlands, waterways, and grasslands, including the expansive Shindeok Wetland. However, the highlight of the park is the canola flower fields, which cover 370,000 square meters. Every April, the park hosts the Canola Flower Festival, drawing countless visitors who come to enjoy the stunning beauty of the vibrant fields in full bloom.   Don’t worry if you miss the spring flowers—the park offers different scenery throughout the year. After the canola flowers bloom and fade, fields of blooming cosmos appear from July to September, and when deep autumn arrives, the pink muhly grass creates a romantic, cloud-like display of pink hues.   In addition to its natural beauty, the park also features a bamboo forest trail near the park’s management office. Created as a nature-friendly leisure space for the public, the bamboo forest has become another iconic attraction in Busan.   At both ends of the park, you’ll find sports facilities like a soccer field and a baseball field, offering opportunities for both exercise and relaxation. Why not visit Daejeo Eco Park, a place with new charms to discover each season?

stories.title: Busan Citizens Park
stories.script: Busan Citizens Park, located in Busanjin District, Busan, is an urban retreat where history, culture, and nature harmoniously blend. The park is organized around five themes, which are the Memory, Culture, Joy, Nature, and Participation. At its center is Hayaria Lawn Square, which is six times the size of a soccer field, surrounded by around 970,000 trees. The park also features the Park History Museum, walking paths, and the Forest of Memory.   Busan Citizens Park was once the site of a U.S. military base called Camp Hayaria. Starting in 1995, there were calls for the area to be returned to the citizens, and after much effort, it was reborn as Busan Citizens Park in 2014. To honor its past, the park chose Memory as one of its five themes. In the Forest of Memory, a tree-lined path was created with plane trees that grew on the former military base, and in the Memory Pillars, old utility poles from the base were repurposed to install solar-powered lights. The Park History Museum, remodeled from the former officers' club at Camp Hayaria, offers a glimpse into the history of the park.   Of course, you can't miss the other themes either! The Five Major Forest Paths, where you can feel the natural beauty of the park, and the 300-meter Metasequoia Path are among the park’s most beautiful walking trails. The forest paths, lined with ginkgo trees, zelkova trees, king cherry trees, and pine trees, create different scenic views with each season. Especially the king cherry tree walk along Bujeon Stream has become a popular spot that many visitors flock to.   In the evening, five 26-meter-high wooden lighting towers around Hayaria Lawn Square light up the park, creating a magical atmosphere. In the Culture and Arts Village, citizens can engage in and enjoy cultural and artistic activities. The Maze Garden is also a great spot for the whole family to have fun together.   How about spending meaningful time with loved ones in Busan Citizens Park, where history, nature, and culture come together?

stories.title: Samnak Eco Park
stories.script: Samrak Eco Park, located in Sasang District, Busan, is the largest ecological park along the Nakdong River estuary. This area, once used for vinyl greenhouse farming, has undergone several rounds of renovation and restoration projects. As a result, it has transformed into a beautiful ecological park with well-preserved natural environments, where migratory birds can stop and rest. The park now offers sports facilities for citizens, walking paths, and a wildflower garden, making it a popular destination for both relaxation and recreation.   Samrak Eco Park is divided into three main sections. The upper and central areas feature sports facilities for citizens. The upper section also includes a vast natural grassland with reed and willow clusters, along with walking paths. The lower section is home to reed wetlands and feeding grounds where migratory birds can stop by.   As an ecological park, Samrak Eco Park serves as a habitat for a variety of species. The Eomgung Wetland is an important wintering site for migratory birds, while the canal-shaped wetland provides a habitat for various bird species and blooms with flowers throughout the four seasons. One of the most interesting features is the habitat of the endangered species, narrow-mouthed toad (Classified as endangered level 2), which can be found in the park! Isn’t that fascinating? From June to August every year, you can hear the croaking sounds of the tree frogs, making this park an excellent spot for natural ecological education.   In addition, at the Gamjeon Wildflower Garden, you can see over 70 species of wildflowers, and at the Samrak Wetland Eco Center, there are lotus flower gardens, reed experience zones, and water reed colonies. The park is also equipped with bike paths, walking trails, and facilities for water sports, offering a perfect combination of health and relaxation.   How about spending a fun and educational time with your loved ones in Samrak Eco Park, where the breath of nature is alive and thriving?

stories.title: Igidae Cliff Park
stories.script: Igidae Cliff, located in Yongho-dong, Nam-gu, Busan, is a coastal rocky area with an attractive walking trail where you can observe the beautiful coastal landforms. Around 80 million years ago, volcanic activity at the end of the Cretaceous period created layers of lava, volcanic ash, and pyroclastic flows, forming various volcanic and sedimentary rock strata in this area. Over time, these natural landforms were shaped by wave erosion, creating dramatic coastal features such as sea cliffs, wave-cut platforms, and sea caves. Thanks to its geological value, Igidae Cliff has been designated as a part of the Busan National Geopark.   The name Igidae comes from the legend that two courtesans were buried here. According to the story, during the Imjin War, after the Japanese forces captured Suyeongseong Fortress, a celebration feast was held, and the two courtesans, drunk with the Japanese generals, fell into the water and met a heroic death. Additionally, Igidae Cliff was opened to the public in 1993, and it now contains a lush forest, which is rare to find in urban areas, as well as a habitat for various wildlife.   If you visit Igidae Cliff, you cannot miss the Igidae Cliff Coastal Walking Trail. This trail extends along the beautiful coastline, continuing all the way to Oryukdo Islets. The total length of the trail is 4.7 kilometers, and as you walk, you’ll be able to enjoy diverse geological and landform landscapes, such as the Guri Mine, Dolgae Hole, Horse Tail Structure, and the Cambrian Rock Formation.   As you walk along the coastal trail in Igidae Cliff Park, take in the breathtaking view of the blue sea and feel the sea breeze against your face. Walking amidst the unique, natural rock formations, you might find that your worries fade away as you marvel at the grandeur of nature.

stories.title: Oryundae Observatory
stories.script: The Oryundae Observatory, located at the summit of Bueongsan in Geumjeong-gu, Busan, is about a 20-minute walk from Oryunsaenae Village, also known as Suwonji Village.   The name Oryundae is derived from a story about five elderly men who, having mastered the Five Relations (a Confucian ethical principle), planted their walking sticks and sat together to admire the view. Perhaps because of this, the scenery from Oryundae Observatory truly lives up to its name, offering a breathtaking panorama. From the observatory, you can see the entire view of Hoedong Reservoir, Ttangmoesan Mountain, and Hoedong Lake, which is said to resemble the shape of the Korean Peninsula. On clear days, you can even catch a distant view of Haeundae Beach and Jangsan. Doesn’t it sound tempting to visit and experience the stunning scenery for yourself?   As there are also several other attractions around Oryundae Observatory, which centered around Hoedong Reservoir, it’s recommended visiting them together. You can take a stroll along the Hoedong Reservoir trail, or relax along the Hwangto Trail, Earth Trail, and the evergreens of the Ttangmoesan Mountain Hwangto Forest Path. Additionally, you can enjoy beautiful natural vistas from the Hoedongho Nuri Bridge, which connects the Geumjeong-Hoedong Lake Trail with the Ahope Mountain Walk. Finally, the Ecological Exploration Trail offers the Bamboo Grove Trail and the Belly Fat Measuring Station, providing both interesting and scenic experiences.   How about visiting Oryundae Observatory, where fascinating stories and beautiful views come together, and feeling the emotions of the five elderly men who once gazed at the scenery from this very spot?

stories.title: Jakcheonjeong Valley
stories.script: Jakcheonjeong Valley, located in Ulsan Uljugun, is a place where clear water flowing down from Ganwolsan Mountain, 1,083 meters above sea level, combines with dramatic rock formations to create a breathtaking scenery. Known also as Jakgwaecheon Stream, the name comes from the unusual and beautiful appearance of the hundreds of boulders, which resemble wine glasses hanging in clusters.  The valley’s biggest charm lies in its unique terrain. The fast-flowing water carves deep, jar-shaped potholes into large rocks, creating a mysterious and captivating landscape. On the wide stones, you can find pools of water, while clear water flows below, forming natural water slides, making it an ideal place for water play during the summer.   Alongside the valley stands Jakcheonjeong Pavilion, which was built in the 20th year of King Sejong's reign. The pavilion offers a perfect spot to enjoy the scenic beauty created by the clear waters and white rocks. It is said that during his exile, the loyal minister Jeong Mong-ju of the Goryeo Dynasty once sat at this pavilion, gazing at the view and composing poetry. As a result, nearby is a rock called Moendae, which commemorates Jeong Mong-ju.   However, Jakcheonjeong Valley was not just a place for leisure and poetic enjoyment. It was also where plans for the March 1st Movement were made, and during the Japanese invasions of Korea, many righteous soldiers sacrificed their lives here. It is also historically significant as the place where Cheondoism and Catholicism first entered the Ulsan region, functioning as an open-air church at one point. Jakcheonjeong Valley, therefore, is not only a site of natural beauty but also one rich in historical and cultural significance.   How about visiting Jakcheonjeong Valley, a place where beautiful natural landscapes and historically meaningful sites come together?

stories.title: Naewonamgyegok Valley
stories.script: Naewonamgyegok Valley, located in Daewoonsan Mountain in Ulju-gun, Ulsan, is one of the 12 Scenic Wonders of Ulsan. This refreshing valley is known for its crystal-clear waters that flow year-round. Together with Daewoonsan Mountain, Naewonamgyegok Valley enhances the beauty of the area with its breathtaking features, including waterfalls such as Aegiso Waterfall and Gusiso, which decorate the mountain landscape. The hiking trail along the valley is gentle, making it an ideal destination for family outings.   As part of the 12 Scenic Wonders of Ulsan, Naewonamgyegok Valley boasts stunning views in all seasons. In spring, the valley and mountains are painted vibrant pink by blooming azaleas, and the Daeunsan Mountain Royal Azalea Festival is held during this time. In summer, the lush forests provide a perfect backdrop for enjoying water activities with family and friends. In autumn, the fiery colors of fall foliage blend with the valley’s rugged rock formations, offering a unique contrast to the spring and summer scenery. Even in winter, the snow-covered valley creates a picturesque, serene wonderland.   The valley is home to Naewonam Temple, an ancient temple from which it derives its name. Naewonam Temple is considered one of the most auspicious sites in the Yeongnam region. It is said that the great monk Wonhyo conducted his final meditations here during the Silla Dynasty. A visit to Naewonam Temple, which holds a millennium of history alongside the valley, is highly recommended.   As you explore the valley, you’ll also come across the entrance to the Ulsan Arboretum. This arboretum features various themed gardens, including a bamboo garden and a camellia garden, providing visitors with opportunities to enjoy a variety of forest experiences.   Why not indulge in the tranquil beauty of Naewonamgyegok Valley and let nature refresh your spirit throughout all four seasons?

stories.title: Myeongseondo Island
stories.script: Myeongseondo Island is a small and uninhabited island floating off the coast of Jinha Beach, which is located in Ulju-gun, Ulsan. While it may seem like an ordinary deserted island during the day, Myeongseondo Island transforms into a magical space at night, captivating visitors with its enchanting charm.   The name Myeongseondo Island holds two meanings. Originally, the name translates to the island where cicadas chirp, with myeong meaning chirping and seon referring to cicadas. However, its modern interpretation is the island where divine beings descended to play, with myeong meaning renowned and seon referring to immortal beings. Isn’t it fascinating that one name holds two distinct meanings?   Living up to its name as an island where fairies once played, this small islet transforms into a dazzling spectacle at night, evoking the ethereal beauty of Pandora from the movie Avatar. Using its natural surroundings as a canvas, the island showcases media art installations that mimic waves lapping against the rocks and waterfalls cascading down the cliffs. These features are enhanced by vibrant, multicolored lights, creating a truly magical and mesmerizing landscape.   While Myeongseondo Island is breathtaking from afar, visitors can experience its charm up close during low tide via a temporary floating bridge. However, access is restricted to designated trails, and extra caution is advised, particularly at night.   Nearby, Jinha Beach further enhances the appeal of the area. With its shallow waters and gentle waves, it’s an ideal spot for swimming and various water activities. The beach is bordered by a serene pine forest, filling the air with a refreshing scent that enriches the experience. During the summer, visitors can also enjoy windsurfing and other exciting water sports.   Why not create unforgettable memories by enjoying the refreshing sea during the day and marveling at the magical night view of Myeongseondo Island?

stories.title: Oktokki Space Center
stories.script: The Oktokki Space Center, is located in Ganghwa-gun, Incheon, is Korea's first space science theme park, blending space exploration, dinosaurs, and robots into one fascinating experience. As a space science-themed park and cultural complex, it is especially designed to provide engaging educational and hands-on experiences for children.   The unique architecture of the center is eye-catching. It features a spiral-shaped structure inspired by the concept of a space airport and the body of a dinosaur. The Oktokki Space Center is divided into the Space Science Museum and an outdoor theme park, each offering its own exciting attractions.   In the Space Science Museum, visitors can explore humanity’s journey toward space and the history of aerospace technology through interactive exhibits. What makes it truly special are the immersive space experiences it offers. From Cyber in Space, where you can feel the resistance of zero gravity like astronauts, to the futuristic Space Elevator and the thrilling G-Force that simulates gravitational acceleration, kids can indulge their curiosity about space in fun and memorable ways. Additionally, the 3D theater presents exciting films, while the crafting zone lets visitors create unique items like custom star constellation necklaces.   The outdoor theme park offers even more adventure. Stroll through the Dinosaur Forest, where 63 life-sized dinosaurs move and roar, or cool off at the Water Cannon Park. There’s also the Logos Garden, featuring sculptures inspired by Greek and Roman mythology, providing a touch of classic elegance amidst the fun.   With its wide variety of attractions and activities, the Oktokki Space Center is an ideal destination for curious kids and their families to embark on an exciting space-themed adventure. Why not ignite your child’s imagination and love for science with a visit to this unique park?

stories.title: Sangmu Citizen’s Park
stories.script: Sangmu Citizen’s Park, located in the Sangmu New Town Civic Park area of Seo-gu, Gwangju, is a serene and cultural oasis amidst the bustling city. Conveniently situated within a residential apartment complex, the park spans over 170,000 square meters and features a harmonious blend of an artificial lake, plazas, sports facilities, and a stunning sculpture park, making it a vibrant cultural space for everyone.   The highlight of the park is the Sangmu Sculpture Park, set along the lakeside. This unique outdoor gallery showcases 22 sculptures created by 18 artists in 2000. Installed under the theme of “Human Park,” the sculptures reflect themes of environment, space, and local culture. What makes this collection special is its interactive nature; most of the sculptures are designed to be touched or climbed on, making them particularly enjoyable for families with children. This combination of viewing pleasure and hands-on fun adds a distinctive charm to the park. At night, illuminated sculptures create a magical, entirely different atmosphere.   Beyond the sculpture park, Sangmu Citizen’s Park offers various sports facilities. Visitors can enjoy soccer on the expansive athletic field with a running track or play tennis and badminton at the well-maintained courts. These amenities provide ample opportunities for healthy leisure activities for locals and visitors alike.   Why not visit Sangmu Citizen’s Park to experience art, nature, and an active lifestyle in one convenient and urban location? It’s a perfect spot to unwind, explore creativity, and enjoy quality time outdoors.

stories.title: Gwangju Arboretum
stories.script: Gwangju Arboretum, is located in Nam-gu, Gwangju, boasts a unique origin story. Unlike most arboretums, which are established in naturally beautiful areas, this arboretum was created by planting trees and restoring the ecological environment on a site that once served as a large-scale sanitary landfill.   Gwangju Arboretum, is opened in October 2023, features attractions such as an exhibition greenhouse, a Korean traditional garden, a grassy plaza, and a flower garden. The exhibition greenhouse is home to over 170 species of tropical plants, including mango, papaya, golden lotus banana, and guava. Its vibrant flowers and foliage make it a perfect spot for capturing memorable photos. In autumn, the Kochia plants surrounding the greenhouse turn a vivid red, creating a striking landscape. Visitors can also experience the serene beauty of the Korean traditional garden or enjoy quality time with family on the spacious grassy plaza. The themed gardens, including the flower garden and the sensory garden, offer diverse seasonal landscapes.   What sets the Gwangju Arboretum apart is its role as more than just a place for relaxation. It serves as an urban nature learning center, allowing visitors to observe a wide variety of rare plants up close and participate in various plant-related programs. Transformed from a neglected site into a beautiful sanctuary for rest and learning, the Gwangju Arboretum invites you to enjoy a tranquil escape within the city.

stories.title: Daegeumgulgul Cave
stories.script: Daegeumgul Cave, is located in Samcheok-si, Gangwon-do, is one of the major caves in the Daei-ri Cave Area, alongside Hwanseongul Cave and Gwaneumgul Cave. These caves are estimated to be around 500 million years old, holding a profound sense of natural history and mystery.   Daegeumgul Cave itself is particularly fascinating, having taken four years to discover and an additional three years to prepare for public access. The cave's entrance wasn’t initially visible, but visitors to the area often reported a curious vibration beneath their feet. This prompted extensive exploration, eventually revealing a massive underground chamber with cascading waterfalls.   Inside the cave, you’ll find stunning formations such as stalactites, stalagmites, and stone pillars, all beautifully preserved. The cave’s name, Daegeumgul, meaning Golden Cave, comes from the golden-hued stalactites that line its walls, creating a dazzling subterranean landscape. A flowing stream winds its way through the cave, accompanied by natural wonders like the majestic Biryongpokpo Falls and Cheonjiyeonpokpo Falls, said to resemble the iconic Heaven Lake on Baekdusan Mountain. These features, along with smaller waterfalls and serene lakes, make the cave a truly enchanting sight.   Visitors can reach Daegeumgul Cave via a monorail, and tickets must be booked online at least a day in advance to secure a spot according to the departure schedule. Exploring the cave takes about an hour, offering a remarkable opportunity to immerse yourself in its inspiring underground world.   Why not take a journey to Daegeumgul Cave to experience the grandeur of its golden landscapes, flowing waters, and hidden treasures? It’s a magical encounter with nature’s artistry deep beneath the earth.

stories.title: Gyeongpohaebyeon Beach
stories.script: Gyeongpohaebyeon Beach, is located in Gangneung of Gangwon-do, is a must-visit destination along the East Coast of Korea. It attracts visitors year-round, offering a perfect mix of activities for every season. In summer, it transforms into a vibrant water park where people of all ages enjoy swimming, while in winter, it becomes a peaceful retreat for strolls along the beautiful winter seascape.   The beach stretches for 1.8 km with an average water depth of 2 meters, making it ideal for families and swimmers. The gentle slope of the beach ensures that it's a safe and enjoyable spot for sunbathing, beach games, and water sports during the summer. Visitors can rent parasols, tubes, and other beach gear, while enjoying the fresh sea breeze and the soft, white sands. Surrounding the beach, a forest of pine trees creates a serene atmosphere, perfect for a relaxing walk or a calming forest bath.   Even beyond the summer months, Gyeongpohaebyeon Beach is a fantastic destination. Walking along the shore, you'll experience the vastness of the sea and a refreshing sense of tranquility. The beach is also renowned for its stunning sunrises, drawing many to watch the red sun rise over the horizon. The surrounding cafes offer a perfect spot to relax and take in the view of the sea.   In addition to the beach, there are several nearby attractions worth visiting. Only 1 km away, you’ll find Gyeongpodae Pavilion and Gyeongpoho Lake, both scenic spots that complement the beauty of the beach. Renting a bike around Gyeongpoho Lake and cycling along the coastline is another great way to explore the area.   With its shining sands, clear blue waters, and a variety of activities, Gyeongpohaebyeon Beach is the perfect place to create unforgettable memories with loved ones.

stories.title: Bobaljae Pass
stories.script: Bobaljae Pass, renowned for its winding roads adorned with vibrant autumn foliage, is located at an elevation of 540 meters, connecting Bobal-ri in Gagok-myeon and Baekja-ri in Yeongchun-myeon. This mountain pass is also a famous driving destination, offering stunning seasonal landscapes throughout the year.   In spring, Bobaljae Pass is covered with a variety of colorful wildflowers, creating a lively and picturesque scene. When autumn comes, the pass transforms into a watercolor painting of vivid red and golden hues, making it an ideal spot for couples and families to enjoy breathtaking views together.   Every year, as the news spreads of the arrival of autumn leaves at Bobaljae Pass, visitors flock to this scenic spot to admire the masterpiece created by the vibrant foliage. The roads often fill with people eager to experience the enchanting natural beauty, turning the pass into a bustling hub of autumn admirers.   At the summit of Bobaljae Pass, there is an observatory where you can take in the breathtaking scenery at a glance. Renowned for its picturesque landscapes, the area attracts numerous photographers eager to capture its beauty. Particularly noteworthy is Sobaeksan Footpath Route 6, Ondal-Pyeonggang Romance Road, which connects Bobaljae Pass to the Yeongchun-myeon office. This trekking course, famous for its stunning autumn foliage, spans approximately 13.8 km and takes around 4 hours to complete.   Towards the latter part of the trail lies Ondal Tourist Site, themed around the legend of General Ondal and Princess Pyeonggang. The site also serves as a filming location for historical dramas, where visitors can wear traditional costumes and take photos.   It is highly recommend visiting Bobaljae Pass to capture beautiful autumn foliage and create cherished travel memories amidst the vibrant colors of fall.

stories.title: Mancheonha Skywalk
stories.script: The Mancheonha Skywalk, located in Danyang-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, is a theme park where you can experience both the beautiful scenery of Danyang and thrilling leisure activities.   At the skywalk observatory on the cliff of the Namhangang River, you can enjoy an exhilarating experience of walking while looking down at the river 100 meters below. The panoramic view of downtown Danyang and the distant Yeonhwabong Peak of the Sobaeksan Mountain are stunning.   At the Mancheonha Skywalk, you can also experience the Mancheonha Zipwire. The Mancheonha Zipwire is an extreme sport where you descend as if flying through the sky using a fixed wire rope. You can feel the refreshing breeze of nature as you descend at high speed. The beauty of the Namhangang River and the surrounding cliffs unfolds like a painting, making it a great memory for those who enjoy thrilling leisure activities.   For those who find the zipwire intimidating, there are other leisure options available, such as the Alpine Coaster. The name might sound a bit unfamiliar, but it is an experience where you ride a monorail along a forest path. It is a leisure activity that anyone, regardless of age, can participate in, which is definitely worth giving it a try.   Additionally, the Mancheonha Slide, the first and longest dry mountain slide in Korea, is a single-rider slide. It is a year-round facility, that you can enjoy it regardless of the season. Doesn't it sound wonderful to enjoy the beautiful forest scenery while sliding down?   At the top of the Mancheonha Skywalk, you can observe the topography of Danyang and the scenic view of the river. You can also see limestone from the Paleozoic era and tuff from the Mesozoic era, so it's worth taking a closer look at the surrounding rocks. Visitors can create wonderful memories at the Mancheonha Skywalk, where they can enjoy both the beauty of Danyang's nature and thrilling leisure activities.

stories.title: Cheonjangho Lake
stories.script: Cheonjangho Lake, located in Cheongyang-gun of Chungcheongnam-do, is an irrigation reservoir filled with clean water for agricultural use. Completed over about seven years starting in 1972, Cheonjangho Lake is recognized as one of Cheongyang's top 10 scenic attractions, thanks to its clear waters and picturesque surrounding landscapes.   Cheonjangho Lake lies at the eastern foothills of Chilgapsan Mountain, and the view of the mountain shrouded in the hazy mist rising from the lake is said to be truly spectacular. Its location along the national highway between Daejeon and Cheongyang also makes it easily accessible.   There’s an interesting legend associated with Cheonjangho Lake. According to the tale, a child living in the area needed to visit a doctor but couldn’t cross the swollen stream. A yellow dragon residing in the lake sacrificed its chance to ascend to the heavens, transforming its body into a bridge to help the child cross. A tiger, moved by this act, became a divine guardian of the village and its people.   The highlight of Cheonjangho Lake is the Cheonjangho Lake Suspension Bridge, a well-known attraction frequently featured in broadcasts. Spanning a remarkable 207 meters, it was the longest suspension bridge in Korea when it opened in 2017. The swaying motion of the bridge offers a thrilling experience, as if riding the legendary yellow dragon.   There are countless ways to enjoy Cheonjangho Lake. In early spring, many visitors come to fish for smelt, and an ecological experience center is also nearby, making it an excellent destination for family outings. Why not create unique memories at the beautiful Cheonjangho Lake?

stories.title: Kohwun Garden
stories.script: Kohwun Garden, located in Cheongyang-gun, Chungcheongnam-do, was established with a slightly unique goal. Unlike other botanical gardens, it aims to harmonize with the existing natural environment rather than being artificially constructed. Since its creation began in 1990, efforts have been made to preserve the natural terrain and minimize environmental damage.   Kohwun Garden opened in 2003, and spans over 110,000 pyeong (approximately 363,000 square meters). It features various gardens, sculpture art installations, a grassy plaza, and even a roller slide. It also actively conducts educational programs for children and contributes to plant conservation and research. The garden serves as an educational nature experience for children and a serene place for adults to stroll and enjoy its diverse gardens.   The garden boasts over 8,000 species of flowers and trees and includes 33 themed gardens, such as the Four Seasons Garden and the Tulip Garden. Be sure to visit the Wildflower Garden, where you can admire wildflowers and sculptures nestled under the pine forest trail. The Four Seasons Garden greets visitors with different flowers and landscapes depending on the time of year.   Additionally, there are 11 enchanting walking trails that follow the flowers and trees, each offering a unique atmosphere and story. Engaging programs like fun plant stories and handkerchief flower dyeing are available for children. The roller slide, which opened in 2010, offers a thrilling ride that lets you view the botanical garden from a new perspective. How about enjoying the harmonious and natural beauty of the flowers blooming at Kohwun Garden that is free from artificiality?

stories.title: Jakcheongyegok Valley
stories.script: Jakcheongyegok Valley, located in Cheongyang-gun, Chungcheongnam-do, is one of the water streams extending from Chilgapsan Mountain. Originating from the mountain, streams like Eoulhacheon River, Jakcheon River, Jicheon River, and Geumgangcheon River carve through the gorges, creating breathtaking scenery. The winding paths of these streams, accompanied by stunning rock formations, are collectively called Jicheongugok, which is the Nine Scenic Valleys of Jicheon River.   Another name for Jakcheongyegok Valley is Kkachinaegyegok Valley. Flowing along the southern side of Chilgapsan Mountain, Jicheongugok passes through Gaegok-ri and Jakcheon-ri in Daechi-myeon, as well as Jicheon-ri in Jangpyeong-myeon. The stream running in front of Jakcheon-ri is called Kkachinae, giving the valley its nickname.   Jakcheongyegok Valley is a well-known summer destination, bustling with visitors seeking to cool off. Its gentle water flow and shallow depth make it both a fun and safe place for water play. The clear and refreshing stream, set against the lush forests and majestic rocks of Chilgapsan Mountain, is sure to whisk away the summer heat just at the thought of it.   In front of Jakcheongyegok Valley lies the Kkachinae Recreation Area, where lifeguards are stationed during summer to ensure visitors' safety. But the charm of Jakcheongyegok Valley doesn’t stop there. Its pristine waters, flowing from the upper to lower reaches, are home to 48 species of aquatic life, including Korean striped bitterling, long-necked loach, and freshwater crabs, making it an ecological treasure trove.   Additionally, local residents near Kkachinae Recreation Area operate guesthouses, allowing visitors to enjoy water activities and accommodation together. The nearby chestnut forest also features a campsite, perfect for those who want to experience camping. Why not enjoy a refreshing and safe water adventure in the beautiful Jakcheongyegok Valley?

stories.title: Bandi Land
stories.script: Bandi Land, located in Muju, Jeollabuk-do, is a space where the whole family can experience and learn about nature. The name Bandi Land naturally brings fireflies to mind, doesn’t it? Indeed, the name comes from fireflies, that is “bandi” in Korean. The park features various attractions related to insects and fireflies, such as the Insect Museum, Firefly Research Center, Youth Campground, Log Cabin, and Firefly Habitat.   The Insect Museum displays a wide variety of insects from Korea and around the world, including fireflies, which are designated as a Natural Monument. In addition to its educational and exhibition functions, the museum also contributes to collecting and preserving biological resources, which are vital assets for future generations. It even has an ecological greenhouse and an aqua zone, allowing visitors to explore not just insects but a diverse range of living organisms.   The Firefly Research Center, operated by Muju-gun, known for its pristine environment, offers firefly observation programs to help children and youth appreciate the beauty and importance of nature.   At the Youth Campground, visitors can learn about the origins and history of the universe, as well as the solar system and constellations. Through telescopes, they can observe the Sun during the day and stars at night.   Additionally, Bandi Land is packed with facilities for children and youth, such as the Firefly Youth Training Center, outdoor water park, and year-round sledding hill, ensuring plenty of fun and educational activities.   Why not embark on a journey into the mysterious and beautiful world of nature, from the tiniest insects to the vast universe, at Bandi Land?

stories.title: Rajetongmun Gate
stories.script: Rajetongmun Gate, located in Muju-gun, Jeollabuk-do, is a popular tourist destination and the first of the 33 scenic spots of Muju Gucheondong. The Gucheondong 33 scenic spots stretch 36 kilometers from Rajetongmun Gate to Hyangjeokbong Peak in Deogyusan Mountain, featuring spectacular views of unique rock formations, dense primeval forests, clear ponds, and cascading waterfalls.   The name Rajetongmun Gate combines the characters “Ra” from “Silla Dynasty,” “Je” from “Baekje Dynasty,” “Tong” meaning to connect, and “Mun” meaning gate, symbolizing a gate connecting the two ancient kingdoms of Silla and Baekje. Historically, this site is thought to have been a border point between the two kingdoms during the Three Kingdoms period. However, its origin remains unclear, with some believing the tunnel was excavated during the Japanese colonial period for gold mining. This gives Rajetongmun Gate a poignant historical significance as a place that bears traces of Korea’s difficult past.   Today, Rajetongmun Gate connects Mupung-myeon and Seolcheon-myeon within Muju-gun. Interestingly, the language and customs on the east and west sides of the cave are different. Mupung-myeon, on the eastern side, was once part of the Silla kingdom, while Seolcheon-myeon on the western side was part of the Baekje kingdom. As a result, people on the eastern side speak the Gyeongsang dialect and follow Gyeongsang customs, while those on the western side speak the Jeolla dialect and follow the customs of the Jeolla and Chungcheong regions.   Why not experience the historical atmosphere of Rajetongmun Gate, a former border of the Three Kingdoms, and continue your journey to explore the breathtaking Gucheondong 33 scenic spots?

stories.title: Muju Meoru Wine Cave
stories.script: Muju Meoru Wine Cave, located halfway up Jeoksangsan Mountain in Muju-gun, Jeollabuk-do, is a remodeled space that was once used as a work tunnel and is now a wine aging cellar. Visitors can taste wine made from meoru, the wild grapes, grown in Muju-gun and enjoy a unique experience called wine footbaths.   Historically, Muju-gun has been a significant producer of meoru. Today, Muju-gun accounts for over 30% of the national production, thanks to the large temperature difference of 11°C between day and night from August to October, which gives the grapes their exceptional sweetness. Various products, such as wine, meoru juice, and meoru-based liquors, are made from these grapes.   The five wineries in Muju produce meoru wine that is known for its high sweetness, rich juice, and deep, intense aroma. Additionally, it is rich in polyphenols, which are beneficial for anti-aging and effective in preventing arteriosclerosis and even cancer. Doesn’t it make you want to try Muju meoru wine, a perfect blend of taste and health?   Muju Meoru Wine Cave was remodeled by Muju-gun in 2007 to showcase the flavor and charm of Muju’s meoru wine to visitors while instilling hope and pride in local grape farmers. The cave, which blocks light and maintains a constant temperature of 13°C to 17°C, is the ideal environment for aging and storing wine. The cave consists of a Wine House and a Secret Door. In the Wine House, you’ll find a specialty store and a café, while the Secret Door offers wine tasting experiences. How about spending some time surrounded by the fragrance of wild grapes at the Muju Meoru Wine Cave?

stories.title: Yeosu Art Land
stories.script: Yeosu Art Land, located in Yeosu, Jeollanam-do, is a resort that offers not only accommodations with stunning ocean views but also a variety of exciting activities and attractions for a truly unique experience. Unlike other resorts, this destination combines lodging with thrilling activities such as kart rides, observatory and a sculpture park. Many of these experiences are set against the breathtaking backdrop of Yeosu's azure sea.   One must-visit spot is the Hand of Midas,” inspired by the Greek mythological figure King Midas. This viewpoint has been featured on Korea's online photo wish lists, making it a prime location for capturing stunning shots of Yeosu’s beautiful sunsets and sunrises. You can also enjoy an adrenaline-filled kart ride with the sea as your backdrop or challenge yourself on the Ocean Skywalk, a thrilling suspension bridge 100 meters above the water, complete with a zipline experience.   After indulging in heart-pounding activities, take some time to appreciate the harmonious blend of art and nature. At the Sculpture Park Scenery, you’ll find a variety of sculptures displayed against the backdrop of the Yeosu sea. The themed 3D Trick Art Museum, 3D Museum Novel, offers a chance to create unique and entertaining memories with your companions while exploring its intriguing exhibits.   With so many activities and exhibits to enjoy, a single day at the resort might feel too short. From thrilling adventures to artistic appreciation, why not create unforgettable memories while taking in the spectacular seaside views of Yeosu?

stories.title: Goso-dong Mural Village
stories.script: The Gosodong Mural Village, located in Yeosu, Jeollanam-do, is a symbolic mural village that represents Yeosu as a cultural city. Originally an old natural village, it was transformed into a mural village in 2012 through the combined efforts of Yeosu City and the residents of Gosodong, coinciding with the Yeosu Expo.   The Gosodong Mural Village often referred to as the “Angel Mural Alley.” It initially earned its name because the mural alley spanned 1,004 meters, which is reminiscent of the Korean word for “cheonsa,” meaning “angel.” Isn’t it a lovely nickname for such a charming place? Today, the mural village stretches 1,650 meters and is divided into 10 sections, each depicting aspects of Yeosu’s history, culture, daily life, and local stories. Among these, the third section, “The Story of the Sea,” and the fifth section, “Yeosu’s Past and Present,” are must-sees.   Walking through the village, you’ll encounter captivating sea views, streets featuring illustrations by cartoonist Huh Young-man, and murals recounting the life of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Along the way, there are rest stops where you can sit and take in the scenery. The village is also home to historical treasures like the Yeosu Tongjeyeong Naval Battle Monument and the Tarubi Memorial Stone, which you won’t want to miss. As you wander through the alleys, you’ll be treated to breathtaking views of Yeosu’s coastline and the Geobukseon Bridge, creating a truly picturesque backdrop.   The mural village has four entrances: Jinnammun Gate, Yi Sunsin Square Gate, Romantic Pochamun Gate, and Jongpomun Gate. Jinnammun Gate comes highly recommended, as Jin-namguan Pavilion is a historic site where Admiral Yi Sun-sin strategized and issued commands during the Imjin War. It’s also a prominent tourist attraction in Yeosu. Why not explore Gosodong Mural Village, where art, history, and stunning ocean views come together, and discover the unique stories of Yeosu?

stories.title: Cheonbu Underwater Observatory
stories.script: The Cheonbu Underwater Observatory, located on Ulleungdo in Gyeongsangbuk-do, is a truly unique attraction. It is the only observatory in South Korea built under the sea. While most observatories are situated in elevated locations to offer scenic views, this one allows visitors to experience the natural underwater world at a depth of 6 meters.   The Cheonbu Underwater Observatory opened in 2014 after a 10-billion-won investment by Ulleung-gun. It stands 22.2 meters tall and features two viewing areas: an underwater observation room located 6 meters below sea level and an above-water observation deck 6 meters above the surface. Ulleung-gun has been actively working to preserve the surrounding marine ecosystem through efforts like deploying artificial reefs.   The observatory situated about 100 meters off the coast in the direction of Seommok from Cheonbu Port. It provides a glimpse into the diverse marine life that inhabits Ulleungdo's pristine waters. Visitors can observe species such as yellowtail, horse mackerel, damselfish, and black sea bream. A feeding station near the observatory attracts fish, offering visitors an up-close view of the marine creatures swimming by. The crystal-clear blue sea and the sight of fish darting through the water create an experience reminiscent of being aboard a submarine.   This observatory is especially ideal for children and seniors who may find it difficult to explore the underwater world directly, making it both an educational and immersive experience. How about visiting the Cheonbu Underwater Observatory to vividly experience the mysterious and captivating marine life of Ulleungdo?

stories.title: Nari Basin
stories.script: The Nari Basin, located on Ulleungdo in Gyeongsangbuk-do, is a unique volcanic terrain formed long ago during the Cenozoic volcanic activity. With its surrounding trails and trekking courses, it’s the perfect place to enjoy the stunning landscapes of Ulleungdo. A “basin” refers to a flat, low-lying area encircled by mountains, and the Nari Basin is surrounded by the outer rim mountains, which create a natural backdrop akin to a folding screen. To the south of the basin is Seonginbong Peak, the highest point on Ulleungdo.   The Nari Basin was created when the northern crater of Seonginbong collapsed after a volcanic eruption. Spanning an area of 2 square kilometers—equivalent to about 28 soccer fields—it is the only expansive plain on Ulleungdo. The name “Nari” comes from seommallari, a native Ulleungdo plant that is both a local specialty and a globally rare species. In the past, the island's inhabitants, facing food shortages, would dig up and eat the roots of this plant. This history gave rise to the area being called Narigol, which eventually became the Nari Basin.   Within the Nari Basin, there is also Al-bong and the smaller Al-bong Basin. After the formation of the Nari Basin, another volcanic eruption created the smaller, egg-shaped basin. Walking along the trails surrounding Al-bong, you’ll encounter unique flora like the Ulleung Chrysanthemum, a plant native to the island. Why not immerse yourself in the mysterious and breathtaking volcanic landscapes of the Nari Basin, an extraordinary feature of this volcanic island that cannot be found on the mainland?

stories.title: Bongnaepokpo Falls
stories.script: Bongnaepokpo Falls, located on Ulleungdo in Gyeongsangbuk-do, is a stunning three-tiered waterfall that flows through lush, pristine forests. As one of the 23 geological attractions designated by the Ulleungdo-Dokdo National Geopark, it showcases breathtaking natural beauty.   In the past, this area was called Guldeung due to a cave at the top of the waterfall that housed a small temple. Although the name Guldeung is no longer used, Bongnaepokpo Falls remains a cherished landmark.   With its abundant water flow, Bongnaepokpo Falls never runs dry, even during the hottest summers. It releases over 3,000 tons of water daily, serving as a vital water source for southern Ulleungdo. The waterfall, with a drop of approximately 30 meters, is beautifully framed by steep cliffs and verdant forests, making it an irresistible attraction and a popular photography spot for visitors to the island.   Starting at the Bongnaepokpo Falls Management Office, visitors can take a scenic walk along a cedar-lined trail. During summer, the trail offers a unique cooling experience at a natural air vent called Pung-hyeol, where refreshing gusts of cold air flow out of the ground. Imagine a natural air conditioner cooling you as you hike—it’s a delightful way to beat the heat. The area also serves as a vibrant ecological learning center, home to diverse plant species such as Ulleung liverleaf, mustard cress, and Korean large bluebell, alongside trees like beech, oriental raisin tree, and glossy privet. Why not visit Bongnaepokpo Falls to enjoy the refreshing sound of cascading water and the serenity of the dense forest, and immerse yourself in the wonders of Ulleungdo’s natural beauty?

stories.title: Naesujeon Mongdol Beach
stories.script: Naesujeon Mongdol Beach, located on Ulleungdo in Gyeongsangbuk-do, is a picturesque shoreline and swimming spot covered with smooth, rounded pebbles. Known for its crystal-clear waters and gentle waves, it’s a popular destination for snorkeling enthusiasts. The term pebble refers to stones that have been naturally polished and rounded by the continuous ebb and flow of the tides.   Unlike typical beaches with white sand or mudflats, Naesujeon Mongdol Beach offers a unique charm with its round, polished stones. The sound of the pebbles clattering against one another as the waves roll in creates a melody of nature, while walking on them provides a soothing, massage-like sensation underfoot. Historically, the beach was once called Jeojeonpo because of the abundance of mulberry trees growing nearby. Later, it was renamed Naesujeon after Kim Naesu, a pioneering resident who cultivated farmland in the area. The story behind its name adds an intriguing layer of history to this charming location.   With its clear waters, shallow depths, and calm waves, Naesujeon Mongdol Beach is an ideal summer retreat for families. Facilities like showers and a seawater pool make it a comfortable and safe place for swimming and relaxation. Visitors can also explore nearby attractions, including the Naesujeon Spring and the Naesujeon Sunrise Observatory. The observatory offers breathtaking views of Ulleungdo’s stunning landscape, especially at dawn. Why not visit Naesujeon Mongdol Beach to enjoy the pristine sea, the unique allure of its pebbles, and the serene beauty of Ulleungdo? It’s a destination that blends natural charm, fascinating history, and modern convenience.

stories.title: Yerimwon Ulleung Dwarf Garden
stories.script: Yerimwon Ulleung Dwarf Garden, located on Ulleungdo in Gyeongsangbuk-do, is the only botanical garden in the Ulleung-gun region. This garden not only showcases the native trees and plants of Ulleungdo, but also transforms into a cultural space featuring letter sculptures and artistic displays.   Yerimwon Ulleung Dwarf Garden opened in 2007, and it houses over 650 bonsai specimens, including unique and rare wildflower bonsai from the region. Visitors can also explore native trees from Ulleungdo, with a highlight being the Seomgaeyagwangnamu Cotoneaster Wilsonii, a species found nowhere else in the world, making it a must-see.   In addition to its plants, Yerimwon Ulleung Dwarf Garden offers stunning letter sculptures that capture the essence of Ulleungdo’s nature. Words such as dream and love are carved into wood, offering a unique experience compared to reading text on paper. As you walk through the garden, take the time to discover your favorite sculptures, many of which include inspiring quotes engraved beneath them, providing a special keepsake for your visit.   Yerimwon Ulleung Dwarf Garden also features large stone sculptures made from natural stones found on Ulleungdo, and the viewing platform offers panoramic views of the island’s beautiful sea. It’s a wonderful place for families to learn about rare plants, appreciate art, and enjoy the breathtaking ocean scenery. More than just a botanical garden, Yerimwon Ulleung Dwarf Garden is a cultural space where nature and art harmoniously coexist, offering a truly special experience. Why not explore this enchanting space and immerse yourself in the unique charm of nature and creativity?

stories.title: Chilpo Beach
stories.script: Chilpo Beach, located 13 km north of Pohang in Gyeongsangbuk-do, is a family-friendly destination with a wide sandy beach and shallow waters, making it perfect for swimming and beach activities. Notably, the charm of this beach extends beyond the swimming season, offering various attractions year-round.   The beach boasts a spacious 4 km-long sandy shoreline that can accommodate up to 100,000 people. During the summer, visitors can enjoy sand play, sand baths, and create memorable moments. Surrounded by pine trees, the beach provides a peaceful spot for a relaxing walk in the fragrant pine forest after swimming.   The waters near the shore are shallow, about 1 meter deep, and gradually deepen, reaching shoulder height for adults further out, making it suitable for all ages to enjoy water activities. Chilpo Beach is also known for its clear water, one of the clearest among the beaches on the East Coast of Korea. The nearby Chilpo Resort offers convenient facilities, including hotels, convenience stores, and shower areas, ensuring a comfortable beach experience for visitors.   Even outside the summer months, Chilpo Beach remains a great place to visit. The beach is located at the junction of two walking trails on the East Coast's Haepalang Trail Courses 17 and 18. Walking along the wooden deck at the end of the beach, visitors can enjoy a scenic trek with the beautiful blue East Sea in the background. Additionally, the Chilpo Jazz Festival, held every September, allows visitors enjoy beautiful jazz melodies while gazing at the night sea. Whether you're visiting for water activities in the summer or trekking and cultural performances in other seasons, Chilpo Beach offers a variety of attractions throughout the year. Why not experience the diverse charms of Chilpo Beach?

stories.title: Hwajin Beach
stories.script: Hwajin Beach, located in Pohang, Gyeongsangbuk-do, is a cozy beach where visitors can enjoy both swimming and camping. It has gained popularity among camping enthusiasts, especially for its unique wild camping experience.   Hwajin Beach is a small, peaceful beach with a sandy shore stretching about 400 meters, making it an ideal spot to escape from the crowds and enjoy a quiet day by the sea. Behind the beach, there is a pine windbreak forest, offering a tranquil setting for a stroll along the peaceful forest paths. However, the highlight of this beach is the camping experience. From July to November, the village association operates a wild camping site in the pine forest, where tents and campers are allowed. The campgrounds are inexpensive, with rates of around 10,000 to 20,000 KRW per night, and facilities like showers are available, making it a perfect spot for a camping trip. Imagine setting up your tent in the shade of the cool pine trees and enjoying the beach right in front of you, it's the perfect summer getaway.   In addition to camping, the beach also offers marine sports facilities like banana boat rides and jet skis, as well as surfing lessons for those looking for more adventure. A visit to the nearby Naeyeonsan 12 Waterfalls in Pohang is also recommended for a more scenic experience. With its combination of camping, water sports, surfing, and natural beauty, Hwajin Beach offers a diverse range of activities. Why not create some unforgettable memories at this charming beach?

stories.title: Odo 1-ri Beach
stories.script: Odo 1-ri Beach, located in Pohang, Gyeongsangbuk-do, is a seasonal beach that opens only during the summer, but it offers a range of enjoyable experiences, including viewing the Odo-ri columnar joint, car camping, and traditional camping.   The beach is positioned between the popular Wolpo Beach and Chilpo Beach, and it is relatively large among small scale beaches. A standout feature is the free camping area nearby, which is perfect for those looking to enjoy both swimming and camping. Visitors can even cook their meals after a refreshing swim. Therefore, why not enjoy a barbecue while taking in the beautiful sea view?   One of the highlights of Odo 1-ri Beach is the Odo-ri Columnar Joint. It is a fascinating geological structure formed through volcanic activity. The entire island is a columnar joint, renowned for its outstanding scenic beauty and academic value. It’s often referred to as “three black rocks like crows” because of its resemblance to the tail of a whale protruding above the water.   The beach is conveniently located for exploring other famous tourist spots in Pohang. Heading south from the beach, you can visit Yeongilman Port and Yeongildae Beach. Additionally, the Homigot Sunrise Square, a must-see destination in Pohang, is just a 30-minute drive away from Odo 1-ri Beach. How about spending a special summer at Odo 1-ri Beach, enjoying both cool waters and the breathtaking views of the columnar joint?

stories.title: Sangju Silver Sand Beach
stories.script: Sangju Silver Sand Beach, located in Namhae-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, is a beautiful beach known for its fine, silvery sand that stretches over a wide area. Surrounded by the breathtaking scenery of Geumsan Mountain, this beach attracts over a million tourists every summer, making it a popular summer destination.   Sangju Silver Sand Beach situated 21 kilometers south of Namhae-eup. It features gentle waves and a serene and crescent-shaped sandy shore that spans 2 kilometers in length and covers an area of 160,000 square meters. The sand here is so soft that it slips smoothly through your fingers, and its fine texture makes it perfect for barefoot walks along the beach. The gradual slope of the beach and warm water temperatures also make it an ideal spot for families with young children.   Behind the silver sand lies a 9,000-square-meter pine forest, where many visitors enjoy forest bathing or camping in the shade of the trees. For those interested in camping, the Sangju community operates the Sangju Campsite nearby, where you can camp to the soothing sound of the waves. Fishing from the nearby tidal rocks is another activity you can enjoy, offering a variety of ways to experience the beach's natural beauty.   During the summer, the beach hosts a Summer Festival, and in winter, the beach celebrates a New Year's sunrise festival. The beach is also famous for its vegetable hot dogs and charming cafes surrounding the area, adding to the appeal of the spot. Why not enjoy a peaceful getaway at the stunning Sangju Silver Sand Beach, with its shimmering sand and relaxing atmosphere?

stories.title: Seolri Beach
stories.script: At the southernmost tip of Namhae-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, lies Seolri Beach, a charming small fishing village that offers year-round activities, from swimming to immersive fishing village experiences.   The name Seolri  is quite poetic, derived from the word Seol meaning snow, as the white sand resembles snow, and Ri meaning village. Another name for this place is Banyongchon, named after the shape of the nearby mountain, which is said to resemble a curled-up dragon.   Seolri Beach features a white sandy shore where visitors can enjoy swimming, but the nearby Seolri Fishing Village Experience Center offers a chance to try unique and traditional fishing activities. You can participate in a pot trap experience, where you haul up traps placed in the sea, or try the Gathuri technique, where nets are spread between land and boats, and then hauled in. There is also the opportunity for Yeojang boat fishing, where you fish from a barge.   For those looking for even more adventure, you can enjoy sea fishing, go kayaking to the nearby island of Sado for snorkeling, or take in breathtaking views at the Seolri Skywalk, which opened in 2020. At a height of 36 meters, the glass floor provides a thrilling yet stunning view of the ocean below. With the stunning emerald-colored waters and lively fishing village experiences, Seolri Beach offers a perfect blend of adventure and beauty. Why not visit and make the most of the vibrant atmosphere and picturesque coastal scenery?

stories.title: German Village
stories.script: German Village, located in Namhae-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, is a unique settlement founded by Korean workers who were sent to West Germany in the 1960s and 1970s as miners and nurses to help with economic development. After completing their work in Germany, these individuals returned to Korea and settled in this village. Approximately 8,000 miners and 10,000 nurses worked in Germany, contributing to South Korea's economic growth.   To honor these workers, the Namhae local government established the German Village, where they cultivated beautiful gardens and introduced various aspects of German culture. The village is particularly famous for its traditional German-style houses, and about 30 of these homes operate as guesthouses, offering visitors the chance to stay in these charming, foreign-inspired homes, making for an unforgettable experience.   In addition, every October, the village hosts a unique event, which is an Oktoberfest-style beer festival modeled after the famous Munich Oktoberfest. During this festival, visitors can immerse themselves in German culture, enjoying authentic German beer and sausages, making it a must-visit for beer enthusiasts. Afterward, be sure to stop by the souvenir shop to pick up beer mugs and openers as mementos.   Moreover, the Dorf Youth Market, a small flea market, is held every second Saturday of the month. Here, you can find creative products from local youth and popular specialties and crafts from Namhae-gun. Visiting German Village offers a fascinating glimpse into Korea's history and an opportunity to experience the charm of German culture right in the heart of South Korea. Why not explore this unique blend of history and culture for a truly distinctive experience?

stories.title: Jungmun Saekdal Beach
stories.script: Jungmun Saekdal Beach, located in Seogwipo, Jeju Island, is a stunning destination where the beautiful coastal scenery of Jeju Island blends seamlessly with the sight of palm trees, creating an exotic atmosphere. The beach is particularly famous for its water sports, drawing over a million visitors each year who come to enjoy various marine activities.   The beach stretches for about 560 meters in length and 50 meters in width. Historically known as Jinmosal, meaning long sandy beach, the area features unique sand colors, including black, white, red, and gray, which blend beautifully with Jeju Island's black volcanic rocks. When the sunlight hits the curved, crescent-shaped beach, the colors of the sand shift depending on the direction of the sun, adding to the beach's natural beauty.   The highlight of Jungmun Saekdal Beach is its suitability for dynamic water sports. The beach experiences frequent and relatively high waves, making it ideal for surfing. In fact, the Jeju Island Jungmun Beach International Surfing Competition is held here every June, which is the largest international surfing event in Korea. In addition to surfing, visitors can enjoy a wide range of water sports, including water skiing, windsurfing, scuba diving, and jet boating.   Jungmun Saekdal Beach is also well-connected to other attractions in the area. Situated within the Jungmun Tourism Complex, the beach is close to popular sights such as Cheonjeyeonpokpo Falls and Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs. Why not experience thrilling water sports against the breathtaking backdrop of Jeju Island's ocean scenery?

stories.title: Gapado Island
stories.script: Gapado Island, located in Seogwipo, Jeju Island, is the fourth largest of the island's satellite islands. Once a lesser-known destination, it has gained popularity due to the development of green barley tourism and the establishment of Olle trails, with ferries running 3-4 times a day. Let's explore the unique charm of Gapado Island, especially its lush barley fields.   The island resembles a stingray when viewed from above, which is where the name Gapado originates. Some believe the name comes from Gapari, which is a variation of gaori, meaning stingray in Korean, while others claim it evolved from Gaedo, meaning lid-shaped island, referring to the shape of the island. Covering only 0.87 square kilometers, Gapado Island is a small island where visitors can rent bicycles near the port to explore the surroundings. With no steep hills, it’s also perfect for a leisurely walk, taking just an hour or two to fully enjoy the sights.   Gapado Island features two Olle trail courses. One runs along the coastline, offering views of the island's perimeter, while the other cuts through the center of the island, passing through villages and green barley fields. The green barley, a plant closely associated with Gapado Island, thrives due to the island's farmers who once struggled to tend crops due to their busy coastal work. The barley fields, swaying in the wind, create a stunning scene, especially during spring.   In April and May, the island hosts the Gapado Island Green Barley Festival with events like barley field walks and treasure hunts along the Olle trails. Visiting during the festival is a great way to experience the island's beauty in full bloom. How about enjoying the refreshing sea breeze and relaxing pace of life on Gapado Island, surrounded by the mesmerizing sight of green barley fields?

stories.title: Red Oreum Natural Recreation Forest
stories.script: The Red Oreum Natural Recreation Forest, located in Seogwipo, Jeju Island, is a pristine nature park that has preserved its original, untouched landscape. Situated on the eastern side of Hallasan, this tranquil retreat is easily accessible from anywhere on the island and offers a variety of trails and accommodations, making it an ideal spot to relax in the refreshing forest.   The name Red Oreum comes from the hill behind the forest, which is covered with reddish soil, giving the area its distinctive appearance. The name of the recreation forest is derived from this striking red hill. At the entrance of the forest, visitors can also enjoy a walk along the Saryeoni Forest Trail, which offers different hiking options.   There is the 1.7-kilometer-long Red Oreum Trail, which takes you to the peak of the hill, offering scenic views. For those interested in history, the 3.2-kilometer-long Sangjatseong Trail features stone walls that were built to demarcate pastures. Additionally, the Haemaji Forest Trail is 6.7 kilometers in length and leads to the Malchach Oreum, where you can witness the beautiful sunrise over Jeju Island. For visitors of all ages and abilities, there is also a 1-kilometer-long barrier-free trail that is equipped with durable wooden pathways and Braille signs, ensuring an inclusive experience for everyone.   The recreation forest offers accommodation in traditional Jeju Island-style houses, allowing families to fully immerse themselves in the natural surroundings. For camping enthusiasts, there is also a forest campsite where you can enjoy a night under the stars. Why not enjoy a peaceful stay at the Red Oreum Natural Recreation Forest, embracing Jeju Island's pristine nature while experiencing the refreshing atmosphere of the island's forests?

stories.title: Eongttopokpo Falls
stories.script: Eongttopokpo Falls, located in Seogwipo, Jeju Island, is a hidden gem that unveils its true magnificence after heavy rain. While it may appear as a regular cliff on a typical day, after a downpour, this waterfall comes to life, showcasing its grandeur and beauty. If you're lucky enough to visit during rainfall, you're in for a spectacular sight!   The name Eongtto comes from the Jeju Island dialect, where Eong means a small cave, and Tto refers to the entrance, together meaning the entrance to a small cave. The waterfall cascades from a height of 50 meters, creating a dramatic scene when the rains come. Many of Jeju Island's rivers are dry during most of the year, with water only flowing after significant rainfall. To see Eongttopokpo Falls in its full glory, at least 70mm of rain is required.   This waterfall, one of Seogwipo's 70 scenic spots and part of the Jeju Island Olle Trail, was once a lesser-known destination. However, after being featured on a popular TV show in 2011, it has become one of the busiest attractions on the island during rainy days. The access road and parking lot have been improved, making it much easier to reach.   The area around the waterfall is surrounded by a lush subtropical forest, providing an exotic and green landscape year-round. If you happen to be visiting Jeju Island on a rainy day, consider experiencing the stunning view of Eongttopokpo Falls as it dramatically pours down the cliff, making it a memorable and unique part of your trip.

stories.title: Iho Tewoo Beach
stories.script: Iho Tewoo Beach in Jeju Island is the closest beach to the city center, making it a popular destination for both locals and tourists. Its proximity to the city and convenient access via public transport make it an easily accessible spot. The beach features a gentle slope, making it safe for swimming, and behind it lies a pine forest, making it perfect for camping or a relaxed day outdoors.   One of the beach's most notable features is its two lighthouses, which are shaped like Jeju Island's iconic jeongmal, refers to Jeju Island's small horses. The red and white lighthouses are 12 meters tall, creating a unique and picturesque landscape, especially during sunset. The lighthouses provide a great photo opportunity, offering stunning views with the setting sun in the background.   During low tide, the wide sandy beach reveals a traditional stone structure known as Wondam, which is used in Jeju Island's fishing methods. Wondam consists of stone walls built to catch fish using the tidal differences between high and low tides. Visitors can also explore the reconstructed Wondam at Iho Mosalwon, where they can see how this traditional fishing practice works. The name Iho Tewoo Beach comes from the fishing activities that once took place here using the traditional Jeju Island boat called the Tewoo.   In July and August, the beach hosts the Iho Tewoo Festival, where visitors can participate in experiences such as Tewoo boat rowing and traditional fishing. It’s a great opportunity to explore Jeju Island’s cultural heritage while enjoying the beautiful beach scenery. How about visiting Iho Tewoo Beach to see its famous lighthouses and experience traditional Jeju Island fishing culture?

stories.title: Geumneung Beach
stories.script: Geumneung Beach, located in Jeju Island, is connected to the popular Hyeopjae Beach but offers a quieter atmosphere, making it a perfect spot for families looking to enjoy Jeju Island's beautiful blue waters away from the crowds. This beach boasts crystal-clear emerald waters and soft white sand, creating an ideal environment for water activities. The shallow waters and gentle slope make it safe for children to play in, especially during low tide when small pools form on the beach.   One unique feature of Geumneung Beach is its sparkling silver sand, which is mixed with crushed seashells. While the sand is beautiful, the sharp edges of the shells can be a bit uncomfortable for bare feet, so wearing water shoes is recommended. On the opposite side of the beach, you can enjoy the view of Biyangdo Island, a small volcanic island that formed a thousand years ago. The picturesque landscape of the beach with Biyangdo Island in the background makes for a popular photography spot. Be sure to catch the sunset, as the island and the surrounding area are bathed in the warm glow of the setting sun.   Geumneung Beach is conveniently connected to a parking lot, making it easy to transport belongings. There are also hot water showers available, ensuring a comfortable experience for the whole family. Nearby, you can also visit Hanlim Park, one of Jeju Island's top tourist attractions. Why not make lasting memories with your family at Geumneung Beach, enjoying both the tranquil atmosphere and stunning views of Jeju Island’s natural beauty?

stories.title: Samyang Beach
stories.script: Samyang Beach, located in Jeju Island, is a beach in the northeastern part of Jeju Island, along with Iho Tewoo Beach. Unlike the blue sea and white sandy beaches that are commonly associated with Jeju Island’s beaches, Samyang Beach has the unique charm of black sand.   While most beaches have white sand due to seashells, the sand at Samyang Beach is made up of black sand formed from broken volcanic rocks, making it special. This black sand contains a lot of iron. It has been known for a long time that burying the body in the heated black sand, which absorbs sunlight, can be very effective for joint pain and nerve disorders. This is called Mosal-teum, a sand therapy on Jeju Island. Even today, during the summer, Samyang Beach gets crowded with people who want to enjoy the warm sand therapy.   Every July, “the Samyang Black Sand Festival” is held here. Visitors can participate in activities like black sand therapy, walking on the sand, and enjoy various performances and events. Compared to Iho Tewoo Beach, Samyang Beach is relatively less known to tourists, so it is a quieter place where you can enjoy a clean and clear sea. Why don’t you experience the unique healing of Jeju Island in the sparkling black sand of Samyang Beach?

stories.title: Yongnunioreum Volcanic Cone
stories.script: Yongnunioreum Volcanic Cone is one of Jeju Island’s representative oreums, known for its gentle ridges. With a circumference of 2,685 meters, its height is 88 meters, making it a low and gradual slope. This oreum is the only one among the more than 360 oreums in Jeju Island to have three craters.   Yongnunioreum Volcanic Cone is situated in the eastern part of Jeju Island. The summit offers views of Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone and Udo Island on clear days. Due to its low height and gentle incline, it is a popular spot for tourists of all ages. At one point, due to the large number of visitors, Jeju Island implemented a natural rest year system to protect the environment and limit access to the oreum.   The name Yongnunioreum Volcanic Cone has two origins. One is that the center is sunken, making it resemble a place where a dragon might have lain, and the other is that from above, the shape of the oreum looks like a dragon’s eye. The shape of the oreum, with three ridges, gives a soft overall impression, and its beautiful curved ridges have made it a favorite of many photographers.   It takes about an hour to walk around the oreum, and it is lovely to visit any time of the year for a relaxing hike. In autumn, when the entire oreum is covered in silver grass, it creates a fantastic atmosphere, attracting many visitors for wedding photos. It is also a great idea to combine a visit to nearby oreums such as Sonji Oreum and Darangshi Oreum. How about enjoying the wide-open views of Jeju Island from the gently alluring Yongnunioreum Volcanic Cone?

stories.title: Saebyeol Oreum
stories.script: Saebyeol Oreum is a representative oreum of the western part of Jeju Island. The beautiful name Saebyeol means new star and is said to come from the idea that it stands alone like the evening star in the sky.   Saebyeol Oreum, located at an elevation of 519 meters, has two hiking trails: one through the eastern entrance and the other through the western entrance. The western trail is steeper and more challenging, so it’s best to choose a trail that suits your fitness level. It takes about 30 minutes to reach the summit, and from the top, you can enjoy a panoramic view of Jeju Island’s beautiful western beaches, including Hyeopjae Beach, Geumnyeong Beach, and Biyangdo Island.   Every March, the Saebyeol Oreum hosts the Jeju Fire Festival, one of Jeju Island’s representative festivals. Known locally as Bang-ae Bul, the fire is part of a traditional Jeju custom where fires are set in pastures of horses or cows to remove old grass and pests and to drive away bad luck in the coming spring. The Jeju Fire Festival celebrates this traditional practice, wishing for peace in the coming year and hoping that people’s wishes reach the sky.
