Among Korea's octopus-producing regions, Muan stands out as one of the best places to enjoy fresh, high-quality octopus. Muan is home to one of Korea's largest mudflats. In 2001, it became the country's first officially designated mudflat wetland protection area, highlighting its pristine natural environment. Muan’s unpolluted mudflats, abundant with food sources, provide an ideal environment for octopuses to thrive. Thanks to this ideal environment, Muan octopus is known for its notably long, slender legs and exceptionally tender texture compared to octopus from other regions.  If you're looking for the best way to experience Muan octopus, a visit to Muan Octopus Specialty Street is a must. This street is home to around 30 restaurants specializing in octopus, letting you sample a wide variety of delicious dishes all in one place. From stir-fried octopus bursting with smoky flavor, to octopus bibimbap mixed with nutty sesame oil and fresh vegetables, incredibly fresh live octopus, and spicy octopus soup with a clear, refreshing broth—each dish is sure to captivate your taste buds.  Enjoy a bowl of chewy octopus to boost your energy and revive your appetite! When fatigue sets in, a culinary journey to Muan is the perfect way to recharge your energy and delight your taste buds.

stories.title: No Pain, No Gain
stories.script: Welcome to your K-local food trip! The highlight of this culinary journey is Mokpo Skate, a delicacy that perfectly embodies the Korean proverb Gojingamrae, meaning Sweetness Follows Bitterness, reflecting how initial hardships lead to rewarding pleasures. Are you ready to discover the hidden culinary treasure behind its uniquely pungent flavor?  Just as the old proverb says, Enduring Bitterness Leads to Sweetness, appreciating the true flavor of skate requires a bit of patience. Skate is a saltwater fish belonging to the ray family, commonly found in Mokpo, Jeollanam-do. Mokpo is famous for hosting Korea's busiest skate auctions, where skate caught near Daecheongdo Island in Incheon is brought in and traded at the local fish market.  While skate is widely enjoyed throughout the Jeollanam-do region, skate caught near Heuksando Island is considered the best of all. Most skate caught in the waters around Heuksando Island is transported to Mokpo Fish Market. It's said that long ago, people transporting skate from Heuksando Island to Mokpo Port accidentally discovered the unique flavor created when the fish naturally fermented during the extended journey at room temperature.  But how can skate stay fresh even at room temperature? The secret lies in the unique structure of its body. Cartilaginous fish like skate, rays, and sharks naturally store urea in their bodies, which helps prevent excessive salt from entering their systems. After the skate dies, the urea breaks down, producing the fish's distinctive pungent aroma and sharp flavor.  To balance the skate’s strong aroma and distinctive flavor, it is traditionally served alongside well-aged kimchi and tender boiled pork. Together, these three ingredients create Hongeo Samhap, a beloved delicacy unique to Jeolla Province.  Why not savor the distinctive, pungent flavor of skate and experience for yourself why it's such an irresistible delicacy in Korea? Visit Mokpo and indulge in this unique culinary experience, savoring a delicacy infused with generations of local history and tradition.

stories.title: A High-Protein Delicacy from the Summer Sea
stories.audioTitle: A High-Protein Delicacy from the Summer Sea
stories.script: Welcome to your K-local food trip! The highlight of this culinary journey is Yeosu Pike Eel—a nourishing, high-protein delicacy harvested from Yeosu's summer waters.  Although pike eel is caught throughout Korea’s southern coast, Yeosu is particularly well-known for producing abundant, high-quality pike eel. Gyeongdo Island in Yeosu alone is home to more than 30 fishing boats dedicated to catching pike eel, and the waters between neighboring Dolsando and Geumodo islands are renowned as prime habitats for this delicacy. In Yeosu, fishermen traditionally catch pike eel using a method known as Junak, a type of longline fishing. This method involves attaching around 100 baited hooks to a single fishing line, strategically designed to take advantage of the pike eel’s powerful bite.  Late Joseon scholar Jeong Yakjeon described the pike eel in his book Jasan-eobo as having a snout as long as a pig’s, uneven teeth like a dog’s, and teeth and bones so hard that it could easily bite and swallow a person. In fact, the Korean name Gaetjangeo is believed to derive from Gae (meaning dog), referencing the eel's notably sharp teeth. You should be especially cautious when handling pike eels, as their bites can cause injuries.  Though pike eel is enjoyed throughout the year, it’s especially favored in summer as a nourishing, stamina-boosting dish. Pike eel is exceptionally nutritious, with protein making up 67% of its nutritional content. It is also rich in amino acids and compounds that enhance its savory umami flavor. It's also about 26% lower in calories compared to chicken, making it an excellent choice if you're looking for something lighter.  One of the most popular ways to enjoy pike eel is as shabu-shabu, a Japanese-style hot pot dish. When freshly prepared pike eel is briefly dipped into boiling broth for about ten seconds, the gelatin in its skin reacts to the heat, creating a beautiful flower-like shape. Eating freshly cooked pike eel placed atop thin slices of raw onion creates a delightful harmony of crisp, refreshing onion and the eel's deep umami flavor, providing an unforgettable culinary experience.  This summer, why not take a culinary trip to Yeosu, and experience the rich, savory flavors and nutritional benefits of fresh pike eel?

stories.title: Jipyeong Makgeolli, the Representative Rice Wine of Yangpyeong
stories.audioTitle: Jipyeong Makgeolli, the Representative Rice Wine of Yangpyeong
stories.script: Welcome to your K-local food trip! The highlight of this culinary journey is Yangpyeong Makgeolli, a delightful traditional Korean rice wine known for its subtle sweetness and refreshing, sparkling finish.  Makgeolli is an indispensable part of Korea's traditional drinking culture. From the earliest days of Korea’s recorded history right up to the present, Makgeolli has remained a constant companion in Korean life. Traditionally known as Takju, Makgeolli appears countless times in historical records like Samguk Sagi and The Annals of the Joseon Dynasty, reflecting its long and storied history.  True to its name, which literally means freshly filtered alcohol, Makgeolli is a traditional Korean beverage made by fermenting rice or wheat with water and Nuruk, a traditional fermentation starter, and then roughly filtering the mixture. Founded in 1925 in Jipyeong-ri, Yangpyeong County, Gyeonggi Province, Jipyeong Brewery has maintained its brewing tradition for nearly 100 years. Long beloved by the local community, Jipyeong Brewery remains the spiritual home and iconic symbol of Jipyeong Makgeolli even today.  The secret behind Jipyeong Makgeolli’s popularity lies in its clean finish, subtle sweetness, and pleasantly gentle carbonation that delivers a refreshing sensation. Thanks to its smooth, approachable flavor, Jipyeong Makgeolli appeals to everyone—from first-time drinkers to seasoned enthusiasts.  Across Korea, nearly every region has its own signature local brewery. If you have the opportunity, why not travel around Korea and savor the unique Makgeolli flavors that each region has to offer? Local restaurants across the country offer their own unique styles of Makgeolli, adding another delightful experience to your travels.

stories.title: Hansan Sogokju, the First Recorded Alcohol in Korean Peninsula History
stories.audioTitle: Hansan Sogokju, the First Recorded Alcohol in Korean Peninsula History
stories.script: Welcome to your K-local food trip! The highlight of this culinary journey is Hansan Sogokju from Seocheon, Chungcheongnam-do—the earliest recorded traditional liquor on the Korean peninsula.  Hansan Sogokju is a traditional rice wine produced in Hansan-myeon, Seocheon-gun, with a history so rich that it was recorded as early as the Samguk Sagi, compiled during the Goryeo Dynasty. There’s even a historical account that King Daru of the ancient Baekje Kingdom once banned the brewing of Sogokju to conserve grain, illustrating just how long-standing and popular this traditional liquor was.  Sogokju is brewed using glutinous rice, regular rice, and Nuruk, a traditional Korean fermentation starter made from grains containing beneficial molds. First, steamed rice cakes made from regular rice flour are mixed with Nuruk to prepare the initial fermentation starter, called Mitsul. Next, cooked glutinous rice and additional Nuruk are added for a second fermentation. A distinctive feature of Sogokju is that it's brewed using very little water, creating a richer, more concentrated flavor. The liquor is then aged for approximately 100 days with red chili peppers to further enhance its unique taste.  Glutinous rice contains glucose, a natural sugar that remains in the liquor even after fermentation, giving Sogokju its subtle sweetness. Because of this, Sogokju pairs exceptionally well with lighter dishes such as beef tartare, shabu-shabu, and beef hot pot, rather than strongly seasoned or oily foods.  Around Hansan-myeon, there are approximately 70 small breweries and specialty shops, forming a unique local drinking culture. The Hansan Sogokju Gallery is especially popular among visitors, showcasing Sogokju varieties from various local breweries all in one place. Visitors can enjoy tastings or even participate in hands-on brewing experiences.  How about experiencing the fragrant sweetness of Hansan Sogokju in Hansan, where the spirit of the ancient Baekje Kingdom still lingers?

stories.title: Andong Soju, Korea's Premier Traditional Liquor
stories.audioTitle: Andong Soju, Korea's Premier Traditional Liquor
stories.script: Welcome to your K-local food trip! The highlight of this culinary journey is Andong Soju, a traditional Korean spirit treasured for its rich history and deep, distinctive flavor.  Andong Soju is a traditional distilled liquor produced in the Andong region of Gyeongsangbuk-do, widely recognized as one of Korea’s signature spirits. Historically abundant in clean water and high-quality rice, Andong naturally became home to many noble families, who established clan villages where brewing alcohol for ancestral rituals became an integral cultural tradition. Today, the Andong Soju Museum operates alongside production facilities to promote the historical value and traditional crafting methods of Andong Soju, preserving this important cultural heritage for future generations.  Dating back to the Goryeo Dynasty, Andong Soju carries a deep-rooted tradition and was highly prized during the Joseon Dynasty, frequently served at royal banquets and state rituals. Crafted from pure, locally sourced ingredients, Andong Soju is known for its crisp bite derived from its high alcohol content, harmonious balance of nutty richness and depth, and a smooth finish that leaves a pleasant, lingering aftertaste.  With its harmonious and balanced flavor, Andong Soju has been cherished by countless people throughout generations. In Andong, Soju has also been traditionally valued as a medicinal remedy—applied topically to wounds or used as a folk treatment for stomachaches and indigestion.  Indeed, Andong Soju is much more than just an alcoholic beverage; it is a precious cultural heritage that embodies the very essence of Korea’s traditional liquor craftsmanship. Each bottle carries within it the skills, dedication, and artisanal spirit passed down through generations. Even today, Andong Soju stands as one of Korea’s most prestigious traditional liquors, widely recognized for its cultural and historical significance both at home and abroad.  Why not savor the rich history and flavor in every sip of Andong Soju, while immersing yourself in the unique culture and charm of Andong?

stories.title: Discovering the True Meaning of Joseon at Gyeonggijeon Shrine
stories.audioTitle: Discovering the True Meaning of Joseon at Gyeonggijeon Shrine
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! For this cultural journey, we're exploring Jeonju's Gyeonggijeon Shrine, a place that beautifully preserves both the heritage and artistic charm of the Joseon Dynasty.  Gyeonggijeon Shrine was built in 1410 to enshrine and honor the portrait of King Taejo Yi Seong-gye, the founder of Joseon. It's a very important place that symbolizes the roots and authentic traditions of the Joseon Dynasty. The shrine has a simple yet elegant exterior that blends beautifully with its neatly maintained garden. Inside the main hall, the beautiful coffered ceiling and detailed pillars clearly show the traditional architectural beauty of mid-Joseon. The shrine is surrounded by bamboo groves and beautiful ginkgo trees, giving it a unique beauty in every season. It's also a favorite spot for taking photos!  Thanks to these charming features, Gyeonggijeon Shrine became a main filming location for the popular film Masquerade. This movie attracted over 10 million viewers! In the movie, Ha-seon, an ordinary storyteller from the market, secretly takes the place of King Gwanghae. This imaginary story blends perfectly with the peaceful, elegant atmosphere of Gyeonggijeon, making viewers feel like they're stepping right into the Joseon era.  Ha-seon (posing as King Gwanghae): Yes, I'd like to be king. But if becoming king means someone has to die just so I can live, if someone must suffer that fate for me, then I don't want it. If that's what being a real king is, I'd rather follow my own dreams.  This line raises the question, What makes a true king? It clearly shows that Ha-seon has grown into someone much more than just a simple stand-in. Gyeonggijeon's peaceful and elegant atmosphere really brings out Ha-seon's inner conflict and moments of change. It makes viewers feel like they're actually experiencing that era themselves.  Jeonju's Gyeonggijeon Shrine is a place where history and art come together. As you stroll through here, you might feel the spirit of the Joseon Dynasty and even be reminded of your favorite scenes from the movie. Enjoy a relaxing stroll through the beautiful gardens, and create romantic memories as if you're the star of a movie.

stories.title: Yeolhwajeong, the Secret Hideaway Colored by the Light of Love
stories.audioTitle: Yeolhwajeong, the Secret Hideaway Colored by the Light of Love
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! This time, we'll visit Boseong Yeolhwajeong Pavilion. It’s a relaxing place, famous for its peaceful pavilion and pond surrounded by a lush forest.  Yeolhwajeong is a pavilion built during the late Joseon Dynasty, located in Ganggol Village in Boseong, South Jeolla Province. It was built in 1845 by a government official named Yi Jin-man to teach younger generations. Its name comes from the poem Returning Home by Tao Yuanming. It means a place to happily talk and spend time with family and friends. Because of its cultural importance, Yeolhwajeong was designated as an Important Folklore Cultural Heritage site in 1984. It has a unique design that works as both a pavilion and a house. The garden has an L-shaped pond in front of a wide yard, along with cherry blossom, magnolia, and pomegranate trees. It makes you feel peaceful, as if time has stopped for a moment.  Because of its romantic feel, Yeolhwajeong became an important location in the touching historical romance drama The Red Sleeve. The drama is based on the true story of King Jeongjo and Consort Ui-bin Seong.  Deok-im: If you keep studying without rest, you'll get sick. Please take a break. Even just for a moment, try doing something you like instead. Sometimes, you need to take care of yourself.  Yi San: I'm already doing what I like, right here, in my favorite place, with the person I like.  As Yi San said these words, he expressed his feelings by offering Deok-im mandarins that he had lovingly grown himself at Cheongsaru Pavilion. Yeolhwajeong has a quiet and warm atmosphere. Here, the hidden feelings between the two characters became even clearer. Because of their social differences, the two characters couldn't openly share their bittersweet feelings. Their emotions matched perfectly with the beautiful atmosphere here, pulling viewers deeper into their story.  Yeolhwajeong was like a secret spot in the drama. It gently brought out the feelings of the two main characters, making their story even more touching. As you quietly walk through the peaceful garden, following traces of their love that crossed social boundaries, you'll find yourself experiencing a special, relaxing moment. You'll feel warmth deep inside your heart. Why not spend some time at Yeolhwajeong Pavilion, where you can really experience the deep feeling of love?

stories.title: Jeonju Hanok Village, Streets Filled with the Flutter of First Love
stories.audioTitle: Jeonju Hanok Village, Streets Filled with the Flutter of First Love
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! This time, we'll visit Jeonju Hanok Village. It's famous for traditional hanok houses and lovely little alleys.  When you think of Jeonju Hanok Village, elegant curved roofs and peaceful hanok houses probably come to mind first. But this place also has a charming retro feel, with old signs, narrow alleys, and a nostalgic vibe blending beautifully with tradition.  Jeonju Hanok Village is full of traditional beauty and everyday charm. It was also the filming location for the drama Our Beloved Summer, which captured viewers' hearts with honest feelings and youthful excitement. Jeonju Hanok Village has a familiar yet special vibe. It wasn't just a background. It became part of the simple daily lives and feelings of the two young characters.  All around Jeonju Hanok Village, you'll find spots full of Yeon-su and Woong’s memories. There's the hardware store drawn by Woong, the street-corner tavern where they met again after breaking up, and the sunny alley where they finally argued after holding back their feelings.Choi Woong: I wanna do the documentary again, with you.  There were words they couldn't say and feelings that got mixed up, all because they didn't want to burden each other. These emotions blend softly with the beautiful scenery of Jeonju Hanok Village.  Now, Jeonju Hanok Village isn't just about traditional scenery. It's become a place full of stories, mixed with the warm feelings of youth, like love, breakups, growing up, and making memories. Why not take a slow walk through Jeonju Hanok Village, following the feelings from the drama? You might just create some memories you'll remember for a long time.

stories.title: Jeonju Arboretum, the Secret Garden of Jinyowon
stories.audioTitle: Jeonju Arboretum, the Secret Garden of Jinyowon
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! This time, we'll visit Jeonju Arboretum, a place where nature beautifully changes colors with each season.  Jeonju Arboretum is a relaxing spot right in the city. With different themed gardens and all sorts of plants, you can enjoy nature's beauty throughout every season. Among them, the Rose Garden is especially charming with traditional tiled roofs and beautiful roses. It attracted many fans as the filming location for Jinyowon in the drama Alchemy of Souls.  Jinyowon is a place full of secrets about the Jin family's powerful magic. The beautiful garden features blooming red roses, traditional tiled roofs lined up on both sides, and wide stone paths. It perfectly shows a world where magic and destiny meet.  Right at the center of the Rose Garden, you'll see a beautiful arched gate decorated with traditional patterns and elegant tiled roofs. Through the gate, you'll see a lush green forest and beautiful blooming roses. It feels magical, like you're stepping into another world.  Makgeolli Vendor: I've never seen a woman this beautiful before!  As you walk along the peaceful stone path past the traditional gate, you might recall Bu-yeon, the drama's female lead, making her first appearance here. When the makgeolli vendor first saw Bu-yeon in the Rose Garden, he was totally charmed by her mysterious vibe. Bu-yeon's secretive first appearance fit perfectly with the magical feeling of the Rose Garden. It really made an impression. The beautiful and dreamlike garden scenery provided the perfect stage, making her presence even more special.  The scenery here makes a lasting impression, leaving you with a dreamy feeling at every step. How about taking a stroll through Jeonju Arboretum, with its natural beauty and romantic vibe? You can make your day feel special, just like you're in a drama.

stories.title: Hanbyeok Tunnel, Where Hearts Lingered That Summer
stories.audioTitle: Hanbyeok Tunnel, Where Hearts Lingered That Summer
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! This time, we'll visit Jeonju's Hanbyeok Tunnel, a place with its own unique charm in every season.  Hanbyeok Tunnel has a special atmosphere all on its own. The natural cool feeling inside blends nicely with the lush green vines that cover the entrance in summer. This place used to be just a regular road. But after appearing in some famous scenes from the drama Twenty-Five Twenty-One, it started getting attention again.  In the drama, one summer day, Hee-do and Yi-jin stood facing each other. They shared a small secret, promising to be happy for a little while when no one else was around.  Hee-do: From now on, when you're with me, let's be happy secretly, without him knowing. When it's just us, let's be quietly happy for a little bit. This is our secret, okay?  Times were tough, and they had to give up many things, but Hee-do smiled and said they shouldn't give up on happiness. Yi-jin found comfort in her words, and that's when love started growing between them, right here at Jeonju's Hanbyeok Tunnel.  The tunnel where they first shared their little secret ended up being the very place where they said their final goodbye. Even though they knew how they felt about each other, they decided to say goodbye to chase their own dreams. Standing in front of Hanbyeok Tunnel, where they'd made happy memories, they eventually ended up looking in different directions.  Every tunnel has a clear start and finish, maybe just like Yi-jin and Hee-do's relationship. Standing at the beginning, unable to move forward, one of them eventually turned away.   Now, Jeonju Hanbyeok Tunnel isn't just a passageway anymore. It's become a place filled with emotions. Why not take a walk through the tunnel, following the footsteps and emotions of Hee-do and Yi-jin?

stories.title: Seohak-dong Art Village, a Neighborhood that Sparkles Like Youth
stories.audioTitle: Seohak-dong Art Village, a Neighborhood that Sparkles Like Youth
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! This time, we'll explore Jeonju's Seohak-dong Art Village, a charming neighborhood filled with art and romance.  Seohak-dong was once known as Teacher's Village, a place where teachers and students used to live together. Over time, though, it slowly became a forgotten neighborhood. Then artists started moving in one by one, bringing art to life in every alley. Seohak-dong came back to life, thanks to the warm touch of people who love art. Murals in every alley, gardens cared for by residents, and creative studios and charming workshops—all of these have turned Seohak-dong into a colorful art village.  This village is full of art and romance, so it's no surprise that it was chosen as a filming location for the drama Twenty-Five Twenty-One. The show captured the bright, youthful lives of its characters perfectly. Seohak-dong is filled with charming murals. Just walking around here feels warm and lovely, like you're stepping into a scene from a drama. If you're a fan of the drama, you'll be excited to see some familiar places here! The sign for Myeongjin Book Rental, where the main character Yi-jin used to work, is still on the outside wall of the Sori Mill. When you stand in front of the Sori Mill, you can easily picture Hee-do, the main character, constantly running in and out to get her favorite comic, Full House.  Hee-do: Volume 12 just came out! Didn't you know I'd come? Is that really all I mean to you?  Hee-do and her rival Yu-rim playfully argued over who gets to read the new volume of Full House first. Watching Yi-jin try to calm them down always makes everyone smile. The scenery here brings back memories of those pure moments from the past, when you truly loved something with all your heart. Even today, Seohak-dong's lovely alleys, lovely murals, and art studios blend beautifully. The village still has that warm feeling full of youthful excitement and romance.  Why not visit Jeonju's Seohak-dong Art Village, where art blends naturally with everyday life? Experience the feeling of being young again, and bring back some of your brightest memories.

stories.title: Hagindang, Home to Joseon's Greatest Wealth and Power
stories.audioTitle: Hagindang, Home to Joseon's Greatest Wealth and Power
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! This time, we'll explore Jeonju's Hagindang, a peaceful traditional house with beautiful gardens and a spacious courtyard.  Jeonju Hagindang is a large traditional house built with special wood from the Amnok River and Odaesan Mountain. Many skilled workers spent a long time carefully constructing this beautiful residence. It's a great example of traditional architecture from late Joseon. You'll notice it's really special, combining royal architectural styles with an ordinary residential house. You can't miss the grand entrance gate connected to the servants' quarters. Its impressive size and beautiful details will instantly catch your eye, letting you feel the dignity and elegance of this traditional house right away.  You might recognize this place from the drama Mr. Sunshine. It appeared in several scenes! In one scene, Eugene Choi, now a U.S. Marine Corps officer, comes here to Jeonju Hagindang to find the person who killed his parents, pointing his gun to get revenge. In the drama, Eugene Choi's parents were house servants, and the man who killed them was one of the richest noblemen in Joseon, second only to the king. Can you think of a more perfect place than Jeonju Hagindang for a story like this? The impressive look and beautiful architecture of this traditional house represent power and wealth, clearly highlighting the conflicts and tension in the drama.  Eugene Choi: Did you take care of my parents' bodies? Did you at least bury them properly? Anpyeong (villain): Back then, that's just how we handled servants' bodies. We just tossed them away! Eugene Choi: Even if that's how things were done back then, you still should've buried them. If you had any humanity at all, you would've done at least that.  These short lines clearly show how harsh the class system was back then. They also remind us about the basic dignity every human deserves. Today, Jeonju Hagindang is more than just a traditional house. It has become a special place filled with historical meaning and scenes from a popular drama. As you walk around this estate, where Eugene Choi's strong emotions played out, take your time and enjoy the peaceful elegance and charm of traditional Korean architecture. In this place full of history, I hope you can find your own special memories.

stories.title: Embracing Love in the Moonlight at Jeonju Hyanggyo
stories.audioTitle: Embracing Love in the Moonlight at Jeonju Hyanggyo
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! This time, we'll explore Jeonju Hyanggyo, an educational space where the noble spirit of Confucianism lives on.  Hyanggyo was a national educational institution established to honor great Confucian scholars, hold memorial ceremonies, and teach Confucianism to local residents. Jeonju Hyanggyo was originally founded during the reign of King Gongmin of the Goryeo Dynasty and moved to its current location during King Seonjo's reign of the Joseon Dynasty, where it still retains its original appearance centuries later.  Inside Jeonju Hyanggyo, buildings such as Daeseongjeon Hall, Dongmu and Seomu Shrines, Gyeseongsa Shrine, and Myeongnyundang Lecture Hall, where students once studied, remain perfectly preserved in their original Joseon-era architectural styles. With its calm, refined beauty and traditional atmosphere still intact despite the passing of time, Jeonju Hyanggyo often serves as a setting in historical dramas.  The charm of Jeonju Hyanggyo was also captured in the drama Love in the Moonlight, too. In the show, Myeongnyundang Hall appeared as Jahyeondang, a dormitory used by Ra-on, who disguised herself as a man, and her bodyguard Byung-yeon, as well as the place where Yoon-sung and Byung-heon studied together during the Crown Prince's youth. This was also the place where the warm scene was shot, with Ra-on comforting Crown Prince Lee Yeong by offering him hearty chicken soup.  Ra-on: “Would you accept some kindness from someone with a rich heart? This kindness comes from me, the richest person in Joseon when it comes to heart.”  Picture Ra-on smiling brightly as she hands Lee Yeong some chicken soup. In that warm moment, his heart flutters, blending perfectly with the peaceful atmosphere of Myeongnyundang and creating a pure, youthful feeling.  In the front courtyard of Daeseongjeon Hall, beneath the blooming red crepe myrtle flowers, a scene was filmed where Lee Yeong helped Ra-on, who was holding a heavy silk parasol, to sit down and rest together.  Lee Yeong: Rest for a bit. I'll read slowly.  They sat beneath a large parasol, Lee Yeong opening a book and gently guiding Ra-on to rest her head on his shoulder. This sweet moment made many viewers' hearts flutter.   Jeonju Hyanggyo is a place where tradition and romance exist side by side. Its refined Joseon architecture and peaceful atmosphere served as the perfect stage to highlight the characters' delicate emotions. The harmony between historical sentiment and the unique charm of Jeonju Hyanggyo deepened viewers' immersion into the characters' story, conveying heart-fluttering excitement and lingering emotions even beyond the screen.   Why not visit Jeonju Hyanggyo yourself? As you recall scenes from Love in the Moonlight, you can experience firsthand the romance and serene atmosphere of this special place.

stories.title: Mystery Beyond the Stained Glass, Jeondong Cathedral
stories.audioTitle: Mystery Beyond the Stained Glass, Jeondong Cathedral
stories.script: "Welcome to your K-Culture journey! The featured destination for this cultural trip is Jeondong Cathedral in Jeonju, a landmark filled with majesty and mystery.  Completed in 1914, Jeondong Cathedral was the first Western-style cathedral in Korea's Honam region, built to honor the country's earliest Catholic martyrs. Thick gray walls, semi-circular arched windows, a central bell tower, and Byzantine-style decorations combine to proudly showcase its historic elegance. Particularly captivating are the stained-glass windows sparkling brightly in the sunlight, showing that this cathedral is more than just a building—it is a spiritual sanctuary.  In this sacred setting, the film Jeon Woochi filmed one of its most suspenseful scenes. The villain ""Hwadam,"" disguised as a woman, enters the cathedral and asks for confession from ""Sinseon,"" who is serving there as a priest, creating a tense moment.  Sinseon (Priest): ""Feel free to speak. God forgives everything."" Hwadam (Woman): ""Um... Is there really a dead cat on my back? Someone told me that before.""  This line might sound like an ordinary conversation, but in fact, it's an important turning point that foreshadows the major conflict between Hwadam and the hero Jeon Woochi. As the conversation continues, Hwadam, disguised as a woman, releases magical creatures sealed inside Sinseon's flask, plunging the peaceful cathedral into chaos. At that moment, Hwadam reveals his true form and recaptures the creatures he had released, successfully gaining Sinseon's trust. In other words, all of this was deliberately planned to provoke conflict between Sinseon and Jeon Woochi.   But why exactly was Jeondong Cathedral selected as the setting for this scene? It’s because the sanctity, peacefulness, and symbolism of light in this place make the message of this scene, where human good and evil collide along with sorcery and faith, even more dramatic and powerful. In this mysterious and majestic space, deception and truth, disguise and revelation sharply contrast.  In this mysterious and majestic space, deception and truth, disguise and revelation stand out even more sharply. Jeondong Cathedral was not merely a backdrop, but an ""actor"" itself, with cinematic tension of its own. Why not stand right now, exactly where the scene unfolded, and relive that breathless moment yourself?"

stories.title: Hagwon Farm, a Little Jeju Island in the Mainland
stories.audioTitle: Hagwon Farm, a Little Jeju Island in the Mainland
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! This time we're visiting Gochang Hagwon Farm. It's a place with breathtaking views, perfect for someone like you who works so hard every day.  Hagwon Farm is located in Gochang County, North Jeolla Province, and covers about 300,000 pyeong, roughly 100 hectares. It's like a huge, living painting of nature, with different flowers blooming every season. In spring, vibrant yellow canola flowers and green barley fill the fields; in summer, sunflowers bloom brightly; and in autumn, white buckwheat flowers create a stunning scene, welcoming visitors with a new beauty each season.  Because it beautifully captures the feeling of all four seasons, Hagwon Farm often appears as a filming location for various movies and dramas. The bright yellow canola flower fields featured in the Netflix drama When Life Gives You Tangerines, which left a lasting impression on viewers, were also filmed right here at Hagwon Farm.  In the drama, the canola flower fields were more than just scenery—they became an important place where feelings of love, conflict, and reconciliation took place.  “I took a long, last look at my eighteen-year-old first love, knowing I would never see him again. And in that yellow spring, I buried my youthful innocence.” As Ae-soon's narration in the drama suggests, these canola flower fields were also a place where the characters could finally let go of the feelings and memories they'd buried deep inside. When the beautiful canola flower fields perfectly contrasted with the turbulent emotions of young men and women, viewers could finally feel deeply immersed, leaving them with a lasting impression.  Hagwon Farm has a timeless warmth and charm that never fades. Why not take your time here and create your own special story? In these fields that warmly embraced the awkward emotions of young people from the island who had very little, perhaps you too can find gentle comfort and relaxation.

stories.title: Mokpo Modern History Museum, a Healing Sanctuary Embracing Time
stories.audioTitle: Mokpo Modern History Museum, a Healing Sanctuary Embracing Time
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture journey! This time, we'll visit Mokpo Modern History Museum, located at the foot of Yudalsan Mountain, where you can enjoy panoramic views of downtown Mokpo.  As the oldest Renaissance-style building in Mokpo, this building is impressive with its stone stairs marked by the passage of time, arched doorways, and ivy-covered red brick façade. All these elements offer a dreamy feeling, as if you've stepped back in time.  In particular, Building No. 1 of Mokpo Modern History Museum condenses the history of Mokpo, from the opening of its port to the Japanese colonial era, into seven key themes. Here, the pain of history closely echoes the sense of emptiness felt by spirits depicted in the popular drama Hotel del Luna, creating a deeply immersive experience for visitors.  Those who linger foolishly, even though their time on earth is over. The guests at my hotel are spirits who've lost their way to the afterlife.  Like the words of Jang Man-wol, the owner of Hotel del Luna in the drama, the symbolism of Mokpo’s oldest building perfectly matches the show's universe as a final resting place for souls and a sanctuary for those lingering between this life and the next. Its solid presence, built over its long history, has transformed the building into a quiet sanctuary where you can momentarily set down unresolved sorrow from life and find peace.  Why not check into Mokpo Modern History Museum yourself? Here, where history and time are layered together, carefully open the door to a moment paused in time. Perhaps here, you'll encounter life's joys and sorrows more deeply than you'd find in any drama.

stories.title: A Stage for Love Set Against a Dramatic Landscape – Seopjikoji, Jeju
stories.audioTitle: A Stage for Love Set Against a Dramatic Landscape – Seopjikoji, Jeju
stories.script: Welcome to K-Culture Travel! This time on K-Culture Travel, our story takes us to Seopjikoji—a beloved gem of Jeju Island that touches the heart in every season.   The name Seopjikoji comes from the Jeju dialect—seopji meaning “narrow land” and koji meaning “cape.” It’s widely known as one of Jeju’s most breathtaking coastal spots, with dramatic views framed by the majestic Seongsan Ilchulbong. The trail begins at the soft white sands of Sinyang Beach and ends in a golden sea of canola blossoms that blanket the hillside—an utterly captivating journey from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll see Jeju ponies calmly grazing, cliffs rising toward the sea, and Seonbawi Rock standing quietly after years of crashing waves—all coming together to show the natural beauty of Jeju.   Every step in Seopjikoji brings a new scenic view. It also served as a symbolic backdrop in the drama  “All In”, where the characters’ lives, love, and separation came together—giving rise to some of the series’ most iconic scenes. With its sea cliffs, crimson hills, and dramatic landscape, Seopjikoji was more than just a backdrop—it breathed with the story, amplified the characters’ emotions, and became a central part of the drama itself.  Inha: “All In... Right now, I’m putting everything on the line to love one person.”  This memorable line, spoken by In-ha as he reflects on the past at the Seopjikoji cliffside, left a lasting impression on many viewers. His all-in devotion to love came together with the dramatic cliffs, walking trails, and ocean views of Seopjikoji to create a powerful finale for the drama.  Walking along the scenic coastal cliffs of Seopjikoji and taking in the view of Seongsan Ilchulbong and the blue sea from the white lighthouse atop the red oreum, you’ll be reminded of some of the most touching scenes from All In.   Why not take a stroll through this dramatic setting—where the two characters' fateful love unfolded—and create a special day of your own?

stories.title: A Sanctuary for Lost Hearts – Mulyeongari Oreum
stories.audioTitle: A Sanctuary for Lost Hearts – Mulyeongari Oreum
stories.script: Welcome to another K-Culture Travel journey! Today’s destination is Mulyeongari Oreum, a dreamy, mystical mountain on Jeju Island.  Mulyeongari Oreum is known for a legend that a water spirit once lived here. Its name comes from the word “Yeongari,” meaning “sacred mountain,” and the unique feature of a crater filled with water. With wide grasslands and forest walking trails, this peaceful and mysterious place was featured in the film “A Werewolf Boy”.  On clear days, Mulyeongari Oreum feels as bright and open as a shepherd’s song. On rainy or foggy days, it turns quiet and dreamlike—just like Cheolsu, the werewolf boy. Cheolsu may look ordinary, but there’s something different and special about him. With his mix of innocence and wildness, strangeness and beauty, there couldn’t have been a better place for his story than Mulyeongari Oreum.  Sooni and Cheolsu tossed a ball back and forth with the neighborhood kids, laughing and running through the open field. Along the forest path, their farewell quietly settled—just like the mist that fills the air.  Soon-i: “I’ll say you ran away, so don’t follow me. Just go, you fool...” Cheolsu: “...Don’t go.”  In the middle of the forest path, Cheolsu stands still, unable to move—while Soon-i slowly walks away. Wrapped in mist, Cheolsu’s gaze lingers in that place—quiet and unmoving, as if frozen in time.  Even now, Mulyeongari Oreum quietly holds someone’s heart. Like it once gave the Wolf Boy a place to rest, it can be a haven for your tired, wandering heart. When you’re worn down by worries you can’t share,  come and feel the quiet comfort that nature offers.

stories.title: A Sea That Embraces the Sky – Pyeongdae Beach
stories.audioTitle: A Sea That Embraces the Sky – Pyeongdae Beach
stories.script: Welcome to the K-Culture Journey. In this episode, we visit the quiet shores of Jeju’s Pyeongdae Beach, where the film Canola comes to life.  Pyeongdae Beach, located in Gujwa-eup on the northeastern coast of Jeju, is a quiet seaside village with clear waters and dark basalt rocks that create a cozy, peaceful atmosphere. It lies along Route 20 of the Jeju Olle Trail, offering gentle comfort to those who pass by on foot.  Pyeongdae Beach is known for its emerald waters, soft sandy shore, and the traditional charm of Pyeongdae Village. Here, generations of haenyeo—Jeju’s legendary women divers—continue their daily lives, harvesting from the sea as their mothers and grandmothers once did. The beauty of Pyeongdae Beach is captured in the film  “Canola”, which gently tells the story of Gyechun, an elderly haenyeo who has lived her life by the sea, and Hyeji, the granddaughter who suddenly enters her world.  Set against the backdrop of Pyeongdae Beach, Gyechun Halmang—who has spent 12 years searching for her lost granddaughter—and the mysterious Hyeji slowly begin to open up to each other, healing old wounds and discovering what it means to be family.  Hyeji: “The reason the sea is wider than the sky… is because it holds the sky within.”  This line brings to mind  Gyechun Halmang herself—a sea that holds the sky. It beautifully reflects the deep, touching bond between Hyeji and her grandmother. The wide sea and blue sky of Pyeongdae Beach were the perfect stage for their emotions.  Why not take a walk along Pyeongdae Beach, where the true spirit of Jeju still lingers, and reflect on your own story? The wide sea, open sky, and the quiet sounds of haenyeo diving come together to create a warm, peaceful scene—perhaps even the perfect place for a new story of your own to begin.

stories.title: A Forest of Life That Breathes with Nature
stories.audioTitle: A Forest of Life That Breathes with Nature
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture Travel. This time, we’re heading into the lush, living forest of Meochewat Trail in Jeju—a place where nature breathes.  The Meochewat Forest Trail, located on the southeastern slopes of Hallasan, means “a field made of stones” in the Jeju dialect. “Meoche” refers to a rocky area overgrown with shrubs, while “wat” means field. Walking through this forest, you can feel the mystery of how this stony land was formed and the powerful life force of nature it holds. This peaceful forest is filled with cypress and cedar trees, camellias, and native azaleas. It’s a place where nature breathes freely—a quiet trail for clearing your mind and finding calm.  Every step along the trail offers a gentle, healing touch. This forest was also featured in the Netflix Korean original film “Kingdom: Ashin of the North”, where the character Ashin first discovers Bulsa Grass—a mythical plant that brings the dead back to life.  “Bulsa grass—the herb that brings back the dead. It comes at a cost.”  That short and strong line shows where the story starts—and when fate begins to change. In the movie, the bulsa grass blends naturally with the deep green forest of Meochewat Trail, making it a powerful symbol of where the story begins.  Outside the screen, the real-life Meochewat Forest Trail has a different kind of pull. It’s far from the busy streets and tall concrete buildings.  As you walk through the forest, the deep greens and browns calm your mind, and the sunlight shining through the trees gently lights up your heart.  Take a deep breath, then slowly let it out. You’ll start to feel the forest’s peace sink into your body. As you walk quietly through nature, why not look for your own bulsa grass? Step by step, you may find a path to healing and peace inside yourself.

stories.title: A Hidden, Mysterious Forest – Sanggari Palm Forest
stories.audioTitle: A Hidden, Mysterious Forest – Sanggari Palm Forest
stories.script: Welcome to K-Culture Travel. Today’s destination is “Jeju’s Sanggari Palm Forest”—a hidden grove of palm trees that looks like a tropical jungle from South America.  Located just a 10-minute drive from Jeju Airport in the western village of Aewol, the Sanggari Palm Forest is an easy-to-reach attraction. Thanks to Jeju’s mild climate, gentle breeze, and abundant sunlight, tall and small palm trees grow thick, creating a tropical scene that feels like you’ve stepped into another country. With photo spots and exotic props scattered throughout, it’s the perfect place to snap memorable pictures.  Thanks to its quiet and mysterious atmosphere, the Sanggari Palm Forest was used for a secret deal scene in the Netflix series  “Narco-Saints”. During the COVID-19 pandemic, when filming abroad was not possible, the crew planted more palm trees to make the forest look like a real South American jungle.  Choi Chang-ho: “Kang, did you eat?” Kang In-gu: “Nah, there wasn’t a rest stop on the way, so I haven’t had a bite. But there’s something tastier than food here, so it’s all good.”  Even in the scene where the main characters talk before a secret deal over two tons of cargo, the palm forest’s exotic and mysterious setting makes it feel like you’re really in South America, heightening the tension and pulling viewers deeper into the story.  A tropical jungle scene you can only find in Jeju! Why not step into this secret and mysterious place and feel like the star of a drama? Create your own unforgettable memory here in the Sanggari Palm Forest.

stories.title: An Emerald Island Where the Blues of Life Drift in the Breeze
stories.audioTitle: An Emerald Island Where the Blues of Life Drift in the Breeze
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture Travel experience. This time, our journey takes us to Udo, a small island embraced by the sea off the coast of Jeju.  Udo is an island where clear waters, beaches with unique scenery, and quiet fishing villages come together to create a peaceful charm. Each season brings a different beauty to this small island. Its name, meaning “Cow Island,” comes from its shape—it looks like a cow lying down. Locals also call it “So-seom” or “Shwe-seom” in the Jeju dialect, both meaning the same thing.  One of Udo’s biggest charms is its variety of beaches. Among them, Seobin Baeksa stands out with its rare pink coral sand, officially recognized as a natural monument. In addition to this white-sand beach with emerald water, Geommeolle Beach is covered with black lava pebbles and offers great views of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Hagosudong Beach, with its clear and calm waters, is perfect for swimming.  Udo’s deep blue sea, sparkling sunlight, unique landscape, and cozy fishing villages made it the perfect setting for the drama “Our Blues”. The show follows people at different points in their lives—some at the end, some at the beginning—capturing their joys and sorrows in a heartfelt way. With Udo’s colorful sea changing with the water’s depth, the island became a powerful backdrop for stories that speak to all of us.  “There is one clear mission we must never forget: we were not born to suffer or to be unhappy—we were born only to be happy. I hope everyone finds happiness!”  This message appeared during the final credits of Our Blues, set against the calm and beautiful sea of Udo. It gently reminded viewers of what truly matters in life—and stayed with them long after the screen faded to black. Just like the people of this small island who rely on one another to live, Udo was the perfect setting to tell the tangled stories of the drama’s characters. With its gentle scenery and heartfelt stories, the island offers comfort and peace to all who visit.  Why not ride a bike along Udo’s scenic coastline or take a peaceful walk on the beach? As you listen to the waves and breathe in the sea breeze, you might feel the same warm message of comfort and hope from Our Blues. And before you know it, the view inside your heart may begin to change, just like the tides.

stories.title: Shindo Port, Where Hearts Meet Dolphins
stories.audioTitle: Shindo Port, Where Hearts Meet Dolphins
stories.script: This time, our journey takes us to Shindo Port, nestled at the western edge of Jeju, home to wild dolphins and stories carried by the sea breeze.  On the eastern side of Jeju, just below Seongsan Ilchulbong, lies Sindo Port—a small harbor with a quiet charm, far from the crowds. Gentle waves roll in, and the slow, steady rhythm of fishermen at work creates a peaceful scene. It’s the kind of place that truly feels like Jeju—where the sea, people, and nature live in quiet harmony. Sindo Port is known as a place where wild dolphins often appear above the waves. After featuring in the drama  “Extraordinary Attorney Woo”, it became a beloved spot for both dolphin lovers and fans of the show.   In the drama, Young-woo, a lawyer who loves whales, travels to Jeju to work on a new case.  Young-woo: Jeju? You mean that Jeju—where Sampal, Chunsam, and Boksun, once made to perform in dolphin shows, were finally set free into the sea with their babies after a ruling by the Supreme Court?  The scene of wild dolphins swimming freely in the Jeju sea—the one Young-woo dreamed of—was found right here in Shindo Port. The dolphins still swim freely in these waters, calling it home—and just like Young-woo, our hearts are filled with excitement as we wait to see them.  Listen closely to the sound of the waves, and you might hear a dolphin's breath in the distance. Suddenly, a fin breaks the calm surface of the sea, and beyond it, Jeju’s wide horizon unfolds.  Watching the dolphins swim freely reminds us of the warm, living spirit that fills Shindo Port. As pods of dolphins pass by, with the clear blue sea and gentle waves around you, a sense of peace washes over—and a smile naturally appears.  Why not take a break from everything and slowly enjoy a peaceful moment here in Jeju, where nature and life move together as one?

stories.title: Gapado, A Romantic Island for Healing
stories.audioTitle: Gapado, A Romantic Island for Healing
stories.script: Welcome to your K-Culture Travel! This time, we’re visiting Gapado Island—a quiet place that still holds the charm of old Jeju.    Just a 10-minute ferry ride from Jeju’s main island, Gapado is a peaceful village where bicycles suit the scenery better than cars, and untouched nature surrounds you. Waves of green barley sway gently in the wind, offering comfort to a weary heart. As you cycle along the long coastal path, a deep sense of peace slowly takes over, as if the outside world has faded away.  With its scenic blend of green barley fields and blue sea, Gapado was also a main filming location for the romantic comedy  “King the Land”, a story about two people healing from past wounds as they search for true happiness and love. In the drama, Won, who strives for perfection, and Sa-rang, who always tries to keep smiling, find comfort on this quiet island and slowly begin to open their hearts to each other.  Won: “They say it’s really nice at the far end.” Sa-rang: “Let’s go.”  While waiting for the boat, Won rents a bicycle and asks Sa-rang to join him. They ride along the coastal trail of Gapado, enjoying the barley fields, the scenic shore, and the cool sea breeze—as their hearts draw naturally closer. It may seem like a light, ordinary moment, but it becomes a small turning point in their relationship.  The blue sea surrounding the island and the golden barley fields swaying gently in the wind create a romantic and dreamy landscape. The warm scenery and atmosphere of Gapado became a natural part of the story, gently reflecting the growing feelings between the two.  Like the characters in the drama, take your time and feel the beauty of Gapado. In the calm of this island, the feelings you forgot in your busy life may quietly return, reminding you that love often begins in the smallest moments. As the breeze brushes past your ear and the waves whisper to the shore, may your own special feelings slowly awaken.

stories.title: Ojo Port, A Place to Pause and Breathe
stories.audioTitle: Ojo Port, A Place to Pause and Breathe
stories.script: Welcome to K-Culture Travel. This time, our story takes you to Ojo Port, a hidden sunrise spot on Jeju Island.  Ojo Port is famous for its view of Seongsan Ilchulbong rising above the sea, and it offers a beautiful landscape that captures the unique mood of Jeju. The name “Ojo” means “When the sun rises over Ilchulbong, it shines on me first.” Known for its sunrise and sunset views, this place is a key setting in the drama “Welcome to Samdalri”, where the main character Samdal returns to her hometown in Jeju to reconnect with her family, friends, and her first love, Yongpil. With its beautiful scenery and emotional connection to the drama, Ojo Port has become a new must-visit spot on Jeju travel itineraries.  Ojo Port was home to familiar spots from the drama, like the “Lucky Convenience Store” and the “Samdalri Bus Stop,” where the five close friends often gathered. It served as a place where the characters laughed, chatted, and shared their daily lives.  Sitting side by side in front of a stone-walled house, they gaze at Seongsan Ilchulbong and the calm sea. The scene unfolds like a quiet movie moment—inviting a pause, and making you want to linger.  Samdal: “In a world where everything changes so quickly, I found the way to stay grounded and true to myself—in my hometown, Samdalli.”  Like this line, Ojo Port became a place to gather scattered thoughts and a setting for rediscovering oneself. It’s not flashy—that’s what makes it feel more sincere. The familiar scent of the sea wraps gently around your heart.  Here at Ojo Port, where the beauty of nature meets the emotion of the drama, why not look out at the sea and quietly reflect on your own story?

stories.title: Woljeongri Beach, Jeju, Unspoken Love Carried by the Wind and Waves
stories.audioTitle: Woljeongri Beach, Jeju, Unspoken Love Carried by the Wind and Waves
stories.script: Welcome to K-Culture Travel. Our destination this time is Woljeongri Beach in Jeju, where emerald waters and dark basalt rocks create a stunning contrast that’s simply captivating.  The name “Woljeongri” means “where the moon lingers.” According to a local story, the full moon rising above the horizon—where the sea meets the sky—was so beautiful that even the moon didn’t want to leave. With its white sand, black lava rocks, and clear emerald waters, this jewel of a beach sits on the eastern side of Jeju, in Gujwa-eup.  Woljeongri Beach, where the charm of the moon meets the breath of the sea, was also the filming location for a key scene in the drama “Tell Me That You Love Me.” This is where the deaf painter Jin-woo and the actress Mo-eun first meet—a setting so perfect, it’s hard to believe it was just a coincidence.  Mo-eun: “Can being too different really be a reason?”  At the beautiful Woljeong-ri Beach, Mo-eun says this line as the cool breeze blows—raising a deep question between two people from different worlds. A painter who can’t hear, and an actress who expresses emotion with her voice—are their differences a wall, or could they become a bridge? This question runs through the heart of the drama.  As the sun begins to set, a scarf flies off in the wind. When one reaches to pick it up, the other joins—and in that quiet moment, their worlds gently come together.At sunset, the soft red glow over Woljeongri Beach blends perfectly with the story of the drama. The sound of the waves speaks without words, and the breeze from Jeju gently carries the unspoken feelings exchanged through their eyes—quiet, tender, and deeply moving.  Why not take a walk along Woljeongri Beach, where the feeling of the drama still lingers? Here, the sound of the waves and the breeze carry a silent message. This beautiful beach, filled with a quiet kind of love, will gently embrace you and offer a comfort and peace that words alone cannot express.

stories.title: Dapdong Cathedral, A Sanctuary of Light and Quiet Reflection
stories.audioTitle: Dapdong Cathedral, A Sanctuary of Light and Quiet Reflection
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today’s destination is Dapdong Cathedral in Incheon, where time stands still and light lingers in quiet reverence.  Perched on a hillside overlooking Incheon Port and the open port district, Dapdong Cathedral was established on July 1, 1889, when Father J. Wilhelm of the Paris Foreign Missions Society became its first priest. The cathedral was originally built in a Gothic style, with pointed spires and sharp lines, but in 1937, it was expanded in Romanesque style—adding red brick exteriors, arches, and rounded domes. Even today, the façade—with its three bell towers and pointed dome—feels like a piece of medieval Europe.  Damaged during the Korean War, the cathedral was later restored and designated as Historic Site No. 287 in 1981. In recent years, the surrounding area has been transformed into a public square and rest area, turning the cathedral into a peaceful cultural space open to all.  As dusk falls and you walk along the quiet alleyways toward the cathedral, you’ll come upon the wide plaza known as the “Way of the Cross”. Bronze sculptures depicting the suffering and sacrifice of Jesus Christ are softly lit, adding a solemn stillness to every step.   At the end of the path, Dapdong Cathedral glows in the darkness, quietly leaving a lasting impression. If you visit outside of Mass hours, you can step inside. There, a high ceiling, serene silence, and soft, diffused lighting come together to create a reverent and tranquil atmosphere. At night, as the noise of the outside world fades away, soft light filtering through the stained glass gently fills the space, creating a feeling as if time is moving more slowly.  On nights when you need a break from the rush of city life, why not find quiet comfort at Dapdong Cathedral, where the spirit of the Middle Ages and the glow of peace still remain?

stories.title: Wolmido Island, A Festival by the Sea, Lit by the Lights
stories.audioTitle: Wolmido Island, A Festival by the Sea, Lit by the Lights
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today’s destination is Wolmido Island in Incheon, where dazzling lights meet dynamic energy.  For generations, Wolmido Island has been a symbol of Incheon and a hub of maritime culture. Once a key military stronghold, it has since transformed into one of the city’s most beloved attractions—welcoming visitors of all ages.   Along Wolmido Island’s Culture Street, fountains, food stalls, and street artists offering portraits add to the joy of walking. At Wolmi Theme Park, the air buzzes with laughter from people riding the Ferris wheel, Viking ship, and Disco Pang Pang—all day long.  As the daytime fun winds down, Wolmido Island begins to shine its brightest—at night. From May to October, the Wolmi Moonlight Fountain Show brings music and water together in perfect harmony, with streams dancing to melodies and lights in six to seven vibrant colors adding a sensory touch. Watching the cool bursts of water shimmer and shift with the rhythm, you’ll feel the stress of the day simply melt away.  At the summit of Mount Wolmi, the observatory in Wolmi Park is one of the best spots to take in the night view. The observatory’s design was inspired by the Olympic flame and the curve of the moon. Its glass exterior offers a breathtaking 360-degree view of the city and sea. Look down, and you’ll see the blue waves of the West Sea, the Incheon Bridge, and the port below. Look up, and the city skyline and Jayu Park unfold before your eyes. At sunset, crimson skies stretch across the horizon, and by nightfall, soft lights add a touch of magic to the view.  Set your worries aside for a while, and let the lights of Wolmido Island guide you into a peaceful night.

stories.title: Subong Park, A Place Where Starlight Stays
stories.audioTitle: Subong Park, A Place Where Starlight Stays
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today’s journey leads us to Subong Park in Incheon—a place where the city’s history blooms beneath the stars.  Nestled along Mt. Subongsan in Incheon’s Michuhol District, Subong Park offers sweeping views of the city below. Once a military outpost, it became an amusement park in 1979—bringing joy and memories to children—and today, it remains a cherished retreat for the people of Incheon.  Reflecting Incheon’s changing history, Subong Park is home to a wide range of community sports facilities—from playgrounds and nature classrooms to archery ranges, badminton, tennis, and basketball courts.  It’s also a place of remembrance, with monuments like the Hyunchungtap, a memorial honoring those who served.  Subong Park is especially famous for its nightscape—it was even named one of Incheon’s Top 10 Night Views in 2018. From sunset to 11 p.m., the park hosts the “Starlight Festival,” where eight themed courses inspired by starlight and memory come alive with colorful lights and art installations, creating a dreamlike atmosphere straight out of a fairytale.  The journey begins at the entrance near the cultural center with “Starlight Dream,” a glowing pink path. Next comes “Starlight Walk,” a forest trail sparkling like the Milky Way; “Starlight Amusement Park,” which evokes memories of Subong’s beloved theme park; and “Star of Birth,” where twinkling lights form a radiant galaxy path. Then there’s “Night of Counting Stars,” a celestial forest trail lit in violet and guided by mystical animals, “Garden of Memory,” where forest spirits guard the memorial tower, “Fountain of Memory,” a scenic overlook with sweeping views of Michuhol, and finally “Harmony of Light,” where white starlight dances over an artificial waterfall, illuminating the history of Michuhol. Subong Park offers more than just a night view—it's a one-of-a-kind evening stroll where history, memory, and nature come together.  On this gentle, starlit night, why not take a walk through the stories that linger in Subong Park and find your own moment?

stories.title: Songdo Central Park, A Fantastic Nightscape in the Heart of the City
stories.audioTitle: SongdoCentralPark, A Fantastic Nightscape in the Heart of the City
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today’s journey brings us to Songdo Central Park in Incheon—where city lights reflect softly on the water.  Located between high-rise buildings, Songdo Central Park is Korea’s first seawater park—an urban green space inspired by the country's natural geography. Modeled after New York’s Central Park, it offers water taxis, canoeing, and a variety of cultural and artistic experiences throughout the park.  The park features five themed gardens, each with its own unique charm. At the western end is the Sunset Garden, home to the West Boat House, a waterfront stage, a children’s garden, and striking cube sculptures. In the Sentimental Garden, you can take in the scenery alongside a unique artwork called “Faces of the World,” featuring masks representing 120 countries.  Chojigwon features playful sculptures like the Peeing Boy and a firefly house, blending whimsy with public art. The Strolling Garden is a traditional-themed space where you may spot deer. On its eastern side stands Songhwajeong Pavilion, offering a moonlit view like a scene from a painting. The Terrace Garden features the UN Plaza, the East Boat House, and a traditional game yard—hosting a variety of events throughout the year.  As the sun slowly sets, the surrounding skyscrapers begin to light up, and their reflections shimmer on the water, bringing the city’s night to life. From the East Boat House, you can board a moon boat that gently drifts across the lake—a unique and romantic way to enjoy a night on the water.  Right next to Central Park stands Tri-Bowl—a striking structure with sweeping curves that looks as if a spaceship has landed in the city. Once the lights come on after sunset, it becomes especially beautiful—making it a popular spot for photographers hoping to capture the city’s night view.  For couples, it’s a romantic date spot. For families, it’s a peaceful place to unwind. Songdo Central Park offers a special night to all who visit. So tonight—why not escape into this beautiful nightscape?

stories.title: Sorae Port, A Seaside Village that Comes Alive After Dark
stories.audioTitle: Sorae Port, A Seaside Village that Comes Alive After Dark
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today, we journey to Sorae Port in Incheon—a harbor town steeped in the charm of Korea’s coastal life.  Sorae Port, one of the easiest seaside destinations to reach from the Seoul area, began as a humble ferry dock where small boats once came and went. In 1931, the Sorae Salt Field was developed, and a railway—the Suin Line—was built to connect Incheon and Suwon, transporting sun-dried salt to Japan. Salt workers and cargo ferries gathered here, gradually shaping the dock into a harbor.  Then in 1974, after the completion of Incheon’s Inner Port, shrimp boats began docking at Sorae Port, and the harbor quickly grew into a thriving shrimp market, known as a “shrimp pasi.” Today, it stands as the largest traditional seafood market in the Seoul metropolitan area, drawing millions of visitors each year in search of fresh seafood and fermented delicacies.  But the true charm of Sorae Port begins after the sun goes down. The old Suin Line railway bridge has been reborn as a pedestrian walkway, offering sweeping night views of the harbor and the scent of the sea all around.  Just across the bridge lies Haeoreum Square—a peaceful walkway perfect for enjoying Sorae Port’s nightscape. At the center of the square stands the Shrimp Tower Observatory—shaped like a shrimp, the harbor’s signature catch, and unmistakable from afar. Come at sunset, and the warm colors of the sky will gently spread across the harbor, creating a calm and peaceful scene. Once night falls, seven colors of LED light illuminate the tower, creating a dazzling night view.  The sound of seagulls above the harbor, the sun setting beyond the horizon, and a landscape shaped by time—all come together here in Sorae Port, where the sea breeze carries the quiet romance of a Korean night.

stories.title: Gangguan Port - A harbor filled with history and energy
stories.audioTitle: Gangguan Port - A harbor filled with history and energy
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today, we journey to Gangguan Port in Tongyeong, a place where you can feel the true spirit of harbor life.  Gangguan Port sits in downtown Tongyeong. This small harbor was formed where seawater flows deep into the land. For centuries, it has been part of local people's daily lives. During the Joseon Dynasty, this was a navy base for war boats. It was called the Samdo Sugun Tongjeyeong, or the Three Provinces Navy Command, and it was in charge of the navy in Gyeongsang, Jeolla, and Chungcheong areas. Later, when Japan took over Korea, this place became a main spot for people fighting for freedom. It was a very hard time. So, Gangguan is a place where Tongyeong's good history and its sad past come together.  Today, Gangguan has transformed into a top tourist spot for Tongyeong. Along the waterfront, you'll see many fishing boats lined up. This area is also full of shops selling Tongyeong's famous Chungmu Gimbap, which are small rice rolls, and honey bread. The nearby Central Traditional Market adds even more lively energy with its fresh seafood stores, drawing in many visitors. Three turtle ships and one panokseon float in the harbor. These majestic vessels, traditional Korean warships from centuries past, stand guard like proud reminders of Korea's great naval history.  When the sun goes down, Gangguan becomes even more beautiful. As you walk along the waterfront, you'll discover the Gangguan Bridge, which has become one of Tongyeong's most popular night viewing spots.  Originally called the Gangguan Pedestrian Bridge, locals voted in November 2023 to give it the friendlier name Gangguan Bridge. At night, colorful lights illuminate the bridge, creating a romantic seaside atmosphere. From a bench on the bridge, you can watch fireworks explode over the tour boats in the harbor. It feels like watching a magical festival of lights come to life before your eyes.  Today, Gangguan is much more than just a working harbor. It's become a vibrant gathering place where Tongyeong's history, culture, and daily life all come together. The sea here is as calm and peaceful as a lake, perfectly blending the energy of the city with the tranquil serenity of the ocean. Tonight, take a stroll through Gangguan and let the gentle sea breeze carry you into the stories of Tongyeong.

stories.title: Walking above the sea at night, Chungmu Bridge
stories.audioTitle: Walking above the sea at night, Chungmu Bridge
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today, we journey to Chungmu Bridge in Tongyeong, a bridge that crosses the boundaries between sea and city.  Chungmu Bridge opened in 1967 as a safer and more efficient way to connect downtown Tongyeong with Mireuk Island. Before this bridge was built, people, cars, horse-drawn carts, and bicycles all traveled through the Tongyeong Undersea Tunnel. However, as the tunnel aged and safety concerns grew, vehicle traffic was moved to Chungmu Bridge, marking the beginning of a new transportation era. Near Chungmu Bridge, you can still find a memorial stone for Chaknyang Bridge, which was built during the Japanese colonial period. This monument shows that this area has been the heart of Tongyeong's transportation network for many decades.  Chungmu Bridge spans the Tongyeong Canal. The canal bustles with boats throughout the day, regardless of the tides, creating a beautiful scene where nature and city life blend together harmoniously. This waterway perfectly captures the charm of Tongyeong, often called the Naples of the East. When you walk onto Chungmu Bridge, you'll feel an incredible sense of openness, as if you're walking on clouds, while gazing down at the sparkling waters of the canal below. Looking east from the bridge, you'll see the lively downtown area and the bustling Gangguan Port district. Turn west, and you'll be captivated by the scenic view of Mireuk Island's mountain slopes meeting the sea.  When night falls, Chungmu Bridge reveals a completely different character. The lights from the surrounding harbor reflect off the calm canal waters, creating sparkling silver waves. The bridge pillars feature beautiful murals inspired by Tongyeong-born artist Jeon Hyeok-rim's paintings Tongyeong Port and Canal Bridge, adding vibrant colors to the spectacular nighttime scenery. Chungmu Bridge is also the perfect spot to enjoy the night views of Tongyeong Bridge, which changes colors throughout the evening.  As you walk across Chungmu Bridge with the cool sea breeze, you'll naturally want to stop and enjoy Tongyeong's beautiful night views. On this path above the sea, take a moment to experience the lights and beauty of Tongyeong.

stories.title: Walking beneath the sea, Tongyeong Undersea Tunnel
stories.audioTitle: Walking beneath the sea, Tongyeong Undersea Tunnel
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today, we journey to a secret path beneath the sea, the Tongyeong undersea tunnel.  Built in 1932 to connect Tongyeong with Mireuk island, the Tongyeong undersea tunnel is known as the first underwater tunnel in East Asia. Mireuk island was naturally accessible on foot during low tide, but became an island during high tide. However, as more Japanese fishermen from Okayama region settled in the area during the Japanese colonial period, this tunnel was built to provide easier and more reliable transportation.  This tunnel sits about 13.5 meters below the water surface. It was built by putting up temporary barriers on both sides to block the seawater. Then workers set up forms and poured concrete. This was very advanced technology for its time. In 2005, the tunnel was recognized as National Registered Cultural Heritage No. 201.  The undersea tunnel was once a major route for people, horses, and even vehicles. Now vehicle traffic is banned, and it's loved as a walking path for pedestrians only. At the tunnel entrance, you'll see carved letters that say Yongmun Dalyang. This means reaching Sanyang through the Dragon Gate. Here, Dragon Gate refers to fast-flowing water from an old Chinese story. The legend says that if a carp swims upstream through these rough waters, it becomes a dragon. Sanyang is the old name for Mireuk island.  When night falls, the Tongyeong undersea tunnel becomes even more special. Warm yellow lights softly brighten the tunnel interior, creating a dreamy feeling like traveling back in time. Unlike other night spots filled with bright colorful lights, this place offers a quiet and peaceful atmosphere. It's a perfect space for couples to have quiet conversations or for solo visitors to enjoy deep thoughts.  The Tongyeong undersea tunnel brings together old-world engineering and modern charm. How about taking a slow walk along this path, feeling the calm energy of the night sea deep in your heart?

stories.title: Tongyeong Tower with 360-degree ocean views
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today, we journey to Tongyeong Tower, where you can experience the refreshing blue sea and the vibrant lights of the city all at once.  Tongyeong Tower sits at the entrance to New Geoje Bridge, which connects Tongyeong and Geoje Island. This 7-story building serves as both a large cafe and observation deck. In the past, this was a rest stop for travelers on highways and national roads. It was a complex commercial facility with restaurants, shops, and various convenience services. After renovation in 2016, a large cafe moved in, and it became a new landmark of Tongyeong.  Tongyeong Tower has an ordering area on the 1st floor, seating on the 2nd floor, an observation deck on the 7th floor, and a rooftop. Order your drinks or desserts downstairs, then go up to enjoy the beautiful coastal views through the large windows. The 7th floor has a special 360-degree rotating observatory that you shouldn't miss. The floor slowly turns, so you can enjoy panoramic views of Tongyeong Port, New Geoje Bridge, and countless South Sea islands while just sitting there.  As time passes, Tongyeong Tower becomes even more amazing. As darkness falls over the calm sea, lights begin to twinkle one by one on New Geoje Bridge and in downtown Tongyeong, creating night views that leave visitors speechless. This scene, where the city's bright lights blend with the peaceful sea, creates unforgettable memories, especially when shared with loved ones or family.  During the day, Tongyeong Tower offers the vast openness of sky and sea. At night, it presents the stunning spectacle of bridge lights and city illumination. Here where Tongyeong's day and night meet,  come and experience the ever-changing landscape of light.

stories.title: A night where art and light come together—Nammangsan Sculpture Park
stories.audioTitle: A night where art and light come together
stories.script: Nightscapes of Korea takes you to places where the night shines even brighter. Today, we journey to Tongyeong Nammangsan Sculpture Park, where the art and spirit of Tongyeong come alive.  Nammangsan overlooks Gangguan Port in Tongyeong. Rather than a mountain, it's more like a charming small hill that has long been cherished as a resting place by local residents. Nammangsan overlooks Gangguan Port in Tongyeong. Rather than a mountain, it's more like a charming small hill that has long been cherished as a resting place by local residents. Nammangsan Sculpture Park sits at the summit of this hill. Since 1997, it has established itself as a new cultural space by displaying works from 15 renowned sculptors representing 10 countries worldwide. As you admire these sculptures freely placed against the beautiful backdrop of Tongyeong's sea, you'll find that your body and mind naturally begin to relax.  Nammangsan Sculpture Park is worth visiting not only during the day but also at night. When the sun sets, the area around Nammangsan comes alive with DPIRANG's colorful media art show. DPIRANG is Korea's longest night digital theme park. It takes inspiration from Tongyeong's mural villages called Dongpirang and Seopirang. The park tells the story of lost murals coming back to life, painted with light.  After passing the ticket booth DPIRANG Lodge, you'll follow a path through 15 themed areas including Strange Footprints, The Forgotten Door, Secret Workshop, and Light Orchestra. Walking through these spaces feels like stepping into a fairy tale. Throughout DPIRANG, the spectacular light shows and music create new moments of wonder with every step you take.  Nammangsan Sculpture Park offers a deep experience of Tongyeong's nighttime atmosphere and emotions. The gentle lights along the walking paths, combined with the night sea and city lights, create a captivating landscape completely different from the daytime. When night falls on Nammangsan, come and experience these special moments filled with light and stories.

stories.title: Where Modern Culture Bloomed from Old Factories, Seongsu-dong Cafe Street
stories.audioTitle: Where Modern Culture Bloomed from Old Factories, Seongsu-dong Cafe Street
stories.script: Welcome to K-Culture Travel! This cultural journey features a place where old factories and trendy modern culture exist together beautifully. This is the story of Seongsu-dong Cafe Street.  Since the 1960s, Seongsu-dong was a major industrial area in Seoul, famous for handmade shoes, steel, and printing industries. However, after the IMF financial crisis, many factories closed down and the area went into decline. But in the 2010s, young artists, designers, and entrepreneurs began moving into the area. Through this change, Seongsu-dong was reborn as a center for culture and arts.  The place that best shows this transformation is Seongsu-dong Cafe Street. This street, centered around Yeonmujang-gil, came back to life as old factories were creatively transformed into stylish spaces.
